title: Can raw green chillies clear blemishes and brighten the skin?
claim_text: Eating raw green chillies with food clears blemishes and brightens the skin.
quick_take: A social media post claims that eating raw green chillies can clear blemishes and brightens the skin. Our fact check shows this is mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Can green chillies help clear blemishes? No, eating raw green chillies won't clear blemishes. Blemishes, especially acne, are caused by factors like hormones, bacteria, clogged pores, and inflammation. Green chillies do contain Vitamin C, which supports skin health, but they don't directly help with blemishes. Vitamin C works best when applied topically, not just through diet. While green chillies have antioxidants and anti-inflammatory properties, their effect on blemishes is minimal. For clearer skin, dermatologists recommend proven treatments like salicylic acid, azelaic acid, benzoyl peroxide, or prescription options. Dr Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant in Lucknow, says, 'Green chillies do contain Vitamin C, which is beneficial for your skin, but they aren't a quick fix for blemishes. Acne and other skin blemishes are usually caused by factors like hormonal changes, bacteria, blocked pores, and inflammation. While chillies have antioxidants that can support overall skin health, they won't directly clear up blemishes. To achieve clear skin, it's important to follow a good skincare routine, eat a balanced diet, and address the root causes of acne.' Dr Rashi Soni, a Dermatologist from Rashi Hospital, Hingoli, Maharashtra, says, 'To tackle acne, pigmentation, and blemishes, stick to a simple routine. Cleanse gently, use acne treatments like salicylic acid or benzoyl peroxide, and moisturise based on your skin type. For pigmentation, try products with Vitamin C or niacinamide. And, of course, always wear sunscreen – it helps prevent further damage. A healthy diet, plenty of water, and managing stress will also make a difference. It takes time, but with the right care, your skin will improve.' Similarly, there are claims that morning saliva can cure acne and offer spotless skin. However, this lacks strong scientific evidence. Can eating green chillies brighten the skin? Maybe, but not as quickly or dramatically as claimed. Green chillies contain Vitamin C, which supports collagen production and protects against skin damage from UV rays and pollution. This can help maintain skin firmness and prevent dark spots, but the effect isn't instant. While eating green chillies provides some Vitamin C, they aren't a quick fix for glowing skin. A more effective approach includes a good skincare routine with Vitamin C serums, exfoliation, hydration, and sun protection. Topical Vitamin C works better for targeting pigmentation directly. However, avoid applying green chillies to the skin, as they can cause irritation and a burning sensation. Are there any risks to consuming raw green chillies for skin benefits? Yes, eating too many raw green chillies can be harmful. Green chillies contain capsaicin, which gives them their heat. While capsaicin has anti-inflammatory benefits when applied topically, consuming it in excess can irritate the stomach, causing heartburn, acid reflux, cramps, or even ulcers, particularly for those with digestive issues. If you're eating green chillies for skin benefits, moderation is key. People with conditions like IBS or gastritis should be especially cautious with spicy foods. Moreover, there are concerns about the potential risks of consuming large amounts of chili peppers. While the connection between chili peppers and cancer is still unclear, some studies suggest that capsaicin might influence cancer risk. High chili consumption has been linked to a higher risk of stomach, gallbladder, and mouth cancer, particularly in India. However, these studies don't prove that chilies directly cause cancer, only that heavy consumption is associated with a higher risk. Can other foods or ingredients provide better skin benefits? Yes, many other foods are better for skin health than green chillies. A diet rich in antioxidants, healthy fats, and vitamins can improve skin clarity and brightness. Berries, leafy greens, tomatoes, nuts, seeds, and oily fish like salmon provide essential nutrients like vitamins A, E, and omega-3s, which protect and nourish the skin. However, some social media claims go a step further, suggesting that diet alone can tighten loose skin, which is incorrect. Staying hydrated is just as important. Drinking enough water keeps the skin moisturised, reducing dryness, irritation, and blemishes. THIP Media Take: The claim that eating raw green chillies can clear blemishes and brightens the skin is mostly false. While green chillies contain beneficial nutrients like Vitamin C, they are not a magical remedy for blemishes or skin brightening. Their impact on skin health is minimal at best, and eating them in excess may cause discomfort. Instead of relying on green chillies alone, a balanced diet, proper skincare routine, and healthy lifestyle are key to achieving clear, glowing skin.

quick_take: A social media video claims that rubbing your wrists together regulates your periods. We did the fact check to term it as False.
doctor_explanation:

No, rubbing your wrists together cannot regulate your periods. There is no scientific evidence to support the idea that wrist rubbing affects menstrual cycles. The claim lacks any basis in gynaecological or medical research. The video suggests that specific "ovary and uterus points" exist on the wrists, but this concept is not present in any medical literature. The idea appears to be a misinterpretation of acupressure, a practice from Traditional Chinese medicine. title: Can shampoo, toothpaste and coffee make your skin super white?
claim_text: A paste of shampoo, toothpaste and coffee can make your skin super white in just one use. The video promotes this combination as a fast, effective, and affordable method to lighten skin tone, stating it is the best home remedy for fair skin.
quick_take: A social media post claims that a paste of shampoo, toothpaste and coffee can make your skin super white in just one use. We did the fact check to term this claim as false.
doctor_explanation: Dr Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant in Lucknow, explains: "None of these ingredients are meant for skincare, and using them together can do more harm than good. Shampoo is formulated for hair, not skin, and can strip away natural oils, leading to dryness. Toothpaste contains abrasives and chemicals like fluoride, which may irritate the skin, causing redness, itching, or even allergic reactions. While coffee has antioxidants, there's no evidence to suggest it can whiten skin." He further explains: "Combining these ingredients disrupts the skin's natural pH, resulting in irritation, dryness, and potential long-term damage. There's also a risk of infections if unsterilized or inappropriate use occurs. Skin colour mainly depends on melanin, and this mixture won't alter melanin production. For safe and effective skin treatments, it's best to consult a dermatologist, who can recommend options like topical creams, chemical peels, or laser therapy based on your skin's needs." Dr Annusuiya Gohil, MD Scholar at the All India Institute of Ayurveda, provides perspective: "Skin fairness primarily depends on genetics, followed by the environment in which we grow up. While a lot can be done to improve skin brightness, the real skin tone cannot be changed—it can only be enhanced. More specifically, one can restore the original skin tone that may have dulled over time due to ageing, exposure to harsh environments, and factors like diet and medication. Topical applications cannot change skin colour in any way." The article notes that no scientific evidence supports this combination as a method for changing skin tone. While coffee has anti-tyrosinase activity according to lab studies from 2016 and 2020, this effect has not been proven in humans. Toothpaste contains abrasive particles and chemicals like fluoride which can irritate or damage the skin when applied. Shampoos are for hair care and are not safe for skin use. Coffee can offer sun protection according to a 2015 study and is rich in antioxidants providing a temporary exfoliating effect, but does not affect melanin production which determines natural skin colour.

title: Can Sheetkari Pranayama cure toothache without medication?
claim_text: An Instagram post claims that Sheetkari Pranayama, a breathing technique, can cure toothache. The post suggests practising this twice a day for fast results without needing medication.
quick_take: A social media post claims that Sheetkari Pranayama can cure toothache without medications. We did the fact check to term this claim as False.
doctor_explanation: Can Sheetkari Pranayama cure toothache? No, there is no scientific evidence to suggest that Sheetkari Pranayama can cure toothache. Sheetkari Pranayama is a traditional breathing exercise known to reduce stress and promote relaxation. A 2017 study also indicates that it has the potential to lower systolic blood pressure in hypertensive people. However, toothaches are caused by dental issues such as cavities, infections, or gum disease, none of which can be cured by breathing techniques. While Sheetkari Pranayama may help reduce stress, it does not address the root causes of dental pain. Dental issues require professional care from a dentist to identify and treat the underlying problem. Dr Snigdha, BDS, MDS, Vananchal Dental College and Hospital, Garhwa, Jharkhand, says, "I understand that people often seek natural or alternative methods to ease tooth pain, like breathing exercises. However, it's essential to recognise that while techniques like Sheetkari Pranayama can reduce stress, they don't address the underlying causes of toothache. Tooth pain is often a sign of issues like decay or infection, which need proper dental treatment. Ignoring these problems in favour of alternative remedies can lead to complications. Breathing exercises can help you feel more relaxed, but only professional care can resolve the root of the problem." We also reached out to Dr Annusuiya Gohil, MD Scholar at the All India Institute of Ayurveda. She states, "Sheetkari Pranayama is a breathing technique that involves inhaling air through the gaps between your teeth while making a hissing sound. It has several benefits like calming the mind, cooling the body, stimulating the endocrine system, etc. I have not heard or read anywhere in yoga sutra or yoga related books that it can help in curing tooth related problems. Toothache is usually related to either tooth problems itself or sometimes it is reflex pain which can only be treated by treating the root cause." Similar to this, people also suggest mustard oil, turmeric and rock salt to cure toothaches. Unfortunately, there's no strong scientific evidence to support this popular home remedy. Can Sheetkari Pranayama improve oral health? Not directly. There is no evidence to suggest that Sheetkari Pranayama improves oral health. Although Sheetkari Pranayama is beneficial for mental relaxation, no scientific study supports its use for dental health or preventing tooth decay, infections, or gum diseases. Maintaining oral health requires regular brushing, flossing, and professional dental care. A 2023 study noted that pranayama could help reduce stress-related conditions such as bruxism (teeth grinding) and burning mouth syndrome. However, it did not suggest that pranayama could "cure" tooth pain or other dental issues. Therefore, it is important to rely on proven dental hygiene practices rather than alternative methods like pranayama for oral health. Does Sheetkari Pranayama relieve stress-related tooth pain? Maybe, but it won't treat the underlying dental problem. Stress-related habits, like teeth grinding (bruxism), can lead to tooth pain. In these cases, breathing exercises such as Sheetkari Pranayama may help reduce stress and, by extension, the severity of teeth grinding. However, this does not address the root cause of the dental pain itself. To manage tooth pain caused by stress, a combination of dental treatments (such as using a mouth guard) and stress reduction techniques is more effective. Sheetkari Pranayama can be part of a stress management routine, but dental care is still necessary to prevent further damage to your teeth. Should you see a dentist for a toothache? Yes, always. Toothache needs professional care to identify and treat the cause. Toothaches can result from cavities, gum infections, or other serious dental problems. These issues require a dentist's evaluation and treatment. Ignoring a toothache can worsen the condition, potentially leading to infections or abscesses. While Sheetkari Pranayama can help reduce stress, it will not cure a dental issue. The best way to treat tooth pain is to consult a dentist who can offer the right diagnosis and treatment. Do not fall for home remedies like potash, alum, salt and pepper for curing tooth pain. Home remedies or breathing exercises should not replace medical intervention in dental health matters. Dr Pooja Sharma, BDS, MDS, NIMS University, Jaipur, Rajasthan, states, "I always advise anyone experiencing a toothache to seek professional help as soon as possible. Tooth pain is often a sign of deeper issues, such as decay, infections, or gum problems, that require proper treatment. Delaying a visit to the dentist could lead to more severe complications, like abscesses or tooth loss. While home remedies may provide temporary relief, only a dentist can diagnose and treat the actual cause, ensuring long-term oral health."

title: Can sitting in chest-deep water at 40°C cause rapid weight loss?
claim_text: Sitting in water at a temperature of 40°C, with the water level up to the chest, can help lose 500 grams to 1 kilogram of weight in an hour. Staying in such water for two to three hours can help achieve weight loss goals of up to three kilograms.
quick_take: A social media post claims that sitting in chest-deep water at 40°C can cause rapid weight loss. We did the fact check and termed this claim as false.
doctor_explanation: It may, but only through water loss. Sitting in warm water can lead to sweating, which results in the loss of fluids from the body. This temporary weight loss is due to dehydration, not fat loss. Once you rehydrate by drinking water, the weight returns. A 2022 study looked at how hot water immersion (HWI) affects weight loss. Athletes sat in hot water (40.3°C) for 20 minutes, followed by a heated blanket. They lost about 2.2 kg, but this weight loss was mostly due to fluid loss, not fat loss. Blood tests showed changes, but these returned to normal once the athletes rehydrated. The weight lost during the hot bath was quickly regained after they drank fluids and ate. This shows that the weight loss from hot water immersion is temporary and not a lasting way to lose fat. It's just fluid loss that gets added back once the body rehydrates. We connected with Dr Brendan Egan, one of the researchers of this particular study. He is the Associate Professor of Sport and Exercise Physiology, and currently Head of School for the School of Health and Human Performance at Dublin City University. He responded: 'That work we did focused on what we term 'rapid weight loss' in the context of combat sports and fighters trying to 'make weight' in their weight category. We used hot water immersion to induce sweating and loss of body weight through dehydration. So yes, we did induce weight loss of that magnitude in a short period of time by hot water immersion, but it was almost certainly all 'water weight'/dehydration. As you can see in the data from our study, all the weight was regained by the next day when the participants were rehydrated. So the weight loss is indeed rapid, but mostly weight lost as sweat, making it transient until the person is rehydrated.' The body sweats to regulate temperature in hot conditions, including warm water immersion. However, this method is not a healthy or effective way to manage weight, as it does not reduce fat. While some weight loss methods, such as sitting in heated water, are gaining attention, it's also important to understand the role of specific foods in promoting weight management. For instance, cucumbers have been touted for their health benefits and might help when included in your daily diet. We reached out to Dr Ubaid ur Rahman, General Physician, Holy Mission Clinic, New Delhi, for his take on warm water immersion method for weight loss. He says, 'Sitting in warm water might lead to temporary weight loss, but this is primarily due to fluid loss through sweating. This is not actual fat loss, and the weight will quickly return once you rehydrate. Sustainable weight loss requires a combination of a balanced diet and regular physical activity. It's important to focus on healthy, long-term habits rather than quick fixes like warm water immersion, which doesn't have lasting effects on body fat.' Is the claimant a reliable source of health information? No, 'Dr Biswaroop Roy Chowdhury' is not a trustworthy source for health advice. He claims to be a doctor, but he doesn't have the proper medical qualifications. In fact, he holds an honorary PhD from an unaccredited university, which is considered a scam. Chowdhury has promoted harmful ideas, like denying the reality of diseases such as diabetes and COVID-19. He has also made false claims, such as using hot water immersion to treat kidney disease, which we have debunked before. His misleading advice has led to legal trouble, including a criminal case for offering fake treatments that caused harm. It's important to be cautious about the information he shares. No, warm water immersion does not lead to long-term weight loss. Fat loss, which is the goal of sustainable weight management, occurs when the body burns more calories than it consumes. This requires a combination of healthy eating, physical activity, and a calorie deficit. The weight loss claimed in the video is only temporary and linked to fluid loss. Dehydration can also cause fatigue, dizziness, and other health risks if prolonged. Yes, prolonged exposure to warm water can be harmful. Sitting in water at 40°C for extended periods increases the risk of dehydration, heat exhaustion, or even heatstroke. Long-term exposure to warm or hot water actually negatively affects the skin barrier too. These conditions can be dangerous, especially for individuals with underlying skin conditions or health issues. Furthermore, rapid fluid loss can lead to an imbalance in electrolytes, which are important for muscle and nerve function. Severe dehydration can strain the heart and kidneys. We spoke with Dr Almas Fatma, MBBS, Diploma in Family Medicine, PG in Digital Health, General Physician from Navi Mumbai, to learn about safe weight loss approaches. She says, 'Losing weight safely and effectively is all about consistency and balance. A healthy diet, rich in whole foods like vegetables, lean proteins, and whole grains, combined with regular physical activity, provides the foundation for lasting weight loss. Extreme diets or quick fixes that promise rapid results can harm your health in the long run. Instead, focus on small, manageable changes and aim for steady progress over time. Quick weight loss methods can lead to muscle loss, nutritional imbalances, and other health issues. Always consult a professional before starting any weight loss plan to ensure it's tailored to your needs.' THIP Media Take: The claim that sitting in chest-deep water at 40°C can cause rapid weight loss is false. While temporary water weight loss is possible, it is not a sustainable or healthy method for weight management. Instead, focus on evidence-based approaches like balanced nutrition and regular exercise for long-term results.

title: Can skipping baths during winter increase lifespan by 34%?
claim_text: A viral Instagram reel claims that not bathing in winter could increase lifespan by 34%. The post says that bathing everyday removes the skin's natural oils, causing dryness and inflammation. It also mentions that in cold weather, the body's immune system works harder to stay warm. Based on this, the post tells people to stop bathing during the winter months.
quick_take: A social media post claims that skipping baths during winter can increase lifespan by 34%. We did the fact check and termed this claim as mostly false.
doctor_explanation:
The fact check addresses several claims:

1. **Does infrequent bathing really improve skin microbiome diversity?** While it's true that the skin's microbiome plays a role in skin health, the idea that infrequent bathing directly supports this biodiversity is misleading. Research suggests that over-washing the skin can disrupt the microbiome, but this doesn't mean skipping baths entirely is beneficial. It's about finding balance - bathing regularly with mild soap and lukewarm water helps maintain natural oils without stripping them away.

Dr Rashi Soni, Co-founder and Consulting Dermatologist at Rashi Hospital in Mumbai, explains: "Regular bathing is good for your skin as it helps remove dirt and oils. However, it's important to use lukewarm water and gentle, moisturising soaps to avoid drying out your skin. After bathing, apply a moisturiser while your skin is still damp to lock in hydration. Bathing properly, along with using the right products, helps maintain a healthy skin microbiome and prevents dryness and irritation."

2. **Can skipping baths in winter prevent skin dryness and inflammation?** Dry skin during winter is a common issue caused by cold weather and low humidity. While skipping baths might seem like a way to prevent dryness, focusing on proper skin hydration and moisture retention is more important. Bathing with harsh soaps or hot water can strip the skin of oils, but using gentle cleansers and applying moisturisers after bathing can help maintain skin health. Regular bathing with right products keeps skin clean and hydrated.

Dr Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant in Lucknow, says: "No, skipping baths in winter is not an effective way to prevent skin dryness and inflammation. In fact, regular bathing, when done properly, helps maintain skin hydration by removing dirt and pollutants. However, during winter, the cold air and indoor heating can dry out the skin, so it's important to use lukewarm water and mild, moisturising soaps. After bathing, applying a good moisturiser is key to locking in hydration and protecting the skin's natural barrier. While over-bathing or using harsh products can exacerbate dryness, skipping baths altogether can lead to other skin issues like bacterial build-up. Maintaining a balance is crucial for healthy skin."

3. **Does the immune system work harder in winter, and can skipping baths support it?** The immune system does adapt to environmental changes including cold weather, but this has nothing to do with whether you bathe or not. The body's immune response depends on factors like nutrition, sleep, and overall health. While cold weather can cause the body to work harder to maintain core temperature, skipping baths doesn't offer any direct benefit to immune function. Good hygiene practices including regular bathing are essential for overall health, especially during winter when people spend more time indoors.

4. **Can skipping baths increase lifespan by 34%?** There is no scientific evidence to support the claim that skipping baths can increase lifespan by any percentage, let alone 34%. Lifespan depends on many factors including genetics, lifestyle choices, diet, and overall healthcare. While bathing habits are important for hygiene and skin health, they do not directly affect longevity. The study in Nature Communications likely discusses how certain lifestyle choices can impact the skin's microbiome, but this doesn't translate into benefits for lifespan.

Dr Almas Fatma, MBBS, Diploma in Family Medicine, PG in Digital Health, General Physician from Navi Mumbai, says: "No, skipping baths will not increase your lifespan by 34%. There are many factors which influence our lifespan like genetics, diet, exercise, and overall health. However, bathing habits are not directly linked to how long you live. Bathing regularly helps maintain hygiene and skin health, but it doesn't have a significant impact on lifespan."

Additionally, some people claim that improper bathing can cause paralysis, brain haemorrhages, and increases the risk of strokes. These claims are not scientifically accurate.

title: Can the double ear pull manoeuvre improve blurry eyesight?
claim_text: Performing the "double ear pull manoeuvre" releases fascia around the eyes and can help improve blurry vision.
quick_take: A social media post claims that double ear pull manoeuvre can improve blurry eyesight. We did the fact check and found it to be false.
doctor_explanation: Fascia manipulation, such as the "double ear pull manoeuvre," may help with muscle relaxation and improve circulation in certain areas. However, blurry vision usually happens because of refractive errors, eye strain, or underlying medical conditions like cataracts or glaucoma. These issues are unrelated to the fascia. Fascia is a connective tissue that surrounds muscles, organs, and other structures in the body. Manipulating it might help reduce tension or improve flexibility, but there's no evidence that it affects your eyes or fixes vision problems. If you have blurry eyesight, it's important to see an eye specialist rather than relying on fascia-related techniques. Dr Shilpa Ghosh, Ophthalmologist, Cataract and Cornea Surgeon at Drishti Netralaya, Dibrugarh, Assam, says, "Fascia manipulation isn't a proven way to fix blurry vision. Vision problems usually come from issues like refractive errors or cataracts, and various other eye conditions, not anything to do with the fascia. While it might help with muscle tension, it won't address what's actually causing blurry eyesight. It's always best to see an eye specialist for the right treatment." Dr Almas Fatma, MBBS, Diploma in Family Medicine, PG in Digital Health, and General Physician from Navi Mumbai, states, "Fascia manipulation is not a proven method to improve blurry vision. Blurry vision typically results from issues with the eyes, such as refractive errors, cataracts, or other eye conditions. While fascia manipulation may help with muscle tension or other body-related issues, it doesn't address the underlying causes of blurry vision. For clearer vision, it's important to consult with an eye care professional to determine the right treatment based on your specific condition." The fascia around the eyes doesn't affect vision. Vision relies on the cornea, lens, retina, optic nerve, and the brain's visual processing centres. While fascia supports the muscles around the eyes, manipulating it cannot change how the eyes focus or process light. Claims that fascia manipulation can "release tension" and improve vision are anecdotal and lack scientific backing. Eye exercises or relaxation techniques may help reduce eye strain, but they cannot correct refractive errors or other causes of blurry vision. For refractive errors, wearing glasses or contact lenses, or opting for surgeries like LASIK, can help. If the problem is eye strain, taking regular breaks from screens (using the 20-20-20 rule) or improving lighting can make a difference. If a medical condition is causing blurry vision, specific treatment is necessary. For example, one can manage dry eyes with artificial tears, while cataracts might require surgery. Dr Isha Agarwalla, Ophthalmologist, from Drishti Netralaya, Dibrugarh, Assam, shares her expert insights: "Blurry vision can usually be improved with the right treatment, but it all depends on the underlying cause. If refractive errors are to blame, glasses, contact lenses, or LASIK surgery can provide clear vision. However, if cataracts are the issue, surgery is often required to restore sight. The key to finding the most effective solution is a proper diagnosis from an eye care professional, who can guide you toward the right treatment based on your specific condition." While the "double ear pull manoeuvre" itself might not directly harm the eyes, pulling on the face too much or in the wrong way can cause discomfort or even injury. Applying pressure near the eyes without knowing the right technique can strain sensitive areas.

title: Can three dates a day prevent hair loss and boost growth?
claim_text: According to an Instagram post, eating three dates a day can prevent hair loss, strengthen hair follicles, and promote faster hair growth due to their iron content.
quick_take: A social media post claims that three dates a day can prevent hair loss and promote hair growth. We did the fact check to term this as mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Dr Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition, says, "Dates are healthy, but their iron content isn't enough to prevent hair loss. They provide around 0.2-1 mg of iron per 100 grams, while adults need 8-18 mg daily. To meet this with dates alone, you'd have to eat far too many." She adds, "Better sources of iron include spinach, lentils, red meat, and fortified cereals. Pairing these with vitamin C-rich foods like oranges improves iron absorption. While dates can be part of a balanced diet, they cannot fix hair loss by themselves." Dates alone cannot strengthen hair follicles or stimulate hair growth. Hair health depends on a variety of nutrients, including protein, biotin, zinc, and vitamin D. While dates contain natural sugars, fibre, and potassium, they cannot provide all the nutrients required for hair growth. Factors such as genetics, hormones, stress, age, and medical conditions also play significant roles in hair health. A 2018 study highlights that date seed oil, rich in amino acids and vitamins, may contribute positively to promoting hair growth. Similarly, a 2022 study notes that date seed oil benefits skin and hair with its bioactive compounds, antioxidants, and nutrients. It supports scalp health, promotes hair growth, and protects skin from UV damage, making it a valuable ingredient in various skincare and haircare products. But these studies do not say anything about the impact of dietary intake of dates on hair. Adding dates to your diet alone won't significantly impact hair growth unless paired with other nutrient-dense foods for healthy hair and a balanced lifestyle. Iron deficiency is just one of many causes of hair loss. While iron-deficiency anaemia can lead to hair thinning, hair loss may also result from hormonal imbalances, stress, medications, or other nutritional deficiencies. If iron deficiency is identified as the cause, a combination of iron-rich foods and, if necessary, iron supplements prescribed by a healthcare provider can help. However, relying on dates alone or any single food will not address the broader causes of hair loss, especially if iron deficiency is not present. Dr Rashi Soni, Co-founder and Consulting Dermatologist at Rashi Hospital in Mumbai, shares, "Hair growth is affected by many factors, including genetics, hormones, and overall health. A diet rich in vitamins A, C, D, E, and minerals like zinc and iron helps promote healthy hair. Managing stress and following a good hair care routine are also key. Healthy hair requires consistent care and attention to truly thrive."

title: Can Tilasmi Moti help soothe teething discomfort in babies?
claim_text: An Instagram post claims that Tilasmi Moti, a teething pendant made of five metals, can ease teething discomfort in babies. It also says the pendant helps prevent fever, diarrhoea, and gum swelling, balances body heat, keeps babies calm, aids digestion, and protects them from negative energies.
quick_take: A social media post claims that Tilasmi Moti can help soothe teething discomfort in babies. Our fact check found that this claim is false.
doctor_explanation: There is no scientific proof that wearing a Tilasmi Moti can ease teething discomfort. Teething symptoms, like gum irritation and mild pain, occur as teeth push through the gums. Experts recommend safe remedies, such as teething rings or gentle gum massages, to soothe these symptoms. The idea that a pendant can relieve pain or irritation isn't backed by science or biology. In fact, in December 2018, the FDA issued a warning against using teething jewellery for babies, children, and even adults with functional needs. They highlighted serious risks, including choking and strangulation, and reported cases of injuries and deaths caused by such items, including amber teething necklaces. Dr Snigdha, BDS, MDS, from Vananchal Dental College and Hospital, Garhwa, Jharkhand, says, "There's no scientific evidence to support that Tilasmi Moti helps ease teething discomfort. For safe and effective relief, it's best to use methods like teething rings, a cool washcloth, or gentle gum massage, which are proven to provide comfort for babies." Dr Pooja Sharma, BDS, MDS, NIMS Jaipur, Rajasthan, clarifies, "Although traditional remedies like Tilasmi Moti are often used, there's no proof they help with teething pain. It's safer and more effective to rely on healthcare professional-recommended methods like chilled teething rings or soft, cool foods to ease your child's discomfort." Regarding prevention of fever and diarrhoea: Teething does not cause fever, diarrhoea, or other systemic symptoms. These issues are usually coincidental and unrelated to the teething process. A 2000 study found that teething in babies is linked to mild symptoms such as drooling, gum-rubbing, irritability, and a slight rise in temperature, all of which typically occur within an 8-day teething window. However, serious symptoms like high fever or illness are not caused by teething. A 2019 study further revealed that many parents mistakenly associate teething with symptoms like fever and diarrhoea. As a result, they often turn to remedies such as necklaces, homeopathic tablets, or over-the-counter medicines. The study also highlighted that many parents are unaware that delayed tooth eruption could be a sign of underlying systemic diseases. Regarding body heat: The notion that Tilasmi Moti has cooling properties to manage body heat is rooted in traditional beliefs, not scientific fact. Body heat changes in babies are usually due to infections or environmental factors. There is no evidence to suggest that metals in a pendant can influence body temperature. Regarding digestion: Teething does not cause digestive problems like loose motions or loss of appetite. It is not linked to fever, diarrhoea, diaper rash, or a runny nose, nor does it make your baby more prone to illness or excessive crying. Blaming teething for fever or crying can delay treatment for serious conditions like ear infections or meningitis. Regarding calmness: While some parents may observe a placebo effect, Tilasmi Moti does not have any inherent calming properties. Restlessness or irritability during teething is best managed through soothing techniques like cuddling, using a cold teething ring, or maintaining a comforting routine. Effective ways to soothe teething pain include: gently wiping away drool with a soft cloth to prevent rashes; offering cool things to chew on like a firm rubber teething ring or chilled apple slice (avoiding liquid-filled teething rings); gently massaging gums with a cool, damp washcloth or clean finger; feeding older babies soft, cool foods like yogurt; and filling bottles with only water to prevent tooth decay.

title: Can toothpaste, lemon and ENO shrink pores instantly?
claim_text: Applying a mixture of toothpaste, lemon juice, and ENO powder on the face can magically shrink open pores in a single application.
quick_take: A viral Instagram reel claims a mix of toothpaste, lemon juice, and ENO can shrink pores instantly. After fact checking, we came to know this claim is false.
doctor_explanation: Is this a safe combination for the skin? No. While toothpaste, lemon juice, and ENO may seem like harmless ingredients, combining them can be irritating and even damaging to the skin barrier. Dr Joyeeta Chowdhury, MD (Dermatology), says, "Toothpaste contains ingredients like detergents and abrasives that are not designed for the skin, especially the delicate skin on your face. Using these ingredients for long periods can lead to irritation and damage to the skin's natural barrier." Dr Iram Qazi, MD (Dermatology), says, "While toothpaste is effective for cleaning teeth, it is not suitable for the skin. The strong ingredients in toothpaste can cause irritation, burning, and redness. I do not recommend using toothpaste for treating skin problems, as it can worsen the condition." Dr Swati Watwani, Medical Director at Persianlly Clinic, says, "Baking soda is highly alkaline and can disrupt the natural pH of your skin. This can lead to irritation, moisture loss, and sensitivity. The abrasive nature of baking soda can also cause excessive exfoliation, making the skin drier and more prone to rashes and dark spots." Dr Neha Khurana, MD (Dermatology), says, "DIY skin treatments like using toothpaste can be harmful. The skin's natural pH is acidic, and using products with a basic pH, like toothpaste, can upset this balance. This can lead to dryness, irritation, peeling, and even allergic reactions like contact dermatitis." Does this mixture of toothpaste, lemon and ENO powder actually shrink pores? No, not really. Open pores are a natural part of everyone's skin. They are the openings for hair follicles and sebaceous glands. While some products can temporarily tighten the skin and make pores appear smaller, they cannot permanently shrink them. Dr Rashi Soni, Co-founder and Consulting Dermatologist, Aesthetician, and Hair Transplant Surgeon at Rashi Hospital in Mumbai, explains, "Pore size depends on genetics, age, and sun exposure. While your genes set your natural pore size, ageing and sun damage can make pores appear larger over time. Home remedies may temporarily clean and unclog pores, improving skin texture, but they won't permanently shrink pores or reverse the effects of ageing. For more lasting results, professional treatments such as chemical peels, microdermabrasion, or laser therapy from a dermatologist are more effective." Are there any safer alternatives for shrinking pores? Yes, there are safer alternatives for managing the appearance of pores. Gentle exfoliation with mild acids like salicylic acid or glycolic acid can help clear out pores and improve their appearance. Hydrating products, such as moisturisers with hyaluronic acid, can also help keep the skin plump, making pores appear smaller. Always choose products that suit your skin type and avoid harsh ingredients that could cause irritation. THIP Media Take: The claim that a DIY remedy using toothpaste, lemon juice, and ENO can shrink pores instantly is false. While the desire for perfect skin is understandable, there is no single remedy for shrinking pores. It's crucial to prioritise gentle, skincare products formulated for your skin type. Consulting a dermatologist is recommended for personalised advice and treatment options.

title: Can turmeric and lemon force sugar out of the body?
claim_text: A Facebook video claims that turmeric and lemon can quickly remove sugar from the body through urination, making it an easy cure for diabetes. It features Dr P Raghu Ram, who supposedly won a Nobel Prize for this discovery and cured England's royal family of diabetes. The doctor claims the royal family is now diabetes-free and happy. He also says he wants to help Indians get rid of diabetes without medication.
quick_take: A social media post claims that turmeric and lemon can force sugar out of the body during urination. After thorough fact checking, we found that this claim is false.
doctor_explanation: We spoke with Dr Almas Fatma, MBBS, Diploma in Family Medicine, PG in Digital Health, General Physician from Navi Mumbai, for her expert opinion on whether turmeric and lemon can remove sugar from the body and cure diabetes. She clarified, "There is no scientific evidence that turmeric and lemon can flush sugar out of the body through urination. Insulin and metabolism regulate blood sugar levels, not sugar elimination through urine. Proper diabetes management includes a balanced diet, regular exercise, and medication as prescribed by a doctor." Dr Ubaid ur Rahman, General physician at Holy Mission Clinic, New Delhi, says, "Diabetes needs lifelong care with healthy habits, regular exercise, and proper medical treatment. Following a doctor's advice, taking prescribed medication, and monitoring blood sugar are key to managing it. Relying on unproven remedies can delay treatment and cause serious health risks." Harita Adhvaryu, Senior Clinical Dietitian at Ezcure Diabetes Care, Ahmedabad, explains, "Many people believe in quick-fix diabetes cures, but managing the condition takes time and effort. There are no shortcuts—controlling diabetes requires a balanced diet, regular exercise, and proper medical care for long-term health." The kidneys regulate blood sugar levels by filtering excess glucose from the blood only when sugar levels are too high. This is known as glycosuria, which occurs in uncontrolled diabetes, not in normal sugar metabolism. Turmeric and lemon do not play a role in forcing sugar out of the body. While turmeric contains curcumin, which has some anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, and lemon is rich in vitamin C, neither ingredient can alter kidney function or regulate sugar excretion. The only way sugar leaves the body naturally is through metabolism, energy use, and insulin regulation—not through a forced process by food items. Diabetes is a lifelong condition that needs continuous management. While certain dietary habits may help regulate blood sugar, there is no instant cure. Turmeric has been studied for its potential to improve insulin sensitivity and reduce inflammation, but research is still ongoing. Lemon, rich in antioxidants and fibre, supports overall health but does not cure diabetes. Some studies suggest it may help manage blood sugar, but more research is needed. A 2007 study found that taking 1,000 mg daily of vitamin C for six weeks lowered blood sugar and fat levels, reducing the risk of complications. Research from 2014 indicated that people with diabetes may need more vitamin C. In 2016, another study suggested that a diet rich in vitamin C could help protect against type 2 diabetes. Proper diabetes management includes: balanced diet, regular exercise, medication as prescribed, and blood sugar monitoring. Ignoring proper medical care might cause blood sugar levels to spike, leading to serious complications like nerve damage, kidney failure, or even diabetic ketoacidosis. Regarding Dr P Raghu Ram: There is no record of Dr P Raghu Ram winning a Nobel Prize for a diabetes cure. He is a senior surgeon in India and a Padma Shri awardee for his contributions to medicine, but there is no evidence of him promoting this remedy. The Nobel Prize database does not list any such achievement, and no medical journals or credible news sources report this discovery. The only Nobel Prize related to diabetes was awarded in 1923 to Banting and Macleod for making insulin widely available. The UK's royal family has also made no such claims about being cured of diabetes. A review of Dr P Raghu Ram's social media and recent news shows no association with this remedy. The video uses an AI-generated voice with poor lip sync and unnatural expressions, a common tactic in misinformation campaigns to exploit public trust.

(Treatment for decayed teeth and swollen gums in just one day!)

title: Can turmeric lemonade treat depression better than Prozac?
claim_text: turmeric lemonade, made with the spice turmeric, can help treat depression better than Prozac
quick_take: A social media post claims that turmeric lemonade treats depression better than Prozac. Our fact check says this is mostly false.
doctor_explanation:
No, turmeric alone cannot treat depression. While turmeric, particularly its active compound curcumin, has been studied for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, the majority of the studies have focused on curcumin supplements, not turmeric in its whole form. Research suggests curcumin may help with mood-boosting effects and potentially alleviate mild depression symptoms. For example, a 2014 study found that curcumin (at a dose of 1000mg) may be a safe and effective treatment for major depressive disorder (MDD), as long as the person doesn't have suicidal thoughts or serious mental health issues. A 2017 review also supports curcumin as a promising natural treatment for depression. Other studies have shown curcumin extracts (ranging from 250mg to 1000mg) combined with saffron helped reduce depression and anxiety in people with MDD.

However, the studies on curcumin used supplements with higher doses, such as 500-1000mg of curcumin taken daily, often twice a day. In contrast, turmeric powder, which is commonly used in cooking, contains only about 3-8% curcumin by weight. A 3g spoon of turmeric powder (around a teaspoon) provides only 30-90mg of curcumin, far less than the amounts used in these studies.

Furthermore, curcumin, the active compound in turmeric, is not easily absorbed by the body on its own. To improve absorption, it's often taken with black pepper (which contains piperine) or in special supplements. Without these, the curcumin in regular turmeric powder is less effective. The turmeric you use in cooking has much less curcumin and is harder for the body to absorb, so it's unlikely to have the same antidepressant effects as the curcumin supplements used in studies.

No, turmeric lemonade cannot outperform Prozac. There is no scientific evidence that turmeric lemonade is more effective than Prozac in treating depression. A 2014 study showed that curcumin, the active compound in turmeric, enhanced the effects of fluoxetine (brand name Prozac) in mice without raising the drug's levels in the brain, suggesting curcumin works through a different mechanism. Additionally, a 2023 study in zebrafish found that both fluoxetine and curcumin helped reduce sickness-like behavior caused by inflammation and lowered certain inflammatory markers. This highlights curcumin's potential as a supplement to antidepressants in managing inflammation-related symptoms.

Antidepressants like Prozac directly affect brain chemistry, balancing serotonin levels, which are critical for mood regulation. The effects of turmeric are general and not as targeted or consistent for managing clinical depression.

Dr Roma Kumar, Senior Consultant Psychologist at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital and Max Hospital in New Delhi, says: "While turmeric has some promising health benefits, including mild mood-boosting properties, there's no comparison between a glass of turmeric lemonade and a medication like Prozac for treating depression. Prozac is a well-researched antidepressant designed to address chemical imbalances in the brain. Turmeric might be a helpful addition to a healthy lifestyle, but it's not a replacement for evidence-based treatments."

Almas Fatma, MBBS, Diploma in Family Medicine, PG in Digital Health, General Physician from Navi Mumbai, clarifies: "Turmeric lemonade is great for hydration and might offer some anti-inflammatory benefits, but it's not a cure for depression. Prozac and similar antidepressants are specifically formulated to treat depression by targeting neurotransmitters. Turmeric's active compound, curcumin, has shown potential in some studies, but you'd need a concentrated supplement to get any real therapeutic effect—not just a homemade drink."

No, it should not replace prescribed medication. While turmeric lemonade may be a refreshing drink, it may complement, but it should never replace professional medical treatment. Depression is a serious condition, and its treatment should be overseen by a healthcare professional. Relying on natural remedies like turmeric lemonade may delay proper treatment and worsen symptoms. Always consult a healthcare provider for accurate diagnosis and treatment.

title: Can turmeric, mustard oil, and alum cure dental pain? - THIP Media
claim_text: Dental pain can be managed by swishing the mouth with dissolved alum and then massaging the affected area with mustard oil and turmeric.
quick_take: A Facebook post suggests using alum, turmeric, and mustard oil to cure dental pain. We fact-checked the claim and found it to be mostly false.
doctor_explanation:
Dental pain, often referred to as odontogenic pain, is the body's signal that the teeth necessitate attention. It originates from the teeth or the structures that support them, such as the mucosa, gingivae, maxilla, mandible, or periodontal membrane. A toothache is caused by an irritated dental pulp that is brought on by various factors. It is critical to acknowledge that dental discomfort is not the same as tooth sensitivity. When gums recede or enamel wears away, exposing the dentine underneath, a brief, intense discomfort known as dental sensitivity occurs. The primary triggers include hot tea, cold water, and even sweet foods. Nevertheless, removing the stimulus causes the discomfort to subside. Conversely, the toothache that doesn't resolve on its own, usually throbs, persists or progressively grows worse with time, which frequently indicates an infection.

Are alum, mustard oil, and turmeric effective remedies for dental pain? No, not really. Due to the distress of tooth pain and their dread of visiting a dentist, patients may be compelled to utilise at-home therapies. Since tooth discomfort has a specific underlying cause that necessitates medical attention, the aforementioned components cannot be utilised as a stand-alone remedy because:

Mustard oil: We begin with mustard oil, which has antimicrobial characteristics and may be beneficial for gums in otherwise healthy individuals. However, as mustard oil also contains the irritant allyl isothiocyanate, it may not be suitable for addressing an acute toothache.

Turmeric: Next is turmeric. The presence of curcumin makes this component promising. Research on the analgesic and anti-inflammatory effects of this medicinal ingredient is substantial. While curcumin has helped manage orofacial discomforts and is just as effective as conventional analgesics following the extraction of the third molar, these results are only available from small-scale research, necessitating larger trials. Turmeric can, therefore, be a useful adjunct but cannot replace established dental care.

Alum: Finally, alum, also known as fitkari; this has been used traditionally as an astringent and antiseptic, but there is not enough substantial scientific data to support its use in relieving dental pain.

Dr Yogita Parmar, BDS, MPH, of Max Healthcare in Saket, New Delhi, explains that in her experience as a dentist, patients frequently consider natural remedies for dental issues, such as turmeric and mustard oil. While these ingredients might have some antibacterial or anti-inflammatory characteristics; however, they won't address the root cause of the issue, such as cavities or infections, or relieve a toothache. Mustard oil can aid with dental cleanliness to some extent, but it won't ease discomfort, and turmeric may even discolour your teeth. If you have a toothache, consulting a dental professional is usually the most appropriate option because they can determine the cause and provide the appropriate therapy.

Dr. Pooja Sharma, BDS, MDS, of NIMS University in Jaipur, adds credence to this by cautioning that using at-home remedies for tooth pain can occasionally trick individuals into believing that they don't require expert care. Gum infections and cavities cannot be cured on their own; a dentist must evaluate and manage them. Using home cures for teeth can lead to carelessness, which can exacerbate small issues, including tooth loss, extreme discomfort, or swelling. Always visit a dentist as soon as possible to avoid conditions getting worse.

While certain home remedies, such as herbal pastes, salt water rinses, or clove oil, may offer temporary comfort, they are not very effective for deeper underlying causes, including pulpitis, abscesses, or broken teeth. The real risk comes from presuming that comfort equates to cure. If pulp-related inflammation is left untreated, it may rapidly escalate to serious complications. Furthermore, delaying expert dental care may exacerbate a manageable condition and require more invasive and expensive procedures. Persistent self-treatment carries risks that could mask symptoms, allowing silent progression of the underlying infection. Therefore, while do-it-yourself solutions could provide marginal temporary benefits, they cannot replace a dentist's evaluation.

title: Can Vitamin C cream remove dark spots in 10 seconds?
claim_text: Vitamin C cream can instantly remove dark spots, freckles, melasma, and acne scars in just 10 seconds. The cream will penetrate deeply into the skin and work on all skin types, regardless of the severity of the spots.
quick_take: A social media post claims that Vitamin C cream can remove dark spots in 10 seconds. We did the fact check to term this claim as false.
doctor_explanation: Vitamin C has well-documented benefits for skin health, such as brightening the skin and reducing the appearance of pigmentation over time. However, it is not a miracle ingredient that can erase dark spots in seconds. Vitamin C works by inhibiting melanin production, which is responsible for dark spots. Over time, this helps lighten pigmentation. However, its effectiveness depends on factors like the formulation of the product, concentration of Vitamin C, and skin type. Deep penetration is not an overnight process, and results take time—usually weeks, not seconds. Vitamin C can brighten the complexion and reduce the appearance of dark spots, but it does not change the natural colour of your skin. It can also protect the skin from UV damage and reduce acne spots. Skin lightening or whitening products often contain other ingredients that can have side effects, and using such products with the expectation of immediate results can be harmful. Vitamin C is effective for treating certain types of pigmentation, such as those caused by sun damage or acne scars. However, it may not be as effective for other types of spots, such as those caused by hormonal changes (like melasma) or deeper skin conditions. The claim that Vitamin C can treat spots of any age or severity in just 10 seconds is misleading. Some spots may require different treatments, and Vitamin C alone may not be enough for severe cases. title: Can walnuts and garlic in copper water cure knee pain?
claim_text: Soaking walnuts and garlic in copper water overnight can alleviate even severe knee pain and prevent the need for surgery (claimed as an Ayurvedic remedy from Charak Sanhita)
quick_take: A social media post claims that eating soaked walnuts and garlic in copper water can treat knee pain and prevent surgery. We did the fact check to term this as False.
doctor_explanation:
The claim that soaking walnuts and garlic in copper water overnight can cure knee pain is false. Here's the detailed medical explanation:

**Copper water effectiveness**: There is no evidence supporting the use of copper water to treat knee pain. Copper has been part of traditional remedies and has antibacterial properties, but research on its effectiveness for knee pain is lacking. Drinking water stored in copper vessels may help maintain copper levels in the body, but that does not equate to curing serious joint issues. Knee pain usually results from arthritis or injury, both of which require proper medical treatment.

**Garlic benefits**: Garlic shows potential in several scientific studies, but this does not mean it can cure severe knee arthritis. A 2020 study found that taking 1000 mg of garlic for 12 weeks helped improve joint symptoms in obese women with knee osteoarthritis. Other evidence showed that women who consumed a lot of garlic had lower levels of osteoarthritis and experienced less pain and inflammation related to rheumatoid arthritis. A 2018 study suggested that garlic might reduce pain for overweight or obese women with knee OA by lowering certain inflammatory markers. Another 2018 study noted that while stiffness improved significantly with garlic, pain and overall knee function did not show a significant difference compared to a placebo. A 2021 review highlighted garlic's health benefits, indicating that it may help reduce pain and inflammation in people with osteoarthritis. However, claiming garlic can cure severe knee arthritis is misleading.

**Walnuts and omega-3**: Walnuts contain omega-3 fatty acids, which have some anti-inflammatory properties. A 2020 review shows that omega-3 fatty acids may help protect against arthritis. Studies in mice showed those fed fish oil developed arthritis later and with less pain. In arthritic mice, daily omega-3 intake reduced swelling and joint damage. In rats, EPA and DHA helped lower arthritis symptoms. However, these benefits do not suggest that walnuts can cure severe knee osteoarthritis; there is no evidence for that.

**Soaking in copper water**: Soaking walnuts and garlic overnight in water in a copper pot does not enhance their potential benefits for knee joints.

**Ayurvedic reference**: This claim is misleading as there is no direct reference to it in the Charak Samhita. Ayurveda promotes balance through diet and natural treatments, but the video's assertion is not accurate. Ayurvedic treatments for joint pain typically involve herbal formulations, massage, and dietary adjustments, not soaking walnuts and garlic in copper water overnight.

**Dr Manan Arora (BAMS) explains**: "The walnut and garlic remedy soaked in copper water is not explicitly detailed in the Charak Samhita regarding knee pain. However, both walnuts and garlic are recognised in Ayurveda for their health benefits. Walnuts, rich in omega-3 fatty acids, are considered anti-inflammatory and may help reduce joint pain. Garlic, known for its warming properties and ability to improve circulation, can help in relieving inflammation. In Ayurveda, copper is believed to have healing properties, particularly for inflammation and joint health. While the specific combination may not be documented in classical texts, the individual components are valued in Ayurvedic practice for promoting joint health. For effective treatment, it's best to consult a qualified Ayurvedic practitioner who can provide personalised recommendations based on your condition."

**Surgery and knee arthritis**: Knee arthritis, particularly osteoarthritis, cannot be cured without surgery. Osteoarthritis does not have a cure, as of now. However, there are ways to manage it without surgical intervention, especially in mild to moderate cases. Lifestyle changes and medications to relieve pain can be effective. Supportive therapies may also help ease daily activities. In severe cases, like grade 3 or grade 4 arthritis, surgery becomes necessary when other treatments fail.

**Dr Smit Dave (Orthopedic Surgeon) warns**: "In severe knee arthritis, total knee replacement is the only viable option. Oils, creams, gels or home remedies may only offer temporary relief and are not a solution." Dr Dave warns against trusting random social media claims which suggest creams or gels for knee repair without surgery.

**Effective management**: It is very important to seek medical care or treatment for knee pain. The appropriate treatment varies on the basis of underlying cause and may include lifestyle changes, physiotherapy, medications, or, in severe cases, surgery. Self-care practices such as maintaining a healthy weight, staying active, and eating a balanced diet rich in anti-inflammatory foods can effectively manage milder symptoms. However, suggesting a simple remedy can replace the need for surgery is misleading and potentially harmful.

Jaundice affects the bloodstream and internal organs; it does not exit the body through the skin or nails. Therefore, the appearance of yellow water is unrelated to the medical condition. Jaundice can be a symptom of serious underlying health issues, such as liver disease, hepatitis, gallstones, or bile duct obstruction. Ignoring medical advice and delaying proper treatment could worsen the condition and lead to complications. In severe cases, untreated jaundice can cause liver failure or other life-threatening problems. Relying on unproven remedies can also lead to dehydration and malnutrition if the underlying cause is not addressed. title: Can water fasting help the body get rid of old blood cells?

doctor_explanation: Water fasting does not affect the removal of old blood cells. The turnover of blood cells is a tightly regulated process primarily managed by organs such as the spleen and liver. These organs do not notably alter their function in response to short-term fasting. While fasting can induce metabolic changes, there is no scientific evidence to suggest it enhances the removal of old blood cells as claimed. Blood cells are categorised into three main types: red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. Red blood cells have a lifespan of approximately 120 days, important for oxygen transport and nutrient delivery. White blood cells, including lymphocytes and neutrophils, play roles in immune defence against infections and pathogens, with lifespans varying from hours to years. Platelets, vital for blood clotting and wound healing, have a lifespan of about 8 to 10 days. Dr Ubaid ur Rahman, a General Physician, at Holy Mission Clinic, New Delhi, shares his expertise: 'Water fasting does not specifically target or help eliminate old blood cells. The body naturally recycles old cells through processes managed by organs like the spleen and liver. Extended fasting without expert supervision can lead to serious health issues, including nutrient deficiencies and electrolyte imbalances. Always consult a physician before starting any new regimen.' Water fasting can lead to changes in blood chemistry, including reduced glucose levels, altered lipid profiles, and adjustments in hormone levels such as insulin, leptin and cortisol. Short-term water fasting may offer benefits like improved insulin sensitivity and enhanced cellular repair processes like autophagy. However, prolonged fasting without proper medical supervision can lead to nutrient deficiencies, muscle loss, and other adverse health effects. After a water fast, you may experience refeeding syndrome if food is reintroduced too quickly, which can cause serious symptoms like weakness, swelling, and even cardiac issues. People with conditions like gout, diabetes (both type 1 and type 2), eating disorders, older adults, and children should avoid water fasting without medical supervision. Pregnant individuals should not practise water fasting.

title: Fact Check: Can you remove kidney/gallstones through the skin without surgery?
claim_text: A so-called "doctor" can remove all kinds of stones, such as kidney or gallstones, without surgery or medicine, through the abdominal skin. The post guarantees 100% success.
quick_take: A Facebook post claims that a so called "doctor" can remove gallstones through the skin, without surgery. Our fact check deems this claim False.
doctor_explanation: What are kidney stones and gallstones? Kidney stones are hard deposits containing minerals and salts that form inside the kidneys. They develop when urine becomes concentrated, allowing minerals to crystallise and stick together. Common types of kidney stones include calcium stones, uric acid stones, struvite stones, and cystine stones. Risk factors for kidney stones include dehydration, certain diets, obesity, and genetic predisposition. Gallstones, on the other hand, are hard deposits of digestive fluid that can form in the gallbladder, a small organ under the liver. They mainly consist of cholesterol or bilirubin and form when there is an imbalance in the substances that make up bile. Gallstones can block the bile ducts, leading to severe pain and potential complications such as infection or pancreatitis. Is it possible to remove kidney stones or gallstones through the abdominal skin, without any surgery or medicine? No, it is not possible to remove kidney stones or gallstones through the abdominal skin. It is anatomically and physiologically impossible to remove kidney stones or gallstones through the abdominal skin without surgery or medicine. The claim is not correct as it lacks scientific evidence and is purely misleading. Also, the person in the video seems a quack and not a qualified doctor, because a true professional would never endorse such unproven medical interventions. The urinary and biliary systems, where kidney stones and gallstones form, are located deep within the body. Kidney stones are located in the kidneys, which are positioned towards the back of the abdominal cavity. Gallstones are present in the gallbladder, which is also deep within the abdomen, nestled under the liver. There are no non-invasive methods or treatments that can reach these stones through the skin to remove them. Moreover, the claim of a 100% success rate is highly exaggerated and unequivocally false. No medical treatment or procedure can guarantee 100% success, as individual responses to treatments can vary widely. Scientific evidence and medical guidelines do not support the possibility of removing stones through the skin. According to the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) and the National Health Service (NHS), the recommended treatments for kidney stones include increased fluid intake, pain relief medication, medical therapy to facilitate stone passage, and various surgical procedures such as extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL), ureteroscopy, and percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL). For gallstones, treatments range from medications to dissolve the stones (though rarely used) to surgical removal of the gallbladder (cholecystectomy) in symptomatic cases. What are the consequences of trusting such unreliable practices for stone removal? Trusting unreliable practices for stone removal can lead to serious health consequences. These methods are not scientifically proven and may result in untreated stones causing severe pain, infections, and potential complications like kidney damage or gallbladder inflammation. For instance, ignoring proper medical advice might mean a small stone turns into a larger problem, requiring more invasive procedures later. Additionally, delaying appropriate treatment can lead to significantly higher medical expenses, as the need for emergency care and advanced interventions becomes more likely. Ultimately, the risks and costs associated with these unproven treatments far outweigh any perceived benefits. Dr Sharad Malhotra, Senior Consultant & HOD Gastroenterology Hepatology & Therapeutic Endoscopy at Aakash Healthcare, New Delhi, strongly advised against seeking medical care from quacks, stating: "Any such action should be at a person's own risk, as no medical evidence supports these methods for stone management." The best treatment for kidney stones depends on their size, type, and location, as well as the patient's overall health. Small stones can often pass naturally by drinking plenty of water and taking pain relievers. Medical treatment may include alpha-blockers to help relax the muscles in the urinary tract and facilitate stone passage. For larger stones, surgical interventions may be necessary. In conclusion, the claim that kidney or gallstones can be removed through the abdominal skin without surgery or medicine is false.

title: Fact Check: Did Cleveland Clinic warn of mass deaths from mRNA vaccines?

## Did the Cleveland Clinic make any warnings about mass deaths?
No, the Cleveland Clinic has issued no such warning. The Cleveland Clinic has consistently supported COVID-19 vaccination as a reliable way to prevent severe illness and hospitalisations. The organisation has not issued any statements linking vaccines to 'mass deaths' or supporting such speculative claims. Assigning these false statements to the Cleveland Clinic appears to be an attempt to mislead the public and undermine trust in vaccines.

## Do mRNA COVID vaccines cause myocarditis-related mass deaths?
No, myocarditis cases associated with mRNA vaccines are very rare and generally manageable. Research, including findings from the Cleveland Clinic, indicates that most myocarditis cases following mRNA vaccination are mild and resolve with proper treatment. In contrast, the risk of myocarditis is significantly higher after a COVID-19 infection. Studies consistently show that the benefits of vaccines in reducing severe illness and hospitalisation far outweigh the small risks of side effects like myocarditis. There have also been speculations about mRNA vaccines harming children's immunity, but this is false and misleading.

## Do mRNA COVID vaccines cause long-term harm?
No, mRNA vaccines have undergone extensive safety evaluations. Clinical trials and long-term surveillance demonstrate that mRNA vaccines are safe and effective. These vaccines teach the immune system to fight COVID-19 by using a short-lived mRNA sequence. This sequence breaks down rapidly in the body and does not interfere with human DNA, relieving concerns about genetic alterations. Rare side effects, such as mild myocarditis, are far outweighed by the vaccines' role in preventing severe illness, hospitalisations, and deaths from COVID-19. We have also debunked similar claims which said COVID vaccines contain nanobots and can cause turbo cancer and autoimmune diseases. However, this is completely false.

## Can myocarditis survival rates be linked to vaccine risks?
No, myocarditis survival rates are being misrepresented in the claim. The statistics fail to consider key details. Myocarditis due to COVID vaccines is much rarer and milder than myocarditis from other causes, like COVID-19 itself. Data from millions of people who have been vaccinated shows no concerning patterns over time. Current research strongly supports the safety of mRNA vaccines, showing that the benefits far outweigh the risks.

## Can we predict health outcomes five years after vaccination?
Not definitively, but historical evidence suggests no reason for alarm. Adverse effects from vaccines usually occur shortly after administration rather than years later. Claims of 'mass deaths' are speculative and remain unsupported. Evidence from millions of vaccinations worldwide indicates the safety of mRNA vaccines over the short and medium term. Ongoing monitoring and long-term studies continue to support the vaccine's favourable safety profile.

## Why do claims like this spread?
The Slay News article combines speculative opinions with selective data to mislead readers. By citing figures like Geert Vanden Bossche, a known critic of COVID-19 vaccines, it gives an illusion of credibility. Such tactics exploit public fears to spread vaccine misinformation, gain traction and harm public health efforts.

## THIP Media Take
The claim that Cleveland Clinic warned of mass deaths caused by mRNA COVID vaccines is false. It represents another instance of misinformation related to COVID-19 vaccines, which undermines trust in vaccines. We advise you to always trust reliable sources, such as health agencies and scientific publications, for accurate information. Vaccination remains one of the most effective ways to protect against severe COVID-19.

doctor_explanation: The claim that COVID vaccines cause deadly heart defects is entirely false. The American Heart Association (AHA) has not announced that 90% of vaccinated people have developed deadly heart defects. This misinformation stems from a mischaracterization of a study published in May 2023, which has been incorrectly linked to COVID-19 vaccines. The study in question, conducted by Harvard Medical School researchers and published in the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA), found that nearly 90% of American adults meet the criteria for a condition called cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome. This condition involves the overlap of cardiovascular disease, kidney disease, Type 2 diabetes, and obesity. Importantly, the study used the American Heart Association's definition of this condition, announced in October 2023. The study did not investigate or discuss the impact of COVID-19 vaccines. The data collection for the study ended in March 2020, months before COVID-19 vaccines were available. Therefore, any suggestion that the study's findings are related to the vaccines is incorrect. The false claim appears to originate from The People's Voice (TPV), a website known for publishing misinformation. The American Heart Association has acknowledged that COVID-19 vaccines, like all vaccines, can have side effects. These can include rare cases of heart health issues like heart inflammation (myocarditis) and blood clots. However, these side effects are extremely rare. Plus, the benefits of vaccination in preventing COVID-19, which can also cause severe cardiovascular issues, far outweigh the risks. COVID-19 itself poses significant health risks, including severe respiratory illness, long-term health complications, and increased risk of cardiovascular problems. Vaccination is a critical tool in minimising these risks and controlling the spread of the virus.

title: Did WHO order lockdowns for a deadly monkeypox strain?
claim_text: The WHO has ordered governments to prepare for 'mega lockdowns' due to the 'strong likelihood' of a deadly pandemic caused by a new strain of monkeypox
quick_take: A website claims that the WHO has ordered governments worldwide to prepare for "mega lockdowns" due to a new deadly strain of monkeypox. Our fact check says it's False.
doctor_explanation:
The claim that the WHO ordered governments to prepare for "mega lockdowns" due to a deadly strain of monkeypox is entirely false. The WHO's role during public health emergencies like the mpox outbreak is to provide technical advice, support, and coordination among its 194 member states. The organisation does not have the authority to enforce decisions or actions on any government. Instead, WHO offers recommendations based on scientific evidence. It is up to individual countries to decide how to implement these recommendations in their own public health policies.

While the WHO did declare a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) on August 14, 2024, regarding the outbreak of mpox in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and other African countries, this declaration is significant because it signals the need for a coordinated international response to contain the outbreak. However, the declaration does not imply or suggest the necessity of lockdowns. The WHO's press release on the matter emphasises the importance of scaling up efforts to control the spread of the virus but makes no mention of lockdowns as a strategy.

Mpox, formerly known as monkeypox, is a viral infection that can spread through close contact with an infected person, animal, or contaminated materials. It primarily spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids, respiratory droplets, or lesions. The symptoms often include fever, rash, and swollen lymph nodes. In some cases, mpox can lead to severe complications, especially in individuals with weakened immune systems.

Preventing the spread of mpox involves several key measures: lockdowns are not part of the WHO's recommended approach for managing mpox outbreaks. Public health responses to the mpox outbreak focus on vaccination, contact tracing, and public education—not lockdowns.

The website making the claim, The People's Voice, has a history of publishing misleading information. This website continues to spread unverified and often sensationalised stories. It is not a reliable source for factual news and frequently publishes claims that are not supported by credible evidence.

Additional misinformation myths circulating include: whether mpox is an airborne disease, whether monkeypox is actually shingles, the baseless claim that monkeypox is psychological bioterrorism, and the false narrative that Bill Gates is integrating HIV into mpox vaccines.

title: Do babies get tears when they cry? - THIP Media

Of course, newborn babies cry. Experts say, "It's normal for a baby to cry for 2–3 hours a day for the first 6 weeks." In fact, a number of complexities have been reported about babies who DO NOT cry.

Do newborn babies get tears when they cry?

No. When an infant is born, in normal conditions his tear glands are still under development. It may take 2 weeks to 3 months for an infant to develop tear glands.

When the tear glands are forming, some newborn babies develop a blocked tear duct, which is a blockage of the pathway that carries tears from the eye to the nose.
