title: Fact Check: Can a 30-second yoga pose reduce belly fat?
claim_text: An Instagram post suggests performing Paschimottanasana (Seated Forward Bend) for 30 seconds, ten times daily can reduce belly fat, promote faster hair growth, and decrease stress and anxiety.
quick_take: A social media post claims that a 30-second yoga pose can reduce belly fat. We fact checked this and found the claim to be mostly false.
doctor_explanation:
Can performing the Seated Forward Bend pose for 30 seconds reduce belly fat? No, spot reduction of fat is a myth. Scientific evidence shows that simply doing one specific exercise won't target fat loss in certain areas. Weight loss occurs when you burn more calories than you consume. Yoga can help in weight management by promoting mindfulness and increasing physical activity, but relying on a single yoga pose for 30 seconds to target belly fat isn't realistic. Fat loss requires a mix of regular exercise, a balanced diet, and consistency. High-intensity workouts, strength training, and healthy eating habits are more effective for overall fat reduction, including belly fat. Expert insight from Hakim Bharmal, Master Trainer and Contest Prep Coach: "Yoga supports flexibility and relaxation, but effective weight loss needs a mix of cardio and strength training exercises. Activities like running or cycling, paired with strength moves like squats and lunges, help burn more calories and boost metabolism. A holistic approach with varied workouts and a calorie-deficit diet is essential to reduce overall body fat." There are many home remedies for fat loss, with some people recommending turmeric and ginger for weight loss. However, it's important to note that there is no solid evidence to support these claims.

Does the Seated Forward Bend pose stimulate faster hair growth? No, hair growth mainly depends on genetics, nutrition, and hormonal factors rather than a specific exercise or pose. Yoga and meditation can improve blood circulation, and may reduce inflammatory markers in the body. But, there is no strong evidence that they directly affect hair growth rates. Additionally, there's an indirect connection: yoga can reduce stress, which can potentially reduce hair fall due to stress. Expert insight from Dr Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant in Lucknow: "Paschimottanasana does not have proven effects on hair growth. While yoga promotes well-being, hair growth mainly depends on genetics, hormonal balance, and nutrition. Some yoga poses may enhance blood circulation, but the specific impact of Paschimottanasana remains unsubstantiated."

Can the Seated Forward Bend pose reduce stress and anxiety? Yes, but only to an extent. Practising yoga regularly can help reduce stress and anxiety over time, but a 30-second session alone is unlikely to achieve this. Poses like the Seated Forward Bend can help calm the nervous system and promote relaxation. Deep breathing and mindfulness stimulate the parasympathetic nervous system (a part of our nervous system), which encourages a state of calm. However, effective stress management generally requires consistent practice that includes multiple poses, breathing exercises, and possibly meditation. A well-rounded yoga practice supports mental health, but a brief session isn't a cure-all. Expert insight from Dr Roma Kumar, Senior Consultant Psychologist at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital and Max Hospital in New Delhi: "Practising Paschimottanasana encourages deep breathing and mindfulness, helping to calm the mind. While research supports yoga's role in enhancing mental well-being and reducing stress, individual experiences may vary. It's important for people to consult an expert if they are experiencing chronic stress or anxiety."

The Seated Forward Bend pose offers several advantages for both body and mind. Incorporating Paschimottanasana into your routine can enhance your physical and mental well-being. However, achieving significant health benefits like weight loss and stress relief requires a comprehensive approach, including a balanced diet and lifestyle.

THIP Media Take: Yoga poses can improve flexibility, relaxation, and overall well-being. However, expecting 30-second poses to reduce belly fat, accelerate hair growth, or eliminate stress is misleading. Therefore, we conclude the claim is mostly false. Holistic approaches, including regular exercise, proper nutrition, and mental health practices, are essential for these outcomes.

title: Fact Check: Can a 5-minute Japanese exercise cure diabetes in 2 weeks?
claim_text: A 5-minute Japanese exercise can cure diabetes in 2 weeks without even cutting off sweets from the diet. I managed to reduce my blood sugar from 15 millimole to 5 and I achieved this in just 2 weeks. During the first week, your well-being improves. Your pancreas begins to recover. It even starts producing insulin. By the second week, your blood sugar levels normalize. I didn't even have to give up sweets. It's nothing short of miraculous.
quick_take: While exercise is a proven tool in the prevention and management of diabetes, there is no scientific evidence or medical consensus to support the claim that any form of exercise—including a 5-minute Japanese routine—can cure diabetes in just two weeks.
doctor_explanation: Exercise plays a major role in both managing and preventing diabetes, but there is no scientific evidence or medical consensus that supports the claim that a 5-minute Japanese workout can cure diabetes in just 2 weeks. Diabetes is a chronic condition that occurs when the pancreas doesn't produce enough insulin or when the body cannot effectively use the insulin it makes. When diabetes is not well managed, it can lead to high blood sugar (hyperglycemia), which over time can cause serious damage to the nerves, blood vessels, and other organs. At present, there is no cure for diabetes; however, many individuals can achieve diabetes reversal, which refers to maintaining blood sugar levels within a healthy range without the need for medication, typically through a consistent commitment to healthy lifestyle habits including a balanced diet and regular physical activity. Type 1 diabetes cannot be reversed because it happens when a mix of genetic, environmental, metabolic, and immune factors causes the immune system to attack the insulin-producing cells in the pancreas. A review published in Diabetes Care stated that exercise plays a significant role in the prevention and management of insulin resistance, prediabetes, gestational diabetes (GDM), type 2 diabetes, and complications related to diabetes — but the review focuses only on prevention and control, and does not mention exercise as a cure for diabetes. Another review published in the American Journal of Medicine Open suggests that high-intensity interval training may be effective in reducing blood glucose levels, but does not claim that exercise can cure diabetes in 2 weeks. A study published in BMJ Journals reported that radio calisthenics, a traditional Japanese exercise, may help prevent the decline in skeletal muscle mass and could be considered beneficial for people with type 2 diabetes — again, the study does not suggest that exercise can cure diabetes in 2 weeks. There is no specific program called 'Japanese gymnastics for diabetes,' and no scientific evidence proving that any form of exercise or gymnastics can cure the condition. There is no medical consensus supporting the claim that Japanese exercise can cure diabetes within two weeks. Dr. Akhil Krishna, Associate Consultant, Endocrinology & Diabetes, KIMSHEALTH Trivandrum, stated: '5 minutes of daily Japanese exercise is not a proven cure or reversal for diabetes, especially not within a mere two weeks. Japanese exercise is indeed a gentle, health-promoting exercise that can play a positive role in diabetes management as part of a comprehensive lifestyle plan. Scientific studies support that regular Japanese exercise practice over the long term can modestly improve blood sugar control, lower stress, improve balance, and enhance quality of life for type 2 diabetes patients. However, the specific claims of the Holistic Japanese exercise healing method go far beyond the evidence. The notion of achieving normal blood sugars while not giving up sweets is a fantasy that ignores basic nutrition science. No exercise, let alone a brief one, can allow unlimited sugar intake without consequences.' Dr. Achintya Sharma, MBBS, MS (General Surgery), MCh (Vascular Surgery), Senior Consultant, Max Healthcare, added: 'Japanese exercise is not a scientifically proven treatment for diabetes. Lifestyle modification is an essential pillar in long term management of Diabetes Mellitus, but unrealistic and false propaganda regarding treatment not only creates wrong narrative but plays with lives of patient. Only proven treatment for DM is following healthy lifestyle and taking medications. A qualified professional is the right person to guide u in this regards.'

title: Fact Check: Can a 5G network affect the immune system?
claim_text: Blocking exposure to electromagnetic fields (EMF's) from 5G produces significantly reduced symptoms in 90% of patients with autoimmune disease like lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, multiple sclerosis, Sjogren's syndrome and celiac disease.

doctor_explanation: No. There is no evidence that suggests the 5G network can affect the immune system. As wireless networks release radiation, many people have raised their concerns after the World Health Organisation (WHO) (2011) classified radiofrequency electromagnetic fields as 'possibly carcinogenic to humans based on an increased risk for glioma, a malignant type of brain cancer associated with wireless phone use'. However, the available studies that provide evidence of adverse health effects of 5G are either preliminary literature studies or done on animals. As scant human trials are available, further research is essential to confirm the 5G network's effects on the immune system. A telecom website has shown that the 5G network is accessible in the 3.5GHz frequency bandwidth. The current 3G, 4G and Wi-Fi networks also operate in 3.5GHz frequency bandwidth. However, 5G networks can reach up to 26GHz frequency bandwidth to achieve higher speeds. A false post shared a news story which claims that a condition called Vaxgenocide is happening, where the heads of vaccinated people are exploding when they turn up 5G. A 5G network band can have a wavelength of 3-30GHz in centimeters and 30-300GHz in millimeters. Moreover, another study has shown that non-ionizing radiation in the frequency range 30kHz-300GHz is carcinogenic for human beings. As the frequency of the 5G network falls in the 30kHz-300GHz bracket, people contemplate whether the 5G network is harmful or not. However, it is also true that the majority of the people are exposed to lower frequencies of the 5G network that do not have any effect on human health. The study on radiofrequency radiation is challenging because the available studies have used different approaches and provided sometimes-conflicting results. These reasons have made it difficult to collate the data and come up with the answer regarding radiofrequency radiation safety. However, the widespread use of the 5G network is a global issue and 'prolonged exposure to radiofrequency radiation causes cancer' cannot be ruled out completely.

This condition primarily links to factors like poor diet, obesity, alcohol consumption, and certain medical conditions like diabetes type 2. Belly fat and fatty liver are both related to metabolic health, but they are not directly caused by one another. While massage can improve blood flow and ease muscle tension, it doesn't directly help with fat loss in the belly or anywhere else. Hakim Bharmal, Master Trainer and Contest Prep Coach, explains: "When you consume fewer calories than your body needs, it creates a calorie deficit, forcing your body to burn stored fat for energy." This can be achieved by combining healthy eating habits with regular physical activity. A calorie-deficit diet is a proven and reliable way to lose weight.

title: Fact Check: Can a banana a day keep the cardiologist away?
claim_text: A banana a day keeps the cardiologist away
quick_take: A viral social media post suggests using bananas for heart health. It claims that a banana a day can keep the cardiologist away. After fact-checking, we rate this claim as mostly false.
doctor_explanation:
What does science say about banana for heart health?

Yes, bananas can support heart health, but only as part of a balanced diet. Banana for heart health has been studied for its potassium content. Bananas are a good source of potassium, a mineral that helps the body get rid of extra sodium. This can help lower blood pressure, which is one risk factor for heart disease. A medium ripe banana contains around 400-450 mg of potassium, about 9% of the daily recommended intake.

Bananas also contain prebiotic fibre, which helps improve digestion and may benefit cholesterol levels. However, no single fruit or food can prevent heart disease or replace a visit to the cardiologist. A heart-friendly lifestyle includes a variety of fruits and vegetables, regular exercise, not smoking, and avoiding excess salt and sugar. Other important factors include family history, diet, lifestyle, and environment. These cannot be managed by eating just one fruit.

How does daily banana intake affect the body?

Maybe helpful, but not a magic fix. Having one banana a day is generally safe for most people and may provide steady energy, improve bowel movements, and help with hydration. But relying on it to prevent serious heart conditions is misleading.

Eating too many bananas may not be ideal either, especially for people with kidney problems, as excess potassium can build up in the blood. People with diabetes need to be careful with their daily banana intake too. For healthy individuals, one banana a day fits well into a balanced diet, but it must be paired with other good habits.

Dr Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition, explains, "A banana a day can definitely be part of a healthy routine. It offers quick energy, supports digestion and provides important nutrients like potassium and vitamin B6. But like any food, it works best when eaten in moderation and as part of a varied, balanced diet. It's important not to expect one fruit to do all the work when it comes to heart health or overall wellbeing."

What is the banana glycemic index and why does it matter?

Bananas have a low to medium glycemic index (GI), which means they raise blood sugar slowly. The banana glycemic index ranges from around 48 to 60. A lower GI is better for keeping blood sugar stable. This makes bananas a better choice than high-GI snacks like white bread or sugary drinks. It is important to note that the glycemic index depends on the ripeness and variety of the banana. Still, people with diabetes or prediabetes should watch their portions, especially with ripe bananas, as their sugar content increases over time.

Does ripe banana glycemic index affect heart health?

Not directly, but it can matter for people with diabetes. Heart disease risk is higher in people with type 2 diabetes. Choosing a slightly less ripe banana or combining it with nuts or yoghurt can help slow down the sugar spike.

For most healthy individuals, this doesn't pose a problem. However, for those managing diabetes or blood sugar levels, it's worth paying attention. While bananas support heart health due to their potassium and fibre, combining them with protein or healthy fat, like nuts or yoghurt, can help slow down the sugar release. It's all about balance, not avoiding the fruit altogether."

In summary, bananas are a heart-friendly food, but claiming that one banana a day can replace the need for a cardiologist is misleading. Banana for heart health is only effective when it's part of a larger healthy routine. Bananas offer potassium and fibre, but they are not a cure or shield against heart problems. Long-term heart health depends on multiple habits, not a single fruit.

title: Can a bedtime spice mix really relieve body pain?

doctor_explanation: There is no strong scientific evidence showing that this specific combination of spices can directly relieve body pain. Most of the known benefits of ajwain, jeera, saunf, and elaichi relate to digestion, gut motility, and mild bloating, not pain arising from muscles, joints, nerves, or inflammation. Laboratory studies suggest that compounds like thymol (in ajwain) and flavonoids (in cumin and fennel) have mild anti-inflammatory or antioxidant effects. However, these findings come largely from test-tube or animal studies using concentrated extracts, not from human studies using small culinary doses. When consumed as a teaspoon of spice powder, the amount of these compounds is too low to act like a pain reliever. While these spices are healthy additions to food, they do not function like analgesics. Dr Sushant Srivastava, an Orthopaedic Surgeon at Mata Gujri Memorial Medical College and Lions Seva Kendra Hospital, Kishanganj (Bihar), emphasises that effective pain management starts with identifying the underlying cause of pain. Whether pain arises from osteoarthritis, injury, inflammation, or infection, treatment cannot be truly effective unless the root problem is properly diagnosed. He cautions that claims of 'instant pain relief' from any spice mix, without a thorough medical evaluation, are unrealistic and potentially misleading. Digestive discomfort can sometimes present as heaviness, dull aches, or general body discomfort, especially after large or late meals. When spices improve digestion or reduce gas, a person may feel lighter and more comfortable, which can easily be interpreted as 'pain relief'. However, this is not the same as treating actual body pain. Muscle soreness, joint stiffness, or inflammation-related pain have different causes and mechanisms. Improving digestion may improve overall comfort, but it does not address the root cause of physical pain. Dr Shalin Nagori, Consultant Pathologist and Industrial Physician, said, 'Relief from digestive discomfort such as bloating or gas can create a temporary feeling of overall comfort, which some people mistake for relief from body pain. However, this does not address musculoskeletal or inflammatory pain at its source.' Roasting and grinding can enhance aroma, taste, and digestibility, but they do not convert digestive spices into pain-relieving agents. Roasting may even reduce certain heat-sensitive compounds, if done excessively. Cardamom, in particular, is traditionally used whole or lightly crushed. There is no scientific basis for leaving it unroasted while roasting the others, nor evidence that this combination enhances pain relief. Dr Mohit Sandhu, Ayurvedic Proctologist and Pain Specialist, Himachal said, 'Ayurveda does not see pain as just a chemical problem. Pain (Śūla) is mainly linked to a Vāta imbalance and the build-up of Āma due to poor digestion. Roasting and grinding spices make them lighter, easier to absorb, and better at improving digestion. By improving digestion and reducing Āma, these spices may indirectly support pain relief. But they do not magically convert digestive spices into analgesics.' Body pain can result from nutrient deficiencies, dehydration, overuse of muscles, poor posture, hormonal changes, or medical conditions. A spice mix cannot correct these underlying issues. Relying on home remedies alone may delay diagnosis and appropriate treatment. While these spices are generally safe in small amounts, daily consumption as a 'remedy' may worsen acidity or cause digestive irritation in some individuals.

title: Fact Check: Can a bee venom spray cure arthritis pain?
claim_text: A Facebook video alleges that a bee venom spray can cure arthritis pain and swelling, enhance joint mobility, and improve flexibility. The spray is said to be made from natural ingredients.

doctor_explanation: Arthritis is a common condition which involves inflammation and pain in the joints. The most prevalent types are osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. Symptoms include joint pain, stiffness, and swelling, which can significantly impact daily activities. Bee venom, also known as apitoxin, contains various chemicals with potential medical applications, including enzymes, peptides, and amines. Melittin, a major component, comprises about 50% of bee venom and has been studied for its potential medicinal properties such as antibacterial, antiviral, anti-inflammatory, and pain-relieving effects. Although bee venom has some anti-inflammatory properties, the scientific evidence supporting its effectiveness in curing arthritis is inconclusive. A study reviewed the effectiveness and side effects of bee venom treatment. While it can cause mild skin reactions like itching, rash, and swelling, bee venom proved effective in treating inflammatory arthritis and musculoskeletal diseases. This study suggests that we need large-scale clinical trials to confirm these benefits and recommends developing a system for reporting side effects to improve the reliability of bee venom therapy. Even though it likely possesses anti-inflammatory properties, it is not a medically approved cure for arthritis. Dr Ubaid ur Rahman, a General Physician, at Holy Mission Clinic, New Delhi, says, 'I advise against trusting unverified claims on social media about products like bee venom sprays for arthritis. There is insufficient scientific evidence to support their effectiveness. Instead, patients should consult medical professionals for evidence-based treatments and management of arthritis.' The product in question, GFOUK™ Bee Venom Joint and Bone Therapy Spray, claims to offer relief from arthritis pain through its active bee venom components. However, this product page provides vague information about its effectiveness against arthritis and other conditions. It lacks detailed clinical trials and a full list of ingredients. The claim of being 'medically recommended' is weakly supported, featuring a photo of a doctor. A reverse image search through Google and Yandex did not verify the doctor's authenticity. The certification displayed is non-specific and similar to those found on other unreliable websites, with no university name or certifying agency identified. The format and design of the certificate is used in the exact same manner on other product pages too, with just the doctor's photo and name being changed, suggesting it is a mere gimmick. The format of these certifications is consistent across various suspicious websites, using fake doctors to gain trust. Overall, the website appears shady and lacks credibility. Humans have used bee venom therapy for over 3,000 years. Bee venom contains a variety of chemicals, including melittin, which may have beneficial effects on health. Current research suggests bee venom may have beneficial effects. A more comprehensive 2020 meta-analysis reviewed several randomised controlled trials on bee venom therapy for various diseases, including arthritis. The researchers concluded that bee venom therapy might be beneficial in treating inflammatory forms of arthritis, but emphasised the need for more large-scale, high-quality clinical trials to confirm its effectiveness. Arthritis cannot be cured. However, its symptoms can be managed with proper treatment, which may include medications, physical therapy, and sometimes surgery. Early diagnosis and a comprehensive treatment plan tailored by healthcare professionals can help manage the condition effectively. Bee venom therapy can have significant adverse effects, including severe pain at the venom site, headaches, coughing, muscle weakness, vertigo, and jaundice. The most serious safety concern is the risk of a severe allergic reaction known as anaphylaxis. Bee and wasp venoms are common causes of anaphylaxis, which can lead to complications such as localised swelling and hives, gastrointestinal issues, respiratory problems, heart complications, and, in extreme cases, death. The claim that a bee venom spray can cure arthritis pain and swelling is mostly false. Even though there's ongoing research which suggests potential benefits related to bee venom, the product's credibility is questionable. There is a lack of solid scientific evidence to support this particular product, and hence we say it is largely false. Until and unless there's conclusive evidence regarding the efficacy of bee venom for arthritis, we cannot call it a cure. Individuals suffering from arthritis should seek advice and treatment from qualified healthcare professionals, instead of relying on bee venom spray for arthritis. You should avoid making your healthcare decisions based on random social media videos, especially if they are not from a qualified doctor.

Claims that beetroot can target all kinds of skin discolouration are exaggerated and misleading. title: Fact Check: Can a Botox serum remove wrinkles instantly?
claim_text: A Facebook video claims that a Botox serum can instantly treat wrinkles and signs of ageing. The video features a woman showing the serum's effects with the help of a hairdryer. She claims the Botox serum removed her wrinkles within 3 minutes.
quick_take: A social media video claims that a Botox serum can remove wrinkles within three minutes. Our fact check found the claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: Botox is a trademarked name for a neurotoxin produced by the bacterium Clostridium botulinum. Medically, it is used to treat certain muscular conditions, and cosmetically, it can reduce wrinkles by temporarily paralysing muscles. Botox works by inhibiting the release of acetylcholine, which is a neurotransmitter responsible for muscle contractions. Thus, it prevents the muscles from contracting and forming wrinkles. Wrinkles are a natural part of the ageing process and usually become more noticeable in individuals during their late 30s to early 40s. They occur due to the breakdown of collagen and elastin, proteins that provide structure and elasticity to the skin. Other contributing factors include repetitive facial movements, sun exposure, smoking, and genetic predisposition. The Botox serum cannot remove wrinkles within 3 minutes or instantly, as claimed in the video. Botox treatments, when administered by a professional, generally take several days to show visible effects. The neurotoxin needs time to interact with the muscles and inhibit their activity. Generally, it takes 3-7 days for the effects to start showing, with full results appearing within 1-2 weeks. The claim that a topical serum can achieve similar results within 3 minutes is scientifically implausible. The use of a hairdryer in the video likely creates a temporary tightening effect on the skin, giving the illusion of reduced wrinkles. But, this effect is superficial and short-lived. According to the product's website, the Botox Face Serum claims to combat fine lines, wrinkles, and hyperpigmentation without surgery. It uses key ingredients like Botulinum toxin, Acetyl Hexapeptide-8 (Argireline), and Collagen Peptide. The serum promises to firm and lift saggy skin, lock in moisture, boost collagen production, and protect against free radical-induced damage. Notably, the website does not provide a full ingredients list, and only mentions key ingredients. This raises doubt on the credibility of the product. Dr Sachin Gupta, a Dermatologist, from Amrita Hospital, Faridabad, states, "The idea of a serum working like Botox in minutes is highly unlikely. Botox is an injectable treatment that requires precise application by trained professionals to work effectively. Topical products may temporarily hydrate or tighten the skin, but they cannot mimic the long-term muscle-paralysing effects of Botox. Claims like these are often misleading and exploit consumer desires for quick fixes." Anti-wrinkle creams containing ingredients like retinoids, peptides, and antioxidants can improve skin texture and reduce the appearance of fine lines over time. However, their effects are generally more subtle and slower compared to medical treatments like Botox or dermal fillers.

title: Fact Check: Can a brain tumour be removed with a herbal remedy?
claim_text: An Instagram post recommends that the consumption of a fine formulation consisting of Tukham siras and kalonji seeds can aid the removal of brain tumours without surgical intervention.

doctor_explanation: Any abnormal cell development in or close to the brain is referred to as a brain tumour (BT). Primary abnormal lumps that develop over time are classified as either benign or non-cancerous. Metastatic, or secondary, tumours are ones that have spread to other areas of the brain. Brain tumours disrupt the normal brain function by: Clinical manifestations are determined by the tumour's location, size, and type. These mostly include seizures, headaches, memory loss, vision impairment, and personality or motor function abnormalities. For brain tumours to be addressed efficiently, diagnostic testing, such as MRI and CT scans, must be performed first, followed by a histopathological assessment. Additionally, advancements in neuro-oncology could shed light on the extent of the tumour. Given the complexity of the brain and the protective blood-brain barrier, the treatment of either primary or secondary brain-related outgrowths continues to be challenging. Are herbal remedies effective for treating brain tumours? No, not at all. While herbal remedies have been explored for their potential for treating several ailments, the one being considered for brain tumours can be life-threatening. One of the many herbs being recommended for treating BTs is a combination of kalonji seeds and Tukham siras. Their efficacy for BT is, however, not well supported by scientific research. Since the combination is under consideration for a potentially fatal condition, such as brain tumours, it needs to be thoroughly evaluated. Kalonji seeds (black cumin seeds) - The component is being considered because of thymoquinone. The active constituent's anti-inflammatory, anti-cancer, and antioxidant capacities are being explored. Thymoquinone preferentially suppresses the clonogenicity of glioblastoma cells, making it a potential adjuvant in the treatment of brain tumours. Additionally, thymoquinone may reduce brain damage by acting as an antioxidant. Nevertheless, these findings are preclinical, and there is insufficient reliable clinical evidence to support their use as the primary treatment for brain tumours. Tukham siras - Despite the fact that kalonji seeds can only be used as an adjunct under a doctor's supervision, there isn't much evidence indicating that tukham sirasis useful in managing BTs. Dr. Joy Mounica, Consultant Neurologist, Renova Hospitals, Langar House, Hyderabad, emphasises that brain tumours are brought on by the aberrant multiplication of brain neurones, which can have a range of causes. Therefore, a single home remedy cannot address the entire spectrum of contributing factors. The tumour's location, size, and kind, as well as the patient's age and general health, all influence the course of treatment. Therapeutic options include surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy. Therefore, using at-home therapy to treat brain tumours has the potential to be fatal. While certain herbal remedies may exhibit supportive potential, they are not a substitute for the conventional BT treatment. Patients should consult clinical experts before incorporating such remedies into their therapeutic regimen. It is not advisable to depend on such unverified home remedies. As previously established, brain tumours are complex and life-threatening conditions that necessitate evidence-based therapeutic intervention. While certain patients explore complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) to provide symptomatic relief or enhance their quality of life, these approaches should not be considered as a substitute for conventional BT treatment. Moreover, these untested natural therapies are not standardised in terms of dosage, therapeutic efficacy, or even safety. Most significantly, certain herbal remedies could influence the metabolism of prescribed pharmaceuticals, which might result in major concerns. Dr. Nishith Vaddeboina, Senior Consultant Medical Oncologist at Renova Century Hospitals in Banjara Hills, Hyderabad, sternly warns against using any non-scientific home remedies for brain tumours or any cancer. Such cures have the potential to delay necessary medical care, causing the illness to deteriorate and the patient's condition to worsen. Due to their complexity, brain tumours are usually treated with surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy, all of which improve outcomes and survival. Home remedies may provide temporary comfort but are not active treatments and may even interfere with standard treatments, reducing their efficacy and increasing the side effects. Patients should always consult an oncologist for evidence-based care, avoid unproven methods, and focus on timely medical intervention to achieve the best possible results. Therefore, even while CAM could provide supporting benefits, it shouldn't be considered the primary intervention for brain tumours. Clinicians employ a comprehensive approach. The management technique depends on the type, morphological traits, anatomical location, and systemic wellness. Surgery is often the first line of treatment for accessible or resectable malignancies. However, it may not be feasible in all circumstances. Therefore, a multidisciplinary team should be consulted for timely and appropriate intervention in every case.

title: Fact Check: Can a cayenne-based recipe address alopecia?
claim_text: An at-home cayenne-based recipe could replace the topical medication of minoxidil for treating alopecia. Furthermore, a concoction of fresh rice starch, olive oil, cayenne pepper, onion, ginger, and garlic juices has the potential to address alopecia.
quick_take: According to a social media post, alopecia could be managed with a cayenne-based remedy. We analysed the claim and found that it is mostly false.
doctor_explanation: The term 'alopecia' describes the loss of hair in areas of the body where it should normally be present. This condition can be regional or diffuse, temporary or permanent, and it can affect both males and females. Despite the fact that the terms alopecia and general hair loss are commonly used interchangeably, alopecia differs in its severity and underlying cause. People frequently lose up to 100 hair strands every day as part of their regular hair growth cycle, which is a prevalent but transient issue. Alopecia, on the other hand, is marked by a disruption in this cycle that results in noticeable bald patches. Alopecia is mostly caused by hormonal imbalances, autoimmune diseases, nutritional deficiencies, chronic stress, genetic inheritance, and certain medications. Dermatologists approach the management of this condition based on its root causes and the level of severity. Due to the rise in the cases of alopecia worldwide, the use of homemade recipes for hair growth has gained popularity on social media. While some of the ingredients of the recipe may exhibit isolated potential for promoting hair health, their combined use lacks robust scientific backing. Of these, the effectiveness of the onion juice has been extensively studied. This could be explained because of its optimal sulphur concentration and antioxidant characteristics. In a similar vein, garlic juice's allicin may complement corticosteroids to increase their efficacy in managing alopecia areata, limiting its sole dependence. Nevertheless, some individuals can find that using garlic irritates their skin. Cayenne pepper contains capsaicin, which could enhance blood circulation. Applying it topically, however, can result in allergic reactions, redness, and irritation, particularly in sensitive individuals. Alopecia is a condition that necessitates targeted medical therapy. Relying solely on unverified homemade preparations may delay proper diagnoses and timely intervention. Minoxidil, initially prescribed for managing hypertension, has proven to be an effective treatment for androgenetic alopecia (AGA) in both males and females over the last 30 years. The topical formulation, usually available in 2% and 5% strengths, stimulates hair follicles to encourage hair growth. Even though its precise mechanism of action is still unclear, several hypotheses have been put out to explain it. Even while minoxidil is not a cure-all for all forms of hair loss, it should not be substituted with the unreliable at-home cayenne-based preparation. This is because the previously mentioned recipe lacks a precise dosage and usage instructions, inclusive of indications and contraindications. Dr. Gurman Singh Bhasin, Director & Chief Dermatologist, Skinclarity Clinic, Nagpur, states that while some of these natural ingredients like garlic and onion juice have been loosely associated with hair regrowth in early studies, none are clinically proven to treat alopecia effectively. Minoxidil, on the other hand, is FDA-approved, well-studied, and works by prolonging the hair growth anagen phase. These home remedies may boost blood circulation slightly but can also cause skin irritation. While ginger juice, rice water starch, and olive oil are being studied for their nourishing or anti-inflammatory qualities, there isn't any solid scientific proof linking them to hair regrowth or alopecia. Relying on anecdotal solutions for hair loss can be misleading, ineffective, and at times, harmful. This is because online remedies might not deal with the underlying reason, which would ultimately delay the necessary medical action. Dr. K Kranthi Varma, Consultant Dermatologist at Renova Hospitals in Sanath Nagar, Hyderabad, says alopecia necessitates specific medical interventions, in contrast to normal hair loss. Treatment for alopecia is usually customised based on the type of hair loss pattern—male or female. Male pattern baldness is usually addressed with topical minoxidil and oral finasteride. For females with high androgen levels, minoxidil may be administered in combination with hormonal therapy, such as spironolactone. Furthermore, based on the patient's response and the nature of the case, treatment options such as low-level laser therapy, platelet-rich plasma (PRP), and microneedling therapy may be recommended. It is critical to acknowledge that bald patches, or alopecia, are not mere shedding of hair. The condition may be linked with a severe underlying cause that needs timely detection and intervention. Self-medication or usage of over-the-counter products without a confirmed diagnosis could be risky.

UTI pathogens can be transmitted from person to person, but this is not the most common way that UTIs are spread. title: Fact Check: Can a child heal without pharmaceutical products?
claim_text: A child's body is born with everything it needs to heal naturally unless disrupted by pharmaceutical products.
quick_take: A social media post claims that a child can heal without pharmaceutical products. We did the fact check to term this claim as mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Not really. While the human body has remarkable natural healing abilities, it doesn't have everything it needs to heal every condition. The immune system can fight off many infections on its own, but some conditions require medical intervention. For minor illnesses, children may not need medicine, but if symptoms persist for two days or worsen, it's best to see a doctor. Urgent care should be sought if there's a fever or other concerning symptoms. Vaccines, antibiotics, and other treatments have been developed to support the body in overcoming diseases it cannot fight alone. While the body's natural healing mechanisms, like the immune response and tissue repair, are crucial, they often need assistance to address more serious health issues. Pharmaceutical products are designed to work in harmony with the body's natural healing processes. In fact, many drugs are created to enhance or support the body's ability to heal. For instance, antibiotics help the body fight bacterial infections that it might not be able to handle on its own. Painkillers can relieve discomfort, allowing a child to rest and heal more effectively. Vaccines stimulate the immune system, preparing the body to defend against future infections. These interventions do not disrupt the body's natural healing; rather, they support it when necessary. Like any medical treatment, pharmaceutical products come with potential risks. However, these risks are carefully weighed against the benefits. Healthcare professionals prescribe medications based on a child's specific needs, considering factors like age, weight, and overall health. While overuse or misuse of pharmaceuticals can be harmful, when used appropriately, they significantly improve health outcomes. There are situations where natural healing alone is insufficient. title: Fact Check: Can a clay pot and candle heat a room?
claim_text: One clay flower pot and a candle will heat the room. The post says it can make the room warm if there is no other source.
quick_take: A viral social media post claims that one clay flower pot and a candle can heat the room. We fact-checked and found the claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: A clay flower pot and a candle can generate some heat. However, it is important to note that they may not be sufficient to adequately heat a room, especially in colder conditions. This concept is a DIY project known as a 'flower pot heater' or 'candle heater'. This involves placing a lit candle inside an overturned clay flower pot, with the pot acting as a heat diffuser. The idea is that the candle heats the air inside the flower pot, and the pot radiates the heat into the room. This method may produce a small amount of localized warmth. But it is generally not considered a reliable or efficient source of heating, and it may not be suitable for providing enough heat for an entire room. A single candle and flower pot cannot generate enough heat to raise the temperature of a whole room significantly, especially in larger spaces. While the clay pot will absorb and radiate some heat, it is a small and inefficient system. Moreover, it might offer localized warmth near the pot, similar to sitting by a fireplace, but it cannot evenly distribute warmth throughout the room. Dr Rohan Pandey (MBBS, MD), Clinical Microbiologist at MKCG, Odisha, informs: 'Ancient China utilized a pot system to heat cottages. While the emissions are not visible without a filter, they may offer some heat in close proximity. However, due to contemporary climatic conditions and housing architecture changes, it is advisable to opt for modern heaters over the obsolete technique'. Safety concerns: Using one clay flower pot and a candle for heat can pose several potential health issues. Firstly, there are significant fire and burn risks associated with open flames from candles. If left unattended or knocked over, candles can lead to burns, property damage, or even house fires. Additionally, the clay pot becomes extremely hot from the candle flame, reaching temperatures high enough to cause burns if accidentally touched—especially dangerous for children or pets who may not be aware of the heat. Another health concern is the risk of carbon monoxide poisoning. Burning candles continuously in a closed room can produce colorless and odorless carbon monoxide, a poisonous gas that can lead to headaches, dizziness, nausea, and even death, if not addressed quickly. Air quality becomes an issue as well, as candles produce soot and other pollutants when they burn. These pollutants can irritate the lungs and worsen respiratory problems, such as asthma, particularly in poorly ventilated spaces. Chemical exposure is another consideration, especially with candles made from paraffin wax. When burned, paraffin wax releases chemicals like toluene and benzene, which are linked to respiratory problems, cancer, and other health issues. Furthermore, using candles for heat can contribute to dehydration by drying out the air. This is a particular concern for vulnerable individuals, such as the elderly or children.

title: Fact check: Can a clove of garlic a day cure high blood pressure?
claim_text: A YouTube short video claims that a clove of garlic a day can cure Hypertension, listing 9 diseases that can be cured by consuming a clove of garlic daily including high blood pressure, high cholesterol, heart disease, colds and flu, digestive issues, joint pain, cancer prevention, skin infections, and respiratory infections.
verdict_original: The claim is False / this claim is FALSE
quick_take: Garlic is not a cure for hypertension as it cannot be cured and can only be managed. While studies show garlic supplements may have some BP-lowering properties, there is no medical consensus that a clove of garlic a day can cure high blood pressure. This claim is FALSE.
doctor_explanation:
Dr Manav Aggarwal, Consultant Cardiologist at Sanjeevan Hospital, explained: 'Hypertension, or high blood pressure, can have various primary and secondary causes. It can be caused by factors such as genetics, unhealthy lifestyle habits like poor diet and lack of exercise, stress, smoking, alcohol consumption, certain medications, underlying health conditions (like kidney disease or sleep apnea), and age-related changes in blood vessels.'

Dr Prem Aggarwal, Cardiologist and Chairman of Sanjeevan Hospitals, said: 'The term "cure" implies that the condition can be completely and permanently eradicated. Hypertension is a chronic condition that typically requires ongoing management, including lifestyle changes, medication, and monitoring. There are many medical studies that show the benefits of garlic on hypertension. But Garlic alone, especially just one clove per day, does not meet the medical definition of a cure for high blood pressure. This claim is false and misleading.'

The article further explains: Garlic has been used for centuries for its medicinal properties. It contains allicin, a compound thought to have vasodilative properties—meaning it can help expand blood vessels, thereby reducing blood pressure. Medical evidence shows that garlic consumption might have some BP-lowering properties. A 2020 systematic review by Kerien Reid of 12 trials and 553 hypertensive participants showed that garlic supplements lower systolic blood pressure (SBP) by an average of 8.3±1.9 mmHg and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) by 5.5±1.9 mmHg, similarly to standard anti-hypertensive medications (PMC6966103). Another study by Rohner et al. in the form of a systematic review and meta-analysis suggested that garlic preparations may lower BP in hypertensive individuals, but the authors noted this evidence is not strong and a well-conducted powered trial of longer duration is needed. It is important to note that in many of the studies showing positive effects of garlic on high BP, these effects are observed with garlic supplements containing concentrated doses of active ingredients, not necessarily with a single clove of garlic. Hypertension or high blood pressure cannot be cured—it can only be managed. Garlic can potentially help manage the condition as part of a broader health strategy, but it cannot cure it alone. Hypertension can cause serious damage to the heart. Excessive blood pressure causes hardening of the arteries, decreasing blood flow and oxygen supply to the heart. It also affects the kidney, eventually resulting in kidney failure. The effect on both the heart and kidneys is life-threatening.

title: Fact Check: Can a collagen hair mask rejuvenate hair?

quick_take: A Facebook post claims that a collagen hair mask can rejuvenate hair. After a thorough fact check, we termed this claim as Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: Collagen is the most abundant protein in the human body, found in the skin, bones, muscles, and connective tissues. It provides structural support, strength, and elasticity. In the context of hair, collagen helps maintain the strength and integrity of hair follicles. However, the body's natural production of collagen decreases with age, which can contribute to the thinning and weakening of hair. The product in question is advertised as a collagen hair mask made of natural ingredients, including soy protein, sunflower seed, Chamomilla recutita, avocado, wheat protein, and shea butter. However, the product website raises several red flags. It lacks certifications that validate the product's safety and adherence to regulations. Furthermore, the website claims to have over 8500 happy customers, but there is no way to verify this claim as reviews are inaccessible. This lack of transparency and regulatory compliance makes the product's claims highly questionable. The idea that collagen can restore hair is appealing, but the scientific evidence does not fully support this claim. Collagen makes up a significant part of our hair, skin, and nails. However, the direct application of collagen to hair does not necessarily translate to rejuvenation or significant repair. Collagen may improve hair's appearance by making it smoother and more manageable temporarily. But, it does not fundamentally rejuvenate or repair hair from within. A recent May 2024 study indicates that collagen supplementation may be more helpful in reaping the benefits, rather than topical application. A 2021 review compares the claims made by collagen companies on social media with existing scientific evidence. While some studies show collagen supplements can improve skin elasticity and hydration, the media's claims exceed the current scientific support. Some evidence suggests that collagen is essential for hair health, but it is more effective when consumed. Topical treatments like hair masks are unlikely to penetrate deeply enough to offer significant benefits. We need more research to understand collagen's effects and mechanisms. Scientific studies have shown that collagen supplements can improve skin elasticity and hydration, but there is no conclusive research on the effects of collagen applied directly to hair. The hair is primarily composed of keratin, another type of protein. And, even when collagen can provide a temporary coating to smooth the hair shaft, it does not penetrate deeply enough to cause true rejuvenation. Therefore, the claim that collagen hair masks can rejuvenate hair is largely false. Dr Sachin Gupta, a Dermatologist, at Amrita Hospital, Faridabad, says, 'Collagen is an essential protein for maintaining skin and hair health. But, the topical application of collagen through hair masks is unlikely to deliver the significant rejuvenation effects that are often advertised. Collagen molecules are actually too large to penetrate the hair shaft or scalp effectively. For substantial improvement in hair quality, I generally recommend a balanced diet rich in proteins and vitamins, along with clinically approved treatments.' Dr Rashi Soni, a Dermatologist, at Rashi Hospital, Hingoli, Maharashtra, states, 'Topical treatments like collagen hair masks can provide temporary cosmetic benefits, such as improved hair texture and shine. However, they do not address deeper hair health issues or damage. There is limited scientific evidence to support the claims that these masks can rejuvenate or restore hair significantly. Patients looking for long-term solutions should focus on overall nutrition and consult with their dermatologist for personalised treatment options.' Collagen hair masks are often marketed alongside other hair treatments such as keratin treatments, deep conditioners, and protein treatments. Keratin treatments, for instance, are more established and have shown more consistent results in strengthening and smoothing hair. Deep conditioners and protein treatments also offer benefits by temporarily filling in gaps and cracks in the hair shaft, providing smoother and shinier hair. Compared to these treatments, collagen hair masks may provide some superficial benefits but lack the scientific backing for significant hair rejuvenation. If one chooses to use a collagen hair mask despite the lack of strong evidence for its efficacy, it is generally recommended to use such masks once a week. Overuse of protein-based treatments, including collagen masks, can lead to protein overload, which can make hair brittle and more prone to breakage. It is essential to balance the use of protein treatments with moisturising treatments to maintain healthy hair. A 2019 study says that taking 2.5 to 15 grams of hydrolysed collagen per day is safe. The side effects of collagen hair treatments are generally minimal, especially if you use the product as per the directions. However, some individuals may experience allergic reactions or scalp irritation. It is important to perform a patch test before applying the product to the entire scalp. Additionally, as with any hair product, overuse can lead to buildup on the hair and scalp, which may cause dullness and potential damage over time. The product lacks transparency and credible certifications, casting doubt on its efficacy. For better hair health, we recommend a balanced diet rich in collagen-promoting nutrients and consulting hair care professionals.

title: Fact Check: Can a combination of turmeric powder, coconut oil, clove essential oil and sea salt reverse cavities and heal tooth decay?
claim_text: A combination of turmeric powder, coconut oil, clove essential oil and a pinch of sea salt can reverse cavities naturally and heal tooth decay.
quick_take: Turmeric, sea salt, coconut oil, and clove essential oil have beneficial properties for oral health, such as reducing plaque. However, they are unable to reverse cavities or heal tooth decay. While they can support oral hygiene, they should not be relied upon as a solution for existing cavities, which require more than natural remedies.
doctor_explanation:
Cavities, once formed, cannot be reversed, and tooth decay cannot heal naturally. Tooth decay/cavitation, in medical terms known as dental caries, was described by Shafer in 1993 as an irreversible microbial disease of the calcified tissues of the teeth, characterized by demineralization of the inorganic portion and destruction of the organic substance of the tooth, which often leads to cavitation. This widespread chronic condition is primarily caused by cariogenic bacteria, such as Streptococcus mutans, which attach to the teeth. These bacteria metabolize sugars into acid, which gradually erodes and weakens the tooth structure. The formation of dental caries requires four key elements: the presence of bacterial biofilm (plaque), fermentable carbohydrates, dental hard tissues, and a sufficient amount of time. There is no cure for tooth decay that has already taken place.

Tooth decay is caused by microorganisms found in dental plaque, and regular removal of this plaque through tooth brushing and flossing is considered the most effective preventive approach. Fluoride helps prevent dental caries by reducing demineralization and promoting the remineralization of tooth structure, forming acid-resistant fluorapatite crystals.

While turmeric, coconut oil, clove essential oil, and sea salt have various health benefits, reversing caries or healing cavities is not one of them. There is no cure for existing dental caries, and no drug or ingredient is recommended by the dental community for their treatment.

Several studies have explored the individual roles of these ingredients in dental health. A review article published in the journal Bioinformation mentioned that turmeric mouthwash is effective in the prevention of plaque, which is the responsible element for the formation of dental caries; turmeric extract is also used to make a coloured pit and fissure sealant applied on the tooth surface for the prevention of dental caries. However, this study does not mention the healing or reversal of caries. Clove essential oil and its two main compounds can inhibit decalcification and/or potentially promote remineralization caused by acidic apple beverages, as concluded in a study published in the International Journal of Dentistry. However, the study does not explore clove oil's effectiveness in healing or reversing tooth decay. A study on the role of coconut oil pulling in plaque-induced gingivitis found that coconut oil pulling, when used as an additional oral hygiene aid, is effective in reducing plaque formation and subsequent plaque-induced gingivitis, published in the Journal of the Indian Association of Public Health Dentistry. There is no information about reverting caries or healing them. A review article published in the American Journal of Dentistry mentions that sea salt aids in dental demineralization but there is no role of sea salt in reversing tooth decay or dental caries.

Although studies have shown that turmeric, sea salt, coconut oil, and clove essential oil individually aid in preventing tooth decay and plaque formation — a key factor in dental caries — there is no research indicating their combined effectiveness in preventing dental caries. Additionally, there is no scientific evidence supporting their ability to reverse or heal cavities. These ingredients are also not recommended by the dental community as a treatment for tooth decay.

Dr Ritu Thawait, Dental Surgeon, Medical Officer, CHC, Risali, Durg, C.G. told Medical Dialogues: 'Turmeric, sea salt, coconut oil, and clove essential oil have properties that may aid in plaque prevention. However, they cannot reverse cavities or heal tooth decay. Effective cavity treatment requires proper oral hygiene and professional dental care, rather than relying solely on these natural remedies.'

Dr Meenakshi Sahu, Senior Associate Dentist, at Vyas Dental Inn, Raipur (C.G.), added: 'While natural ingredients like turmeric, sea salt, coconut oil, and clove essential oil have benefits for oral health, they are not substitutes for professional dental treatments. Currently, there is no cure for dental caries, and no ingredient can reverse it. According to its standard definition, caries is an irreversible disease process — means it cannot revert back and can only be managed manually in dental clinics.'

title: Fact Check: Can a concoction of mango, peepal, and jamun leaves heal a perforated eardrum?
claim_text: An Instagram reel suggests that a perforated tympanic membrane (hole in the eardrum or 'kaan ka parda fatna') can be treated at home using a concoction made from mango, peepal, and jamun leaves. The preparation involves boiling 10 leaves of each type in 400 mL of water until it reduces to half (200 mL), mixing the remaining liquid with 100 mL of mustard oil, and further boiling it to create a concentrated mixture. This oil-leaf concoction is then applied to the ear daily, with the promise of healing the perforation within 30 days. The claimant cites a Sanskrit shloka from Ayurveda to support this remedy.
quick_take: A social media post claims that a concoction of mango, peepal, and jamun leaves can heal a perforated eardrum. We fact checked this and have deemed it false.
doctor_explanation: The claim references a Sanskrit shloka: 'दुःखवर्धनकं सिक्त्वा जम्ब्वाम्राश्वत्यपत्रजैः | क्वाथैस्तैलेन सुस्निग्धं तच्चूर्णैश्चावधूलयेत् || 3 ||' This translates to: 'Sprinkle (the wound or affected area) with a decoction made from the leaves of jamun (Syzygium cumini), mango (Mangifera indica), and peepal (Ficus religiosa). Then, apply well-prepared oil mixed with these ingredients, ensuring it is smooth and well-soaked. Finally, dust the area with appropriate medicinal powders.' While the shloka discusses wound healing in general, it does not mention ear conditions, or perforated eardrums. Applying this advice to a delicate issue like an eardrum perforation is not appropriate or supported by evidence. The eardrum, or tympanic membrane, is a thin, delicate structure that needs proper medical care. Small perforations may heal on their own, but larger ones or persistent cases require medical treatment, such as surgery (Tympanoplasty or Myringoplasty). Homemade remedies like the one suggested can do more harm than good. Mustard oil is not sterile and can irritate the ear canal or cause infections. An older study from 1997 showed that mustard oil increased ear swelling and plasma leakage in mice, peaking around 30 minutes after application. Similarly, boiling leaves does not guarantee sterility, and plant extracts may introduce allergens or bacteria. Most importantly, we found no evidence in modern medicine that this concoction can treat perforated eardrum at home. Additionally, two 2024 Ayurvedic case reports show that ear drum perforations can occur due to injuries, infections, or pressure changes, leading to pain, hearing loss, and sometimes dizziness. While Ayurveda doesn't directly mention treatments for ear drum perforations, it offers effective wound care methods. In both cases, Ayurvedic medicines, used locally and systemically, helped heal large perforations and restore hearing. However, none of these methods, or any other Ayurvedic texts, mention that a concoction of mango, peepal, and jamun leaves with mustard oil can heal a perforated eardrum at home. We found no evidence to support this claim. Dr Annusuiya Gohil, MD Scholar at the All India Institute of Ayurveda, explains: 'In Ayurveda, there is no direct reference to treating a perforated eardrum with a concoction of mango, peepal, and jamun leaves mixed with mustard oil. Tympanic membrane perforations are delicate conditions requiring precise care. Ayurvedic texts focus on general wound healing (Vranachikitsa) using herbs and oils, but these treatments are not specific to ear injuries. Applying unverified remedies in the ear can risk infections or worsen the condition. It is always best to consult a qualified doctor for such issues.' Dr Manan Arora, BAMS, Specialised in Chronic Disorders & Mental Wellness, New Delhi, said: 'The mango leaves are known for their anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. Peepal (Ashvattha) leaves are considered soothing and healing in Ayurveda, often used for wounds and inflammation. Jamun is recognized for its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, primarily benefiting digestive health and blood sugar control. When boiled in water and mixed with mustard oil (which also has anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties), this mixture may offer soothing effects and help reduce inflammation. However, there is no strong scientific evidence to support its ability to heal a perforated eardrum specifically.' Dr Mohit Sandhu, BAMS, Shri Shubhda Ayurveda Wellness Clinic, Gurugram, states: 'Ayurveda focuses on enhancing the body's natural healing processes by supporting tissue repair and reducing dosha imbalances. For minor perforations, Ayurvedic remedies might show results in reducing pain and inflammation within a month. However, significant perforations often require surgical intervention for full recovery. The efficacy of this concoction for completely healing a perforated eardrum remains uncertain without proper clinical evidence. Consulting an experienced Ayurvedic physician for a personalized treatment plan is essential.' Using this concoction can be harmful. The risks include ear canal irritation, infections, and worsening of the condition. A perforated eardrum often heals naturally within a few weeks, but consulting a doctor is essential to avoid complications. Treatments include keeping the ear clean and dry, and not putting anything in the ear unless advised by a healthcare professional.

title: Fact Check: Can a corn-silk-based formula manage kidney stones?
claim_text: According to an Instagram post, a concoction of corn silk, lemon juice, salt, and black pepper is a highly effective remedy for kidney calculi. According to the post with the description, "क्या आप किडनी स्टोन की समस्या से परेशान हैं?", consuming this formula daily may aid in the dissolution of kidney stones of any size.
quick_take: An Instagram reel claims that a corn-silk-based formula has the potential to dissolve kidney stones. We fact-checked the assertion and found that it is mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Renal calculi, or stones, are solid aggregates of specific minerals and salts that develop in the kidney. These are usually induced by supersaturated urine, resulting in crystallisation. Smaller stones are usually asymptomatic; however, larger calculi are highly obstructive and might lead to haematuria, significant pain, hydronephrosis, and even potential urinary infections. In addition to renal calyces, crystallisation also occurs in the gall bladder, where it manifests as gallstones. These cholesterol or bilirubin aggregates usually develop due to supersaturation of bile, nucleation, and impaired gallbladder motility. While these may be variable in size, the larger obstructive ones can result in biliary colic, jaundice, or even pancreatitis. Both aggregations are crystalline formations, but they differ in their composition, location, risk factors, and aetiology. Usually, knowing this distinction aids in selecting the most effective diagnostic and management approach. Analysis of ingredients: Corn silk may support kidney function because of its high polysaccharide and anti-inflammatory characteristics. Furthermore, it may lessen the likelihood of renal stones by reducing oxidative stress and preventing crystal adhesion. Lemon juice, due to its high citrate content, usually prevents calcium oxalate from aggregating. Supplementing with lemon juice may also help patients with oxalate-related nephrolithiasis prevent recurrent stones. Salt: Daily consumption of salt is associated with an increased risk of kidney stone formation. This is because the high sodium concentration of salt could produce hypercalciuria. Consequently, salt consumption can be more detrimental than advantageous. Black pepper: While it is high in antioxidants and has an excellent bioactive profile, there is no substantial evidence suggesting that black pepper plays a role in the prevention of kidney stones. Dr. Bhanu Mishra, a consultant nephrologist at Delhi's BLK Max Hospital, suggests the aforementioned combination is ineffective at dissolving stones. While drinking adequate water and consuming calcium can help prevent kidney stones from forming, the notion that an at-home formulation will effectively dissolve and eliminate kidney stones is inaccurate. Patients should seek medical help right away if they suspect kidney stones or if they experience any of the following symptoms: fever with chills, burning in the urine, nausea or vomiting, or back pain. Professionals manage renal stones after a thorough clinical and diagnostic assessment. Dr. Archana Daftardar, Consultant Nephrologist and specialist in transplants and hypertension at Renova Hospitals in Kompally, Hyderabad, reinforces that there are several misconceptions associated with kidney stone management and prevention. Unproven natural substitutes, however, can make the condition worse rather than better. Dr. Sharad Malhotra, HOD Gastroenterology, Hepatology & Therapeutic Endoscopy, Aakash Healthcare, New Delhi, advises against adopting home remedies as a long-term treatment for kidney stones. Even while they may offer moderate benefits for digestive or urinary health, these unregulated remedies shouldn't replace conventional medical intervention for renal calculi, as they lack strong scientific support. Dr. Ganesh Srinivasa Prasad P, a consultant nephrologist at Narayana Health City in Bengaluru, suggests limiting quantities of sugary foods, alcohol, tobacco, carbohydrates, and animal products to further reduce the incidence of uric acid stones. While optimal hydration, dietary citrate, or medically supervised herbal supplements may play preventive roles, they are not effective for the dissolution or expulsion of larger calculi. Relying on such unregulated home cures could cause renal function to deteriorate by delaying medical intervention.

title: Fact Check: Can a cream made from carrot juice, coconut oil, almond oil, and Vaseline eliminate wrinkles overnight?
claim_text: Applying a cream made from carrot juice, coconut oil, almond oil, and Vaseline every night before bed can eliminate wrinkles overnight.
doctor_explanation:
Two board-certified dermatologists provided expert commentary refuting the claim. Dr. Manjot Marwah, MD Dermatologist, Director of LHR Clinics (Punjab and Himachal), Founder of EnagenBio, stated: "There is no cream or treatment in the world that can make wrinkles go away overnight. Not even Botox works overnight. Wrinkles are seen because of muscle movements on our faces and creams don't even penetrate till the muscles so this claim itself is baseless. Moisturizers like coconut oil, almond oil or Vaseline only hydrate the skin while carrots have beta carotene which may help pigmentation over a period of time but has no effect on wrinkles at all." Dr. Asha Zacharia, Consultant in Dermatology & Cosmetology at KIMSHEALTH Trivandrum, added: "Cream containing carrot juice, almond juice, coconut oil and Vaseline have moisturising properties which helps in hydration to some extent but do not erase wrinkles which are due to loss of elasticity of the skin. Oil application can block the pores causing breakouts and also can cause irritation of the skin giving rise to a dull appearance." 

The article further provides scientific context: Carrots contain carotenoids, flavonoids, vitamins, and minerals acting as antioxidants; coconut oil (90–95% saturated fats, mainly lauric acid ~47.5%) has antibacterial, antifungal, and anti-inflammatory properties used in Ayurveda; almond oil has been used in Chinese, Ayurvedic, and Greco-Persian medicine for dry skin conditions like psoriasis and eczema; and Vaseline acts as an effective barrier to lock in moisture, soothe dry skin, and has antibacterial and anti-inflammatory effects useful for minor cuts, burns, chapped lips, eczema, and atopic dermatitis. 

Regarding wrinkle science: Wrinkles are visible lines/folds; fine wrinkles are <1 mm, coarse wrinkles ≥1 mm; they form due to internal factors (ageing, hormonal changes, health conditions) and external factors (sun exposure, smoking), causing skin to become thinner, less elastic, and more fragile. Wrinkles cannot be fully eliminated as they are part of the natural ageing process, though treatments (injectables, topical creams, chemical peels, dermabrasion, laser treatments) can reduce their appearance.

Specific scientific evidence cited: A study in Nutrients (PMC10459432) found that methanol extract from powdered red carrot (Daucus carota L.) cell lines (R4G), rich in anthocyanins with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, may support healthy skin and reduce signs of ageing — but does NOT mention eliminating wrinkles overnight. A review in the International Journal of Life Sciences mentions coconut oil's potential in delaying wrinkles and skin sagging — but no evidence it eliminates wrinkles overnight. A study in Phytotherapy Research (PMC6916293) found that daily almond consumption may reduce wrinkle severity in postmenopausal women — but did not indicate overnight elimination. A review in the International Journal of Pharmaceutical and Clinical Research notes petroleum jelly protects skin from wind and cold and works as a moisturizer — but no mention of wrinkle elimination. The article concludes there is no scientific evidence — individually or combined — that these ingredients can eliminate wrinkles overnight, and no medical consensus supporting such a claim.

title: Fact Check: Can a cream treat various orthopedic problems?
claim_text: A Facebook post advertises a cream that claims to cure various bone and joint diseases in a few weeks without any side effects. The video shows that several bone and joint conditions were treated within a few weeks after applying a cream.
quick_take: A social media post claims that with the help of a cream, various bone and joint diseases can be cured in a few weeks without any side effects. We fact-checked and found this claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: It is not possible to treat all orthopedic diseases and conditions with a single product. Orthopedic diseases and conditions consist of a wide range of issues affecting the musculoskeletal system, including bones, joints, muscles, ligaments, and tendons. Orthopedic problems can include fractures, arthritis, sprains, strains, tendonitis, spinal disorders, and more. The treatment approach for the specific orthopedic disease or condition varies depending on the specific diagnosis and severity of the condition. The treatment includes a multidimensional approach with non-surgical interventions such as physical therapy, medication, braces, and assistive devices, and surgical interventions like joint replacement, fracture fixation, or spinal surgery, depending upon the condition. Tailored treatment is needed for a specific condition and the overall health of the patient that addresses the specific underlying causes and symptoms. There is no scientific evidence to prove that a single cream can treat various orthopedic conditions. Creams or topical treatments aid in managing certain orthopedic conditions, particularly those involving localized pain, inflammation, or mild soft tissue injuries. However, creams alone typically cannot treat the underlying causes of most orthopedic conditions. Any topical creams can provide only temporary relief from symptoms such as pain, inflammation, or muscle soreness. They often contain ingredients like analgesics (pain relievers), anti-inflammatories, or counterirritants that work by numbing the area, reducing inflammation, or providing a cooling or warming sensation. The product endorsed in the advertisement is 'Perfectx Instant Concentrate Cream.' As seen on the page, it claims to have ingredients like Chondroitin, Vitamin K2, Methylsulfonylmethane, arnica montana flower extract and glucosamine. All of these have properties that might aid in treating the symptoms, such as pain, inflammation, etc, but cannot cure the disease. Also, there are several types of musculoskeletal diseases and these can't help with all of them. Dr Rachit Gulati, Medical Director at SAAOL Ortho Care clarifies: 'There are a lot of topical diclofenac (a potent painkiller), capsaicin, lignocaine and other ointments or gels in the market which can only offer an extremely short-lived symptomatic relief when rubbed on the skin. However, the level of evidence is very low. These preparations, in no way, can alter or modify the disease process and cure deformities. One must take proper holistic treatment comprising oral medications, injectables, rehabilitation, orthosis, diet and other lifestyle changes for proper long-lasting management of the pinpoint cause of body pain.' Certain orthopedic conditions, such as osteoarthritis, joint deformities, spinal cord injuries, etc., can be irreversible, i.e., the damage or changes that occur cannot be fully reversed or healed completely. The extent of irreversibility depends on the specific condition and its severity. However, even in cases where a condition is irreversible, there are often treatments and interventions that can improve symptoms, restore function, and enhance the quality of life. In conclusion, while topical creams can offer symptomatic relief, they are not a comprehensive solution for all orthopedic conditions. Orthopedic conditions often require a multifaceted treatment approach, which may involve other interventions like physical therapy, medication, injections, or in some cases, surgery.
