title: Fact Check: Can a daily spoon of turmeric prevent cancer?
claim_text: Consuming one teaspoon of turmeric daily prevents cancer
quick_take: A social media video claims that consuming one teaspoon of turmeric daily prevents cancer. We fact checked and found this claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation:
Turmeric is a vibrant yellow spice made from the roots of the Curcuma longa plant. It is a staple ingredient in Asian cooking, renowned for its distinctive flavour and intense colour. Beyond its culinary uses, turmeric has a rich history in traditional medicine, primarily due to its active compound, curcumin. This compound possess anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties which potentially offers a range of health benefits. Curcumin may help alleviate symptoms of various conditions. These health conditions include arthritis, digestive issues, and even certain types of cancer. Additionally, turmeric has been linked to promoting heart health, improving cognitive function, and supporting overall well-being.

Curcumin is a compound responsible for the anti-cancer property of turmeric. Curcumin is a bioactive substance available in turmeric and has been extensively studied for its potential therapeutic effects. These effects include ability to inhibit the growth of cancer cells and induce apoptosis (cell death) in cancer cells. Numerous laboratory studies and some clinical trials shows that curcumin has the potential to interfere with the progression of different cancers of breast, colon, prostate, lung, and pancreatic cancer.

Curcumin's anti-cancer properties are believed to be attributed to its ability to modulate various molecular pathways involved in cancer development and progression, including inflammation, oxidative stress, and the proliferation of cancer cells. However, we need more research to fully understand its required quantity and quality along with the underlying anti-cancer effect of curcumin.

Dr Manish Singhal, Senior Oncologist, Apollo Hospitals in an interview with THIP emphasized the uncertainty surrounding the effective dosage of turmeric for cancer prevention.

It may. Turmeric, containing curcumin, is often a part of cancer's complementary treatment. Its historical use in Asian medicine is due to curcumin's anti-inflammatory properties. Clinical trials investigating curcumin's effects against cancer suggest it may counteract inflammation, a key aspect of cancer. However, there is no conclusive evidence that turmeric or curcumin can cure or prevent cancer in humans.

Additionally, limitations exist in curcumin's use, such as determining the proper dosage, absorption, and medication interactions. These factors highlight the need for further clinical trials to establish turmeric's efficacy in cancer treatment. Oncologists acknowledge turmeric's potential but emphasise the necessity for more research before considering it a reliable cancer treatment.

Turmeric contains curcumin which has shown promising anti-cancer properties in laboratory studies. But it is important to note that consuming just one teaspoon of turmeric is unlikely to prevent cancer on its own. The studies examining the effects of curcumin on cancer have typically used much higher doses than what you would get from a teaspoon of turmeric.

Additionally, cancer prevention is a complex issue influenced by various factors, including genetics, lifestyle, diet, and environmental exposures. Incorporating turmeric into the diet as part of a healthy and balanced eating pattern may offer some potential health benefits. But relying solely on it to prevent cancer does not have a support from enough scientific evidence.

In India, where turmeric is a staple in almost every meal, the incidence of cancer remains a significant concern. Recent statistics reveal that in 2022, an estimated 1,461,427 new cases of cancer were reported, with a crude rate of 100.4 cases per 100,000 individuals. Shockingly, the data suggests that one in every nine individuals in India is at risk of developing cancer during their lifetime. Notably, lung cancer tops the list of cancers affecting males, while breast cancer ranks highest among females.

Dr Shalin Nagori, Consultant Pathologist and Industrial Physician says, "Consuming one teaspoon of turmeric daily may offer some potential benefits, including its anti-inflammatory properties. This could theoretically contribute to cancer prevention. However, there is currently insufficient scientific evidence to conclusively support the claim that one teaspoon of turmeric can prevent cancer."

Voomika Mukherjee, Health and Nutrition Life Coach, emphasises that no specific food or food group can guarantee the prevention of cancer. Also, avoiding certain items will not necessarily reduce the risk. In the context of cancer treatment, maintaining a healthy body weight, particularly minimising visceral fat and enhancing muscle strength, alongside a balanced diet, is crucial. Mukherjee recommends a well-rounded diet and reducing the intake of sugar, caffeine, salt, and alcohol. She underscores that consuming meals of adequate quality and quantity plays a role in lowering the risk of cancer and other chronic diseases. However, it is essential to note that no single food can serve as a cure for cancer.

Shivashankar T. is the Chief Clinical Nutritionist and Dietician at Tata Memorial Cancer Hospital, Mumbai informs, "Eating a balanced diet can help maintain a healthy weight and provide the necessary nutrients to support the immune system. The best 'anti-cancer diet' is the Mediterranean diet. In this diet, there is less red meat and good amount of white meat".

title: Can a decoction of herbs make you lose weight? - THIP Media
claim_text: An Instagram post claims that preparing a drink with ajwain, ginger, cinnamon, cumin, fenugreek seeds, and lemon and consuming it on an empty stomach can lead to such dramatic weight loss in just one week that even your parents wouldn't recognise you. It also suggests that after drinking it, you won't need to visit the gym for the next seven lifetimes.
quick_take: A social media post claims that a herbal decoction can help you lose weight within just 7 days. We fact checked and found the claim to be false.
doctor_explanation: No, consuming cinnamon, ginger, ajwain, elaichi, jeera, methi, and lemon will not make you slim in 7 days, nor can it replace exercise forever. Weight loss happens when you consistently burn more calories than you consume through a healthy diet and regular physical activity. Relying solely on spices and herbs, no matter how beneficial, won't lead to meaningful or lasting fat loss. The idea of skipping exercise 'for 7 lives' is a humorous exaggeration, but it risks misleading people. Exercise supports not just weight control but also heart health, bone strength, and mental well-being. These ingredients can be part of a healthy routine, but they're no substitute for overall lifestyle changes. Dr P. Rammanohar, Research Director at the Amrita Centre for Advanced Research in Ayurveda (ĀCĀRA), notes that Ayurveda views obesity as a particularly difficult condition to manage. Classical Ayurvedic texts even describe it as nearly incurable, with the saying Karshyameva varam sthaulyat na hi sthoolasya bheshajam— meaning it's better to be lean than obese, as treating obesity is extremely challenging. There are no instant cures; neither internal nor external medicines alone can resolve it. Instead, Ayurvedic treatment emphasises stress reduction, a suitable lifestyle, and a tailored diet, with medicines serving only a supportive role. The success of the treatment greatly depends on adopting a personalised and holistic approach. Dietitian Priyanka emphasises the need for a holistic approach to achieve sustainable weight loss. This involves uncovering the root causes behind weight gain—such as inflammation, leaky gut, hormonal imbalances, or a sluggish metabolism. By addressing these underlying factors, targeted lifestyle adjustments can support effective fat loss and improve overall well-being. Long term effective weight loss requires: Healthy Eating - Focus on a balanced diet that includes plenty of fruits, vegetables, lean protein sources, and whole grains. Limit foods high in sugar and unhealthy fats. Controlling portion sizes and cutting down on high-calorie snacks and sugary drinks is also important. Physical Activity - Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise or 75 minutes of vigorous activity each week. Include strength training exercises to build muscle and boost metabolism. Activities like walking, running, cycling, and swimming are effective for burning calories and improving fitness. Lifestyle and Behavioural Changes - Adopt mindful eating habits, manage stress levels, and get enough quality sleep. Keeping a food journal, avoiding eating late at night, and being aware of emotional eating triggers can help maintain a healthy routine. Medical Options - For individuals with severe obesity, medical treatments such as weight-loss medications or bariatric surgery may be advised if lifestyle changes alone aren't effective. The idea that a herbal drink can make you lose weight in just 7 days is inaccurate. Fat loss is a complex process that relies on maintaining a consistent calorie deficit over time. No single drink can produce such results, particularly not in such a short and unrealistic period.

title: Fact Check: Can a 'Dip Diet' reverse Cancer naturally? - THIP Media
claim_text: An Instagram post claims that a Dip Diet can heal or reverse cancer naturally by following a strict plant-based and time-sequenced eating plan, eliminating the need for medical treatment.
quick_take: A social media post suggests that a cancer patient, after years of unsuccessful treatments such as chemotherapy and radiotherapy, found significant improvement through the Dip Diet and is now completely cancer-free. We fact checked and found the claim to be false.
doctor_explanation: Once you have been diagnosed with cancer, cancer cannot be reversed naturally using food or lifestyle alone. Scientific evidence consistently shows that once cancer develops, medical treatments such as surgery, chemotherapy, radiation, or immunotherapy are necessary to control or eliminate cancer cells. While a healthy diet and lifestyle can strengthen immunity and improve treatment outcomes, they cannot shrink tumours or destroy cancer cells on their own. Claims of natural reversal often stem from anecdotal stories or misunderstandings of spontaneous remission, which is rare and unpredictable. Relying solely on 'natural cures' may delay timely treatment, allowing cancer to progress. Dr Muskan Thakur, an Ayurveda specialist based in Indore, warns against depending solely on alternative remedies for cancer treatment. She highlights that this serious condition demands a multifaceted approach to medical intervention, such as immunotherapy, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and various hospital-based procedures. No credible research supports the idea that relying exclusively on home-prepared or Ayurvedic beverages/diet and meals can eradicate cancer. That said, Ayurvedic practices can complement recovery efforts by easing symptoms, mitigating treatment side effects, and enhancing general health. Boosting immunity through nutrient-rich foods, plant-based regimens, or natural juices must never substitute for proven, science-backed therapies. The Dip Diet, short for 'Disciplined and Intelligent Person's Diet,' was created by Dr Biswaroop Roy Chowdhury, who claims it can treat chronic diseases, including cancer, without medication. The diet promotes eating raw fruits and vegetables in a specific order, avoiding processed and cooked foods, and maintaining a certain meal schedule. It focuses heavily on plant-based nutrition and natural foods, which are indeed beneficial for general health. However, its founder has faced criticism and controversy for making unverified medical claims. There is no credible scientific evidence supporting its claims. The Dip Diet has not been tested in clinical trials or reviewed in peer-reviewed medical journals. Mainstream nutrition science does agree that fruits, vegetables, and whole foods help reduce the risk of cancer and support recovery during treatment. However, this is very different from curing cancer. Cancer is caused by complex genetic and cellular changes that diet alone cannot reverse. Sports Nutritionist Manasi Bandhuni warns that strict diets can cause big problems, like missing important nutrients, losing too much weight, and the worst one: cancer cachexia (a dangerous wasting away of the body). Many cancer patients on chemo or other treatments lose their appetite. This makes those problems even worse and lowers their quality of life a lot. Telling these people to eat only raw veggies and thinking it'll kill cancer cells is just silly and not helpful at all. Dr Sarthak Moharir, the lead radiation oncologist at Apollo Cancer Centre in Bilaspur, explains that cancer isn't one simple disease, it's more than 200 different ones, each caused by unique things. So, no one food, diet, or eating change can guarantee it won't happen again. However, munching on lots of green veggies and fruits every single day, for years, can cut the risk of some cancers. These foods help protect cells from damage and reduce body swelling. But the key is sticking with it as a long-term habit; starting it only after a cancer diagnosis won't make a big difference. Remember, no food is a miracle cure for cancer. It's a tough, tricky disease, and relying just on certain foods won't erase all the dangers.

title: Fact Check: Can a DIY mask make you look 18 again? - THIP Media
claim_text: A face mask combining banana peel, rice, cornstarch, milk powder, and lemon can reverse skin aging, reduce wrinkles, enhance collagen production, and restore a youthful, 18-year-old complexion.
quick_take: A social media post suggests that applying a DIY mask made of banana peel, rice, cornstarch, milk powder and lemon will reverse their skin's aging process and make you look 18 again. We fact checked and found the claim to be false.
doctor_explanation: Skin ageing is a natural biological process influenced by both internal factors (like genetics and hormones) and external ones (such as sun exposure, pollution, and stress). As we age, our body produces less collagen and elastin, the proteins responsible for firm, bouncy skin. Cell turnover slows, fine lines develop, and skin becomes thinner and more prone to sagging. Homemade pastes cannot undo the natural ageing process. The idea that a topical paste could make someone look 18 again is simply not supported by dermatological science. These ingredients may give you a smoother, slightly brighter appearance temporarily, but they cannot reverse wrinkles, firm sagging skin, or recreate youthful cell structure. Dr Ekansh Shekhar, a Dermatologist and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant from Lucknow, explains, 'Just because a skincare remedy is made from kitchen ingredients doesn't automatically make it safe. Facial skin is sensitive, and applying raw or untested mixtures can lead to irritation, allergies, or worsen existing issues. Some natural substances may be too harsh, block pores, or upset your skin's natural balance. It's important to always do a patch test and consult a dermatologist if you're unsure. Remember, natural isn't always harmless especially when it comes to your skin.' Dr Rashi Soni, Co-founder and Consulting Dermatologist at Rashi Hospital, Mumbai, emphasises that glowing skin requires more than just DIY face masks. A consistent routine with proper cleansing, exfoliation, moisturising, and daily sun protection is crucial. She adds that lifestyle habits like eating a balanced diet, staying hydrated, and getting enough sleep significantly impact skin radiance. While the banana peel, rice, and cornstarch paste can be applied, it does not reduce wrinkles, reverse ageing, or restore youthful skin texture. The paste gives temporary brightness and smoothness, but these benefits fade in hours and have no lasting structural impact on your skin. The psychological factor, feeling like you're doing something natural and good for yourself, can also trick you into believing it works better than it actually does. Regarding risks, lemon juice is highly acidic and can disrupt the skin's natural pH balance, making it overly acidic. Unlike the stabilized ascorbic acid found in Vitamin C serums, which is good for the skin, raw lemon juice can cause issues. Direct application followed by sun exposure may trigger phytophotodermatitis, a skin reaction. Dr Sonali Kohli, a Consultant Dermatologist at Sir HN Reliance Foundation Hospital, explains, 'Lemon is rich in Vitamin C and contains beneficial antioxidant and antibacterial flavonoids. However, its high acidity can disrupt the skin's natural pH balance.' Banana peel and ground rice can cause micro-abrasions or irritation when overused. Cornstarch can clog pores if not rinsed properly and may worsen acne or blackheads in oily skin types. For those with eczema, rosacea, or sensitive skin, this paste could lead to flaring or inflammation. Dr Jyothy Kannangath, a Consultant Dermatologist, explains, 'Fruit peels are packed with essential nutrients like dietary fiber, phytonutrients such as carotenoids and flavonoids, vitamins, potassium, and minerals. Consuming them with the fruit pulp offers numerous health benefits. Certain peels, including those from oranges, apples, papayas, bananas, kiwis, and pomegranates, may temporarily brighten or lighten the skin. While some peels may promote collagen production, they are unlikely to significantly reverse or delay aging.' A consistent skincare routine with the right ingredients, like niacinamide, peptides, AHAs, and retinoids, will always outperform any random kitchen concoction. While applying a banana peel, rice, cornstarch, and lemon juice paste might give your skin a temporary glow, it's not a magic recipe to regain your teenage skin. It won't make you look 18 again, and regular use, especially with lemon juice, can irritate your skin or even cause long-term damage. Instead of chasing internet beauty trends, focus on science-backed skincare, regular sun protection, and healthy habits.

title: Fact Check: Can a DIY mix give spotless skin in 2 minutes?
claim_text: A social media post claims that mixing aloe vera gel, toothpaste, haldi (turmeric) powder, and ENO (sodium bicarbonate) can brighten the face, remove spots, treat hyperpigmentation, and give spotless skin in just 2 minutes.
quick_take: A social media post claims that mixing aloe vera gel, toothpaste, haldi (turmeric) powder, and ENO (sodium bicarbonate) can brighten the face, remove spots, treat hyperpigmentation, and give spotless skin in 2 minutes. Our fact check reveals this claim is false.
doctor_explanation: Our fact check examined each ingredient in this DIY mix: Aloe vera: Aloe vera has soothing properties and contains compounds like aloin, which may help reduce inflammation and hydrate skin. Some studies suggest it can improve skin texture over time. However, there is no evidence that aloe vera can brighten skin or deliver spotless skin in 2 minutes. Skin brightening typically requires consistent use over weeks, not minutes. Toothpaste: Toothpaste is designed for oral hygiene, not skincare. It contains ingredients like fluoride and menthol, which can irritate the skin or cause allergic reactions. There is no scientific evidence supporting toothpaste as a treatment for spots or hyperpigmentation. Using it on the face may even lead to redness or dryness, especially for sensitive skin. Dr Iram Qazi, Dermatologist at Life Medical Centre & Clinic, UAE, explained that toothpaste is meant for oral hygiene, not for use on the skin. While some believe it can dry out pimples or lighten spots, it actually contains harsh ingredients like menthol, hydrogen peroxide, and baking soda that can irritate the skin. These can lead to burning, redness, peeling, or even worsen pigmentation in some cases. Dr Qazi strongly advises against using toothpaste as a spot treatment, as it may damage the skin barrier and make the issue worse. Haldi (turmeric): Haldi, or turmeric, contains curcumin, which has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. Some studies suggest it may reduce hyperpigmentation by slowing melanin production, but this usually requires weeks of regular use with properly formulated products. A 2025 review highlights curcumin's potential to protect the skin from sun damage and ageing. It may help reduce wrinkles, dark spots, and inflammation caused by UV rays. However, since curcumin doesn't absorb well into the skin, researchers are working on better ways to deliver it in skincare. A single use of haldi powder in a skin whitening DIY mix is unlikely to show noticeable results in just two minutes. Additionally, haldi can stain the skin yellow, which may be mistaken for brightening. ENO (sodium bicarbonate): ENO is a sodium bicarbonate-based antacid meant to relieve indigestion. It is not formulated for skin use. Sodium bicarbonate is alkaline and can disrupt the skin's natural acidic barrier, leading to irritation or dryness. There is no research supporting ENO for skin whitening or treating hyperpigmentation. Applying ENO to the face could harm sensitive skin, especially in combination with other ingredients. Skin lightening or brightening is a complex process involving melanin reduction, cell turnover, and hydration. No scientific evidence supports the idea that any topical mixture can achieve these results in two minutes. Most effective skincare treatments, like those with vitamin C or retinoids, require weeks of consistent use. The claim's timeframe is unrealistic and misleading. Dr Ekansh Shekhar, a Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant in Lucknow, says, 'Not always. Just because a remedy uses kitchen ingredients doesn't mean it's safe for your skin. The skin on your face is delicate, and applying raw or untested mixtures can cause irritation, allergic reactions, or even worsen existing problems. For example, some ingredients might be too harsh, clog your pores, or change your skin's natural balance. It's always best to patch test first and speak to a dermatologist if you're unsure. Natural doesn't always mean harmless, especially when it comes to skincare.' Combining random ingredients like toothpaste and ENO can be risky. These products are not designed for skin application and may cause irritation, allergic reactions, or long-term damage. Skin types vary, and untested mixtures can worsen existing issues like hyperpigmentation. There is no scientific evidence that mixing aloe vera gel, toothpaste, haldi powder, and ENO can brighten the face, remove spots, treat hyperpigmentation, or give spotless skin in 2 minutes. Some ingredients, like aloe vera and haldi, may offer skin benefits over time, but toothpaste and ENO are unsafe for topical use. This DIY remedy is misleading and could harm the skin.

title: Fact Check: Can a DIY remedy help get rid of dental cavities?
claim_text: A homemade preparation made with toothpaste, ginger, salt, and turmeric is a surefire way to address dental cavities, even those in children. Additionally, the recipe may help mask oral malodour and address gingival issues.
quick_take: According to a social media post, a DIY remedy is a definitive solution for dental cavities. After fact-checking the claim, we determined that it is false.
doctor_explanation: Dental cavities, also called dental caries, are persistent lesions brought on by microbiological activity that damages the teeth's calcified and inorganic tissue permanently. Due to their dread of the dentist, patients who have developed cavities have been compelled to rely on homemade or dubious online recipes. As a result, these at-home techniques are growing in popularity across several social media platforms. One such formulation involves combining toothpaste, salt, turmeric, and ginger. Turmeric, which has antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties, may help lessen gingival irritation and tooth plaque. Next comes ginger, that exhibits antibacterial effects that combat oral pathogens. Last but not least, salt, a gentle abrasive, has long been used to alleviate moderate gum inflammation. Given these benefits, the scientific evidence backing its effectiveness to reverse or halt the progression of dental caries remains inconclusive. Additionally, using abrasives like salt and turmeric powder on teeth frequently might gradually erode enamel. This progressive erosive activity may worsen tooth sensitivity and eventually lead to cavities, which could be more detrimental than beneficial. Dr Shalini Aggarwal, Professor in the Department of Endodontics and Conservative Dentistry at Dr. DY Patil Dental College & Hospital in Pimpri, Pune, additionally points out that tooth decay is an irreversible process. A cavity indicates the loss of enamel, the tooth's outermost covering, and a non-essential tissue that cannot be restored. Certainly not by the aforementioned ingredients. Moreover, none of the previously mentioned components can regenerate the dentin, the essential tissue that rests beneath the enamel. Dr. Aggarwal cautions that while these ingredients can't prevent or reverse decay, their excessive use can worsen damage to the tooth's remaining structure. It is imperative to recognise that cariogenic bacterial invasion can irreversibly damage teeth and must be evaluated and repaired by a qualified dentist. Therefore, it might be rather risky to rely on such unregulated temporary online remedies for tooth cavities. Dr. Gagandeep Singh Sodhi, Dental Specialist in Delhi, adds that most online shortcuts lack an adequate scientific foundation. Dependence on such do-it-yourself fixes may cause irreversible harm and delay a professional diagnosis. Furthermore, certain products that are sold online might not even have an authorisation. Therefore, any cases of bleeding, swelling, or oral pain should always be evaluated by a qualified dentist. Therefore, the safest and most efficient method of treating cavities and the pain they cause is still evidence-based dental care, which includes preventive fluoride application and appropriate restorative dental procedures.

doctor_explanation: Effective methods for reducing body fat include a balanced and calorie-controlled diet, emphasizing whole foods and portion control. Regular aerobic exercise, such as brisk walking or jogging, helps burn calories and improve overall fitness. Incorporating strength training builds lean muscle mass, enhancing metabolism. Adequate sleep and stress management contribute to a healthy lifestyle, supporting weight management. Stay hydrated, limit processed foods and sugary drinks. Consistency in these lifestyle choices is key for sustainable and healthy fat loss. According to Dr. P. Rammanohar from the Amrita Centre for Advanced Research in Ayurveda, 'Ayurveda considers obesity a challenging condition. There are no quick fixes or magical solutions. Treatment revolves around managing stress, adopting a healthy lifestyle, and following a specific diet. There's no one-size-fits-all remedy. The key to success lies in a comprehensive and personalized approach, where individuals actively participate in their treatment by making lifestyle changes to address obesity'. Regarding lemon: Lemon may aid in weight loss due to its rich vitamin C and antioxidant content, supporting digestion and possessing diuretic properties for detoxification. Additionally, it is recognized for boosting metabolism. However, excessive consumption may lead to stomach upset and impact dental health. Clinical Nutritionist Pariksha Rao explains that fat burners are substances enhancing lipid metabolism and weight loss. Lemon, rich in Vitamin C, dilutes fat and reduces cholesterol levels, improving fatty acid oxidation. Thermogenic foods, like ginger, induce heat, aiding fat burning. Ginger compounds like gingerols and capsaicin boost metabolism, lipolysis, and control appetite, contributing to weight loss. Rao emphasizes that these effects take time, and fat reduction cannot occur in just 15 days. Regarding black pepper: Piperine, a compound found in black pepper, has been studied for its potential to enhance metabolism and fat metabolism. It may also help in reducing fat levels in the bloodstream. However, black pepper alone is not a magic solution for weight loss. It should be considered as part of a comprehensive approach that includes a balanced diet and regular exercise. Regarding cinnamon: Only if consumed in higher dosage for more than 12 weeks. Cinnamon powder may have a modest impact on weight loss. In a 2020 study out of 679 records, 12 trials involving 786 participants were reviewed. The combined findings revealed that using cinnamon led to a significant decrease in body weight (BW), body mass index (BMI), waist circumference (WC), and fat mass (FM). The effects were more pronounced in individuals under 50 years and those with a baseline BMI of 30 or more. Higher doses of cinnamon for at least 12 weeks showed greater reduction in fat mass. Cinnamon alone is not a solution for significant weight loss. Regarding turmeric: Turmeric, containing curcumin with anti-inflammatory properties, might assist in regulating fat tissue. However, any weight loss effects are expected to be minor and should be seen within the context of a comprehensive weight management strategy. Sustainable weight loss primarily relies on a balanced diet, consistent exercise, and overall lifestyle choices. Turmeric is not a guaranteed remedy for weight loss. According to Dt. Harita Adhvaryu, 'Turmeric and ginger are considered beneficial for weight loss due to their antioxidant properties. Turmeric's curcumin helps reduce inflammation and boost metabolism, while ginger inhibits oxidative stress and has anti-inflammatory effects'. However, Adhvaryu emphasizes that there are no shortcuts to weight loss. A holistic approach, combining a calorie deficit through diet and exercise, is essential. While incorporating turmeric and ginger into meals can contribute to overall health, they are not standalone solutions for weight loss. Conclusion: Consuming this drink for only 15-20 days will not give significant results, and expecting all body fat to melt within this short time frame is unrealistic. Effective weight loss requires attention to various factors, including diet, stress management, hormonal balance, and physical activity. A holistic and consistent approach, encompassing these aspects, is essential for sustainable and meaningful weight loss rather than relying solely on a short-term solution. Consulting with Dt. Priyanka emphasizes that losing fat is a complex process that requires a multifaceted approach. According to her, relying on such a drink is insufficient. To effectively address fat loss, it's crucial to identify the underlying causes of weight gain, such as inflammation, leaky gut, hormone imbalance, toxins, low metabolism, or medication effects like steroids. Once the root cause is determined, modifying one's diet and lifestyle in alignment with the specific factors becomes essential for successful fat loss.

These ingredients offer some benefits to the skin like helps against acne, inflammation, and hyper pigmentation but achieving tight and plump skin also depends on genetics, diet, skincare routine, hydration, and lifestyle. Incorporating a variety of nutrient-rich foods and beverages into your diet, along with proper skin care practices, can support skin health. Chia seeds don't directly stimulate collagen formation but offer nutrients that indirectly support it. Rich in omega-3 fatty acids, they reduce inflammation, aiding skin health. Antioxidants like vitamin E in chia seeds protect against free radicals, preserving collagen. Additionally, their protein content provides amino acids crucial for collagen synthesis. While chia seeds alone won't spur collagen production, their inclusion in a diet can promote overall skin health. Maintaining collagen levels requires a holistic approach, encompassing various nutrients, skincare practices, and lifestyle habits for optimal skin integrity and elasticity.

Are chia seeds rich in vitamins? Chia seeds are not particularly rich in vitamins compared to some other foods. While they do contain small amounts of certain vitamins, such as vitamin B and vitamin E, their main nutritional benefits come from their high content of omega-3 fatty acids, fiber, protein, and minerals like calcium, phosphorus, and magnesium. title: Can a flax seed and rice water mask make hair super shiny and smooth instantly?
claim_text: A Facebook post suggests that applying a hair solution made with flax seeds and rice water (boiled and strained), mixed with aloe vera gel and glycerin, can make your hair super shiny, soft, and smooth. The video claims this happens naturally. The post says the mix should be left on for 45 minutes before washing. It also claims to fix frizzy and rough hair, making it glossy.
quick_take: A social media post claims that a flax seed and rice water mask make hair super shiny and smooth instantly. However, it is mostly false.
doctor_explanation:
Do flax seeds offer benefits for hair shine and smoothness? Maybe. Flax seeds are rich in omega-3 fatty acids and vitamin E. Omega-3 fatty acids can help nourish hair follicles and improve elasticity, potentially reducing breakage. Vitamin E is an antioxidant that helps reduce damage from free radicals, which can affect hair health and appearance. The mucilage (a thick, gel-like substance) produced when flax seeds are boiled creates a gel-like substance that can coat the hair shaft. This coating may provide a temporary smoothing effect and enhance shine by creating a more uniform surface. However, comprehensive scientific studies specifically proving a 'super' shine or smoothness from topical flaxseed application are limited. While popular in DIY recipes, the perceived benefits are often anecdotal. Similarly, another social media post claims that consuming flaxseeds can increase breast size. However, this is false.

Can rice water genuinely improve hair texture and gloss? Probably. Rice water, the starchy liquid left after soaking or boiling rice, has been used in traditional hair care for centuries. It contains inositol, a type of carbohydrate that may help repair damaged hair and stay in the strands even after rinsing. This could offer mild protection and a smoothing effect. Rice water also contains amino acids, B vitamins, and minerals, which might help strengthen hair and improve its shine. Some small studies suggest that rice water may reduce surface friction and increase hair elasticity, which can make hair feel smoother. Rice bran, found in the outer layer of the grain, might also support hair growth by encouraging certain signals in the skin. However, most of this evidence comes from lab-based studies rather than real-world use. Experts also warn that excess starch in rice water could make some hair types dry or stiff. Overall, rice water may offer minor, temporary benefits for some people. But there is no strong scientific proof that it can transform hair or boost growth in a significant way. Results can vary depending on how it is prepared and applied.

Is aloe vera effective in combating frizz and promoting softness? Yes, to some extent. Aloe vera is already popular for its moisturising and soothing properties. Its gel consists mainly of water but also contains vitamins, enzymes, minerals, and amino acids. For hair, it can act as a good conditioner, helping to hydrate the hair shaft. Dry hair often appears frizzy because its outer layer, the cuticle, is rough and open, absorbing moisture from the air. Aloe vera can help to smooth this cuticle and lock in moisture, thereby reducing frizz and increasing softness. While beneficial, it's a good hydrator rather than a miracle smoother. Similarly, another post tells viewers to eat capsicum for rough hair. However, this claim lacks any scientific evidence.

Does glycerin contribute to smoother, less rough hair? Yes, but may not work for everyone. Glycerin is a well-known humectant, which means it attracts moisture from the atmosphere into the hair shaft. This ability to draw in and retain moisture can significantly improve hydration levels in dry, coarse, or rough hair, making it feel softer and appear smoother. By plumping the hair with moisture, glycerin can temporarily improve its texture. It's important to note that in very high humidity, glycerin might attract too much moisture potentially leading to some types of hair becoming overly voluminous or frizzy, though this is less of a concern in a rinse-out mask balanced with other ingredients.

Will this specific combination and method provide 'super shiny' and 'super smooth' results as claimed? Unlikely to be 'super'. The ingredients in this hair solution may offer some short-term benefits, calling the results "super" is an exaggeration. Flaxseed gel and rice water can form a light film on the hair, adding temporary shine and smoothness. Aloe vera and glycerin help hydrate the hair, which may reduce dryness, frizz, and roughness. However, how well it works depends on many factors, such as hair type, condition, porosity, and how the mask is prepared. Natural ingredients do not guarantee dramatic or lasting changes. The effects are mostly surface-level and short-lived. With regular use, hair might feel easier to manage, but it is unlikely to transform hair structure or deliver outstanding results instantly, as mentioned in the post, for everyone.

Dr Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant in Lucknow, explains, "Although ingredients like flaxseed, rice water, aloe vera, and glycerin have some beneficial properties for hair, claiming they will make your hair 'super shiny' or 'super smooth' is an overstatement. These ingredients can certainly help with hydration, and they may provide a temporary smoothness and shine, especially for dry or frizzy hair. However, the results are usually short-lived, and the extent of the effect can vary depending on your hair type and condition. For some, it might improve manageability or reduce frizz in the short term, but it's unlikely to deliver long-term, transformative results."

Dr Rashi Soni, Dermatologist and Co-founder of Rashi Hospital in Mumbai, says, "This mask may provide temporary smoothness and shine, but the 'super' results are unlikely. It primarily offers a quick boost of hydration, which can help with frizz and dryness. However, the effectiveness will depend on your hair type, condition, and individual needs, so the results may vary from person to person."

THIP Media Take: The claim that a flax seed and rice water mask make hair super shiny and smooth instantly is mostly false. The promise that this DIY hair mask makes hair "super shiny, soft, and smooth" and solves frizz is a significant overstatement. While its natural ingredients might offer some mild, temporary improvements to hair texture and shine, the dramatic transformation claimed is not scientifically proven for this mixture. Benefits are typically modest, temporary, and vary by hair type, so the assertion of "super" results is largely misleading.

title: Fact Check: Can a fruit smoothie naturally cure UTIs in 14 days?
claim_text: A homemade blend of pre-soaked chia seeds, pineapple, apples, and lemon juice can naturally cure UTIs in 14 days
quick_take: A Facebook post claims that a fruit smoothie can effectively cure UTIs in 14 days. After fact-checking the claim, we found it to be completely false.
doctor_explanation:
UTIs are microbiological ailments affecting any part of the urinary system – kidneys, ureters, urinary bladder, or urethra. Bacteria, particularly uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC), are usually responsible for UTIs. Clinical signs usually include a burning sensation in the urine, frequent urges to urinate, discomfort during urination, cloudy urine, and perhaps fever. Bacterial migration usually poses a greater risk to women. Dr. Anita Gupta, Associate Director of Obstetrics and Gynaecology at Fortis La Femme in New Delhi, explains that certain anatomical features make women more vulnerable to UTIs. The female urethra is shorter than the male urethra and is more affected by sexual activity. Considering the proximity of the urethral opening to the vagina, an infection in the vaginal region is readily transmitted to the urinary tract. As women age, their outermost urethral lining gets thinner and drier, making them more vulnerable to UTIs. Dr. Ritu Sethi, MBBS, MD, Associate Director of Gynaecology and Obstetrics at Max Hospital in Gurgaon, Haryana, states that a woman's uterus expands during pregnancy, exerting more pressure on the bladder. This lowers the urethral capacity, and the bladder does not empty completely, leading to urinary retention. The resulting leftover urine increases the risk of UTIs by creating an environment that is conducive to bacterial growth. Along with the uterus, the developing foetus presses against the kidneys and other nearby organs. When the associated symptoms get progressively worse, persist longer, or occur frequently, UTIs become a concern. Therefore, timely management, appropriate antibiotic therapy, and closely monitored preventative measures are crucial to avoid issues and preserve long-term urinary tract health.

Although fruit smoothies containing pineapple, apple, lemon juice, and chia seeds are being promoted as a natural remedy for urinary tract infections, their relevance is confined to social media. Pineapple is often considered a popular fruit because it contains bromelain, which may have some minor anti-inflammatory properties. Nevertheless, there isn't sufficient scientific evidence to support pineapple's effectiveness in treating UTIs. Apples usually offer fibre and hydration. These are nutrient-dense foods that can promote regular bowel motions and support general urinary health due to their high fibre content, but they can't treat an active infection. In fact, for some people with an ongoing illness, extremely acidic foods such as apples may momentarily irritate the bladder and exacerbate symptoms. Lemon juice is believed to alkalise the body or may even inhibit bacterial growth. Nonetheless, it has no impact on urinary pH, suggesting that its intake cannot replace clinically validated antibiotic therapy. Chia seeds are packed with omega-3 fatty acids and soluble fibre. They may help with hydration and digestion, but there is no scientific evidence to support their use in treating UTIs. Therefore, even if the fruit smoothie might be hydrating, there isn't much solid scientific proof that it can treat infections, avoid complications, or act as the condition's primary intervention. The standard therapeutic regimen for UTIs continues to be medical examination followed by prescribed antibiotic therapy.

The majority of UTIs are bacterial infections that call for timely and targeted antibiotic therapy. Even while cranberry products, probiotics, or certain herbal preparations that are promoted as natural, safe, or chemical-free alternatives may offer mild preventive benefits, they lack the potential to eradicate active infections. Delaying the appropriate intervention may permit the existing bacteria to multiply and contribute to the development of recurrent UTIs and antimicrobial resistance. Furthermore, unmonitored home cures may interfere with ongoing medical therapy and conceal early warning indicators, causing the condition to proceed silently. Consequently, relying solely on such unregulated solutions—which vary in terms of dosage, purity, and safety—may delay the required action and contribute to serious complications, including sepsis and pyelonephritis.

For UTIs, medical experts employ a meticulous, clinically validated therapeutic approach. The clinical recommendations state that a complete evaluation of the symptoms together with diagnostic examinations, such as a urine analysis or culture to identify the causative organism—most commonly Escherichia coli—should be performed to make the diagnosis. For uncomplicated UTIs, short-course antibiotics might be therapeutic. In patients with complicated conditions such as diabetes or structural abnormalities, prolonged or parenteral therapy may be advised. To preserve long-term urinary health, recurring episodes may be managed via prophylactic antibiotics.

Dr. Ayush Chandra, (Diabetologist and Yoga instructor), Founder and Director of Nivaran Health in Delhi NCR, recommends that the most crucial precaution is to consume two to three litres of water each day. Additional precautions include emptying your bladder frequently, wearing breathable underwear, cleaning your body from front to back while using the restroom, and always seeking medical advice before taking a birth control pill. Above all, the doctor recommends washing the genitalia before and after sexual activity.

title: Can a garlic and turmeric enema help in weight loss? - THIP Media
claim_text: A garlic and turmeric enema can aid in weight loss and help reduce cholesterol by 1 kg

They can be given by a healthcare provider or self-administered at home with an enema kit. It's crucial to observe proper hygiene and safety protocols when performing an enema. Some alternate healthcare practitioners claim that coffee enema helps detoxify the body, which is not true.

Enemas are not typically used as a method for weight loss. While they may temporarily decrease the number on the scale due to removing waste from the colon, any weight loss is usually minimal and not sustained. Enemas primarily serve purposes related to bowel health, constipation relief, medical preparation, or medication administration, rather than weight loss. Eating vegetables is helpful, but believing a juice can replace medical care is not.

title: Fact Check: Can a healthy lifestyle help reverse type 1 diabetes?

In most cases, the illness manifests in childhood or adolescence, requiring lifelong insulin medication. Despite the development of novel experimental therapies, including immunomodulation, islet cell transplantation, and stem cell-based research, there is no reliable scientific evidence to support the notion that type 1 diabetes can be cured or reversed. However, these measures cannot replace prescribed insulin therapy, which remains essential for survival. Kapha Prameha, the early stages of the condition, can be controlled and even reversed with lifestyle changes and supportive therapy. Diabetes, however, cannot be reversed once it reaches Pitta Prameha and necessitates lifetime care. Once the ailment reaches its most severe level – Vata Prameha – managing it becomes particularly challenging. Dr. Rammanohar emphasises that no single herb or ingredient is an effective diabetes cure; research into potential cures is still underway. Dr. Naseemuddin N. Shaikh, Consultant Endocrinologist at Renova Century Hospitals, explains the difference between cure and remission: cure occurs when the ailment is entirely gone and will not return, while remission is the stage at which the disease is under control and does not require therapy, albeit it may recur. While type 1 diabetes requires insulin therapy for the rest of one's life and cannot be remitted, early-onset type 2 diabetes can be remitted with proper care. The assertion that diabetes can be cured is illegal in India under the Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act of 1954 and Schedule J of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules of 1945, which expressly prohibit advertising for the treatment of diabetes.

title: Fact Check: Can a heart attack be predicted a month in advance?
claim_text: A viral Instagram video claims that the body gives warning signs one month before a heart attack including dizzy spells, nausea, persistent fatigue with headache, body numbness on one side, and blurred vision. doctor_explanation: Feeling lightheaded, dizzy or nauseous can occur during a heart attack, but these are not proven early warning signs one month in advance. The NHS lists dizziness and nausea among possible heart attack symptoms, but ideally with chest pain or other urgent symptoms. The American Heart Association notes that true warning signs often involve recurring chest pressure or pain, which the video never mentioned. Occasional dizziness or nausea on its own usually has many other causes (like dehydration or stomach issues), so it isn't a reliable early indicator of a future heart attack. Chronic tiredness by itself is common in many illnesses and is not a classic sign of a pending heart attack. Harvard Health explains that constant new fatigue can sometimes hint at heart failure or underlying heart disease, but this is about overall heart health, not an immediate alarm for an oncoming attack. Daily headaches are even less related; they're not listed as heart attack symptoms at all. In fact, a sudden severe headache usually raises stroke concerns, not heart attack risk. Unexplained fatigue might warrant a check-up, but pairing it with headaches is not recognised as a heart attack warning in medical guidance. Dr Rachit Saxena, Director: Cardiac and Aortic Surgery, Narayana Hrudayala, Gurugram, explains that in many cases, a heart attack may not be completely sudden. Some individuals do experience early warning signs like new-onset acidity without a clear reason, breathlessness during regular activities, unusual tiredness, or vague chest discomfort that eases with rest. These may appear mild but can signal underlying heart disease, especially in people with risk factors like diabetes, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, or a family history of heart problems. Early recognition and timely check-up with a doctor, even for seemingly minor symptoms, can make a big difference in preventing serious cardiac events. Sudden numbness on one side of the body (arm, leg or face) is a well-known stroke warning, not a heart attack sign. Heart attacks generally cause pain or pressure (often spreading to shoulders or arms), but they do not cause half-body numbness. Dr Sreenivas Meenakshisundaram, Consultant Neurologist, Apollo Speciality Hospitals, Chennai, explains that when someone suddenly feels numbness or weakness on one side of the body, especially the arm, leg, or face, we immediately think of a possible stroke, not a heart problem. This kind of numbness usually means there's an issue with blood flow to the brain. It's a medical emergency and needs urgent attention. Heart attacks, on the other hand, more often involve chest pain, shortness of breath, or pain spreading to the arm or jaw. Confusing the two can delay the right treatment, which can be dangerous. A good rule of thumb to remember is that strokes are painless, while heart attacks are usually painful. Blurry or double vision generally points to issues in the eyes or brain blood vessels, not the heart. Harvard Health notes that sudden visual disturbances can signal a blocked artery in the eye (an eye stroke) or risk of a brain stroke. Long-term conditions like high blood pressure or diabetes also affect eyesight. Vision changes are not recognized as early signs of a heart attack. There is no reliable evidence that taking the herbal supplement shilajit will prevent a heart attack. Research on shilajit is very limited and mostly in animals. For example, one rat study found fewer heart lesions after dosing shilajit. But such findings don't prove any benefit for humans. The NHS and experts warn that claims for herbal remedies are usually based on tradition, not rigorous proof. Moreover, supplements like shilajit are not regulated like medicines, so even lab-tested products may vary in purity or contain undisclosed substances. Dr Almas Fatma, General Physician, from Navi Mumbai, explains, There's no strong scientific evidence that shilajit can prevent heart attacks. Some early research shows it may have antioxidant properties, but most of it is in animals or lab settings. We don't have enough reliable human data. It's safer to focus on proven steps like healthy eating, regular exercise, and managing blood pressure rather than relying on untested supplements. Additionally, the video features a person claiming to be a cardiologist. However, we couldn't verify this, as reverse image searches yielded no results. The video also does not mention any name or medical qualification, further raising questions about the person's credibility. Health authorities stress that if you are worried about heart disease, you should rely on information from doctors and official guidelines, not social media claims. NHS guidance even warns that some online sites selling remedies may be run by people pretending to be medical experts.

title: Can a herbal concoction help dissolve kidney stones in just 8 days?
claim_text: A well-circulated Instagram post with the caption "पथरी बाहर kidney Stone Remedy" promotes the consumption of a combination of fennel (methi), carom (ajwain), and cumin (jeera) seeds for the dissolution of kidney stones of any size in just 8 days.
quick_take: An Instagram post suggests that a herbal concoction can remove kidney stones in just 8 days. After analysing the notion, we found it false.
doctor_explanation:
When components such as calcium, oxalate, and uric acid precipitate and aggregate together into solid or firm lumps in the renal urinary or Bowman's space, they are known as kidney stones, medically known as renal calculi. While the herbal concoction formulated with fenugreek (methi), cumin (jeera), and carom (ajwain) seeds has been promoted as a kidney stone elimination agent, its significance is confined to social media platforms. 

Regarding fenugreek seeds (Trigonella foenum-graecum): Methi seeds may prevent kidney stones from forming rather than dissolving them by reducing the deposition of calcium-oxalate renal crystals. Since these results are only supported by animal research, large-scale human trials are required to validate fenugreek as a primary intervention for renal stone dissolution.

Regarding carom seeds (Trachyspermum ammi): The carom seed extract is under examination due to its antiurolithic activity, which includes diuretic effects and suppression of calcium-oxalate crystal aggregation. Additionally, carom seeds may facilitate passage or prevent the formation of stones. However, these potential advantages are limited to preliminary research and rat models. Therefore, additional solid medical evidence that carom seeds can remove kidney stones in humans is still required.

Regarding cumin seeds (Cuminum cyminum): Although cumin seed extracts may reduce the nucleation and development of calcium oxalate crystals, their effects remain restricted to preclinical investigations. Therefore, the ingredient's consumption for renal stone dissolution requires more extensive and thorough testing.

Dr. Sharad Malhotra, HOD Gastroenterology, Hepatology & Therapeutic Endoscopy, Aakash Healthcare, New Delhi, cautions against using home remedies as a long-term treatment for kidney stones, even though they can be beneficial for digestive or urinary health. He further emphasised that there is not sufficient evidence that these measures may eliminate or manage existing kidney calculi. It is never advisable to use these unsubstantiated substitutes for adequate medical care.

Although fenugreek, cumin, and carom seeds have promising anti-lithogenic or preventative qualities, there is no definitive evidence that they can efficiently dissolve kidney stones in humans, either alone or in combination. They might enhance urinary health or help avoid the formation of stones, but they shouldn't be the primary course of action for existing renal calculi.

It is not advised to utilise unregulated online alternatives, particularly those that promote kidney stone dissolution timelines. Despite their attractive packaging and widespread use as natural, chemical-free substitutes, such unsubstantiated remedies lack scientific backing. Moreover, these unverified therapies lack standardisation in terms of dosage, safety, and efficacy.

Dr. Archana Daftardar, Consultant Nephrologist and transplant and hypertension specialist at Renova Hospitals in Kompally, Hyderabad, asserts that there are many myths regarding the treatment and avoidance of renal stones. Unproven natural remedies might make the condition worse rather than better. Hence, it is recommended to consult a licensed Ayurvedic or allopathic doctor for timely evaluation and correct intervention.

While some online options may provide symptomatic relief and may help reduce stone formation risk or assist passage over time, their role is limited to being used as an adjunct and not a primary treatment option for kidney stones. Therefore, competent physician evaluation and evidence-based therapy remain the safest course of action, especially for stones that cause discomfort or complications.

Medical professionals suggest that renal stones undergo therapy as per their chemical composition, anatomical location, and geometric characteristics. Clinicians focus on preventing recurrence after the first painful episode, which would include nutritional guidance based on stone composition and metabolic assessment. Urinalysis and blood testing may help identify any underlying medical conditions.

title: Can a herbal cream lighten vitiligo patches within a week?
claim_text: A Facebook post promotes a herbal topical cream for vitiligo patches, claiming that using the product three times a day may reduce the spots by 60% in the first week, and the cream will demonstrate 100% results in the second week.
quick_take: According to a Facebook post, a herbal cream can help lighten vitiligo patches in a week. We checked the claim and discovered that it is completely false.
doctor_explanation: Vitiligo is characterised by depigmented skin patches caused by melanocyte loss or dysfunction. In essence, melanocytes are the cells that produce melanin, the pigment responsible for the colour of skin. With time, these symmetrical depigmented lesions might progress into larger ones anywhere on the body. Even though the condition is painless, it is more than a cosmetic issue. This is because, particularly when lesions are visible on exposed regions like the hands and face, it can have a substantial impact on an individual's physical, emotional, and social well-being. Additionally, the illness may be linked to thyroid-related disorders, diabetes, pernicious anaemia, and other autoimmune diseases. The post touts Sumifun herbal cream for vitiligo. For any product to be utilised as a successful treatment modality for an autoimmune skin condition, it must have a valid authorisation and a reliable chemical breakdown. The topical ointment is advertised as being made entirely of natural plant extracts or as being herbal on its promotional websites. However, during our research, we could not obtain a complete list of product ingredients. While one version of the website states that the cream contains Herba Asari, Radix Angelicae Dahuricae, Zebrachis, Tribulus, Rhizoma Zingiberis, and additional herbs, the other page mentions a more generic herbal extract. A potential drawback here is the paucity of publicly accessible information on how these elements affect melanocyte regeneration. Additionally, the product pages don't include any peer-reviewed studies that demonstrate its efficacy. Most importantly, just because a product is labelled as herbal does not mean that it is safe or effective. For a product to be approved as a therapeutic intervention for vitiligo, it must have a standardised formulation, a consistent dosage, and be backed by rigorous testing. The product's listing on Indian market websites appears to indicate that it is imported and promoted as a cosmetic item rather than a licensed medication. Any herbal cream making claims to cure or treat vitiligo normally needs to abide by National Drug Regulatory Standards. There is no peer-reviewed research or clinical trials assessing Sumifun Vitiligo Cream's effectiveness. Our search for the product in the PubMed database yielded no results, implying that it lacks solid scientific backing and cannot effectively replace the tried-and-true methods of topical corticosteroids, calcineurin inhibitors, and phototherapy. Dr. Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Cosmetician, trichologist, and Consultant in Aesthetic Medicine from Lucknow explains there is currently no long-term cure for vitiligo. Conventional therapy can help control it, restore some skin pigmentation, and prevent it from spreading. Using products that lack scientific validation may delay the necessary management of the condition. Dr. Gurman Singh Bhasin, Director & Chief Dermatologist, Skinclarity Clinic, Nagpur stresses that vitiligo is a complex autoimmune disease that needs an expert assessment and customised intervention. Despite their widespread promotion, internet products frequently lack scientific validation, stability evaluations, and formulations appropriate for vitiligo phases. From an Ayurvedic perspective, Dr Pallav Prajapati, BAMS, founder of Chetanya Ayurveda in Varanasi states that Ayurveda provides a very specific and all-encompassing approach to vitiligo, also known as 'Shwitra' or 'Kilasa', by emphasising the underlying causes of the condition rather than merely its symptoms. Dr Annusuiya Gohil, an Ayurvedic expert and MD Scholar at the All India Institute of Ayurveda points out that Ayurveda never supports the use of a particular formulation for all patients because its foundation is PURUSHAM VIKSHEYAM, which holds that each person is unique. Long-term interventions are usually necessary for significant repigmentation. It normally takes weeks to months for vitiligo therapies such as narrowband UVB therapy, ritlecitinib, or Janus kinase inhibitors to provide visible results.

title: Can a herbal ear spray treat tinnitus?
claim_text: According to a social media post, apparently shared by Dr Mahi Singh, one can treat tinnitus with the use of a herbal ear spray, that too, within mere 10 days. It further states if you do not apply the ear spray it can lead to hearing loss.
quick_take: A social media post claims that a herbal ear spray can treat tinnitus. After fact checking, we term it asfalse.
doctor_explanation:
Herbal and homemade remedies are very popular around the globe due to their ease of access and affordability. But they can pose serious threats to one's health if not used properly and without professional advice.

What is Tinnitus?
Tinnitus refers to the perception of sound without an external source, meaning others cannot hear it. While often described as a ringing sound, it can also manifest as roaring, buzzing, or other auditory sensations. Surveys suggest a highly variable range of 4% to 37% of adults experiencing tinnitus, and even children can be affected. Though for some, tinnitus may improve or disappear over time, it can also worsen and become chronic, persisting for three months or longer.

The exact causes of tinnitus are still unclear, but most individuals with the condition have some level of hearing loss. Tinnitus can impact quality of life by affecting mood, sleep, and concentration. In severe cases, it may even lead to anxiety or depression.

Can a herbal ear spray treat tinnitus?
No, herbal ear sprays can not treat tinnitus. While herbal remedies may claim to alleviate tinnitus symptoms, there is limited scientific evidence to support their effectiveness. Herbal ear sprays, like other herbal remedies, are often marketed as natural alternatives for various health conditions, including tinnitus. However, it's essential to approach such claims with caution and scepticism.

Moreover, this claim has been shared from the fake social media page using the name of Dr Mahi Singh. Other than a photo, there are no credentials mentioned on the page. Upon doing a reverse Google Reverse Image Search we found out that the photo belongs to Dr Mugdha D Vartak (Obs & Gyn) from Ameya Clinic, Pune.

It is also claimed in the video that the St Luke's Hospital, Singapore has created the herbal ear spray. But, we found no such ear spray or medication for tinnitus on the hospital's website. In fact, the word tinnitus did not yield any results on their website. Furthermore, any reputed and trustworthy pharma company would never use a fake profile to advertise their product, it just diminishes the credibility of the product.

Tinnitus is a complex condition with diverse underlying causes, ranging from hearing loss to medical conditions and exposure to loud noises. There is no one-size-fits-all solution for tinnitus, and what works for one person may not work for another.

Dr Kanchan Chaudhary says, "It's important to understand that relying on herbal ear sprays to treat tinnitus is completely wrong and should be avoided at all costs. Tinnitus refers to any continuous sound in the ear, like ringing, that disrupts daily activities and sleep. It can stem from various causes such as ear infections like acute otitis media (AOM) or chronic otitis media (COM), noise-induced hearing loss, or benign lesions. It could also signal underlying inner ear issues or even a brain tumour."

Dr Chaudhary further continues, "Ignoring tinnitus can have serious consequences, including the risk of depression, if left untreated. Herbal sprays are not effective in treating tinnitus; in fact, they can create an environment conducive to fungal infections in the ear, leading to a condition called otomycosis. This condition can be particularly severe in diabetic patients. Hence, it's important for patients to seek proper medical care for tinnitus rather than relying on herbal remedies."

Is there a cure for tinnitus?
As of now, there is no universally recognised cure for tinnitus. Tinnitus has various underlying causes, and its management involves addressing those causes and alleviating associated symptoms rather than completely eliminating the perception of tinnitus itself.

However, while there may not be a cure in the traditional sense, many individuals find relief from tinnitus through various treatment approaches. These may include sound therapy, counselling, medications, lifestyle modifications, and management of underlying conditions contributing to tinnitus.

Research into potential treatments for tinnitus is ongoing, and advancements are being made in understanding the mechanisms behind the condition and developing a cure. While a definitive cure has not yet been found, many individuals with tinnitus are able to effectively manage their symptoms and lead fulfilling lives with the support of healthcare professionals.

title: Can a herbal mouthwash manage dental caries in seven days?
claim_text: Swishing the mouth daily with a homemade combination of crushed cloves, Himalayan salt, and lemon juice can readily eliminate caries and tooth stains in just seven days. doctor_explanation:
Dental caries, often known as cavities, are multifactorial, sugar-driven, biofilm-mediated defects brought on by an imbalance between tooth mineral loss and repair. These are mostly caused by two bacteria that generate organic acid: Lactobacillus species and Streptococcus mutans. Long-term microbial activity by these bacteria demineralises dentin and enamel by turning carbohydrates into organic acids.

Regarding the claim that the combination of clove, lemon juice, and Himalayan salt can cure dental caries in seven days: NO - this is inaccurate and dangerous. The three elements must be thoroughly examined:

1. Crushed Cloves: An age-old remedy for dental pain containing eugenol, an active ingredient with potent, mild analgesic and antimicrobial characteristics. However, clove—whether crushed or in oil—should only be used as an auxiliary, temporary dental pain reliever. It CANNOT eradicate carious lesions or restore tooth structure.

2. Himalayan Salt: Well known for its capacity to reduce bacterial loads via osmotic mechanisms. Nevertheless, there is a Dearth of scientific evidence supporting that salt can arrest or reverse caries.

3. Lemon Juice: Regardless of being packed with vitamin C and citric acid, it has NO established capacity to repair dental tissue. Regular use is LINKED TO DENTAL ENAMEL LOSS, which may exacerbate pre-existing dental conditions.

Dr. Shalini Aggarwal, Professor in the Department of Endodontics and Conservative Dentistry at Dr. DY Patil Dental College & Hospital in Pimpri, Pune, maintains that tooth decay is an irreversible process. A cavity is an indication that enamel—the vital dental tissue that cannot be replaced—has been lost and cannot be repaired by the aforementioned elements. Similarly, natural materials cannot take the place of dentin, the vital tissue that lies beneath dental enamel. While these substances cannot stop or reverse decay, Dr. Aggarwal cautions that an overdose of them may cause additional damage to the tooth's remaining structure.

Dr. Pooja Sharma, BDS, MDS, of NIMS University in Jaipur, concurs, cautioning that using home remedies for dental caries may frequently lead individuals to think they do not require professional care. Gum infections and cavities cannot be cured on their own; a dentist must diagnose and treat them. When employing natural remedies for teeth, carelessness might exacerbate small issues like swelling, excruciating pain, or tooth loss.

The best methods for managing dental caries are: fluoride exposure, biofilm control, dietary sugar reduction, and restorative therapy when cavitation occurs. Dependence on such unregulated online options cannot only delay the required dental treatments but may also lead to severe complications.

title: Fact Check: Can a herbal powder remove teeth cavities?

doctor_explanation:
Dental cavities, also called caries or tooth decay, occur when oral bacteria produce acids that attack and demineralize tooth enamel. This can result in small holes or cavities. These acidic attacks are often caused by frequent consumption of sugary and starchy foods, as well as poor oral hygiene. The first sign of decay is usually a white spot, indicating mineral loss in the enamel. Fortunately, at this stage, the enamel can self-repair with the help of minerals from saliva, fluoride from toothpaste, or with the assistance of a dental professional. ESP plays a crucial role in bone and dental metabolism and has been shown to form high-quality hydroxyapatite. However, ESP can only be used to arrest the enamel cavities. ESP has demonstrated effectiveness in laboratory studies, although its efficacy in real-world settings remains uncertain. Furthermore, it is not effective for cavities that have progressed to the inner layers of the tooth. In such cases, professional dental treatment is necessary.

Coconut oil has been associated with enhancing oral health and aiding in the prevention of cavities. While it is not a complete solution for reversing cavities, some studies suggest that oil-pulling or swishing coconut oil in the mouth can have a positive impact on oral health by decreasing harmful bacteria and plaque buildup. The antimicrobial properties of coconut oil can help reduce bacteria in the mouth and potentially prevent the formation of new cavities when used consistently.

Baking soda is a commonly used at-home method to eliminate surface stains from teeth and prevent the formation of new stains and plaque. Its alkaline properties can also help balance the acidity in the mouth, which may assist in preventing cavities. However, due to its abrasive nature, excessive or improper use of baking soda could potentially damage teeth.

Dr. Gagandeep Sodhi (BDS), dental surgeon and certified implantologist, stated: 'This herbal mixture is not a recognised or validated treatment for dental caries. Consulting a dentist is essential for appropriate dental care and tooth decay prevention.'

The most reliable ways to address cavities and maintain good oral health are through dental care and professional guidance, including fluoride toothpaste, flossing daily, maintaining a balanced diet low in sugary and acidic foods, regular dental check-ups, dental sealants, and antibacterial mouthwash.

title: Fact Check: Can a herbal recipe replace root canal treatment?
claim_text: A social media post claims that a herbal recipe using Irimedadi oil, turmeric, rock salt, and crushed cloves can effectively replace root canal therapy (RCT) for managing discomfort induced by dental caries. The Hindi caption reads: "दांत में कीड़ा या RCT का डर? अब महंगे ट्रीटमेंट नहीं… ये घरेलू नुस्खा ही काफी है!" (Fear of tooth worms or RCT? Now no expensive treatment needed... this home remedy is enough!)
quick_take: An Instagram post claims that a herbal recipe can successfully replace root canal therapy. We analysed the claim and found it to be completely false.
doctor_explanation:
Root canal therapy (RCT) is a dental intervention used for managing infection or inflammation in the dental pulp, the tooth's innermost soft tissue containing blood vessels and nerves. RCT is recommended when the pulp is irreversibly damaged due to deep cavities, trauma, or severe gum disease. If timely intervention is not administered, pulpal infections can cause significant pain, bone loss, and abscess formation. The procedure involves removing inflammatory or infected pulp, meticulously cleaning and disinfecting the canals, then sealing the canal space with a biocompatible material to prevent reinfection. Root canal therapy is a tooth-saving treatment that reduces discomfort, removes infection, and restores dental function, avoiding the need for extraction.

Analysis of each claimed ingredient:

**Irimedadi Oil (Arimedadi taila)**: An Ayurvedic medicinal oil used for oral massage and oil-pulling. It contains Yashti, Trijatha, Manjishta, Gayatri, Lodhra, Katphala, and other ingredients. Its use has been assessed only as an adjunct to mechanical plaque control for early gingival inflammation management, NOT for dental caries. Dr. Sanjeev Kumar, BDS, MPH, Senior Consultant (Medical), NPCCHH (MoHFW), Centre for Community Medicine, AIIMS, New Delhi explains: "Oil pulling may help reduce bacteria and improve overall oral hygiene, but it does not address the underlying causes of toothaches, such as cavities, gum disease, or dental abscesses. These conditions need to be managed by a dentist. Relying only on oil pulling could worsen the issue and delay the necessary therapy."

**Turmeric (Haldi)**: While curcumin has demonstrated antimicrobial, analgesic, and anti-inflammatory effects against cariogenic bacteria in preclinical or experimental research, these benefits are confined to laboratory settings and have not been proven clinically effective for treating established cavities.

**Rock Salt (Sendha Namak)**: Warm saline rinses can help reduce oral bacterial counts and inflammation and aid in wound healing following dental procedures, but rock salt cannot restore necrotic dental tissue.

**Crushed Cloves**: Contains eugenol which has demonstrated antimicrobial efficacy against oral infections and offers quick, transient analgesic impact. However, this is only a temporary numbing effect and does not address the underlying infection or decay.

Dr. Shalini Aggarwal, Professor at the Department of Endodontics and Conservative Dentistry, Dr. DY Patil Dental College & Hospital in Pimpri, Pune, emphasises: "Tooth decay is an irreversible process. A cavity is an indication of the loss of enamel, the tooth's outermost layer, and a non-vital tissue that cannot be replaced. Definitely not by the aforementioned ingredients. Moreover, none of the previously stated components can rebuild the dentin or pulp, the essential tissues that reside beneath the enamel. Hence, neither of these ingredients can stop nor can they protect the tooth from further damage."

Tooth decay (dental caries) is a progressive bacterial invasion. Irreversible pulpal damage may occur if the carious lesion extends to the dental pulp. If left untreated, it could result in severe discomfort, abscess development, and even tooth loss. While accessibility issues, budgetary limitations, and fear may drive people to herbal oils and home remedies, these cannot penetrate the tooth's deeper layers or restore necrosed dental tissue. Relying only on such unregulated alternatives could aggravate the infection, enhance systemic complication risks, and delay essential professional care.

Dr. Gagandeep Singh Sodhi, a dental expert from Delhi, adds: "Most online shortcuts have no established scientific foundation. Dependence on do-it-yourself fixes may cause irreversible damage and delay a professional assessment. Every toothache condition needs to be evaluated by a qualified dentist."

Proper dental treatment involves identifying the underlying cause through clinical and radiographic assessment. When pulpitis is manageable, deteriorated tissue can be removed and replaced with restorative filling (GIC or composite resin). For necrotic or diseased pulp, root canal therapy is necessary - removing afflicted pulp, cleaning canals, and filling with biocompatible material. If carious lesions are not timely addressed, they could seriously damage teeth, necessitating extraction followed by prosthetic replacement.

**Conclusion**: Despite the aforementioned ingredients demonstrating anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and antimicrobial effects, they cannot eradicate cariogenic bacteria within a deep carious lesion or infected pulp. Cases progressed to irreversible pulpitis or pulpal necrosis necessitate root canal treatment. This timely removal of infected tissue can prevent abscess formation or systemic spread. Hence, this Irimedadi-based herbal formulation may be a useful adjunct but should NOT be a replacement for endodontic treatment for irreversible pulpal damage.
