title: Fact Check: Can a mist cure spinal and shoulder pain? - THIP Media
claim_text: A video on Facebook claims that a medicated neck topical mist named South Moon: Cervical Position Type Condensation Spray can cure cervical and lumbar spine pain and shoulder pain.
quick_take: A video on social media claims that a medicated neck topical mist can cure cervical and lumbar spine pain and shoulder pain as well. We fact-checked and found that claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: The treatment for spinal and shoulder pain depends upon the cause. A neck topical mist may soothe sprains, cramps, or muscle strains to reduce the intensity of the pain. We have not fact-checked the effectiveness of the South Moon: Cervical Position Type Condensation Spray. We have only fact-checked the marketing claims related to the product, especially their content. That said, the video falsely shows a damaged cervical spine recovering to good condition. A damaged spine cannot be reversed to its original condition. However, some research papers have shown that researchers are working on new treatments to improve spinal health after an injury. Besides this, we also ran a Google Reverse Image Search and found no evidence showing the professional experience of the people in the claimed video. Dr Kiran Kulkarni, FIFA- AFC Medical Officer, and Consultant in Sports & Exercise Medicine from Dharwad, Karnataka, says, "It's a counter irritant spray which may for a brief period of time reduce pain and discomfort, but the underlying pathology cannot be corrected in the long run." Additional medical context: Cervical pain (pain in the neck) occurs due to cervical spondylolysis or osteoarthritis, which change the bones, discs, or joints connected to the neck. The cervical spine contains the spinal cord to send messages from the brain to the body, so pain can reach the neck to affect the shoulders. Most cervical pains are due to wear and tear of cartilage and bones, common in aging people. Treatment depends on underlying cause: muscle strain or ligament sprain typically involves rest, ice, physical therapy, and over-the-counter pain medications. Doctors may also prescribe nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, corticosteroids, muscle relaxants, anti-seizure medications, and antidepressants. Lumbar pain (pain in the back) involves the lumbar spine consisting of five vertebrae in the lower back, which provides support to body weight, protects the spinal cord, and is responsible for body motions. Damage to the lumbar spine can negatively affect the spine causing lower back pain, arthritis, degenerative bone and disk disease, and stenosis. Lumbar spine pain is treated using over-the-counter pain relievers, anti-inflammatory drugs, muscle relaxants, injections, neuromodulatory agents, and prescription pain relievers. Additional treatments include cold packs, limiting exercise, improving lifestyle, physical therapy, acupuncture, and other alternative treatments. If these treatments do not work, doctors can prescribe surgery: laminectomy, discectomy and microdiscectomy, spinal fusion, foraminotomy, disc replacement surgery, laser surgery, radiofrequency lesioning, and spinal cord stimulation.

title: Fact Check: Can a Mix of Flaxseed Oil and Homemade Paneer Cure Cancer?
claim_text: If flaxseed oil, extracted through a cold process, is mixed with homemade paneer (from Indian cow, goat, or buffalo milk) and consumed morning, afternoon, and evening before meals, it can cure the patient from cancer.
verdict_original: The claim is FALSE. Hence, the claim is FALSE.
doctor_explanation:
Dr. Prashant Chandra - Associate Consultant Surgical Oncology, Aditya Birla Memorial Hospital said: "Flaxseed oil is rich in fiber, omega-3 fatty acids, and antioxidants. Thus, overall, it has good nutritional value. A fiber-rich diet is a known protector against colon cancer. Omega-3 fatty acids themselves prevent inflammation, a critical precancerous event, and antioxidants prevent the generation of free radicals, which are known to cause cancer. Similarly, paneer is high in calcium and vitamin D, both have known cancer-preventive action. In a few animal studies, flaxseed oil has shown the potential to prevent cancer genesis, but this is too early to draw conclusions. Until the benefit is demonstrated in large-scale cohort studies, it will be premature to infer. All the benefits are preventive in nature, and stating that flaxseed oil and paneer can cure cancer wouldn't be correct. Flaxseed oil and dairy products are a healthy part of the Indian diet. Theoretically, they may have cancer-preventive action, but would recommend them only if we see any benefit in human-based cohort studies. Also, I would also like to caution readers against animal fat in dairy products like paneer, as it itself is a risk factor for colon, breast, and prostate cancer if consumed in large amounts."

Dr. Siddhesh Tryambake, Associate Consultant Medical Oncology, Aditya Birla Memorial Hospital further said: "While some natural ingredients are often promoted as having cancer-curing potential, it's crucial to understand the difference between preventive nutrition and proven medical treatment. Natural foods like flaxseed and paneer are often highlighted in cancer-related conversations for their potential health benefits. However, it's important to separate nutritional value from therapeutic claims.

For postmenopausal women with breast cancer, a daily intake of 25g of ground flaxseed has been shown to reduce tumor proliferation and enhance apoptosis. Observational studies indicate around a 20% lower risk of breast cancer in postmenopausal women who consume higher amounts of lignans, such as a ¼ cup of flaxseed daily. However, for premenopausal women, the preventive effects remain less conclusive. While the findings are promising, they are yet to be confirmed through larger, universally accepted randomized trials.

In the case of paneer, a high intake of dairy, particularly whole milk and paneer, is biologically linked to increased IGF-1 and mTORC1 signaling, mechanisms associated with prostate cancer progression. Cohort data supports a modestly elevated risk, though this is not yet universally accepted. For other cancers such as breast and colorectal, observational studies and reviews suggest no direct harmful effect."

The article further clarifies: Cancer is a condition in which certain cells grow uncontrollably and can spread to other areas. While remission is possible, declaring cancer "cured" is rare due to recurrence risk. The American Cancer Society states that whether a cancer can be cured depends on the type, stage, treatment, and other factors — there is not one cure for cancer. The European Journal of Medical Research study (PMC10353157) notes flaxseed oil may help lower risk of cardiovascular disease, atherosclerosis, diabetes, cancer, arthritis, osteoporosis, and certain autoimmune and neurological disorders, but these are risk-reduction associations, not curative claims. There is no scientific evidence linking paneer to cancer prevention or cure. Cancer is a chronic disorder and cannot be cured by diet alone.

title: Fact Check: Can a mixture of clove, cinnamon, coconut oil Stop Tooth Pain and Bad Breath in 5 Minutes?
claim_text: If you are troubled by tooth decay and bad breath, then you must try this powerful home remedy. Simply take cloves and cinnamon, grind them into a powder, and mix one teaspoon of clove powder, one teaspoon of cinnamon powder, and one teaspoon of coconut oil in a bowl. Apply this mixture to your teeth, especially where there is pain, and massage gently with your finger. After just 5 minutes, rinse your mouth with water and feel the difference—no pain, no bad breath, and no tooth decay.
quick_take: While clove, cinnamon, and coconut oil have beneficial properties, including antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory effects, they cannot completely eliminate tooth pain, decay, or bad breath within 5 minutes. Tooth decay is irreversible and requires professional dental treatment, while pain and bad breath are best managed by addressing their underlying causes. Maintaining good oral hygiene and seeking professional care remain the most effective ways to ensure oral health.
doctor_explanation:
Dr. Prakhar Pragya, MDS, Orthodontics and Dentofacial Orthopaedics, Consultant Orthodontics at South Delhi Region, told Medical Dialogues: 'While clove, cinnamon, and coconut oil have natural benefits like reducing bacteria and soothing discomfort, they cannot magically eliminate tooth pain, decay, or bad breath in just 5 minutes. Tooth decay is permanent and needs professional dental care. Good oral hygiene, regular brushing, flossing, and dental check-ups, along with addressing underlying issues, are the real solutions for a healthy smile.' Dr. Ritika Punjabi, MDS, Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery (OMFS), Senior Lecturer, ITS Dental College, Muradnagar, added: 'Natural remedies like cloves, cinnamon, and coconut oil can offer temporary relief, but they are not a quick fix for tooth decay, pain, or bad breath. Tooth decay doesn't heal on its own, and bad breath often signals an underlying issue. The best way to keep your teeth healthy is to brush twice daily, floss, stay hydrated, and visit your dentist regularly. There's no shortcut to good oral health.'

Scientific evidence cited: The article reviews multiple studies showing that while these ingredients have individual benefits, none support the 5-minute elimination claim. A study in the International Journal of Dentistry found that clove oil-treated teeth exhibited reduced de-calcification and may support re-mineralization, but does not claim clove oil can eliminate tooth decay within 5 minutes. A review in the World Journal of Pharmaceutical Research states that chewing cloves can help reduce bad breath and tooth pain but only provides temporary relief and does not mention effectiveness within 5 minutes. A review in the journal Molecules highlights that cinnamon has antibacterial properties against oral pathogens linked to caries or tooth decay, helping in caries prevention and reducing bad breath, but does not state that cinnamon can cure or eliminate bad breath or tooth decay once formed, nor claims effectiveness within 5 minutes. A review in the AL-AZHAR Dental Journal mentions that ancient civilizations used cinnamon to treat tooth pain and combat bad breath, but this claim is anecdotal and lacks scientific experimental evidence. A systematic review published in Heliyon suggests that oil pulling with coconut oil may help improve oral hygiene, but does not state that coconut oil can eliminate tooth pain, tooth decay, or bad breath within 5 minutes.

Tooth decay (dental caries) is an irreversible bacterial disease that leads to breakdown of the tooth's mineral content and destruction of its organic structure (Shafer, 1993). It is caused by cariogenic bacteria like Streptococcus mutans, which produce acids that erode enamel. The four key factors in caries formation are bacterial plaque, fermentable sugars, tooth structure, and time. Tooth pain (odontogenic pain) originates from teeth or surrounding structures and can be caused by pulp inflammation from cavities, dental abscesses, bruxism, or sensitivity. Bad breath (halitosis) has multiple causes: approximately 80–85% of cases originate inside the mouth (gum infections, cavities, dry mouth, poorly fitted dentures); other causes include digestive problems, acid reflux (GERD), H. pylori infection (Kinberg et al., 2010 found over half of 94 halitosis patients had stomach-related issues), and habits like smoking and alcohol. The article concludes that studies acknowledge the role of clove, cinnamon, and coconut oil in reducing tooth decay, pain, and bad breath, but none confirm their ability—individually or combined—to completely eliminate these issues within 5 minutes.

title: Fact Check: Can a mixture of garlic and olive oil cure pain in ears?
claim_text: A mixture of garlic and olive oil cures pain in the ears. The remedy involves taking a clove of garlic, peeling and slicing it thinly, cooking the garlic slices in olive oil until golden brown, then pouring the mixture into a container. A small piece of cotton is soaked in the oil mixture and placed in the ear. This is claimed to cure ear pain, discharge from the ear, ear boils, and any other ear-related issues from the root.
quick_take: There is no scientific evidence supporting the claim that a mixture of garlic and olive oil can cure pain in the ears. Experts warn that blind application may worsen symptoms of infection, cause chemical burns, and lead to fungal infection, eardrum damage, and worsening of ear conditions.
doctor_explanation: Ear pain (otalgia) is categorized into primary otalgia (originating from within the ear — infections, mechanical problems, inflammation of the external, middle, or inner ear) and secondary or referred otalgia (caused by conditions outside the ear such as dental issues, temporomandibular joint disorders, pharyngeal problems, and even distant causes like cardiac, gastrointestinal, or pulmonary conditions). While garlic (Allium sativum L.) does contain organosulfur compounds with documented anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immunostimulant properties, and its active compound allicin exhibits antibacterial, antifungal, antiparasitic, and antiviral activities in vitro, these properties do not translate into a safe or effective ear treatment. Olive oil has demonstrated benefits in softening ear wax and facilitating wax removal, but there is no evidence it cures ear pain. A study in Turkish Archives of Otorhinolaryngology found that garlic compounds (allicin and S-allyl cysteine) exhibited certain antimicrobial activity against microorganisms linked to external ear canals and chronic middle ear infections in laboratory settings — but this is preliminary research with no clinical application as a home remedy. The National Library of Medicine notes that warm olive oil can help soften ear wax in the outer ear canal, and Rosemary Rodgers et al. found that lubricating the ear canal with olive oil facilitated wax extraction — both related to wax management only, not pain cure. Medical Dialogues spoke to two ENT specialists. Dr. Chanchal Pal, Senior Consultant ENT and Head & Neck Surgery at Indraprastha Apollo Hospital, said: 'I have never used it and never found anyone using in 35 years of practice, however, some people come after putting sarson oil heated with garlic for ear cleaning. Scientifically putting oil inside the ears is not advisable, Ears have a self-cleaning mechanism of their own and don't need any interference except in wax accumulation. For wax, we also have solvent drops available; on the other hand, if you put oil in the ears, there are high chances of fungal infection.' Dr. Sheetal Radia, Consultant Otorhinolaryngology and Head & Neck Oncosurgery at Wockhardt Hospitals, Mira Road, explained: 'Applying garlic or olive oil in the ear canal can lead to irritation, a burning sensation, and in some cases, tingling or numbness. This is especially concerning if the individual has an ear infection or a perforated eardrum, as the oil can seep into the middle ear, potentially spreading infection. The skin of the middle ear is particularly delicate, and exposure to these substances can cause swelling (edema). Additionally, the external ear canal is sensitive, and warm garlic or olive oil can result in chemical burns.' She further elaborated on harmful effects of garlic in the ear: 'Garlic is used due to its antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties but it can lead to potentially harmful effects.' The doctors concluded that oils in the ear are not recommended and consulting an ENT specialist is essential for proper diagnosis and safe treatment. Side effects documented include skin irritations, burns, infections, allergic reactions, blockage of the ear canal, damage to the eardrum, and worsening of ear conditions.

title: Fact Check: Can a mixture of lemon and baking soda kill Coronavirus? - THIP Media
claim_text: mix lemon and baking soda (soda bicarbonate) and drink it as hot tea every afternoon, the action of the lemon with hotter baking soda will immediately kill the virus; and the claim that this mixture has prevented any Covid related death in Israel

A few such posts also claimed that this mixture has prevented any Covid related death in Israel. We fact-checked and found that the claim is False.

Hence, any idea of changing the pH balance of the body through food and thereby killing a virus, bacteria, or any disease is unscientific". While multiple research is underway, so far, only the COVID-19 vaccines seem to be the only way of handling the pandemic. Lemon and Sodium bicarbonate is neither scientifically proven as a cure or approved by the World Health Organization (WHO) as a treatment to COVID-19.

title: Fact Check: Can a mixture of lemon and cream (malai) treat wrinkles? - THIP Media
claim_text: A Facebook post claims that wrinkles can be treated by applying a mixture of lemon and malai (milk cream), leaving it overnight, and washing it in the morning.
quick_take: A social media post claims that wrinkles can be treated by the application of a mixture of lemon and milk cream. We fact-checked and found this post to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: Wrinkles are creases, folds, or ridges in the skin which appear naturally as people get older. As a person ages, the skin becomes thinner and less elastic over time. However, certain other factors such as sun exposure, smoking, dehydration, some medications and environmental and genetic factors also play a vital role. Blemishes and wrinkles are signs of skin ageing. Both signs occur due to irreversible structural and biological changes in the layers of the skin. However, medical treatments under the guidance of experienced doctors can reduce the appearance of blemishes, wrinkles and other visible signs of ageing. Our Dermatology expert, Dr. Jyothy Kannangath, describes the etiology behind wrinkles by stating, "Wrinkles occur as people age or due to repeated muscle contractions. As we age, the skin cells divide more slowly, and the middle layer of your skin, the dermis, begins to thin. The dermis has a network of elastin and collagen fibres, which offer support and elasticity. As this network loosens and becomes weak, depressions form on your skin's surface. Aging skin is also less able to retain moisture, less efficient in secreting oil and slower to heal. All of these factors contribute to the development of wrinkles." There is no scientific evidence that the application of lemon with milk cream can eliminate wrinkles. On researching, we could not find any credible scientific evidence regarding this combination. However, some studies on individual ingredients of this mixture indicate anti-aging properties, but one needs further research to prove this. Research stated that the external use of lemon increases collagen production, which makes the skin smoother and tenser. Therefore, it is used in anti-aging products, to reduce shallow wrinkles, and as a synergistic antioxidant in combination with vitamin E. But, the amount used in skin products is medically evaluated by experts. However, the same is not practised while using it at home. Additionally, even though lemon is a good source of Vitamin C and is an antioxidant, using lemon directly on the skin is not recommended as it is highly acidic and can change the pH of your skin. It can lead to skin irritation, dryness, and sun damage, especially if you have sensitive skin. Dr. Sonali Kohli, Consultant Dermatologist, Sir HN Reliance Foundation Hospital, Mumbai, explains, "Lemon is a vibrant source of Vitamin C and has antioxidant and anti-bacterial flavonoid properties which are great for the skin. Vitamin C serums prepared for the face are of a particular formulation and other additions that help balance the pH. Lemon juice is highly acidic, and the Vitamin C serums we use are not citric acid but the ascorbic acid version of the lemon juice, which is beneficial for the skin and is stabilized. When a person applies lemon directly to the face, you disturb the skin's pH and make it completely acidic. In such cases, sun exposure can lead to Phytophotodermatitis (a skin reaction). Hence, it must be avoided." Also, even though an external application is not advised, there are studies which indicate that the consumption of citrus-based juice can prevent oxidative stress-induced premature skin ageing. Additionally, milk products have high biological potential, and due to their natural origin and non-toxicity, they have many uses in cosmetics and dermatology. Milk is considered to improve the skin's condition through various means, including antiaging effects. Furthermore, the amino acids also have positive effects on the skin, such as proline has antiaging properties, which reduce wrinkles and sagging. However, even though milk is believed to have antiaging properties, there needs to be further research to see if milk cream or malai can treat wrinkles. In conclusion, many factors affect the elasticity of the skin, such as sun exposure and diet. Getting wrinkles and age lines is a natural process and reversing them or eliminating them through an external application is not possible.

title: Fact Check: Can a mixture of Lemon and Milk cure Piles? - THIP Media
claim_text: Lemon and milk can cure piles completely - claimed as a 'sure shot' cure for piles
verdict_original: Mostly False (also stated as 'Partly False' in conclusion)
quick_take: An article on a website claims that mixing cow milk with lemon juice will cure piles completely. We fact-checked and found the claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation:
Haemorrhoids (commonly called piles) are recognized by swollen veins in the anus and rectum, causing inflammation/swelling, anal itching, anal pain, lumps near the anus, bleeding from the rectum, or hemorrhoid falling through the anal opening. Piles occurs due to increased pressure in the lower rectum that stretches blood vessels, caused by chronic constipation, lifting heavy weights, chronic diarrhoea, or straining while passing stool. Risk factors include pregnancy, age, weight, and diet.

Dr Sharad Malhotra, Gastroenterologist, explained: 'Diet may not cure piles but can help in symptom improvement. Helpful diets should include whole grains, legumes, fruits with peel and fibre in any form to avoid constipation. Food rich in processed fats and carbohydrates should be avoided because they decrease the intestinal motility and aggravate constipation.'

Dr Malhotra further stated that 'treatment for piles include fiber-rich diet, incorporating laxatives or stools softener, avoiding other medications or food causing constipation, medicines for decreasing pressure in veins of the anal canal, endoscopy guided injection therapy or banding and surgery to remove diseased venous column.'

Dietician Kamna Tank stated: 'Diet cannot cure the pile disease but it can reduce the symptoms. Eating food that are high in fiber can make stool softer and easier to pass. This can make piles less painful. Drinking water and other liquids can help the fiber in your diet works better.'

There is no evidence that lemon and milk can cure piles. In fact, milk is often on the 'not to have' list for piles due to its tendency to cause constipation. While some proportion of lemon and milk results in buttermilk (a popular Indian summer drink) suggested as a home remedy for piles, there is no scientific evidence to support this.

Regarding lemons individually: some evidence shows lemon juice can strengthen capillaries and blood vessels, potentially reducing piles disease. Another research paper recommended topical application of lemon on piles.

Regarding milk: available evidence recommends avoiding it because milk does not have fibre and can cause constipation, aggravating the condition. Trying to treat piles with home remedies without understanding the underlying cause can leave piles untreated, potentially causing anaemia and gangrene (death of tissues).

title: Fact Check: Can a mixture of mango seed, neem, cinnamon, and nutmeg make teeth as white as pearls?
claim_text: A mixture of mango seed powder (the kernel of the mango), neem powder, cinnamon powder, and nutmeg powder can make teeth as white as pearls when used daily as a paste after brushing.
verdict_original: The claim is MISLEADING. Hence, the claim that a mixture of mango, neem, cinnamon, and nutmeg can make teeth as white as pearls is misleading.
quick_take: While mango seed, neem, cinnamon, and nutmeg possess antioxidant, antibacterial, and oral health benefits (e.g., mango extract reduces Streptococcus mutans, neem reduces plaque), there is no scientific evidence that a mixture of these ingredients can whiten teeth to the degree of making them as white as pearls. Cinnamon extract may even cause discolouration of tooth enamel.
doctor_explanation:
Dr. Prinita Tirkey, Periodontist at Rajmata Smt. Devendra Kumari Singh Deo Govt. Medical College and Hospital, Ambikapur, Surguja, Chhattisgarh, stated: "In dental clinics, we frequently encounter individuals curious about natural remedies for teeth whitening. While the mixture of mango seed powder, neem, cinnamon, and nutmeg does have some benefits for oral health—including neem's ability to fight bacteria, there's no solid scientific evidence that they can make your teeth as white as pearls. Whitening your teeth involves breaking down stains that are deep in the enamel, which typically requires professional treatments. Natural remedies like this mixture may help with general oral health, but they simply don't have the power to significantly whiten teeth. If you're looking for noticeable and safe results, it's always a good idea to consult a dentist about your options."

Dr Meenakshi Sahu, Senior Associate Dentist at Vyas Dental Inn, added: "While I have heard of many natural remedies around teeth cleaning but I have not come across any evidence supporting the idea that ingredients like mango seed, neem, cinnamon, or nutmeg can effectively whiten discoloured teeth. In fact, research has shown that cinnamon extract solutions may lead to unwanted colour changes in tooth enamel, causing the teeth to appear more discoloured rather than whiter. To remove extrinsic stains, such as those from coffee or tea, and to achieve noticeable whitening results, professional dental treatments are the most effective approach."

The article further explains that tooth stains consist of chromogens accumulated either within the tooth (intrinsic) or on the tooth surface (extrinsic). Intrinsic staining can be caused by genetics, ageing, certain antibiotics, excessive fluoride, and developmental issues. Extrinsic staining is caused by smoking, pigments in foods and drinks (wine, coffee, tea), antibiotics, and metals. Teeth whitening requires either physically removing surface stains or a chemical process that lightens the tooth's colour, typically using ultrasonic scalers or professional treatments under dentist supervision.

Scientific evidence cited: A study in Nutrition and Metabolic Insights found mango extract prevents dental caries by reducing Streptococcus mutans count and increasing salivary pH, but no evidence it whitens teeth. A study in Pharmacognosy Review confirmed neem-containing toothpaste reduces plaque, prevents caries, and enhances oral immunity, but no role in teeth whitening. A study by J. Anggono et al showed cinnamon extract antibacterial compounds may benefit oral health but cause clinically unacceptable colour changes to tooth enamel. A review in the International Journal of Chemical and Biochemical Sciences noted nutmeg containing eugenol has been used in dentistry to relieve toothache, but no evidence for teeth whitening.

title: Fact Check: Can a mixture of mustard oil, turmeric and rock salt cure toothache?
claim_text: A mixture of mustard oil, turmeric and rock salt cures toothache. The Instagram post by user dr.nitasha_gupta further states: 'If you experience tooth pain and swollen gums, to quickly relieve them, you need to take a little mustard oil, add a bit of turmeric to it and some rock salt. Mix them well, and with the help of your finger, apply them properly on your teeth and gums. Afterwards, spit out the saliva that comes out. You will see that the yellowing of your teeth has gone, your tooth pain has disappeared, and your gums have returned to normal.'
verdict_original: The claim is MOSTLY FALSE. Mustard oil, turmeric and rock salt may reduce plaque accumulation, help prevent oral disease, and provide relief to mild gingival inflammation but these natural ingredients cannot cure toothache.
quick_take: While mustard oil, turmeric, and rock salt may help manage mild gum inflammation and plaque, there is no scientific evidence that their mixture can cure toothache. Professional dental treatment is necessary for underlying causes such as cavities, infections, or gum disease.
doctor_explanation:
Toothache, also known as Odontogenic pain, refers to pain initiating from the teeth or their supporting structures, including the mucosa, gingivae, maxilla, mandible, or periodontal membrane. Toothache is often triggered by inflammation of the dental pulp, commonly due to dental caries (tooth decay). It can also result from dentine sensitivity to cold, sweet, or physical stimuli; apical periodontitis; dental abscesses; iatrogenic pain following dental procedures; or bruxism (teeth grinding). In primary care, managing toothache is based on its cause, symptoms, and severity. Treatment for odontogenic pain focuses on symptom relief, with analgesics like paracetamol and NSAIDs being the preferred options. Antibiotics are recommended only when there are signs of local or systemic spread of a dental infection. For cases involving an infected root canal system, referral for root canal therapy or tooth extraction is necessary.

Mustard oil contains MUFA and PUFA and has antibacterial/antifungal properties. Turmeric (Curcuma longa L.) exhibits anti-inflammatory activity, strong antimicrobial properties, and anticancer activities, and is used in Ayurvedic medicine for various conditions. Rock salt (halite) consists of 95-98% sodium chloride along with polyhalite minerals, fluoride, and iodine.

While a review article published in Evidence-based Complementary and Alternative Medicine suggests that gingivitis and periodontitis may be managed with a paste consisting of 1 teaspoon turmeric, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon mustard oil applied to teeth and gums twice daily — and turmeric mouthwash aids in plaque control — there is no evidence or consensus amongst dentists that a concoction of mustard oil, turmeric, and rock salt can cure toothache. A study led by V Aravinth et al. found salt water rinse can improve plaque control alongside regular brushing and flossing. A study published in PloS One found that salt solution as a mouth rinse in conjunction with routine oral care may help promote oral wound healing. However, these benefits are limited to plaque control and mild gum management.

Dr Ritu Thawait, Dental Surgeon, Medical Officer, CHC, Risali, Durg, C.G., said: 'While turmeric and mustard oil may have anti-inflammatory properties and soothe the gums to a certain extent but this mixture doesn't address the root cause of the tooth pain. Toothaches often stem from issues like cavities, infections, or gum disease, which need professional treatment. Relying on home remedies like this could delay the care you need and make the situation worse. While this remedy might offer brief comfort, it's important to see a dentist for a proper diagnosis and treatment to prevent more serious dental problems down the line. So, don't wait on tooth pain — seek professional care.'

Dr. Twinkale Parekh, Orthodontist, Sanjeevani Multispeciality Clinic, Kanika New Colony, Cuttak, added: 'As we all love a good home remedy, and salt, mustard oil with turmeric sounds like a natural way to manage mild oral inflammation. But while it might provide some temporary relief, it's really important to understand that these remedies don't solve deeper issues like gum disease or cavities. They may offer temporary relief for minor gum discomfort, but they won't cure the root causes of toothache like tooth caries or infection. Seeing your dentist is the best way to prevent bigger problems.'

doctor_explanation: Human skin comes in many different tones and colors. The main factor determining skin color is our genes. Inside our bodies, there's an enzyme called tyrosinase that plays a big role in controlling our skin color. Another important factor is melanin, which decides how light or dark our skin is. Melanin is made by special cells in our skin called melanocytes. The genes we inherit control how much and what kind of melanin we have, which then determines our skin color. Some other processes like facultative melanogenesis and tanning reactions also add to this genetic mechanism. There's something called Vitamin D, which is similar to melanin, and it helps with the growth and differentiation of cells in different parts of our body, including the skin. This could also have an effect on our skin color. Dr. Sonali Kohli, a Consultant Dermatologist at Sir HN Reliance Foundation Hospital explains, "Lemon truly stands out as a vibrant Vitamin C powerhouse, packed with beneficial antioxidant and anti-bacterial flavonoids that nourish the skin. Nonetheless, the citric acid found in lemon juice has the potential to upset the skin's natural pH balance, leading to excessive acidity. On the other hand, Vitamin C serums designed for skincare often incorporate a stabilized form of ascorbic acid derived from lemon juice, ensuring it remains gentle and friendly to the skin." "Applying lemon juice directly to the face can change the skin's pH, making it more vulnerable to potential skin reactions when exposed to sunlight. This could result in a condition called Phytophotodermatitis. To protect your skin's health, it is advisable to refrain from using lemon directly on the skin. Instead, consider using Vitamin C serums designed to be gentle on the skin, providing the desired benefits without any harmful effects," Dr Kohli cautions. Furthermore, toothpaste has the potential to trigger allergic contact dermatitis, highlighting its unsuitability for use on the skin. By following these practices, one can achieve a natural radiance that cannot be replicated by any artificial whitening product. Dr. Agarkar also highlights the importance of selecting skincare products tailored to individual skin types, as this ensures optimal results and care for the skin.

The harsh and active ingredients in toothpaste can harm your sensitive and delicate facial skin. Instead of this hack, try exfoliating your skin with an exfoliator for better results. title: Fact Check: Can a mobile phone near your pillow cause death?
claim_text: An Instagram post alleges that sleeping with a mobile phone near your pillow can be fatal. The post suggests this happens gradually because smartphones emit dangerous levels of radiation, which enter the body through the nose and wreak havoc on the brain.
quick_take: A social media post claims keeping a mobile phone near your pillow can cause death due to harmful radiation affecting the brain. We have investigated this claim and can confirm it's false.
doctor_explanation: Mobile phones emit non-ionising radiation, which is low-energy and doesn't have enough power to damage DNA or cells directly. Non-ionising radiation, including radiofrequency (RF) waves (used in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth), is like a gentle breeze, while ionising radiation (like X-rays) is a powerful storm. Non-ionising radiation doesn't cause the kind of immediate or cumulative damage that could lead to death. Dr Almas Fatma, MBBS, Diploma in Family Medicine, PG in Digital Health, General Physician from Navi Mumbai, says, 'There is no scientific evidence to support the claim that radiation from mobile phones can cause death. Mobile phones emit low levels of non-ionising radiation, which is not strong enough to damage DNA or directly harm the brain. While excessive phone use may contribute to sleep disturbances or stress, it does not pose a fatal risk when kept near your pillow.' Regarding brain health, Dr Sreenivas Meenakshisundaram, Consultant Neurologist at MGM Healthcare, Chennai, clarifies, 'People often worry about mobile phone radiation, but there's no scientific proof that it harms the brain. The radiation from phones is very weak and doesn't have the power to cause damage to brain cells. It's not like the strong radiation used in medical scans or X-rays. In fact, large studies over the years haven't found any clear link between phone use and brain disorders. So, while it's good to take breaks from screens for your overall well-being, there's no need to fear brain damage from your phone. However, keeping the phone near your bed can be more harmful for your sleep. The light from the screen can interfere with your natural circadian rhythm, leading to poor-quality sleep.' Dr Kunal Bahrani, Director and HOD of Neurology at Marengo Asia Hospitals, Faridabad, adds, 'Mobile phone radiation isn't something to be afraid of when it comes to brain health. Phones emit low-level radiation that doesn't even come close to the type that can harm human tissue. It's more like the energy from a Wi-Fi router or a microwave—not dangerous in everyday use. The brain is well-protected, and current research shows no link between mobile phone use and brain diseases. The real concern with phones is distraction, not radiation.' Addressing the claim that radiation can enter through the nose, Dr Pooja Khullar, Radiation Oncologist at Dharamshila Narayana Super Speciality Hospital, explains, 'Cell phones emit low-energy radiation called radiofrequency, which is too weak to harm our DNA. Older phones (2G, 3G, 4G) use frequencies between 0.7–2.7 GHz, while 5G phones may use up to 80 GHz. This radiation is much weaker than harmful types like X-rays, which can damage DNA and increase cancer risk. However, research so far shows no link between cell phone use and cancer.' The WHO and IARC haven't found conclusive evidence linking mobile phone radiation to brain damage. The human skull also acts as a natural barrier, reducing exposure levels to brain tissues. Radiation from mobile phones spreads in all directions and is not concentrated enough to specifically target or penetrate through the nose. The real risk of sleeping with a phone near a pillow is overheating, particularly if it's charging under a pillow, which can in rare cases cause fires.

title: Can a moong dal-based ayurvedic recipe cure diabetes?
claim_text: An Ayurvedic preparation made from sprouted moong dal in a copper vessel, consumed with jamun seeds and neem leaf powders, is a potent therapy that can cure persistent diabetes (10 साल पुरानी शुगर भी हो जाएगी कंट्रोल में)
quick_take: According to an Instagram reel, a moong dal-based ayurvedic recipe is an effective remedy for persistent diabetes. We fact-checked the assertion and found that it is false.
doctor_explanation:
Dr. P Rammanohar, Research Director of the Amrita School of Ayurveda, explains that Diabetes is recognised in Ayurvedic texts as 'Madhumeha', a form of Prameha linked to the tridosha imbalance. Traditional science classifies the illness into different stages based on its progression. Early stages of the disease, known as Kapha Prameha, can be managed and even reversed with supportive therapy and lifestyle modifications. However, once diabetes reaches Pitta Prameha, it cannot be cured and requires lifelong care. When the condition advances to its most severe stage, Vata Prameha becomes particularly difficult to manage. Despite ongoing research into potential remedies for diabetes, no single herb or ingredient has been proven to effectively treat the condition. While Ayurveda supports diabetes management, it does not assert a cure for the disease that complies with contemporary biomedical criteria.

On sprouted moong dal: Sprouted moong dal is a nutrient-dense legume that may help inhibit the absorption of glucose and regulate glucose levels. Soaking it in a copper vessel may further enhance its antioxidant properties, as copper ions may work in conjunction with the sprouted plant-based legume. However, there is no definitive scientific evidence that the combination supports the management of insulin-dependent type 1 or type 2 diabetes that necessitates comprehensive care. Overdependence on such unverified practices can delay essential treatment, potentially leading to severe complications.

On jamun seeds and neem: Jamun seed powder contains a bioactive compound called 'jamboline,' which may slow down the conversion of carbohydrates to glucose. Neem leaf powder is also well-known for its ability to regulate blood sugar levels and enhance insulin sensitivity, albeit its exact function in hyperglycemia is still unknown. Sports nutritionist Manasi Banduni acknowledges that while jamun seeds and leaves might complement the management of diabetes, relying solely on them for an extended period of time could be risky. Dr. Shraddha Sanghani, Consultant Internal Medicine at Renova Century Hospitals in Banjara Hills, Hyderabad, advises that neem has long been used in traditional medicine due to its blood-purifying, anti-inflammatory, and antibacterial properties. Although neem leaves are effective as a supplement for some chronic disorders, such as diabetes, due to their insulin-sensitising properties, they cannot be used for addressing the medical condition. Dr. Sanghani further warns that unregulated daily consumption of neem leaves could be more detrimental than helpful. It may cause liver damage, gastrointestinal irritation, hormonal imbalances, or even miscarriage during pregnancy. Neem should never be used in place of evidence-based conventional medical care; instead, it should be used carefully and under a doctor's supervision. There is no tangible evidence that powdered jamun seeds and neem leaves could cure diabetes of any kind.

Dr. Ashirwad Pawar, Mumbai-based general practitioner and diabetologist, advises that effective diabetes control requires a lifetime commitment to good habits, consistent exercise, appropriate medical care, and periodic blood sugar evaluations. Reliance on unverified solutions could lead to severe health-related issues by delaying the required medical intervention.

Diabetes is a persistent metabolic illness that necessitates timely, evidence-based intervention. Implementing unregulated natural solutions or social media recommendations might delay the healing of wounds and increase the risk of life-threatening complications such as irreversible organ damage. Unregulated social media treatments may include pharmacologically active ingredients, such as steroids or even allopathic medications, in dangerously high concentrations that could be harmful. Furthermore, bypassing long-term prescribed medications, such as insulin therapy, may result in dysregulation of blood glucose levels.

title: Fact Check: Can a morning walk cure depression? - THIP Media
claim_text: A morning walk can cure depression (without relying on medicines). One post claims morning sunlight can cure depression by 100%. Another post claims morning walk can be a better option than medicines. Additionally, claims suggest morning walks may cure long COVID-19 infections.
quick_take: Several social media posts claim that a morning walk can cure depression. We fact-checked and found the claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: Depression is a mental health disorder characterized by persistent feelings of sadness, loss of interest in activities, and disruptions in sleep and appetite. It significantly impacts thoughts, emotions, and daily functioning, sometimes leading to severe consequences such as self-harm or suicidal thoughts. Key common signs of depression include persistent low mood, decreased interest or pleasure, changes in sleep and appetite, fatigue, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, difficulty concentrating, and, in severe cases, thoughts of death or suicide. Depression is a complex mental health condition, and its treatment can vary from person to person. While there may not be a definitive cure for depression in the sense of permanently eliminating the possibility of experiencing depressive symptoms, many individuals can successfully manage and alleviate their symptoms with appropriate treatment. Common approaches to treating depression include: Psychotherapy (Counseling): Various forms of psychotherapy, such as cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), dialectical behavior therapy (DBT), and interpersonal therapy (IPT), are effective in treating depression. Medication: Antidepressant medications can be prescribed by healthcare professionals to help regulate neurotransmitters in the brain and alleviate depressive symptoms. Lifestyle Changes: Adopting a healthy lifestyle can have a positive impact on mood, including regular exercise, a balanced diet, sufficient sleep, and stress management. Supportive Relationships: Building and maintaining strong social connections can provide emotional support. Mind-Body Practices: Practices like mindfulness meditation and yoga have shown promise in reducing depressive symptoms. CAN A MORNING WALK CURE DEPRESSION? No, it is not true that going for a walk or run in the morning is a guaranteed cure for depression. While walking can be helpful, it may not be sufficient for everyone experiencing depression. Professional treatment is necessary for full recovery. Research shows that depression has various causes, and its treatment typically involves a combination of approaches. Physical activity, like walking or running, can be beneficial for managing depression symptoms, but it is not a standalone cure. Exercise, including running or walking, can be a helpful component of a holistic approach to managing depression. Regular physical activity has been shown to release endorphins, which can improve mood and reduce symptoms of depression. Moreover, morning sunlight can boost energy by regulating the sleep-wake cycle to improve sleep quality and reduce stress or anxiety. Walking can induce mindfulness to promote relaxation. Daily walks, even short ones, can boost self-esteem, fostering a sense of accomplishment and improved self-worth. However, the effectiveness of exercise can vary from person to person, and it is not a guaranteed cure. It is essential for individuals experiencing depression to seek guidance and support from mental health professionals who can help determine the most appropriate and effective treatment plan for their specific circumstances. Dr Rahul Bansal, Consultant psychiatrist in an interview with THIP adds, 'Any delay in treatment will worsen the health'. Dr Madhu Vamsi, Psychiatrist practicing in Hyderabad informs, 'I often recommend morning walks as an adjunctive strategy for individuals dealing with depression, considering its multifaceted impact on both physical and mental health. They boost endorphins and regulate sleep. Regular walking improves mood, cognitive function, and hippocampal volume. Social walks enhance therapeutic benefits, and outdoor walks reduce stress, promoting mental well-being. As a psychiatrist, I advocate for incorporating morning walks for a holistic approach to depression'. The idea that exercise alone can cure depression is an oversimplification of a complex condition, and it is essential to approach depression treatment with a comprehensive and individualized approach.

title: Can a mulethi and honey face mask banish skin pigmentation?
claim_text: You're about to get crystal clear skin! Start your day with mulethi (liquorice) powder. Take a small amount of honey, add mulethi powder to it, mix it with your hands, and apply it to your face. Then massage your face for 3 to 4 minutes every day. Honey and mulethi will remove pigmentation, uneven skin tone, and tanning, clean your pores, and your skin will start to glow.
quick_take: A social media post claims that a mulethi and honey face mask can banish skin pigmentation. We fact checked this claim and found it to be mostly false.
doctor_explanation:
Mulethi root extract contains compounds like glabridin, which has shown some promise in inhibiting tyrosinase, an enzyme involved in melanin production. This could potentially lead to a lightening effect on hyperpigmentation over time. Honey possesses antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties that might contribute to a healthier skin tone. However, the claim of complete removal of pigmentation is likely exaggerated. Significant pigmentation issues often require more potent treatments and addressing the underlying cause. Also, what works for one person may not work for another, as skin responses vary widely.

As Dr Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant in Lucknow, explains, "Mulethi and honey are commonly used in skincare for their potential to reduce pigmentation. Mulethi contains glabridin, a compound known for its skin-brightening effects, while honey works as a natural humectant, drawing moisture into the skin and promoting hydration. These ingredients can help with dark spots and uneven skin tone over time, but it's important to note that results are gradual. Pigmentation can be influenced by various factors, such as sun exposure and genetics, so it's essential to manage expectations and be consistent with the application. For persistent pigmentation, it's always best to consult a dermatologist for a tailored treatment plan."

Regarding skin tone and tanning: The potential tyrosinase-inhibiting effects of mulethi may help promote a more even skin tone by reducing melanin production. Honey's moisturising and antioxidant properties could also enhance the skin's appearance, possibly reducing mild tanning. However, for significant sun damage or unevenness, this simple mask is unlikely to deliver dramatic results. Consistent sun protection and targeted treatments are usually needed for effective tan reduction and evening out skin tone.

Regarding pore cleaning: Honey has some antibacterial and humectant properties that could help to cleanse the skin's surface and keep it moisturised. Mulethi powder, if finely ground, might offer a gentle exfoliating effect, potentially helping to unclog pores. However, this mixture is unlikely to deeply clean the pores. It may not work well for problems like blackheads and whiteheads. These usually need stronger products made for such issues. Ingredients like salicylic acid or benzoyl peroxide are often more effective for all skin types.

Regarding skin glow: Both mulethi and honey may contribute to a healthier and more radiant complexion in some. Mulethi's potential to reduce hyperpigmentation and even skin tone can lead to a brighter appearance. Honey's moisturizing and antioxidant properties can hydrate the skin, giving it a natural glow. Consistent application and gentle massage, as suggested, can also improve blood circulation, contributing to a healthy radiance. However, the extent of the glow will vary depending on individual skin type and existing skin condition. Skin health is also influenced by factors like diet, lifestyle, environment, social habits (like smoking or drinking), genetics and emotional wellbeing, so a holistic approach is essential for lasting results.

Dr Rashi Soni, Co-founder and Consulting Dermatologist, Aesthetician, and Hair Transplant Surgeon at Rashi Hospital in Mumbai, explained, "Achieving glowing skin goes beyond just using mulethi and honey. While mulethi can brighten the complexion and honey can hydrate the skin, glowing skin requires a holistic approach. A consistent skincare routine that includes proper cleansing, exfoliation, and moisturisation is essential. Don't forget the importance of daily sun protection; SPF is key to preventing damage and maintaining skin health. Along with a good skincare regimen, lifestyle factors such as a balanced diet, hydration, and enough sleep play a huge role in skin radiance. Mulethi and honey can certainly support skin health, but glowing skin is the result of overall care and patience."

THIP Media Take: The claim that a mulethi and honey face mask can banish skin pigmentation is mostly false. Even though mulethi and honey possess properties that may offer some benefits for skin tone, mild tanning, and overall skin health, the Instagram post's claim that this mixture will remove skin pigmentation and deliver "crystal clear skin" is a significant overstatement. Effective treatment for pigmentation often requires targeted ingredients and professional advice. This DIY mask might offer mild improvements, but it is unlikely to be a complete solution for significant skin concerns in everyone.

title: Can a multani-mitti-based recipe whiten skin in just a week?
claim_text: An Instagram post claims that an at-home recipe composed of multani mitti, curd, lemon juice, turmeric, alum, and gram flour may make the skin fairer in just one week.
quick_take: According to an Instagram post, a multani-mitti-based recipe may whiten skin in just one week. After fact-checking, we found that it is completely false.
doctor_explanation: Skin colour is the visible shade, or hue, of the skin. This is usually determined by the type and concentration of melanin synthesised. The amount of melanocytes, carotene, oxygenated haemoglobin, and regional blood circulation all influence skin pigmentation, which varies greatly from person to person. Skin's primary pigment, melanin, exists in two forms. An individual's baseline or constitutive skin colour is mostly determined by their genetic composition; more than 150 genes have been found to affect skin pigmentation. Genes such as MC1R, SLC24A5, and TYR regulate melanin concentration and dispersion, preserving the equilibrium of the pigments. External variables may also profoundly impact the appearance of skin by altering the quantity of melanin that is synthesised. Of all external influences, sunlight's UV rays usually have the biggest impact on changing skin tone. Skin pigmentation may also be influenced by age-related or pregnancy-related hormones. This could end up in melasma or age spots. Furthermore, many medications and chemicals may result in pigmentation by preventing melanocyte activation. Therefore, the origin of human skin pigmentation is multifaceted and contributes to the range of skin tones. For centuries, people have relied on home remedies for skin care and facial radiance, but such approaches might not be able to address the primary driver that determines skin tone. Given that ingredients such as alum, gram flour, turmeric, curd, lemon juice, and Multani mitti (or Fuller's earth) are being considered for the facial skin, they should be thoroughly analysed. We begin with Multani mitti, which may absorb excess oil and contaminants. Next on the list is turmeric, which is known for its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. Then comes lemon juice, a popular home remedy for skin care due to its moderate exfoliating properties from citric acid. We now have alum, which is employed because of its astringent properties. Finally, curd and gram flour are considered since they help moisturise the skin and improve its texture. Despite the preparation possibly aiding in skin clarity and encouraging a more radiant complexion, it has no effect on the basic production of melanin, which determines skin colour. Furthermore, using certain ingredients excessively—such as lemon juice, especially when it's undiluted—can do more harm than good. Likewise, applying turmeric and alum every day may damage the skin's protective layer. Dr Sachin Gupta, MBBS, MD (Dermatology and Venereology from AIIMS Delhi), of Amrita Hospital, cautions that "natural ingredients are not always synonymous with safety or efficacy, and what might seem harmless can actually be risky" in the field of dermatology. Seeing a dermatologist is the safest and most effective way to address skin issues. It's critical to acknowledge that unproven organic skin whitening solutions are not scientifically validated. Skin specialists strongly advise against such uncontrolled skin-lightening attempts because skin tone or pigmentation is primarily genetically determined. It is neither safe nor scientifically verified to depend on online promises that skin can be whitened in just a week. As previously mentioned, skin colour is primarily determined by melanin production and genetics, and it can't be modified in a short period of time, such as a week. Furthermore, unregulated procedures that ensure quick skin whitening sometimes use harsh chemical additives or astringent or acidic ingredients like lemon juice, which can harm the skin's protective layer and trigger irritation, allergic responses, and even long-term pigmentation disorders. Apart from augmenting photosensitivity, excessive application of these ingredients could raise susceptibility to UV-induced harm and perhaps expedite the onset of premature ageing. Dr. Annusuiya Gohil, MD Scholar at the All India Institute of Ayurveda, adds additional credence to this by asserting that, after heredity, environmental factors are the second most important factor influencing skin fairness. Skin pigmentation cannot be altered; it can only be improved, despite the fact that there are numerous approaches to making the skin appear more radiant. More precisely, the natural skin tone that could have been diminished over time as a result of ageing, exposure to harsh environments, and additional factors, including nutrition and medicine, can be restored. Topical treatments cannot change the colour of the skin. Therefore, unsubstantiated claims making the promise of a one-week skin colour transformation disregard its natural physiology, can result in unrealistic expectations and may cause potential harm.

title: Can a Multani-mitti-based recipe whiten teeth in three days?
claim_text: A Facebook post captioned "Teeth will shine with this mix" advertises the use of multani mitti, lemon juice, salt, and garlic to whiten teeth in just three days.
quick_take: A social media post claims that a Multani-mitti-based remedy could potentially whiten teeth in just three days. We fact-checked the notion and found it to be false.
doctor_explanation: Teeth whitening is a well-liked, non-invasive cosmetic dentistry procedure that can either brighten or remove stains from teeth. This could be accomplished by either chemical oxidation reactions that break down the organic compounds causing tooth discolouration, or physical removal of surface stains. When compounds develop externally coloured on the enamel surface, teeth whitening becomes necessary. It is also crucial to highlight that individuals who suffer from gingivitis or halitosis are often at a higher risk of developing such stains, as these conditions are associated with plaque accumulation and enhanced microbial activity in the mouth, primary contributors to tooth discolouration. Do garlic, salt, lemon juice, and multani mitti whiten teeth? No, absolutely not. Even while individuals who are more likely to have gum conditions, teeth stains, or foul breath frequently search for quick, less expensive, and safer at-home solutions, their relevance is limited to social media platforms. Because the mixture is being suggested for use in the oral cavity, it is crucial to examine each component. Garlic: While the strong-tasting, aromatic bulb has been extensively researched in dentistry for its antibacterial chemicals and its ability to reduce the microbial load in contaminated root canals, these characteristics do not result in enamel whitening. Lemon Juice: The popular culinary ingredient may help temporarily brighten teeth and perhaps remove surface stains because of its high concentration of citric acid. However, regular use might alter the surface properties of the enamel, make it rougher, and ultimately cause tooth structure loss instead of enamel whitening. Salt: Although it may work as a moderate abrasive, it is not a viable tooth whitener. Multani Mitti: Also known as Fuller's Earth, this is a popular skincare product; however, it has no established use in enamel bleaching or dental hygiene. It may even harm enamel if used on a daily basis. It is vital to emphasise that teeth whitening works by either gently removing surface stains with regulated abrasives or by using scientifically formulated bleaching agents to break down stain-inducing chemicals within the enamel. Agents like hydroxyapatite and hydrogen peroxide, which have undergone extensive clinical testing for their capacity to safely lighten tooth colour, are essential to effective enamel whitening therapies. Can teeth be whitened in three days? Is it safe to depend on such claims? No, not at all. Even though peroxide-based professional clinical teeth whitening can result in noticeable improvement in a matter of days, the procedure is usually closely monitored and controlled to avoid any harm to the dental tissues. Quick or unsupervised attempts at teeth whitening, particularly with unproven home cures or strong, aggressive chemicals, can cause gum irritation and tooth sensitivity along with contributing to increasing the risk of enamel erosion. Dr Ketan Rajput, an oral implantologist and periodontist from Dhule, Maharashtra, provides support by pointing out that no natural substance can whiten teeth in three days. Surface stains may be removed by several at-home remedies, but their efficacy necessitates regular use and careful observation. Moreover, they are not intended to replace expert dental care. For optimal therapeutic results, always consult a specialist. This is further backed by Delhi-based dentist Dr Gagandeep Singh Sodhi, who cautions that using unproven teeth-whitening remedies at home before visiting a dentist could delay vital care and pose unforeseen health concerns. Although they can supplement professional teeth-whitening methods, some of these natural remedies cannot completely replace them. Therefore, even if significant whitening may happen in a few days in professional settings, it is not advisable to depend on quick "three-day whitening" claims without professional guidance. Dental practitioners usually employ hydrogen peroxide or carbamide peroxide for teeth whitening, which have the ability to change the natural colour of teeth. These therapies are typically administered at higher concentrations during in-office procedures. These formulations may be used in conjunction with light or laser activation to speed up the whitening process and achieve higher-quality outcomes. For patients who would want to progressively whiten their teeth, dentists may suggest customised trays with lower-concentration gels for use at home. This ensures a controlled application with minimal drawbacks. Professional scaling may be considered for people with extrinsic tooth discolouration brought on by coloured foods, drinks, or cigarette smoking. Given that high-risk individuals frequently think alternative cures are safe or are reluctant to see a dentist, such blends are popular on social media. However, there isn't much scientific data to support their use. Moreover, over the counter tooth whitening products or unregulated online at-home options may not beneficial for everyone. Therefore, the safest and most efficient strategy is still to use evidence-based whitening procedures under dental supervision.

title: Fact Check: Can a natural remedy save a heart attack patient?
claim_text: A viral Burmese Facebook post claims that consuming a natural preparation containing hot water and chili powder can cure people suffering from heart attacks. The caption 'How to immediately save a person who has a sudden heart attack?' suggests a natural recipe could save someone having a heart attack.
quick_take: According to a Facebook post, a natural recipe could save someone suffering from a heart attack. We verified the claim and found that the assertion isFalse.
doctor_explanation: We used Google reverse image search and discovered that images of hot tea and red chilies had been combined to create a collage. We even translated the written portion of the shared image, which does not even mention the exact herbal recipe that could save a patient suffering from a heart attack. Also, the claim does not specify how the shown herbal therapeutics are used to save a heart attack patient. Additionally, no cardiologist, alternative medicine practitioner, or cardiac research institute has shared this post. As a result, our analysis shows that the assertion is false and should not be trusted. Heart attacks and strokes are typically sudden events caused by an obstruction that prevents blood from flowing to the heart or brain. The most common cause is an accumulation of fatty deposits on the inner walls of blood vessels that supply the heart or brain. Strokes can also be caused by blood clots or bleeding from a blood vessel in the brain. These conditions are usually caused by a combination of risk factors such as tobacco use, an unhealthy diet, obesity, physical inactivity, harmful alcohol use, hypertension, diabetes, and increased lipid levels. Heart condition is one of the world's leading causes of death, including hypertension, thromboembolism, coronary heart disease, heart failure, endocarditis, stroke, peripheral vascular disease. Some people experience no symptoms, while others feel pressure, tightness, pain, squeezing, or aching in the chest; pain that spreads to the shoulder, arm, back, neck, or even the jaw; cold sweats; weakness; heartburn; sudden dizziness; nausea; and shortness of breath. Herbal ayurvedic formulations can help lower cholesterol and improve certain cardiac conditions, but they cannot treat heart attacks. Chandraprabha and cinnamon with honey are two herbal remedies that are commonly used to lower blood cholesterol levels. The combination of Arjuna, Ashwagandha, and Shatavari not only promotes healthy cholesterol levels but also helps regulate blood pressure. Amla promotes the growth and maintenance of new tissues, as well as the production of red blood cells. And garlic is the most important ingredient for controlling blood pressure, lowering cholesterol, boosting immunity, fighting infections, and even preventing cancer. While Ayurveda has provided novel remedies for the management of cardiovascular diseases, herbs such as Arjuna, garlic, and cinnamon and their formulations appear to be very beneficial in the treatment and prevention of heart diseases. However, more research is needed to determine their role in cardiac emergencies such as heart attacks and strokes. Dr. Annusuiya Gohil, our Ayurvedic expert, advised that, 'A person experiencing a heart attack should not look out for immediate ayurvedic treatment. Despite the fact that ayurveda has many medicines and procedures for maintaining good cardiac health, there is still a lot that needs to be done for emergency care and treatment of vital organs. There are also many restrictions due to the prohibition on the use of certain drugs. Allopathy has done an excellent job in terms of emergency care and treatment, and it should be used whenever needed. Once the patient is out of danger, he can seek alternative medicine to maintain his cardiac health.' The most commonly used treatment for CVDs remains conventional drug therapy and surgical management. The majority of risk factors for cardiovascular disease and stroke are modifiable or completely avoidable. Tobacco use, high blood pressure, physical inactivity, high blood cholesterol, obesity, heavy alcohol consumption, and poor nutrition are all modifiable risk factors. While age and family history are not modifiable risk factors, remember that a heart attack necessitates emergency management. THIP Media Take: We conclude that the post claiming the use of a herbal remedy to save a person from a heart attack is untrustworthy. Our analysis also reveals that, while natural remedies may aid in the treatment of cardiac conditions, they cannot be relied on to manage medical emergencies such as heart attacks and strokes. Hence, the claim is false.

title: Fact Check: Can a new airborne mRNA vaccinate people without consent?
claim_text: Scientists at Yale University have invented a new way (airborne mRNA) to give people vaccines through the air without them knowing or agreeing to it.
quick_take: An article on a media website claims that a new airborne mRNA can vaccinate people without their consent. We fact-checked and found the claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: There is no evidence that a new airborne mRNA vaccine can vaccinate people without their consent. The claim that a new airborne mRNA vaccine can vaccinate people without their permission has been circulating online, but it is false. There is no such vaccine in existence, and even if there were, it is unlikely that it would be effective in vaccinating people without their consent. The claimed article referenced a research paper authored by a team of Yale scientists. This paper was published in the August 16, 2023, edition of Science magazine. However, the paper's freely accessible summary did not address the purported objective of bypassing consent. Instead, it primarily focused on a novel vehicle for vaccine delivery. This delivery system had shown promise but, at the time of publication, had only been tested on mice and not on humans. Our research found that the People's Voice website often shares wrong and confusing information on social media. Once, they said that the Dutch were killing people without their agreement, but we proved that wasn't true. They also wrote an article saying that Pope Francis supported euthanasia, which wasn't accurate either. We looked into this website more and found out that they often write stories that don't have any proof to back them up. Also, The People's Voice used to be called Newspunch, and they've been spreading false information for a long time. They often share stories that aren't trustworthy or real. Vaccination typically requires a person's informed consent, and administering a vaccine without consent would raise serious ethical and legal issues. The development and distribution of vaccines involve rigorous scientific and ethical processes, including obtaining informed consent from individuals who receive the vaccine. Airborne transmission of vaccines, especially without the individual's consent, would not align with established ethical and legal standards. The mRNA vaccines work by delivering instructions to the body's cells to produce a protein that will trigger an immune response to a specific pathogen. In order for an mRNA vaccine to be effective, it must be delivered inside the cells of the body. This is typically done through an injection, but research is underway to develop other methods of delivery, such as inhalation. Yes, inhaled mRNA can vaccinate people. Inhaled mRNA vaccines are still under development, but preclinical studies have shown that they can elicit strong immune responses against a variety of pathogens, including SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19. Inhaled mRNA vaccines work by delivering mRNA directly to the lungs, where it is taken up by cells and translated into proteins. These proteins are then recognized by the immune system, which triggers the production of antibodies and other immune cells that can protect against infection. Inhaled mRNA vaccines have several potential advantages over traditional injectable vaccines. First, they are needle-free, which may make them more appealing to some people. Second, they are delivered directly to the lungs, which is the main site of infection for many respiratory viruses. This could lead to more effective and rapid immune responses. Third, inhaled mRNA vaccines are relatively easy to use. Overall, inhaled mRNA vaccines are a promising new technology with the potential to revolutionize the way we vaccinate people against infectious diseases. However, even if an inhaled mRNA vaccine were to be developed, it is unlikely that it would be effective in vaccinating people without their consent. This is because the vaccine would need to be delivered in a sufficiently high dose to be effective, and it would also need to be delivered directly to the lungs. It is unlikely that this could be done without the person's knowledge or consent. In conclusion, it is important to note that vaccination is a voluntary medical procedure. No one can be forced to get vaccinated without their consent.

title: Fact Check: Can a paste of flaxseed oil and honey remove moles and warts?
claim_text: Use honey with a little bit of flaxseed oil. Mix a little bit of honey and flaxseed oil and apply it onto the mole of your skin. This paste can get rid of all your moles and warts
quick_take: Multiple social media posts and health blogs claim flaxseed oil and honey remove moles and warts. We fact-checked the claim and found it to be False.
doctor_explanation: A mole is a skin growth that looks black or brown. It develops when pigment-producing cells called melanocytes grow in groups. It is normal to have 10 to 40 moles till 25 years of age. A wart is a dermatological condition that causes small and fleshy growth on the skin. Also known as Verruca vulgaris, a wart is caused by Human Papillomavirus (HPV). A dermatologist can either cut the mole and stitch the skin or use a surgical blade to remove the mole. However, research suggests a doctor may further examine the mole as overgrowth of cells is a sign of skin cancer. A wart often goes away on its own. However, a dermatologist may want to cut it or use Cantharidin to provide instant relief. The doctor may also use Cryotherapy or Electrosurgery for a soft wart. Also, if the wart is hard the doctor can recommend Immunotherapy, Laser treatment, Chemical peels and Bleomycin. No. This is a popular home remedy suggested by many blog posts with no scientific evidence to back the claim. No study suggests that flaxseed oil and honey can remove moles permanently. title: Fact Check: Can a Paste of Natural Ingredients Fix Toothache and Tooth Decay in Two Days?
claim_text: Applying a paste of mustard oil, salt, clove, and turmeric can fix tooth decay and toothache within two days.
quick_take: There is no scientific evidence that a mix of mustard oil, salt, clove, and turmeric can fix tooth decay and toothache within two days. Tooth decay causes permanent damage and cannot be resolved with these natural ingredients.
doctor_explanation: Tooth cavity, medically known as dental caries, is an irreversible microbial disease of the calcified tissues of the teeth, characterized by demineralization of the inorganic portion and destruction of the organic substance of the tooth, which often leads to cavitation (definition by Shafer). The main cause is acid-producing bacteria like Streptococcus mutans, which stick to the tooth surface and convert sugars into acid, gradually eroding and weakening the tooth structure. The formation of dental caries depends on four key factors: bacterial biofilm (plaque) on tooth surface, fermentable carbohydrates, tooth structure, and sufficient time. Once cavities develop, they cannot be reversed and have no cure. Dr. Jesu K Joseph, MDS, Prosthodontist, Lecturer, Sanjay Rungta Group of Institutions, Bhilai, C.G., said: 'Mustard oil, salt, clove, and turmeric have certain antibacterial and soothing properties, but there is no scientific evidence that they can eliminate toothache or decay within two days. These ingredients might reduce discomfort briefly, but they don't reverse decay or eliminate infection. Tooth decay is a progressive disease that needs professional cleaning and treatment by a dentist. Depending on home remedies instead of proper dental care can delay healing and lead to more severe pain or complications later.' Dr. Akash Kumar Swarnkar, Dr Swarnkar's Dental Clinic, Bhilai, Durg (C.G.), added: 'Using these kitchen ingredients like mustard oil, salt, clove, and turmeric might help calm toothache for a short time, but they cannot eliminate toothache or decay as no natural mix can remove tooth decay or pain within two days. Tooth pain often indicates an underlying issue such as infection or decay, which needs proper diagnosis to identify the exact cause.' Regarding clove specifically, an in vitro study published in the International Journal of Dentistry suggests clove essential oil and its two lead molecules eugenol and eugenyl acetate may inhibit decalcification and/or promote remineralization of tooth structure, but the study does not suggest that tooth decay will resolve — and certainly not within 2 days. A study on salt published in the International Research Journal of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences demonstrated only a decrease in pain intensity with salt water rinsing, not complete elimination of toothache within two days. A study published in Cureus concluded that mustard seed extract exhibits strong antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties against oral microorganisms, but does not mention mustard oil specifically or provide evidence supporting its effectiveness in eliminating tooth decay or toothache within two days. A review article on turmeric's effect on oral health published in Bioinformation highlighted that massaging and rinsing with turmeric powder helps in reduction of painful teeth and decreases microorganisms causing dental caries, but does not claim it can entirely eliminate tooth decay and toothache within 2 days. None of these studies provide evidence that combining these ingredients can eliminate toothache or tooth decay. Tooth decay involves the destruction of tooth structure, and no ingredient or medication currently available can reverse or repair this damage. Toothache can only be fully resolved when the underlying cause is properly treated by a dental professional. Managing toothache involves relieving pain and ensuring referral to a dentist for accurate diagnosis; NSAIDs are used for pain control, antibiotics only if infection is spreading, and root canal or extraction may be needed for deep infections.

title: Fact Check: Can a person get visible abs without exercise? - THIP Media
claim_text: OMG the fastest way to lose Belly fat & get abs👇🏼 You don't have to do belly workouts or an exercises to see your abs. Everybody has abs and it's just a matter of losing the layer of belly fat covering them.
