title: Fact Check: Can Applying vodka on the face cleanses skin, tighten pores, and prevent acne?
claim_text: Applying vodka on the face cleanses the skin, tightens pores and prevents acne breakout.
quick_take: A recent Instagram post claims that applying vodka on the face cleanses the skin, tightens pores and can prevent acne breakout. This post is Misleading. Vodka has some temporary effects due to its alcohol content, such as tightened skin or a temporary reduction in bacteria. However, the potential for skin irritation, dryness, and worsening of acne outweighs any short-term benefits. Vodka is neither appropriate nor effective for skincare and harms the skin. The claim oversimplifies and exaggerates the benefits while ignoring the negative consequences.
doctor_explanation:
Dr. Rinky Kapoor, Consultant Dermatologist, Cosmetic Dermatologist & Dermato-Surgeon, The Esthetic Clinics, Mumbai, responded to the claim: 'Applying it directly on the face easily irritates the skin. The drying nature of vodka allegedly strips out the essential oils from the skin making it look dry, flaky, and dull. This worsens existing skin conditions like dermatitis, eczema, psoriasis, and rosacea. The likelihood of experiencing skin breakouts, acne, redness, inflammation, itching, and burning sensation is higher.' She further states that 'vodka is a bit harsh on the skin which significantly causes harm to the skin's protective barrier. It does not address the root cause of acne which is essential in reducing frequent acne breakouts on the skin. Regular use of alcohol or vodka makes skin more sensitive to environmental factors like UV rays, pollution, dirt, and dust particles. People with sensitive or acne-prone skin should avoid making these risky choices and instead opt for safe and gentle alternatives. For permanent and effective solutions to treat acne, one can consider consulting a dermatologist. He/she might recommend some skincare products according to skin type, texture, and need for better results. Habits like frequently touching your face with dirty hands can aggravate the symptoms of adult acne.'

Dr. Soumya Sachdeva, Consultant Dermatologist, Theya Wellness Skin Hair and Aesthetics Clinic, Kaushambi, Ghaziabad, explained: 'I would not recommend applying vodka or any form of alcohol directly to the skin. Vodka or any alcohol can worsen acne and lead to allergies and contact dermatitis on the skin with serious consequences.' She further states that 'alcohol has the potential to deplete the skin of its natural oils, causing dryness and irritation that may weaken the skin's protective layer. Skin disorders like rosacea or eczema may become worse as a result of this disturbance and become more challenging to treat. Additionally, some people may experience allergic responses and increased skin sensitivity when using vodka. It is far preferable to utilize skincare products that are specifically formulated for skincare of different skin conditions while maintaining a healthy skin barrier to guarantee the health and integrity of the skin.'

Scientific evidence cited in the article: According to The Indian Journal of Dermatology, skin cleansers are surface-active chemicals (emulsifiers/detergents/surfactants/soaps) that reduce skin surface tension and emulsify dirt, sebum, oil from cosmetic products, microorganisms and exfoliated corneum cells. An ideal cleanser should do all of this without harming or irritating the skin. (1)

The National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases defines acne (Acne Vulgaris) as a common skin condition in which hair follicles beneath the skin become blocked. Sebum oil keeps skin from drying out and dead skin cells clog pores, causing pimples. The combination of oil and cells causes bacteria to thrive in clogged follicles, causing inflammation. (2)

According to Dermatologic Surgery, skin pores are characterized by apparent topography alterations on skin surfaces. The three main clinical causes of enlarged face pores are excessive sebum, decreased flexibility around the pores, and increased hair follicle volume. (3)

Scientific evidence indicates that the use of ethanol and ethanol-based creams are associated with skin irritation and contact dermatitis. A study by Lin Liu et al., published in Clinical, Cosmetic, and Investigational Dermatology, found that alcohol consumption negatively impacts skin health by increasing inflammation and sensitivity. The ethanol is metabolized into acetaldehyde and then acetic acid, which aggravate skin conditions by enhancing inflammatory cytokine production in keratinocytes and promoting lymphocyte proliferation, worsening inflammatory skin disorders such as psoriasis. (6)

A study by Dirk W Lachen Meier et al., published in the Journal of Occupational Medicine and Toxicology, revealed that the use of ethanol-based creams increases skin penetration and facilitates transdermal absorption of xenobiotics. In persons with aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) deficiency, ethanol usage is associated with skin irritation or contact dermatitis. Alcohol usage is linked to skin cancer, psoriasis, discoid eczema, and superficial infections. (7)

A study by Partha Mukhopadhyay et al., published in The Indian Journal of Dermatology, concluded that gentle, non-foaming cleansers are best for sensitive or dry skin, while active ingredients like salicylic acid or benzoyl peroxide are recommended for acne-prone skin. The study advises against harsh ingredients, including high concentrations of alcohol, as they can disrupt the skin's natural balance and worsen conditions. (1)

Final Take: Scientific studies demonstrate that the use of ethanol can clean the skin but it is also associated with skin irritation and contact dermatitis. Alcohol is also associated with exacerbating various skin conditions, including psoriasis, discoid eczema, and superficial infections. The application of alcohol-based products, such as vodka, on the skin is likely to result in adverse effects rather than providing benefits like cleansing, pore tightening, or acne prevention. There is no scientific evidence or medical consensus that clearly stated that applying vodka can directly prevent acne.

title: Fact Check: Can applying vodka prevent acne?
claim_text: Applying vodka on the face cleanses the skin, tightens pores, and prevents acne breakouts.
quick_take: A social media post suggests that applying vodka can prevent acne. However, this claim is false and potentially harmful.
doctor_explanation:
Vodka is often promoted for its supposed ability to cleanse the skin due to its alcohol content, but it is not an effective skincare ingredient. While alcohol has some antiseptic properties, it can actually disrupt the skin's natural barrier. Alcohol-based products can strip the skin of essential oils, causing dryness and irritation rather than providing a deep cleanse. A good skincare routine involves gentle cleansing methods that don't damage or dehydrate the skin, and vodka does the opposite. The American Academy of Dermatology recommends using 'alcohol-free' skincare products.

The idea that vodka can tighten pores is a misconception. Pore size depends on genetics and factors like age, skin type, and sun damage, not by applying astringent substances. While alcohol might temporarily cause the skin to appear tighter, this effect is short-lived. In the long run, alcohol can dehydrate the skin, leading to increased oil production and possibly making pores appear larger, not smaller. It can also enhance the absorption of harmful substances through the skin. For pore care, it's best to use gentle toners with ingredients like witch hazel or niacinamide, which are known for their calming and pore-refining properties.

Applying vodka on the face is not a solution for preventing or treating acne. In fact, alcohol can irritate the skin and worsen acne in many people. The skin's natural oils help maintain a healthy, balanced barrier, and alcohol can strip away this protection. This disruption can lead to an increase in oil production, causing clogged pores, which can trigger or exacerbate acne breakouts. Instead of alcohol, effective acne treatment includes using non-comedogenic products, gentle exfoliation, and active ingredients like salicylic acid or benzoyl peroxide, which target acne without causing harm to the skin.

Using vodka on the skin is not a safe practice. The high concentration of alcohol can cause skin irritation, dryness, and even lead to an allergic reaction for some individuals. Alcohol can weaken the skin's natural barrier, making it more susceptible to environmental damage, redness, and sensitivity. Moreover, alcohol in skincare products can increase the skin's vulnerability to sunburn and damage, as it dehydrates the skin. It is essential to choose skin-safe, dermatologist-approved products instead of relying on harsh ingredients like vodka.

Dr Rashi Soni, Co-founder and Consulting Dermatologist at Rashi Hospital, Mumbai, explained: 'Pore size is mainly influenced by genetics, age, and sun exposure. While home remedies like clay masks and exfoliating scrubs can temporarily improve skin texture, they cannot permanently shrink pores or reverse ageing. For lasting results, professional treatments like chemical peels, microdermabrasion, or laser therapy are more effective.'

Dr Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant in Lucknow, clarifies: 'Using vodka on the skin is not a good idea. While it might seem like it could cleanse or tighten the skin, alcohol can actually harm the skin's natural barrier. It strips away essential oils, causing dryness, irritation, and even redness. Over time, this can make the skin more vulnerable to damage and increase sensitivity. For healthy, balanced skin, it's better to stick with gentle, dermatologist-approved products that nourish and protect, rather than using harsh substances like vodka.'

title: Fact Check: Can applying Yam Cream Restore Hormone Imbalance naturally in 1 year?
claim_text: Applying yam cream will restore hormone imbalance naturally in 1 year, and can cure conditions like PCOS, endometriosis, and fibroids caused by hormonal imbalance.
verdict_original: This claim is False. Hence, the claim that applying Yam Cream Restore Hormone Imbalance naturally in 1 year is FALSE.
quick_take: There is no scientific evidence to support the claim that applying yam cream restores hormonal imbalances. PCOS cannot be cured — it is a chronic disorder that requires a multifaceted treatment approach including lifestyle changes and medications. Wild yam contains diosgenin, but studies have disproven its ability to convert into estrogen or progesterone in the body.
doctor_explanation:
Dr. Nirmala Chandrashekar, Senior Consultant Obstetrics and Gynecology at Gleneagles BGS Hospital, Kengeri, Bengaluru, explained: 'Hormonal imbalance caused by PCOS includes irregular menstrual cycles, infertility, weight gain, acne, excess facial male pattern hair growth due to increasing the androgens (male hormones) and mood disturbances. In PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome), the imbalance of hormones, particularly insulin and androgens, disrupts normal ovulation. This results in the formation of ovarian cysts, irregular periods, and challenges in conceiving. Addressing hormonal imbalance is crucial for managing PCOS and preventing long-term complications like type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Weight reduction by diet, exercise and lifestyle modification play a key role in managing PCOS.'

Dr. Sowmya K N, Consultant Obstetrician & Gynaecologist at Gleneagles BGS Hospital, Kengeri, Bengaluru, stated: 'Yam, an edible tuber native to Africa, Asia, and America, is traditionally used to treat inflammation, fungal infections, and spasms, and as a natural alternative for hormonal supplements. However, there's no scientific evidence supporting these claims. Although wild yam contains diosgenin, once believed to stimulate hormone production, studies have disproved its ability to convert into estrogen or progesterone. Despite claims that yam boosts collagen production and alleviates menopause symptoms, these effects also lack scientific validation.'

The article further explains: Wild yam (Dioscorea villosa) extracts administered topically as cream are known to contain steroidal saponins, including diosgenin, which has been linked to endogenous steroidogenesis. However, no studies have been conducted on the safety or efficacy of these medicines in the therapy of menopausal symptoms (PubMed: 11428178). Wild yam is frequently touted as a natural source of DHEA because it contains diosgenin, which can be synthesized in the lab to produce estrogen — although there is no scientific evidence that it can treat and cure hormonal imbalances. Yams have a high polysaccharide content and have shown anti-diabetic and anti-obesity properties in studies, but these relate to metabolic effects, not direct hormone replacement. Yam cream is not recognized or approved by major health regulatory bodies (FDA or EMA) as a treatment for hormone-related disorders. The article concludes: 'Hormonal imbalance affects the entire body, requires multi-faceted treatment approach that may include lifestyle changes, medications, and sometimes surgery. PCOS can be managed with adequate food control, regular physical exercise, and the use of appropriate medications. Applications of such lotions should not replace expert medical counsel or treatment.'

title: Fact Check: Can Arjun chaal help reduce hair greying?- THIP Media
claim_text: A social media video where a woman claims that applying Arjun chaal can prevent greying of hair by nourishing hair roots and restoring natural pigment.
quick_take: A social media post claims that Arjun chaal is a natural remedy for reversing or slowing down hair greying. We fact checked and found the claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: There is no scientific proof that Arjun chaal prevents or reverses greying of hair. Arjun chaal, or Terminalia arjuna, is a tree native to India and has long been used in Ayurvedic medicine, mainly for heart health. It contains natural compounds like tannins, flavonoids, and antioxidants. While these might sound beneficial, none of them have been clinically shown to stop or reverse greying of hair. Hair greying is a complex biological process, usually caused by a decline in melanin production in hair follicles. This drop is often due to ageing, genetics, oxidative stress, or deficiencies in certain nutrients. Arjun chaal hasn't been scientifically linked to any mechanism that influences melanin production or grey hair reversal. Dr Mohit Sandhu, Ayurveda Consultant from Hamirpur, Himachal Pradesh states: "As per Ayurveda, Arjun chaal is considered beneficial for individuals with heart conditions. It helps support cardiovascular health, which is well-documented in Ayurvedic texts. However, there is no traditional script or strong evidence suggesting that Arjun chaal has any role in preventing or reversing greying of hair." Dr P Rammanohar, Research Director at the Amrita Centre for Advanced Research in Ayurveda, emphasizes that while age-related or genetically driven greying is irreversible, there's some potential to slow down greying caused by external factors such as lifestyle habits or environmental stressors. Regarding antioxidants: while Arjun chaal is rich in antioxidants that help fight oxidative stress linked to ageing, hair greying due to oxidative stress is primarily internal and cellular. There's no research showing that antioxidants from Arjun chaal, whether applied topically or consumed, reach the follicle in meaningful amounts to make a difference. Dr Swati Watwani, Dermatologist and Medical Director at Persianlily Clinic, notes that while most people begin to experience greying in their late 40s or early 50s, premature greying can start as early as the 20s. Although it's not possible to reverse the process entirely, identifying the underlying cause of early greying—whether nutritional, hormonal, or stress-related—may help slow its progression through proper treatment and care. While Arjun chaal contains small amounts of calcium, magnesium, and zinc important for overall hair health, the quantities are relatively low and not a substitute for actual dietary sources or supplements. Traditional uses of Arjun chaal in hair oils or decoctions are anecdotal and not supported by scientific trials. What actually works for slowing or managing grey hair includes nutrition, managing stress, correcting vitamin B12 or copper deficiencies, stress management, healthy eating, and avoiding smoking. Arjun chaal has no established role in these pathways—it's not harmful in small amounts, but using it to 'treat' greying hair could give people false hope and delay more effective approaches.

title: Can Arjuna bark with cinnamon clear arterial blockages in 3 days?
claim_text: Consuming presoaked Arjuna bark with cinnamon can significantly clear clogged arteries and regulate blood glucose levels by raising HDL and lowering LDL. The caption of the post stated: 'कोलेस्ट्रॉल कम करने का जादूई नुस्खा सिर्फ तीन दिन कर्लो' (Magical recipe to reduce cholesterol in just three days).
verdict_original: We verified and found it to be false
quick_take: An Instagram post claims that using cinnamon and Arjuna bark can clear arterial blockages in 3 days. We verified and found it to be false.
doctor_explanation: Cholesterol refers to a lipid molecule that serves as a key component of cell membranes, along with being a precursor for steroid hormones, bile acids, and vitamin D. In the blood, cholesterol is transported by attaching itself to proteins to create lipoproteins. These primarily fall into the following categories: LDL and HDL. When elevated LDL-C enters the arterial wall, it oxidises and initiates an inflammatory cascade that encourages plaque development. As plaques accumulate, the arterial lining becomes unstable. Ultimately, this confluence of thrombosis, inflammation, and fat accumulation results in the formation of arterial clots, which can result in sudden artery constriction or obstruction. If elevated cholesterol levels are not timely evaluated and appropriately treated, they could raise the risk of myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, and coronary artery disease. Even while the combination of Arjuna bark and cinnamon is being touted for elevated cholesterol and 'blocked' or coagulated arteries, its relevance is confined to social media platforms. There are insufficient large-scale clinical trials to support the combination or individual ingredients as the primary therapeutic approach to reversing arterial blockages. Furthermore, neither of the two ingredients can directly dissolve existing atherosclerotic plaques. Therefore, for elevated cholesterol or atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, Arjuna bark and cinnamon may be used as an adjuvant rather than as a substitute for the clinically established therapeutics. Dr. Anusha Dewan, a Consultant General practitioner at Jeevan Anmol Hospital in New Delhi, advises against opting for unverified home remedies in place of scientifically validated treatments. While there may be health benefits to some at-home cures, they shouldn't be the sole treatment for conditions like hypertension or blocked arteries. Most importantly, there are uncertainties regarding the efficacy and dependability of unregulated at-home solutions because they are not as rigorously controlled or evaluated as prescription medications. Cholesterol levels cannot be controlled in three days. This may be explained by the long-term nature of metabolic processes involving liver synthesis, dietary intake, and lipoprotein clearance. Considering that brief dietary modifications may result in slight variations, a healthy diet with physical activity requires time to act. Furthermore, clinically recognised potent lipid-lowering medications like statins – which typically provide quantifiable and long-lasting LDL-C reductions in randomised controlled trials – may take weeks rather than days. Therefore, it is impractical and unscientific to imply that cholesterol can be corrected quickly in three days. Dr. P. Rammanohar, Research Director at the Amrita School of Ayurveda, adds credence to this by stating that home remedies cannot immediately remove cardiac obstructions. Even with Ayurveda, any recovery requires months or even years of strict dietary and lifestyle adjustments. Blockages have not yet been completely removed by any medication, either conventional or new. There could be dire repercussions if one relies on these assertions and delays necessary medical care. Complications linked with elevated cholesterol levels include atherosclerosis, coronary artery disease, and stroke. Uncontrolled bad cholesterol typically calls for a combination of lifestyle alterations (healthy way of living, diet, physical exercise, weight management, managing comorbid conditions), pharmacological interventions (statins, ezetimibe, PCSK9 inhibitors), and interventional techniques (angioplasty or coronary artery bypass grafting). Dr. Mohit Bhagwati, MBBS, DNB in General Medicine and Cardiology at Holy Family Hospital in Delhi, emphasised the need for recommended medicines and lifestyle changes for heart blockages. He highlighted the pleiotropic effect of statins, which means that they may reduce the risk of stroke along with decreasing cholesterol by stabilising plaques and thickening their caps, which lowers the chance that they will rupture. Most critically, surgery might be necessary in more complex cases. Procedures like coronary artery bypass grafting and angioplasty with stent implantation are feasible. To prevent long-term issues, effective management requires a customised risk assessment and continuous cholesterol monitoring.

title: Fact Check: Can arthritis be cured by consuming haldi, sonth and methidana?
claim_text: Haldi (turmeric), sonth (dried ginger) and methi daana (fenugreek seed) with 2 glasses of water daily for 3 months cures arthritis.
verdict_original: The claim by the user is False. / Hence, the claim by the user is FALSE.
quick_take: While haldi and sonth have anti-inflammatory properties that may provide modest symptomatic relief, there is no scientific evidence that turmeric, dried ginger, and fenugreek seed water can cure arthritis—especially in a fixed 3-month period. Arthritis is a chronic condition and cannot be cured through home remedies alone.
doctor_explanation:
Arthritis is a chronic condition involving inflammation in the joints. While medications can help control inflammation and manage symptoms, there is no cure. Ingredients such as haldi (turmeric) and sonth (dry ginger) possess anti-inflammatory properties and may provide symptomatic relief, but they cannot cure arthritis.

Dr Muhammed Nazeer, Senior Consultant and Group Co-ordinator, Department of Orthopedics and Trauma, KIMSHEALTH Thiruvananthapuram, stated: 'There are various causes of arthritis. One common type is osteoarthritis, which is primarily due to degenerative changes that occur in the joints. Another type is rheumatoid arthritis, which results from inflammation in the joints and can affect individuals at any age—including children, in which case it is referred to as juvenile rheumatoid arthritis. It can also occur in older adults. While there are various medications available that can help control the inflammation associated with arthritis, none of the natural remedies you mentioned—such as Haldi (turmeric), Sonth (dry ginger), or Methi Dana (fenugreek seeds)—can cure arthritis. These may offer some relief because they contain natural anti-inflammatory properties, but they can only help manage the symptoms to a certain extent. No current medication or remedy can cure arthritis, but inflammation can be controlled using anti-inflammatory treatments.'

Dr Mir Zia Ur Rahaman Ali, Sr. Consultant Orthopaedic & Joint Replacement Surgeon, CARE Hospitals Outpatient Centre, Banjara Hills, Hyderabad, stated: 'Arthritis is a long-term disease that causes inflammation in the joints. Natural herbs like haldi (turmeric), sonth (dry ginger), and methidana (fenugreek) can help reduce inflammation, but they can't cure arthritis. If you use these as part of a healthy lifestyle, they might help with some weak symptoms, but they don't stop joint damage or treat the underlying causes. Moreover, prolonged or excessive use of these ingredients may lead to side effects like acidity and other abdominal issues. title: Can ash gourd juice with jaggery dissolve kidney stones?
claim_text: Consuming ash gourd juice with jaggery on an empty stomach can effectively dissolve kidney stones.
quick_take: According to a Facebook post, kidney stones may be removed by consuming ash gourd juice with jaggery. After verifying, we found it to be false.
doctor_explanation:
Kidney stones, medically considered as renal calculi, are solid masses composed of urinary minerals and salts, such as struvite, uric acid, or calcium oxalate. When urine becomes concentrated, these often rise to the surface, which facilitates the clumping of these components. Even though these aggregates are extremely common, certain triggers may contribute to the risk. While smaller renal calculi don't cause any symptoms, larger ones can cause various symptoms. Being aware of these symptoms may make it easier to reach out to a nephrologist for early detection and an appropriate course of treatment.

Although ash gourd and jaggery juice are frequently being promoted as a kidney stone remedy, their relevance is confined to social media. This may be explained by the clinical literature's strong emphasis on the preventive nature of dietary modifications and adequate hydration. This suggests that optimal fluid intake enhances urine volume, which subsequently lowers the concentration of substances that form stones and prevents stone recurrence.

Ash gourd, also known as Benincasa hispida, has a substantial amount of water, modest antioxidants, and renal-protective characteristics that may protect the kidneys from damaging compounds but do not dissolve stones. In fact, consuming more of the ingredient, particularly in juice form, may increase the risk of calcium deposition, which, due to oxalates and phytates, may induce or worsen kidney stones.

Similarly, the biochemical processes that remove kidney stones have not been shown to be impacted by jaggery, a traditional unprocessed sugar product. Moreover, high-sugar consumption can significantly influence urinary composition, ultimately increasing the risk.

Dr. Sharad Malhotra, HOD Gastroenterology, Hepatology & Therapeutic Endoscopy, Aakash Healthcare, New Delhi, warns against utilizing them as a long-term kidney stone cure. Furthermore, Dr. Malhotra maintains that because these unreliable therapies lack substantial scientific backing, they shouldn't be employed as an alternative to standard medical therapies for renal calculi. Crucially, in addition to delaying essential therapy, using ash gourd and jaggery juice to remove renal calculi can result in consequences such as discomfort, obstruction, or infection. For stones larger than a few millimetres, imaging, hydration, citrate therapy, and suggested urological procedures are necessary.

Dr. Archana Daftardar, a consultant nephrologist, hypertension specialist, and transplant physician at Renova Hospitals in Kompally, Hyderabad, underlines that there are many misconceptions about kidney stone care and prevention. Unproven natural remedies might actually make the illness worse rather than better. Consultation with a qualified allopathic physician is the recommended course of action.

Dr. Ganesh Srinivasa Prasad P, a Consultant Nephrologist at Narayana Health City in Bengaluru, also maintains that the kidney stone type primarily determines the medical course of action. Even while kidney stones cannot be effectively cured at home, the associated risk can be successfully decreased by drinking enough water, eating meals high in calcium, avoiding foods high in oxalate, and consuming less salt. Moreover, moderate use of animal products, sugar, alcohol, nicotine, and carbohydrates may help reduce the incidence of uric acid stones. Relying entirely on questionable remedies may worsen the condition by delaying the required intervention. For kidney stones, a precise diagnosis and individualised treatment are vital. Only under professional supervision may home-based therapies be utilised as therapeutic assistance; a thorough medical examination is required to establish the appropriate course of action.

Medical therapies based on the morphological features, anatomical position, and chemical profile of renal calculi include imaging, hydration, citrate therapy, and suggested urological procedures. Neglecting the prescribed course of therapy could exacerbate symptoms, increase the risk of serious infections such as urinary tract infections and hydronephrosis, and possibly result in renal failure, endangering one's overall health.

This comes from the fact that stress is a known contributor to digestive issues like bloating and gas. Additionally, some believe that its anti-inflammatory properties can soothe the digestive tract, potentially relieving symptoms like gas and indigestion. However, these claims are largely anecdotal, with little direct scientific evidence supporting the specific use of Ashwagandha for digestive and gas-related issues. Some preliminary research hints at its potential to support gut health by modulating gut microbiota, but these findings are not yet conclusive. There is also limited evidence suggesting that Ashwagandha may help in reducing inflammation, which could theoretically benefit digestive health. In contrast, Ayurvedic texts do suggest that Ashwagandha can balance Vata dosha, which often has association with gas and bloating issues. Yet, this perspective is rooted in traditional knowledge. And, due to the lack of sufficient evidence it is difficult to substantiate the claim. Ashwagandha may have a general stress-reducing effect that could indirectly benefit digestion. However, there is insufficient scientific evidence to support the specific claim that it can directly help with bloating, gas issues, or significantly improve digestion. The idea that Ashwagandha can relieve gas and enhance digestion appears to be more of a traditional belief than a medically proven fact, as of now. The available studies focus on its broader health benefits rather than its specific impact on digestion. Therefore, Ashwagandha may contribute to overall well-being and reduce stress-related digestive issues. But it is not yet a proven remedy for gas or digestive problems. Dr Annusuiya Gohil, MD Scholar at the All India Institute of Ayurveda, explains, 'Each dravya (substance) has its unique Rasa (taste), Virya (potency), and Vipaka (post-digestive effect), which influence how it interacts with the body. While it is thought to improve symptoms of gas, acid, and IBS, there is no conclusive evidence to support this, and no one-size-fits-all solution can be prescribed for every condition.' Potential side effects of Ashwagandha include gastrointestinal discomfort, nausea, diarrhoea, and drowsiness. THIP Media Take: Ashwagandha has a well-documented history in traditional medicine and is supported by some modern research for its stress-relieving properties. The evidence supporting such claims is largely anecdotal and not backed by strong scientific research at present. Therefore, even when Ashwagandha may offer indirect benefits through stress reduction, it should not serve as a standalone treatment for digestive issues.

title: Fact Check: Can baking soda and aloe vera treat stretch marks?
claim_text: A Facebook post claims that a mixture of Aloe Vera and Baking soda (bicarbonate) can be used as an organic stretch marks cream. quick_take: A social media post claims that the mixture of baking soda and aloe vera can remove stretch marks. We fact-checked and found this claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: Stretch marks are indented streaks that occur from skin stretching quickly and beyond its elastic capacity. Genetics and the degree of stress on skin play an essential role in producing stretch marks. Additionally, a protein named collagen is responsible for making skin more elastic. So, if the skin does not have enough collagen, stretch marks may show up. The ability to completely remove stretch marks depends upon the skin. A permanent treatment will involve rebuilding new healthy tissues beneath the stretch marks to fade away the appearance of the marks. The available chemical treatments may fade away stretch marks depending upon the case, but home remedies only reduce the appearance. Dr. Jyothy Kannangath, Dermatologist, explains, 'Stretch marks can not be removed, they can only be reduced. Textural changes and colour alteration can be improved with procedures like fractional lasers, radiofrequency, PRP, etc. The topical products used for the treatment of stretch marks may fade them if used regularly for a minimum of 3-6 months.' There is no credible scientific evidence to prove that the mixture of baking soda and aloe vera can treat stretch marks. These are two common ingredients that are often suggested for various skincare remedies, but when it comes to treating stretch marks, their effectiveness is limited. Dr. Parwaaz Matharoo, MBBS, MD (Dermatology) informs, 'To understand this, let's dive into the mechanism of why we get stretch marks. The main pathology circles around three components i.e. collagen, elastin and fibrillin that are present in our skin. Sudden changes in our body weight whether more or less cause aberrant interaction among these proteins and leads to the formation of striae or as we call stretch marks. Hence their mainstay of treatment is based on reinstituting the balance, which is difficult but not impossible. There's no scientific evidence that aloe vera and baking soda have any kind of deeper impact on collagen or elastin. In fact, both of them act superficially, with aloe vera as a soothing moisturizing agent and baking soda as a chemical irritant. Also, they may not suit everyone and cause adverse events leading to more harm than help. Therefore, please do not try such remedies at home as it isn't safe or helpful at all.' Baking soda is commonly used as an exfoliant and can help remove dead skin cells, but it has no proven effects on reducing or eliminating stretch marks. It is not a targeted treatment for stretch marks. Dermatologists do not recommend baking soda on the skin because it can strip off the natural oil to irritate the skin. Dr. Iram Qazi, MD (Dermatology) says, 'I will never suggest baking soda as a home remedy treatment. It can have damaging effects on the skin. That is because baking soda can interfere with the skin pH. The normal pH of the skin ranges from 4.5-5.5. This pH keeps the skin healthy and forms a protective oil barrier around it keeping it well moisturized with healthy oils and protecting it from bacteria as well. Baking soda, on the other hand, has a pH of 9. Thus applying a strong alkaline base on the skin can remove the natural protective oils from the skin and make it more prone to bacterial infections and skin damage. Also, baking soda can cause skin irritation and inflammation which may worsen acne and increase pigmentation and scarring of the skin. It can also increase skin dryness which causes overproduction of skin oils leading to more acne breakouts and scarring of the skin.' The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health says there's not enough definitive evidence to support all the purported benefits of aloe, though it's safe when used on the skin. Aloe vera has soothing and hydrating properties that may help reduce inflammation and promote skin healing. It can be applied topically to the affected areas to moisturize and potentially soothe the skin but it is unlikely to have a significant impact on existing stretch marks. Dr. Jyoti Kannangath comments on the use of Aloe vera by stating, 'Aloesin, a compound extracted from Aloe vera, has demonstrated the ability to competitively inhibit tyrosinase, the enzyme responsible for skin pigmentation. However, there have been several published case reports documenting hypersensitivity reactions and contact dermatitis caused by aloe vera preparations.' Dr. Soumya Sachdeva, Consultant Dermatologist suggests, 'Aloe vera decreases the itching associated with the stretch marks and prevents progression to some extent. But alone aloe vera is not a way to completely get rid of stretch marks, though it can be useful to decrease the itching. Additionally, baking soda is not recommended for stretch marks, because it may cause contact dermatitis leading to redness, itching and scaling over the sites of the stretch marks.'

Similar false claims have circulated in the past, such as Dr Naresh Trehan supposedly endorsing a quick fix for high blood pressure or Dr Devi Shetty promoting a diabetes cure in just 37 hours.

Baking soda does not cure diabetes. Diabetes is a chronic condition that affects blood sugar regulation. It requires proper medical management, including lifestyle modifications, prescribed medication, and in some cases, insulin therapy. Some studies suggest that baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) may help reduce inflammation in certain conditions, but there is no clinical evidence to support its use as a diabetes cure. No credible research supports baking soda as a treatment for diabetes. Reliable treatments involve a combination of medical guidance, lifestyle changes, and medication, not unproven home remedies.

In fact, using baking soda on the skin can cause irritation or dryness due to its highly alkaline nature. This makes it unsuitable for sensitive skin, especially in areas where hair removal is desired.

DOES LEMON JUICE LIGHTEN SKIN OR HELP WITH HAIR REMOVAL? Not really. Lemon juice is sometimes used as a natural remedy for lightening dark spots, but its effectiveness is limited. Also, it does not work as a hair removal agent. Even though the citric acid in lemon juice may provide slight exfoliation, it won't dissolve hair or affect its growth cycle. Moreover, applying lemon juice to the skin and exposing it to sunlight can increase the risk of irritation and even lead to hyperpigmentation (darkening of the skin). Having said that, lemon juice has anti-inflammatory and anti-microbial properties. But, this does not justify the claim that lemon juice can remove hair permanently.

CAN BABY OIL MAKE SKIN ULTRA-SOFT AFTER HAIR REMOVAL? Yes, but it won't remove hair. Baby oil has the potential to moisturise skin, which can make it feel soft and smooth. However, baby oil has no hair removal properties. It can be helpful to soothe the skin after hair removal through other methods. However, in this recipe, it serves no real purpose beyond moisturising.

WILL TOOTHPASTE REDUCE REDNESS AND SOOTHE THE SKIN AFTER HAIR REMOVAL? No, there is no scientific evidence which suggests this. Some believe that toothpaste can help reduce redness due to its menthol content, but it is not a scientifically proven skin treatment. In fact, toothpaste can cause irritation, especially on sensitive skin. Applying toothpaste to areas where hair has been removed may lead to redness, irritation, or even chemical burns, which makes it a poor choice for any skincare routine.

DOES THIS MIXTURE PERMANENTLY STOP HAIR FROM GROWING BACK? Absolutely not. There is no evidence that any of the ingredients in this mixture—flour, baking soda, lemon juice, baby oil, or toothpaste—can stop hair from regrowing. Hair removal techniques that are proven to have long-term effects, like laser hair removal or electrolysis, work by targeting the hair follicles, which this DIY mixture cannot do.

Permanent hair removal methods like laser hair removal and electrolysis can significantly reduce hair growth by targeting and destroying hair follicles. However, they may not completely stop hair from regrowing. Even these methods often require multiple sessions and maintenance treatments. Over time, some hair may regrow, though it is generally finer and lighter. Natural or DIY remedies, like the one in the claim, cannot achieve permanent hair removal.

Some of the ingredients may have minor benefits for the skin, like exfoliation or moisturisation, but they cannot remove hair permanently or even effectively. For reliable hair removal, we recommend scientifically proven methods such as shaving, waxing, or laser treatments. Always consult with a dermatologist or healthcare professional before trying any new hair removal technique to avoid potential skin damage.

Not Exactly. Anemia is a kind of blood condition. Iron deficiency, pernicious, aplastic, and hemolytic anemia are some of its forms. Thus, managing anemia involves increasing red blood cells, relieving symptoms, resolving the underlying condition, minimizing anemic complications, and thus enhancing overall quality of life. Furthermore, mild anemia can be treated with dietary modifications and supplements. Severe anemia, on the other hand, is treated with medications, blood transfusions, and, in certain cases, by addressing the underlying pathology.

Thus, banana flowers may help with mild anemic symptoms caused by iron deficiency anemia. However, there is no evidence that banana flowers alone could manage severe or life-threatening anemic cases.

Three major mechanisms contribute to anemia. These include failure to develop RBCs, an excess of RBC destruction, and blood loss. Anemia caused by nutritional deficiencies continues to be the predominant cause of anemia worldwide. Following this are underlying illnesses and possibly hereditary issues. Anemia management is not limited to nutrition rather, it includes medical management along with dietary modifications. Further, it is vital to acknowledge that nutritional supplements could help with mild symptoms. Dr. Kashyap explained that, "determining the cause of anemia is crucial in the overall management of anemia. THIP Media Take: Banana flower is unquestionably a nutritious edible component of the banana plant. doctor_explanation: Teeth discoloration can happen for a number of reasons. Common substances like those found in tea and coffee, as well as antibiotics like tetracycline or food dyes, can seep into the teeth. As a result, these stains may endure in the porous structure of the enamel. Smoking contributes to dental discoloration as well because of how tobacco smoke's toxins build up over time. In addition to the gradual erosion of the enamel to reveal the yellow dentin, teeth that are aging tend to become discolored with the accumulation of various stains. Bananas contain large amounts of potassium as well as vitamins A, B6, C, and D. This high nutritional status promotes the strength of the teeth and soft tissues, as well as the heart, brain, and bones. Bananas' potassium helps increase bone mineral density. Additionally, it collaborates with magnesium to stop the blood from getting too acidic, which could prevent calcium loss from the bones and teeth. Banana peels do not contain strong enough natural chemicals to bleach teeth, despite being naturally sweet and low in acid, and there is no evidence that rubbing or abrasive action of the peel on the teeth will remove intrinsic stains. A banana peel can be used as a cleanser to help remove surface stains from the teeth. During our research, we couldn't find any definite evidence that banana peels actually whiten teeth. The minerals in bananas might support dental health, but they are unlikely to whiten a discolored smile. When we questioned our dental expert, Dr. Pratyasa Bagchi, about the possibility of using banana peels to whiten teeth, she responded that there is no scientific evidence to support the claim. Although banana peels contain phosphorus, iron, calcium, magnesium, and sodium, which could strengthen teeth, the enamel surface does not absorb those minerals because it is as hard as bone. Therefore, from this perspective, it would be difficult to assert that banana peels whiten teeth. The dental bleaching process lightens your teeth and makes them whiter. Although the procedure can lighten your teeth's color by several shades, it cannot completely whiten them. Commercial teeth-whitening products could be harmful to your teeth. Thus, herbal remedies are consequently growing in popularity. When compared to hydrogen peroxide or hydroxyl carbamide alone, natural ingredients are known to whiten teeth more safely. These primarily consist of limonene, which has shown great promise for teeth whitening and is a major component of citrus fruit peel essential oils. L-ascorbic acid is another well-known antioxidant that aids in preventing tooth decay, gum disease, and tooth loss. For teeth whitening, this ascorbic acid from organic fruits and vegetables has been recommended as a good substitute for carbamide peroxide or hydrogen peroxide. The vanilla fruit's phthalimido peroxy caproic acid has been shown to contain a substance that can whiten teeth. The fruits of the pineapple and papaya, respectively, contain the mouth-clearing enzymes bromelain and papain. The actinidain found in Kivi fruits can be used to remove dental biofilms. There isn't much data to back up the use of these natural teeth-whitening methods, though. Due to a lack of knowledge regarding their safe dosage and concentration for human teeth, these cannot be used to whiten teeth. THIPMEDIA TAKE: Many social media posts suggest rubbing the peel against your teeth for a brief period of time in order to whiten them. Brushing your teeth is still the most efficient method, even though some surface stains may be able to be removed with a banana peel. We draw the conclusion that this assertion is mostly false because banana peels lack any distinctive whitening characteristics.

title: Fact Check: Can bandages cause cancer?

doctor_explanation: Is it true that bandages can cause cancer? No, not really. But there is more to it than just a simple 'Yes' and 'No'. A study conducted by Environmental Health News and Mamavation, found that popular brands of bandages contain chemicals called PFAS (per- and poly-fluoroalkyl substances). These are also known as 'Forever chemicals'. The PFAS pose numerous health consequences like: Reduction in immunity, reduced vaccination response, increased risk of allergies and asthma in young children, effects on growth and learning abilities of infants and older children, increased cholesterol level, metabolic diseases (obesity and diabetes), cardiovascular diseases, reduced female and male fertility, risk of kidney and testicular cancer, causes endocrine disruption, disruption of normal thyroid function, and risk of acute lymphoblastic leukaemia in children. With that being said, using bandages will not cause cancer immediately, because we use bandages for a short time and very sparingly. Prolonged use over a long period of time may have some health effects. Also, as per Department of Health Rhode Island, the permissible limits for PFAS in drinking water is 70 parts per trillion. In the Mamavation and Environmental Health News study, the detected levels of organic fluorine (indicative of PFAS) came in the range of 11 to 328 parts per million. We also need to note that there aren't enough studies, data and evidence to accurately find out what concentration of PFAS is actually carcinogenic and under what conditions. We also need more information and research on the interaction of PFAS with open wounds. Furthermore, the precise risk of PFAS exposure through the skin remains uncertain. Nonetheless, earlier lab research conducted by the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health indicate that exposure to PFAS through the skin presents comparable health risks to ingesting the chemicals through food or water. The Mamavation study discovered PFAS traces in well-known bandage brands like Band-Aid, Equate, and CVS Health. However, it's reassuring that certain brands like 3M and Tru Colour were devoid of organic fluorine and other harmful compounds.

title: Fact Check: Can Barley (Jaun) Water Completely remove Kidney stones?

quick_take: The claim that barley water can completely remove kidney stones is false. doctor_explanation: In a conversation, Dr Tanima Das Bhattacharya, MD DM Nephrology, Consultant Nephrologist, Narayana Hospital Howrah said: 'Barley is a cereal grain being used worldwide for ages for various health benefits. It contains fibres, vitamins and minerals. Regarding kidney stones, if stones in the urinary tract are 5mm or less, they can be flushed out through urine by maintaining adequate hydration. Hydration may be with water or barley water. Barley being a mild diuretic increases the flow of urine which helps in small stone removal. Barley contains vitamin B6 or pyridoxine. B6 can reduce oxalate excretion by reducing its production in the liver. Less Calcium oxalate formation means less calcium oxalate stones which is only one type of kidney stone. Barley can cause alkalinization of urine making it less acidic and therefore less chances of acidic stones. However kidney stones have multiple variables therefore one is to one benefit is not always true. Beta glucan present in barley has been studied in chronic kidney disease for reducing uremic toxins and also in kidney stones. However direct benefit has not been proved. Barley is rich in minerals and electrolytes like calcium, potassium, iron, magnesium, selenium etc. Individuals having other issues like hypertension, diabetes, cardiac or kidney diseases and on other prescription medications might have problems with potassium levels in their blood if on regular barley drinks. Monitoring of potassium, phosphorus levels is essential in such cases. Barley water comes in various forms and with various added ingredients. It should not be an alternative treatment. It can be an additive treatment to standard treatment for kidney stones. As stones with swelling or obstructed urinary tract or urinary infections, pain, fever and large impacted stones should be managed with definitive medical and surgical methods.' Dr. Rajesh Loonia, Consultant, MBBS; MS (General Surgery); MCh (Urology), Narayana Super Speciality Howrah further said: 'Barley water cannot completely remove kidney stones. It may help support kidney health by promoting hydration and flushing out toxins due to its diuretic properties, potentially aiding in preventing stone formation or passing very small stones. However, there's no scientific evidence to confirm that barley water can dissolve or completely eliminate all kidney stones entirely. For kidney stones, medical treatments like increased fluid intake, medications, or procedures (e.g., lithotripsy, ureteroscopy) are typically required, depending on the stone's size, type, and location. Always consult a healthcare professional for proper diagnosis and treatment.' The article also notes: Kidney stones are hard, pebble-like deposits that form in one or both kidneys when mineral concentrations become too high. They can be composed of calcium oxalate, calcium phosphate, cystine, struvite (magnesium ammonium phosphate), or uric acid. Smaller stones often pass naturally with increased fluid intake. Larger stones typically require medical intervention — Shock Wave Lithotripsy (SWL), Cystoscopy and Ureteroscopy, or Percutaneous Nephrolithotomy. A study in the International Journal of Nutrition, Pharmacology, Neurological Diseases found that barley demonstrated significant diuretic effects and helped reduce calcium deposits in the renal parenchyma, suggesting its potential in supporting renal function and preventing kidney stone formation. The National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases states that staying well-hydrated is the most effective way to prevent most types of kidney stones. While barley may provide health benefits and adequate water intake may help prevent kidney stones, there is no scientific evidence to suggest that they can fully dissolve or eliminate existing stones. A review by Arif Ali et al. highlights barley's potential to support gut health and strengthen the immune system via high β-glucan content and microbiome-modulating effects. A study by Ancuța Boantă et al. noted that barley is rich in essential vitamins, minerals, and soluble dietary fiber, particularly beta-glucans, and green barley is valued for its antioxidant properties.

title: Fact Check: Can bay leaf powder remove plaque and whiten teeth?
claim_text: Massaging your teeth with ground bay leaf powder every two or three days can remove plaque and restore lost tooth shine. The post specifically claims this method is useful for people who consume tobacco and smoke cigarettes.

doctor_explanation: Ground bay leaf powder cannot remove plaque. Plaque is a sticky film of bacteria that forms on your teeth and gums. It can harden into tartar if not removed regularly by brushing and flossing. Only mechanical cleaning methods like brushing with a fluoride toothpaste and professional dental cleanings can effectively remove plaque and prevent tartar buildup. Bay leaf powder has applications in traditional remedies for various purposes. However, it has no scientific backing to support its effectiveness in cleaning teeth or removing plaque. Simply massaging teeth with a powder won't have the necessary abrasive action to effectively clean plaque from the tooth surfaces. During our investigation, we found an older study from 2008 on Eugenia polyantha Wight (Bay leaf). The study indicates that bay leaf has antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties useful in dental treatments. Nonetheless, it lacks evidence supporting its effectiveness in removing plaque or whitening teeth. Dr Pooja Sharma, BDS, MDS, NIMS University, Jaipur, says, "Bay leaf powder might seem like an easy fix, but there's no scientific backing for its ability to remove plaque. Plaque is a sticky layer of bacteria that really needs to be cleaned away with regular brushing and flossing. While home remedies might feel natural, they can sometimes do more harm than good, especially if they damage your enamel. It's always best to stick with proven dental care methods." Tooth discolouration is a complex issue that can result from several factors including poor oral hygiene, smoking, consumption of staining foods and drinks, or even natural ageing. Restoring the natural whiteness of teeth needs more than applying a herbal remedy. Professional teeth whitening treatments, proper dental care, and lifestyle changes (like quitting smoking) are far more effective in restoring tooth brightness. Bay leaf powder itself is generally safe for consumption in small amounts, but it doesn't mean it's appropriate for use in dental care. The abrasiveness of such powders can sometimes damage enamel if used aggressively. Tooth enamel does not regenerate, so once it's damaged, it's gone for good. Additionally, this type of DIY remedy doesn't address the underlying causes of dental issues like plaque buildup and discolouration, both of which require regular dental care. There is a new trend suggesting that oil pulling can whiten teeth, but this claim has not been scientifically proven yet. Smoking and chewing tobacco are infamous for causing plaque buildup, tartar, and significant tooth discolouration. The yellow or brown stains due to these habits cannot be removed by simply applying bay leaf powder. Tobacco users should seek professional dental cleanings to remove stubborn stains and plaque buildup. To add more, quitting tobacco use is extremely essential to prevent further discolouration and improve overall oral health. Regular use of tobacco can also increase the risk of gum disease, oral cancer, and tooth decay. The stains from tobacco are deep and require professional treatment. Quitting tobacco and maintaining regular dental visits are the real keys to keeping your smile healthy and bright. It's important to also remember that tobacco use increases the risk of serious conditions like gum disease, which need proper care." The claim that ground bay leaf powder can remove plaque and restore tooth whiteness is false. title: Can bay leaves really cut your heart attack risk? - THIP Media
claim_text: drinking bay leaf tea twice in a day can reduce the risk of heart attack
quick_take: A social media post suggests that bay leaves reduce the risk of heart attacks. We fact checked and found the claim to be false.
doctor_explanation: Do bay leaves actually help prevent heart attacks? Nope, not really. Bay leaves do not have strong scientific evidence to support claims of preventing heart attacks. Heart attacks occur when blood flow to the heart is blocked, often due to plaque buildup from high cholesterol or inflammation. While bay leaves are used in traditional remedies there's no robust human research confirming they lower cholesterol or prevent heart issues. Without large-scale, long-term studies showing reduced heart attack risk, relying on bay leaves for prevention is speculative. What's the deal with studies on bay leaves and your heart? There's a flicker of hope, but it's faint. One small study with 40 folks who had type 2 diabetes found that munching 1 to 3 grams of ground bay leaves daily for a month dropped blood sugar by 20-26% and improved cholesterol, cutting total cholesterol by up to 24%, boosting the good HDL kind, and trimming the bad LDL and triglycerides. Since diabetes and high cholesterol can up your heart attack risk, that's a bit exciting. Another study hinted that bay leaf team might help cholesterol levels in people with heart issues, possibly by boosting antioxidants. But here's the catch: these studies are tiny, often short, and sometimes done on rats, not people. The results don't always hold up, and nobody's pinned down how much bay leaf you'd even need. Scientific reviews say the plant's natural compounds might help with diabetes or heart symptoms in theory, but we're nowhere near calling it a heart attack preventer. It's like finding a promising recipe but not knowing if it'll taste good when you make it. Could bay leaves still be good for your heart in some way? Maybe a little. Bay leaves have goodies like polyphenols, antioxidants that might calm inflammation or tweak blood fats, which could be kind to your heart. Some rat studies showed bay leaf extracts lowering cholesterol by blocking an enzyme that makes it. In people, one small trial paired bay leaf decoction with light exercise and saw cholesterol drop. But don't get too excited, these effects are spotty, and bay leaves aren't a cure-all. They could mess with blood sugar meds, risking low levels, or cause trouble if you swallow them whole since they're hard to digest. Tossing a leaf into your soup adds a cozy flavour without harm, but don't expect it to be your heart's bodyguard. It's just one small ingredient in a much bigger health recipe. What should you do instead of counting on bay leaves? Have a heart-to-heart with your GP if you're worried about your ticker. They can check your blood pressure, cholesterol, and other signs to see where you stand. If you love bay leaves keep using them in your cooking, they make soups and curries sing without any fuss. But don't expect them to save your heart. Focus on the big stuff: eat fresh, move often, chill out, and follow your doctor's advice. If you're curious about natural boosts, ask your GP about things like omega-3 supplements or plant sterols, they've got stronger science behind them. Dr Almas Fatma, a general practitioner from Navi Mumbai, encourages that small daily choices are key to preventing heart attacks. Adopting a balanced diet, staying active, and avoiding smoking are vital preventive steps. Regular checkups are essential for managing conditions like hypertension, diabetes, and high cholesterol. Simple changes, such as reducing stress and limiting alcohol, can make a big difference. Prioritizing prevention over treatment is the most effective approach to maintaining heart health. Dr Naresh Kumar Monigari, Director of the Cath Lab and Consultant Interventional Cardiologist at Renova Century Hospitals in Banjara Hills, Hyderabad, stresses that individuals with a family history of coronary artery disease (CAD) should undergo regular cardiac check-ups. Early identification of silent heart issues can prevent serious incidents. Furthermore, people can safeguard their heart health by avoiding tobacco, maintaining a healthy weight, managing blood pressure, and adopting stress-reduction practices. At the end of the day, bay leaves are a kitchen gem, but they're not your heart's knight in shining armour. The evidence is too thin, and leaning on them might steer you away from what really works. Your heart's worth the best care, stick to what science knows, don't just follow DIY's blindly.

claim_text: Bay leaves water with apple cider vinegar eliminates gall stones and kidney stones in 3 days, with positive results in the first three days of use. The reel claims it is 100% effective, the perfect treatment to avoid risky surgical interventions, and ideal for anyone suffering from kidney or gallbladder stones.
verdict_original: The claim by the user is FALSE.
quick_take: The claim that bay leaves water with apple cider vinegar can eliminate gallstones and kidney stones in three days is false. While both bay leaves and apple cider vinegar have general health benefits, and apple cider vinegar may help manage the condition, no scientific evidence or medical consensus supports their ability to eliminate gallstones or kidney stones.
doctor_explanation: Dr. Harshvardhan Chaukulkar, Department of Minimal Access and General Surgery, Ruby Hall Clinic, explained: 'No, there is no scientific evidence that bay water with apple cider vinegar can dissolve or remove gallstones in three days. Apple cider vinegar is sometimes touted as a natural remedy, but it has no proven efficacy in treating gallstones. The composition of gallstones, especially cholesterol stones, requires specific treatments such as medication or surgery for effective removal. Gallstones are hard deposits that don't dissolve easily. Natural remedies cannot address large stones or those causing complications like infection or blockages. If you feel you have gallstones, it is best to consult your physician when you are experiencing severe pain or other symptoms. Receiving an accurate diagnosis and thus proper treatment can avoid serious complications, such as inflammation, infection, or damage to the gallbladder or bile ducts, from waiting any longer to seek medical attention.' Dr. Shashank M S, Consultant - Urology and Renal transplant, Aster CMI Bangalore, further explained: 'The question arises whether the combination of bay water and apple cider vinegar can effectively dissolve kidney stones within a span of three days. This inquiry reflects a growing interest in natural remedies for managing kidney stones, which are often painful and can lead to significant health complications. While some anecdotal evidence suggests that apple cider vinegar may aid in breaking down certain types of stones due to its acidic properties, the efficacy of such a remedy, particularly when combined with bay water, remains largely unverified by scientific research. Therefore, it is essential to approach this topic with caution and to consider consulting a healthcare professional for evidence-based treatment options.' Gallstones are solid deposits that form within the gallbladder or biliary tract due to an imbalance in bile components. Cholesterol gallstones form when cholesterol in bile becomes excessively high; pigment gallstones are composed of bilirubin and are more common in individuals with liver conditions or blood disorders. Treatment options include cholecystectomy (surgical removal of the gallbladder), ERCP for stones lodged in the common bile duct, and shock wave lithotripsy. Kidney stones are solid pebble-like masses developing in kidneys due to elevated mineral levels, linked to higher risk of chronic kidney disease, end-stage renal failure, cardiovascular conditions, diabetes, and high blood pressure. Treatment depends on size and location — smaller stones may pass naturally with increased fluid intake and pain relief, while larger stones require procedures such as extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy, ureteroscopy, or percutaneous nephrolithotomy. While National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases notes that a high-fiber diet can lower gallstone risk, and a study by Ferraro et al. in the Journal of American Family Physicians showed that increasing fluid intake to 2.5–3 L per day, consuming high fiber and vegetables with normal calcium content, limiting sodium and animal protein can help prevent recurrent kidney stones, no credible research or clinical study proves that bay leaves water with apple cider vinegar can dissolve or eliminate either gallstones or kidney stones, let alone in three days.

title: Fact Check: Can bee venom cream remove dark spots?
claim_text: Bee venom cream can remove dark spots, repair skin, hydrate, and is suitable for all skin types with 100% natural ingredients.
quick_take: A social media post claims that bee venom cream can remove dark spots and repair skin while moisturising. We did the fact check and found out it's False.
doctor_explanation: No, bee venom cream cannot remove spots. Bee venom has been under research for certain potential health benefits, such as anti-inflammatory effects. But there is no reliable evidence suggesting it can remove skin spots. Spots on the skin can include hyperpigmentation, acne scars, or age spots. Dark spots can result from a number of factors, like sun exposure, hormonal exposure and ageing, to name a few. Spot removal usually requires treatments like chemical peels, laser therapy, or proven topical ingredients such as retinoids and vitamin C. Evidence supporting bee venom includes two studies—a lab study from 2019 and a 2016 study on 30 human subjects, both indicating its potential to treat acne spots. But we cannot generalise these results for large population sizes, yet. Supporters of bee venom believe it stimulates collagen production in small doses, which may improve skin texture. But, this is far from the claim that it can remove spots. Based on this, some posts on social media promote bee venom cream for a younger looking skin. However, we still need to prove this through strong clinical trials. Most of the scientific studies on bee venom are in controlled environments and the results are still inconclusive. Dr Ekansh Shekhar, Internationally Acclaimed and Awarded Board Certified Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant, Lucknow, states: 'There is no scientific evidence to support the claim that bee venom cream can effectively remove spots from the skin. Even though bee venom has anti-inflammatory properties, it is still under research for its ability to treat conditions like hyperpigmentation, acne scars, or other types of skin spots. In such cases, it's important to consult a dermatologist for a professional skin analysis and personalised advice. Depending on the situation, dermatologists may recommend treatments such as chemical peels, microdermabrasion, laser therapy, or IPL, along with topical creams or serums containing ingredients like hydroquinone, retinoids, or vitamin C. A customised skincare routine will help achieve the best results.' Dr Hitesh Aggarwal, Dermatologist at Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences, New Delhi, explains: 'There are no studies to support the use of bee venom for pigmentation, and evidence-based practice is crucial when it comes to skincare. Unfortunately, many companies market products without proper research. Although some mention bee venom for its potential in reducing wrinkles and managing pain, scientists have not proven its effectiveness in treating pigmentation.' Dr Kumar Abhishek, Consultant Dermatologist, Dermatosurgeon & Aesthetician, at Skinstitute, Bhubaneswar, says: 'Bee venom creams have shown encouraging results in some dermatological concerns like psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, and fine wrinkles. There have been attempts to use them for spot removal, but more research and clinical trials are needed before we can recommend them for regular use as a depigmenting agent. So far, the studies are experimental, and without strong randomised controlled trials (RCTs), we cannot confidently endorse bee venom as an effective spot removal treatment.' Regarding skin repair: No, there is no substantial evidence that bee venom cream can repair skin damage. Bee venom is popular for its potential to rejuvenate skin by promoting collagen production and improving skin elasticity. However, these claims are largely speculative, or based on lab or animal studies and lack strong scientific backing. Studies on humans generally use small sample sizes, making it difficult to generalise the results to larger populations. They have not proven the collagen-boosting effects of bee venom to repair significant skin damage, such as scars, deep wrinkles, or wounds. Skin damage repair usually requires proven treatments like retinoids, ceramides, or growth factors, while bee venom's use in dermatology is mostly experimental and its ability to 'repair' skin is doubtful. Regarding safety: No, bee venom cream is not necessarily safe for all skin types. Bee venom is a potential allergen and can trigger allergic reactions, especially in individuals who are sensitive to bee stings. Even in topical form, bee venom may cause skin irritation, redness, or swelling. People with sensitive skin or pre-existing skin conditions like eczema or rosacea should particularly be more cautious. Dr Rashi Soni, Dermatologist at Rashi Hospital, Hingoli, Maharashtra, shares: 'There are many well-researched options available for spot removal and skin repair that are worth considering. Ingredients like retinoids, vitamin C, and niacinamide are often recommended by experts for tackling hyperpigmentation and uneven skin tone. When it comes to skin repair, hyaluronic acid and peptides work wonders by keeping your skin hydrated and helping it heal naturally. While bee venom is sometimes mentioned in skincare, it doesn't have the same strong scientific backing as these other ingredients, which have been thoroughly studied and proven to deliver real results.'

title: Fact Check: Can bee venom cure nail fungus?
claim_text: According to a Facebook post, bee venom can effectively cure nail fungus instantly.
quick_take: A social media post claims that bee venom can cure nail fungus completely. We did the fact check to term this claim as Mostly False.
doctor_explanation:
Nail fungus, medically known as onychomycosis, is a widespread infection caused by various fungi. It often leads to discoloured, thickened, and brittle nails, which can be unsightly and uncomfortable. Treatment usually involves antifungal medications, available as topical creams or oral pills. The effectiveness of these treatments varies based on the type and severity of the infection.

Honeybees produce bee venom as a defence mechanism, which contains components like melittin and phospholipase A. We know that these compounds have anti-inflammatory and pain-relieving effects. While some studies have explored the potential therapeutic uses of bee venom, particularly for arthritis, researchers are still investigating its role in treating fungal infections, including nail fungus.

Currently, there is little scientific evidence supporting the use of bee venom as an effective treatment for nail fungus. Most research on bee venom has focused on its potential benefits for conditions like arthritis and skin diseases, not fungal infections. That being said, bee venom does have antifungal properties, but these findings are still not clinically proven in humans. We still need more studies to support its use for treating nail fungus.

The claim video promotes a bee venom product for nail fungus, but fails to provide important details. It doesn't mention the ingredients, price, or how and from where to purchase the product. Instead, it shows dramatic before-and-after visuals, suggesting quick results without any real evidence. The social media page has no website link and there is nothing mentioned in the 'About' section. This lack of transparency is concerning, as viewers cannot properly evaluate the product's safety or effectiveness.

Dr Rashi Soni, Co-founder and Consulting Dermatologist at Rashi Hospital, Mumbai, says: 'Nail fungus can be tough to treat and often needs prescription antifungal medications for full recovery. Home remedies and over-the-counter products rarely provide lasting results. Consulting a dermatologist ensures an accurate diagnosis and effective treatment, which can prevent the condition from worsening or causing permanent damage.'

Dr Sachin Gupta, Consultant Dermatologist at Amrita Hospital, Faridabad, states: 'Proper elimination of nail fungus usually requires prescription-strength antifungal medications. Over-the-counter treatments are often insufficient. It's crucial to consult a doctor for an accurate diagnosis and appropriate care, as delaying treatment can result in persistent infection or long-term damage to the nails.'

Using bee venom products can pose risks, particularly for individuals with allergies to bee stings. Symptoms of an allergic reaction may include swelling, hives, or more severe reactions such as anaphylaxis. It's important to consult a healthcare professional before using any bee venom products, especially for conditions like nail fungus, to avoid potential allergic reactions or ineffective treatments.

Healthcare professionals recommend proven antifungal treatments like clotrimazole, terbinafine, or oral medications such as fluconazole and itraconazole, as these have been thoroughly tested for safety and effectiveness. In contrast, bee venom lacks clinical evidence for treating nail fungus. If nail fungus is suspected, it's important to consult a doctor for an accurate diagnosis and proper treatment. Relying on unverified remedies can delay care and worsen the infection.

title: Can bee venom foot patches detox your body overnight?
claim_text: A viral Facebook post suggests that bee venom foot patches can detox the body while you sleep. The video suggests it can extract toxins from the liver, arteries, and legs. The post also claims these foot patches promote lymphatic health and reduce swelling after just one or two applications.
quick_take: A social media post claims that bee venom foot patches can detox the body overnight. After fact checking, we found this claim to be false.
doctor_explanation: The human body has highly effective organs – primarily the liver and kidneys – which filter and eliminate waste products and toxins. These processes occur internally through metabolic pathways, expelling toxins from the body via urine, faeces, sweat, and breath. The skin plays a minor role in elimination through sweating. However, it is not capable of drawing out significant amounts of toxins from deep within the body, let alone major organs like the liver or from arteries. The idea that a patch applied to the soles of the feet could reverse the direction of toxin elimination and pull harmful substances from organs lacks any support from our understanding of human physiology. Dr Almas Fatma, Diploma in Family Medicine, PG in Digital Health, General Physician from Navi Mumbai, says: 'Substances applied to the feet cannot draw toxins out of the body overnight. The human body already has highly efficient systems, like the liver and kidneys, that work around the clock to process and eliminate toxins. The skin does release small amounts of waste through sweat. But it is not capable of extracting toxins from deep organs or the circulatory system. The concept that a patch can reverse the body's natural detox processes lacks any credible scientific or medical understanding.' The liver is the body's primary detoxification organ, processing harmful substances and making them soluble for elimination. The kidneys filter waste from the blood. Arteries are blood vessels, not organs that accumulate toxins to be 'drawn out' by external means. There is no known mechanism by which a foot patch could target and extract toxins from internal organs like the liver or from within the circulatory system overnight. Medical science does not support this method of detoxification. In fact, due to such misleading health claims, the US Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has previously taken action against sellers of detox foot patches. Regarding lymphatic health: The lymphatic system is crucial for fluid balance, immune function, and transporting waste products. Certain therapies, like manual lymphatic drainage massage or compression garments, can support lymphatic function and reduce swelling. But, applying a patch to the foot has no scientifically proven direct effect on the overall health or function of the lymphatic system across the body. Swelling (oedema) can have many causes. Some topical applications might offer minor, temporary relief for superficial swelling. This can be due to effects like warmth or mild irritation increasing circulation in the immediate area. But, claiming significant swelling reduction and lymphatic health promotion after only one or two uses via a foot patch is highly exaggerated and lacks scientific backing. Dr Ubaid ur Rehman, General Physician, Holy Mission Clinic, New Delhi, clarifies: 'Bee venom foot patches are not likely to promote lymphatic health or reduce swelling. That too, after just one or two uses. Bee venom has some potential therapeutic effects, such as anti-inflammatory properties. But there is no evidence to suggest that it can provide noticeable benefits to the lymphatic system or significantly reduce swelling in such a short time. Lymphatic health and swelling require more comprehensive, long-term approaches, rather than a quick fix from topical patches.' The discolouration often seen on these patches after use is generally a result of sweat mixing with ingredients in the patch. It can also be due to oxidation, or a reaction between moisture and patch materials – not toxins being drawn from the body. In addition, bee venom carries significant risks. For some individuals, it can cause serious side effects, including anaphylaxis, a severe and potentially life-threatening allergic reaction. Despite these risks, bee venom remains highly popular on social media, with numerous myths circulating about its supposed benefits. Claims have been made that bee venom can treat back pain, pigmentation, nail fungus, and even breast cancer. Some also suggest it as a potential approach for diabetes care. However, most of these are misleading.
