doctor_explanation:
Gallstones are solid deposits in the gallbladder, made of cholesterol or bilirubin, that form over time. Dissolving them requires breaking down these hard structures, which is a complex process. Muskmelon peel contains fibre, water, and some antioxidants, but there's no scientific evidence to suggest it has properties capable of dissolving gallstones. Medical treatments, such as ursodeoxycholic acid, can sometimes dissolve small cholesterol-based gallstones, but this process takes months or years and isn't guaranteed. Boiling the peel in water doesn't release any compounds that can break down gallstones, as the peel lacks the necessary chemical agents to do so.

Adding sugar to the boiled muskmelon peel water does not help dissolve gallstones. Sugar is a simple carbohydrate that provides energy but has no effect on gallstones. It doesn't interact with the chemical composition of gallstones—whether cholesterol or pigment-based—in a way that would dissolve them. In fact, excessive sugar intake can contribute to obesity, a risk factor for gallstone formation.

The idea that gallstones can dissolve within 30 minutes is medically inaccurate. Gallstones are hard, often taking months or years to form, and dissolving them naturally (if possible) or through medicine is a slow process. Even with medical treatments like bile acid medications, dissolution can take months, and only for specific types of stones (small, cholesterol-based ones). The 30-minute timeframe is unrealistic, as no natural or medical intervention can break down solid gallstones that quickly.

Dr. Sharad Malhotra, Senior Consultant and Head of Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Therapeutic Endoscopy at Aakash Healthcare, New Delhi, explained: "Gallstones are hard, solid masses that develop in the gallbladder and cannot be dissolved or broken down just by making dietary changes. Their presence often suggests that the gallbladder is not functioning properly. For many individuals, surgical removal remains the most effective treatment. It's essential to consult a healthcare professional to get an accurate diagnosis and determine the best treatment approach."

If gallstones cause symptoms like severe pain, nausea, or complications such as a blocked bile duct, surgery (called cholecystectomy) is often the recommended treatment. For asymptomatic gallstones, doctors may suggest monitoring, but there's no evidence that a muskmelon peel mixture can dissolve stones and eliminate the need for surgery. Relying on this remedy instead of seeking medical advice could delay proper treatment, potentially leading to serious health issues like infections or gallbladder inflammation.

While muskmelon peel cannot dissolve gallstones, it does contain fibre and antioxidants, which can support overall digestive health. However, simply drinking muskmelon peel water will not provide the necessary fibre, as much of it may remain in the discarded pulp. A diet rich in whole fibre can help reduce the risk of forming new gallstones over time because fibre supports healthy digestion and reduces cholesterol levels in bile. But this is a preventive measure, not a treatment for existing gallstones.

Dr. Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition, shared: "Muskmelon peels do have fibre and antioxidants that can promote gut health, which is essential for proper gallbladder function. However, drinking muskmelon peel water alone won't give you enough fibre to make much of a difference. A better way to reduce the risk of gallstones is by following a balanced, high-fibre diet that includes plenty of fruits, vegetables, and whole grains."

title: Can bottle gourd replace blood thinners for arterial blockages?
claim_text: An Instagram post with the caption "The Magic of Lauki" claims that bottle gourd is a natural blood thinner and that consuming it daily may help get rid of arterial blockages. It also suggests that the bottle gourd may help remove stomach ulcers caused by blood thinners.

ARTERIAL BLOCKAGES EXPLANATION: Dr. Amit Bhushan Sharma, Associate Director and Unit Head of Cardiology at Paras Hospitals, Gurugram, explains that arteries are vital blood vessels carrying oxygen-rich blood from the heart to organs. Damage to the arterial wall triggers inflammation, encouraging accumulation of fatty substances like cholesterol, forming a rigid plaque composed of calcium, fat, cholesterol, and cell waste products. This leads to atherosclerosis, limiting blood flow by constricting arteries. While initially silent or asymptomatic, if risk factors are not controlled, plaques may rupture, leading to clots causing peripheral artery disease, angina, heart attacks, and strokes.

BOTTLE GOURD ANALYSIS: Bottle gourd (Lagenaria siceraria) is high in potassium, vitamin C, and dietary fibre, low in saturated fat. The high fibre helps reduce LDL (bad cholesterol), and antioxidants could lessen oxidative stress and inflammation - contributing factors of atherosclerosis. However, NO SCIENTIFIC EVIDENCE supports that consumption of bottle gourd can solely reverse or unclog blocked arteries. Arterial blockages involve complex processes like plaque build-up and endothelial dysfunction requiring pharmacological therapeutics, lifestyle alterations, and surgical procedures.

AYURVEDIC PERSPECTIVE: Dr. P. Rammanohar, Research Director of the Amrita School of Ayurveda, states that home remedies cannot clear heart blockages. Any progress, even in Ayurveda, requires months or even years of strict dietary and lifestyle adjustments. No medication—conventional or traditional—has completely eliminated cardiac blockages. It could be detrimental to depend on such assertions and delay receiving necessary heart-related therapeutic intervention.

GENERAL PHYSICIAN WARNING: Dr. Anusha Dewan, General Practitioner at Jeevan Anmol Hospital in New Delhi, cautions against substituting scientifically proven treatments with unverified home cures. Even though some at-home remedies may have health benefits, they shouldn't be the only treatment for illnesses such as arterial blockages or hypertension. Most significantly, home remedies are not as rigorously tested or regulated as medicines, raising concerns about their reliability and efficacy.

BLOOD THINNER-INDUCED ULCERS: While bottle gourd is hydrating and may have gut-soothing characteristics, there isn't sufficient scientific backing to support its use for managing stomach ulcers brought on by blood thinners (Warfarin, Aspirin). Any digestive discomfort for individuals on blood thinners should be evaluated and managed by a medical expert.

TOXICITY WARNING: Overdependence or careless consumption—especially of bitter bottle gourd—has been linked to serious toxicity including vomiting, diarrhoea, and gastrointestinal bleeding. Excessive consumption may result in hypotension or hypoglycemia in vulnerable people.

He underlines the pleiotropic effect of statins, which in addition to reducing cholesterol, can also reduce stroke risk by stabilizing plaques and thickening their caps to reduce rupture chance. Treatment is stage-based: early stages require healthy lifestyle and managing comorbidities; moderate blockages need statins, antiplatelet agents, and antihypertensives; complex situations may require coronary artery bypass grafting or angioplasty with stent implantation.

title: Fact Check: Can Broccoli help fight air pollution toxins? - THIP Media

In addition, a dentist may recommend proper brushing techniques, good oral hygiene through flossing and tongue cleaning, and a diet rich in fiber, calcium, and phosphates in the early stages when the cavity is small. Although enamel remineralization occurs early on, it cannot be reversed once bacterial infiltration reaches the deeper layers. And the existing damage necessitates the intervention of a professional. Furthermore, these cavities form as a result of a combination of causative agents. Among them are poor oral hygiene, as well as genetic and environmental factors. As a result, maintaining good oral hygiene may be critical to preventing caries. Brushing, on the other hand, will not be able to reverse the established lesion.

Preventive measures include using fluoride-containing toothpaste, mouthwash, flossing, and toothbrushing. Other measures include eating more nutrient-rich foods and quitting smoking. Natural remedies that could help strengthen the enamel and keep it from demineralizing include calcium-, phosphorus-, and vitamin D-rich foods; oil pulling; aloe vera tooth gel; sugar-free gum; and phytic acid-rich cereals and legumes. title: Can butterfly yoga normalise blood sugar levels in just one week?

doctor_explanation: Can butterfly yoga alone "normalise" blood sugar within 7 days? No. One yoga posture is not a shortcut to "normal" glucose, especially if blood sugar is high due to insulin resistance, long-standing diabetes, steroid medicines, poor sleep, illness, or missed medication. Butterfly pose mainly stretches the hips and inner thighs and encourages calm breathing. That's useful, but it's not the same as sustained muscle work that consistently uses up glucose, like brisk walking, cycling, or resistance training. When research shows yoga helps blood sugar, it's usually not "butterfly pose for a week." It's structured yoga programmes (multiple postures + breathing + relaxation, repeated regularly) and the benefits tend to be seen across weeks to months, not as guaranteed normalisation in 7 days. Meta-analyses do suggest yoga can improve measures like fasting glucose and HbA1c in type 2 diabetes, but that is an average effect over time, not a one-week promise. Dr Ishita Sachdev, MBBS, Specialist in Diabetology, strongly refuted the claim, stating, "This is completely incorrect. There are at least 12 recognised causes of diabetes, and it is unrealistic to believe that a single yoga posture practised for seven days can treat all of them. Any improvement people notice from yoga is largely due to mental and emotional relaxation. When you are calmer and less stressed, blood sugar levels may temporarily improve — which simply shows how important stress management and self-care are. However, self-care is not the same as curing diabetes. It can positively influence your mood and overall wellbeing, but it does not eliminate the underlying condition. Claims that suggest otherwise are not only misleading but dangerous. Relying only on such methods — especially when captions promote practices like soaking feet in karela and fenugreek without emphasising the need for proper medical treatment — can keep blood sugar levels uncontrolled for long periods. Persistently high glucose can silently damage vital organs, and once serious complications set in, the harm is often permanent and cannot be reversed, even with alternative therapies." The claim is also medically vague — it doesn't specify whether "normal blood sugar" means fasting, post-meal, or HbA1c, which is a red flag. Butterfly pose can be useful as a calming daily practice that helps with stress and stiffness, and stress reduction can support healthier choices, but it should be paired with after-meal movement (10-15 minute walk), regular weekly activity (150 minutes/week of moderate exercise), fibre-rich meals, adequate protein, and medication consistency if prescribed. title: Fact Check: Can buttermilk rinses resolve recurrent mouth ulcers?
claim_text: Rinsing the mouth with buttermilk can resolve recurrent mouth ulcers
quick_take: According to a trending Instagram post, buttermilk mouth rinses can effectively manage recurrent mouth ulcers. We fact-checked the claim and found it to be false.
doctor_explanation:
Mouth ulcers, also known as aphthous ulcerative lesions, are small, shallow oral lesions that develop from the mouth's soft lining. These are painful, unpleasant, red-haloed ulcers on the tongue, lips, and inner cheeks that interfere with eating and talking. Usually, these oral lesions are brought on by various factors. When the aforementioned contributors persist, ulcers may recur – known as Recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS). Immune dysregulation, characterised by a breakdown in the normal control mechanisms of the immune system, often leads to an overactive inflammatory response. This persistent inflammation can cause chronic tissue damage and is associated with conditions that result in repeated ulcer formation. While occasional oral ulcers are common and usually harmless, recurrent lesions can be a sign of an underlying systemic condition. Some of the illnesses may include coeliac disease, inflammatory bowel disease, Behçet's disease, and other immunological disorders. Recurrent ulcers become concerning if they last longer than two weeks, occur frequently, enlarge, cause excruciating pain, or are accompanied with symptoms like fever, exhaustion, gastrointestinal problems, or unintentional weight loss.

Buttermilk mouth rinses are often promoted as traditional home care for mouth ulcers; their relevance is limited to social media platforms. Buttermilk may be taken into consideration because it contains lactic acid bacteria, which may help balance the oral microbiota and contribute to a slightly acidic environment that can help alleviate irritated oral tissues. Although buttermilk rinses may help balance oral flora and inflammation, there is no conclusive scientific evidence that they can effectively treat or prevent recurrent mouth ulcers. Moreover, the condition of recurrent aphthous stomatitis is multifactorial in origin, which may not be resolved solely via topical rinses. Effective management of recurrent ulcers depends on the identification and correction of the underlying factors.

People at a high risk of developing painful mouth ulcers usually resort to online remedies because they are considered safe, natural and chemical-free. Some of the popular web-based at-home solutions include honey, ghee, and certain herbal decoctions. While some of these may provide symptomatic relief due to their anti-inflammatory or cooling effects, their role in the management of mouth ulcers lacks rigorous clinical evidence. Hence, dependence on unverified at-home formulations may delay timely evaluation and appropriate management of the mouth ulcers.

Delhi's dental expert Dr. Gagandeep Singh Sodhi cautions against implementing unproven home cures for mouth ulcers before consulting a specialist because doing so might delay necessary therapy, aggravate symptoms, and cause unanticipated complications. Therefore, a licensed dentist should be consulted for timely and effective intervention.

Dr. Surya Kiran Mudigonda, Consultant Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeon at Renova Hospitals in Hyderabad, states that using ice, butter, or ghee on mouth ulcers usually reduces pain while maintaining moisture for wound healing. However, these are not the suggested therapies for mouth ulcers. When managing oral ulcers, stay away from irritants like turmeric powder or clove oil. They might exacerbate the inflammation and pain. The first line of treatment is topical corticosteroids. Severe cases can be managed via systemic medication. For some patients with both oral and vaginal lesions, immunosuppressants may be recommended.

Clinical management includes topical corticosteroids (to reduce pain, inflammation, and speed healing), antimicrobial mouthwashes such as chlorhexidine (to prevent subsequent infections), and systemic medications such as thalidomide, dapsone, or colchicine for severe or recurrent ulcers associated with systemic diseases like inflammatory bowel disease or Behçet's syndrome. Nutritional supplements are recommended when deficiencies are established, and long-term control is further strengthened by lifestyle changes including stress management and avoiding trigger foods.

title: Can cancer be effectively managed with an alkaline drink?
claim_text: An alkaline drink prepared by infusing slices of cucumber, lemon, and carrot with mint leaves for 12 hours might boost immunity and potentially cure cancer and other diseases.
quick_take: According to a Facebook post, an alkaline drink can effectively cure cancer. However, fact-checking reveals that this assertion is false.
doctor_explanation: While the notion that consuming alkaline foods might make the body less acidic is gaining popularity, it lacks scientific validation. Alkaline water is just regular water that has undergone ionisation. This approach enhances its pH to between 8 and 9 when compared to normal drinking water. Even with these short-term advantages, these treatments might not be able to affect the pH of the body in any way. This is because, through intricate mechanisms, the kidneys and lungs regulate the blood's internal pH between 7.35 and 7.45, which may not be altered by external variables, including a specific food or drink. Alkaline water is safe for most people to drink, but the benefits it claims to offer are mostly exaggerated marketing tactics rather than clinically verified therapies. The term 'alkaline diet' encourages consuming nutritious foods that are considered to establish an alkaline environment in the body while refraining from the intake of processed foods, meat, and sugar. As was previously noted, the kidneys and lungs strongly regulate the body's pH. Plant-based diets high in antioxidants, vitamins, and fiber may help lower systemic inflammation but are unable to effectively change systemic pH levels. Furthermore, there is no empirical evidence that an alkaline environment prevents the growth of cancer. Therefore, while incorporating fruits and vegetables in one's diet may help prevent cancer, it cannot be a primary approach for managing it effectively. Dr. Manish Singhal, Consultant Oncologist at Apollo Hospital in Delhi, shared with THIP Media that cancer cells may create an acidic tumour microenvironment around themselves, which could aid in the growth and dissemination of the condition. Nutrition may affect overall health, but it has little influence on the acidity of the tumour microenvironment or the body's alkalinity. These findings, however, are restricted to controlled settings and might not fully reflect the intricate workings of the normal human body. Furthermore, excessive alkaline conditions may impair the body's normal processes and could potentially require hospitalisation. Dr. Pooja Khullar, Radiation Oncologist at Dharamshila Narayana Superspeciality Hospital in New Delhi, notes that certain studies have demonstrated that acidic environments stimulate the growth of cancer cells. Thus, a diet packed with alkaline foods (high pH) and low in acidic food items has been proposed to enhance the body's alkalinity and prevent or even cure cancer. Dr. Khuller points out that these studies, however, concentrate on cancer cells in a culture plate and fail to capture the intricacy of tumour behaviour in the human body. Contrary to common perception, a life-threatening illness such as cancer cannot be cured by an alkaline drink prepared with infused lemon, cucumbers, carrots, and mint leaves. The lemon slices are often rich in antioxidants and vitamin C, which promotes the immune system. The carrot slices have antioxidant properties and are high in beta-carotene. Cucumbers may provide hydration and dietary fibre. Mint leaves might exhibit modest digestive benefits. While these nutrients might help the body when undergoing medical therapy and enhance overall systemic wellbeing, there is no substantial clinical evidence to support their use in both the prevention and management of cancer. It is highly discouraged to self-medicate for severe medical conditions, including cancer. This is due to the fact that cancer is a complicated, progressing disease that requires tailored, evidence-based treatment strategies. Based on the tumour or cancer type, stage, severity, genetic variations, and patient-specific factors, clinicians might opt for immunotherapy, chemotherapy, surgery, or a combination of these therapeutic approaches. Dr. P. Rammanohar, Research Director at Amrita School of Ayurveda, emphasises that cancer is a complex disease that is challenging to manage. Distinct therapies need to be administered for each form, and these frequently include chemotherapy, radiation, or specific (targeted) medications. All forms of cancer cannot be cured by a single herb or natural cure. While certain herbs have demonstrated potential in early lab studies, there isn't enough solid evidence from human trials to consider them to be useful medications. Before trying any alternative remedies, it is imperative to speak with trained medical specialists and rely on established therapies. Delaying or replacing conventional cancer therapies with unverified home remedies might worsen the disease's progression, lower survival rates, and cause more complications. This could be particularly problematic when it comes to aggressive or advanced tumours, where timely and reliable intervention is essential.

title: Fact Check: Can cardamom cure hair fall and insomnia?
claim_text: Before going to bed at night, chew two cardamoms well and drink a glass of lukewarm water. This cures the problem of hair fall and insomnia. Cardamom nourishes the hair.
quick_take: A viral post claims that cardamom can cure hair fall and insomnia. We did the fact check to term this claim as false.
doctor_explanation:
## Does cardamom prevent hair loss?
No, cardamom alone is not proven to prevent hair loss. While cardamom is known for its rich antioxidant content, which supports general health, there is still no conclusive scientific evidence linking its consumption to reduced hair fall.

However, a 2022 study shows that Alpinetin (AP), found in cardamom, boosts hair growth by keeping hair follicles active longer and stimulating certain stem cells through Wnt signalling (a process that helps cells grow and develop). Researchers found that AP worked better than standard treatments in mice and was safe for human and mouse skin cells. Scientists still need to confirm these results in people.

Hair health depends on a variety of factors such as genetics, overall nutrition, and lifestyle. While antioxidants can reduce oxidative stress, which may contribute to hair damage, simply chewing cardamom won't provide sufficient nutrients to directly impact hair loss prevention. For healthier hair, a diet rich in iron, zinc, biotin, and other vitamins is more beneficial.

We reached out to Dr Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant in Lucknow, for his opinion on cardamom for hair fall. He says, "While cardamom has some health benefits due to its antioxidant properties, there is no scientific evidence to support its role in preventing hair loss. For effective hair care, it's important to focus on a balanced diet, proper hair hygiene, and medical treatments backed by research."

## Can cardamom improve sleep quality?
Not really. No definitive evidence supports the idea that cardamom can directly enhance sleep quality or treat insomnia. Although cardamom has been traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine for its potential calming properties, research confirming its efficacy for sleep is lacking. A 2024 study on mice found that cardamom oil reduced anxiety in sleep-deprived mice. It increased calming brain chemicals like GABA (which helps relax the brain) and serotonin, and boosted antioxidants. However, since this study was on mice, we need more research on humans to confirm these effects.

Its pleasant aroma and soothing flavour might contribute to a sense of relaxation, but there's actually no scientific evidence for its effect on sleep. Drinking warm water, on the other hand, may have a calming effect as part of a bedtime routine. However, for consistent sleep improvements, evidence-based practices like maintaining a regular sleep schedule, reducing caffeine intake, and practising relaxation techniques are more effective.

We interviewed Dr Ubaid ur Rahman, General Physician, Holy Mission Clinic, New Delhi, for his perspective on cardamom for insomnia. He says, "Cardamom might make you feel relaxed with its soothing aroma and taste, but there's no solid evidence that it can improve sleep or treat insomnia. While some studies on mice suggest it could reduce anxiety and help calm the brain, we need more research on humans to know for sure. For better sleep, it's best to stick to proven habits like a regular sleep schedule, cutting down on caffeine, and practising relaxation techniques."

## Does cardamom provide essential nutrients for hair and sleep health?
Cardamom contains small amounts of vitamins and minerals, but it is not a significant source of the essential nutrients needed for strong hair or quality sleep. For example, magnesium, zinc, and B vitamins are crucial for these purposes, and cardamom is not a major source, especially since we consume such small quantities of the spice.

## What are the benefits of cardamom?
Cardamom is a spice with antioxidant and diuretic properties (animal study) that may help lower blood pressure and support overall health. Animal and lab studies show it could reduce tumour growth, fight inflammation, and help digestion, but human research is limited. Cardamom may also improve breath freshness, prevent cavities (animal study), and help with certain bacterial infections, though most findings are from lab tests.

Some studies suggest cardamom might improve breathing, lower blood sugar (animal study), and reduce anxiety, but these effects need more research in humans. Still, including it in your diet can be a safe and healthy choice. However, do not rely on it to cure hair loss or insomnia. Hair loss and insomnia can be related, so it's important to consult an expert to determine the root cause of your health issues and find an effective solution.

## THIP Media Take
Cardamom is a flavourful spice with some health benefits, thanks to its antioxidants. However, the claim that cardamom can cure hair fall and insomnia is false, because there is conclusive no evidence. A balanced diet and proven practices are more effective for maintaining hair health and sleep quality.

While cavities are common, the risk tends to rise for those with dry mouth, systemic illnesses, inadequate dental hygiene, a habit of snacking, and inadequate fluoride exposure. The principal cariogenic bacterium, Streptococcus mutans, usually has a greater influence on kids, adolescents, and senior adults. Tooth decay is an irreversible process, explains Dr. Shalini Aggarwal, Professor, Department of Endodontics and Conservative Dentistry at Dr. DY Patil Dental College & Hospital in Pimpri, Pune. Dr. Aggarwal cautions that while these ingredients can't prevent or reverse decay, their excessive use can exacerbate damage to the tooth's remaining structure. Cardamom can provide mild antibacterial assistance when applied topically or consumed, but it cannot halt decay or replace research-based dental care. As a result, while the spice could assist with oral hygiene, it is not a miracle cure for tooth decay.

title: Fact Check: Can Celery Juice Help Reverse Tooth Decay?
claim_text: Celery Juice helps reverse tooth decay & receding gums
verdict_original: The claim is false. / Hence, the claim is FALSE.
quick_take: The idea that celery juice can reverse tooth decay is False. While celery has some oral health benefits, such as aiding saliva flow and being low in sugar, it does not have the ability to repair or regenerate tooth structure. Tooth decay is a progressive condition that requires professional dental care.
doctor_explanation:
Tooth decay starts when bacteria in the mouth produce acids that wear away the tooth's outer layer, known as enamel. Over time, this can create a small hole in the tooth, commonly referred to as a cavity. If left untreated, the decay can progress, leading to discomfort, infection, and potentially the loss of the affected tooth.

Tooth decay begins when teeth are frequently exposed to acids, often due to regular consumption of sugary or starchy foods and drinks. These acids cause the enamel to lose minerals. In the early stages, this results in a white spot on the tooth. At this point, the process can still be stopped or reversed, as enamel can repair itself by taking in minerals from saliva and fluoride. However, if the acid exposure continues and mineral loss worsens, the enamel becomes too weak and breaks down, forming a cavity. Once a cavity develops, the damage is permanent and must be treated by a dentist, usually with a filling.

While celery (Apium graveolens) is rich in phytochemicals like phenolic acids, flavonoids, and antioxidants such as vitamin C, beta-carotene, and manganese, and does offer oral health benefits such as stimulating saliva production, there is no scientific evidence that it can repair or regenerate decayed enamel. A study by Genatrika et al. concluded that celery-containing toothpastes can be used as natural antibacterial agents for the prevention of dental caries caused by Streptococcus mutans. Another article by Hayati et al. concluded that there is an inhibition effect of celery leaf extract toothpaste on the growth of Streptococcus mutans. However, these studies show celery may have mild antibacterial effects for prevention — not reversal of existing decay.

Dr Aravind Krishnan R, MDS, Consulting Orthodontist, Kerala told Medical Dialogues: 'Despite some viral claims, celery juice cannot cure tooth decay. Tooth decay is caused by bacterial damage to the enamel and dentin, requiring professional dental treatment such as fillings or fluoride therapy. While celery juice contains nutrients and hydration benefits, it lacks any proven remineralizing properties to reverse cavities. Relying on it as a cure can delay necessary care, worsening dental health. Always consult a dentist for evidence-based solutions.'

Dr. Sayantini Das, MDS, Consulting Pedodontist, Kolkata told Medical Dialogues: 'Celery juice is often promoted as a wellness elixir but there's no scientific evidence that it can reverse tooth decay. Tooth decay is caused by the breakdown of enamel due to acids produced by bacteria, and once enamel is lost, it doesn't grow back. However, celery itself can be beneficial for oral health — its high water content stimulates saliva production, which helps neutralize acids and rinse away food particles. Drinking celery juice isn't harmful in moderation, but it should never replace proven dental care practices like brushing, flossing, using fluoride, and regular dental check-ups.'

Once enamel is lost, it cannot be regenerated, and professional dental treatment is necessary to restore the damaged tooth structure.

title: Fact Check: Can certain herbs treat acne, hair fall, and PCOD?
claim_text: A concoction of saffron, elaichi (cardamom), ginger, ghee, and mulethi (licorice) can treat acne, tanning, hair fall, and PCOD symptoms.
quick_take: A social media post claims that certain herbs like saffron, elaichi, ginger, ghee and mulethi can treat acne, hair fall and PCOD. We did the fact check to term this claim as False.
doctor_explanation:
For Acne: No, there is no scientific evidence to support that this concoction can effectively treat acne. Acne has various causes like excess oil production, bacteria, clogged pores, and hormonal imbalances. Some of the ingredients like saffron and ginger are popular for their antioxidant properties, but there is no research that confirms their effectiveness in directly treating acne. Skincare treatments for acne usually involve topical retinoids, salicylic acid, or medical intervention depending on the severity. Dr Sachin Gupta, Dermatologist, Amrita Hospital, Faridabad, adds, "Acne is a medical condition that requires targeted care based on the individual's skin type and severity of the problem. It's essential to use evidence-based treatments like topical retinoids, benzoyl peroxide, or seek advice from a dermatologist for more persistent cases."

For Tanning: No, this home remedy likely can't treat or reverse tanning. When your skin is exposed to UV rays, it produces more melanin, which leads to tanning. Although some cultures have traditionally used saffron for skin brightening, it doesn't actually reverse tanning. UV rays from prolonged sun exposure harm the skin and cause damage. Some studies suggest that saffron offers anti-sun properties and may protect against UV rays. Research on animals and lab tests even show that saffron-based lotions could outperform homosalate as a natural sunscreen. Its antioxidants might also help prevent skin cancer (in an animal study). However, no conclusive evidence in humans proves that saffron can reverse or prevent tanning. The best ways to avoid tanning are using sunscreen with the right SPF, wearing protective clothing, and limiting sun exposure.

For Hair Fall: Not really. Hair fall can result from various factors, including genetics, hormonal changes, nutritional deficiencies, and stress. The claim that this concoction can prevent or treat hair fall is not supported by scientific research. While ginger and mulethi (licorice) have been suggested in traditional remedies for improving hair health, there is no solid evidence in humans to show they can effectively address hair fall. However, during our investigation, we found a few studies that highlight their potential. More research is needed to substantiate these anti-hair fall claims. For instance, a 2013 study on mice found that 6-gingerol, the active compound in ginger, actually suppresses hair growth rather than promoting it. On the other hand, lab tests and animal studies show that licorice may have the potential to promote hair growth. To manage hair loss, focus on eating well, reducing stress, and using proven treatments like minoxidil.

For PCOD: No, this concoction of common herbs cannot treat PCOD (Polycystic Ovarian Disease). It is a hormonal disorder that often requires a combination of lifestyle changes, medications, and sometimes hormonal treatments. Ingredients like saffron and mulethi have been used in traditional remedies for various health benefits. However, there's no clinical proof that they can treat PCOD symptoms like irregular periods, weight gain, or insulin resistance. Dr Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition, explains, "Some common herbs like saffron and ginger have antioxidant or anti-inflammatory properties. But, there is no strong scientific evidence to suggest that they can cure or effectively manage PCOD symptoms. To manage PCOD you need a balanced diet, regular exercise, and medical treatment based on individual needs. PCOD can only be controlled through lifestyle changes & medicines, if required. Don't overdo home remedies or google searches". Soumam Dutta, PhD Scholar in Nutrition from the Department of Endocrinology at the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition, says, "These spices and herbs are good for general health and wellbeing, as they are rich in beneficial phytochemicals having antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. However, more clinical trials are required to arrive at any conclusive evidence for their specific use in PCOD management."

Proven treatments: For acne, dermatologists recommend benzoyl peroxide, or consultation for severe cases. For tanning, apply sunscreen regularly and limit sun exposure. For hair fall, options like minoxidil or hair transplants are available. For PCOD, management involves diet changes, regular exercise, and medications like metformin or hormone treatments depending on doctor's recommendations.

title: Can charcoal toothpaste whiten teeth in 5 minutes? THIP Media
claim_text: A Facebook post displays an image titled, 'Great effect for teeth whitening' of a before and after effect of using charcoal toothpaste. It shows that the teeth miraculously turned white in 5 minutes.
quick_take: A social media post claims that charcoal toothpaste can whiten teeth in 5 minutes. We fact-checked and found this claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation:
The fact check addresses whether charcoal toothpaste can whiten teeth in 5 minutes. First, it explains that the natural color of teeth can vary naturally, usually from light to medium shade of yellow or grayish-yellow, influenced by genetics, age, diet, and oral hygiene. The color may darken over time and stains may appear on both the surface and within the dentine. There are three main categories of tooth stains: internal, external, and age-related. External staining is caused by consumption of foods, beverages, and tobacco products. Internal tooth staining can be brought on by tooth decay, injury, and certain medications.

Regarding the claim, there is no scientific evidence to prove that charcoal toothpaste can whiten teeth in 5 minutes. Firstly, it takes a few weeks of regular use to see any noticeable difference, and that occurs only because charcoal toothpaste is mildly abrasive, which can help remove surface stains. However, it does not have any effect on stains below the enamel. In order to whiten teeth, a product needs to work on both surface and intrinsic stains. Activated charcoal is a common component of teeth-whitening toothpaste, but there isn't any substantial proof that it works to whiten teeth. The charcoal is a fine-grained powder made from wood, coconut shells, and other natural materials that have been oxidized at high temperatures and might serve as an occasional surface cleaner. But, using it for a long period of time could harm enamel because of its abrasive nature. Furthermore, it can also result in tooth sensitivity, staining, and cavity fillings dislodgement.

Dr. Pratyasa Bagchi, our dental expert, about whether activated charcoal could whiten teeth, cautioned that there was no proof that activated charcoal whitened teeth. The fact that activated charcoal acts as an abrasive cannot be ignored, despite the fact that it has been widely used in toothpastes for teeth whitening. However, while it undoubtedly gets rid of some surface stains, it cannot stop severe stains like yellowing or plaque development. Thus, it should only be used in moderation under the guidance of your dentist.

Dr. Aashnaa Pillai, BDS, FILD, confirms this and says, "Whitening toothpaste contains abrasive agents that are meant to scratch the external surface of your teeth to give them a shinier and whiter appearance. Prolonged use of such abrasive agents can eventually cause thinning of the enamel, the hardest part of your tooth that does not grow back. This can lead to tooth sensitivity and the risk of developing dental caries."

The effectiveness of charcoal toothpaste can vary from person to person. Some people may see noticeable improvements in teeth whiteness, while others may not experience significant changes. Additionally, its effectiveness depends on the cause of the discoloration. Surface stains caused by food, drinks, and smoking can often be removed with abrasives, such as charcoal toothpastes. However, deeper or intrinsic stains caused by certain medications or trauma may not respond to such agents and may require professional teeth whitening treatments.

Preventative measures: Only external stains can be avoided, whereas internal stains affect the internal structure of the teeth and are challenging to prevent. Tooth discoloration can be avoided by eating a high-fibre diet, drinking lots of water, and brushing and flossing on a regular basis. Avoiding smoking, consuming acidic juices and beverages, and limiting the consumption of foods and beverages that can stain teeth, such as cola, coffee, and red wine, are additional preventive measures. Trying out unproven remedies, such as cleaning teeth with lemon and baking soda can do more damage than good.

title: Fact Check: Can Charcoal Whiten Teeth?
claim_text: Activated charcoal naturally whitens teeth. The method involves opening an activated charcoal capsule into a small jar or bowl, wetting the toothbrush, dipping it into the charcoal powder, brushing the teeth for 3-5 minutes, rinsing the mouth, and brushing with toothpaste to remove remaining charcoal. This process is suggested to be done daily for 3-5 days to achieve desired results, and for maintenance, it can be repeated every few months, possibly with the change of seasons.
doctor_explanation: Medical Dialogues Fact Check team spoke with Dr. Satender Singh, Dentist at Sanjeevan Hospital New Delhi, who said: "Charcoal-based toothpastes have gained significant popularity in recent years, particularly due to their ability to remove surface stains like those caused by coffee, tea, or turmeric. While these products may offer a temporary improvement in the appearance of teeth, it is crucial to understand that there is no substantial scientific evidence supporting their effectiveness in actual teeth whitening. They primarily work by scrubbing off surface stains rather than changing the natural color of the teeth. Another important consideration is the abrasive nature of charcoal-based toothpastes. Regular use of these products can lead to erosion of tooth enamel, which does not regenerate. This enamel loss can make teeth more susceptible to sensitivity, decay, and discoloration over time. Additionally, for those with dental restorations like composite fillings or veneers, charcoal toothpaste can roughen the surface, affecting the aesthetics and longevity of these restorations. In light of these risks, I advise patients to exercise caution with charcoal-based toothpaste. If you are seeking a whitening solution, it's best to consult a dentist for safer, clinically tested alternatives. Professional treatments or whitening products approved by dental professionals are far more effective and less likely to cause harm." Dr. Nandita Mohan added: "Charcoal-based toothpastes have become popular for their stain-removal abilities, especially for tea and coffee stains. However, there is little scientific backing to suggest they can whiten teeth effectively. Moreover, their abrasive nature raises concerns about potential damage to enamel and dental restorations over time. While they may offer temporary cosmetic benefits, they are not a long-term solution for teeth whitening. I encourage patients to consult their dentist before using charcoal toothpastes and to consider safer, clinically proven whitening methods at dental office." Scientific evidence cited: An article in the International Journal of Dentistry (PMC10188264) reported that charcoal-containing toothpaste may enhance the color of enamel and resin composites without compromising microhardness, but noted potential for roughening of composite restorations. A study by Aldridge J Fernandes et al. (PMC10351494) revealed that charcoal-based whitening dentifrice, non-charcoal-based whitening dentifrice, and distilled water were all equally effective in removing coffee stains — the color change from charcoal was NOT significantly different from non-charcoal products or even plain water. Dolores Bibiana Montero Tomás et al. (PubMed: 36183933) found that activated charcoal toothpastes have a weaker whitening effect compared to other options and are considered less safe due to high abrasiveness. The American Dental Association has raised concerns about the long-term safety and effectiveness of charcoal for teeth whitening. Historical context: While charcoal use for teeth whitening dates back to ancient Egypt, Greece, and Rome (Hippocrates and Pliny the Elder documented its oral care use — PMC4263393), modern scientific scrutiny shows the abrasive nature of charcoal can erode tooth enamel over time. Ayurvedic practices in India also used charcoal for oral detoxification (PMC3705899), but this traditional use does not equate to proven whitening efficacy.

title: Fact Check: Can chia seeds burn belly fat and clear your skin?
claim_text: Eating chia seeds will burn belly fat, boost digestion, support heart health, and clear the skin
quick_take: A social media post suggests using chia seeds for fat loss and calls them a "superfood" that can burn belly fat, boost digestion, support heart health, and even clear the skin. After fact checking, we have termed this claim mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Chia seeds alone won't magically melt away fat. They are very high in fibre and help you feel full, which can assist weight control. A 6-month study from 2017 found slightly more weight loss and waist reduction in people eating chia seeds than in a control group. However, major reviews note that human trials generally show no clear weight-loss benefit from chia. Belly fat is lost by overall calorie control and exercise, not by a single "fat-burning" seed. Clinical Dietitian Melanie Dsouza says, "Chia seeds can be a healthy part of a weight loss plan, but they are not a magic solution on their own. A qualified dietitian would never recommend just chia seeds for fat loss. Any weight management plan should be based on a balanced, personalised diet that considers a person's medical history and nutritional needs. Quick-fix approaches may seem appealing, but they often lead to imbalanced nutrition, upset gut health, and even long-term health problems if followed unsupervised." Shruti K. Bhardwaj, Chief Clinical Nutritionist at Zydus Hospital, Ahmedabad, states, "Yes, chia seeds are rich in fibre and nutrients. But no single food or drink, including chia seeds for fat loss, can trigger weight loss by itself. A healthy diet combined with regular exercise and portion control is what works. Also, using words like 'fast' or 'quick' in the context of weight loss is misleading. Sustainable fat loss takes time, and it's best to get guidance from a certified professional who can build a diet plan based on your body composition and overall health." On digestion: chia seeds are rich in dietary fibre, which helps digestion. When eaten with water, they swell and form a gel that softens stool and helps prevent constipation. On heart health: chia seeds contain heart-healthy nutrients including soluble fibre and omega-3 fats (ALA), which are linked to lower cholesterol and heart disease risk. However, results have been mixed - one older trial in overweight adults saw no change in cholesterol, blood pressure or inflammation after chia supplementation. On skin: there is no strong evidence that eating chia seeds will give clear skin. While chia seeds contain omega-3 fats and zinc which generally support health and reduce inflammation, Dr Rashi Soni, Consultant Dermatologist at Rashi Hospital, Mumbai, explains: "Chia seeds are rich in omega-3 fatty acids and antioxidants, which can support overall skin health. These nutrients help reduce inflammation in the body, and in theory, that may have some indirect benefit for the skin. But eating chia seeds alone will not clear acne or other skin conditions. Clear skin depends on many factors like hormones, skincare habits, diet, sleep, and stress levels. Including chia seeds in a balanced diet can be helpful, but they are not a cure or a replacement for proper dermatological treatment." In summary, chia seeds are indeed nutritious and can be part of a healthy diet, but they are not a magic bullet for burning belly fat or curing skin issues.

title: Fact Check: Can chicken cause cancer and UTIs? - THIP Media
claim_text: Stop eating chicken. Chicken causes pancreas cancer, liver cancer, urinary tract infections, contamination with fecal matter.
quick_take: A social media post claims eating chicken can cause cancer and Urinary Tract Infections. We fact-checked and found this claim to be Half-true.
doctor_explanation: CAN CONSUMING CHICKEN CAUSE UTI? Sometimes. It is possible for chicken to contribute to the development of urinary tract infections (UTIs), but it is not a direct cause always. Eating contaminated meat or food does not directly lead to a UTI. While some types of E. coli can cause serious intestinal disease, most of these E. coli bacteria can live in the intestine without causing problems. UTIs are typically caused by bacteria, such as E. coli, entering the urinary tract and causing an infection. Poultry are considered to be a major source of the bacteria that cause urinary tract infections (UTIs) in people. Chicken can be a source of bacteria that may contribute to the development of UTIs if it is not cooked or handled properly. If chicken is not cooked to the appropriate temperature or is not stored at the correct temperature, harmful bacteria such as Salmonella and Campylobacter can be present. These bacteria can cause foodborne illness, including UTIs if they are not properly eliminated from the body. Furthermore, a research published by the University of Minnesota stated that ST131 sublineage of E coli, multidrug-resistant E coli strain can serve as a vehicle for human exposure and UTI. Antibiotic-resistant bacteria in chicken can escape our digestive system and travel into the urinary system. To minimize the risk of developing a UTI, it is important to practice good food safety habits, such as washing your hands thoroughly before and after handling raw chicken, cooking chicken to the appropriate temperature, and refrigerating or freezing chicken promptly after purchasing it. Additionally, drinking plenty of water and urinating regularly can help flush out any bacteria that may have entered the urinary tract. CAN CONSUMING CHICKEN CAUSE CANCER? Not always. There is currently no conclusive evidence that chicken will definitely cause cancer. This has been a debatable matter and the way chicken is cooked or processed can affect its potential to increase the risk of cancer. A study concluded that enhanced intake of white meat or poultry was found to be negatively associated with some types of cancers. There have been studies which even state that the consumption of poultry may even lead to a decreased risk of certain types of cancer. On the other hand, another research states that eating chicken is associated with an increased risk of cancers, such as, malignant melanoma, prostate cancer and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. Grilling, frying, or barbecuing chicken at high temperatures can produce harmful chemicals called heterocyclic amines (HCAs) and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). These chemicals have been linked to an increased risk of cancer, particularly colon, stomach, and prostate cancer. Additionally, processed chicken products may contain preservatives and additives that have been associated with an increased risk of cancer. To reduce the risk of potentially harmful effects from chicken, it is recommended to cook it at lower temperatures, use gentler cooking methods such as boiling, casseroling or microwave heating rather than high-temperature grilling, barbecuing or pan-frying. It's important to maintain a balanced and varied diet that includes a variety of foods, including vegetables and fruits, to maintain good health.

title: Can chlorine dioxide cure dozens of health conditions? - THIP Media
claim_text: Chlorine dioxide cures dozens of health conditions
quick_take: A social media post claims that chlorine dioxide can cure dozens of health conditions. We fact-checked and found the claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: Chlorine dioxide (ClO2) is a chemical compound composed of one chlorine atom and two oxygen atoms. It is a yellow to reddish-yellow gas at room temperature and pressure, and it dissolves easily in water. Chlorine dioxide is a powerful oxidising agent and biocide, meaning it can effectively kill bacteria, viruses, and other microorganisms. It is often used as a disinfectant in water treatment processes, particularly for municipal water supplies and in industries such as food processing and healthcare. Chlorine dioxide has several advantages over other disinfectants like chlorine bleach. It is effective over a wide pH range, it does not produce harmful disinfection byproducts like chlorinated compounds can, and it does not leave a residual taste or odor in treated water when used properly. However, it is important to handle chlorine dioxide with care, as it can be hazardous in concentrated form and should only be used according to recommended guidelines and safety precautions. Chlorine dioxide is NOT safe for human consumption. Ingesting chlorine dioxide can cause serious health problems, including irritation and corrosion of the gastrointestinal tract, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and even damage to the red blood cells, leading to potential organ failure and death in severe cases. Chlorine dioxide was also touted as a cure for COVID-19 during the peak of the outbreak. However, this is not the case. Despite some misleading claims online, chlorine dioxide is not a safe or effective treatment for any medical condition when ingested. It is essential to follow the advice of healthcare professionals and avoid ingesting substances like chlorine dioxide that are not intended for human consumption. Chlorine dioxide cannot cure dozens of health conditions. While it is used in very small, controlled amounts to disinfect water, it is unsafe and harmful for human consumption. Taking large doses of chlorine dioxide, sometimes sold under the name Miracle Mineral Solution (MMS), can cause serious health problems. Chlorine dioxide mixed into mouthwash has been studied for fighting dental infections and reducing the amount of virus in the saliva of people with SARS-CoV-2. What you're doing is injuring the skin, not treating the wart. This can lead to burns, infection, scarring, or even worsening of the condition. Safe and effective wart treatments are available, including salicylic acid, cryotherapy, or minor procedures done under medical supervision. I strongly advise people not to use such home remedies with caustic substances." Dr Almas Fatma, Diploma in Family Medicine, PG in Digital Health, General Physician from Navi Mumbai, says, "Quick lime, or choona, is not only unsafe for the skin, but it's also dangerous. Many people try these harmful home remedies thinking they're simple solutions, but they often make things worse. For any skin condition, including warts, it's best to stick to clinically proven treatments or consult a healthcare professional. Home remedies with harsh chemicals are never a safe option." Applying quick lime on the skin is not safe. Quick lime reacts with water and produces a significant amount of heat. When applied to skin, it can lead to irritation, blisters, or even serious burns. Wart removal is not instant, even with medical treatment. Medical options for wart treatment include cryotherapy (freezing), salicylic acid applications, laser therapy, or minor surgical removal. These treatments usually require days to weeks to fully clear the wart. Even cryotherapy, often considered fast, takes several days for the wart to dry up and fall off after freezing. doctor_explanation: There is no conclusive scientific evidence that cilantro and chlorella together can effectively remove heavy metals at the claimed levels. Cilantro (also called coriander) and chlorella (a green algae) are often touted for their supposed detoxification properties. Advocates claim they bind to heavy metals in the body and facilitate their removal. However, most studies supporting these claims are either limited to animal models, in vitro experiments, or lack robust methodologies. For example, a 2017 study in mice suggested cilantro might help remove lead when combined with other treatments, but these findings cannot be directly applied to humans. Similarly, while chlorella is rich in nutrients and has shown some potential for binding heavy metals in test tubes, its effectiveness as a chelating agent in the human body remains unproven. The human digestive system may not allow chlorella to digest because of the cellulose wall in the same way it does in controlled laboratory settings, limiting its real-world application. Soumam Dutta, PhD Scholar (Nutrition), Department of Endocrinology, ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition, said, 'There is no solid scientific evidence to support the claim that cilantro and chlorella can effectively remove heavy metals at the levels often advertised. Effective heavy metal detox requires medically supervised chelation therapy.' Chelation therapy is a medical treatment specifically designed to remove heavy metals from the body. It involves the use of synthetic chelating agents, such as EDTA, that bind to metals like lead or mercury, enabling their excretion through urine. This process is closely monitored by healthcare professionals due to potential risks, including kidney damage and mineral imbalances. The claim that cilantro and chlorella can achieve similar results lacks substantial evidence. No credible studies to date have demonstrated that cilantro and chlorella can achieve the dramatic removal percentages stated in the claim (87% of lead, 91% of mercury, and 74% of aluminium). Liver and kidneys primarily handle the detoxification in the body, which naturally filter and eliminate toxins when functioning properly. Nutrient-dense foods like cilantro and chlorella may support overall health but should not be mistaken for proven medical treatments. Relying solely on these remedies can delay effective treatment and pose health risks. Heavy metal poisoning is a serious condition requiring professional medical attention. Symptoms can range from fatigue and headaches to more severe issues like neurological damage and organ failure. Self-treating with unverified remedies like cilantro and chlorella may lead to delays in seeking proper medical care, exacerbating health problems. Additionally, consuming large amounts of these foods in hopes of achieving detoxification can cause side effects. For example, chlorella supplements may lead to digestive discomfort or allergic reactions in some individuals. There is also the risk of contamination in poorly regulated supplements, which might ironically introduce heavy metals into the body.

title: Can Cinnamon cure knee pain in 24 hours? - THIP Media
claim_text: A Facebook video features Dr. Biswaroop Roy Chowdhury claiming that one spoonful of cinnamon can cure knee pain within 24 hours.
quick_take: A social media post claims that consuming cinnamon can cure knee pain in just 24 hrs. We fact checked and found the claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: No, it can't. There's no reliable scientific evidence showing that cinnamon can cure or even significantly reduce knee pain in a single day. Cinnamon comes from the bark of the Cinnamomum tree and is packed with compounds like cinnamaldehyde, which have anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. These properties sound promising, but they don't translate to a quick fix for knee pain. Knee discomfort often stems from complex issues, think arthritis, torn ligaments, or overuse injuries. These conditions involve inflammation, tissue damage, or structural problems that a home remedy or a single spice simply can't resolve in 24 hours. Studies on cinnamon's effects are mostly lab-based or focused on general inflammation, not specific joint pain relief in humans. Some research suggests cinnamon could have mild anti-inflammatory effects. For instance, a 2015 study in Food & Function found that cinnamon extracts reduced inflammation markers in animal models. Another small study in Nutrition Research (2018) noted that cinnamon supplements slightly lowered inflammation in people with chronic conditions, but it wasn't specific to joints or knees. These effects, if real, would take weeks or months to show up, not hours. Plus, human studies on cinnamon for joint health are scarce and inconclusive. So, while it's not harmful to sprinkle some cinnamon on your porridge, don't expect it to overhaul your creaky knees. Cinnamon itself is safe in small amounts, but overdoing it, especially Cassia cinnamon, can lead to problems. It contains coumarin, which, in large doses, might stress your liver. The real danger, though, is ignoring proper treatment. Knee pain could signal serious conditions like rheumatoid arthritis. If you skip seeing a doctor and bet on cinnamon instead, you might let the problem worsen. For example, untreated osteoarthritis can damage your joint permanently. Time and money spent on unproven remedies could delay the care you actually need. Dr Smit Dave, an Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sterling and Orthocure Hospitals in Ahmedabad, states that total knee replacement is the only effective solution for severe knee arthritis. He cautions that oils, creams, gels, or home remedies provide only short-term relief and are not cures. Dr Dave advises against believing unverified social media claims promoting creams or gels as alternatives to surgery for knee repair.

title: Can cinnamon, ginger, turmeric, and lemon cure PCOS in a month?
claim_text: A social media claim says that combining cinnamon, ginger, turmeric, and lemon can completely cure PCOS in just one month. The Instagram page promotes this homemade drink as a quick-fix solution for managing the condition.
quick_take: A social media post suggests that drinking a mixture of cinnamon, ginger, turmeric, and lemon can cure PCOS within a month. We fact checked and found the claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: Can a mixture of cinnamon, ginger, turmeric, and lemon cure PCOS in a month? No. There is no credible scientific evidence supporting the idea that this specific blend can cure PCOS, let alone in such a short timeframe. PCOS is a chronic endocrine disorder driven by complex factors, including insulin resistance, elevated androgen (male hormone) levels, and genetic predispositions. These lead to symptoms like ovarian cysts, irregular menstrual cycles, and metabolic issues, which cannot be fully resolved in 30 days. Research on herbal remedies, such as a study comparing cinnamon and ginger to metformin (a common PCOS medication), showed modest improvements in insulin sensitivity after 8–12 weeks, but these were not cures. The idea of a rapid fix ignores the intricate hormonal and metabolic imbalances at play. Such claims can mislead women, potentially delaying proper medical care and fostering unrealistic expectations about recovery. Dr Saumya, a specialist in Obstetrics and Gynaecology at ESIC Medical College & Hospital, Patna, clarifies that PCOS and PCOD are long-term conditions influenced by hormonal imbalances and genetics, as supported by findings in the Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism (2020). While symptoms such as irregular periods, weight gain, and excess hair growth can be managed, the underlying condition remains. Although treatments like medication, lifestyle adjustments, and diet can help women manage symptoms well, fenugreek or other home remedies cannot address the root cause of these disorders. Do these ingredients have any benefits for PCOS symptoms? Yes, but their effects are supportive, not curative. Each ingredient in the mixture has been studied for potential health benefits, some of which align with PCOS symptom management, but their impact is limited and gradual. Cinnamon, or dalchini, has shown promise in reducing insulin resistance, a core issue in PCOS that contributes to weight gain and irregular periods. A 2014 clinical trial found that daily cinnamon supplementation lowered blood sugar levels in women with PCOS over 8 weeks, mimicking some effects of diabetes medications. Ginger, similarly, has anti-inflammatory properties and may aid in weight management, with one study noting improved hormonal profiles in women with PCOS after three months of use alongside other interventions. Turmeric's active compound, curcumin, is well-regarded for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects, which could help reduce chronic inflammation linked to PCOS, as highlighted in a 2023 review of human trials. Lemon, while rich in vitamin C and antioxidants, lacks robust evidence directly tied to PCOS; however, animal studies suggest lemon peel extracts may support ovarian health, though human data is scarce. Together, these ingredients might form a soothing tea or supplement that supports overall wellness, but their benefits are incremental and best used as part of a broader, medically supervised plan. Why is PCOS so difficult to treat quickly? PCOS is not a simple condition that can be eradicated with a single remedy. It stems from a mix of genetic, hormonal, and environmental factors, leading to a unique combination of symptoms for each individual. Insulin resistance, for instance, drives excess androgen production, which disrupts ovulation and causes issues like acne and hirsutism (excessive hair growth). These processes are deeply embedded and require sustained effort to manage. Even medical treatments, such as oral contraceptives to regulate periods or anti-androgen drugs to address hair growth, take months to show significant results. Lifestyle changes, like adopting a low-glycaemic diet or increasing physical activity, can improve insulin sensitivity by up to 30% over time, according to research, but these too are gradual. The notion of a one-month cure oversimplifies a condition that often persists throughout a woman's reproductive years, requiring ongoing care to manage effectively. What are the most effective ways to manage PCOS symptoms? Managing PCOS effectively involves a tailored, long-term approach under professional guidance. Lifestyle changes are a cornerstone: studies show that losing 5–10% of body weight through a balanced diet low in processed sugars and regular exercise (such as 30 minutes of brisk walking or yoga daily) can significantly improve insulin resistance and menstrual regularity. Medications like metformin address blood sugar issues, while hormonal therapies, such as combined oral contraceptives, help regulate cycles and reduce symptoms like acne. For women seeking to conceive, fertility treatments like clomiphene or assisted reproductive technologies, such as in vitro fertilisation, are evidence-based options. Incorporating anti-inflammatory foods, including the spices in this remedy, can complement these efforts, turmeric in curries or cinnamon in oatmeal, for example, but they should not replace prescribed treatments. Always consult a healthcare provider before starting supplements, as high doses of ingredients like turmeric can interact with medications or cause side effects like stomach upset. Regular monitoring through blood tests, ultrasounds, and check-ups ensures progress is tracked and adjustments are made as needed. Are there risks in relying on this remedy alone? Yes. Relying solely on a home remedy like this risks delaying proper diagnosis and treatment, which can worsen PCOS symptoms over time. Untreated insulin resistance, for example, increases the risk of type 2 diabetes, while irregular ovulation can complicate fertility. Moreover, unverified remedies may lead to inconsistent dosing, too much cinnamon, for instance, can affect liver function in rare cases. Women may also feel discouraged if the promised cure fails, potentially impacting their mental health. A holistic approach, combining evidence-based medical care with sensible lifestyle tweaks, offers the best path forward.

title: Fact Check: Can Cinnamon Powder, Warm Water and Apple Cider Vinegar Fix Diabetes Overnight?
claim_text: Cinnamon Powder, Warm Water and Apple Cider Vinegar can Fix Diabetes Overnight. Before bedtime mix one teaspoon of cinnamon powder in a glass of warm water and add a tbsp of apple cider vinegar. Stir this well and drink this mixture to take advantage of cinnamon's ability to improve insulin sensitivity and apple cider vinegar has the potential to lower blood sugar levels. Additionally consume a small handful of soaked fenugreek seeds which are known for their glucose-lowering properties. This combination can aid in maintaining stable blood sugars overnight which supports overall diabetes management.
verdict_original: This claim is False. Cinnamon Powder, Warm Water and Apple Cider Vinegar cannot Fix Diabetes Overnight.
doctor_explanation:
Dr. J. Rajesh Kumar, Senior Consultant & Diabetologist, MD (Internal Medicine), Prashanth Hospitals, said: "Diabetes is a complex, chronic condition that cannot be cured or managed effectively overnight with any single remedy, including cinnamon powder, warm water, and apple cider vinegar. While cinnamon may have a modest effect on lowering blood sugar levels, this impact is minimal and should not be considered a substitute for comprehensive diabetes management. Similarly, apple cider vinegar might slightly influence post-meal blood sugar levels, but its effects are limited and certainly not curative. Warm water, though beneficial for overall hydration, does not have any direct or meaningful impact on blood sugar control. The notion that these three ingredients together could 'fix' diabetes overnight is not only misleading but also dangerous, as it might encourage individuals to abandon proven medical treatments in favor of unproven, anecdotal remedies. Effective diabetes management requires a consistent approach, including a balanced diet, regular exercise, and, in many cases, prescribed medications. Patients must consult doctors before making any significant changes to their treatment plans, rather than relying on oversimplified and unsupported claims."

Dr. Divya Tripathi, Assistant Professor, Department of Nutrition and Dietetics, Manav Rachna International Institute of Research and Studies, said: "As a dietitian, I must emphasize that the claim that cinnamon powder, warm water, and apple cider vinegar can fix diabetes overnight is entirely false and misleading. Diabetes is a chronic condition that demands consistent management through a balanced diet, regular physical activity, and often prescribed medications. While cinnamon is rich in antioxidants and contains compounds like cinnamaldehyde, which may help improve insulin sensitivity and reduce inflammation, these effects are modest and should not be viewed as a cure. Apple cider vinegar also offers some nutritional benefits, such as acetic acid, which may help lower post-meal blood sugar spikes and support digestion, but these effects are limited. Warm water aids in hydration, which is essential for overall health, but it has no direct impact on diabetes. Relying solely on these ingredients for diabetes treatment is not just ineffective, but also potentially dangerous. Proper diabetes management requires a comprehensive and professional approach."

The article further explains: Diabetes is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by high blood sugar levels due to either insufficient insulin production or the body's inability to use insulin effectively. While lifestyle changes, medications, and dietary adjustments can help manage diabetes, it is considered a lifelong condition that cannot be cured. Nothing can fix diabetes overnight. An article by Robert W. Allen in the Annals of Family Medicine reported that consuming cinnamon is linked to a statistically significant reduction in fasting plasma glucose, total cholesterol, LDL-C, and triglyceride levels, as well as an increase in HDL-C levels; however, it did not show a significant impact on hemoglobin A1c. A systematic review and meta-analysis published in BMC Complementary Medicine and Therapy suggested that Apple Cider Vinegar consumption may positively influence adults' glycemic control and lipid levels, but also noted side effects such as stomach burning and ACV intolerance, and concluded that further research is required. Another study by Tine Launholt et al. concluded that the evidence for the health benefits of Apple Cider Vinegar is insufficient due to a lack of high-quality research. There might be studies that show the benefits of these ingredients in lowering blood sugar, but no evidence could be found that supported these ingredients as first-line therapy for treatment of diabetes, nor is there any evidence that these can fix diabetes in a particularly time frame that too overnight. While cinnamon might help reduce certain cardiovascular risks, it does not significantly affect hemoglobin A1c, a critical indicator of long-term blood sugar control. The notion that these natural remedies can 'cure' diabetes is not backed by solid scientific evidence. Medical Dialogues' final take states: "While there is some evidence suggesting that cinnamon powder and apple cider vinegar may have benefits in managing certain metabolic markers, such as fasting glucose and lipid levels, the notion that they can cure diabetes is unsupported by scientific evidence. Diabetes is a chronic and complex condition that requires comprehensive management, including lifestyle changes, medication, and regular monitoring under the guidance of healthcare professionals. Claims that cinnamon or apple cider vinegar can fix diabetes or provide significant benefits without additional interventions are misleading and lack scientific evidence. There is no evidence that these can fix diabetes overnight."

title: Can clove, alum, ajwain and neem water cure all oral problems?
claim_text: A viral Instagram video advises people to fill a glass jar with half a litre of water, add alum (phitkari), 8–10 cloves, one tablespoon of ajwain, and a neem twig with leaves. The mix should be left for two days and then used to rinse the mouth twice daily. The video claims this remedy can relieve all kinds of oral problems—ranging from sensitivity and ulcers to cavities, pyorrhoea, and pus from gums. The person in the video adds, "Try it, you will feel relieved after the second use only!"
quick_take: A social media post claims that clove, alum, ajwain, and neem water can cure all oral problems. After fact checking, we found that this claim is mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Can this mixture of cloves, alum, carom seeds and neem in water cure all oral problems? No, it cannot cure all oral problems. There is no universal remedy for every dental issue. Toothaches, cavities, bleeding gums, and ulcers have different causes and require different treatments. For example, a cavity is a bacterial infection that damages the structure of the tooth and often needs cleaning and filling by a dentist. Sensitivity may need a desensitising toothpaste or fluoride application. Bleeding gums could point to gum disease, which may need professional cleaning and antibiotics. Home remedies like this herbal mix cannot replace professional dental care. Along similar lines, some claims suggest that a mix of mustard oil, salt, and turmeric can prevent all dental diseases. Others promote combinations like rock salt, alum, cloves, and mustard oil as cures for every dental issue. However, none of these claims hold true. Do the ingredients have any proven benefits for oral health? Yes, a few of these ingredients may provide mild relief for minor oral issues. However, there is no strong scientific evidence to support their effectiveness in treating serious dental conditions. While these herbs might provide a short-term soothing effect, they are not substitutes for proper dental care. Homemade mixtures like this lack standardisation in preparation, dosage, and concentration. Importantly, the effectiveness of such remedies depends on how the ingredients are processed and combined — something the viral video does not explain. Dr Annusuiya Gohil, MD Scholar at the All India Institute of Ayurveda, states, "Ayurveda texts do include detailed information on dental care, and we study this in our undergraduate curriculum. In fact, there's even an MD specialisation in Shalakya Tantra, which includes dental sciences. But such vague social media claims are not correct. The way herbs are prepared and used matters. Broadly saying they can cure all dental issues without specifics is misleading." Dr Gohil adds, "Moreover, it is incorrect to suggest that all dental problems — especially serious conditions like pyorrhoea — can be cured with a generalised herbal rinse. If someone claims support from Ayurvedic texts, they must provide the exact reference or shlok, so trained Ayurvedic professionals can interpret it correctly and advise accordingly." Likewise, some people claim that a mouthwash made from bay leaf, clove, and lemon can cure toothaches at home. This is too misleading. Can this homemade rinse treat cavities or pus from gums? No, it cannot treat infections or structural damage. Cavities and pus in gums (which may indicate an abscess or advanced gum disease) require professional diagnosis and intervention. These are bacterial infections that do not heal with herbal rinses. Delaying proper treatment may lead to serious complications like tooth loss, bone infection, or spreading of the infection to other parts of the body. Dr Snigdha, BDS, MDS, from Vananchal Dental College and Hospital, Garhwa, Jharkhand, says, "No, a homemade mouth rinse like this cannot treat cavities or infections that cause pus from the gums. Cavities are permanent damage to the tooth structure and need proper dental treatment like fillings. Pus from gums usually indicates an advanced infection such as periodontitis, which requires professional care. Rinsing with herbs may provide temporary relief, but it will not address the root cause or stop the damage." Similarly, we have debunked claims that coconut oil, cloves and salt mixture can cure all dental issues. Can such home remedies delay needed dental care? Yes, and this can be harmful. Relying on unverified remedies may give a false sense of relief and cause people to postpone necessary treatment. Dental diseases often progress silently. For example, early gum disease may not hurt but can lead to severe bone damage if left untreated. Home rinses may mask symptoms temporarily but won't stop the disease process. Dr Pooja Sharma, BDS, MDS, from NIMS University, Jaipur, Rajasthan, explains, "Yes, home remedies can sometimes do more harm than good—not because the ingredients are dangerous, but because they give the impression that professional care isn't needed. Dental problems like cavities or gum infections don't heal on their own. They need proper diagnosis and targeted treatment. By delaying care, what starts as a small issue could turn into severe pain, swelling, or even tooth loss. It's always safer to see a dentist early rather than wait until things get worse." THIP Media Take: The claim that clove, alum, ajwain and neem water can cure all oral problems is mostly false. While some ingredients may have minor benefits, they cannot cure dental diseases like cavities, gum infections, or ulcers. Oral health issues need proper diagnosis and treatment by qualified dental professionals. Relying on this kind of remedy can delay necessary care and lead to complications. Always consult a dentist for persistent or painful dental symptoms.
