title: Fact Check: Can dirty chai bring down cholesterol levels?
claim_text: As per an article on a website called Herzindagi, a tea coffee mix drink is good for health. And, it can bring down bad cholesterol levels.
quick_take: An article claims that a tea coffee mix drink can lower cholesterol levels. We did the fact check and found out it is false.
doctor_explanation: Dirty Chai is a popular beverage that combines the flavours and ingredients of traditional masala chai and espresso. It is made with masala black tea, steamed milk, and a shot of espresso, creating a unique blend of tea and coffee. This tea coffee mix drink is known by various names, including Espresso Chai, Red Eye Chai, and Chai Charger. It is consumed hot throughout the day and can also be enjoyed cold. Many people appreciate dirty chai for its refreshing taste and the energising kick from the espresso. Dirty chai, or the tea coffee mix drink, like many beverages, may have certain health benefits due to its ingredients. Masala chai contains black tea, which is rich in antioxidants called polyphenols that can support heart health and may reduce inflammation. The spices in masala chai, such as ginger, cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves, have various health-promoting properties, including anti-inflammatory and digestive benefits. The addition of espresso provides caffeine, which can improve alertness and cognitive function. However, it's essential to note that the health benefits depend on the quantity and quality of the ingredients used, as well as how the drink is prepared. The addition of sweeteners and high-fat dairy can reduce the potential health benefits of dirty chai. Can dirty chai really bring down bad cholesterol levels? No, there is no scientific evidence to support the claim that dirty chai can lower bad cholesterol levels. While some components of the tea coffee mix drink, such as black tea and certain spices, are associated with heart health, including potential cholesterol-lowering effects. These benefits are usually modest and part of a broader, balanced diet and healthy lifestyle. Expert opinion from Dr. Ubaid ur Rahman, General Physician at Holy Mission Clinic, New Delhi: 'I can tell you that consuming coffee or tea can significantly enhance your alertness and energy levels for several hours. The caffeine in these drinks stimulates the central nervous system, which can improve focus, reduce fatigue temporarily, and provide a temporary boost in mental and physical performance. Dirty chai, which combines the benefits of both tea and espresso, can offer a strong caffeine boost that may enhance these effects.' Dr Rahman further informs, 'But, it's important to be mindful of the potential negative effects too. Excessive consumption of caffeine can lead to jitteriness, increased heart rate, anxiety, digestive issues, and sleep disturbances. Additionally, the sugar and high-fat content in some dirty chai preparations can contribute to weight gain, raised cholesterol levels and other health issues if consumed regularly. It's best to enjoy these drinks in moderation and be aware of your body's response to caffeine and other ingredients. Also, one must avoid having tea or coffee after meals or with meals.' Side effects discussed include: Caffeine Content risks from high caffeine intake; Sugar Content from added sweeteners; Dairy Content considerations; Allergies and Sensitivities to spices like cinnamon, ginger, and cardamom which can cause allergies leading to skin rashes, itching, or respiratory issues; Interactions with Medications with certain ingredients. Bad cholesterol refers to low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol. LDL cholesterol is considered 'bad' because high levels can lead to the buildup of plaque in the arteries, which increases the risk of heart disease and stroke. Plaque is a fatty substance that can narrow or block arteries, leading to cardiovascular problems. Actual recommendations for bringing down bad cholesterol include lifestyle changes and, in some cases, medications. A balanced diet plays a pivotal role in managing cholesterol levels. Including a variety of nutrient-rich foods and reducing the intake of unhealthy fats (trans fats and saturated fats) is effective. Choosing heart-healthy options like physical activity and proper sleep can collectively contribute to better cholesterol management. So, choosing black tea or herbal tea without the milk and sugar is a much better option. THIP Media Take: Dirty chai or the tea coffee mix drink, may offer some general health benefits due to its ingredients. But, there is no direct evidence to suggest that it can significantly lower bad cholesterol levels. Maintaining heart health and managing cholesterol require an all-inclusive approach that includes a balanced diet, regular exercise, and, when necessary, medical intervention.

title: Fact Check: Can DNA unlock immortality and reverse aging? - THIP Media
claim_text: In an Instagram video, American spiritual teacher and author JZ Knight claims that individuals utilize less than a third of their DNA, that immortal genes and immortal DNAs exist within them, that people can grow and transform any part of their body through their DNA, and that by harnessing the power of DNA, one can achieve immortality and reverse the aging process.
quick_take: A social media post alleges that individuals utilize less than a third of their DNA, suggesting the existence of immortal genes and immortal DNAs. The post goes on to assert that one can harness their DNA to achieve immortality and reverse the aging process. We fact-checked and found this claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: The claim that humans can become immortal or reverse aging by harnessing their DNA is not supported by scientific evidence. A gene is a DNA segment containing the information needed to make a specific protein, and the human genome contains about 20,000 to 25,000 genes. There is no scientific evidence to suggest that humans can become immortal using their genes. However, research shows certain genes may play a role in aging and longevity. For example, one gene called SIRT6 has been shown to extend lifespan in mice. By targeting such genes, scientists may be able to develop treatments that slow down or even reverse the aging process, but currently, no such treatment is available. Aging is a complex process influenced by many factors, including genetics, environment, and lifestyle. It is unlikely that any single gene therapy can completely prevent aging. There are also ethical concerns about using gene therapy to extend lifespan, including issues of fairness and potential overpopulation. Regarding aging reversal: DNA plays a crucial role in the aging process through genetic factors influencing cellular repair mechanisms, telomere length, and susceptibility to age-related diseases. Several experimental approaches such as gene therapy and genetic manipulation have shown promising results in laboratory settings and animal models, but their translation to humans is still in early stages. A study published in Nature in 2019 showed that mice with restored telomeres lived longer and had healthier bodies than mice that did not receive the treatment. Telomere shortening is a significant factor in aging, so if it were possible to restore telomeres in humans safely, it could reverse some effects of aging. However, more research is needed to determine whether this approach is safe and effective in humans. Other factors contribute to aging, such as DNA damage, inflammation, and changes in metabolism. While genetic interventions may potentially slow down aspects of aging, achieving a complete and comprehensive reversal of aging is a complex challenge that requires further scientific advancements.

title: Fact Check: Can drink made with garlic, lemon, turmeric, and black pepper cleanse kidneys naturally in two weeks?
claim_text: A homemade drink made with garlic, lemon, turmeric, and black pepper cleanses the kidneys naturally in two weeks. After two weeks, your kidneys will be as good as new, your digestive and respiratory systems will be completely cleared, and all your organs will be working in complete harmony. Think of this, and you'll never set foot in a hospital again.
quick_take: An Instagram post falsely claims that a drink made with garlic, lemon, turmeric, and black pepper can cleanse the kidneys naturally in two weeks. There is no scientific evidence to support this claim.
doctor_explanation: Dr Sashi Kiran A, Consultant Nephrologist at Yashoda Hospitals, Malakpet, Hyderabad, stated: "There's a lot of buzz around natural detox drinks, but the idea that a mixture of garlic, lemon, black pepper, and turmeric can cleanse the kidneys isn't backed by scientific evidence. Kidneys are already highly efficient at filtering waste and toxins from your blood. While these ingredients do have some antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, they don't directly 'detoxify' the kidneys. For example: Lemon contains citrate, which may help prevent kidney stones. Garlic has antimicrobial and heart-health benefits. Turmeric contains curcumin, which has anti-inflammatory effects. Black pepper enhances curcumin absorption but doesn't directly impact kidney function. The best way to support kidney health is staying hydrated, eating a balanced diet, and avoiding excessive salt and processed foods. If you're looking for kidney-friendly drinks, water, lemon water, and cranberry juice are better options." Dr Tarun Kumar Saha, Sr. Consultant Nephrologist & Transplant Physician at Yashoda Hospitals, Secundarabad, Hyderabad, further said: "This is in response to the video which is being circulated claiming that the mixture of clove, garlic, turmeric and lemon can heal and cure kidney diseases. This is not the true scientific statement. Although the mixture is helpful to prevent the metabolic syndrome but when there is established kidney disease, these mixtures cannot cure kidney diseases. In fact, in a patient whose kidney function is impaired, this may cause high potassium level in the blood which can be dangerous for kidney disease patients. These claims give a false hope in kidney patients and may endanger their life." The article explains that while each ingredient has individual benefits, no scientific evidence supports the claim that this combination detoxifies or cleanses the kidneys. Garlic may reduce inflammation linked to kidney function (Elham Zare et al., BMC Nephrology: 400 mg standardized garlic extract twice daily for 8 weeks decreased IL-6, CRP, and ESR). Lemon juice may help protect against kidney stone formation by increasing urinary citrate levels (Yazeed Barghouthy et al., PMC8625077), but has minimal impact on urine pH. Curcumin in turmeric shows promise for chronic kidney disease management due to anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties (Siddhartha S. Ghosh et al., PMC6271001). Piperine in black pepper may protect kidneys from acute ischemia-reperfusion injury (Maryam Mohammadi et al., PMC7588331). Honey may help prevent kidney damage by reducing inflammation (R. B. Nerli et al.). However, none of these ingredients, individually or combined, can cleanse kidneys within two weeks or act as a detox treatment. The kidneys naturally clean themselves through filtration via nephrons; no external drink can accelerate or replicate this process. Furthermore, in patients with impaired kidney function, the high potassium content of such a drink can be dangerous and potentially life-threatening.

title: Fact Check: Can drinking a mixture of carrot, tomato, onion, and orange juice every night remove cataracts without surgery?
claim_text: Drinking a mixture of carrot, tomato, onion, and orange juice every night removes cataracts without the need for surgery.
quick_take: Carrots, tomatoes, onions, and oranges support eye health but cannot cure cataracts. Cataracts require medical treatment, and this mixture is no substitute for professional care.
doctor_explanation: Dr. Manu S Kumar, Consultant Ophthalmologist (MBBS, DNB), Allen and Habour Eye Hospital, Kanjirappally, described early signs of cataract: 'Blurring of vision, seeing halos or rings around light, need for brighter light in low light conditions, fading or yellowing of colours, frequent change of glass prescription, increased sensitivity to light etc. There may be no symptoms in some early cataract patients as well.' A cataract is an eye condition where the clear lens becomes cloudy, blocking light from passing through. It develops gradually and is a major cause of blindness worldwide. Cataracts are diagnosed through careful examination with a torchlight and a slit lamp, both with and without dilated pupils. Cataracts can occur from various causes: present at birth, develop with age, eye injuries, excessive sunlight or radiation exposure, health issues like diabetes, skin allergies, or muscle disorders. Smoking, heavy alcohol use, and poor nutrition also increase risk. Certain medications such as steroids and long-term eye conditions like uveitis or glaucoma can contribute. Dr. Sukanya Meikandasivam, Consultant Ophthalmology, Gleneagles BGS Hospital Kengeri, Bengaluru, stated: 'Drinking a mixture of tomato, onion, carrot, and orange juice will not cure cataracts. Cataracts refer to the clouding of the eye's natural crystalline lens and are typically caused by ageing, metabolic disorders, UV light exposure, or certain medications. The primary treatment for cataracts is surgical intervention. While carrots, onions, tomatoes, and oranges are rich in vitamins A, C, and E—powerful antioxidants—they may help delay the onset of cataracts by supporting overall eye health. However, there is no scientific evidence to suggest that consuming these foods can cure cataracts once they have formed.' Dr. Manu S Kumar added: 'One-word answer would be no. Drinking a combination of juices daily is not going to cure cataracts. With the currently available medicines and technology, there is no way to cure cataracts and restore vision other than by surgically removing the cataractous lens and replacing it with an artificial lens.' While individual studies suggest some benefit: a review article in the SSRN Electronic Journal highlighted that carrots contain bioactive compounds (carotenoids including Carotenes, Lutein, and Zeaxanthin) which help manage eye conditions such as nyctalopia, myopia, cataracts, age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and glaucoma. A study in Nature concluded that consuming certain fruits and vegetables, including legumes, tomatoes, apples, and pears, is linked to a reduced risk of cataracts. A study in the Journal of Physics: Conference Series concluded that silver nanoparticles derived from the skin of Allium cepa (onion) showed promising effects against cataract cells. A study in the World Journal of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences suggested that the ethanol extract of orange peel possesses anticataract activity. However, no research has examined the combined impact of all four ingredients together in completely eliminating cataracts, and there is no medical consensus supporting the claim that drinking this juice mixture can remove cataracts without surgery. The article's final take states: 'Cataracts typically require medical intervention, such as surgery, for complete removal. Drinking a mixture of these ingredients may be nutritious but should not replace professional medical advice or treatment for cataracts.'

title: Can drinking ACV, turmeric, ghee, and lemon really burn belly fat?
claim_text: Mixing apple cider vinegar, turmeric, ghee, and lemon in lukewarm water and drinking it can help burn belly fat.
quick_take: A social media video suggests that consuming a mixture of apple cider vinegar, turmeric, ghee, and lemon can help melt away belly fat. We factchecked and found the claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: Dr. Jyothy Kannangath, Dermatologist explains that there are no instant solutions for losing belly fat. There are several lifestyle changes that one should adopt rather than undergoing procedures like liposuction, or considering treatments such as cryolipolysis. Dr Umesh Wadhavani highlights that the development or prevention of chronic health conditions cannot be linked to a single food item. Instead, overall health is shaped by a mix of factors such as diet, daily habits, work-related stress, relationships, sleep quality, and levels of physical activity. Hakim Bharmal, Master Trainer and Contest Prep Coach explains that losing belly fat requires a combination of healthy lifestyle habits. Dr. P. Rammanohar, Research Director at the Amrita Centre for Advanced Research in Ayurveda says that according to Ayurveda, obesity is a difficult condition to treat, described in classical texts as nearly incurable. There's no single remedy or medicine, whether internal or external, that can cure it. The primary treatment lies in managing stress, following a healthy lifestyle, and maintaining a proper diet. Dr Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition shares: 'Losing fat isn't as simple as adding one particular food or drink to your routine. It involves a combination of reducing overall calorie intake, staying physically active, and maintaining healthy eating habits over time. Drinking ghee water alone won't specifically burn belly fat.' While some small studies have shown that apple cider vinegar may have a minor effect on appetite control and blood sugar levels, the effect is very slight. It is certainly not powerful enough to burn away stubborn fat just by drinking it. Turmeric contains curcumin, a compound with anti-inflammatory properties, but there is no strong scientific proof that curcumin helps to melt away fat. Ghee is pure fat, adding extra calories if not controlled. Lemon water is simply a source of vitamin C and hydration, not a fat-burning miracle. Ghee is very high in saturated fat, and while small amounts can fit into a balanced diet, regularly drinking fat-laden mixtures might contribute to increased calorie intake and cholesterol levels. Apple cider vinegar is highly acidic and can damage tooth enamel, irritate the throat, and upset the stomach if not properly diluted. Turmeric, when consumed in very high amounts, can also cause digestive upset or interact with certain medications like blood thinners. Relying on such drinks not only distracts from making meaningful dietary and exercise changes but could also create new health issues if overdone.

title: Fact Check: Can drinking apple cider vinegar help cure UTIs?
claim_text: A mixture containing apple cider vinegar (ACV), turmeric, black pepper, water, and honey can act as a powerful remedy to cure UTIs. The post claims that this drink provides antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and detoxifying benefits.
quick_take: An Instagram post claims that drinking apple cider vinegar can help cure urinary tract infections. Our fact check reveals it's Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: No, there is no scientific evidence to support the claim that drinking apple cider vinegar can cure a UTI. A study from 2018 concluded that ACV has antimicrobial properties against E. coli in lab settings. But, there is no current evidence to suggest that drinking ACV can effectively treat UTIs in humans. Apple cider vinegar may have antimicrobial properties, but there's no evidence it can treat or prevent UTIs. It's important to see a doctor for proper treatment, usually antibiotics, to avoid serious complications. Misusing antibiotics can lead to resistance, so always follow the prescribed course. While ACV won't cure a UTI, it can still be included in a balanced diet for other potential health benefits. Turmeric contains curcumin which is well-known for its anti-inflammatory properties. According to a 2013 study, curcumin's benefits are largely related to inflammation reduction in general health conditions. An animal study from 2017 suggests that curcumin can potentially treat chronic urinary tract infection in rats. However, several studies, including a 2019 study, point out that curcumin has low bioavailability in the body. This makes it unlikely to have a significant impact on urinary tract infections, even when consumed with black pepper to enhance absorption. Black pepper primarily enhances the absorption of curcumin from turmeric, but it has no documented ability to cure UTIs. There is evidence which indicates that black pepper has antimicrobial properties, and a 2016 study suggests it has antibacterial effects. However, no credible studies link black pepper to any effect on urinary infections. Staying hydrated helps flush bacteria from the urinary tract, but it won't cure a UTI once the infection has developed. Scientific evidence highlights that drinking water is helpful as a preventive measure, not a treatment. Some UTIs may resolve on their own. A 2014 study found that 25% to 50% of mild UTIs clear up within a week without antibiotics, as the immune system fights the infection. However, the body can only handle mild cases. For those that don't resolve on their own, antibiotics remain the standard treatment. While Manuka honey is known for its antibacterial properties and is effective in treating wound infections, it also shows activity against antibiotic-resistant bacteria, as noted in a 2020 study. A 2015 lab study demonstrated honey's ability to inhibit UTI-causing bacteria like E. coli and P. mirabilis. However, health experts agree that diet alone cannot treat UTIs. Maintaining a healthy diet during a UTI may help manage symptoms, but it is not a cure. The American Urological Association (AHA) states that antibiotics are the most effective treatment for UTIs. Home remedies, such as the one in this Instagram post, may help alleviate minor symptoms but cannot eliminate the bacterial infection. Untreated UTIs can lead to severe complications, including kidney infections, which is why seeking medical advice is crucial. Dr Avreen S. Shah, a Consultant Urologist at Shah Hospital Advanced Laparoscopic Gynae and Urology Centre in Ludhiana, stresses on the importance of not relying on home remedies, especially in more severe cases. He advises that delaying proper treatment by depending on unproven remedies can lead to complications. He states: "To treat urinary infections effectively, it's crucial to identify the underlying cause, as treatment depends on the specific bacteria or agent involved. Be cautious with home remedies and always seek expert advice for an accurate diagnosis and appropriate treatment." Dr Saumya, a Consultant Gynaecologist at ESIC Medical College and Hospital in Patna, says: "It's really important to get medical attention as soon as symptoms start. If left untreated, a UTI can quickly turn into something much more serious, like a kidney infection or even sepsis. While some home remedies might provide temporary relief in mild cases, they won't tackle the actual bacterial infection causing the problem. Waiting too long for proper treatment not only prolongs the discomfort but also increases the risk of the infection spreading. That's why it's so important to consult a healthcare provider who can prescribe the right antibiotics and help prevent complications eventually." The claim that apple cider vinegar, turmeric, black pepper, honey, and water can cure a UTI is mostly false. Some ingredients like ACV, water and honey have general health benefits. But, they are not substitutes for proper medical treatment. UTIs are bacterial infections that require antibiotics to prevent complications. Always consult a healthcare provider for the appropriate treatment of UTIs.

title: Can drinking banana stem juice help prevent kidney stones?
claim_text: An Instagram reel suggests that extracting the pulp of a banana stem and consuming its juice can effectively treat kidney stones.
quick_take: A social media post suggests that banana stem juice can completely cure existing kidney stones. After reviewing the available evidence and expert opinions, we found this claim to be false.
doctor_explanation:
Kidney stones are hard deposits formed inside the kidneys when certain substances in the urine, such as calcium, oxalate, or uric acid, become too concentrated and start sticking together. Instead of staying dissolved, they crystallise and gradually build into pebble-like structures. The most common trigger is not drinking enough water - when the body is dehydrated, urine becomes more concentrated, making it easier for minerals to clump together and form stones. Diet also plays a role; people who consume large amounts of animal protein, salty foods, or oxalate-rich ingredients like spinach and nuts may increase their risk. High sodium intake raises calcium levels in urine, creating the right environment for stones to form. Family history of kidney stones increases likelihood, and being overweight or having metabolic syndrome can also promote stone formation. Certain digestive conditions, medications, and supplements can alter urinary balance.

Regarding banana stem juice: In many Indian households, banana stem (Vazhaithandu) has long been considered beneficial for urinary health. Ayurveda describes it as cooling and cleansing, recommended for digestive and metabolic support. Nutritionally, banana stem is rich in fibre, potassium, vitamin B6, and antioxidants. Its high fibre content supports digestion and may help with constipation. It is linked to kidney health due to its mild diuretic effect, which can increase urine output slightly and may help dilute urine and reduce crystal formation. However, while banana stem juice may contribute to overall urinary wellness, there is currently no strong scientific evidence proving that it can dissolve or eliminate existing kidney stones. It should be viewed as supportive nutrition rather than actual treatment.

Dr Sharad Malhotra, Head of Gastroenterology at Aakash Healthcare, New Delhi, cautions against relying on home remedies as primary treatment. According to him, there is no convincing clinical data showing that such remedies can remove kidney stones. Delaying proper medical care in favour of unproven solutions can sometimes lead to complications.

Dr Archana Daftardar, Consultant Nephrologist, Hypertension & Transplant Physician at Renova Hospital, Kompally, Hyderabad, echoes this concern, noting that many myths surround kidney stone management. Natural remedies may sound appealing, but without proper evaluation, they may not address the underlying cause, and in some cases, may even worsen the condition.

Potential harms: Banana stem is high in fibre, and excessive intake, especially suddenly, can cause bloating, abdominal discomfort, or loose motions. It is relatively rich in potassium - for those with compromised kidney function or high potassium tendency, elevated potassium can affect heart rhythm. There is possibility of interaction with medications (blood thinners, diabetes medications, thyroid drugs).

Actual medical treatments: Treatment depends on stone size and location. Small stones under 5mm often pass on their own with increased water intake and medications that relax the ureter. Larger stones may require surgical intervention - extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL), ureteroscopy, or percutaneous nephrolithotomy. Prevention includes blood tests, urine analysis, and dietary advice tailored to specific stone type.

title: Fact Check: Can drinking carrot, bay leaf, honey, and sweet orange-infused water remove gallbladder and kidney stones?
claim_text: An Instagram post by tip2recipes titled 'Remove the stone from the gallbladder and kidneys' claims that drinking a daily infusion of carrot, bay leaf, honey, and sweet orange on an empty stomach for three months can dissolve gallbladder and kidney stones and help avoid an operation.
quick_take: Carrots have antioxidant properties, bay leaf has antiviral and immunostimulant properties, honey has wound-healing and antimicrobial properties, and sweet oranges have antioxidant properties and boost immunity. However, no scientific evidence or medical consensus supports the claim that drinking carrot, bay leaf, honey, and sweet orange-infused water can remove gallbladder and kidney stones.
doctor_explanation: Scientific studies show that carrot has antioxidant properties, bay leaf has antiviral and immunostimulant properties, honey has wound-healing and antimicrobial properties and sweet oranges have antioxidant properties and help boost immunity. However, no scientific evidence or medical consensus supports the claim that drinking carrot, bay leaf, honey, and sweet orange-infused water can remove gallbladder and kidney stones. Dr. Kartikeya Kohli, Nephrologist and Internal Medicine Consultant at Sitaram Bhartia Hospital, responded: 'Kidney stones are the solid masses formed from crystals in the urinary tract, arise due to high mineral and salt levels in urine. Consumption of specific foods, including carrots, bay leaves, honey, and sweet oranges does not have an effect on kidney stones. While honey, carrot, bayleaf and sweet orange offer various health benefits, carrots being rich in antioxidants, honey have antimicrobial property, bayleaf have immunostimulant property and sweet orange have ability to boost immunity but they all do not have ability to manage kidney stones. Increasing fluid intake, limiting oxalates, and reducing sodium help reduce stone risk. Hydration can aid in flushing out small stones, but larger stones require medical intervention. Infused water from these ingredients should not replace professional medical advice or treatment. Consult a nephrologist for proper management rather than relying on unproven remedies.' Dr. Prashanth Krishna, Gastroenterologist and Consultant in the Department of Gastroenterology and Transplant at Prashant Hospital, responded: 'There are two types of gallstones: cholesterol stones and pigment stones. Cholesterol stones primarily consist of undissolved cholesterol. Pigment stones consist of excess bilirubin, which is a pigment that forms during the breakdown of red blood cells. Not everybody with gallstones will experience symptoms. When symptoms do develop, they can include pain in the right upper quadrant, fever, jaundice, bloating, heartburn, vomiting.' Dr. Prashanth further stated: 'Drinking infused water made from carrot, bay leaf, honey, and sweet orange is unlikely to remove gallstones. Gallstones are solid particles that form in the gallbladder and typically require medical intervention for removal if they cause symptoms or complications. While some home remedies and natural therapies are promoted for gallstones, such as certain diets or herbal treatments, their effectiveness is often not scientifically proven or sufficient for treating established gallstones. It's essential to consult with a healthcare professional for appropriate diagnosis and treatment options if you suspect you have gallstones or are experiencing symptoms related to them.' A detailed search of scientific databases found no study linking any of the ingredients (carrot, bay leaf, honey, sweet orange) to the removal of gallstones. A study by NIDDK found that a high-fiber diet (rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, brown rice, oats) while limiting sugar and refined carbohydrates can lower gallstone risk; healthy fats like fish oil and olive oil promote gallbladder emptying and help prevent gallstone formation. A study by Ferraro et al. published in the Journal of American Family Physician showed that increasing fluid intake to 2.5–3 L per day and decreasing carbonated drinks (especially those acidified with phosphoric acid) can prevent recurrent kidney stones; a high-fiber and vegetable diet with normal calcium (1.0–1.2 g/day), limited sodium (4–5 g/day), and limited animal protein (0.8–1.0 g/kg/day) also helps prevent stone occurrence. A study by Pietro Manuel et al. published in the Journal of American Society of Nephrology found that carbonated drinks (rich in fructose) increase stone formation risk; however, citrus fruits such as orange, lemon, and sweet oranges contain citric acid which increases urine citrate excretion and reduces stone risk. No scientific research has indicated that drinking honey, bay leaf, carrot, and sweet orange-infused water can remove kidney and gallbladder stones.

title: Fact Check: Can Drinking Carrot Juice repair vision?
claim_text: A video on YouTube titled '8 drinks that can protect eyes and repair vision' claims that drinking carrot juice can repair vision.
verdict_original: The Claim is False. ... Hence, the claim that carrot juice can repair vision is false.
doctor_explanation:
Dr A. K. Grover, Chairman of the Department of Ophthalmology at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, explained: 'Carrot juice is a very useful nutritional component which contains carotenoids. The carotenoids are convertible into vitamin A. It is useful for those who have a vitamin A deficiency. However, it has no role in the repair of damaged vision, which can be due to many causes. There can be some diseases which are affecting vision. The role played by carrot juice would be limited only to those with a nutritional deficiency of vitamin A, and that category is fairly limited. Vitamin A deficiency as a cause of blindness in India is now quite rare.' He further mentioned: 'The nutrients, as we mentioned, are precursors to vitamin A, and their role in eye health is confined to providing those nutrients. Eye health depends on many other factors, so the role of carrot juice will be extremely limited. The harm that can happen because of a reliance on carrot juice is that you may not be treating other conditions appropriately, which requires management in different ways. So, this myth should not be propagated. It is a good nutrient, like many other nutrients which are important for eye health and can be good nutrition, but it should not be taken as a be-all and end-all for eye diseases as reliance only on this can harm the person's eye health.'

Dr Digvijay Singh, Director, Noble Eye Care Gurugram, stated: 'Well, it really depends upon what has been the cause of damage. If the cause of damage has been ageing, then the antioxidant effect of carrots can have some role to play. But if the cause of damage to the eyesight has been some other form of trauma, whether physical or related to, let's say, highlight exposure, or related to some form of injury or related to some other deficiency, then carrots on their own can't do much. The various nutrients in carrot juice are beta carotene, lutein, Zia, and xanthine, which are micronutrients, and these have a role to play in the proper functioning of the tear film. In addition to the retina, beta carotene forms vitamin A, which our photoreceptors require. These cells convert the light we see into an electrical impulse the brain can perceive. If this is deficient, you can have problems such as night blindness, dry eyes, cataracts and age-related macular degeneration. So, it does help to supplement carrots, particularly in the form of carrot juice, which is an extract of many carrots. However, one must remember that there are many other nutrients beyond just these that the eye requires; therefore, a holistic, balanced diet is important for proper eyesight. We do prescribe carrots along with a lot of other fruits and vegetables. So, while carrots play a role, they're not the sole solution for maintaining good vision.' He also noted: 'Carrots are important for the eyes because they can contain micronutrients like beta carotene which helps form vitamin A in the body, lutein and zeaxanthin which are antioxidants and all of them have a role to play for eyesight. But eyes require a lot more than just vitamin A. Vitamin A and antioxidants play an important role in the proper functioning of the retina, particularly the rod cells or the photoreceptors, as well as for proper eye surface health of the cornea and of the tear film.'

Scientific context: Vision impairment means a person's eyesight cannot be corrected to a 'normal' level, caused by loss of visual acuity or visual field. Glaucoma is a group of eye diseases that can cause vision loss and blindness by damaging the optic nerve. Carrot (Daucus carota subsp. sativus) is a root vegetable with carotenoids, flavonoids, polyacetylenes, vitamins, and minerals. Carrot juice is a source of potassium, magnesium, iron, copper, and manganese. Raw carrots are rich in beta carotene, lutein, and zeaxanthin, which are important nutrients for the retina and visual pigment. Rhodopsin, the light-sensitive pigment in eye cells that aids night vision, is partly formed by vitamin A. A study by Sadaharu Miyazono et al. found that lutein, which may help prevent age-related macular degeneration (AMD), is found in yellow carrots. However, once vision is damaged, it cannot be repaired — no scientific evidence exists that carrots can reverse vision loss caused by diseases like glaucoma or refractive errors like myopia or hyperopia.

title: Can drinking clove water for two weeks truly cleanse your lungs?
claim_text: Drinking clove tea for two weeks can cleanse the lungs
quick_take: An Instagram post suggests that drinking clove water for two weeks can help cleanse the lungs. We fact checked and found the claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: The claim that clove water can cleanse the lungs is not supported by strong scientific evidence. Cloves are dried flower buds from a tree native to Indonesia, containing eugenol, a natural oil with some medicinal properties used in folk remedies for tooth pain or stomach issues. However, when it comes to 'cleansing' the lungs, the evidence is lacking. Your lungs have built-in cleaners: tiny hair-like structures called cilia that wave back and forth, pushing out mucus, dust, and pollutants. The notion of a 'cleanse' comes from detox trends, but your body already handles detox through the liver, kidneys, and sweat. There is no strong scientific study from sources like PubMed and Cochrane reviews showing clove water detoxes lungs in humans. Lab tests on cells or animals suggest eugenol has antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects which could theoretically protect against oxidative stress from pollution or smoking. A 2018 study in Food and Chemical Toxicology found that clove extracts reduced inflammation in rat lungs exposed to toxins, but rats aren't people, and these experiments used concentrated doses, not homemade brew. Human trials focus on oral health or digestion, not respiratory detox. No randomised controlled trial supports two weeks of clove water as a lung cleanser. The term 'cleanse' is vague—online claims talk about expelling black phlegm or feeling clearer-headed, but that's anecdotal. Placebos can make you feel better, and staying hydrated helps mucus flow naturally. Dr Muskan Thakur, BAMS, Ayurveda Consultant from Indore, explains that cloves are known in Ayurveda for heat-producing and antimicrobial qualities, useful in managing respiratory issues, easing throat discomfort, and supporting lung health. However, she warns that cloves alone should not be used as a cure for bronchitis or respiratory infections. Ayurveda encourages a personalized and comprehensive treatment approach including diet, herbs, and lifestyle changes. For severe or long-lasting symptoms, consult a qualified medical professional. Some minor benefits exist: eugenol has mild antiseptic qualities that could help with throat tickle from colds; in traditional systems like Chinese medicine or Ayurveda, clove teas act as natural expectorants, loosening sticky mucus. A 2020 review highlighted how clove oil might inhibit bacteria and reduce swelling in airways. A 2017 paper tested clove extracts on mice with induced coughs, showing reduced symptoms. A small clinical trial in Complementary Therapies found a clove-based syrup helped soothe coughs in kids with upper respiratory infections, but it was combined with other herbs, not just water. For chronic issues like asthma or smoker's cough, clove water is no substitute for inhalers or quitting bad habits. Two weeks is arbitrary; benefits would be subtle and short-lived, not a full reset. Risks include: overdoing eugenol can cause nausea, diarrhea, acid reflux, and possibly liver harm. Some people may get rashes, swelling, or breathing difficulties from allergies. Pregnant women should avoid it as it might stimulate contractions. Blood thinners like warfarin—cloves could amplify effects, raising bleeding risks. A British Medical Journal case described severe mouth burns from clove oil overuse. Dr Almas Fatma, General Physician from Navi Mumbai, cautions against relying solely on home remedies for cough. While natural ingredients may offer temporary relief, there is no solid clinical proof they can completely stop a cough. They might worsen conditions or cause side effects. Safer alternatives include honey, steam inhalation, or prescribed medicines. For persistent cough, consult a doctor instead of depending on unverified remedies. Evidence-based lung health tips: quit smoking (slashes lung cancer risk by half in 10 years), exercise 30 minutes daily, diet rich in fruits, veggies, nuts, berries, spinach, and omega-3 rich fish, stay hydrated, avoid pollutants, get vaccinated against flu and pneumonia, see healthcare professional for persistent symptoms.

title: Can drinking clove water help kill stomach worms? - THIP Media
claim_text: Soaking cloves in water and drinking it helps remove intestinal worms. They say it destroys the worms and flushes them out of the body.
quick_take: A social media post suggests that drinking clove water for 2 weeks will kill/remove stomach worms. We fact checked and found the claim to be false.
doctor_explanation:
Stomach worms, also called intestinal worms, are parasites that live in the digestive system. They enter the body through contaminated food, unclean water, or poor hygiene. Common types include roundworms, tapeworms, and pinworms. These worms feed on the nutrients from your food, causing tiredness, stomach pain, bloating, or weight loss. In children, they can lead to anaemia and poor growth. The World Health Organization says that over a billion people around the world are affected by these infections, especially in areas with poor sanitation. Doctors diagnose them by checking stool samples or using special tape tests for pinworms. If left untreated, the worms can move to other parts of the body, such as the lungs or liver, and cause serious illness. This is why professional diagnosis and proper treatment are important.

Cloves contain a compound called eugenol, which has shown some ability to fight specific worms in laboratory studies. In test tubes and animal experiments, eugenol can damage the outer layer of worms, stop them from using energy, and even kill their eggs. Traditional medicine systems like Ayurveda and Chinese medicine have also used cloves for stomach problems for centuries. However, most of these studies were done in labs or on animals, not on humans. When humans drink clove water, the body quickly breaks down eugenol in the liver, meaning very little of it reaches the intestines where worms live. So while cloves may help in theory, drinking clove water is too weak to have a real medical effect.

Dr Sharad Malhotra, Senior Consultant and Head of Gastroenterology, Hepatology & Therapeutic Endoscopy at Aakash Healthcare, New Delhi, firmly cautioned against this approach, stating that such remedies are not medically effective and anyone attempting them does so entirely at their own risk.

There is no scientific proof that clove water removes worms from the human body. While it might soothe your stomach or make you feel better temporarily, it does not kill the worms or their eggs. Health experts say that home remedies like clove water or 'parasite cleanses' are not effective and could even be risky. High doses of clove oil or eugenol can cause mouth irritation, allergic reactions, or bleeding in people taking blood-thinning medicines.

Dr Almas Fatma, a general practitioner from Navi Mumbai, explains: There is currently no scientific proof that drinking clove water alone can eliminate intestinal worms in humans. While clove contains natural compounds such as eugenol with antimicrobial and antiparasitic properties, studies show that their effects are limited and inconsistent, making clove an unreliable treatment option. If you suspect a worm infection, it's important to consult a doctor and use clinically approved antiparasitic medicines like albendazole or mebendazole instead of depending on home remedies. Clove should not be considered a cure for intestinal worms.

The safest and most effective way to get rid of worms is to take proper anti-parasitic medicines prescribed by a doctor. Dr Anusha Dewan, General Physician at Jeevan Anmol Hospital in Mayur Vihar, New Delhi, explains that the best way to treat intestinal worm infections is with doctor-prescribed antiparasitic medicines like albendazole or mebendazole. These drugs effectively kill the worms and help the body get rid of them. She adds that maintaining proper hygiene is equally essential to avoid getting re-infected. For threadworms, doctors may advise repeating the dose after two weeks to kill any newly hatched worms. In more serious infections, like those caused by strongyloides or tapeworms, medicines such as ivermectin or praziquantel may be used. It's also important to treat the whole family, wash hands regularly, cook food properly, and keep nails short to prevent reinfection. The World Health Organization supports deworming programmes in areas where these infections are common, especially for children.

title: Fact Check: Can Drinking Coconut Water Once a Day Cure Acne?
claim_text: Drinking coconut water once in a day for daily helps to get rid of frizzy hair naturally, reduce hair fall, cures acne, protects against skin infections and makes skin glowing and healthy.
verdict_original: The claim is False. Hence the claim drinking coconut water once a day cures acne is False.
quick_take: Coconut water offers several health and skincare benefits, but there is no scientific evidence or medical consensus supporting the claim that drinking it once a day cures acne.
doctor_explanation:
Acne is a widespread skin problem that affects more than 85% of teenagers and can significantly impact emotional health, causing low self-esteem, anxiety, depression, and social withdrawal. It occurs when sebaceous glands (oil glands) in the skin get clogged and bacteria called Propionibacterium acnes start to grow. Certain medications like corticosteroids, oral contraceptives, and chemicals such as dioxins can trigger acne, as can endocrine disorders like Cushing's syndrome and PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome). Acne features include oily skin (seborrhea), blackheads, whiteheads, and inflamed lesions like pustules, papules, nodules, and cysts, typically on the face, chest, and back.

Acne cannot be completely prevented or cured, but it can be effectively managed with appropriate treatment. Managing acne involves a personalized approach based on the severity of the condition. For mild to moderate cases, topical treatments that reduce inflammation and prevent clogged pores are often effective. Severe cases may require oral antibiotics or hormonal therapies.

Dr Shireen Furtado, Sr. Consultant - Medical & Cosmetic Dermatology, Aster CMI Hospital, Bangalore, explained: 'Hydration orally, though not directly related to acne. Adequate water intake helps maintain skin elasticity and overall health, which can prevent the overproduction of sebum, a key contributor to acne development. When the skin is well-hydrated, it is better equipped to regulate oil production and maintain a balanced microbiome, both of which are essential for preventing clogged pores and subsequent breakouts. Hydration also supports the skin's barrier function, reducing inflammation and irritation that can arise from dryness, thereby decreasing the severity of acne lesions.'

Coconut water offers several health benefits, containing bioactive enzymes like acid phosphatase and catalase that aid digestion, along with essential nutrients such as sugars, vitamin C, folic acid, free amino acids, and vitamins B1, B2, and B6. However, there is no scientific evidence that mentions the role of coconut water in curing acne, and there is no consensus within the medical fraternity that supports the claim that drinking coconut water daily cures acne.

A review article published in the International Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences and Research mentioned that tender coconut water restores strength and elasticity to the skin and also reduces wrinkles and sagging of the skin. However, this study does not mention any role of coconut water in curing acne. Another study published in the Journal of Functional Foods highlighted that fresh coconut water is abundant in kinetin, a cytokinin plant hormone, which can help delay ageing signs in human skin cells. Yet another review published in the International Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences Review and Research noted that coconut water, with its balanced electrolytes like sodium and potassium, helps restore electrolyte losses through the skin and urine. Cococin, a freeze-dried form of coconut water, has been used in dietary supplements and anti-ageing skincare. All these studies highlight the role of coconut water in skincare and its anti-ageing properties — none mention coconut water as a cure for acne.

Dr Priyanka Kuri, Consultant - Dermatology, Aster Whitefield Hospital, Bengaluru, told Medical Dialogues: 'Coconut water has many anti-microbial properties that help reduce inflammation caused by acne. There is no specific study that indicates that drinking coconut water once a day will heal acne, but it can surely be included in the skincare routine along with other ingredients to attain hydrated and glowing skin.'

Dr Shireen Furtado added: 'Coconut water is rich in essential nutrients, including vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants, which may contribute to overall skin health. Its hydrating properties can also play a role in maintaining skin moisture, potentially aiding in the prevention of acne exacerbated by dryness. However, while coconut water may offer some benefits, it is essential to recognize that acne is a complex condition influenced by various factors, including hormonal fluctuations, dietary habits, and individual skin types. While incorporating coconut water into one's diet may support skin health due to its nutrient profile, it should not be viewed as a standalone solution.'

title: Fact Check: Can Drinking Coconut Water With Lemon Juice Dissolve Stones?
claim_text: Drinking Coconut Water With Lemon Juice For Some Days Can Dissolve Stones
verdict_original: The claim mentioned in the viral video is False.
quick_take: The post does not specify the type of stones being addressed. Although coconut water and lemon juice may each contribute to kidney stone prevention, there is no evidence supporting their combined effectiveness for the purpose of dissolution of kidney stones. It is also important to note that gallstones cannot be dissolved and typically require medical treatment. There is no scientific evidence or medical consensus to support the claim that Drinking Coconut Water With Lemon Juice For Some Days Can Dissolve Stones.
doctor_explanation:
The claim in the viral Instagram post — that drinking coconut water mixed with two teaspoons of lemon juice for a few days can dissolve and pass kidney stones — is FALSE. The post fails to specify which type of stones it targets, which is a critical omission. Stones (calculi) in the human body include kidney stones (calcium oxalate, uric acid, etc.), gallstones (cholesterol or bilirubin), bladder stones, salivary gland stones, pancreatic stones, and tonsil stones. The two most common are gallstones and kidney stones, and they are treated very differently.

Gallstones (cholelithiasis) are solid deposits that form in the gallbladder due to an imbalance in bile components. The most common type, cholesterol gallstones, forms when cholesterol in bile becomes excessively high. Pigment gallstones are composed of bilirubin and are more common in individuals with certain liver conditions or blood disorders. Gallstones cannot be dissolved by consuming coconut water and lemon juice — they require medical intervention. The primary treatment is cholecystectomy (surgical removal of the gallbladder), particularly for symptomatic patients. Medical dissolution therapy with ursodeoxycholic acid is an option for uncalcified gallstones smaller than 5 mm but is not very effective and carries a high risk of recurrence. Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) can remove gallstones lodged in the common bile duct non-surgically. Shock wave lithotripsy is rarely used.

Kidney stones (renal calculi, nephrolithiasis) are solid pebble-like masses that develop in the kidneys when mineral levels are elevated. They can form from calcium oxalate, calcium phosphate, cystine, struvite, magnesium ammonium phosphate, and uric acid. Kidney stones are associated with higher risks of chronic kidney disease, end-stage renal failure, cardiovascular conditions, diabetes, and high blood pressure. Treatment depends on stone size, location, and symptoms. Small stones may pass naturally with increased fluid intake and over-the-counter pain relievers. Larger stones require procedures such as Extracorporeal Shock Wave Lithotripsy (ESWL), Ureteroscopy, Percutaneous Nephrolithotomy (PCNL), or medications like alpha-blockers to relax ureter muscles.

Coconut water and lemon juice individually have shown some promise in kidney stone PREVENTION but not in DISSOLUTION. A study by Dr. R. Kalai et al. found that coconut water's potassium content may help alkalize urine, potentially preventing kidney stone formation. The Natural Beverages reported that coconut water can help prevent kidney stones by reducing crystal and stone formation. Piero Ruggenenti et al. (PMC8683665) found that adding fresh lemon juice to a standard diet may help prevent reoccurrence of calcium-oxalate kidney stones. Research published in Nutrients (PMC8625077) confirmed that lemon juice increases urinary citrate levels, providing a protective effect against kidney stones, though it does not significantly alkalize urine pH. Importantly, all cited benefits relate to prevention and inhibition of stone formation, not dissolution of existing stones.

Dr. Arun P, Associate Consultant, Gastroenterology, KIMSHEALTH Trivandrum, said: 'There is no scientific evidence to support the idea that drinking coconut water with two spoons of lemon juice for several days can dissolve gallstones. Gallbladder stones cannot dissolve so it is unlikely that this remedy would be effective.'

Dr Arun Kumar J, Consultant Nephrologist, Gleneagles BGS Hospital, Kengeri, Bengaluru, said: 'While coconut water and lemon juice are popularly believed to benefit kidney health, there is no proven benefit to using them specifically for dissolving kidney stones. Coconut water may support natural stone passage by helping with hydration, and lemon juice provides citrate, which can inhibit the formation of certain stone types. However, effective treatment requires proper evaluation of the stone's cause and type, tailored to each patient's needs, to prevent recurrence and manage symptoms. Always consult a nephrologist for the most effective treatment options based on your condition.'

The post also contains the alarming and medically dangerous rhetoric: 'People would rather die by consuming poison than tell you the remedy for stones,' which may discourage people from seeking timely medical care. The reel has 1,437,882 likes, 3,176 comments, 3.2 million shares, and 107 million views, indicating massive misinformation reach.

title: Can drinking coriander seeds water fix skin problems in 2-3 weeks?
claim_text: Soak coriander seeds in water overnight, then drink it every day in the morning on an empty stomach. They claim it fights bad stuff on skin, and gets rid of dark spots, pimples, and dullness. All this in just 2-3 weeks.
quick_take: A social media post suggests that drinking coriander seed water every day will help you get rid of pimples and help achieve glowing skin. We fact checked and found the claim to be Mostly false.
doctor_explanation:
## Does coriander seeds water have helpful antioxidants for skin?
Yes, but not enough to make a big difference when you drink it. Antioxidants are like shields that fight harm from sun or dirt, which can hurt skin. Coriander seeds have things like vitamin C that do this. One study on coriander leaves showed it might protect skin cells from sun rays in a lab. But when you soak seeds and drink the water, those good bits get weak in your tummy. They help a little for whole body health, not just skin fixes. Eating fresh fruits is better for strong antioxidants.

## Is it good for reducing dark spots on skin?
No, there's not much proof it works well or fast. Dark spots, or pigmentation, happen from sun, body changes, or old pimples. Some say coriander's vitamins A and C can fade them. Animal tests hint it calms swelling, which might help a bit. But no big studies on people show drinking the water clears spots in weeks. Health experts say research is limited. Instead, use sun cream every day to stop more spots. Creams with things like vitamin C or special acids work better over time.

## Can it clear up pimples?
No, it's not a strong way to fight pimples by itself. Pimples come from blocked skin holes, germs, and extra oil. Coriander has stuff that kills some germs in tests. It might calm red skin too. It could help your gut, which links to skin sometimes, but it's not direct. Food like sugar causes more pimples for many. Use face washes with salicylic acid to clean pores. See a doctor for bad pimples to avoid scars. Dr Sandeep Arora, MBBS, MD, an experienced dermatologist explained that coriander seeds and its aerial parts, commonly used in cooking, contain essential oils such as linalool, which possess anti-inflammatory and antibacterial properties effective against acne-causing bacteria. However, casual use of coriander may not be sufficient, as the oils need to be adequately concentrated to be effective. He recommends using coriander as a supplementary treatment alongside standard acne therapies, but only after consulting a dermatologist, as some products may worsen acne. Dr Ekansh Shekhar, a dermatologist, cosmetologist, trichologist, and aesthetic medicine consultant based in Lucknow, stated, "There is no scientific evidence supporting the use of coriander water as an acne remedy. Acne typically stems from hormonal fluctuations, excess oil production, and bacterial growth. Effective acne management requires a comprehensive approach, including a healthy diet, proper skincare, and, in some cases, medical intervention. Relying solely on coriander water or any single food will not yield significant results."

## Will it make your skin glow in 2-3 weeks?
Unlikely, though it might help a tiny bit. Glow means soft, even skin that looks fresh. The seeds have vitamins and bits that clean your body lightly. Drinking more water from this habit keeps skin moist. Some studies say plant goodies build better skin over months, not days. For quick glow, sleep well, eat nuts and fish, or use a soft scrub. The water alone won't wow you fast. Dr Rashi Soni, consulting dermatologist, aesthetic physician, and hair transplant surgeon at Rashi Hospital, Mumbai, noted, "While coriander water contains some nutrients, it is not a dependable solution for achieving glowing skin. Optimal results come from maintaining hydration, eating a balanced diet rich in fruits and vegetables, following a consistent skincare routine, and adopting healthy lifestyle habits."

## Are there any bad sides to trying this?
Yes, but nothing major for most people. Coriander is safe in food amounts, but too much water might upset your belly or cause allergies like rash. It can make skin more sun-sensitive, so you burn easier. If pregnant or on pills, ask a doctor, it might mix badly. The real problem is waiting on this while skin gets worse. Don't skip real help.

## What are better ways to fix these skin problems?
There are some proven ones. For dark spots, use creams with azelaic acid or peels to fade them. Sun cream is key to stop new ones. Glow comes from drinking water, eating greens, and using vitamin C on skin. See a skin doctor for plans that fit you, like lasers if spots are tough. Herbs like coriander can add to meals, but not lead the way.

In short, coriander seeds water is safe to try and might give a small health lift. But don't count on it for clear, glowing skin in weeks, that's not what science shows. Real skin care takes steady steps. If your skin bothers you, talk to a doctor. It's better than chasing quick tips online.

title: Can drinking diluted raw milk prevent all types of urinary problems?
claim_text: Drinking diluted raw milk keeps you safe from all kinds of urinary problems.
quick_take: A social media post states that consuming diluted raw milk can prevent all kinds of urinary problems. We fact checked and found the claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: The fact check examines three key aspects: First, diluting raw milk does not eliminate harmful bacteria - adding water doesn't make raw milk safe because bacteria like E. coli, Salmonella, and Listeria remain present; they're just spread out in a larger volume. The World Health Organization (WHO) states that only pasteurisation or boiling can make milk safe. Second, there is no scientific evidence that diluted raw milk can prevent urinary tract infections (UTIs). UTIs are caused when bacteria from the gut enter the urinary tract, and the main defence is good hydration through regular urination. Milk doesn't change urine acidity, coat the urinary lining, or stop bacteria from sticking to bladder walls. Clean, safe water is the best choice for flushing the urinary system. Third, drinking raw milk actually increases infection risk. Raw milk exposure to bacteria can cause foodborne illness, and severe E. coli infections can damage kidneys and cause haemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS), especially in children. When raw milk causes vomiting or diarrhoea, dehydration leads to concentrated urine that can worsen urinary problems. Dr Shalin Nagori, Consultant Pathologist and Industrial Physician, states: "The urinary tract depends on steady hydration and safe nutrition, but raw milk can interfere with both. It introduces harmful germs while increasing the chances of dehydration. In short, drinking raw milk in any form including diluted carries risks that can directly and indirectly make urinary problems worse." Dr Abhishek Juneja, Neurologist, clarifies: "Pasteurised milk is safe to consume. On the other hand, raw milk can contain harmful contaminants that pose risks to human health." Dietitian Priyanka responds: "There is no scientific proof that raw milk can prevent urinary problems. In fact, there is no evidence that either raw or pasteurised milk plays a role in preventing such issues. This claim is simply a myth." Evidence-based prevention methods include: adequate hydration, timely urination, wiping front to back for women, urinating after sex, wearing breathable cotton underwear, and managing blood sugars for diabetics.

title: Fact Check: Can drinking from a tin give you bacterial infection? - THIP Media
claim_text: A Facebook post warns readers to rinse soda cans before drinking because they are contaminated with bacteria and can cause diseases such as leptospirosis. The post claims two people were hospitalized and one died after drinking from a tin can having dried up urine of an animal infected with leptospira bacteria. It also claims a study shows the top of all beverage cans are more contaminated than public toilets and people can catch leptospirosis from them.
quick_take: A social media post claims drinking from a tin can give you Leptospirosis. We fact-checked and found the claim to be Mostly False. Leptospirosis is a relatively rare disease, and the risk of contracting it from drinking from contaminated beverage cans is low.
doctor_explanation:
Leptospirosis is a bacterial infection caused by Leptospira bacteria. This disease can cause potentially fatal infections of a number of organs, including the kidney, liver, and brain. Evidence shows that Leptospirosis can pass from animals to humans through the infected urine of animals. There is evidence that animals can carry leptospirosis and can spread it to humans who have direct contact with infected urine.

No evidence confirms that drinking from a tin can causes leptospirosis. Leptospirosis is a bacterial infection that can be transmitted to humans through contact with infected animal urine or contaminated water or soil. While it is possible to contract the disease from contaminated beverage cans, it is not a common mode of transmission.

The Facebook post claims that two people were hospitalized and one died after drinking from the tin can, having dried up urine of an animal infected with leptospira bacteria. The post also talks about a study to claim that the top of all beverage cans are more contaminated than public toilets and people can catch leptospirosis from them. No evidence confirms that people should avoid drinking from tin cans to prevent leptospirosis.

Evidence shows that Leptospira survives in a moist environment, so the bacteria would not survive on the sealed dry surface of a tin can. Leptospira is a genus of bacteria that can cause a disease called leptospirosis, which can be contracted by humans and animals. These bacteria are typically found in soil and water contaminated with the urine of infected animals and can survive for a limited time outside the host.

Based on the evidence that Leptospira survives in moist environments, it is possible that the bacteria could survive on the surface of a tin can if it is moist. However, if the can is sealed and dry, it is less likely that the bacteria could survive for an extended period of time. The evidence also informs that the tin can needs to have holes for the bacteria to survive because most soft drinks are acidic in nature.

Regarding the transmission of leptospirosis through drinking from a tin can, it is possible but highly unlikely unless the can have been previously opened and contaminated with urine or soil containing the bacteria. In general, the risk of contracting leptospirosis from drinking water or beverages is low, and proper sanitation and hygiene can greatly reduce the risk of infection.

The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) website informs that people can prevent leptospirosis by avoiding contact with animal urine or contaminated water. Other measures are wearing protective clothing, and practicing good hygiene, such as washing hands thoroughly with soap and water.

title: Fact Check: Can drinking Kishmish (Raisin) water in morning on Tuesday and Friday clear pimples and prevent heart attack?
claim_text: Drinking Kishmish (raisin) water in the morning on Tuesday and Friday clears pimples, makes skin glow as it purifies the blood, and prevents heart attack.
verdict_original: The claim made by the user is False. ... Thus, the claim that drinking Kishmish water in the morning on Tuesday and Friday clears pimples and prevents heart attacks is FALSE.

Dr. Soumya Sachdeva, MBBS, MD (Dermatology), DNB (Dermatology), ECFMG (USA), Consultant Dermatologist, Theya Wellness Skin Hair and Aesthetics Clinic, Kaushambi, Ghaziabad explained: 'Acne is a common skin condition that occurs when hair follicles become clogged with oil (sebum), dead skin cells, and bacteria. It often appears as pimples, blackheads, whiteheads, or cysts, and can occur on the face, chest, back, and shoulders. The main causes of acne include overproduction of oil by the sebaceous glands, an excess of dead skin cells, and the growth of Cutibacterium acnes (formerly known as Propionibacterium acnes), a bacteria that thrives in clogged pores. Hormonal changes, particularly during puberty, menstruation, or pregnancy, can lead to an increase in sebum production, exacerbating acne. Other factors like stress, certain medications, diet, and even genetics can also contribute to the development of acne. Proper skincare and medical treatments are essential for managing the condition effectively. It is important to consult a dermatologist for proper treatment and management of pimples and acne.' Regarding the specific claim: 'The idea that drinking Kishmish (raisin) water on specific days like Tuesdays and Fridays can clear pimples is more of a myth than a reality. Pimples are usually caused by a combination of factors, including excess oil production (sebum), dead skin cells clogging pores, bacterial buildup, and inflammation. Hormonal changes, especially during puberty or menstrual cycles, can also trigger acne. Stress, diet, and even certain skincare products may worsen the condition. While raisins are nutritious and can support general skin health, drinking them in water isn't a cure for pimples. For real results, focus on a consistent skincare routine, a healthy diet, and, if needed, treatments prescribed by a dermatologist.'

Dr. Prem Aggarwal, MBBS, MD (Medicine), DNB (Cardiology), Sanjeevan Hospital, Delhi said: 'The claim that Drinking Kishmish (raisin) water specifically on Tuesday and Friday that too in the morning can prevent a heart attack has no medical basis. There is no scientific evidence to support the timing of raisin water consumption for heart attack prevention. Having said that, raisins are rich in antioxidants, potassium, and fiber, which have been associated with improved heart health. Regular consumption of raisins, as part of a balanced diet, may contribute to lowering blood pressure, reducing cholesterol levels, and improving overall cardiovascular health. However, to state that their consumption on certain particular days is a part of prevention strategy for heart attack is false. It's important to follow evidence-based practices for heart disease prevention, such as maintaining a healthy diet, regular exercise, and adhering to prescribed medical treatments.'

Scientific evidence cited: A study from University of Alabama at Birmingham's Department of Dermatology indicates that raisins may protect healthy adults' skin from UV radiation damage; the polyphenols in grapes can help reduce immediate UV damage and lower levels of proteins that trigger inflammation. A review published in the Journal of Nutrition and Health by Margaret J. Schuster et al. found that eating raisins, compared to other carbohydrate snacks with the same calorie content, lowers LDL cholesterol, blood pressure and raisin consumption is linked to decreased risk of cardiovascular diseases. However, researchers emphasized further studies are needed and cautioned that raisins should not replace sunscreen. As per the National Heart, Lung and Blood Institute, US: 'A heart attack, also known as a myocardial infarction, happens when the flow of blood that brings oxygen to a part of your heart muscle suddenly becomes blocked and the heart can't get enough oxygen. If blood flow is not restored quickly, the heart muscle will begin to die.' Heart attack risk is influenced by: unhealthy diet high in saturated fats or sodium, lack of physical activity, smoking, high cholesterol, high blood pressure, high blood sugar or diabetes, high triglycerides, obesity, and metabolic syndrome.

title: Fact Check: Can Drinking Lemon Ginger Tea Every Day Bid Diabetes Goodbye?
claim_text: Drinking Lemon Ginger Tea Every Day can Bid Diabetes Goodbye
verdict_original: This claim is False. Hence, the claim by the Pinterest User is False.
quick_take: Ginger, lemon, and tea may have potential benefits for managing type 2 diabetes, such as improving blood sugar control, enhancing lipid profiles, and supporting insulin resistance and pancreatic health. However, there is no evidence of their impact on other types of diabetes. Diabetes is a chronic, incurable condition — no scientific proof or medical consensus supports the claim that Drinking Lemon Ginger Tea Every Day can bid it goodbye.
doctor_explanation:
Dr. Uzma Khan, Sr. Consultant Diabetes, Endocrinology & Metabolism, Apollo Sugar Kondapur, Hyderabad stated: 'Lemon ginger tea offers antioxidant and anti-inflammatory benefits, but it's crucial to understand that diabetes is a chronic condition without a cure. Managing diabetes requires a comprehensive approach, including medication, balanced nutrition, regular exercise, and consistent blood sugar monitoring. While healthy dietary habits can support overall health, drinking lemon ginger tea daily will not 'bid diabetes goodbye.' Misconceptions like these can lead to poorly managed diabetes.' Dr. Rajesh Bendre, National Technical Head, Apollo Diagnostic further stated: 'While lemon ginger tea can be a healthy addition to your diet due to its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, it is important to understand that diabetes is a chronic, dysregulated lifestyle-related condition. Managing diabetes effectively involves a comprehensive approach, including proper diet, medication, regular exercise, and consistent monitoring of blood sugar levels. There is no evidence to support that only drinking lemon ginger tea daily can 'bid diabetes goodbye.' Relying solely on this approach may lead to poorly managed diabetes and serious health complications. The only way to work on diabetes is through maintaining weight, eating healthy diet without added sugar, and regular exercise.'

The article provides detailed scientific context: Diabetes is a long-term condition arising when the pancreas produces insufficient insulin or the body cannot use insulin efficiently. Hyperglycemia over time causes significant damage to nerves and blood vessels. WHO classifies diabetes into four major types: Type 1 (insulin-dependent, approximately 9 million people affected in 2017, no known prevention), Type 2 (accounts for more than 95% of cases, often preventable through weight management and exercise), Gestational diabetes (during pregnancy), and Impaired glucose tolerance (IGT)/Impaired fasting glycemia (IFG). Currently, there is no cure for diabetes; diabetes reversal through blood sugar management is possible but not elimination.

Regarding individual ingredients: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial published in Complementary Therapies in Medicine demonstrated that consuming three one-gram capsules of ginger powder daily for 8 weeks benefits type 2 diabetes patients by reducing fasting blood sugar, lowering HbA1c levels, and improving insulin resistance indices. A study by Nafiseh Khandouzi et al. revealed that ginger supplementation notably lowered FBS, HbA1c, Apo B, Apo B/Apo A-I ratio, and MDA levels while boosting Apo A-I levels in individuals with type 2 diabetes. A study by Petrus Mantur et al. showed lemon extract can help regulate blood sugar levels and promote pancreatic beta cell regeneration in alloxan-induced mice. A meta-analysis in the Journal of General Internal Medicine suggests tea consumption could reduce the risk of developing type 2 diabetes.

The article emphasizes that while individual compounds in lemon, ginger, and tea may support type 2 diabetes management, there is no scientific evidence supporting their combined efficacy for other types of diabetes. Most importantly, diabetes is a chronic condition that cannot be cured — drinking lemon ginger tea daily cannot 'bid diabetes goodbye' and relying solely on this may lead to poorly managed diabetes and serious health complications.
