title: Fact Check: Can eating cashew nut tree bark neutralize snake venom? - THIP Media
claim_text: Chewing the bark of a cashew nut tree can effectively counteract snake venom, including the highly poisonous bite of an anaconda.
quick_take: According to a Facebook post that has received thousands of shares, chewing cashew tree bark can "destroy snake venom," including the highly poisonous bite of an anaconda. We analyzed the claim. Our research determined that the assertion isFalse.
doctor_explanation: Snake bite toxins could lead to fatal conditions notably in rural areas of the tropical developing nations. Snake venoms are tissue-specific, protein-rich toxins and can be divided into three major classes: hemotoxic, cytotoxic, or neurotoxic. Hemotoxic venoms impact the cardiovascular system, cytotoxic venoms target certain cellular locations, and neuro-toxic venoms injure the human body's nervous system. Anti–snake Venom (ASV) is a specialized countermeasure to the effects of snake venom, prepared by capturing snakes, milking snakes in a lab, and immunizing horses with venom. Snake venom is a complex mixture of many components including non-toxic proteins, carbohydrates, metals, and enzymatic and non-enzymatic components. However, circulating venom is the only one that the antivenom neutralizes. No amount of ASV will be able to neutralize or combine with venom once it has adhered to or been absorbed by the target organs. Thus, the prevention of organ damage depends on early venom detection and antidote administration. There isn't any substantial evidence that cashew nut tree bark can counteract snake venom. Even though a study mentions that cashew fruit can only reliably counteract viper venom, due to the remedy's specificity, polyvalent toxins may not benefit from it. Thus, it is ineffective for treating all snake venoms, including that of the anaconda. Additionally, no references to cashew tree bark being used as a snake venom antidote were found in research. Dr. Kashyap Dakshini, General Physician in Mumbai, stated: "Ethnobotanical procedures have been extensively used to identify a practical treatment for snake bites, which is a major cause of fatalities in the tropics. Pharmacological testing has been done on some plants to determine how well they neutralize snake venom. However, there is no data available to support the assertion that chewing the bark of the cashew nut tree renders snake poison ineffective, nor is there any evidence of any clinical trials published in reliable and reputable publications. It would be best to get advice from a doctor who would think about utilizing anti-snake venoms that are available after administering a test dosage while keeping in mind the risks involved." According to the World Health Organization, antivenom is the only standardized, targeted treatment for addressing the medically relevant consequences of snake venom toxins. Even so, several herbal treatments, including Touch Me not, Indian sarsaparilla, Turmeric, Amla, and Cashew Fruit, have been described as having antivenomous properties. Their use as efficient antivenomous antidotes is, however, restricted by the lack of supporting data.

title: Fact Check: Can eating cashews kill bacteria and cure infections?
claim_text: A new study said that the bacteria that cause tooth decay, acne, tuberculosis, and leprosy can be killed off by eating cashews!
quick_take: A social media post claims that eating cashews can kill bacteria and cure infections. After fact checking we found that this claim is false.
doctor_explanation: The claim that eating cashews can kill bacteria and cure infections is false. The article addresses each bacteria claim separately: TOOTH DECAY: Eating cashews does not kill the bacteria that cause cavities. Tooth decay happens when bacteria like Streptococcus mutans make acids that slowly wear down the teeth. Some lab studies have tested cashew nut shell extract, and not the cashew nut itself, for possible dental benefits. A 2014 lab study found that a compound from cashew shells, called anacardic acid, helped protect tooth samples from acid damage better than fluoride and green tea extract. A 2012 study showed that this same compound could block enzymes that break down tissues, but this was only seen in cell tests. A 2022 lab study found that both natural and processed cashew shell liquids could kill certain bacteria linked to tooth decay and gum infections and stop them from forming sticky layers called biofilms. But all these studies were done in labs, and not in people. So far, there's no proof that eating cashews or using cashew-based products can prevent or treat tooth decay in real life. Dr Pooja Sharma, BDS, MDS, from NIMS University, Jaipur, clarifies, 'Cashews have shown some mild antibacterial effects in lab tests, but there's no proof they kill the bacteria that cause tooth decay, like Streptococcus mutans. Munching on cashews won't prevent cavities. The best way to protect your teeth is to brush twice a day with fluoride toothpaste, floss daily, and limit sugary foods and drinks.' ACNE: Acne is mainly linked to a skin bacterium called Cutibacterium acnes, along with excess oil and inflammation. Although cashews contain zinc, which supports skin health, there's no evidence that eating cashews can kill acne-causing bacteria or clear acne. A 2020 lab study tested cashew fruit pulp—not the nut itself—for potential acne benefits. Dr Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant in Lucknow, explains, 'While cashews contain antioxidants and anti-inflammatory compounds that may benefit skin health, there is no evidence to suggest that they specifically target or kill the bacteria responsible for acne, such as Propionibacterium acnes. Acne is a complex condition influenced by hormones, oil production, and bacteria, and treating it requires a more targeted approach. For effective acne treatment, it's best to follow a skincare routine that includes cleansing, proper moisturising, and, if necessary, consult a dermatologist for personalised advice.' TUBERCULOSIS: Tuberculosis (TB) is a serious infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It must be treated with proper antibiotics over several months. There is no evidence that cashews can kill TB bacteria or treat the disease. A 2016 lab study looked at anacardic acid, a compound found in cashew nut shells. It helped immune cells trap and kill, or slow the growth of, some Gram-positive bacteria in test tubes. But it was not tested on TB bacteria or in humans. A later 2020 animal study found that cashew nuts reduced inflammation and tissue damage in a different condition, not related to TB. These studies do not prove that cashews can treat infections in humans. LEPROSY: Leprosy, or Hansen's disease, is caused by Mycobacterium leprae and needs proper antibiotic treatment. Cashews have not been proven to treat or kill the bacteria that cause it. Some lab studies (2013 study) have explored the antimicrobial properties of cashew plant parts like leaves, apples, and nut shells. A 2015 review found that compounds such as anacardic acid, flavonoids, and tannins showed action against certain bacteria, fungi, and viruses in test settings. title: Can eating chia seeds daily for 2 weeks transform your body?
claim_text: According to an Instagram video, eating chia seeds every day for two weeks will flatten your belly in one day, give you glowing skin in 3 days, increase energy by day 10, curb cravings and promote weight loss, and reset gut health in 14 days.
quick_take: A viral social media video claims that eating chia seeds daily for 2 weeks can transform your body. While real chia seed benefits do exist, our fact check shows this claim is mostly false.
doctor_explanation: ## Can chia seeds flatten the belly in one day? No, chia seeds don't work instantly. One of the known chia seed benefits is improved digestion due to their high fibre content. Chia seeds may help grow good gut bacteria, improve digestion, and support better nutrient absorption. Some studies also suggest they can reduce how much sugar and cholesterol the body absorbs, which might help lower the risk of heart disease and diabetes. However, eating them for a day won't flatten your belly. In fact, without enough water, they may cause bloating and discomfort. Losing belly fat requires weeks or months of consistent eating habits, not a quick fix. ## Why are chia seeds linked to glowing skin? There is growing interest in chia seeds for skin because they're rich in antioxidants and omega-3 fats. These nutrients may help reduce inflammation and support skin repair. As per current evidence, consumption of a more anti-inflammatory diet can help people with acne. But claiming skin glow in just three days is a stretch. Any visible improvement would take weeks and depends on overall diet and hydration, not chia seeds alone. Dr Rashi Soni, Consultant Dermatologist at Rashi Hospital, Mumbai, explains that chia seeds are rich in omega-3 fatty acids and antioxidants, which are known to reduce inflammation in the body. Since skin problems like acne often involve inflammation, these nutrients may indirectly support clearer skin. However, she stresses that eating chia seeds alone won't treat acne or other skin concerns. "Clear skin depends on many factors, including hormones, diet, sleep, stress, and skincare habits," she says. While adding chia seeds to a healthy diet can be a good step, Dr Soni adds that they are not a cure and should never replace proper medical or dermatological care. ## Do chia seeds really increase energy by day 10? Not dramatically. Chia seeds do provide steady fuel, because they contain fibre, healthy fats, and plant protein. These can support energy levels over time, especially when part of a nutritious diet. However, claiming that energy will "skyrocket" by day ten is misleading. The effect is mild, not dramatic, and certainly not guaranteed. ## Can chia seeds curb cravings and promote weight loss? They may, but only to a small degree. It's true that chia seeds for weight loss are commonly promoted. They absorb water and swell in the stomach, which may help with feeling full. Some small studies show they can slightly reduce appetite. But dropping five pounds in two weeks is unlikely from chia alone, and most of that might be water loss, not actual fat burn. Shruti K. Bhardwaj, Chief Clinical Nutritionist at Zydus Hospital, Ahmedabad, explains that while chia seeds are high in fibre and packed with nutrients, they cannot cause weight loss on their own. "No single food or drink, including chia seeds, can melt fat or make you lose weight quickly," she says. The fibre in chia may help reduce cravings by keeping you full for longer, but real and lasting weight loss comes from a balanced diet, regular physical activity, and portion control. She also warns that terms like 'fast' or 'quick' weight loss are often misleading. "Healthy fat loss takes time," she adds, and it's best done under the guidance of a certified expert who can personalise your plan based on your body and health needs. ## Can eating chia reset gut health in 14 days? No, gut health doesn't reset so quickly. The idea that any one food can "reset" the gut is not backed by medical evidence. Fibre in chia seeds supports good gut bacteria, but changes take time and a well-balanced diet. There's no proof that eating chia alone can dramatically improve or reset digestion in two weeks. ## What are the actual chia seed benefits backed by science? Chia seeds are a healthy addition to meals, but not a miracle. Science shows they're a good source of dietary fibre, omega-3 fats, and antioxidants. Regular intake may support heart health, digestion, skin repair, and weight control over time. But they work best as part of a balanced lifestyle, not as a solo solution for fast results. In summary, there are numerous chia seed benefits, including for skin, digestion, and weight management. However, the video's claims are overhyped. There's no solid evidence that chia seeds alone can cause glowing skin, fat loss, or energy spikes in just 14 days. They're a nutritious choice, but not a quick body-transforming fix.

title: Can eating cucumber 2-3 times a day help you lose weight?- THIP
claim_text: Eating cucumber 2-3 times a day can help in weight loss
quick_take: A social media video claims that eating cucumbers 2-3 times a day can help in weight loss. We fact checked and found the claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation:
Not really. Eating cucumbers 2-3 times a day alone won't cause significant weight loss. While cucumbers are undoubtedly a healthy food choice—being low in calories and high in water—they don't have any magical properties that directly lead to weight loss. The key to shedding pounds is creating a calorie deficit, meaning you burn more calories than you consume. Eating cucumbers regularly may help you control your calorie intake, but they won't automatically cause you to lose weight. Cucumbers can be part of a healthy diet, but eating them several times a day won't guarantee results unless it's part of an overall balanced eating plan combined with physical activity. Weight loss requires a holistic approach. While incorporating cucumber into your diet might contribute to weight loss, it's essential to consider other methods and factors that can also impact your health.

Does eating cucumber help curb hunger? Yes, cucumbers may help reduce hunger—temporarily. Cucumbers contain both fibre and a lot of water, which can help you feel fuller for longer. When you eat cucumbers, the water and fibre expand in your stomach, which may help reduce your appetite for a short time. This could lead you to eat fewer calories throughout the day, indirectly supporting weight loss. However, this effect is temporary. While cucumbers are a good, low-calorie snack to incorporate into meals, they won't provide lasting satiety on their own. For long-term hunger control, it's essential to eat a balanced meal with protein, healthy fats, and complex carbohydrates.

Are cucumbers low in calories? Yes, cucumbers are low in calories. Cucumbers are known for their very low calorie count. This makes them an excellent food choice for anyone trying to lose weight or reduce their overall calorie intake. If you replace higher-calorie snacks like crisps, chocolate, or sugary drinks with cucumbers, you'll lower your total calorie consumption, which can help with weight management. But while cucumbers are a healthy, low-calorie food, they should not be the sole focus of your diet. A balanced eating plan includes a variety of foods, including protein, fibre, vitamins, and minerals, which cucumbers alone can't provide.

Do cucumbers help you stay hydrated? Yes, cucumbers are great for hydration. With around 96% water content, cucumbers are excellent for keeping you hydrated. Staying well-hydrated is important for overall health and can even help prevent overeating. Sometimes, when we feel hungry, we're actually just thirsty, and drinking enough water can help prevent unnecessary snacking. Including cucumbers in your diet is a great way to boost hydration, which can, in turn, support weight loss efforts by reducing feelings of hunger. However, hydration alone won't lead to fat loss.

Do cucumbers boost your metabolism? No, cucumbers do not significantly boost metabolism. There's no solid scientific evidence to support the idea that cucumbers increase metabolism. Metabolism is mainly influenced by factors like your age, genetics, body composition, and activity level. While certain foods (like those high in protein) can slightly increase metabolism due to the energy required to digest them, cucumbers don't have this effect.

Can eating cucumbers 2-3 times a day help you lose weight in the long-run? Only if they're part of a balanced, calorie-controlled diet. Incorporating cucumbers into your meals a few times a day can certainly help with weight loss in the context of a broader, well-rounded eating plan. They can help reduce your overall calorie intake by replacing higher-calorie snacks or adding bulk to meals without piling on extra calories. However, relying on cucumbers alone won't lead to significant, sustainable weight loss.

Dr. P. Rammanohar, Research Director at the Amrita Centre for Advanced Research in Ayurveda (ĀCĀRA), explains, "In Ayurveda, obesity is considered a challenging condition to treat. The texts even state that it is almost incurable, saying 'na hi sthulasya bheshajam'. There is no miracle cure for obesity. No single medicine, whether internal or external, can solve the problem. The main approach to treatment involves stress management, lifestyle changes, and diet. Medicines, both external and internal, serve as supportive measures. The more patients follow the comprehensive treatment plan, the better the outcomes. Obesity also requires a personalised treatment approach."

Manasi Banduni, Senior nutritionist, Clinic Living Plus, Bangalore said, "To lose weight and keep it off, you need to focus on creating a healthy eating pattern that includes a variety of nutrient-dense foods, not just cucumbers. A diet rich in vegetables, lean proteins, whole grains, and healthy fats, paired with regular physical activity, is the best approach for long-term weight management."

Dietitian Priyanka suggests, "Fat loss requires a multi-faceted approach. To effectively lose fat, it's important to first identify the underlying cause of weight gain, such as inflammation, a leaky gut, hormone imbalances, toxins, low metabolism, or the use of medications like steroids. Once the cause is identified, you can then adjust your diet and lifestyle to address it and promote fat loss."

title: Fact Check: Can eating dates cure bed-wetting in kids?
claim_text: Eating dates can cure bed-wetting in kids.
quick_take: A social media post claims that eating dates can cure bed-wetting in kids. We did the fact check to term this claim as False.
doctor_explanation:
No, eating dates cannot cure bed-wetting in children. Bed-wetting, also called nocturnal enuresis, is a common issue in kids, especially those under the age of 5. Although dates are rich in nutrients like potassium, magnesium, and fibre, there is no scientific evidence supporting the claim that they can directly treat bed-wetting. Bed-wetting is generally a developmental issue that can result from various factors. Studies have not proven that dietary interventions, including dates, address the underlying causes of bed-wetting.

Dr Unmesh Upadhyay, President of Paediatric Association of Ahemdabad (2023-24), Founder and Senior Consultant Pediatrician at Vismay Childcare Hospital, Ahmedabad says: "Bed-wetting is a common occurrence in children, often due to factors such as delayed bladder development, deep sleep, hormonal imbalances, obstructive sleep apnea or snoring, constipation, and stress. It may also be hereditary. While it can be concerning for parents, most children grow out of it over time."

Dr Upadhyay further explains: "Effective management strategies include regular voiding during the daytime, passing urine before bedtime, avoiding high-sugar and caffeine-based drinks, and keeping a diary of bed-wetting events. Regulating fluid intake is also helpful, with daily intake ideally divided into 40% in the morning (7 AM to 12 PM), 40% in the afternoon (12 PM to 5 PM), and 20% in the late evening (after 5 PM). Using bed-wetting alarms is another option. Although dates are nutritious, there is no scientific evidence to suggest they can cure bed-wetting, as the condition is not influenced by diet."

Dr Sudip Chowdhury, Senior Consultant in Pediatrics and Neonates Dept, Manipal Hospitals, Gurugram states: "Bedwetting, or nocturnal enuresis, is common in children, especially under the age of 5. Common causes include delayed bladder development, hormonal imbalances like low production of antidiuretic hormone (ADH), deep sleeping, genetics, emotional stress, constipation, and, in some cases, medical conditions like UTIs or diabetes. Management typically involves behavioral strategies such as regular toilet trips before bed and limiting evening fluids, bedwetting alarms to train the child to wake when the bladder is full, and sometimes medications like desmopressin. Emotional support is crucial, as bedwetting is often beyond the child's control. Although dates are a healthy food, they cannot cure bedwetting. Dietary changes alone, such as eating dates, are not a proven solution."

Dr Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition says: "No single food can directly prevent or cure bed-wetting in children. Providing a balanced diet to your child is important for their overall health, adding foods like dates won't have an impact on bed-wetting. Instead, it's more helpful to focus on healthy eating habits and limiting fluids—especially sugary or caffeinated drinks—later in the day, as these can increase the chances of bed-wetting. If bed-wetting continues to be a concern, it's always a good idea to talk to a healthcare professional rather than trying to fix it through diet alone."

Bed-wetting can happen due to a combination of factors, and diet alone does not play a significant role in preventing or treating the condition. Bed-wetting can also be a complication of juvenile diabetes due to increased urination caused by high blood sugar levels. None of these causes can be directly influenced by the consumption of dates. There are no specific dietary changes that are scientifically proven to cure or significantly reduce bed-wetting. It is advisable to avoid excess fluid intake, especially caffeinated or sugary drinks, in the evening. Proven methods to manage bed-wetting include behavioral strategies, bedwetting alarms, and sometimes medications like desmopressin — dietary interventions are not one of them.

title: Can eating flaxseed oil with paneer really cure cancer? - THIP Media
claim_text: Consuming flaxseeds and paneer (cottage cheese) can cure cancer
quick_take: A social media post claims that a budwig diet can cure cancer. We fact checked and found the claim to be false.
doctor_explanation:
The Budwig diet is a nutritional approach developed in the 1950s by German biochemist Dr. Johanna Budwig. At its core, the diet combines cottage cheese (or quark) with flaxseed oil, often taken alongside fruits, vegetables, and whole grains. Advocates claim this mixture supports cell health and may even help in managing diseases, including cancer.

Does this combination cure cancer?
No, the combination of flaxseed oil and cottage cheese does not cure cancer. Although flaxseed oil contains omega-3 fatty acids and cottage cheese is rich in protein, there is no scientific evidence or clinical trial proving that this mixture can treat or cure the disease. At most, it may play a small role in supporting a balanced diet and overall health. However, it should never be used as a substitute for proven medical treatments such as surgery, chemotherapy, or radiotherapy prescribed by doctors.

How is this combination supposed to work?
Dr. Budwig believed that mixing flaxseed oil, rich in omega-3 fatty acids, with sulfur-containing proteins from cottage cheese created a powerful nutritional combination. According to the claimant, this mixture could improve oxygen supply to cells, enhance cellular metabolism, and support detoxification. The Budwig diet theory is that unsaturated fatty acids, especially linoleic and linolenic acids, play a vital role in keeping cell membranes healthy. Without them cells would become oxygen-deficient and prone to disease. By combining flaxseed oil with protein-rich cottage cheese, Budwig believed that stored energy could be released, boosting cellular function. While this sounds promising, it is based on scientific understanding from the mid-20th century. Today, we know fatty acids are important for health, but research has not confirmed the dramatic effects that Budwig described.

Does any research say about the Budwig diet?
The biggest limitation of the Budwig diet is the absence of clinical research. There are no controlled studies proving that this diet can treat or cure cancer. Much of the support comes from personal stories rather than scientific evidence. That said, parts of the diet such as eating more vegetables, fruits, whole grains, and healthy fats, do align with modern dietary guidelines. These habits may help lower cancer risk indirectly by supporting a healthy weight, reducing inflammation, and improving overall well-being. Still, experts warn against seeing the Budwig diet as an alternative to medical care. Cancer requires evidence-based treatments such as chemotherapy, radiotherapy, surgery, or targeted therapies depending on the case. Nutrition can complement these treatments, but it cannot replace them.

What do experts recommend for diet and cancer?
Voomika Mukherjee, a Health and Nutrition Life Coach, explains that avoiding or eating certain foods alone cannot guarantee cancer prevention. Instead, she highlights maintaining a healthy body weight, lowering visceral fat, building muscle strength, and following a balanced diet. Limiting sugar, caffeine, salt, and alcohol also helps reduce long-term health risks.

Shivashankar T., Chief Clinical Nutritionist at Tata Memorial Cancer Hospital, Mumbai, points to the Mediterranean diet as one of the most effective approaches. This diet encourages high intake of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, nuts, olive oil, fish, and poultry while reducing red meat. It supports the immune system and helps maintain a healthy weight, both crucial during cancer treatment and recovery.

Should you try the Budwig diet?
The Budwig diet is an interesting nutritional idea that mixes flaxseed oil with cottage cheese to promote better cell function. While it includes healthy components like omega-3 fats and whole foods, there is no scientific proof that it treats or cures cancer. Cancer is a complex condition that requires proper medical care. Nutrition can play a supportive role, helping patients stay strong, recover faster, and reduce long-term risks, but it cannot replace standard treatments. The strongest evidence today supports balanced eating patterns like the Mediterranean diet rather than single 'miracle' food combinations.

title: Fact Check: Can eating gooseberry improve fertility?
claim_text: Eating gooseberry (amla) flushes out toxins, regulates the menstrual cycle, and causes hormonal balance, thereby improving fertility in women.
quick_take: A social media post claims that eating gooseberry improves fertility. The post further recommends women should eat it regularly. We fact-checked and found the claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: Gooseberry, also known as amla, is a fruit that is rich in vitamin C and various antioxidants. Amla is often considered a beneficial fruit for overall health due to its nutritional content. We found no scientific evidence that confirms eating gooseberry improves fertility. While maintaining a balanced diet and consuming nutrient-rich foods is generally advisable for overall health, specific claims related to fertility, detoxification, and hormonal balance require more substantial scientific evidence. Menstrual cycles can vary in length and regularity for various reasons, including hormonal imbalances, stress, underlying medical conditions, and lifestyle factors. However, there is limited scientific evidence to support the specific claims that consuming gooseberry is rich in antioxidants such as vitamin C and phenolics, so it may reduce oxidative stress to improve fertility. Oxidative stress happens when there's an imbalance between harmful particles (free radicals) and protective agents (antioxidants) in your body. This can make it harder for your body to work properly, including your ability to have babies. Menstrual cycle regularity and hormonal balance are complex processes influenced by various factors, including genetics, lifestyle, and underlying health conditions. Likewise, fertility is a complex process influenced by multiple factors, including hormonal balance, ovulation, and reproductive organ health. While gooseberry is a nutritious fruit, there is limited scientific evidence to suggest that it directly improves fertility or enhances the chances of conception. Fertility-related concerns are best addressed through a comprehensive approach, including medical evaluations, lifestyle modifications, and, if necessary, assisted reproductive techniques. The concept of flushing out toxins is often mentioned in alternative health practices. However, the human body has its own detoxification mechanisms primarily performed by the liver, kidneys, and lymphatic system. While antioxidants found in gooseberry may have potential benefits for overall health, the claim that they can specifically flush out toxins from the body is not supported by robust scientific evidence. While a study suggests that certain nutrients, such as vitamin C found in gooseberry, may have a positive impact on reproductive health, more research is needed to establish a direct link between gooseberry consumption and menstrual cycle regulation. Dr. Puja Sharma, a gynecologist based in Delhi, states: "Amla or Indian gooseberry has vitamin c and antioxidants like vitamin K and carotenoids. Antioxidants can eat up free radicals to prevent cell damage. So, eating amla can be beneficial for a healthy menstrual cycle and support endometrial growth. However, it does not mean that people should rely on amla to improve fertility. They must visit a doctor to find any health-related issue". Besides this, hormonal balance is crucial for overall well-being, including reproductive health. While gooseberry is a good source of vitamin C and antioxidants, which may have general health benefits, its direct impact on hormonal balance is not well-documented. Hormonal imbalances can result from various factors, and addressing them typically requires a comprehensive approach, including medical evaluation and potential hormone therapy if necessary.

title: Fact Check: Can eating green chillies cure heart attacks?
claim_text: Eating green chillies during a heart attack can cure it or make it go away.
quick_take: A social media post claims that eating green chillies can cure heart attacks. We did the fact check and termed this claim as False.
doctor_explanation: There is no evidence that green chillies can treat a heart attack. They contain capsaicin, a compound known for its potential health benefits. However, these benefits do not extend to curing heart attacks. Capsaicin is known to have anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which can be part of a healthy diet. However, during a heart attack, the heart is in a state of distress, requiring immediate medical intervention. A 2017 study suggests that capsaicin may be beneficial for heart health because it helps improve HDL cholesterol levels and reduces other risk factors for coronary heart disease, such as triglycerides and inflammation. However, these effects are long-term and not particularly useful in emergency situations. In fact, consuming chilli may further stimulate or irritate the person, causing additional discomfort. Dr Annusuiya Gohil, MD Scholar at the All India Institute of Ayurveda, states, "For individuals undergoing a heart attack, eating something at home is not advisable. While Ayurveda offers numerous remedies and practices for promoting heart health, emergency care and the treatment of critical organs require significant attention. Additionally, there are restrictions concerning certain medications. Allopathy excels in emergency care and should be utilised when necessary. After the patient is stable, they may consider alternative medicine for ongoing cardiac health." Dr Amit Bhushan Sharma, Associate Director and Unit Head of Cardiology at Paras Hospitals, Gurugram, explains, "A heart attack or stroke can occur when a piece of plaque breaks off and enters the bloodstream, obstructing blood flow." He adds, "Blockages in the arteries may also lead to conditions such as brain strokes, angina, and peripheral artery disease." When plaque builds up inside the arteries, they can become blocked, restricting blood flow. While no specific food can remove plaque, maintaining a healthy diet can help in the prevention and management of heart disease. Dr Swati Dave, PhD in Food & Nutrition, says, "Relying on food for heart attack treatment is risky because, in an emergency, immediate medical intervention is essential. While a healthy diet is vital for long-term heart health, no food can replace the urgent care needed to restore blood flow during a heart attack. Delaying proper treatment in favour of home remedies can have serious, even life-threatening consequences." During a heart attack, blood flow to part of the heart is blocked, usually by a clot, causing damage to the heart muscle. Typical symptoms include chest pain, shortness of breath, and nausea. Atypical symptoms, such as jaw pain, fatigue, or indigestion, can also occur, especially in women. In such situations, time is critical—every second counts, and only medical intervention, like medication or surgery, can save lives.

title: Fact Check: Can eating guava daily clean the arteries?

However, it's important to understand that while guava can certainly help manage cholesterol and blood pressure, it won't clear blockages in your arteries. Atherosclerosis, or the build-up of plaque in the arteries, is a serious condition that requires medical attention and treatment. Guava can be a wonderful addition to a heart-healthy diet. But, it should be seen as part of a broader approach to maintaining cardiovascular health, which includes regular exercise, a balanced diet, and following your doctor's advice." While guava is full of healthy compounds like Vitamin C, antioxidants, and fibre, it can't actually clean or clear blockages in your arteries. The build-up of plaque in your arteries (atherosclerosis) is a serious health issue that requires proper treatment, not just a diet change. Eating guava can help support overall heart health, but it won't undo any damage already done to your arteries. Regarding the 1960s Vitamin C study mentioned in the claim: Vitamin C has long been considered beneficial for heart health. Several studies have explored the benefits of Vitamin C for heart health, though it remains unclear whether Vitamin C alone can effectively prevent or treat atherosclerosis in humans. A 2008 study suggests that consuming more antioxidant vitamins (C, E, and beta-carotene) can lower the risk of heart disease, particularly when obtained from food. However, Vitamin C supplements did not show a strong effect. While Vitamin C is beneficial for overall health, it is not a magic cure for clogged arteries. Vitamin C is good for your heart in many ways - it helps reduce inflammation, protect blood vessels, lower blood pressure, and improve blood flow. But taking high doses of Vitamin C won't clear out plaque or reverse heart disease. Dr Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition, says, "Guava is an excellent addition to a heart-healthy diet. Rich in fibre, antioxidants, and Vitamin C, it helps lower cholesterol levels, reduce inflammation, and support overall heart function. While it won't reverse heart disease or clear blockages, regularly eating guava can contribute to better heart health when combined with a balanced diet and an active lifestyle. Think of it as part of a bigger picture for maintaining a healthy heart." title: Fact Check: Can eating hot sauce, chocolate brownie, or cereal before bed be fatal?
claim_text: An Instagram post claims that eating hot sauce, chocolate brownies, and cereals before bed can be fatal. It states that hot sauce, due to capsaicin, burns the tongue, relaxes the oesophageal valve, and allows stomach acid to flood the throat, supposedly damaging cells overnight. Chocolate brownies, with their high sugar content, cause an insulin spike, trigger adrenaline, overwork the heart, and fragment sleep. Cereals, containing refined carbs, cause a sharp insulin surge and blood sugar crash, leading to 'survival mode,' fat storage, cortisol release, and even pauses in breathing. The video also recommends shilajit to reduce stress and improve sleep.
quick_take: A social media post claims that eating hot sauce, chocolate brownie, or cereal before bed can be fatal. Our fact check shows this claim is mostly false.
doctor_explanation:
## Can hot sauce let stomach acid flood your throat as you sleep?
Possibly, though it's overstated. Hot sauce contains capsaicin, which can cause temporary discomfort like heartburn or acid reflux, especially if consumed in excess. However, the claim exaggerates the effects. While spicy foods may cause irritation or disturb sleep for some people, they do not cause severe cellular damage or pose life-threatening risks. The oesophageal valve can loosen due to reflux, but this usually leads to symptoms like indigestion—not death. In fact, some research suggests that moderate consumption of chili (rich in capsaicin) may even lower the risk of dying from certain health conditions.

## Can eating chocolate brownies cause a dangerous adrenaline surge while you sleep?
No, this is misleading. While chocolate contains sugar and caffeine that might disrupt sleep if eaten close to bedtime, there's no evidence that a sugar spike from chocolate brownies can trigger an "adrenaline surge" that makes your heart dangerously overactive. Claims that it sends the brain "into panic mode" are also exaggerated. Regular excessive sugar intake can impact sleep quality, but occasional consumption won't cause sudden heart strain or death. According to the American Heart Association, dark chocolate has heart-friendly flavonoids that may reduce the risk of heart disease, blood pressure, and insulin resistance. However, since most store-bought chocolate contains only low flavanol levels, experts suggest enjoying it in moderation.
Dr Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition, explains, "Eating chocolate brownies at bedtime isn't likely to cause a dangerous adrenaline surge, but it could affect your sleep. Brownies contain sugar and caffeine, which may keep you awake or disrupt deep sleep cycles. Regular overconsumption of sugary foods can also lead to issues like insulin resistance and weight gain. To enjoy brownies without harming your health, it's best to eat them occasionally, earlier in the day, and balance them with a nutrient-rich diet."

## Can eating cereal cause a blood sugar crash so severe your brain forgets to breathe?
Absolutely not. Cereal with refined carbohydrates can cause a temporary insulin spike, which might lead to mild blood sugar drops later. However, the body has mechanisms to prevent a total "crash." A drop in blood sugar won't make your brain forget to breathe. Severe blood sugar drops, like in untreated diabetes, can cause serious complications, but this scenario is highly unlikely in healthy individuals eating cereal before bed.
Shruti K Bhardwaj, Chief Clinical Nutritionist at Zydus Hospital, Ahmedabad, states, "Sugary cereals can cause a quick rise and fall in blood sugar, which might leave you feeling sluggish or hungry soon after. However, claims that they cause a 'breathing shutdown' are exaggerated. Eating high-sugar foods close to bedtime isn't ideal, as it could disturb your sleep, but an occasional late-night cereal bowl won't harm you. For better sleep and steady energy, choose whole-grain cereals with fibre and protein, and try to finish eating at least an hour or two before bed."

## Does shilajit improve sleep and reduce cortisol?
Possibly, but it is not a magic solution. Shilajit is an herbal supplement sometimes promoted for reducing stress and improving energy. Some studies suggest it may help manage cortisol (a stress hormone), but we need more research in humans. It's not a guaranteed solution for sleep problems, and relying on it without addressing other sleep hygiene factors is unlikely to be effective.

## THIP Media Take
The claim that eating hot sauce, chocolate brownie, or cereal before bed can be fatal is mostly false. The post makes extreme, fear-based statements about common foods, exaggerating their effects on the body. Eating hot sauce, chocolate brownies, or cereal before bed might disrupt sleep for some, but it won't cause cellular damage, adrenaline surges, or life-threatening blood sugar crashes. There's no solid evidence that shilajit can magically improve sleep quality either. Balanced eating habits and good sleep hygiene are far more effective ways to support overall health.

title: Fact Check: Can eating kiwi really fix weak immunity?
claim_text: Weak immunity? Eat Kiwi!
quick_take: A social media post claims that eating kiwi is the solution for weak immunity. After fact checking, we found that this claim ismostly false.
doctor_explanation: The fact check examines three key aspects: First, does kiwi contain nutrients that support the immune system? Yes, kiwi is well-known for its high concentration of Vitamin C, a crucial nutrient that plays a significant role in various aspects of the immune system. Vitamin C supports the production and function of white blood cells, which are key players in fighting off infections. Beyond Vitamin C, kiwis also contain other vitamins and antioxidants, such as Vitamin K and Vitamin E, along with fibre, all of which contribute to overall health and indirectly support a healthy immune response. Dr Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition, explains, 'Yes, kiwi is a nutrient-rich fruit that supports the immune system. It's especially high in vitamin C, which helps your body fight off infections by supporting white blood cell function. Kiwi also provides vitamin K, vitamin E, folate, and antioxidants, all of which contribute to reducing inflammation and protecting cells from damage. Its natural fibre also supports gut health, which plays a big role in how well your immune system works.' Second, can eating kiwi alone cure weak immunity? No, eating kiwi alone may not cure weak immunity in everyone. Although kiwi is a beneficial addition to a healthy diet, no single food can cure weak immunity. Immune function is a complex interplay of various factors, including genetics, overall nutritional intake, sleep quality, stress levels, physical activity, and underlying health conditions. Relying solely on kiwi to address weak immunity would be an oversimplification and could lead to neglecting other critical aspects of health that are vital for a strong immune system. A balanced diet that includes a wide variety of fruits, vegetables, lean proteins, and whole grains, alongside a healthy lifestyle, is essential for supporting immunity. The article also notes that some claim kiwi fruit can cure eye diseases and improve eyesight, but this is yet another oversimplification not backed by solid evidence. Third, is kiwi a good addition to a healthy diet for immune support? Yes, absolutely, including kiwi into a balanced and varied diet can contribute to supporting your immune system. Its rich nutrient profile makes it a good choice as part of an overall healthy eating pattern. However, even with a nutritious diet that includes foods like kiwi, some people may still experience a weakened immune response. Factors such as chronic stress, poor sleep, smoking, excessive alcohol use, and prolonged use of certain medications (like steroids or immunosuppressants) can all impact immune health. Underlying conditions such as diabetes, autoimmune disorders, cancer, HIV, or other chronic illnesses can also compromise immunity. If someone experiences frequent infections, slow wound healing, constant fatigue, or other persistent symptoms, it may be a sign of an underlying issue that requires medical attention. In such cases, dietary changes alone may not be enough, and a doctor's evaluation becomes essential. Shruti K Bhardwaj, Chief Clinical Nutritionist at Zydus Hospital, Ahmedabad, explains, 'Kiwi is a great fruit to include in your daily diet if you're looking to support your immune system. It's not just rich in vitamin C, and one kiwi can actually provide more than the daily recommended intake. It also contains vitamin E, potassium, folate, and dietary fibre. These nutrients work together to reduce inflammation, protect against oxidative stress, and keep your gut healthy, which is closely linked to immune function. While kiwi alone won't prevent illness, adding it to a balanced, colourful diet can certainly give your immune health a helpful boost.' THIP Media Take concludes that while kiwi offers valuable nutrients that support immune health, the claim that simply eating kiwi can fix weak immunity is an overstatement. Immune strength depends on a holistic approach to health, not just one food.

title: Fact Check: Can eating Kulthi lentils cure gallstones in 15 days?
claim_text: You can get rid of gallstones in just 15 days by regularly eating Kulthi lentil (Horse Gram). The post implies you can cure gallstones at home.
quick_take: A social media post claims that eating Kulthi lentils can cure gallstones in 15 days only. We did the fact check to term it as False.
doctor_explanation: Gallstones are solid deposits that form in the gallbladder which mainly consist of cholesterol or bilirubin. Once formed, these stones do not dissolve through diet alone. Kulthi lentils are rich in fibre and nutrients. However, there is no evidence to suggest that they can break down or eliminate gallstones. A 2022 review highlights the traditional use of Kulthi for treating kidney stones, but it does not provide any proven evidence of its effectiveness, and it says nothing about its ability to cure gallstones. Similarly, a 2014 review mentions Kulthi's anecdotal and traditional use in treating kidney and urinary stones, without addressing its role in gallstone treatment. Research into gallstones highlights various dietary factors that may influence their formation but does not endorse any specific food as a cure. For example, a 2023 study indicates that a high-fibre diet can reduce the risk of gallstone development. However, this does not mean that eating specific foods like Kulthi lentils can dissolve existing stones. Additionally, evidence shows that dietary modifications can play a role in gallstone prevention. A balanced diet rich in fruits, vegetables, and whole grains, combined with healthy fats, can support overall gallbladder health. However, existing gallstones need medical treatment, ranging from observation to surgical options, depending on their size and symptoms. Dr Prerna Chaudhary, BAMS, Founder of Shri Shubhda Ayurveda Wellness Clinic, Gurugram, provides Ayurvedic perspective: 'No, Ayurveda has no such interventional medicinal treatment for gallstones. However, according to Acharya Sushruta (the father of Ayurvedic Surgery), gallstones are a type of Shalya (foreign body) formed through a disbalance of doshas. These Shalyas should be removed from the body through Shalya Karma (surgical management). According to the radiological size of gallstones (Pitta-Ashmari), those below 3-4 mm can be dissolved using Ayurvedic medicines as prescribed by an Ayurvedic physician.' Dr Sharad Malhotra, Senior Consultant & HOD Gastroenterology Hepatology & Therapeutic Endoscopy, Aakash Healthcare, New Delhi, states: 'While a balanced diet, including foods like Kulthi lentils, is essential for overall health, it's important to understand that there is no evidence that these lentils can dissolve gallstones. Gallstones are solid masses that form in the gallbladder and cannot simply break down through dietary changes. The presence of gallstones indicates that the gallbladder is not functioning properly, making surgical removal the most effective treatment for many individuals. It's crucial to consult a healthcare professional for a proper diagnosis and guidance on the best course of treatment.' Shruti K Bhardwaj, Chief Clinical Nutritionist at Zydus Hospital, Ahmedabad, says: 'It's a myth that Kulthi Dal can help cure gallbladder stones. To reduce the risk of gallstones, one should avoid very low-calorie diets, eat a balanced diet that includes healthy fat sources, and maintain a healthy weight. Additionally, it's important to verify the credentials of those providing information. Qualified professionals discuss evidence-based practices.' Malvika Fulwani, Founder and Chief Dietician, Healthitude, explains: 'Research shows that a diet rich in nutrient-dense foods like fruits, vegetables, and whole grains can significantly lower the risk of developing gallstones, while diets high in refined sugars and unhealthy fats, especially fried and fatty foods, may increase the risk. The gallbladder, which stores bile from the liver, is compromised when poor dietary patterns are followed, leading to a higher incidence of gallstones and other gallbladder conditions.' She further explains: 'Diets such as the Mediterranean and DASH, which emphasise lean proteins, whole foods, and healthy fats, have been shown to support gallbladder health. Foods rich in fibre, including legumes, cruciferous vegetables, and whole grains, aid digestion and may reduce gallstone formation. Healthy fats from sources like olive oil, nuts, and omega-3-rich fish also promote proper gallbladder function and bile flow.' Dr Swati Dave, PhD in Food & Nutrition, says: 'A healthy balanced diet is applicable to everyone. We need to know the cause of gallstones before starting any diet to prevent gallstones. A more fibrous and less fatty food diet is advisable. This combination means that for people with diabetes, mangoes are likely to increase blood sugar levels. While mangoes and other sweet fruits do contain beneficial fiber, calcium, and potassium, their high sugar content and glycemic index are the primary factors impacting blood sugar for individuals with diabetes. Research by Jennie Brand-Miller and colleagues showed that replacing high GI foods with low-GI options can significantly improve medium-term blood glucose control. Bananas provide essential nutrients that support eye health but they are not a magical cure for vision problems caused by refractive errors (like myopia or hyperopia), cataracts, glaucoma, or other underlying medical conditions. Claims of rapid and dramatic improvements in vision from a single food item are usually baseless and people should view them with scepticism. title: Fact Check: Can eating peanut butter improve oxygen in your body and strengthen bones? - THIP Media
claim_text: Peanut butter contains iron and Calcium and helps to improve oxygen in blood. Some other posts claim that peanut butter helps to transfer extra oxygen to bones and make them strong.
quick_take: A social media post a few health blogs claim that eating peanut butter can help to improve the Oxygen level in our body. Some other posts claim that peanut butter distributes oxygen to bones and make them strong. We fact-checked and found that the claim is half true.
doctor_explanation:
The claim about improving blood oxygen levels is partially true but misleading. Iron rich diet can improve haemoglobin, the red protein that facilitates transporting oxygen in the blood. While the haemoglobin holds the Oxygen, it is the red blood cells (RBC) that carries the haemoglobin transporting it to the different tissues in the body. Hence, count of RBC is another defining factor in blood Oxygen level. But the most important factor that decides the Oxygen level in our body is the health of our lungs (and overall respiratory system). The respiratory system controls the amount of Oxygen we can take in to our body and transfer to the internal cells. Experts usually suggest a combination of good diet, regular exercise, and lifestyle improvements like reducing smoking habits to improve blood oxygen level.

Dr. Ambrish Srivastava, MBBS, MD says, "Oxygen saturation is mainly a function of lungs. In anaemic patients, an iron rich diet can help improve the haemoglobin and thereby flow of Oxygen in blood to some extent. But if your lungs suffer, no amount of iron rich diet will be able to replace the function of the lungs."

Dr. S Krishna Prasanthi, MBBS, MD (PGIMER) agrees, "Diet has an effect on improving haemoglobin levels to a certain extent which plays a part in Oxygen distribution of the body. But it will be a wrong statement to make if we say diet can improve blood oxygen levels."

Regarding the claim about peanut butter improving oxygen in blood: The claim is based on the fact that peanut butter is a rich source of iron that will improve blood Oxygen levels. However, the claim is not true. Peanut butter can help in proper distribution of Oxygen to certain extent but cannot increase the amount of Oxygen in body. Dr. Srivastava says, "There are some nutrition value in Peanut butter to suggest it as a good dietary supplement in moderate amount. But it has no relation with blood Oxygen levels." Dr. Prasanthi says, "there is nothing special in peanut butter that can improve blood Oxygen level."

Regarding bone strength: Not exactly. It can play a role in some cases but yet, not recommended by experts. The claim is based on the fact that peanut butter has calcium that improves bone strength. This is true to some extent. As per USDA, per 100 gm of peanut butter has 43 mg of Calcium. However, this is far lower than Calcium present in peanuts (92 mg per 100 gm). The further claim that peanut butter has iron which helps transfer oxygen to blood to improve bone health. This claim is also partially true. Dr. Srivastava says, "Oxygen is required by bones and all parts of the body. If Oxygen is present in blood it gets absorbed by body organs. That's a normal process. There is no extra requirement of oxygen to strengthen bones. Also, peanut butter is no super food that can contribute to bone health. There are a number of other calcium rich foods." Dr. Prasanthi says, "It is an established fact that oxygen is critical for both bone repair and development. But there is nothing exceptionally special about peanut butter to facilitate the process. The iron content of peanut butter is merely 1.9 mg per 100 gm. There are a number of other cost effective yet iron rich food available. For example, jaggery has 10 to 11 mg iron per 100 gm. I don't think it makes sense to relate peanut butter to source of iron."

Peanut butter is full of fibre, mineral and nutrients which makes it a fairly nutritious food. However, it is also high on calories which can also be detrimental to body weight and heart health, if consumed in larger amounts. In moderate amounts, peanut butter is not known to pose any health risks.

They also contain magnesium, which can help in relaxation and reduce muscle tension, and niacin (vitamin B3), which supports brain function and relaxation. Insomnia is a complex sleep disorder caused by various factors like stress, mental health issues, lifestyle habits, and medical conditions. Eating peanuts alone will not fix underlying sleep problems. Research on insomnia treatment mainly focuses on cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT), lifestyle changes, and, in some cases, medication. While peanuts have nutrients that may support relaxation, they are not a cure. The claim that peanuts can "strengthen brainwaves and frequencies" lacks scientific basis. Brainwaves are patterns of electrical activity in the brain, and their regulation is influenced by factors like sleep cycles, mental activity, and external stimuli. While peanuts provide healthy fats and antioxidants that support overall brain health, they do not have a specific effect on brainwave activity or frequency modulation. Scientific studies on brain function and nutrition focus more on a balanced diet, including omega-3 fatty acids, which are found in fish and flaxseeds, rather than peanuts alone. There are also risks of eating peanuts before bed: they are high in calories and fats, which take time to digest. Eating too many before bed may cause bloating, acid reflux, or discomfort. They also contain tyrosine, which can be mildly stimulating for some. People with peanut allergies should avoid them, as even a small amount can trigger severe reactions. Poorly stored peanuts may develop aflatoxin, a toxin that can harm the liver. Peanuts also have phytic acid, which slightly reduces iron and zinc absorption. They can be part of a healthy routine, but anyone noticing ongoing hair thinning should speak to a dermatologist for proper diagnosis and treatment." There are also viral claims suggesting that watermelon seeds are the most nutritious among all seeds, or that almonds and dry fruits are a "nutritional scam." These statements are often misleading. All seeds and nuts have unique benefits when eaten in the right amount. No single food is a miracle fix or a scam, it all comes down to balance and overall dietary habits. Zinc and phytosterols may offer some support. Pumpkin seeds contain zinc, which plays a role in tissue growth and repair, including the scalp and hair follicles. Zinc deficiency has been linked to hair thinning in some studies. These seeds also contain phytosterols, which some lab studies suggest might help block DHT (a hormone linked to hair loss in both men and women). But again, most of the evidence is indirect. There are no high-quality clinical trials showing that pumpkin seeds, when eaten regularly, can stop or reverse hair loss in humans. Maybe, but the evidence is still limited. Some small studies have looked at pumpkin seed oil supplements. One 2014 Korean study found that men with androgenic alopecia (male pattern baldness) who took 400 mg of pumpkin seed oil daily for 24 weeks saw a modest increase in hair count compared to those who didn't. However, this study used concentrated oil in capsules, not whole seeds, and had a small sample size. This doesn't prove that eating pumpkin seeds has the same effect. We still need more research to confirm these findings. Yes, in moderation. Pumpkin seeds are a healthy snack and provide protein, fibre, antioxidants, and key minerals. Including them in your diet is safe for most people and can support general wellness. But expecting them to "cure" hair loss is misleading. Also, excessive intake might lead to digestive issues due to high fat and fibre content. So, moderation is key. Dr Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition, explains, "Yes, pumpkin seeds are absolutely safe for most people and can be a great addition to a balanced diet. They're packed with nutrients like zinc, magnesium, iron, protein, and healthy fats that support everything from immunity to heart and hair health. I often recommend a small handful a day as a wholesome snack or topping for salads, soups, or porridge. Just remember, they're high in fat and fibre, so eating too much at once can upset your stomach. Keep it balanced and enjoy them as part of your daily routine." There are also claims that a compound in pumpkin seeds called cucurbitin may help get rid of worms and parasites. This may be partly true, but it is not a proven or reliable treatment. THIP Media Take: The claim that eating pumpkin seeds can prevent hair loss is mostly false. While pumpkin seeds are nutritious and may indirectly support scalp and hair health, there is no strong clinical evidence that eating them can prevent or treat hair loss. Claims suggesting they can stop hair loss on their own are exaggerated. A balanced diet, proper medical assessment, and evidence-based treatment remain the best approach for managing hair loss.

title: Can eating raw turmeric prevent autoimmune diseases and extend life?
claim_text: Eating raw turmeric daily can prevent autoimmune diseases forever, protect against cancer and flu permanently, balance Vata, Pitta and Kapha doshas, make skin glow, and help you live a healthy, 100-year-long life.
quick_take: A social media post claims that eating raw turmeric can prevent autoimmune diseases and extend life. We fact checked this claim and found it to be mostly false.
doctor_explanation: No, eating raw turmeric cannot prevent autoimmune diseases forever. These diseases occur when the immune system attacks healthy tissues due to genetic, environmental, and lifestyle factors. Turmeric contains curcumin, known for its anti-inflammatory properties, but there's no proof that eating it daily prevents conditions like rheumatoid arthritis or lupus. Studies show curcumin may reduce inflammation and improve symptoms in autoimmune diseases. A 2007 study found it helpful for multiple sclerosis and rheumatoid arthritis. A 2019 review noted similar benefits for osteoarthritis and ulcerative colitis. However, curcumin is poorly absorbed by the body, limiting its effects. Adding piperine (from black pepper) or using modified curcumin may help, but more research is needed to confirm its safety, dosage, and effectiveness. Dr Almas Fatma clarifies: 'Turmeric has potential anti-inflammatory benefits due to its active compound, curcumin, but expecting it to prevent autoimmune diseases entirely is unrealistic. Autoimmune conditions are complex, involving genetic and environmental factors that turmeric alone cannot control. While some research suggests curcumin may help manage symptoms by reducing inflammation, its poor absorption in the body limits its impact. For better effectiveness, combining curcumin with black pepper (which contains piperine) can enhance absorption, but even then, it's not a substitute for medical treatment. Managing autoimmune diseases typically requires a combination of lifestyle changes, medication, and regular medical care.' Turmeric must also be used cautiously. High doses or prolonged use may irritate the stomach, cause nausea, ulcers, or worsen gallbladder problems. It can increase bleeding risk for people with bleeding disorders or those taking blood thinners like aspirin. Additionally, raw turmeric contains bioactive compounds that can be harmful if not dried properly. Regarding cancer: No, turmeric cannot fully prevent cancer or viral infections like the flu. While curcumin, a compound in turmeric, has shown antioxidant and anti-cancer potential in lab studies, these effects were observed mainly with high-dose curcumin extracts used in research—not from consuming small amounts of raw turmeric. There is no scientific evidence proving that eating turmeric can eliminate cancer risk or cure the disease. Dr Pooja Khullar, Radiation Oncologist explains: 'No single food, including turmeric, can completely prevent or cure cancer. Cancer prevention requires a holistic approach, including a balanced diet rich in fruits and vegetables, regular physical activity, avoiding smoking and alcohol, limiting sun exposure, and attending routine health check-ups. While turmeric's curcumin shows promise in lab studies, effective cancer treatment relies on targeted medical therapies. Prioritising overall health and seeking professional advice are essential.' Turmeric's anti-inflammatory properties may also help ease mild cold symptoms, but it doesn't provide guaranteed or lifelong protection against flu or viral infections. Preventing the flu typically requires regular vaccinations and maintaining good hygiene. Regarding skin and longevity: No, eating turmeric cannot guarantee glowing skin or a disease-free 100-year life. Turmeric is known for its antioxidant effects, which may support skin health by reducing oxidative stress. However, glowing skin depends on nutrition, hydration, and skincare, not just turmeric consumption. As for longevity, there is no food or herb that can extend lifespan to 100 years. Longevity is influenced by genetics, lifestyle, and healthcare access. Regarding Ayurvedic doshas: It might help, but the effect depends on how and how much you consume it. Ayurveda views turmeric as helpful for balancing Kapha and calming Pitta when used in moderation due to its pungent, dry, and heating properties. However, excessive use can aggravate Vata and even increase Pitta, leading to issues like dryness, constipation, acidity, or excess body heat. Dr Muskan Thakur, BAMS, Ayurveda Consultant explains: 'Turmeric can support dosha balance when used thoughtfully, but it's not a universal solution. In Ayurveda, its heating and drying qualities make it helpful for balancing Kapha and reducing Pitta when consumed in small amounts. However, excessive consumption may aggravate both Pitta and Vata due to its heat-producing and drying nature, which can lead to issues like acidity, increased body heat, or dryness. The key lies in personalised usage based on your prakriti (body constitution) and current health state. Ayurveda emphasises moderation, balance, and incorporating herbs like turmeric as part of a holistic lifestyle rather than depending on them as standalone remedies.'

title: Fact Check: Can eating soaked almonds fight cancer?
claim_text: Eating four overnight soaked almonds daily is beneficial. It improves brain function and fights cancer.
quick_take: A social media post claims that eating soaked almonds fight cancer. We fact-checked and found the claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: Soaking dried fruits is good for health as it helps break down nutrients that might stop the body from using nutrients properly, making them easier to absorb. Soaked almonds have better nutritional value and are easier to chew. They improve digestion by neutralizing enzyme inhibitors and tannins, making them easier to digest. It may also enhance nutrient absorption by reducing phytic acid content. A research paper has shown that soaked almonds can reduce phytic acid in the body. However, there is no evidence that suggests soaked almonds can fight cancer. However, almonds may reduce the risk of cancer as they are rich in several nutrients. The studies are still few in number, and reports on the efficacy of almonds against cancer still leave many aspects to be resolved. In another fact check, we have discussed that almonds can prevent certain cancers - almonds can have a protective role against prostate, breast and colon cancer. This means almonds have anti-cancer properties, so people can incorporate them in their diet. However, it is important to understand that almonds cannot provide 100% immunity against all types of cancers. Even though almonds, including soaked almonds, are a nutritious food and part of a healthy diet, it is essential to approach claims about specific foods preventing or fighting cancer with caution. The relationship between diet and cancer is complex and multifactorial. The overall impact of almonds on cancer prevention or treatment is unclear, and it is important to consider them as part of a healthy diet. Moreover, there is no significant scientific evidence to suggest that almond skins possess carcinogenic properties. Dr Kavitha Jain, Consultant Surgical Oncologist at Rangadore Memorial Hospital, Bengaluru informs, "Soaking the nut is harmless and not cancer-causing. It actually enhances the digestibility. Almond skin contain various compounds such as antioxidants and dietary fibre which contribute to their potential health-promoting effects". Dr. Sarthak Moharir, Chief Radiation Oncologist Apollo Cancer Centre, Bilaspur further adds, "Special diet or diet modifications do not cure cancer. Diet is very important for patients undergoing cancer treatment and it is advised they take a balanced meal with all macros and micronutrients as prescribed by their dietary counsellor." The American Society of Cancer website informs that cancer treatment depends on several factors such as cancer type, stage, available treatment options, and other important variables. So, people cannot rely on almonds to fight against cancer. Nutritionist Umesh Wadhawani adds, "No single food item can cause or prevent a chronic health condition. It is the amalgamation of various factors including your diet, daily routine, workplace stress, relationships, sleep, movement, etc., that affect health".

title: Fact Check: Can eating soaked almonds help in removing glasses?
claim_text: A viral post on Facebook suggests that you can get rid of your glasses by consuming soaked almonds and white pepper every morning. Additionally, the post mentions that walking on green grass with morning dew can improve eyesight and help remove spectacles.
quick_take: A post on Facebook claims that eating soaked almonds every morning, along with white pepper, can help in removing glasses. Our fact check says it's False.
doctor_explanation: Eye problems can occur due to a variety of factors, including genetic predisposition, age-related changes, environmental influences, and lifestyle habits. Common issues like refractive errors—such as myopia (nearsightedness), hyperopia (farsightedness), astigmatism, and presbyopia—arise when the shape of the eye prevents light from focusing directly on the retina, leading to blurred vision. Other eye problems can be caused by conditions like cataracts, glaucoma, and macular degeneration, or by external factors such as allergies, infections, or prolonged exposure to screens. We need glasses to correct these refractive errors and other vision problems. Glasses work by adjusting the way light enters the eye, allowing it to focus properly on the retina and providing clearer vision. While lifestyle changes and eye exercises can support overall eye health, they cannot reverse or correct the structural issues that require glasses. Therefore, glasses or contact lenses remain essential for those with vision impairments to see clearly and comfortably. Dr Neha Rastogi Panda, Senior Infectious Diseases Specialist at Fortis Hospital, Gurgaon, explains, 'Problems in the eyes can arise from various causes, including allergies, diseases and deficiencies, dust, injury and unsanitary practices like rubbing your eyes with unclean hands. These issues need prompt treatment to prevent infections or worsening of the symptoms. Relying on unproven methods can be dangerous. It's essential to seek professional medical advice and use evidence-based treatments for effective management and to maintain eye health.' Soaked almonds are a popular health food, known for their nutrient-rich profile. They are a good source of vitamins and minerals such as vitamin E, magnesium, and healthy fats. People believe that soaking almonds makes these nutrients more bioavailable and easier to digest. Some benefits of soaked almonds include improved digestion, better skin health, and potential support for brain function. There is also evidence that almonds are good for eye health. However, even though they offer numerous health benefits, the idea that they can directly improve vision to get rid of glasses at home, is not supported by scientific evidence. No, eating soaked almonds with white pepper cannot help you get rid of glasses. There is evidence that diet and nutrition can help in prevention and maintenance of eye conditions. But, there is no scientific evidence to support the claim that consuming these foods can correct refractive errors or improve vision to the extent of eliminating the need for glasses. Refractive errors are structural issues with the eye, and certain nutrients (like vitamin A and vitamin E) are essential for eye health. But, they cannot reverse conditions that require corrective lenses. The only proven methods to reduce dependence on glasses are surgical interventions like LASIK or other refractive surgeries, or using corrective lenses like contact lenses. Dr Naveen Gupta, an Ophthalmologist, explains, 'There's a difference between 'good for eye health' and 'can improve vision,' which many people tend to confuse. Almonds are high in Vitamin E, which may help delay certain eye conditions like Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD) or Cataracts. However, if by improving eyesight you mean reducing the need for spectacles, there's no connection.' Research aligns with Dr Gupta's insights, indicating that diet may play a role in delaying conditions like Cataracts and AMD. However, not all studies have reached the same conclusion. Dr Aftab Alam, Consultant ophthalmologist at Dr Aftab eye care, Bareilly, states, 'While most plant-based diets are beneficial for maintaining eye health, this does not mean they will improve vision and help you get rid of glasses at home. There is no scientific evidence to support such claims.' Dr Alam advices against believing on such unverified health claims, and always follow a healthcare professional's advice for your eye health. Ranjani Raman, Dietitian and Nutrition Therapist, explains, 'Foods beneficial for eyesight generally help maintain the current functioning of the eyes and vision in older adults. In children, during their growth phase, these vitamin A-rich foods can aid in the development of good vision.' Experts unanimously agree that diet and nutrition can help in preventing certain eye conditions, but cannot remove glasses. No, walking on green grass with morning dew cannot improve eyesight. The idea that walking on green grass with morning dew can improve eyesight or help remove spectacles is a popular folk belief, but it lacks scientific backing. Walking on grass, especially in the morning, may be calming and promote a sense of well-being. But, there is no evidence that it can correct refractive errors or enhance vision. This belief may come from the idea that grounding or earthing (walking barefoot on grass or natural surfaces) has health benefits. However, these benefits do not extend to vision correction. Improving eyesight requires addressing the underlying issues with appropriate treatments, such as corrective lenses, eye exercises for specific conditions, or surgery. No, you cannot get rid of glasses at home. Some lifestyle changes and exercises may help in maintaining overall eye health. But, there is no home remedy or food that can eliminate the need for glasses if you have a refractive error. Techniques like eye exercises or dietary changes may contribute to general eye wellness. However, they cannot alter the shape of your eye or correct vision defects. For those seeking alternatives to glasses, consulting with an eye specialist about options like contact lenses or laser eye surgery is advisable. Dr Pradeep Dahale, an Ophthalmologist at Manipal Hospital Baner, Pune, clarifies, 'Eyeglasses are prescribed by Ophthalmologists or Optometrists to correct vision issues caused by anatomical variations in the eyeball's dimensions. These variations, such as axial length and corneal curvature, cannot be altered by exercises, eye drops, or dietary supplements. Therefore, it's misguided to believe that vision can be naturally corrected without glasses.' Failing to use glasses when needed can lead to several issues, including eye strain, headaches, and blurred vision. For children, not wearing prescribed glasses can result in developmental issues like amblyopia (lazy eye). This can eventually cause permanent vision impairment if not treated. For adults, uncorrected vision can affect daily activities, such as reading, driving, and overall quality of life. It's essential to use corrective lenses as prescribed to avoid these complications. The claim that eating soaked almonds and white pepper every morning can remove the need for glasses is false. Almonds are nutritious and beneficial for overall health. But, there is no evidence to suggest they can correct refractive errors or eliminate the need for spectacles.
