title: Can your state of mind make food less poisonous? - THIP Media
claim_text: Being happy while eating can make poisonous food less harmful. The claim references an Ohio State University study where rabbits fed high-cholesterol diet but handled with love and kindness had lower cholesterol levels than rabbits not shown kindness, suggesting emotions can turn bad things into good things.
quick_take: A viral video circulating on social media claims that your state of mind while eating makes food less poisonous. However, upon fact-checking the claim, we found it to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: No. Your happy state of mind while eating does not make food less poisonous. Happiness or positive emotions cannot neutralise the harmful effects of poisonous substances in food. Contaminated foods contain toxic substances that can cause adverse reactions or damage to your body, irrespective of your emotional state. It can lead to serious health consequences regardless of your emotional state while eating. The effects of consuming such substances can range from mild discomfort to severe illness, organ damage, or even death. The person in the video has made an incorrect statement quoting the research done at the Ohio State University. We also ran a quick Google reverse image search and found that the speaker was Deepak Chopra. He is a well-known figure in the self-help and wellness industry. While he has a background in medicine as a former physician, he is now more widely recognized as a self-help guru, known for blending Eastern philosophies, alternative medicine practices, and spiritual principles into his teachings. However, Chopra's ideas have been criticized by many in the scientific community for their lack of empirical evidence and promotion of pseudoscience. In the claimed YouTube video, Chopra talks about research conducted at Ohio State University. However, the video does not have a reference link to this research. So we began our Keyword search to find this research paper online. As a result, we found a link that talks about the Rabbit Effect – a study done the Ohio State University. In the late 1970s, scientists studied rabbits on high-fat diets to investigate heart disease links. Surprisingly, those cared for with love showed significantly fewer fatty deposits in blood vessels. This sparked the rabbit effect concept, emphasizing the hidden impact of love, friendship, and dignity on our health. The study found that rabbits that were fed a high-cholesterol diet but were also handled with kindness and love, had lower cholesterol levels than rabbits that were fed the same diet but were not handled with kindness and love. Even research papers informs that stress can increase cholesterol in the body which can lead increase plaque formation in the veins. So, eating more food while being stressed can lead to higher buildup formation in the veins. The study's findings highlights that our emotions and mindset can play a role in our physical health. When we feel happy and loved, our bodies release chemicals that can have a positive impact on our health. Conversely, when we feel stressed or anxious, our bodies release chemicals that can have a negative impact on our health. It is also possible that the difference in cholesterol levels was due to the release of oxytocin, a hormone that is released during social bonding and positive interactions. Oxytocin has been shown to have a number of health benefits, including reducing inflammation and improving cardiovascular function. It is important to note that the study was conducted on rabbits, so it is not clear whether the same findings would apply to humans. However, there is a growing body of research that suggests that our emotions and mindset can have a significant impact on our overall health and well-being. So, while it is unlikely that simply being happy while eating can make poisonous food less harmful, it is possible that our emotions and mindset can play a role in how our bodies process food. Eating in a relaxed and enjoyable environment may help us to digest our food better and absorb more nutrients. Additionally, eating with loved ones and friends can promote social bonding and release oxytocin, which may have other health benefits. Dr. Sharad Malhotra, HOD, Gastroenterology, at Akash Hospital, New Delhi adds, "Positive thinking, good thoughts, and strong family support have the potential to positively impact the course of various diseases. However, this does not mean that we should completely abandon our lifestyle choices. Rather, it emphasizes the importance of moderation. People must consistently maintain a healthy lifestyle and routine checkups for their health conditions". Dr Amrita More, Plastic Surgeon informs that a positive attitude goes a long way and that a happy person makes a happy patient.

title: Fact Check: Can having a root canal cause cancer? - THIP Media
claim_text: Root canal treatment causes cancer and puts cancer patients at risk of losing their teeth
quick_take: A Twitter post asserts that root canal treatment causes cancer. We happened to verify the claim. According to our findings, the claim is False.
doctor_explanation: Root canal therapy is a dental procedure used to treat an infection in the tooth's center. The pulp is located in the center of the tooth. The pulpal infection develops when bacteria enter this region. These infections can cause a variety of symptoms, such as pain while chewing, sensitivity to hot and cold stimuli, and loose teeth. If not treated, pulpal infections can cause excruciating pain, swollen gums near the affected tooth, pus oozing from the infected area, and even visible swelling on the face. The root canal efficiently removes dead and dying pulpal tissue. Once the bacterial infection is removed, the tooth will be sealed. Additionally, to prevent future problems, a crown is placed on the tooth. During this procedure, the original tooth is left in place to help maintain the jaw's integrity. Dr. Weston A. Price proposed the theory that bacteria trapped in dentinal tubules could leak during root canal treatment. This bacterial leakage has the potential to cause nearly any type of degenerative systemic disease, including arthritis. However, this was before medicine discovered the true cause of such diseases. The American Academy of Endodontics rejected this concept and declared root canal therapy to be a safe procedure. The Journal of the American Dental Association reviewed Dr. Price's research techniques from the 1920s and found that they lacked many aspects of modern scientific research, such as the absence of proper control groups and the induction of excessive doses of bacteria. Thus, decades of research contradict Dr. Price's concept of focal infection, as there is no credible, scientific evidence linking endodontically treated teeth to systemic disease. There is almost no evidence linking root canal treatment to other diseases. No research on the links between cancer and root canals is available. There are no other studies that show any similarity, causality, or correlation between them. On the other hand, poor oral health, a lack of proper tooth brushing, tobacco use, and alcohol consumption are the primary risk factors for head, neck, and esophageal cancers. Furthermore, untreated periodontal disease and excessive mouthwash use have been identified as distinct causes of head and neck cancer. Dr. Pooja Bhardwaj, our dental expert, said: "Weston Price's 1922 focal infection theory, which claims that RCT can cause terminal cancer, is misinformation and a threat to the public because it lacks sound research." She further explained that it wasn't until 1965 that the correct technique was discovered. Prior to that, no one was aware of RCT protocols such as irrigation, debridement, medication, and so on. Thus, Price's study was unconventional and had a poor experimental design.

title: Fact Check: Can heart diseases be caused by root-canaled teeth?
claim_text: A tweet titled "Say No to Root Canal" asserts that a root canal is highly toxic and has been associated with the development of cardiac diseases. The tweet states: "More and more doctors would advise against #rootcanal. They recommend avoiding it like a plague. Find out why."
quick_take: According to a social media post, root-canaled teeth are a source of infection that contributes to the development of heart conditions. We checked the claim and our research determined that the claim is False.
doctor_explanation: Root canal treatment involves the removal of infected pulp, followed by cleaning and disinfection. Endodontic treatment aims to prevent tooth abscesses, swelling, excruciating toothache, bone loss, and infection. Once treated, it keeps the natural tooth in place and prevents severe bone damage. The root canal myth began in the 1920s when Dr. Weston Price, a dentist, popularized his theory that some chronic diseases are caused by local infections. He believed that decayed or infected teeth that had a root canal procedure harbored harmful toxins, creating a breeding ground for a range of health issues. However, Price's research is extremely unreliable because the conditions for his experiment were poorly controlled. Other researchers have been unable to replicate his findings and confirm his theory. Price's theory has been refuted by better-designed and better-researched experiments over the years. Root canal therapy is now a common and widely accepted dental practice that relieves pain and promotes good oral health. A false post claims that one root canal tooth can shut down 63% of your immune system. There is no scientific evidence to suggest that pulpless teeth can cause infection. Furthermore, scientific evidence has shown that once the pulpless tooth's root canal has been debrided and disinfected according to modern endodontic principles, the body's immune system can deal with any residual infection. Regardless of the fact that the concept of 'focal infection theory' has had a significant impact on medical and dental practices, the majority of systemic illnesses according to this theory are caused by small, localized 'foci' of bacterial infection. This is because infected teeth are natural harbors for bacterial infection and were thought to cause a variety of diseases and conditions. This misconception, however, has been falsified. Bacterial infections, no matter where they occur or how small they are, have the potential to grow and affect various areas of the body. As a result, root canal treatment is performed solely to eradicate the bacterial infection, thereby preventing the occurrence of heart problems and improving oral health. Dr. Pooja Bhardwaj, our dental expert, stated: "The American Association of Endodontists asserts that RCT does not cause illness. Correlation has also been shown to be false because untreated dental diseases, such as acute abscess infection, can exacerbate systemic illness. This is because tissue bacteria and debris that putrefy could release toxins that are harmful to human health. Hence, there is no scientific evidence that RCT is a cause of heart disease." Regarding oral hygiene and heart disease prevention: While there does appear to be a link between oral health and heart disease, more research is required to fully comprehend it. Although there is research that supports the possibility of a link between periodontal disease and cardiovascular disease, poor oral health is linked to an increased risk of heart problems, and there is a strong link between heart disease prevention and periodontal treatment. Nevertheless, more research is needed to substantiate this association. THIP MEDIA TAKE: We conclude that there is no substantial evidence to support the claim that root canal therapy is toxic and causes the development of cardiac conditions. In addition, it has been found that periodontal treatment could help with the management of cardiac diseases. However, more research is needed to confirm this link. As a result, the assertion is false.

title: Fact Check: Can herbs be a real remedy to remove heart blockages? - THIP Media
claim_text: An Instagram post claims that mixing kitchen herbs like cinnamon, black pepper, bay leaves, sugar, melon seeds, walnuts, and flaxseeds is claimed to clear heart blockages within 1 to 2 months.
quick_take: A social media post suggests that some kitchen herbs can unclog the arteries in 1-2 months. We fact checked and found the claim to be False.
doctor_explanation:
Can kitchen herbs and seeds remove heart blockages?

No, kitchen herbs and seeds cannot remove existing heart blockages. Heart blockages are caused by a build-up of plaque, mainly fat, cholesterol, calcium, and other substances, in the walls of arteries. This condition is called atherosclerosis. Once plaque is formed, it hardens and narrows the arteries, making it difficult for blood to flow. There is currently no scientific evidence that kitchen herbs or seeds can "melt" or "flush out" these plaques.

Medical interventions such as lifestyle changes, medications, angioplasty, or bypass surgery are required to manage or treat blocked arteries. According to the British Heart Foundation, while a healthy diet can prevent further plaque build-up, it cannot reverse existing severe blockages on its own.

Dr P. Rammanohar, Research Director at the Amrita School of Ayurveda, explained: "Heart blockages cannot be cleared instantly with home remedies. Even in Ayurveda, it takes months or even years of disciplined diet and lifestyle changes to see any improvement. So far, no medicine, modern or traditional, has proven capable of removing blockages entirely. Relying on such claims and delaying urgent medical treatment after a heart attack could have serious consequences."

Do ingredients like cinnamon and flaxseed support heart health?

Yes, some of these ingredients do support heart health, but not in the way the claim suggests. Dr Mohit Bhagwati, MBBS, DNB in General Medicine and Cardiology, explained that plaque build-up in the arteries can reduce blood flow and lead to serious complications. While no single food can remove these plaques, maintaining a healthy diet plays a key role in preventing and managing heart disease. He also highlighted that statins offer a pleiotropic effect - they not only help lower cholesterol but can also reduce the risk of stroke by stabilising plaques, turning them from thin to thicker caps, which makes them less likely to rupture.

Cinnamon (dalchini), flaxseeds, and walnuts contain compounds that may reduce certain heart disease risk factors. While these foods can support heart health, they work gradually and are preventive, not curative in nature. They cannot "clear" existing blockages quickly or on their own.

Dr Almas Fatma, a General Physician from Navi Mumbai with qualifications in Family Medicine and Digital Health, emphasised that prevention begins with everyday habits. According to her, following a balanced diet, staying active, and avoiding smoking are essential steps. She added that regularly managing conditions like high blood pressure, diabetes, and high cholesterol through check-ups is just as important. Even small lifestyle changes, like cutting down on alcohol and managing stress, can have a significant impact. As she rightly put it, "prevention is always better than cure."

Can a daily mixture of herbs replace medical treatment?

Absolutely not, such mixtures are not a substitute for evidence-based medical care. The suggestion that kitchen herbs can replace proper cardiovascular treatment is not just misleading; it can be dangerous. People who follow such advice and stop taking their prescribed medications, or delay getting medical attention, put themselves at risk of serious events like heart attacks or strokes.

The NHS and other health bodies strongly recommend consulting a doctor for proper diagnosis and treatment. The causes of heart block should be known first. Heart blockages don't improve with home remedies alone. While natural ingredients can be part of an overall heart-friendly lifestyle, they should never be viewed as standalone treatments.

Dr Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition, stated: "The quantity of spices and cinnamon used in everyday cooking is minimal, and no single home remedy can clear blocked arteries. Heart blockage is a serious health issue, and depending on such claims can be dangerous. It is always safer and wiser to consult a qualified doctor and follow appropriate medical treatment."

Why do such heart blockage home remedies go viral?

Because they offer false hope and play into fears about modern medicine. Social media posts often use emotional appeals, promising "miracle cures" with no side effects, low cost, and no need for hospitals. For people scared of surgery or worried about lifelong medications, this sounds very appealing.

Is there any harm in trying these mixtures anyway?

Yes, there can be. Especially if it delays or replaces real medical care. Although most of these ingredients are safe when used in cooking, consuming them in high or concentrated amounts can cause side effects. Moreover, people with diabetes, high blood pressure, or who are on blood thinners should be particularly cautious before adding these in supplement-like quantities to their daily routine.

What's the right way to manage or prevent heart blockages?

Through evidence-based care, long-term healthy choices, and regular check-ups. Preventing and managing heart blockages requires a combination of medically sound practices. Herbs and seeds can support some of these goals, but they are just one small part of a much bigger picture.

title: Fact Check: Can herbs cure HIV AIDS and cancer? - THIP Media
claim_text: A Facebook product advertisement claims that a herbal concoction made from pure natural roots and herbs can cure HIV/AIDS, cancer, diabetes, stroke, STDs, STIs, and herpes with a 100% guaranteed cure through herbs and the healing power of God.

doctor_explanation: No. Available published research does not confirm whether eating herbs can cure dangerous diseases like HIV AIDS and cancer. We found no evidence that shows herbs can cure HIV/AIDS or cancer. While herbal medicine is a type of complementary and alternative therapy that uses plants or plant extracts for treating illness and promoting health, there is insufficient scientific evidence to support its effectiveness as a treatment for HIV/AIDS and cancer. Herbal medicine is a type of complementary and alternative therapy often considered by people with HIV AIDS and cancer. It can use plants, or mixtures of plant extracts, to treat illness and promote health. It is believed that herbs are a natural way to deal with a disease as it has 'no to less' side effects. People might also use herbal medicine to feel better or more in control of their situation. We further researched and found that some herbs may have certain medicinal properties and can be used as complementary treatments to support conventional medical care. The FAO website has provided a list of herbs claimed to be beneficial for people suffering from HIV AIDS. The website clearly recommends people use all herbs and spices in moderate amounts. Excessive consumption may cause problems and have a toxic effect. Moreover, the function of the herbs and spices will not be increased. They cannot replace healthy eating and should not be used in place of a healthy and balanced diet. The Cancer Research UK website has provided a list of herbs that are studied for their properties to fight against cancer. However, it is important to note that there is currently no scientific evidence to support the claim that herbs alone can cure HIV/AIDS or cancer. Dr Sumit Aggarwal, Scientist D and Program Officer, Division of Epidemiology & Communicable Diseases at the ICMR, Department of Health Research, MoHFW, GOI, said: 'Herbs in simple terms are raw plants. Unless their efficacy is proven, and validated in the lab and field, they can not be used as medication. Apart from this, any medication is regulated by CDSCo in India. So one needs to take a license on this. To the best of my knowledge, no herb or ayush medication is available that can cure HIV AIDS or cancer. They have some role in improving immunity. More validation studies and research is needed. To date, as of CDSCo, no AYUSH medicine has been given a license, that can cure HIV.' Dr Sarthak Moharir, Chief Radiation Oncologist, Apollo Cancer Centre, Bilaspur, informs: 'AIDS is the acute immunodeficiency state caused by the HIV virus. The gift of modern evidence-based medicine has made HIV treatable. With the right drug cocktail, HIV patients can live long fulfilling lives without having to dread about landing in AIDS. There are carefully researched protocols in place that help doctors keep their patients healthy. As of 2023, no herb or herbal drug has been shown to do the same in any quality-controlled peer-reviewed study. Modern evidence-based medicine is based on solid irrefutable evidence, and unless we have evidence of any herb/herbal drug/herbal cocktail working, it's not used in the disease management algorithm. Similarly, in the case of cancer medicine and Oncology, no drug has been proven to cure cancer. Hence no herb/herbal drug/herbal drug cocktail is used in any treatment algorithm for any kind of cancer. Cancer treatment protocols are made by clinicians and scientists after analyzing thousands of patients backed with robust data and evidence. The day a herb is proven beyond a reasonable doubt to help cure cancer, with acceptable side effects, it will become a part of the treatment protocol.' The primary treatment for HIV/AIDS involves antiretroviral therapy (ART), which helps manage the virus and prevent its progression to acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS). Other options are Non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs), Nucleoside or nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs), Protease inhibitors (PIs), Integrase inhibitors, and Entry or fusion inhibitors. Cancer treatment depends on various factors, including the type and stage of cancer. It often involves a combination of treatments such as surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy. HIV AIDS and cancer are complicated diseases requiring more than herbs for treatment. Relying solely on herbs and not seeking proper medical treatment can worsen the condition making the condition incurable. HIV AIDS and cancer multiply quickly and spreads throughout the body in a short span. Any delay in the treatment will make the condition difficult to treat.

title: Can hibiscus and fenugreek instantly boost hair growth?
claim_text: hibiscus and fenugreek seeds work together to promote rapid hair growth
quick_take: According to a popular Facebook post, hibiscus and fenugreek seeds work wonders for promoting rapid hair growth. After fact-checking, we found that it is mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Hair growth is a cyclical process characterised by three distinctive phases—anagen, catagen, and telogen—during which hair follicles grow, rest, and shed hair strands. The anagen phase, which is noticeably longer than the other phases, is when adult hair follicles are most prevalent. The duration of the anagen phase, which is highly individualised and frequently influenced by age, hormones, genetics, and general health, determines overall hair length. Even while there is no biological necessity for long hair, people may desire it for aesthetic, cultural, or spiritual reasons, to stand out and attract attention, or for personal style and self-expression. Long hair must, however, grow steadily with minimal breakage or damage in order to retain its length. Therefore, the maximum length that can be attained depends on hair growth, and hair care may help to maintain it. The combination of hibiscus and fenugreek seeds is frequently touted as a natural formulation for hair growth. The two ingredients are associated with hair health promotion because: Hibiscus flowers and leaves have been traditionally employed for hair health. This could be attributed to the fact that the ingredient is packed with vitamins A and C, amino acids, and antioxidants. This high bioactive profile enhances scalp circulation, nourishes hair follicles, and may potentially reduce oxidative stress. Hibiscus extracts have also shown efficacy for improving hair density. Similarly, lecithin, nicotinic acid, and proteins found in fenugreek seeds may fortify hair shafts and possibly lessen hair breakage. Additionally, their antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties might promote scalp health. Despite these benefits, the aforementioned ingredients have not been thoroughly tested in clinical settings to be accepted as a viable treatment modality for rapid hair growth. The multifactorial basis of hair growth further raises concerns about the effectiveness of the homemade composition. Dr. Rashi Soni, Dermatologist and co-founder of Rashi Hospital, Mumbai, confirms that hair grows gradually. The hair usually grows approximately half an inch per month. The notion that a homemade preparation can substantially expedite the process seems impractical. Moreover, there is insufficient evidence to support the recipe's dramatic impact. The claim is, therefore, definitely exaggerated. Even though they are not a dependable source of rapid hair growth, hibiscus and fenugreek seeds can both make a substantial contribution to healthy hair. It is always advisable to seek professional advice for appropriate evaluation and management. There is no magic potion for hair growth acceleration, points out Dr. Sachin Gupta (MBBS and MD in Dermatology and Venereology from AIIMS Delhi), of Amrita Hospital in Faridabad. Dr. Gupta strongly emphasises that relying only on unregulated formulations may not work because hair growth is influenced by several factors, including hormonal fluctuations, diet, family history, and overall well-being. Optimal hair development can be supported by a nutritious diet, appropriate hair care practices, and expert advice for any underlying medical concerns. Dr. Rashi Soni supports this further, stating that 'natural ingredients have traditionally been used for to promote healthy hair, but their role in achieving significant hair growth or preventing hair loss is still uncertain.' These remedies may be helpful for minor hair loss and texture problems, but it's preferable to see a specialist and look into medical options. Hair growth in any individual is primarily influenced by their genetics. Genetic inheritance mostly determines hair's density, texture, and growth development rate. The hair cycle is also regulated by hormones, particularly androgens. Adequate consumption of certain proteins, biotin, vitamin D, iron, and zinc contributes to healthy hair follicle function. Furthermore, external influences, including stress, sleep patterns, and exposure to pollutants, can have an impact on hair health. Medical experts employ a comprehensive approach to hair growth by determining the root cause of either excessive hair loss or delayed hair growth. Once the core cause is established, clinicians employ evidence-based interventions. Some of the popular options include topical medications such as minoxidil, prescribed oral medications, procedural options of platelet-rich plasma therapy or hair transplantation, along with nutritional supplementation and hormone-based therapies.

title: Fact Check: Can high-intensity exercise destroy cancer cells?
claim_text: High-intensity exercise like HIIT, heavy weightlifting, and sprints can destroy cancer cells in the bloodstream through high shear stress.
quick_take: A social media post claims that high-intensity exercise can destroy cancer cells. However, after fact checking, we found that this is mostly false.
doctor_explanation: The claim that high-intensity exercise can destroy cancer cells lacks solid clinical evidence. While high-intensity exercise does increase blood flow and create shear stress in the bloodstream (reaching up to 60 dynes/cm² according to a 2017 Nature Scientific Reports study), this alone cannot destroy cancer cells in the human body. The 2017 lab study showed that high shear stress at 60 dynes/cm² killed over 90% of cancer cells in the blood within 4 hours in a controlled lab setting using a microfluidic system. However, this study was conducted in a lab, not in humans. When exercising, blood pressure elevation typically lasts less than an hour, unlike the sustained 4-hour pressure in the study. Additionally, the human body is far more complex than a lab setup, with factors like the immune system and fluctuating blood flow influencing outcomes. A small 2018 human study with 23 colon cancer patients found that regular exercise reduced circulating tumour cells but did not test whether exercise directly kills cancer cells through shear stress. Dr. Pooja Khullar, Radiation Oncologist at Dharamshila Narayana Super Speciality Hospital, New Delhi, explicitly states: 'High-intensity exercise offers numerous health benefits—improving cardiovascular fitness, boosting mood, and supporting the immune system—but there is no solid evidence to suggest it can directly destroy cancer cells as a treatment. Cancer cells are complex; they do not simply await elimination through physical activity.' She adds that while exercise can play a supportive role in cancer care by reducing inflammation and improving resilience, it cannot replace proven treatments like chemotherapy, radiation, or immunotherapy. Research from the American Cancer Society shows regular physical activity can reduce the risk of certain cancers (breast and colon) by 20-25%, but this is about risk reduction, not cure. The Instagram post takes lab results and applies them to real life without solid proof. Cancer involves primary tumours and ongoing cell production, which CTC destruction wouldn't address.

title: Fact Check: Can HIV be cured with some home remedies?
claim_text: A person can cure HIV by consuming tea made with water, papaya leaf, and black seed.
quick_take: A social media post claims that a person can cure HIV by consuming tea made with water, papaya leaf, and black seed. We fact-checked and found this claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: Dr. K. S. Satish, Senior Chest Specialist and HIV Physician at Fortis Cunningham Road and Manipal Hospital, Millers Road, Bangalore, clarifies: 'A person living with HIV can suppress the virus with antiretrovirals, there is no cure for HIV till date. A cure for HIV would refer to total eradication of the virus from the body, which is still under research.' As of now, there is no cure for HIV. However, Antiretroviral treatment (ART) can control the infection. The virus multiplication in the body is limited, which can lead to long and healthy lives. The treatment lowers the viral load (virus concentration in the blood). Successful viral suppression restores the immune system, halts the onset and progression of the disease, and reduces the chances of getting opportunistic infections. Regarding the tea ingredients: There is a lack of definitive scientific research proving that HIV can be cured with a tea made with papaya leaf, water and black seeds. These ingredients show some anti-viral properties of their own, but there is a lack of study proving the efficacy of the mixture. An extract of papaya, namely a pentacyclic triterpene, shows a broad range of antiviral activities against human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). There are various studies which suggest an anti-HIV potential of the papaya leaf extract due to the synergistic action of multiple bioactive constituents. Similarly, there are studies which suggest that there are possible therapeutic agents in Nigella sativa (Black seed) that may effectively control HIV infection. Another study published by the International Journal of Medical Reviews states that Nigella sativa can be used alone or in combination with the authentic treatment, HAART therapy. It can miraculously produce seroreversion of the viral load in many cases. However, its mechanism of action is still needed to be studied in depth. Dr. Saurabh Gaba, Associate Consultant, Internal Medicine, Paras Hospitals, Panchkula, adds: 'HIV cannot be cured by consuming black seeds. There is absolutely no scientific evidence to support this claim, and delaying proper treatment can lead to life-threatening complications.' In conclusion, most of the effects and applications of these ingredients require further clinical and animal studies to establish if they can be considered as a treatment module. HIV is a viral infection that attacks the immune system, and currently, there is no known cure for HIV. However, antiretroviral therapy (ART) can effectively manage the virus and prevent it from progressing into AIDS. Medical attention is essential as soon as a person is exposed to a potential risk of HIV infection. Any non-scientific and unapproved treatment can lead to certain side effects or even be dangerous as it may lead to disease progression. Any unauthentic treatment and avoiding scientifically proven medication such as ART can lead to fatal complications.

While survey has shown that most men wrongly believe that the average size of penis is over 6 inches and most men wish that they had longer size. This has led to a flourishing market of medically non-validated penis increasing creams, lotions and devices. Does the size of penis increase after birth? Yes. The penis reaches its full size around the age of 19. There is very little chance of the penis growing beyond early 20s. That said, the body development during puberty varies from individual to individual. A research done in 2010 shows that in most males the penis grows less than half inch between 11 to 15. title: Fact Check: Can home remedies cure skin problems? - THIP Media
claim_text: A Facebook reel with the caption, "Skin brightening facial at home" shares the video of a woman where she displays a multistep facial claiming to remove dark circles, acne scars and suntan using aloe vera, rice powder, honey, raw milk, and turmeric.
quick_take: A social media post claims that a DIY brightening facial remove skin imperfections. The post claims that a skin-brightening facial at home can remove dark circles, acne scars and suntan. We fact-checked and found this claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation:
Dark circles under the eyes (DC) are dark, discoloured areas of skin that appear underneath the lower eyelids. They are typically round or semi-circular in shape and can range in colour. Various factors such as genetics, age, lack of sleep, stress, allergies, and certain medical conditions cause dark circles. The skin in the infraorbital region is thin and delicate, which can make these dark circles more noticeable.

The American Academy of Dermatology Association states that acne breakouts that penetrate the skin deeply can cause damage to both the skin and the underlying tissue. As the acne resolves, the body initiates the healing process, which involves the production of collagen, a supportive substance for the skin. The formation of acne scars depends on the balance of collagen production. Insufficient or excessive collagen production can result in either depressed or raised acne scars.

A suntan is a temporary darkening of the skin caused by exposure to ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun or from artificial sources, such as tanning beds. The darkening is caused by an increase in the production of melanin, a pigment that helps to protect the skin from UV radiation. The amount of melanin in the skin varies from person to person, which is why some people tan more easily than others. People with darker skin tones tend to have more melanin, so they are less likely to burn and more likely to tan.

It is not possible to permanently eliminate dark circles, acne scars and suntan at home. Home remedies using the mentioned ingredients, such as aloe vera, rice powder, honey, raw milk, and turmeric may help improve the appearance of dark circles, acne scars, and suntan to some extent, but cannot remove it completely. However, it's important to note that the effectiveness of these remedies can vary from person to person, and results may not be as significant as professional treatments.

Dr Parwaaz Matharoo, MBBS, MD (Dermatology) comments, "In the Cleopatra era the famous milk bath ritual became the way to brighter glowy skin. There are a few recommendations that can help you to reduce unwelcome pigmentation. Advisory before using any kind of ubtan is to always prepare yourself for unfriendly outcomes.

Milk and curd do their magic in reducing suntan because of its star ingredient i.e. lactic acid which is an alpha hydroxy acid (AHA) causes exfoliation, reduces pigmentation and improves skin texture. As they say when there's a but take caution while pursuing it. Milk and curd can exacerbate acne in predisposed individuals. Additionally, tomato contains various acids like oxalic acid, citric acid, malic acid and ascorbic acid which have benefits like decreasing dark circles and suntan. But, dark circles have a multifactorial etiology. Good sleep hygiene, a healthy diet, antioxidants, breaking free of a sedentary lifestyle, de-stress and correction of nutritional/hormonal deficiencies can all help in the prevention and reduction of dark circles. For promising results, Dermatologist's assistance is recommended.
Acne scars can be prevented by avoiding picking/squeezing/scratching the acne. Once formed their reduction can be assisted by your nearest dermatologist at the clinic with various available procedures. Lastly, not many ingredients are helpful when it comes to scarring. It's always best to consult your doctor."

Dr. Jyoti Kannangath comments on the use of Aloe vera by stating, "Aloesin, a compound extracted from Aloe vera, has demonstrated the ability to competitively inhibit tyrosinase, the enzyme responsible for skin pigmentation. However, there have been several published case reports documenting hypersensitivity reactions and contact dermatitis caused by aloe vera preparations."

Dr. Kannangath comments, "Honey is a natural ingredient that has many healing properties, but that does not mean it is totally safe. Honey can cause problems if you are allergic to pollen or celery (honey) or if you have sensitive and dry skin." However, it can lead to an allergic reaction or symptoms, such as hives, itching, inflammation, and redness on the skin. Also, in rare cases, its application can lead to contact dermatitis, causing symptoms such as burning, itching, stinging, or soreness. flushed skin and inflammation.

Dr. Soumya Sachdeva, Consultant Dermatologist suggests, "Home remedies should be used with caution as many of the ingredients in these home face masks can cause various allergies and contact dermatitis. So as a dermatologist, I do not recommend such treatments. Sometimes these allergies can be severe, and later on, healing can leave resistant pigmentation on your face."

Dr Kannangath summarizes by stating, "At-home remedies can be helpful in improving the appearance of dark circles, acne scars, and sun tan to some extent, but it's important to manage expectations. These remedies may not completely eliminate these issues, but they can contribute to gradual improvement over time. If you have severe concerns or are not seeing improvement with home remedies, it's best to consult a dermatologist for professional advice and treatments. Additionally, while trying these remedies, it's essential to perform a patch test on a small area of your skin to check for any adverse reactions before applying it to larger areas of your face or body."

It's advisable to perform a patch test before applying any new ingredient to ensure there are no adverse reactions. If you have severe or persistent skin concerns, it is recommended to consult a dermatologist for professional advice and appropriate treatment options.

title: Can home remedies permanently treat a lice problem?
claim_text: Applying a mixture of garlic juice, lemon juice, and mustard oil can treat lice in just one use. The post further claims that this remedy prevents lice infestations forever, lasting 100 years.
quick_take: A social media post claims that a mixture of garlic, lemon juice, and mustard oil can cure lice forever in just one use. Our fact check shows this is false.
doctor_explanation: The claim that garlic completely eliminates head lice in 30 minutes is not supported by robust scientific evidence. While laboratory studies (2010, 2016) have demonstrated that garlic juice can kill lice under controlled conditions, these studies were not conducted on human subjects, and crucially, often failed to eliminate the lice eggs. A 2020 study showed garlic's effectiveness at high concentrations but was limited to a small number of lice (28 lice subjects) in a lab setting. Conversely, a 2018 study involving children found garlic oil to be largely ineffective. Similarly, lab-based studies from 2010 indicated that lemon juice could kill lice, but the real-world application of these findings remains uncertain. Lemon and mustard oil may offer temporary weakening effects, but they do not reliably eradicate lice or their eggs. A 2023 study in Nepal explored affordable alternatives, finding a salt, vinegar, and wetting agent solution to be more effective than mustard oil, and plastic lice combs to be as effective as metal ones. This highlights the potential for accessible treatments. However, due to the resilience of lice and the difficulty in eliminating their eggs, relying solely on single natural remedies like this is unlikely to resolve an infestation completely. Therefore, clinically proven lice treatments remain the most dependable option for effectively addressing head lice. Lice spread through direct contact and shared items like combs, hats, and bedding. No home remedy can offer permanent protection against reinfestation. If a person is exposed to lice again, they will likely get infected, regardless of past treatments. The idea that this remedy can prevent lice for '100 years' is an exaggerated and false claim. Dr Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant in Lucknow, clarifies, 'Although some natural remedies like garlic, lemon, and mustard oil may offer temporary relief or have shown limited effects in lab settings, they are not a reliable, one-time cure for head lice. Clinically proven pediculicides (medicated treatments designed to kill lice) remain the most effective and recommended treatment option. It's crucial to consult a dermatologist for proper diagnosis and treatment to avoid prolonged infestation and potential complications.' Dr Rashi Soni, Dermatologist and Co-founder of Rashi Hospital in Mumbai, explains, 'Scientifically proven treatments for head lice primarily involve pediculicides, which are medications specifically designed to kill lice and, in some cases, their eggs. These include over-the-counter options containing permethrin or pyrethrin, and prescription medications like malathion, spinosad, or ivermectin. It's essential to follow the product's instructions carefully for optimal effectiveness. Additionally, thorough nit combing and environmental measures, such as washing bedding and clothing, can help prevent re-infestation. Always consult a dermatologist or healthcare provider to determine the most appropriate treatment plan for your specific situation.'

title: Fact Check: Can home remedies replace angioplasty or bypass surgery?
claim_text: A Facebook post claims eating lemon, ginger, garlic, and apple cider vinegar can remove the need for angioplasty and bypass surgery.
quick_take: A social media post claims home remedies can replace angioplasty or bypass surgery. We fact-checked and found the claim to be Half True.
doctor_explanation: What is angioplasty? Angioplasty is a medical procedure for opening a blocked vein. The process involves using a balloon to stretch open a blocked artery. The modern procedure can also involve inserting a stent during the procedure to help the blood flow freely. What is bypass surgery? Bypass surgery provides a new vein for blood flow when a vein is blocked that reaches the heart. The procedure involves taking a healthy vein from the leg, arm, or chest and connecting it below or above the blocked vein. title: Can homemade Botox oil help keep the skin wrinkle-free?
claim_text: Homemade Botox Oil—Natural Skin Tightening Secret: An organic formulation consisting of Johnson's baby oil, cloves, vitamin E capsules, aloe vera gel, and rosemary leaves is a beneficial substitute for chemical-based Botox and a natural way to get wrinkle-free skin.
quick_take: A Facebook post is promoting a homemade Botox for wrinkle-free skin. We analysed the claim and found that it was false.
doctor_explanation: Wrinkles that could be natural, age-related, or genetic in origin usually show up as creases or lines on the face, hands, and neck. These are usually brought about by a combination of environmental variables and ageing. Some of the environmental variables that may accelerate the process of ageing may include: smoking, pollutants, UV exposure, dehydration, and repetitive facial movements. Because our skin loses elastin, collagen, and hydration as we age, it becomes less elastic and more prone to creases. As the epidermis becomes thinner, the dermal support structure is jeopardised. Furthermore, a lower rate of cellular regeneration and greater oxidative stress may result in the formation of an additional layer of cells. All of this causes the skin to progressively sag, become more sensitive, and form permanent lines and wrinkles. Wrinkles are one of the earliest noticeable signs of ageing; thus, their appearance is concerning. This is because they demonstrate the structural and functional changes in the dermal matrix. Beyond appearance, wrinkles are a sign of underlying cellular damage and a breakdown in the skin barrier. Thus, they require preventive skincare as well as appropriate dermatological interventions. It is vital to establish that the term 'homemade Botox oil' is just prevalent on social media. As per the viral claims, the do-it-yourself preparation combining Johnson's Baby Oil, cloves, vitamin E capsules, aloe vera gel, and occasionally rosemary leaves replicates the wrinkle-reducing effects of the scientifically validated botulinum toxin injections. Despite being widely popularised, this formulation's ability to reduce wrinkles is not supported by substantial scientific evidence. Botox, scientifically known as botulinum toxin type A, temporarily paralyses specific facial muscles. Under medical supervision, Botox may reduce dynamic wrinkles brought on by muscular movements, which topical or organic solutions cannot replicate. Because the alleged at-home Botox alternative exhibits moisturising, modest anti-inflammatory, or antibacterial qualities, it is incapable of preventing neuromuscular transmission or inducing an obvious reduction in wrinkles. Furthermore, there is no standardisation in the preparation's efficacy or dosing. Some ingredients have dermatological value; nonetheless, there is not enough evidence of their full-scale ability to reduce wrinkles. Johnson's Baby Oil is mostly a mineral oil composition with a protective barrier that keeps skin hydrated by reducing transepidermal water loss. Vitamin E is a strong antioxidant that shields the skin from oxidative damage. Aloe vera gel is the most popular ingredient in skincare products because of its mild anti-inflammatory and moisturising properties. The active chemicals in cloves and rosemary are eugenol and rosmarinic acid, respectively. While the two components are employed for their antimicrobial and antioxidant activities, these effects are confined to preliminary research. Despite these being commonly used skin care kitchen ingredients, they lack randomised controlled trials for wrinkle-free skin. Using unproven formulations like the one mentioned in the claim on a daily basis should be avoided. This might be explained by their propensity to induce inflammation, acne, and long-term barrier disruption. Additionally, cloves and rosemary may be associated with contact dermatitis. Therefore, even while the preparation might momentarily hydrate the facial skin, it cannot replace scientifically established wrinkle-reduction approaches. Online treatments such as homemade botox oil for facial wrinkles happen to be popular due to affordability, accessibility, and and social media-driven cosmetic trends. Web-based remedies are also promoted as natural and chemical-free alternatives to expensive dermatological options. Most significantly, internet claims often use influencer endorsements and anecdotal testimonials to shape consumer skincare behaviours. Consequently, their synergistic influence outweighs the clinically tested wrinkle-reducing agents, including retinoids, peptides, antioxidants, and professional procedures. Scientifically validated wrinkle removal methods may enhance skin suppleness, reduce oxidative stress, and promote collagen formation; they cannot be substituted with unreliable internet alternatives. Furthermore, uncontrolled formulations with questionable safety and effectiveness may result in contact dermatitis, allergic responses, and phototoxicity. Dr. Sachin Gupta, Consultant Dermatologist at Amrita Hospital in Faridabad, provides his insightful thoughts: 'Considering the limited and inconclusive nature of studies backing such remedies, it is advisable to opt for treatments with documented effectiveness and established clinical benefits.' While do-it-yourself skincare solutions are frequently promoted as safe substitutes, relying too much on them may delay required therapy and even deteriorate skin health. Dr. Rashi Soni, Co-founder and Consulting Dermatologist, Aesthetician, and Hair Transplant Surgeon at Rashi Hospital in Mumbai, explains that doctors usually rely on procedures that have strong scientific backing when it comes to wrinkle reduction. 'Applying a high-quality sunscreen daily is one of the greatest ways to prevent further damage. Retinoids help by encouraging collagen synthesis and cell turnover. The protective layer of the skin is maintained by skin-plumping moisturisers that contain ceramides or hyaluronic acid. Lifestyle choices are also important; refraining from smoking, having a nutritious diet, and getting adequate sleep can all have a big impact. In-clinic therapies such as chemical peels or laser treatments may be beneficial for deeper wrinkles.' Conclusion: Retinoids, injections of botulinum toxin, and certain peptide-based formulations exhibit quantifiable effectiveness in the correction of wrinkles. As a result, while unsupervised homemade Botox oil could improve skin hydration and smoothness, it cannot replace the mechanisms and effects of dermatologically tested effect of botulinum toxin for wrinkles.

title: Can homemade coconut oil concoction guarantee thick & long hair?
claim_text: You can get thick and long hair if you regularly apply a concoction of coconut oil and several herbs and seeds, namely fenugreek seeds, rice, aloe vera gel, flax seeds, black pepper, tea powder, aliv seeds. The post tells us to mix all the dry ingredients and then boil it in coconut oil for five minutes. Upon cooling, it can be sieved, stored and applied daily.
quick_take: Social media is full of videos that guarantee thick and long hair through homemade remedies using coconut oil and other ingredients. Given the complex nature of hair growth, which majorly depends on the genetics of an individual, DIY remedies may not prove to be beneficial always. We fact checked one such claim and found it to be mostly false.
doctor_explanation:
Not exactly. Hair growth has more to it than just topical application of coconut oil concoction. While coconut oil has numerous benefits proven for skincare and haircare, it alone cannot guarantee a 100% result for thick and long hair, as mentioned in the claim. There exists a complex interplay of factors which affect hair growth. The factors that can affect hair growth are diet (can cause nutritional deficiencies which can lead to hair loss — iron deficiency causes hair loss), lifestyle, stress, ongoing medication, hormonal imbalance, sudden and significant weight loss, trauma, certain diseases and disorders, age, pregnancy and most importantly genetics. If you are experiencing hair thinning or hair loss we suggest you consult a qualified healthcare professional for your concern.

Coconut oil gets a lot of hype for its hair benefits, but it might not be the magic solution for hair loss. Hair loss stems from various issues like genetics, hormones, health conditions, diet, and stress. While a good coconut oil hair massage (regular and consistent) can hydrate the scalp, encourage hair growth, and reduce breakage, it doesn't tackle these underlying causes directly. Still, by keeping your scalp healthy and providing nutrients, coconut oil could indirectly help with hair growth and possibly lessen some types of hair loss. Remember, it's crucial to identify and treat the root cause of hair loss alongside using coconut oil as part of your overall hair care routine.

Hair growth follows a cycle with three primary phases: anagen, catagen, and telogen. During the anagen phase, hair actively grows from the root, usually lasting several years. The catagen phase signals a transition where hair growth slows, and the follicle starts to shrink. In the telogen phase, hair rests for a few months before shedding, which is a normal part of the cycle with individuals typically shedding 50 to 100 hairs per day. However, deviations from this cycle can lead to conditions like alopecia or telogen effluvium, where hair follicles undergo abnormal patterns of growth or shedding. Factors like genetics, hormones, diet, stress, and overall health can influence these conditions, as well as external factors like hair care practices and environmental stressors.

Dr Sachin Gupta (MBBS and MD in Dermatology and Venereology from AIIMS Delhi), an experienced dermatologist at Amrita Hospital, Faridabad, highlights that, "There's no scientific backing to the notion that a blend of coconut oil, some herbs and seeds can increase hair growth significantly. While each ingredient is believed to offer health benefits, attributing accelerated hair growth solely to this mixture is baseless." He emphasises that hair growth is influenced by various factors such as genetics, hormones, diet, and overall health. There's no quick-fix solution to speeding up hair growth. Dr. Gupta suggests maintaining a healthy diet and good hair care practices for optimal hair health. In case of underlying medical conditions, consulting a dermatologist is recommended. Hair typically grows at a rate of 1-1.5 cm per month, indicating the gradual nature of the process. He advises against relying on unverified remedies and encourages seeking professional advice for genuine concerns regarding hair thinning and hair loss, emphasising the importance of a holistic approach for desired outcomes. Delay in professional consultation may lead to missed opportunities of early and effective treatment that can stall or prevent hair loss.

Lifestyle changes that can help prevent hair loss and promote hair thickness include: maintaining a balanced diet rich in essential nutrients such as vitamins A, C, D, E, and biotin; regular exercise to improve blood circulation which nourishes hair follicles; avoiding harsh hair treatments such as excessive heat styling and chemical treatments; managing stress through relaxation techniques like meditation or yoga; adequate sleep for body repair and regeneration; staying hydrated; good head massage and scalp treatments can help too, provided nutrition and genetics support the same.

title: Can homemade mouthwash eliminate oral malodour in a day?
claim_text: Rinsing the mouth with a combination of baking soda, salt, and lemon juice in warm water can effectively eliminate oral malodour, or foul breath, in a single day.
quick_take: According to a Facebook post, a homemade mouthwash can effectively eliminate oral malodour in a day. We fact-checked the claim and found it to be mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Oral malodour, or halitosis, popularly referred to as bad breath, is an unpleasant stench coming from the mouth. This is primarily brought on by anaerobic bacteria, which may break down sulphur-containing amino acids to form volatile sulphur compounds (VSCs). Potential contributors include poor oral hygiene, tongue coatings, advanced gum disease, particularly severe gingival diseases, and certain medications, along with additional conditions such as infections, systemic ailments, dry mouth, or xerostomia. Dr. Ketan Rajput, a Periodontist and Oral Implantologist at Dr. Rajput's Advanced Dental Care and Implant Centre in Dhule, Maharashtra, explains that halitosis can be caused by a range of systemic and local conditions, and advises receiving professional dental care in addition to correcting the root cause. Even while the combination of warm water with baking soda, salt, and lemon juice is being touted as an inexpensive, natural mouth cleanser, its relevance is confined to social media platforms only. While the aforementioned ingredients may offer short-term symptomatic relief, they neither individually nor synergistically can address the core cause of true halitosis – including periodontal disease, tongue coating, xerostomia, or dental infection. Since oral malodour is primarily brought on by VSCs produced by anaerobic bacteria – not by surface debris alone – evidence-based management remains the most effective. Additionally, frequent usage of acidic lemon juice might irritate oral tissues and erode enamel. Dependence on such unapproved home cures may therefore be more detrimental than beneficial. The key to managing halitosis is comprehending the distinction between transient foul breath (which develops after cigarette smoking, consuming specific meals, and experiencing dryness in the morning, and may improve in hours with regular dental hygiene) and chronic halitosis (which is mostly associated with persistent intraoral conditions such as tongue coating, periodontal inflammation, dental decay, and decreased salivary flow, which emit volatile sulphur-containing compounds). Even though certain at-home remedies may momentarily reduce unpleasant odour, the bacterial reservoirs and underlying inflammatory diseases cannot be completely eradicated in a single day. The effective and long-lasting treatment of chronic halitosis necessitates clinical evaluation, periodontal therapy, tongue management, and regular oral hygiene habits. Dr. Pooja Sharma, BDS, MDS, of NIMS University in Jaipur, further explains that home remedies can sometimes be more harmful than beneficial—not because the ingredients are potentially harmful, but rather because they may create the false impression that medical care is not required. Cavities and gum infections are two dental problems that need to be accurately evaluated and addressed as they don't go away on their own. Furthermore, unapproved herbal mouthwashes are not a universally effective remedy; their application should be confined to complementary oral hygiene; they should not be utilised in place of expert advice, diagnosis, or individualised, evidence-based medicinal products. Managing oral malodour requires a cautious, evidence-based approach. Controlling plaque effectively usually begins with maintaining proper oral hygiene practices, such as regular toothbrushing, interdental cleaning, and mechanical tongue scraping. Antimicrobial mouthwashes containing zinc salts, cetylpyridinium chloride, or chlorhexidine may also be advised. It is also essential to make dietary changes, drink lots of water, and abstain from alcohol and tobacco. Addressing oral malodour necessitates an all-encompassing approach that aims to both restore oral ecological balance and eradicate its fundamental causes.

title: Fact Check: Can Homemade tea cure hypothyroidism within days?
claim_text: Homemade tea made with cayenne pepper, ginger, and garlic cures hypothyroidism within days.
quick_take: While ginger, garlic, and cayenne pepper may offer general health benefits, they cannot cure hypothyroidism. These natural ingredients may support overall well-being, but managing hypothyroidism requires proper medical diagnosis and prescribed hormone therapy. Relying solely on home remedies can delay effective treatment and potentially worsen the condition.
doctor_explanation:
Dr Mahesh D M, MBBS, MD (General Medicine), DM (Endocrinology), DNB (Endocrinology), Consultant Endocrinology, Aster CMI Hospital, told Medical Dialogues: 'No, a homemade tea with cayenne pepper, ginger, and garlic can't cure hypothyroidism in a few days. While these ingredients have anti-inflammatory and circulation-boosting properties, hypothyroidism is a hormonal condition that usually requires proper medical treatment, often with thyroid hormone replacement. Natural remedies may support overall wellness, but they can't replace prescribed medications or correct hormonal imbalances overnight. Always consult a doctor before making changes to your treatment.'

Dr Divya Tripathi, Assistant Professor, Department of Nutrition and Dietetics, Manav Rachna International Institute of Research and Studies, added: 'While ingredients like ginger, garlic, and cayenne pepper are great for overall wellness and may support digestion and immunity, they do not cure hypothyroidism. Hypothyroidism is a hormonal condition that requires proper medical care, usually in the form of lifelong thyroid hormone replacement. Relying on home remedies alone can delay treatment and worsen symptoms. Always speak to your doctor before trying alternatives—natural doesn't always mean effective for every health issue.'

Hypothyroidism is a condition in which the thyroid gland is underactive and fails to produce adequate amounts of thyroid hormone needed for normal body functions. This hormonal deficiency slows down the body's metabolism and leads to a range of symptoms. It is commonly caused by autoimmune conditions such as Hashimoto's thyroiditis, thyroid gland removal surgery, or radiation therapy.

Currently, hypothyroidism has no cure. However, it can be successfully managed in most individuals. Treatment focuses on restoring hormone balance by using synthetic thyroxine (T4), which replaces the deficient thyroid hormone.

Regarding scientific evidence: An animal study published in the Journal of Istanbul Veterinary Sciences suggests that capsaicin—a key compound in cayenne pepper—may help partially reduce oxidative stress associated with hypothyroidism. However, the study does not indicate that capsaicin has any effect on correcting thyroid hormone imbalances.

An animal study published in the AIP Conference Proceedings suggests that garlic extract may influence thyroid hormone levels in hyperthyroidism. But the study does not indicate any benefit of garlic in correcting low thyroid hormone levels seen in hypothyroidism.

A study published in the journal Evidence-Based Complementary and Alternative Medicine demonstrated that daily consumption of 1000 mg of ginger powder in patients with primary hypothyroidism who were already on proper thyroid medication (with normal hormone levels) helped reduce their symptoms significantly. This study does not suggest that ginger can cure hypothyroidism.

There are no studies confirming the role of cayenne pepper or garlic in managing hypothyroidism. No studies have shown that garlic, ginger, or cayenne pepper—either individually or together—can cure hypothyroidism. Research has shown that ginger may help reduce the symptoms of hypothyroidism, but it cannot cure the condition.

title: Fact Check: Can Honey and Cinnamon be combined to cure a long list of diseases such as Cancer, Arthritis, etc.? - THIP Media
claim_text: Boiled Cinnamon And Honey Is The Cure For Cancer, Arthritis, Cholesterol And Many More Health problems
quick_take: A social media post claims that Honey and Cinnamon together can cure a long list of diseases such as Cancer, Arthritis, etc. We fact-checked and found this claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: Honey has several potential health benefits and plays a role in many home remedies and alternative medicine treatments. It has high antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. Honey can help treat wounds, coughs, and upper respiratory conditions. It is also believed to improve gut health. Cinnamon primarily contains vital oils and other derivatives, such as cinnamaldehyde, cinnamic acid, and cinnamate. In addition to being an antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, lipid-lowering, and cardiovascular-disease-lowering compound, it is also said to help in lowering blood pressure and blood sugar. Consuming too much honey may cause adverse effects due to its high sugar and calorie content. Few people may be allergic to honey which can cause an allergic reaction to them. Since Cinnamon is a rich source of coumarin, consuming too much of it may cause liver toxicity and damage. Furthermore, studies on animal have shown that eating too much coumarin may increase the risk of certain cancers. Therefore, it is generally safe to use it in small amounts as a spice. Even though honey and cinnamon have a lot of medicinal benefits on their own, there is insufficient medical substantiation that the mixture of honey and cinnamon can cure diseases, such as arthritis, cancer, etc. According to the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, labels must adhere to the full context of the particular food they describe, and foods cannot establish a relationship between a substance or disease-related condition unless the FDA authorizes it. title: Fact Check: Can hot water act as a natural blood thinner?

Blood thinners work by interfering with the clotting ability of the blood. They can be of two main types: anticoagulants and antiplatelet drugs. Anticoagulants, such as warfarin and heparin, reduce the action of clotting factors, which are proteins in the blood that control bleeding. Antiplatelet drugs, like aspirin and clopidogrel, prevent platelets (a type of blood cell) from clumping together to form clots. Both types of blood thinners help prevent the formation of dangerous clots that can lead to conditions like heart attacks, strokes, and deep vein thrombosis.

No, hot water cannot act as a natural blood thinner. There is no scientific evidence to support the idea that drinking hot water can thin the blood. Blood thinners, medically known as anticoagulants, are substances that help prevent blood clots. Common blood thinners include medications like warfarin, heparin, and newer anticoagulants like rivaroxaban. These medications work by interfering with the blood's clotting mechanisms.

Hot water does not contain any active ingredients that can influence blood viscosity or clotting factors. Staying hydrated is essential for overall health, but water temperature does not have a specific impact on blood thickness. Drinking too much water can dilute the proteins and electrolytes in your blood, but it won't thin your blood or prevent clot formation. Overhydration can lead to hyponatremia, a condition where the body lacks enough sodium, which is different from affecting blood clotting.

Dr Ashok Kumar Boss, Senior Cardiologist at HDNA Aarogyam Hospital, Patna, shares his expertise, "There is no evidence that hot water acts as a natural blood thinner. Of course hot water causes vasodilation, i.e., dilation of blood vessels. This may help delay the clotting process causing more bleeding, just opposite to cold ice packs which causes vasoconstriction i.e., constriction of blood vessels, and less bleeding."

When we asked Dr Debasish Mohapatra, Associate Consultant at BM Birla Heart Research Centre in Kolkata, if water can act as a blood thinner, he said, "Water cannot replace prescription blood thinners like warfarin. It does not have anticoagulant properties, but staying hydrated is beneficial. However, too much water can worsen symptoms in heart failure patients. Blood thinners are necessary to prevent serious conditions like heart attacks, strokes, and blockages."

Managing high cholesterol involves a balanced diet, regular exercise, and sometimes medications like statins. The temperature of the water you drink does not affect cholesterol levels. Although some claims suggest hot water can improve digestion and cholesterol levels, there is no scientific evidence to support this. Proper hydration is beneficial, but water temperature is irrelevant for cholesterol management.

Blood clots form when platelets and proteins in your blood work together to stop bleeding, and medications prevent or treat clots by inhibiting stages of this process. Drinking hot water does not affect blood clot formation or prevention. People at risk should follow their doctor's advice. These usually include prescribed drugs, regular exercise, and avoiding prolonged sitting. People should also keep in mind that excess water intake can, in fact, worsen heart failure symptoms. It cannot replace prescription blood thinners. Therefore, anticoagulant drugs are important to prevent heart attacks, strokes, and blockages.

Hot water can not thin the blood or reduce cholesterol. But, it can provide some general health benefits, such as soothing a sore throat and helping in digestion.

Drinking hot water is generally safe, but it's essential to ensure the water is not too hot to avoid burns or scalds. Extremely hot water can damage the tissues in your mouth and oesophagus, leading to burns. Research suggests that the correct temperature is in the range of 54.4-71.1°C or 130-160°F.

Proper hydration is important for maintaining blood volume and viscosity. Dehydration can lead to thicker blood, increasing the risk of blood clots. Drinking enough water daily helps maintain an optimal balance of electrolytes and blood plasma, promoting smooth blood flow and reducing the strain on the heart. According to guidelines from the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, men aged 19 and above are advised to consume approximately 3.7 litres (or about 15.5 cups) of water daily, while women in the same age group should aim for around 2.7 litres (equivalent to roughly 11.5 cups) per day.

Research published in the Journal of Education and Health Promotion found that acupressure did not statistically improve self-efficacy and pregnancy occurrence in infertile women, though further studies are recommended. The cause behind infertility could be physical abnormalities like blocked fallopian tubes or fibroids or cysts in the ovary, which cannot be treated through such practices. Such conditions require medical or surgical interventions. While stress is reported in many infertile women and can interfere with pregnancy ability, massage therapy is believed to aid in relieving stress, anxiety and depression only in the short term. The American College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists notes that disinformation exists and many women engage in non-conventional therapies without medical advice, which can sometimes delay needed care.

title: Can inhaling steam through a cinnamon stick detox the lungs?
claim_text: Inhaling steam through a cinnamon stick in lemon detox water cleanses smokers' lungs
quick_take: A social media post claims that inhaling steam infused with cinnamon sticks and lemon can detoxify smoker lungs. We fact checked and found the claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: Steam inhalation can sometimes provide temporary relief from congestion by moistening the mucous membranes in the airways, which can make breathing slightly easier. However, this is a temporary effect, and it doesn't 'cleanse' the lungs in the way the claim suggests. It doesn't address the underlying damage caused by smoking. Overly hot steam can also be a risk for burns. While cinnamon has some anti-inflammatory properties due to its cinnamaldehyde content, there's no scientific evidence to support the idea that inhaling cinnamon steam detoxifies or cleanses lungs, especially from the damage caused by smoking. In fact, inhaling cinnamon in this way could potentially irritate the respiratory tract. Cinnamon contains volatile oils that, when inhaled in concentrated amounts, can cause inflammation and discomfort. The idea of 'detox water' removing toxins from specific organs like the lungs is a marketing myth. The body has its own highly efficient detoxification systems – primarily the liver and kidneys – which are far more effective than any detox drink. Inhaling lemon water can be hydrating, which is beneficial for overall health, but it won't magically undo the damage caused by smoking. There's no scientific basis to suggest that lemon water specifically targets lung toxins. Smoking causes significant and lasting damage to the lungs, including inflammation, destruction of alveoli (air sacs), and an increased risk of serious diseases like lung cancer, emphysema, and chronic bronchitis. No home remedy, including steam inhalation with cinnamon and lemon, can reverse this damage. Quitting smoking is the only proven way to slow the progression of lung damage and reduce the risk of smoking-related illnesses. While short periods of steam inhalation might be okay for some, inhaling steam through a cinnamon stick poses potential risks. Cinnamon contains volatile compounds that can irritate the airways, especially with repeated or prolonged exposure. This could lead to coughing, wheezing, or even more serious respiratory problems, particularly for individuals with asthma or other respiratory sensitivities. This method does nothing to address the highly addictive nature of nicotine, which is a major barrier to quitting smoking. Effective smoking cessation requires addressing both the physical and psychological dependence on nicotine, often through a combination of counselling, medication (like nicotine replacement therapy or other prescription medications), and support groups. Dr. Rohan Bartake, a Tobacco Treatment Specialist from Mumbai, explains, 'The idea of detoxifying the lungs is misleading. Once damage has occurred, such as the destruction of alveoli or the accumulation of tar, no food or drink can reverse it. However, adopting a healthy diet and lifestyle can support the body's overall function, improving lung capacity and preventing further harm. Key actions like quitting smoking, avoiding pollutants, and staying hydrated can help the lungs with their natural healing processes, but herbal teas or specific foods cannot directly cleanse the lungs.' Dr. P. Rammanohar, Research Director at the Amrita Centre for Advanced Research in Ayurveda, states that treatment strategies depend on the level of lung damage. He stresses that Ayurveda does not provide a detox or a miracle cure to reverse lung damage. However, Ayurvedic therapies can help prevent further harm to the lungs. Quitting smoking is crucial, and if the damage is detected early, partial recovery of lung function may be possible.
