title: Can Lemon, Eno, Black Pepper and Black Salt dissolve rocks in the Body?
claim_text: A Facebook post claims that mixing lemon juice with Eno, black pepper (kali mirch), and black salt (kala namak) creates a powerful drink capable of helping with indigestion. The claimant even exaggerates further, saying that 'even if someone eats rocks, this drink will digest them'.
quick_take: A social media post shows a man loudly claiming that he has so much confidence in his drink made with Eno, lemon, black salt and black pepper that it can even dissolve rocks when consumed. We fact checked and found the claim to be false.
doctor_explanation: Dietitian Shikha Sharma, MSc in Foods and Nutrition, Noida, explains, "The claim that a mixture of lemon juice, Eno, black pepper and black salt can dissolve rocks inside the human body has no scientific basis. The digestive system is designed to break down nutrients from food such as carbohydrates, proteins and fats, not solid mineral materials. Even the stomach's own acid, hydrochloric acid, which is quite strong, cannot dissolve stones or rocks. Lemon juice contains citric acid, but it is significantly weaker than stomach acid, and Eno mainly creates a fizzing reaction due to the release of carbon dioxide gas when its ingredients react with water. This bubbling may look dramatic, but it does not mean the mixture has any ability to break down or dissolve hard substances inside the body." Dr Durga Priyadarshini, PhD, Nutrition Researcher & Founder, Nutrition Research Hub, Chennai, says, "Some ingredients in this mixture may provide mild relief from temporary digestive discomfort. Eno works as an antacid that can neutralise excess stomach acid for a short period, and black pepper contains compounds that may stimulate digestive enzymes. However, this effect is limited and should not be confused with the ability to dissolve stones or rocks. Viral claims often exaggerate simple digestive remedies and present them as powerful cures, which can mislead people. Good digestive health is supported through balanced eating, fibre intake, hydration and medical guidance when needed, not through home remedies that promise unrealistic results." The article explains that rocks are made of hard minerals such as silica, calcium compounds, or other geological materials that require extremely strong acids or high temperatures to break down. The human digestive system simply does not function in that way. Even stomach acid, which has a pH of around 1.5 to 3.5, cannot dissolve stones or rocks. If someone were to swallow a rock, the body would not 'digest' it at all - it would either pass through the digestive tract or potentially cause injury or blockage. The fizzing reaction when lemon juice and Eno are mixed is just a simple chemical reaction producing carbon dioxide gas. When sodium bicarbonate (in Eno) reacts with acid, bubbles form - the same reaction that happens when baking soda is mixed with vinegar in school science experiments. The bubbles may look dramatic, but they do not indicate that anything powerful is happening inside the body. Once consumed, this reaction quickly settles in the stomach. The fizzing may temporarily relieve acidity by neutralising some stomach acid, which is why products like Eno are sometimes used for indigestion. But the effect is mild and short-lived. Importantly, the bubbles have nothing to do with dissolving stones or breaking down hard materials - the reaction simply releases gas and forms salts and water. It does not produce any compound capable of dissolving rocks or mineral deposits.

title: Fact Check: Can Lemon, Garlic, Turmeric and Honey Cure Fatty Liver in 8 Days?
claim_text: Lemon, Garlic, Turmeric and Honey Cures Fatty Liver in 8 Days — "In just eight days, your fatty liver will become as good as new with this home remedy. The liver is such an organ in our body that even after being 90% damaged, it can still heal itself. However, we often rely on medicines for it — tablets, capsules, and injections — which end up doing more harm than good. Because of their side effects, the liver gets further damaged, more toxins accumulate, and fat builds up... [remedy of lemon juice, crushed garlic, turmeric, and honey in water consumed overnight and on empty stomach for eight days] ...God willing, you'll see your liver starting to cleanse, toxins being released from your body, energy returning within you, and diseases moving away from your system."
quick_take: The claim by the user that Lemon, Garlic, Turmeric and Honey Cures Fatty Liver in 8 Days is FALSE. While it's true that foods like turmeric and garlic may play a supportive role in liver health, the idea that a simple mixture of lemon, garlic and turmeric can cure fatty liver in 8 days is unsubstantiated and potentially harmful if it leads someone to delay proper care.
doctor_explanation:
Dr. Naveen Polavarapu, Senior Consultant Gastroenterologist, Liver Specialist & Advanced Therapeutic Endoscopist & Endosonologist, Yashoda Hospitals, Hyderabad explained:

"The 'Liver Cleanse' Myth: First, it's important to understand that your liver is not a dirty filter that needs periodic flushing or cleansing. It is your body's primary and highly efficient detoxification organ already. It continuously filters your blood, metabolizes medications, neutralizes toxins, and produces bile to carry waste out of the body.

The Role of the Individual Ingredients:
- Turmeric: Turmeric has an anti-inflammatory property. Fatty liver disease is mainly caused by chronic inflammation and Turmeric may offer benefit.
- Lemon: Lemons are rich in vitamin C which is a potent anti-oxidant that offers anti-inflammatory benefits.
- Garlic: Garlic is rich in allicin and selenium which carry potent anti-oxidant property.
- Honey: Honey has anti-inflammatory effects. However, Honey is rich in sugars (fructose and glucose) which may raise the blood sugars.

In conclusion, although these have anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, there is no scientific evidence that these can detoxify the liver. The idea of a quick-fix 'cleanse' is an oversimplification of a complex, ongoing process.

To keep your liver healthy:
1) Eat balanced and nutritious diet
2) Exercise regularly
3) Keep Diabetes, high cholesterol levels under control
4) Avoid liver toxic agents like alcohol, indigenous medications
5) Use medications wisely."

Dr. D. Chandra Sekhar Reddy, Senior Consultant Gastroenterologist, Hepatologist and Therapeutic Endoscopist, Yashoda Hospitals, Hyderabad further added:
"This message of lemon, garlic, turmeric and honey curing fatty liver in eight days is fake. Fatty liver is mainly caused by Obesity, uncontrolled diabetes, high cholesterol level and usage of some drugs. In fatty liver disease we have to control all these risk factors to reverse the fatty liver. Fatty liver main stay of treatment is weight reduction and usage of drugs like Resmiterom at least for one year. Claiming of lemon, garlic, turmeric and honey cures fatty liver disease is false and sometimes turmeric in genetically susceptible individuals can cause severe liver damage."

The article further states:
There is no scientific evidence or medical consensus that fatty liver disease can be cured within such a short period (8 days) just by consuming lemon, garlic, turmeric and honey. While some of these foods may support liver health, they do not replace medical treatment and sustained lifestyle changes.

Fatty liver (Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease, NAFLD) is classified into NAFL (simple steatosis, fat without inflammation or damage) and NASH (Non-Alcoholic Steatohepatitis, with inflammation, hepatocyte ballooning, Mallory hyaline, and inflammatory cell infiltration that can progress to fibrosis or cirrhosis). The distinction requires a liver biopsy.

Fatty liver progresses through four stages: Type 1 (fat accumulation without inflammation, generally harmless), Type 2 (fat build-up with lobular inflammation), Type 3 (fat accumulation and ballooning degeneration indicating liver cell injury), and Type 4 (most advanced — fat accumulation, ballooning, Mallory hyaline or fibrosis potentially progressing to cirrhosis). Types 1 and 2 are reversible with lifestyle changes; Types 3 and 4 cause significant and often irreversible damage.

While garlic has demonstrated hepatoprotective properties in a study published in Food Chemistry Advances, and curcumin supplementation (per Roghayeh Molani-Gol et al., PubMed: 37918958) may enhance liver function, lower serum triglycerides, improve insulin sensitivity, and reduce obesity in NAFLD patients, these are supportive findings — not evidence of a cure within 8 days.

The claim that a simple mixture of these ingredients can cure fatty liver in 8 days is unsubstantiated and potentially harmful if it leads someone to delay proper medical care.

title: Fact Check: Can lemon, ginger, garlic and apple cider vinegar remove blockages from heart veins?
claim_text: Consuming a mixture of lemon juice, ginger juice, garlic juice, and apple cider vinegar — combined with honey, boiled down, and taken one tablespoon daily before breakfast — can open heart veins and gradually eliminate blockages.
doctor_explanation: Dr. Prem Aggarwal (MBBS, MD - General Medicine, DNB - Cardiology, DNB - General Medicine), Senior Cardiologist, Sanjeevan Hospital, New Delhi: 'In cardiovascular medicine, it is the arteries, not the veins, that typically become blocked due to plaque buildup, leading to conditions like coronary artery disease. Arteries are responsible for delivering oxygen-rich blood to the heart muscle, and when they narrow or get blocked, it can result in a heart attack or angina. Treatments such as angioplasty and stenting are designed to open blocked arteries, not veins. Heart veins, particularly the coronary veins, have a different function. They carry deoxygenated blood from the heart muscle back to the right atrium of the heart. Veins do not typically develop the same kind of blockages as arteries. In rare cases, vein-related issues, such as blood clots, can occur, but these are managed with anticoagulation therapy, not procedures to open them. Patients need to differentiate between arteries and veins when discussing heart health. If someone is experiencing symptoms of coronary artery disease, such as chest pain or shortness of breath, they should consult a cardiologist for proper diagnosis and treatment focused on the arteries.' Dr. Manav Aggarwal, Interventional Cardiologist, Sanjeevan Hospital, New Delhi: 'Blockages are in the heart's arteries, not veins, are typically due to atherosclerosis, which involves the buildup of plaque (composed of fat, cholesterol, and other substances). This condition requires medical treatment such as lifestyle changes, medications, or interventional procedures like angioplasty or bypass surgery. While lemon, ginger, garlic, and apple cider vinegar may offer some health benefits—such as lowering cholesterol levels or providing antioxidant properties—these are supportive measures that cannot reverse or unclog blocked arteries. They may contribute to overall heart health when included in a balanced diet, but they are not substitutes for proven medical treatments in cases of arterial blockages. Patients should always seek proper medical advice by doctors for conditions like coronary artery disease and avoid relying on unproven remedies. Early diagnosis and treatment are key to managing cardiovascular conditions effectively, and cardiologists can provide the appropriate interventions based on a patient's specific needs.' The article further explains that lemons (Citrus limon) are a rich source of Vitamin C supporting immune function, packed with antioxidants that combat oxidative stress and inflammation, and may help improve cholesterol levels and reduce blood pressure. Ginger (Zingiber officinale) contains bioactive compounds with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties and aids in muscle relaxation. Garlic (Allium sativum L.) contains organosulfur compounds with anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immune-enhancing properties; it has been shown to lower blood pressure, improve cholesterol levels, and may help reduce heart disease risk. Apple Cider Vinegar (ACV) retains nutrients from apples including pectin, B vitamins, biotin, folic acid, niacin, pantothenic acid, and vitamin C; research suggests it may reduce hemoglobin A1C (HbA1C), lower LDL cholesterol and triglycerides, and increase HDL cholesterol. However, none of these individual ingredients — whether consumed separately or combined — can reverse or remove arterial blockages. Arterial blockages (atherosclerosis) involve a complex process of plaque accumulation requiring medical interventions such as lifestyle changes, medications, and surgical procedures like angioplasty or bypass surgery. The images in the viral post depict arterial blockages, not venous blockages. Heart veins (coronary veins) carry deoxygenated blood from the heart muscle back to the right atrium and do not get blocked in the manner described. There is no scientific evidence or medical consensus supporting the claim that consuming this mixture can open blocked arteries or veins.

title: Fact Check: Can lemon ginger tea make your hair long and strong?
claim_text: Drinking lemon ginger tea every day can make your hair long and strong, reduce inflammation and pain, treat ovarian cysts naturally, get rid of diabetes, improve digestion, and boost your skin health.
quick_take: A social media post claims that drinking lemon ginger tea can make your hair long and strong. Our fact check found that this claim is mostly false.
doctor_explanation:
Dr Sachin Gupta, Consultant Dermatologist at Amrita Hospital, Faridabad, explains: 'Healthy hair is not the result of a single ingredient or remedy. It comes from a combination of good nutrition, proper hair care practices, and genetic factors, which means that while herbal teas like lemon ginger can be part of a healthy diet, they are not a miracle solution for hair growth.' While both lemon and ginger offer certain health benefits, there's no strong evidence to suggest that drinking lemon ginger tea will magically make your hair grow longer or stronger. Lemon is rich in vitamin C, which supports collagen production, an important protein for healthy hair. Ginger contains antioxidants that may improve circulation, which could benefit your scalp. Although ginger may help reduce inflammation on the scalp, some research suggests that certain substances in ginger (gingerol) could actually hinder hair growth. On the other hand, a 2024 study indicates that cedrol, a compound found in ginger, could potentially stimulate hair growth. This adds to the controversy surrounding the current evidence. Furthermore, there isn't enough scientific proof to guarantee significant hair growth or strength. Healthy hair actually depends on a balanced diet, hydration, and proper hair care.

On inflammation: Ginger has pro-inflammatory properties. Studies show that ginger can help reduce inflammation and pain, especially for joint pain and muscle aches. It contains a compound called gingerol, which has been shown to ease inflammation in some cases. Lemon also has antioxidants that help combat oxidative stress. So, drinking lemon ginger tea might provide some mild relief from inflammation or general pain, but it shouldn't serve as a replacement for professional treatments.

On ovarian cysts: Unfortunately, no. Ovarian cysts are fluid-filled sacs that form either inside or on the surface of the ovaries. While many are harmless and resolve on their own, persistent or problematic cysts require medical attention. Although ginger has anti-inflammatory benefits for some conditions, there is no scientific evidence to suggest that lemon ginger tea can treat or shrink ovarian cysts. Similarly, while lemon is rich in vitamin C and antioxidants, it does not influence the formation or resolution of cysts.

On diabetes: Ginger has been studied for its potential to help lower blood sugar levels, but drinking lemon ginger tea won't cure diabetes. Type 2 diabetes is a serious, chronic condition that requires careful management through diet, exercise, and medication. As of now, there's no cure for diabetes. Dr P Rammanohar, Research Director at the Amrita School of Ayurveda, explains: 'In Ayurveda, diabetes is classified into different stages based on its progression. Early-stage diabetes, or Kapha Prameha, can often be managed and even reversed with lifestyle changes and supportive treatments. However, advanced diabetes, known as Pitta Prameha, cannot be cured but can be controlled with lifelong medication. In its most severe form, Vata Prameha, diabetes becomes very difficult to manage. Despite extensive research, no single herb or remedy has been found to offer a complete cure for diabetes.' Dr V Mohan adds: 'The terms 'Diabetes Reversal' or 'Diabetes Cure' have gained a lot of attention recently, though they are not entirely new. A more accurate term would be 'Diabetes Remission,' as it means the condition has temporarily improved but could return. Currently, there is no cure for diabetes.'

On digestion: Ginger has long been used to soothe the stomach, reduce nausea, and improve digestion. It can help calm indigestion and bloating. Lemon, with its acidity, may also support digestion by stimulating bile production. Dietitian Anuradha Sharma says: 'Lemon ginger tea can definitely help with digestion! Ginger is known for its ability to reduce bloating, improve gut motility, and ease nausea, while lemon adds a dose of vitamin C and can stimulate digestive juices. Together, they make a soothing drink that supports your digestive system, especially after a heavy meal. However, it's not a magic cure—pair it with a balanced diet and healthy habits for the best results.'

On skin health: Lemon is rich in antioxidants and vitamin C, which plays a crucial role in collagen production—important for healthy skin. Ginger's antioxidants can help protect the skin from damage caused by free radicals. Drinking lemon ginger tea might help keep you hydrated and provide some protection against skin ageing. Dr Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant based in Lucknow, explains: 'Lemon ginger tea is often thought to help with acne, reduce wrinkles, and brighten the skin. While both lemon and ginger have antioxidants and anti-inflammatory properties, there's limited scientific evidence to support these claims. The tea might offer mild benefits like helping digestion and promoting overall health, but it won't significantly address skin concerns. For healthy skin, it is more important to maintain a good skincare routine, protect your skin from the sun, and live a balanced lifestyle, rather than relying on this tea as a miracle cure.'

Additionally, ginger may not be safe for individuals in late pregnancy, those with a history of pregnancy complications, or those with clotting disorders.

title: Can lemon, holy basil, and coconut water cure kidney stones in one day?
claim_text: Consuming a mixture of lemon (Nimbu), holy basil (tulsi ke patte), and coconut water (nariyal pani) will remove any and every type of kidney stone in just one day. The post guarantees a permanent cure with no recurrence.
quick_take: A social media post claims that lemon, holy basil, and coconut water can cure kidney stones in one day. After fact checking, we conclude that this claim is false.
doctor_explanation: There is no scientific evidence that lemon, holy basil, and coconut water can dissolve kidney stones in a single day. Lemon juice contains citrate, which can help prevent certain stones (like calcium oxalate) and slow their growth, but it doesn't dissolve them instantly. Coconut water has shown some protective effects, such as increasing urinary citrate and reducing stone formation in rats, according to 2013 and 2018 studies. Tulsi leaves were found to reduce kidney damage in rats exposed to harmful chemicals in a 2020 study, but this had nothing to do with kidney stones. Kidney stones differ in size and type. Some small stones may pass naturally with fluids over time, but larger stones or certain types often need medicines or procedures. No natural mix can promise a one-day, permanent cure. Dr Ubaid ur Rehman, General Physician, Holy Mission Clinic, New Delhi, clarifies, "There's no evidence to suggest that a mixture of lemon, holy basil, and coconut water can dissolve kidney stones in just one day. While some ingredients may help support kidney health, passing or breaking down stones usually requires more than just natural remedies." Kidney stones are complex and their treatment depends heavily on their size, location, and type (e.g., calcium oxalate, uric acid, struvite, cystine). A single home remedy, regardless of its ingredients, cannot effectively treat the vast array of kidney stone types. Medical treatments, ranging from medication to break down certain stones to procedures like lithotripsy or surgery for larger stones, are specific to the individual's unique condition. Relying solely on this mixture could delay necessary medical care. Dr Ganesh Srinivasa Prasad P, Consultant Nephrologist at Narayana Health City, Bengaluru, shared with THIP Media that kidney stones are common in tropical countries, often due to dehydration. He emphasised that no home remedy can guarantee the prevention or cure of all types of kidney stones. "The key to reducing the risk involves staying well hydrated, limiting salt intake, maintaining a healthy weight, consuming calcium-rich foods, and avoiding high-oxalate foods. For those at risk of uric acid stones, reducing red meat, sugar, refined carbs, alcohol, and smoking can also help manage the risk," he explained. Dr Almas Fatma, Diploma in Family Medicine, PG in Digital Health, and General Physician from Navi Mumbai, says, "There is no guaranteed cure for all types of kidney stones. The treatment varies based on the size, type, and location of the stones. While some smaller stones may pass naturally with increased fluid intake, larger or more complex stones often require medical intervention such as medication, shockwave therapy, or surgery. What works for one person may not be effective for another, and not all stones respond to the same treatments." Kidney stones can recur (lifetime recurrence rate is 60%–80%), especially if the underlying causes aren't addressed. Factors like genetics, diet, hydration levels, and certain medical conditions contribute to stone formation. Adequate hydration (which coconut water contributes to) and consuming citrate-rich fluids (like lemon water) are often recommended as part of a strategy to prevent future stone formation. But, they do not offer a guaranteed, permanent prevention against recurrence for everyone. Managing kidney stone risk usually involves dietary changes, increased fluid intake, and sometimes medication, guided by medical professionals. The management of kidney stones depends on the size and type of the stone. Small stones often pass on their own if you drink plenty of water. Pain relief is important during this time. If the stone is large or causes problems, doctors may use medicines to help it pass or suggest treatments like shock wave therapy to break it into smaller pieces, using a thin tube to remove it, or surgery for very large stones. To prevent new stones, doctors usually recommend changes in diet, such as drinking more water, eating less salt, and reducing animal protein, depending on the type of stone. The claim that lemon, holy basil, and coconut water can cure kidney stones in one day is false. The claim is scientifically baseless and potentially harmful if it leads people to forgo evidence-based medical treatment. While components of the mixture offer general health benefits and hydration is vital, they are not a miraculous, instant cure for all kidney stones. Kidney stone treatment requires proper medical diagnosis and management.

title: Fact Check: Can lemon juice with oregano be a substitute for antibiotics? - THIP Media
claim_text: A mixture of lemon juice, oregano and water can substitute for antibiotics
quick_take: A social media post claims that a mixture of lemon juice, oregano and water substitute for antibiotics. We fact-checked and found this claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: Research by THIP states, 'Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacterial infections and prevent their rampant growth and multiplication. They are quite effective against strep throat, urinary tract infection and diseases caused by Escherichia coli. Even though antibiotics are beneficial, you must consider taking antibiotics only when necessary. It is because they have side effects that may cause antibiotic resistance.' No. There is no scientific evidence that a mixture of lemon juice, oregano and water substitute for antibiotics. In fact, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) does not list oregano oil in their FDA-approved drug database to use in place of antibiotics. Even though research has shown that oregano essential oil may be effective against some potentially antibiotic-resistant bacteria. But, further investigations are needed. While oregano has some antimicrobial properties as noted by a few researchers, it should not be used as a replacement for clinically studied medications as a full antibiotic course. Human trials are still left to be tested and prove their efficiency. Similarly, research on lemon juice, lemon peel extract and citric acid was carried out and it was found that all above three samples at a certain dilution in combination with antibiotics modulated the activity of antibiotics which resulted in the inhibition of drug-resistant bacteria. Dietitian Atasi Konar regarding the usage of lemon juice and oregano as antibiotics replied that, 'Nobody should replace antibiotics with home ingredients. However, natural ingredients can be consumed along with antibiotics for a better immune response against bacterial infection'. For lemon juice, Dt. Atasi said 'Antibiotic inhibits bacterial replication by damaging components of the bacteria, like cell walls, that allow them to protect themselves. Not much scientific evidence is present that shows how lemon juice, oregano and water attacks bacteria. Some evidence suggests that lemon concentrate can inhibit the growth of salmonella, staphylococcus, and candida infections. Lemon juice might also attack antibiotic-resistant bacteria, which causes pneumonia and blood infections. Citrus products in dilution and in combination with antibiotics can modulate the activity of antibiotic to inhibit a drug resistant bacterium.' For oregano, Dt. Atasi said 'Carvacrol is an active phytonutrient found in oregano essential oil, that helps to treat sinus infection and fungal infection of skin. It has important therapeutic properties that help to heal the body when inhaled. Oregano oil has been found to heal gastric ulcers and reduce inflammation. It can also be paired with white vinegar, distilled water, and lemon juice to create a natural homemade disinfecting cleaner, be an antimicrobial remedy, still it should not replace medical treatment'. According to a social media post oregano can reduce viral activities from human respiratory syncytial virus within 15 minutes. Dietitian Bhavita Shah explains it further saying, 'Lemon juice and oregano help in reducing inflammation and improves fungal infection. But, neither oregano nor lemon can act as a substitute for antibiotics.' If antibiotics have been prescribed to a patient, one should definitely not opt for any homemade substitute for it. Else, the disease might spread and serious complications might occur.

title: Fact Check: Can lemon shot 20 mins before lunch cure migraine?
claim_text: Whoever has issues like acidity, migraine, or headache we must definitely give them a lemon shot. That means, 20 minutes before your lunch. Take half a lemon, add a little hing (asafoetida), some black pepper, and black salt. Drink that lemon juice mix. Guaranteed you won't have acidity or migraine.
quick_take: There is no scientific evidence or medical consensus that drinking a lemon shot before lunch cures migraines. While lemons contain vitamin C and antioxidants that contribute to general health, they do not treat or cure migraines, which are complex neurological disorders. Moreover, citrus fruits like lemon may actually trigger migraines in some individuals.
doctor_explanation:
Dr Rahul Chawla, Associate consultant, Department of Neurology, PSRI Hospitals, New Delhi explained, "There is no scientific evidence to support the claim that drinking a lemon shot before lunch can cure migraines. Migraine is a complex neurological disorder involving genetic, vascular, hormonal, and environmental factors. It cannot be 'cured' by any single food or remedy—including lemon. Lemons are rich in vitamin C and antioxidants, which can support general health, but they do not target the specific pathophysiological mechanisms of migraine—such as cortical spreading depression, trigeminovascular activation, or serotonin imbalance. Additionally, citrus fruits like lemon may actually trigger migraines in some individuals due to their tyramine content and potential to irritate the stomach lining, especially if consumed on an empty stomach. While some people believe natural remedies help reduce frequency or severity, these should never replace evidence-based medical care. Self-treating chronic migraines with unverified remedies can delay proper diagnosis and management, potentially worsening the condition."

Ms. Veena V, Chief Clinical Dietician, Aster Whitefield Hospital, Bengaluru further said, "There is no scientific studies, proven data, or scientific facts indicating that a lemon shot can cure migraine. While a lemon shot is not presented as a remedy or cure for migraines in the source, it does explain that some people might experience a small relief or feel better after taking one. This potential feeling of improvement is attributed to several possible factors: Hydration: Lemon with water provides hydration, and dehydration is identified as a possible trigger for migraine. Hydration can help reduce this trigger. Digestion Support: Lemon can promote mild digestive stimulation. The source notes that gut health is considered very important for preventing headaches like migraines, suggesting a link between gut tissues and migraines. Antioxidants and Vitamin C: Lemon is described as being very rich in Vitamin C and antioxidants. These are said to support overall health and may help reduce oxidative stress, which is mentioned as another potential reason for migraine. Reducing this stress could lead to some small relief. Alkalizing Effect: Lemon is stated to have an alkalizing effect. Some people feel this helps in balancing pH. These factors are presented as potential reasons why some individuals might feel better or experience slight relief. However, the source explicitly states that these effects do not constitute scientific evidence or facts proving that a lemon shot cures migraine. For severe migraines or headaches, the recommendation is to consult a doctor or seek proper treatment."

Supporting scientific evidence cited: A randomized controlled trial by Mehrnaz Jafarpour et. al. reported that lemon consumption could help reduce the intensity of migraine episodes (PubMed: 26721220). However, a study by Camboim Rockett F et al found that citrus fruits were significant potential triggers for migraines with aura (PubMed: 22732972). According to University of California's Migraine Diet Table, citrus fruits and juices containing lemon/lime are potential migraine triggers and should be reduced, avoided or limited by migraine patients. An article in the American Journal of Health-System Pharmacy also lists citrus fruits and juices under common diet-related triggers of migraine. Therefore, multiple studies and expert guidelines have identified citrus fruits, including lemon, as dietary triggers for some individuals, and there is no evidence that lemon shot with hing, black pepper and black salt can cure migraines.

title: Fact Check: Can lemon, turmeric and garlic cure stage 4 cancer?
claim_text: Drinking a mix of lemon, raw turmeric, one garlic clove, and apple cider vinegar—followed 30 minutes later by eating 10-12 neem and tulsi leaves—can cure stage 4 cancer at home within 40 days, for free.
quick_take: A social media post suggests home remedies for cancer. It claims that a mix of lemon, raw turmeric, garlic, and vinegar can be a home remedy for cancer and cure stage 4 cancer at home within 40 days, for free. However, this is false.
doctor_explanation: While both turmeric and garlic contain compounds with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, they are not proven cancer cures or a reliable home remedy to kill cancer cells. Curcumin in turmeric and allicin in garlic have shown some promise in lab studies. But these were mostly done in test tubes or on animals, not in real-life patients. Also, the body does not absorb curcumin very well. Eating raw turmeric or garlic cannot treat stage 4 cancer, which is a severe and advanced form of the disease needing urgent medical care. There is no evidence that lemon juice or apple cider vinegar can kill cancer cells in the body. Some people believe these ingredients make the body "alkaline," which they claim stops cancer. But this idea is a myth. The body controls its pH balance very tightly, and food or drinks cannot change it enough to kill cancer. Cancer is a complex disease, and changing your diet alone is not a cure. So far, what kills cancer cells in the body effectively is proper medical treatment, not folk remedies. Neem and tulsi (holy basil) have traditional uses in Ayurveda and may support general immunity. But they cannot replace cancer treatment. There are no good human studies that prove neem or tulsi can treat or cure cancer. Some lab studies show they might have anti-cancer properties, but again, these are early-stage findings—not treatment-level solutions. Relying only on these leaves can delay proper medical treatment and worsen the condition. Because delays can be life-threatening. Stage 4 cancer is very serious. It means the cancer has spread to other parts of the body. Waiting 40 days to try a home remedy for cancer instead of starting treatment like chemotherapy, radiation, or surgery can give the cancer time to grow further. This can lower the chances of survival. Cancer treatment works best when started early and done under medical supervision. Dr Pooja Khullar, Radiation Oncologist at Dharamshila Narayana Super Speciality Hospital, New Delhi, explained: "After being diagnosed, many patients look for alternative treatments in hopes of fewer side effects or more natural approaches. As an oncologist, I completely understand that instinct. But I don't recommend using such alternatives alongside or in place of evidence-based cancer therapies." She further explained: "Most alternative remedies lack strong clinical backing and haven't been studied with the same scientific rigour as standard treatments. While they may provide temporary relief or emotional comfort, they can interfere with proper treatment and may delay timely care, which is risky. I strongly advise patients not to mix or replace their prescribed treatment with any alternative method without medical supervision. Always check with your oncology team before starting anything new. In cancer care, science-backed medicine is what saves lives, and that must remain the priority." Dr P. Rammanohar, Research Director at Amrita School of Ayurveda, explained: "Cancer is not a single illness but a group of diseases, each requiring a customized medical approach involving treatments like chemotherapy, radiation, or targeted drugs. There isn't one herb or natural remedy that can treat all forms of cancer. Some herbal ingredients have shown encouraging results in early laboratory research, but we lack strong, large-scale human studies to confirm their effectiveness. Until such evidence exists, it's crucial to stick with scientifically tested treatments and seek advice from qualified medical professionals before exploring alternative options." In summary, there is no scientific proof that lemon, turmeric, garlic, vinegar, neem, and tulsi can cure stage 4 cancer in 40 days. The claim is misleading and dangerous.

title: Fact Check: Can lemon used with vaseline transform your face into a porcelain doll? - THIP Media
claim_text: Use the Vaseline with the lemon to transform your face into a porcelain doll.
quick_take: A social media post claims that the use of vaseline with lemon can transform your face into a porcelain doll. We fact-checked and found this claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: Skin that is clear, smooth, blemish-free, and flawless that has tight pores and is radiant irrespective of skin color is referred to as porcelain skin. This is not only controlled by the products that we used but also by genetics and nutrition. Although it's normal to have skin that has texture and tone. Skin that has lost melanin (a pigment that gives color to human skin, hair, and eyes) is usually called hypopigmented skin. If no pigment is present, the skin is diagnosed as depigmented. No. There is no research that indicates that lemon used with vaseline transforms your face into a porcelain doll. The pictures which show the skin without texture and tone are edited and thus, deceiving. Until and unless you have translucent skin due to genetics or lack of melanin, you can't have it. Also, using lemon on the skin is not recommended as it is highly acidic and can cause skin irritations, dryness, and sun damage, especially if you have sensitive skin. Therefore, the claim is false. Dr. Sonali Kohli, Consultant Dermatologist, Sir HN Reliance Foundation Hospital, Mumbai, says "Using lemon along with Vaseline for porcelain skin is a complete myth. Vitamin C serums that are prepared for the face are of a particular formulation along with other additions which help balance the pH. When a person applies lemon directly to the face, you're disturbing the pH of the skin and making it completely acidic and in such cases, if there is sun exposure, it can lead to Phytophotodermatitis (a skin reaction). Hence, must be avoided." Regarding vaseline, she says, "Vaseline can work very well as an occlusive moisturizer primarily. However, people with oily and acne-prone skin will cause more trouble on their skin than benefit if they use Vaseline. So, the combination of lemon and Vaseline is a horrible idea. For people with sensitive skin, it is advised not to try these techniques and remedies as they can cause massive breakouts."

title: Fact Check: Can lemon water cure eyesight problems in 7 minutes?
claim_text: A home remedy using lemon water can fix all eyesight problems in just 7 minutes. Eye surgery and consultations with doctors are unnecessary.
quick_take: A social media post claims that lemon water can cure eyesight problems in just 7 minutes. Our fact check says this claim is False.
doctor_explanation:
The video featuring Anjana Om Kashyap and Dr Rahil Chaudhary is manipulated using AI. There is a clear lack of lip sync and natural facial expressions, and the gestures appear out of place. The Deepfakes Analysis Unit's investigation found that the video has AI-generated audio. Both personalities have strong online presence and have not endorsed any home remedy to get rid of glasses. Dr Rahil Chaudhary stated, 'We are not associated with any such video. The video must have been faked using modern AI tools.'

Dr Isha Agarwalla, Ophthalmologist from Drishti Netralaya, Dibrugarh, Assam: 'That claim is entirely false. There is no scientific basis to suggest that lemon water (nimbu paani) can cure eyesight problems, let alone in 7 minutes. Eye health is influenced by factors such as genetics, nutrition, lifestyle, and underlying medical conditions. While a balanced diet that includes vitamins and antioxidants can support overall eye health, no single remedy—especially lemon water—can provide a miraculous cure for complex vision issues. Claims like these can mislead people and prevent them from seeking proper medical advice.'

Dr Pradeep Dahale, Ophthalmologist at Manipal Hospital Baner in Pune: 'Eyeglasses are prescribed by ophthalmologists or optometrists to fix vision problems caused by differences in the eye's structure, like the length of the eyeball or the shape of the cornea. Dr Neha Rastogi Panda, Senior Infectious Diseases Specialist at Fortis Hospital in Gurgaon: 'Eye problems can happen for many reasons, including allergies, diseases, nutritional deficiencies, dust, injuries, and poor hygiene, like rubbing your eyes with dirty hands. It's important to treat these issues quickly to avoid infections or worsening symptoms. Relying on unproven methods can be risky. That's why it's essential to seek professional medical advice and use evidence-based treatments to manage your eye health effectively.'

Selenium is an important mineral that helps maintain eye health and acts as an antioxidant, protecting the eyes from damage. Some studies suggest that getting enough selenium may reduce the risk of certain eye diseases like AMD and cataracts, but selenium is not a cure for eyesight problems. title: Fact Check: Can lemon water relieve tooth pain?

doctor_explanation: No, lemon water does not help with tooth pain. Although lemon water is a popular home remedy with a reputation for various health benefits, it should not be used to manage tooth pain. Lemons are highly acidic, and when their juice is diluted in water, it still holds significant acidity. Direct exposure to acidic substances can erode the enamel, the protective layer on your teeth, which is likely to increase sensitivity and pain, rather than relieving it. For temporary relief, remedies like clove oil or salt water rinses are safer and more effective options for dental pain. Some people use mustard oil, turmeric and rock salt for tooth pain. However, it is important to seek professional dental care. Dr Sanjeev Bhankhur, BDS, MPH, AIIMS, New Delhi says: "Lemon water might seem like a soothing remedy, but it's not the best choice for tooth pain. The acidity can erode your enamel, which can make teeth more sensitive and likely to worsen any pain. For a true remedy, I recommend sticking to warm salt water rinses or using clove oil, or OTC pain relieving meds, these have been shown to help with pain. Most importantly, consult your dentist to know the root cause." Dr Snigdha, BDS, MDS, Vananchal Dental College and Hospital, Garhwa, Jharkhand clarifies: "While lemon water has its benefits, using it for tooth pain could actually backfire. Its acidity can wear down the enamel and increase tooth sensitivity over time. If you're dealing with tooth pain, focus on tried-and-true methods like over-the-counter pain relief or warm salt water rinses. And remember, severe or ongoing pain is a sign to visit your dentist." Regarding oral health benefits: Not really. Lemon water, despite its antioxidant properties and high vitamin C content, poses more risks than benefits for oral health. The acidity can erode enamel, leading to weakened teeth and increased vulnerability to cavities. This effect counteracts any potential antibacterial properties the lemon might offer. Drinking plain water or water infused with neutral herbs like mint is better for oral health. Regarding immune system: Yes, lemon water can contribute to boosting your immune system. Lemons are rich in vitamin C, a nutrient known to support immune function. Drinking warm lemon water regularly can help maintain hydration and provide a mild immune boost, though it should not be seen as a cure-all. A balanced diet rich in a variety of nutrients is essential for optimal immune health. Regarding weight loss: Somewhat, but lemon water alone is not a magic solution for weight loss. That being said, it still can cause heartburn in some people. Lemon is rich in vitamin C, a deficiency of which is associated with obesity. Due to this, some people think that lemon tea can help reduce belly fat effectively. But, lemon water should be complemented by a balanced diet and regular exercise for effective weight loss. Regarding blood purification: No, lemon water is not a blood purifier. Claims about lemon water "purifying" the blood are misleading. The body has its own sophisticated systems, such as the liver and kidneys, to filter and cleanse the blood. While lemon water can support hydration and liver function, it does not directly purify the blood or remove toxins. THIP Media Take: The claim that lemon water can relieve tooth pain is false. Its acidic nature can actually worsen tooth pain and erode enamel. While lemon water offers benefits like hydration and a vitamin C boost, it is not a remedy for pain or a cure-all. For tooth pain, rely on evidence-based treatments and consult a dentist. Drinking lemon water in moderation can be healthy, but be cautious of exaggerated health claims and prioritise proven health practices.

title: Fact Check: Can lemongrass really reduce anxiety? - THIP Media
claim_text: A social media post claims that lemongrass can naturally reduce anxiety and stress.
quick_take: A social media post suggests that adding some leaf of lemongrass in your tea will relieve anxiety and stress. We fact checked and found the claim to be Mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Lemongrass contains bioactive compounds like citral, myrcene, and limonene. Research shows mice treated with citral spent more time in open areas and showed less stress-related movement in tests like the elevated plus maze and open-field test. Scientists believe citral interacts with GABAA and serotonin (5-HT1A) receptors, which are the same pathways targeted by some prescription anti-anxiety medications. However, it is important to stress that these effects were observed in mice at controlled doses far higher than what a typical human would consume in tea or aromatherapy. Translating animal results directly to humans is not reliable. While lemongrass tea is widely consumed and generally considered safe, studies on human anxiety are extremely limited. Most claims about anxiety relief from lemongrass tea are anecdotal or based on traditional medicine. A human body processes herbs differently than a mouse, and the concentration of citral or other compounds in a cup of tea is much lower than the doses used in animal experiments. Drinking lemongrass tea may feel relaxing simply because drinking a warm beverage can reduce stress, but this is not the same as chemically reducing anxiety. Dr Madhu Wamsi, MBBS, MD (Psychiatry), Consultant Psychiatrist, Hyderabad said: 'Lemongrass aromatherapy may provide a mild, short-term calming effect, but it should only be seen as a complementary option. While small studies suggest benefits in reducing situational anxiety, there is no strong evidence to support it as a primary treatment. In my practice, I recommend it as a safe add-on for relaxation in selected patients, while structured therapy and, when required, medication remain the cornerstone of anxiety management.' Some studies suggest that inhaling lemongrass essential oil might have a mild calming effect due to its scent and interaction with the brain's olfactory system. A review highlighted that aromatherapy could influence mood and relaxation, but these studies were often small, short-term, and sometimes poorly controlled. While aromatherapy with lemongrass may enhance a sense of calm, it cannot replace evidence-based treatments for anxiety, such as therapy or medications prescribed by a healthcare professional. Dr P Dharaneedhar, MBBS, MD (Psychiatry), Consultant Psychiatrist and Assistant Professor at the Kamineni Institute of Medical Sciences, Narketpally, Telangana said: 'Lemon grass has anxiolytic properties as per some clinical trials but its effectiveness varies around 10 to 20% only, this can be useful for mild anxiety symptoms but is not reliable for the majority of cases who suffer with moderate to severe anxiety. Valid and long term studies in future may prove otherwise.' There are some potential side effects, especially if taken in high doses or as concentrated supplements. Lemongrass essential oil can irritate the skin or mucous membranes, and in rare cases, it can trigger allergic reactions. Drinking moderate amounts of lemongrass tea is usually safe for most adults, but pregnant women, children, or people with liver conditions should consult a doctor before using it regularly. Relying solely on lemongrass for anxiety could delay seeking proven treatments, which might worsen symptoms over time. Bottom Line: Lemongrass is a fragrant herb with compounds that show calming effects in laboratory studies, but these results do not automatically apply to humans. Drinking lemongrass tea or using its essential oil might provide a comforting ritual or mild relaxation, but it cannot cure or treat anxiety. Claims that lemongrass significantly reduces anxiety are exaggerated and not backed by human evidence.

title: Fact Check: Can licorice and curd make your skin fair? - THIP Media

doctor_explanation:
Can licorice powder actually lightEN skin? It may, to an extent. Licorice powder can help with skin tone. It contains glabridin, a compound known for its skin-lightening effects. Glabridin works by inhibiting tyrosinase, an enzyme involved in melanin production. Melanin is the pigment responsible for skin colour. Therefore, licorice may help reduce hyperpigmentation, such as dark spots. However, it won't dramatically change your skin tone to 'fair.' Because, that depends on genetics.

Is curd beneficial for the skin? It may, but there's no strong evidence yet. Curd can offer several skin benefits and has been used in our traditional face masks. It contains lactic acid, which acts as a gentle exfoliant, helping to remove dead skin cells and promote a smoother complexion. Curd also has moisturising properties that keep skin hydrated. These benefits can enhance overall skin appearance, but they won't lead to a significant lightening of skin tone.

Dr Rashi Soni, Co-founder and Consulting Dermatologist, Aesthetician, and Hair Transplant Surgeon at Rashi Hospital in Mumbai, says: "Curd is beneficial for the skin in several ways. It contains lactic acid, which acts as a gentle exfoliant, helping to remove dead skin cells and reveal a brighter complexion. Additionally, curd is naturally rich in moisture, which can keep your skin hydrated and supple. This makes it particularly helpful for those with dry or flaky skin." Dr Soni adds: "Moreover, the probiotics found in curd can help maintain a healthy skin barrier, supporting overall skin health. However, while curd can be a valuable part of your skincare routine, it's important to remember that it should complement a well-rounded approach. This includes using sunscreen, staying hydrated, and following a balanced diet. Embracing your skin's natural state is key to achieving a healthy glow!"

Can combining licorice powder and curd enhance skin fairness? Not exactly. The combination of licorice powder and curd can be soothing and may help improve skin texture and tone. While this blend can promote moisture and mild exfoliation, the claims of achieving 'fair' skin are misleading. Skin lightening is a complex process influenced by various factors, including genetics and sun exposure.

Dr Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant in Lucknow, says: "While licorice powder and curd can contribute to a healthier-looking complexion, it's important to understand that no natural remedy can drastically change your skin tone. The goal should be to achieve healthy, radiant skin rather than focusing solely on fairness. Embrace your natural skin colour and prioritise skincare routines that nourish and protect your skin."

Dr Annusuiya Gohil, MD Scholar at the All India Institute of Ayurveda, says: "Skin fairness is mainly determined by genetics, along with environmental factors. While you can improve skin brightness, you can't change your natural skin tone—it can only be enhanced. Over time, factors like ageing, exposure to harsh conditions, and diet can cause skin to dull, but you can work to restore its original glow. However, topical products won't alter your inherent complexion." Dr Gohil adds: "Mulethi, if taken internally, might help brighten the skin, and applying it can reduce pigmentation, but it won't change your natural skin colour."

Are there any side effects of licorice powder and curd on the skin? Generally, both licorice powder and curd are safe for topical use. However, some individuals may experience skin irritation or allergic reactions, especially those with sensitive skin. It's a good idea to perform a patch test before applying any new product to a larger area. If any adverse reactions occur, it's best to stop using it and consult a healthcare professional.

THIP Media Take: In summary, while licorice powder and curd can provide some benefits for the skin, the claim that they can make your skin 'fair' is mostly false. Both ingredients may improve skin health and appearance, but they are not miracle solutions for drastic skin lightening. Achieving an even and radiant complexion requires a holistic approach that includes proper skincare and sun protection. Instead of chasing unrealistic beauty standards, focus on nurturing your skin.

title: Fact Check: Can Maggi noodles cause anemia, joint pain, memory and hearing loss, kidney and liver swelling, and other health issues?
claim_text: Harmful Effects of Eating Maggi: deficiency of blood (anaemia), joint pain problems, memory loss, swelling in kidney and liver and hearing problems.
quick_take: An Instagram post claims that eating Maggi noodles causes blood deficiency or anaemia, joint pain, memory problems, kidney and liver swelling, and hearing issues. The claim is Mostly False. Current research does not directly link Maggi noodles to these conditions; while instant noodles may lack key nutrients, no study confirms Maggi as the cause of these issues.
doctor_explanation:
The article examines each claimed health effect individually against published scientific literature. 

Blood deficiency / Anaemia: Blood deficiency, medically known as anaemia, occurs when the body lacks enough red blood cells that contain haemoglobin, an iron-rich protein responsible for carrying oxygen. Anaemia is not a disease itself but a sign of an underlying problem. When severe, it can lead to fatigue, weakness, and shortness of breath. A study published in Applied Biological Chemistry states that Maggi noodles are high in fat and low in important nutrients like fiber and iron. However, it does not claim that Maggi causes anemia or blood deficiency.

Joint pain: Joint pain is a broad term that includes various types and causes. It can result from inflammation, cartilage damage, nerve irritation, or underlying conditions like arthritis, injury, or infection. Common types include inflammatory joint pain (as in arthritis), mechanical pain (from wear and tear), and neuropathic pain (due to nerve involvement). A study published in the journal Research Society and Development states that regular instant noodles contain very low calcium, a mineral essential for bone and joint development. The study does not specifically mention Maggi instant noodles or state that instant noodles cause joint pain.

Memory loss: Memory loss, also called amnesia, can be short-term or long-lasting and may have physical or psychological causes. It can result from head injury, brain infections, lack of oxygen, stroke, alcohol misuse, or certain surgeries. One study published in JAMA Network mentions that those whose diets consisted of more than 20% ultra-processed foods experienced a 28% faster global cognitive decline which includes memory and thinking decline. The study does not emphasize any relation of memory loss with Maggi or any instant noodle.

Kidney swelling: Kidney swelling, known medically as hydronephrosis, is a condition where urine builds up and causes one or both kidneys to enlarge. It can be caused by blockages such as kidney stones, tumors, or problems present from birth, and may affect kidney function if not treated. An article published in The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition highlighted that higher consumption of ultra-processed foods, including instant noodles, was significantly associated with a decline in kidney function over time. Again, the study has no relation with Maggi noodles and kidney swelling.

Liver swelling: Liver swelling, also known as hepatomegaly or an enlarged liver, may indicate conditions such as fatty liver disease, excessive alcohol use, hepatitis, or liver cancer. The research published in The Tohoku Journal of Experimental Medicine found that individuals who frequently consumed instant noodles, often during lunch, had significantly higher levels of liver enzymes ALT and GGT, which are indicators of liver stress or damage. But the research does not refer to Maggi noodles by name or include any mention of liver swelling.

Hearing issues / Hearing loss: Hearing loss can happen due to loud noise, aging, infections, certain health conditions, or even some medicines. It may also be caused by earwax buildup or a damaged eardrum. The study published in BMC Geriatrics mentioned that ultra-processed food intake causes high-frequency hearing loss compared to those who ate the least because of low nutritional value of ultra-processed food. But this study does not highlight anything about instant noodles or Maggi noodles.

Overall, the above studies indicated that Maggi noodles have low iron and calcium content, both essential for daily nutritional needs. Additionally, some studies suggest that instant noodles may elevate liver enzymes and impact liver function; however, there is no specific evidence linking these effects to Maggi noodles. While Maggi has low nutritional value, there is no scientific evidence to support claims that it causes blood deficiency, joint pain, memory problems, kidney or liver swelling, or hearing issues.

Dr. Leena Saju, Group Manager, Department of Clinical Nutrition, KIMSHEALTH told Medical Dialogues: "There is no clinical evidence linking instant noodles to joint pain, hearing loss, memory problem and anemia. Joint issues and memory problems are typically associated with inflammatory conditions or nutritional deficiencies (e.g., vitamin D, omega-3s, antioxidants). While processed foods with additives may promote low-grade inflammation when consumed in excess, occasional instant noodles consumption isn't directly harmful."

Ms. Deepa Mishra, Manager, Nutrition & Dietetics, Narayana RN Tagore Hospital, Mukundapur added: "Claims linking instant noodles like Maggi to conditions such as anaemia, joint pain, memory loss, or organ swelling lack scientific backing. These health issues are multifactorial and typically arise from chronic nutrient deficiencies, underlying medical conditions, or lifestyle factors. While instant noodles are low in key nutrients like iron, calcium, and fiber, occasional consumption as part of a balanced diet is unlikely to cause harm. However, regular reliance on ultra-processed foods can contribute to poor dietary quality and long-term health risks if not countered with adequate nutrition and lifestyle care."

Dr. Shubhadeep Das, MD, FRCPCH, FRCP (London & Edinburgh), Pediatric Cardiac Intensivist said: "There is no scientific or clinical evidence that occasional consumption of packaged noodles like Maggi causes blood deficiency, joint pain, memory loss, or swelling of the liver, kidneys, or hearing problems in children or adults. Such claims are misleading and lack any backing from peer-reviewed medical literature. While excessive consumption of highly processed foods high in sodium, preservatives, and saturated fats is discouraged for growing children due to long-term health implications. Attributing severe multisystemic issues like organ swelling or hearing loss to a single food item without context is unfounded and alarmist."

title: Fact Check: Can magnesium improve sleep quality?
claim_text: According to a post on Threads, "Magnesium helps you sleep better, calms the mind, reduces muscle cramps, relieves headaches, strengthens bones, lowers blood pressure, and is involved in over 600 enzymatic reactions, implying that most people aren't getting enough."
quick_take: A viral post claims that magnesium can improve sleep quality. We did a thorough research and found this claim to be mostly false.
doctor_explanation:
Magnesium is an essential electrolyte for the body and offers numerous health benefits. We have evidence that a deficiency of magnesium may lead to insomnia. This is because magnesium plays a role in the production of GABA, a neurotransmitter that promotes relaxation. Some studies suggest that magnesium supplementation can reduce stress and improve sleep in people with deficiencies or conditions like insomnia. Additionally, magnesium helps regulate melatonin, the hormone responsible for controlling the sleep-wake cycle. However, there is actually little evidence to show it has a notable impact on sleep in healthy individuals. It's important to note that sleep quality depends on various factors, including lifestyle, stress levels, and underlying health conditions, and not just magnesium intake.

Dr Roma Kumar, Senior Consultant Psychologist at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital and Max Hospital in New Delhi, states: "Magnesium may contribute to relaxation, but its impact on sleep is often exaggerated, especially in individuals without deficiencies. While it's true that magnesium can support the body's natural processes, including the regulation of stress and muscle function, sleep disturbances are rarely caused by magnesium deficiency alone. A holistic approach, addressing lifestyle factors, mental health, and overall well-being, is far more effective for improving sleep quality."

Dr Almas Fatma, MBBS, Diploma in Family Medicine, PG in Digital Health, General Physician from Navi Mumbai, clarifies: "Magnesium can be helpful in improving sleep for individuals who are deficient in it, as it plays a key role in relaxation and muscle function. However, it's not a one-size-fits-all solution. If you're struggling with sleep, it's important to consider a range of factors – from your diet and lifestyle to stress levels and mental health. A holistic approach, focusing on overall well-being, is often the most effective way to improve sleep quality. For chronic cases, consider consulting a professional."

Regarding calming the mind: Magnesium supports the nervous system by regulating stress responses and lowering cortisol levels. Evidence suggests it can reduce symptoms of anxiety, particularly in people with low magnesium levels. However, magnesium supplementation isn't a substitute for medical interventions or therapy for stress or mental health issues.

Regarding muscle cramps: Magnesium is vital for protein production in the body, supporting muscle growth and proper function. While it plays a key role in muscle relaxation, its effectiveness in relieving cramps is inconsistent. Research suggests it may help with pregnancy-related cramps, but there's limited evidence for other types, such as those from exercise or dehydration.

Regarding headaches: Magnesium deficiency has been linked to migraines. Supplements may reduce the severity and frequency of migraines for some individuals, especially those with low magnesium levels. However, magnesium isn't a universal headache remedy, and its effectiveness depends on the type of headache and the person's magnesium status.

Regarding bones: Magnesium supports calcium absorption and vitamin D metabolism, both essential for bone health. Low magnesium levels are associated with reduced bone density. However, bone strength also depends on factors like age, physical activity, and intake of other nutrients like calcium and vitamin K.

Regarding blood pressure: Research shows magnesium supplementation can lead to reductions in blood pressure, particularly in people with hypertension. Its effects are mild and should not replace other interventions like medication, exercise, or dietary changes.

Regarding deficiency: Magnesium deficiency is uncommon in healthy people. It's widely available in foods like leafy greens, nuts, seeds, and whole grains. However, certain groups, such as older people, individuals with gastrointestinal disorders, long-term alcohol abuse or those with type 2 diabetes, may be more prone to low magnesium levels. For the average healthy person, a balanced diet usually meets daily magnesium needs. The safe limit for magnesium supplements is 350 mg per day. They can cause nausea, cramps, or diarrhoea. Magnesium can also affect medicines like antibiotics, muscle relaxants, and blood pressure drugs. Talk to your doctor before using it if you have a health condition or take any medications.

THIP Media Take: The claim that magnesium helps you sleep better is mostly false. While magnesium can support sleep in people with deficiencies or specific conditions, it's not a universal solution for improving sleep. The other claims about magnesium's benefits, though partially true, are often exaggerated or depend on specific contexts. A balanced diet generally provides sufficient magnesium for most individuals.

quick_take: A social media post claims massaging onion on feet twice a day can lower high fever in children. We fact-checked and found the claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: No. Massaging onions on the feet cannot reduce fever. We could not find any evidence that shows keeping onion in touch with skin can cure bacterial or viral fever. A study has highlighted that onions may prevent the growth of certain pathogens as it has certain antibacterial properties. However, this study does not suggest rubbing onion on feet is beneficial in any manner. The Healthy Indian Project (THIP Media) has previously discussed that putting onion in socks cannot cure a cold and flu. We asked Voomika Mukherjee, Health & Nutrition Life Coach, if massaging onion on feet can cure fever. To this, she said "In general, cold happens when a virus causes inflammation into your throat and nose membranes. A stronger immunity can somehow protect you against this. So, instead of believing unproven, unscientific claims like massaging onions on feet, it is better to eat onions. Onion contains dozens of medicinal chemical compounds that have antibacterial and anti-inflammatory actions in the body. The sulphur compounds in onions also have a powerful antibacterial and antiviral action. But rubbing onion on feet is not going to help anyway in fighting cold." We also found a study that has confirmed onions have anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory and acquired immunity components which play an essential role in strengthening overall immunity. In conclusion, massaging onion on feet must not be followed in any group especially children as mentioned in the claim. Because their immune system is evolving in young age and practice like this can delay the required line of treatment. THIP MEDIA TAKE: No evidence confirms massaging onion on feet reduces fever. Rather eating onions may help strengthen overall immunity.

title: Fact Check: Can massaging with garlic, coconut oil, turmeric, black pepper and Vicks cure arthritis?
claim_text: Massaging with garlic, coconut oil, turmeric, black pepper and Vicks cures arthritis. The reel instructs to grate a garlic clove, mix in black pepper, coconut oil, turmeric powder, and Vicks, apply the mixture before bed massaging the painful area, cover with plastic wrap, and clean the next day — claiming 'the pain will be gone' and that repeating this three times a week means 'goodbye to knee pain, arthritis and muscle aches'.
quick_take: While ingredients like garlic, turmeric, and black pepper have anti-inflammatory properties that may help manage arthritis symptoms, there is no scientific evidence or medical consensus supporting the claim that applying them topically with coconut oil and spices can cure arthritis. Arthritis is a chronic, incurable condition.
doctor_explanation: Dr. Atul Shrivastava, Consultant - Orthopaedic Surgeon at Narayana Hospital, Howrah, stated: "It's a common misconception that arthritis can be cured. In reality, arthritis is a broad term for joint inflammation, and while it can't be reversed, its symptoms can be managed with the right treatment and lifestyle changes. Natural supplements like garlic, turmeric, coconut oil, and black pepper do have anti-inflammatory properties and may help ease the pain, but they do not cure the condition. Products like Vicks may offer temporary relief, but they're not a long-term solution. Our joints naturally age over time, they don't regenerate or grow younger." Dr. Sourav Saha, Consultant Orthopaedic & Joint Replacement at Narayana Hospital, Barasat, further added: "While ingredients like turmeric, garlic, and coconut oil have mild anti-inflammatory properties, there is no evidence that a topical mix of these — along with Vicks — can cure arthritis. At best, such remedies may offer temporary relief. Arthritis is a chronic condition that requires medical treatment, including medications, physiotherapy, and lifestyle management. Relying solely on home remedies can delay proper care and worsen outcomes." The article cites scientific evidence: a 2023 review by Silvana Zugaro et al. in Bioactives and Inflammation highlights garlic's anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immunostimulant properties through organosulfur compounds; Georgia Schäfer et al. note garlic's immune-enhancing potential. A 2022 review in Food & Function reported that garlic-derived compounds demonstrate anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial effects. A study by S. Ankri et al. emphasized that allicin, released when garlic is crushed, shows potent antibacterial, antifungal, antiparasitic, and antiviral activity. Turmeric, especially its active ingredient curcumin, has drawn interest for alleviating arthritis symptoms; a review of randomized clinical trials by James W. Daily and colleagues states the effectiveness of turmeric extract consumption in managing arthritis-related symptoms. Black pepper contains piperine; a study by Heerasing Takooree et al. highlighted its anti-inflammatory, analgesic, anticonvulsant, and neuroprotective effects. Coconut oil is noted for its antibacterial, antifungal, antiviral properties, and anti-inflammatory roles in Ayurvedic medicine. However, the article emphasizes that while these ingredients have documented anti-inflammatory properties, there is no scientific evidence that topical application can cure arthritis — a chronic condition that requires medical treatment and cannot be reversed or eliminated by home remedies.

title: Fact Check: Can massaging with olive oil make breast firmer, toned and bigger?
claim_text: Massaging your breasts with olive oil will help you increase blood flow in your bust and help the lymph to do their job. With olive oil breast massage, you will get firmer, toned, and bigger breasts. Your skin will be soft, moisturized, and more elastic.
quick_take: Oil massage may have some benefits, such as improving skin texture and blood circulation, which can help nourish the skin and make the breasts look firmer; however, it does not significantly change the size or structural integrity of the breasts. Breast sagging cannot be reversed naturally.
doctor_explanation:
Breast sagging, medically known as breast ptosis, is a natural change that occurs as part of the ageing process in which the breasts lose their elasticity and suppleness, leading to a downward shift. Breast ptosis occurs when the skin and tissues that support the breast stretch and become less effective — either because the breast tissue becomes heavier or because of significant weight loss, leading to excess skin. Multiple factors can cause saggy breasts: larger breast size, ageing, decreased skin elasticity, collagen deficiency, wrong posture, higher BMI, and multiple pregnancies. Gaining and losing sudden weight can stretch the skin and tissues, resulting in stretch marks and sagginess. During pregnancy, breasts grow larger due to hormonal changes; after pregnancy, the enlarged breast might shrink but may not return to its original state due to stretching of skin and ligaments.

Dr Preethika Shetty, Consultant Obstetrician & Gynaecologist, Motherhood Hospitals, Kharadi, explained: 'Breast sagging or ptosis is a common concern in various women. As women get older, they start to lose the natural shape of their breasts, making them look saggy. The female breasts are made up of various fat and ligaments but lack muscle tissue, which is responsible for providing posture and stability, making breasts look saggy and deflated. One of the major mistakes that can cause breast sagging is not choosing the right type of bra; most of the time, women are highly unaware of their bra size. A well-fitted bra supports your breast and improves their posture, giving them a slight lift.'

Regarding olive oil specifically: the chief active elements of olive oil include oleic acid (a monounsaturated fatty acid), phenolics, and squalene. The major phenolics include hydroxytyrosol, tyrosyls, and oleuropein, which have antioxidant, antibacterial, anti-fungal, and anti-inflammatory properties that moisten breast skin, treat breast infection, and enhance wound healing. Some studies have shown the effectiveness of olive oil breast massage in breast engorgement and swelling. A study by Ghattas et al. mentioned that olive oil breast massage considerably lowers the signs and symptoms of breast engorgement (redness, discomfort, oedema, and pyrexia) and assists in good latch-on or effective breastfeeding. Another study by Chaudhary et al. reported that the application of olive oil massage is found effective in reducing breast engorgement and breast pain among postnatal mothers with Lower segment Cesarean section (LSCS). Despite these benefits for breast engorgement, no scientific evidence or consensus in the medical fraternity supports the claim that olive oil massage can make breasts firmer, toned, and bigger.

Dr Rajashri Tayshete Bhasale, Consultant Gynaecologist & Obstetrician, Laparoscopic Surgeon, Wockhardt Hospitals, clarified: 'Breast sagging cannot be reversed naturally. There is no scientific evidence to back up the idea that massaging oil can make your breasts look bigger. Breast size depends on genetics, body weight, and hormones. Massaging the breasts is highly rewarding and improves blood circulation, which can help nourish the skin, making the breasts look firmer. It is essential to understand that massaging your breast is not a one-time process; it requires consistency and a fixed routine for better results. A gentle 10 to 15-minute breast massage can help improve skin elasticity and reduce stretch marks. Choose the right type of oil for optimal results, natural oils such as coconut oil, almond oil, and jojoba oil. These oils are naturally moisturizing and hydrating. Individuals are advised to slightly warm the oil before applying it to the breast for better absorption. After applying the oil, gently massage your breast in a circular motion for at least 15 to 20 minutes. Most benefits of massaging breasts are related to improving skin and muscle health rather than drastic physical changes. Massaging the breasts during breastfeeding helps avoid milk lumps or abscesses. It is advised to massage and empty the breasts after every feed. Massage should include the breasts and the axilla, as breast tissue (breast tail) extends into the axilla. Self-breast examination is important and should be taught to all women for early detection of breast cancer.'

title: Fact Check: Can meditation prevent cancer? - THIP Media
claim_text: Meditation can prevent cancer
quick_take: A social media post claims that meditation prevents cancer. We fact-checked and found the claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: Cancer is a disease caused by uncontrolled cell growth that damages the normal functioning of the affected body part and spreads to other regions. Reducing the risk of cancer involves adopting a health-conscious lifestyle including maintaining a balanced diet, staying physically active to manage weight, abstaining from tobacco while limiting alcohol consumption, protecting the skin from sun exposure, receiving vaccinations for viruses like HPV and HBV, regular cancer screenings, minimizing exposure to environmental carcinogens, incorporating stress management techniques, and prioritizing adequate sleep. While proactive measures can reduce cancer risk, genetic factors can still play a significant role in predisposing individuals to the disease. There is no evidence that meditation can treat or cure cancer or any other disease. Meditation and mindfulness practices have been associated with various health benefits including stress reduction and improved overall well-being. However, there is currently insufficient scientific evidence to suggest that meditation alone can prevent cancer. However, meditation can be a valuable component of a holistic approach to health and may contribute indirectly to cancer prevention by helping individuals manage stress, maintain a healthy lifestyle, and support their overall physical and mental health. Research shows that stress reduction techniques such as meditation may play a role in supporting the immune system and reducing inflammation, which could potentially have positive effects on overall health and potentially influence cancer risk. Cancerresearchuk.org informs that people with cancer use meditation to feel better, and that meditation can reduce anxiety and stress, relieve pain, difficulty sleeping, tiredness, feeling sick, and high blood pressure. Cancer.gov shows that stress is indirectly related to cancer - people under chronic stress may develop certain unhealthy behaviors such as smoking, overeating, becoming less active, or drinking alcohol, that themselves are associated with increased risks of some cancers. However, cancer is a complex disease influenced by a combination of factors including genetics, lifestyle choices, environmental exposures, and chance. Dr Sarthak Moharir, a Radiation Oncologist informs, 'There is no evidence to prove meditation directly prevents cancer. Meditation might help some people in reduction of stress'. While meditation can be a valuable tool for promoting well-being and managing stress, it should not be viewed as a substitute for other evidence-based cancer prevention strategies such as maintaining a healthy diet, regular exercise, avoiding tobacco, and participating in cancer screenings.
