Oats, on the other hand, are rich in soluble fibre, which absorbs water and adds bulk to the stool, making it easier to pass.

However, simply eating these foods without addressing other factors such as hydration, regular physical activity, and a balanced diet won't resolve constipation in three days. Effective relief depends on the root cause of the problem.

Yes, they can help relieve constipation over time, but not instantly. Papaya is high in water content and contains a good amount of fibre, which can stimulate bowel movements. Similarly, bananas are known for their high levels of resistant starch and pectin, both of which contribute to stool softening. Oats are rich in beta-glucan, a soluble fibre that absorbs water and helps to form bulky stools, which can be easier to pass.

However, their effects take time. If you're experiencing occasional constipation, including these foods in your diet can promote more regular bowel movements. Yet, expecting dramatic results in just three days is unlikely. Improving bowel health is often a gradual process and involves more than just one dietary change.

Yes, but the amount of fibre from these foods alone may not be sufficient for quick relief. These three foods are high in fibre, but fibre alone isn't always the full solution to constipation. A healthy digestive system requires both soluble and insoluble fibres. While papaya, banana, and oats provide good sources of soluble fibre, insoluble fibre—found in whole grains, nuts, seeds, and vegetables—also plays a key role in improving bowel movements. Insoluble fibre adds bulk to the stool, helping to speed up its passage through the intestines.

While the combination of papaya, banana, and oats can contribute to your daily fibre intake, relying solely on them for quick relief may not be enough. A balanced diet with a variety of fibre-rich foods is essential for maintaining regular bowel movements.

Yes, proper hydration is essential for easing constipation. Water plays a critical role in preventing and relieving constipation. Fibre needs water to move through the digestive system properly. Without adequate hydration, the body can absorb too much water from the stool, causing it to become hard and difficult to pass.

Dietician Kamna Chauhan explains, "Hydration is just as crucial as fibre when dealing with constipation. Without enough water, fibre can't do its job properly, which is why drinking water alongside high-fibre foods like papaya and banana is the key."

title: Fact Check: Can papaya eliminate intestinal parasites?
claim_text: Papaya fruit kills parasites because it contains high concentrations of papain, an enzyme that naturally eliminates intestinal parasites. Papain reduces gas and bloating and promotes healthy digestion.
verdict_original: The claim made by user on Instagram is MISLEADING. Hence, the claim that papaya can eliminate intestinal parasites is MISLEADING.
quick_take: Papaya's papain enzyme may aid digestion, and there is limited evidence suggesting papaya seeds may help treat intestinal parasites in some circumstances. However, there is no strong scientific evidence or medical consensus supporting the claim that papaya can eliminate intestinal parasites completely.
doctor_explanation: Intestinal parasitic infections are caused by helminths and protozoan parasites and are among the most widespread infections affecting humans, particularly in developing countries with inadequate water, sanitation, and hygiene. Helminths (parasitic worms) include nematodes (roundworms), cestodes (tapeworms), and trematodes (flatworms). The four major helminth species — Ascaris lumbricoides (roundworm), Trichuris trichiura (whipworm), Ancylostoma duodenale, and Necator americanus (hookworms) — infect over a billion people worldwide. Protozoan parasites such as Giardia intestinalis, Entamoeba histolytica, Cryptosporidium spp., and Cyclospora cayetanensis can multiply within the host and cause diseases like giardiasis, amoebiasis, cryptosporidiosis, and cyclosporiasis. While papaya (Carica papaya L.) does contain bioactive compounds including papain, carpaines, benzyl isothiocyanate (BITC), latex, zeaxanthin, and choline, and is rich in vitamins A, B, C, E, K, folate, magnesium, copper, calcium, and potassium, no strong scientific evidence or medical consensus supports its use as a primary treatment for eliminating intestinal parasites. A randomized controlled trial by John A. O. Okeniyi et al. (PubMed) found papaya seeds may be effective in treating human intestinal parasites without notable side effects. A study by Claus Muss et al. demonstrated papaya helps maintain digestive tract health by alleviating functional disorders like IBS symptoms. A review in the Arabian Journal of Chemistry noted papain enzyme has been used in traditional medicine for indigestion. An article in Nutrients journal highlighted papain's role in enhancing intestinal motility and reducing transit time. title: Fact Check: Can paracetamol damage organs or cause piles? - THIP
claim_text: Paracetamol is the most harmful medicine, causing damage to the kidney, liver, and even piles.

doctor_explanation: Paracetamol, also called acetaminophen, is a widely available over-the-counter medicine used to alleviate pain and lower fever. Classified as an analgesic and antipyretic, it differs from non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) by having minimal impact on inflammation. Its mechanism involves inhibiting specific brain enzymes related to pain perception and body temperature regulation. According to Dr Kashyap Dakshini, General Physician in Mumbai, 'Paracetamol is considered the safest antipyretic for treating fever. While other drugs like ibuprofen and NSAIDs also possess antipyretic effects, caution is advised due to potential adverse effects on organs such as the stomach, liver, and kidneys when used excessively or for extended periods. NSAIDs are not recommended for patients with kidney disease, gastric ulcers, heart failure, or liver disease.' Paracetamol is not inherently the most harmful drug, but like any medication, it carries potential risks and side effects, particularly when used improperly. It is generally safe for regular use over many years, as long as the recommended dose is not exceeded. Problems with the liver and kidneys are associated with medication overdose. Regarding piles (haemorrhoids), Dr Shalin Nagori, Consultant Pathologist and Industrial Physician, stated, 'There is no established evidence suggesting that paracetamol (acetaminophen) causes piles (haemorrhoids). Paracetamol is generally considered safe if taken in advisable dosages and commonly used as a pain reliever. Any medicine if taken excessively can give major side effects to your body. Haemorrhoids are often caused by factors such as straining during bowel movements, obesity, and a lack of dietary fibre.' A 2018 study indicates that regular use of paracetamol at doses exceeding 2-3 grams per day may increase the risk of gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding. This risk appears to be dose-dependent and can be exacerbated when paracetamol is combined with NSAIDs. Paracetamol is generally safe even for pregnant ladies when used correctly, but it can be dangerous in certain situations. Taking too much can harm the liver, especially if one already has liver issues or drinks alcohol. It can also cause problems when mixed with certain medicines or if allergic.

title: Can Parsley Tea reduce swelling and boost blood circulation? - THIP
claim_text: Drink this tea and you will never have swollen legs, ankles or feet again! (claiming that drinking parsley tea can help reduce swelling in the body and improve circulation)
quick_take: A social media post claims that Parsley tea is an effective natural remedy for reducing swelling and improving blood flow. We fact checked and found the claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation:
Does Parsley Tea reduce swelling? Maybe, but there's no solid proof that parsley tea can reduce swelling in any meaningful way. Swelling, or oedema as doctors call it, happens when fluid builds up in your tissues (think puffy ankles after a long day on your feet). Parsley has been praised as a diuretic, meaning it might make you pee more, which could theoretically flush out excess water. A 2002 study on rats showed that parsley extract increased urine output, hinting at this effect. Plus, swelling can stem from serious issues like heart or kidney problems and conditions tea can't fix. So, while parsley might give your bladder a nudge, it's not a cure for puffy legs. Dr Shalin Nagori, Consultant Pathologist and Industrial Physician, stated, 'Parsley can help reduce swelling to some extent, but if the swelling is caused by kidney disease or another chronic condition, it could be risky. If the swelling is due to wound inflammation, one may try this remedy, but it should not be relied upon for chronic issues like kidney problems.'

Can Parsley Tea improve blood circulation? No, there's no convincing evidence that parsley tea boosts circulation either. Good circulation means blood flows smoothly through your veins and arteries, delivering oxygen where it's needed. The idea here is that parsley contains nutrients like vitamin C and antioxidants, which might support healthy blood vessels. True, vitamin C helps maintain vessel strength, and parsley has a decent amount (about 133mg per 100g of fresh leaves, according to nutritional data). Studies, like one from 2021 on antioxidants, show they can benefit heart health broadly, but there's nothing specific linking parsley tea to better blood flow. It is vague to say a cup will get your blood pumping more efficiently.

Is there any real benefit to drinking parsley tea? Manasi Banduni, Senior Nutritionist at Clinic Living Plus, Bangalore said: 'Yes, but it's modest and not what the claim promises. Parsley tea isn't useless—it's hydrating, low-calorie, and might offer a sprinkle of vitamins if you sip it fresh. It's got a bit of folate and vitamin K, which help with cell repair and blood clotting. But these perks are tiny compared to eating parsley raw in a salad. The problem is, boiling it into tea dilutes most of its goodness, and no study backs up the big claims about swelling or circulation. It's more of a comforting ritual than a health hack.'

Could Parsley Tea cause any harm? Yes, it can, if you overdo it. Parsley's generally safe in small amounts, but chugging litres of the tea isn't smart. It contains compounds called oxalates, which in large doses might increase the risk of kidney stones, ironically for something meant to reduce swelling! Also, if you're on water pills or blood thinners, parsley's diuretic vibe or vitamin K could mess with your meds. A case report once flagged parsley overdoses causing skin rashes in rare instances. So, moderation's key—don't treat it like a magic potion.

Conclusion: In the end, parsley tea's a nice idea, but it's no fix for swelling or sluggish circulation. Science says it's more folklore than fact. If you're dealing with puffiness or poor blood flow, skip the teapot and chat with a doctor. Supposing that swelling is caused by any wound then you can even start anti-inflammatory diet. If the swelling are persistent, consult a doctor—they'll point you to real solutions like elevating your legs or checking your heart health rather than leaving you steeping in false hope.

title: Can Patharchatta plant dissolve kidney stones in 2 days? - THIP
claim_text: Drinking patharchatta juice or using its extract can dissolve kidney stones in just two days
quick_take: A social media post claims that patharchatta (Bryophyllum pinnatum) can dissolve kidney stones in two days. We fact checked and found the claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: No, the claim is not supported by any reliable scientific evidence. The idea that patharchatta plant is beneficial for stone and can break it in just 72 hours has spread across social media and home remedy forums. But no clinical research confirms this. Kidney stones are solid crystals that form inside your kidneys. They don't dissolve easily or quickly, especially not with one herbal remedy. The speed at which a kidney stone passes or breaks down depends on many factors: the size and type of the stone, your body's hydration levels, urine output, and whether you've had stones before. For example, small stones under 5 mm may pass naturally within days or weeks, but larger stones often require medical help. Even if someone felt relief after taking patharchatta for two days, there's no way to prove the herb alone caused it. The timing might just be a coincidence. Dr Ubaid ur Rehman, General Physician at Holy Mission Clinic in New Delhi, explains, 'There is no scientific proof that patharchatta plant benefits or dissolve kidney stones within two days. Although certain compounds in the plant may support kidney function, breaking down or passing stones typically needs more than just herbal remedies.' Dr Ganesh Srinivasa Prasad P, Consultant Nephrologist at Narayana Health City, Bengaluru, says that no home remedy can promise to prevent or cure all kinds of kidney stones. 'The best way to lower your risk is by drinking plenty of water, cutting down on salt, keeping a healthy weight, eating calcium-rich foods, and avoiding foods high in oxalates. People prone to uric acid stones should also reduce their intake of red meat, sugar, refined carbohydrates, alcohol, and quit smoking,' he advised. Aayushi Agarwal, Certified Dietician & Diabetes Educators said 'Patharchatta (Bryophyllum pinnatum) is valued in Ayurveda for kidney stone relief due to its diuretic and anti-inflammatory properties. While some anecdotal reports highlight benefits, no clinical evidence supports complete stone dissolution in three days. Effectiveness depends on various factors, and unsupervised use may delay medical care, increasing risks of obstruction, infection, or kidney damage.' Some lab studies show promise, but there's no solid proof it works in humans. Researchers have studied patharchatta for its diuretic, anti-inflammatory, and lithotriptic (stone-breaking) effects. Some studies using animal models and lab tests have shown that the plant may help reduce the formation of calcium oxalate crystals, which are the most common type of kidney stones. For example, a lab study published in the Journal of Ethnopharmacology found that extracts from the plant may help prevent the growth of kidney stones in rats. That sounds hopeful, but here's the catch: these studies were done in test tubes or animals, not in real people. And none of them say anything about working in just two days. Doctors rely on human trials to recommend treatments. And so far, no human studies have confirmed that patharchatta can dissolve stones, quickly or otherwise. Until then, it remains a folk remedy, not a proven cure. If you're already on medication for kidney health, blood pressure, or diabetes, combining it with herbs like patharchatta could lead to side effects. Always check with a doctor before using it, especially if you have an existing health condition. Warning signs that you need professional treatment include severe pain, blood in urine, fever, or vomiting. These could be signs that the stone is too large or stuck, or that an infection has developed. Waiting too long while depending only on herbs can lead to kidney damage or even hospitalization. Doctors may prescribe painkillers, hydration therapy, or medications that help stones pass. In more serious cases, procedures like shock wave therapy or surgery might be needed. And none of these should be replaced by herbal remedies alone.

title: Can PCOS or PCOD be cured at home with fenugreek seeds?
claim_text: PCOD and PCOS can be treated at home using fenugreek seeds and honey (claiming a cure for PCOD and PCOS naturally)
quick_take: A social media post claims that consuming fenugreek seeds can cure PCOS or PCOD at home. We fact checked and found the claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation:
PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome) and PCOD (Polycystic Ovarian Disease) are often confused but different. PCOS is a hormonal disorder involving irregular periods, high male hormone levels, and sometimes ovarian cysts, often linked to insulin resistance. PCOD is a condition where ovaries produce many immature eggs leading to cysts and irregular cycles, but may not involve the same hormonal imbalances. PCOS is a broader syndrome while PCOD is less consistently defined and often considered a subset or milder form. Both require medical management, not home cures.

Dr Saumya (Obstetrics and Gynaecology) at ESIC Medical College & Hospital, Patna said: Neither PCOS nor PCOD can be cured. They're chronic conditions driven by hormonal and genetic factors, as noted in the Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism (2020). Symptoms like irregular periods, weight gain, or excessive hair growth can be managed, but the conditions persist lifelong. With the right treatment—medication, diet, or lifestyle changes—many women control symptoms effectively, but fenugreek or any home remedy won't eliminate the root issue.

Natural steps like eating a balanced diet and exercising regularly can help manage symptoms at home. The NHS suggests losing 5-10% of body weight to improve menstrual regularity and insulin resistance. Foods like whole grains, vegetables, and lean proteins support blood sugar control. However, home remedies, including fenugreek, aren't enough alone. A 2021 study in Complementary Therapies in Medicine found supplements like inositol may help ovulation, but these require medical oversight.

Dr Swati Dave (PhD in Food and Nutrition) confirms that including fenugreek seeds in the diet can be beneficial, but most studies on fenugreek are dose-dependent so definitive conclusions can't always be made. When it comes to PCOD and PCOS, these conditions cannot be cured, only managed. While natural home-based management is possible, it's essential to consult a doctor initially to accurately understand the condition.

Soumam Dutta (PhD Scholar in Nutrition, Department of Endocrinology, ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition) said: No, fenugreek cannot cure either condition. A 2015 study in the International Journal of Medical Sciences showed a fenugreek extract (Furocyst) reduced ovarian cysts and improved periods in some women after 90 days. However, this used a specific extract, not raw seeds, and didn't prove a cure. PCOS and PCOD are too complex for a single remedy, and symptoms often return without ongoing care. Fenugreek may offer minor support, but it's no fix.

Fenugreek's fibre and compounds like furostanolic saponins may improve insulin sensitivity, helping with weight or period issues. A 2024 study in the Journal of Reproduction & Infertility found fenugreek improved menstrual cycles and reduced cysts in some women, but it used controlled extracts, not home-soaked seeds. Results vary, and raw seeds may have weaker effects. It's a small help, not a cure, and should be paired with medical advice.

Risks: Fenugreek is safe in food amounts, but high doses can cause stomach upset or allergies. It may interact with medications like blood thinners or affect blood sugar, risky for diabetics. A 2018 BMJ Case Reports study linked fenugreek to serotonin syndrome with antidepressants.

Best way to manage PCOS or PCOD: Consult a doctor (GP, endocrinologist, or gynecologist) to develop a tailored plan involving lifestyle changes and treatments. A dietitian can assist with weight management, balanced diet, and exercise. Some may require medications to regulate periods or insulin levels. While home remedies like fenugreek may offer support, they should not substitute professional medical care.

Certain treatment modalities that may help to reduce the fine lines include medications such as retinoids, dermabrasion, botox, fillers, etc. Lastly, it may help in unclogging and purifying your pores, making them visibly smaller, but the pore size is mostly a result of your genetics, and it is not possible to shrink them permanently. In conclusion, the peel-off mask, such as the black mask, penetrates deep into your pores and gently removes the dead cells in the outermost layer of your skin, along with any impurities sitting over it, making the skin cleaner by removing the dirt, bacteria, and debris. However, it must be noted that the process of peeling off the mask is not safe as it strips away the surface layer of the skin. Other vital factors include diseases such as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), pollution, smoking, and stress. Some medications can cause acne too (especially steroids and lithium), and greasy cosmetics such as hair products, makeup, and other products we put on our skin can also contribute to clogged pores, thus leading to acne. On wrinkles: Wrinkles are creases, folds, or ridges in the skin which appear naturally as people get older. As a person gets old, the skin becomes thinner and less elastic over time. However, certain other factors such as sun exposure, smoking, dehydration, some medications and environmental and genetic factors also play a vital role. Side effects of peel-off masks: Peel-off masks, such as charcoal masks, can harm the skin in various ways. It can even cause contact dermatitis from the chemicals and ingredients in them. Excessive use can make your skin lose its elasticity, ultimately leading to sagging skin. Also, it shall not be used by people with sensitive skin as it can make the skin even more sensitive, making it prone to redness, breakouts, dry patches or overall dull skin. Also, suppose a person is having a predisposing skin condition such as eczema, rosacea, or acne. In that case, it makes him/her more likely to experience an adverse reaction to peel-off masks. title: Can peepal and neem juice cure kidney failure in 3 months?
claim_text: An Instagram video claims that if a patient is dealing with total kidney failure, he or she can be cured just by drinking peepal and neem juice for three months.
quick_take: A social media video claims that drinking peepal and neem juice can completely cure kidney failure within just three months. We fact checked and found the claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: Dr Sudeep Singh Sachdev, Senior Consultant & Director – Nephrology, Narayana Hospital, Gurugram said "Everything depends upon the stages. Kidney diseases are often silent and gradually worsening, it can severely damage the kidneys and lead to a host of troublesome symptoms and complications. The positive news is that kidney disease is largely preventable, and in its early stages, it can even be reversed. But kidney failure cannot be reversed with herbal juices like peepal or neem." Chronic kidney failure is a serious medical condition where the kidneys lose their ability to filter waste from the blood. By the time a person is diagnosed with kidney failure, the damage is often permanent. Modern medicine can manage the condition with dialysis, medications, and sometimes kidney transplants, but there is no herbal shortcut to reverse the damage. While some herbs may support general kidney health in early stages or help with inflammation, they cannot "cure" failure. Peepal and neem both have traditional uses in Ayurveda. Neem is known for its antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties. Peepal has been used for respiratory and digestive issues. But no clinical study or medical guideline supports their use in curing kidney failure. Relying on herbal juices instead of medical treatment can delay proper care and worsen the disease. Dr Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition, explains, "Food can certainly help support how our organs function, but it can't reverse an existing disease. I get concerned when people think that simply eating something like fermented millet will heal damaged organs — the body doesn't work that way." Harita Adhvaryu, Senior Clinical Dietitian at Ezcure DiabetesCare in Ahmedabad, says, "I often remind my clients that good health comes from the overall diet, not just one food. For example, millets are beneficial, but they can't replace proper medical care or a well-rounded lifestyle." There is no solid scientific evidence that either plant can regenerate damaged kidney tissue. Research on peepal and neem is limited, especially when it comes to their effect on kidneys. More importantly, these herbs haven't gone through the strict human trials that are needed to prove they work safely and effectively. Drinking them in large quantities can also be risky, as high doses of neem have been linked to liver and kidney toxicity in some cases. One of the most dangerous outcomes of such claims is that people may stop taking prescribed medication, skip dialysis, or delay seeing a nephrologist. Kidney failure is not a condition that can wait. If the body can't remove toxins properly, it can lead to dangerous levels of fluid, waste, and electrolytes. Left untreated, it can result in coma or even death. Herbal remedies might seem like a gentle, natural solution, but in serious conditions like kidney failure, they're simply not enough. They can even interact with prescribed medications and cause harmful side effects. They might be safe in very small quantities, but they're not a replacement for treatment. Some people drink neem or peepal juice as part of general wellness practices. In tiny, occasional doses, they might not cause harm for healthy individuals. However, for someone with kidney issues, especially advanced disease, even "natural" remedies can be risky. For example, some herbs can increase potassium levels, a dangerous thing for people with kidney failure.

title: Can peepal leaf tea prevent the recurrence of a heart attack? - THIP
claim_text: peepal tea removes 99% of the blockage and prevent recurrence of heat attack
quick_take: A social media post claims that drinking peepal tea can prevent a heart attack from happening again. We fact checked and found the claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: There is no food, herb, or drink that can guarantee a heart attack will never recur. A heart attack is not a one-time plumbing problem that gets "fixed" and forgotten. It is the result of long-term damage to the blood vessels supplying the heart. After one heart attack, the arteries remain vulnerable. Cholesterol plaques can rupture again, blood clots can form again, and the heart muscle itself may already be weakened. Even with the best medicines and lifestyle changes, doctors talk about risk reduction, not certainty. So when a remedy promises a "guarantee," it crosses from hope into misinformation. Dr Divya Chauhan, Pratha Ayurveda as Senior Ayurveda Researcher, clarified that, "There are no human clinical studies showing that peepal leaf tea reduces the risk of a second heart attack." Some laboratory and animal studies have explored peepal leaves for antioxidant or anti-inflammatory properties. These findings are often misunderstood or exaggerated online. Antioxidant activity in a test tube does not mean a substance can protect human coronary arteries, prevent clot formation, or stabilise plaques inside blood vessels. For a claim like "prevents heart attack recurrence" to be valid, it must be tested in heart patients over years. Peepal leaf tea has not undergone such trials. Without this level of evidence, the claim remains unsupported. Dr Almas Fatma, a general physician based in Navi Mumbai, stresses that everyday lifestyle decisions play a crucial role in preventing heart attacks. She highlights the importance of a well-balanced diet, regular physical activity, and avoiding smoking as key preventive measures. Routine health check-ups are also essential to keep conditions such as high blood pressure, diabetes, and raised cholesterol under control. She adds that managing stress and cutting back on alcohol, even in small ways, can have a significant impact, and that focusing on prevention rather than treatment is the best way to protect long-term heart health. Peepal leaf tea cannot remove arterial plaque or repair heart muscle damage. Blocked arteries develop through a slow, complex process involving cholesterol deposition, inflammation, calcium buildup, and scarring of vessel walls. Once plaque is formed, it does not simply melt away with herbal drinks. Even aggressive dietary changes cannot fully reverse established plaque, this is why medicines like statins are prescribed long-term. Similarly, heart muscle damaged during a heart attack does not regenerate through teas or herbs. Recovery depends on medical care, rehabilitation, and careful long-term management. Dr Naresh Kumar Monigari, Director of the Cath Lab and Consultant Interventional Cardiologist at Renova Century Hospitals, Banjara Hills, Hyderabad, emphasises that people with a family history of coronary artery disease (CAD) should have regular heart evaluations. He notes that detecting hidden cardiac problems early can help prevent major complications. He also advises protecting heart health by staying away from tobacco, keeping a healthy body weight, controlling blood pressure, and practising effective stress-management techniques. Replacing prescribed heart medicines with peepal leaf tea is unsafe and medically unsound. After a heart attack, patients are commonly prescribed blood thinners, cholesterol-lowering drugs, blood pressure medicines, and sometimes medicines to control heart rhythm. These treatments are backed by decades of large-scale studies showing reduced deaths and fewer repeat heart attacks. Herbal teas, including peepal leaf tea, have not been tested to show similar benefits. Worse, some herbal products may interact with heart medicines, either increasing bleeding risk or reducing drug effectiveness. Stopping medicines because a "natural cure" seems safer can significantly increase the risk of another, possibly fatal, heart attack. Peepal leaf tea may be consumed occasionally as a traditional beverage, but it should not be presented as heart-protective therapy. "Natural" does not automatically mean harmless. Herbal preparations vary widely in strength and purity, and their effects are not always predictable. For people taking blood thinners or multiple heart medicines, even mild interactions can matter. Any regular use should be discussed with a healthcare professional, especially in those with established heart disease. Peepal leaf tea or any other leaf tea does not prevent the recurrence of a heart attack, does not unclog arteries, and does not replace evidence-based treatment.

title: Fact Check: Can peepal leaves cure heart blockages? - THIP Media
claim_text: A Facebook post claims peepal leaves strengthen the cardiovascular system and cure heart blockages.
quick_take: A social media post claims that eating peepal leaves cures heart blockages. We fact-checked and found the claim to be Mostly False. The available evidence shows that peepal leaves may prevent heart blockages but they cannot cure existing blockages.
doctor_explanation: Heart blockage, or coronary artery disease (CAD), results from the gradual buildup of plaque (composed of cholesterol, fat, and other substances) on the inner walls of coronary arteries. Contributing factors include atherosclerosis, risk factors like high blood pressure and cholesterol, smoking, diabetes, family history, inflammation, and blood clots. Unhealthy lifestyle choices also play a role. Managing these factors through a healthy lifestyle and medical intervention is crucial for preventing or slowing the progression of heart blockage. Heart blockages are treated through a combination of lifestyle changes, medications, and medical procedures. Lifestyle modifications include a heart-healthy diet, regular exercise, and smoking cessation. Medications like statins, antiplatelet drugs, and blood pressure medications may be necessary. Medical procedures include angioplasty with stent placement, coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), atherectomy, and thrombolytic therapy. Diet alone cannot fully treat heart blockages. However, adopting a heart-healthy diet is crucial for managing and preventing the further progression of coronary artery disease (CAD). Dr Amit Bhushan Sharma, Associate Director and Unit Head of Cardiology at Paras Hospitals, Gurugram, informs that "When plaques build up inside a person's arteries, they can become clogged, leading to restricted blood flow. While individual foods cannot remove plaque from the arteries, a healthy diet can help manage and prevent heart disease". There is no scientific evidence to support the claim that eating peepal leaves can cure heart blockages. However, scant evidence shows that have specifically investigated the effects of peepal leaves on heart blockages. A study shows that an extract of peepal leaves was able to reduce cholesterol levels in rats. Another study shows that peepal can counter the atherothrombotic effect. Atherothrombotic diseases typically involve the formation of blood clots in arteries with underlying atherosclerosis. However, this evidence is not enough to confirm that eating peepal leaves cures heart blockages. Also, even if peepal leaves are good against heart blockages, we have no information on their dosage. As per the available evidence, peepal leaves have been used in traditional Indian medicine for centuries to treat a variety of ailments. The leaves contain compounds that have antioxidant and anti-inflammatory, antibacterial activity, anthelmintic activity, immunomodulatory activity, wound-healing activity, anticonvulsant activity, hypolipidemic activity, and hypoglycemic properties. So eating peepal leaves may be beneficial for heart health. Dr Debasish Mohapatra, Associate Consultant at BM Birla Heart Research Centre, Kolkata informs, "Ficus religiosa (peepal tree) is a rich source of nutrients as well as phytochemicals. Richness in vital components make it a wholesome tree with several medicinal and health properties. There is no current scientific evidence to support the claim that peepal leaves cure heart blockage. While traditional medicine systems may advocate the use of various herbs and plants for health purposes, it is crucial to rely on scientifically proven treatments for serious medical conditions like heart blockage. Consulting a qualified healthcare professional for proper diagnosis and treatment options is recommended". The current treatment for heart blockages involves lifestyle changes such as a heart-healthy diet, exercise, and smoking cessation, along with medications like antiplatelet agents, statins, beta-blockers, and calcium channel blockers to manage risk factors and symptoms. Invasive procedures like angioplasty with stent placement or coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery may be necessary to address severe blockages. As per our research, traditional medicine is not always based on scientific evidence. Moreover, the benefits of peepal leaves for heart health are unclear. We need more research/trials to determine whether peepal leaves can actually cure heart blockages. Relying solely on quick fixes and not seeking proper treatment can worsen heart blockages which can induce heart attack or even stroke. Dr Sharma adds, "Brain strokes, heart strokes, angina, and peripheral artery disease can be caused by blocked arteries. When a particle of plaque breaks off and becomes lodged in the bloodstream, blood flow is reduced, which can result to a heart attack or stroke."

title: Can periwinkle leaves manage diabetes, and high blood pressure?
claim_text: Periwinkle (Sada Bahar) is a natural remedy that can help regulate blood sugar, manage weight, skin diseases, cough and support healthy blood pressure.
quick_take: A social media post claims that periwinkle leaves can manage diabetes and high blood pressure. Our fact check concludes this claim is mostly false.
doctor_explanation:
## Can periwinkle effectively manage diabetes?
Not really. Some studies have explored the potential anti-diabetic properties of compounds from the Vinca rosea plant, but there's no strong evidence to support the idea that this plant can effectively manage diabetes. A 2010 study on rats did show that Periwinkle extracts helped lower blood sugar and improve pancreatic function, particularly at higher doses. However, these results have not been confirmed in humans, and we need more research to determine its safety and effectiveness. Diabetes is a complex condition that requires comprehensive management, including medication, dietary changes, and regular monitoring by a healthcare professional. Relying on Periwinkle leaves alone could cause dangerous fluctuations in blood sugar and lead to serious complications. It's important to follow a doctor's prescribed treatment plan for diabetes care.

## Can regularly consuming periwinkle as tea or by chewing fresh leaves support healthy blood pressure?
No, this claim is misleading. While some studies have examined certain compounds in periwinkle for their potential effect on blood pressure, there is not enough scientific evidence to support the idea that chewing the leaves or drinking periwinkle tea can reliably manage hypertension. Research has focused on specific, standardised extracts used in controlled doses—not on raw plant parts taken without guidance. High blood pressure is a serious condition that requires lifestyle changes and prescribed medication. Relying on periwinkle leaves alone, without medical advice, may delay proper treatment and put one at risk of complications.

Dr Ubaid ur Rahman, General Physician at Holy Mission Clinic in New Delhi, states, "Even though compounds from the periwinkle plant have been studied for their possible effects on blood pressure, there's no reliable evidence that chewing its leaves or drinking it as tea can safely manage or lower blood pressure. In fact, parts of the plant can be toxic if consumed incorrectly. High blood pressure needs careful and personalised treatment. Plus, relying on home remedies like periwinkle without medical supervision could be dangerous and delay essential care."

## Can periwinkle flowers provide benefits for skin diseases, weight loss and cough problems?
Maybe. Periwinkle flowers contain compounds such as alkaloids, which have been shown to possess antibacterial and antifungal properties in some studies. This suggests they might have a role in treating certain skin infections or conditions caused by bacteria or fungi. However, there is no robust clinical evidence supporting their use for common skin diseases like acne, eczema, or psoriasis. As for weight loss, there is no scientific proof that Periwinkle flowers directly help in reducing body weight. Healthy diet and exercise are still the most effective methods for weight loss. When it comes to coughing, some traditional practices use Periwinkle to relieve mild cough symptoms, possibly due to its mild antitussive (cough-suppressing) properties. However, clinical evidence on its effectiveness is lacking. Other herbs like thyme and licorice have more established benefits for cough relief.

## What are the side effects of consuming Periwinkle leaves or flowers?
While Periwinkle contains important compounds like vincristine and vinblastine, which are used in cancer treatments, it also has significant toxicity for humans. These compounds can be harmful when consumed in large amounts or over long periods. Consuming Periwinkle leaves or flowers can cause side effects such as nausea, vomiting, low blood pressure, dizziness, and even more severe effects like respiratory failure or organ damage in extreme cases. The plant contains alkaloids that, when consumed improperly, can interfere with normal cell function, potentially leading to serious health issues. Therefore, it is unsafe to consume Periwinkle leaves or flowers without professional guidance, and it should never be used as a self-treatment.

Dr Almas Fatma, Diploma in Family Medicine, PG in Digital Health, General Physician from Navi Mumbai, says, "Periwinkle leaves and flowers may seem like a natural remedy, but they can be harmful when consumed. While the plant contains compounds that have shown medicinal properties, they can also cause serious side effects. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and low blood pressure. In more severe cases, consuming Periwinkle can lead to respiratory failure, organ damage, and neurological issues, such as confusion or even seizures. The plant's toxicity, especially when taken in large amounts, makes it unsafe for self-treatment. It's important to consult a healthcare professional before considering any part of the Periwinkle plant for medicinal purposes, as its use can be risky without proper medical supervision."

title: Fact Check: Can Pfizer COVID vaccine cause genital herpes?
claim_text: You can get genital herpes through the Pfizer COVID shot.
quick_take: As per a social media post, Pfizer COVID vaccines can cause genital herpes. We did the fact check to term it as Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: Genital herpes is a sexually transmitted infection (STI) caused by the herpes simplex virus (HSV). There are two types of HSV: HSV-1, usually causing oral herpes, and HSV-2, generally responsible for genital herpes. The infection is spread through sexual contact and results in sores and blisters in the genital area. Genital herpes is a chronic condition, often with recurrent outbreaks, but it can be managed with antiviral medications. Genital herpes is caused by the herpes simplex virus. HSV-2 is the most common cause of genital herpes, though HSV-1 can also cause genital infections through oral-genital contact. The virus is highly contagious and can spread even when an infected person shows no visible symptoms. It enters the body through mucous membranes or breaks in the skin. Then, it travels to nerve cells where it can remain dormant until reactivated by triggers such as stress, illness, or immune suppression. The Pfizer COVID vaccine cannot cause genital herpes. The Pfizer COVID vaccine, like other COVID vaccines, protects against the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which causes COVID-19. It uses mRNA technology to instruct cells to produce a protein similar to the spike protein of the virus, triggering an immune response without using live virus. This technology does not involve any form of herpes virus and cannot cause herpes infections. Clinical trials and extensive post-marketing surveillance of the Pfizer COVID vaccine have established its safety. The evidence does not link the vaccine to genital herpes conclusively. The vaccine's side effects are well-documented. These include common reactions like soreness at the injection site, fatigue, headache, and mild flu-like symptoms. Very limited studies have examined the potential link between COVID-19 vaccines and herpesvirus reactivation. These studies indicate that there are a few reports of herpes virus reactivation following COVID-19 vaccination. But, the overall risk remains low, and the vaccine does not cause new herpes infections. The Pfizer post-marketing experience document includes reports of herpes simplex virus (HSV) infections following vaccination. Specifically, it lists herpes simplex among various adverse events, noting occurrences such as herpes simplex cervicitis, colitis, encephalitis, gastritis, hepatitis, meningitis, meningoencephalitis, meningomyelitis, necrotizing retinopathy, esophagitis, otitis externa, pharyngitis, pneumonia, reactivation, sepsis, viremia, virus conjunctivitis neonatal, and visceral herpes simplex infections. However, these reports do not establish a causal relationship between the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine and new herpes simplex infections. Rather, they indicate instances where herpes simplex virus (HSV) reactivation was reported post-vaccination. Reactivation refers to the resurgence of symptoms from a virus already present in the body, not a new infection caused by the vaccine. This reactivation is seen in some individuals with underlying health conditions or other contributing factors. The document underscores that while there are instances of HSV reactivation, these do not imply that the vaccine directly causes new HSV infections. Therefore, the Pfizer COVID vaccine does not cause genital herpes or other new herpes simplex infections. Instances of herpes simplex reported post-vaccination are cases of reactivation in individuals already carrying the virus.

title: Fact Check: Can Pfizer vaccines harm the heart and brain? - THIP Media
claim_text: According to a widely shared YouTube video titled 'Vaccine Brain Injury,' the COVID vaccines, particularly the gene-based COVID-19 vaccines made by Pfizer, may be to blame for heart and brain damage. According to the video, the increased levels of spike proteins discovered in the brain and heart tissue are linked to the vaccine rather than an actual infection.
quick_take: A widely shared YouTube video that equates spike proteins with all COVID vaccines rather than the actual virus is misleading. After checking the claim's accuracy, our research showed that it is only Half True.
doctor_explanation: What purpose do spike proteins serve? The virus that has been responsible for the global COVID-19 disease outbreak is known as SARS-CoV-2. One of their crucial biological characteristics is the presence of spike proteins, which allow SARS-CoV-2 and a number of other viruses to enter host cells and spread infection. The S protein is essential for invading host cells and starting an infection, in contrast to the M and E proteins, which are primarily involved in virus assembly. Notably, the S proteins found on coronaviruses are what cause their spike-like surface protrusions. Considering that the S proteins allow for virus-host interaction, therefore, research on vaccines and antivirals should focus on the S protein. In addition to its role in penetrating cells, the S protein of viruses, particularly the SARS-CoV-2 virus, is a significant inducer of neutralizing antibodies (NAbs). Our humoral immune system naturally produces protective antibodies called NAbs. Do Pfizer vaccines have the potential to produce spike proteins that are harmful to the heart and brain? First and foremost, it needs to be made clear that many vaccines introduce weakened or inactive germs into our bodies in order to elicit an immune response. However, with mRNA vaccines, this is not the case. And Pfizer is an mRNA vaccine. These mRNA vaccines instruct our cells to produce a protein—or even just a portion of a protein—that sets off an immune response in our bodies using mRNA that was created in a lab. The immune response that results in the production of antibodies aids in preventing future infections from that germ. mRNA vaccines do not contain any components of the virus that causes COVID-19, but protein subunit vaccines do. These virus fragments are the spike proteins. It should be made clear that the SARS-CoV-2 infection as well as vaccination could both result in the development of anti-spike protein antibodies. The mRNA vaccine has been linked to cases of myocarditis, but despite our research, we were unable to discover any clear scientific evidence to support the theory that Pfizer-induced spike proteins can indicate damage to the heart and brain. What side effects are brought on by COVID-19 vaccines? The World Health Organization states that experiencing mild side effects following vaccination is common. Like with any vaccine, some recipients of the COVID-19 shot may experience mild to moderate side effects. This is a typical indication that the body is creating defenses. Fever, exhaustion, headache, muscle ache, chills, diarrhoea, and pain or redness at the injection site are all side effects of the COVID-19 vaccine. The majority of these usual side effects go away on their own within a few days. However, if your side effects persist after a few days or if the pain in the arm where you received the injection worsens, you should seek advice from your doctor. It must be emphasized that the doctor could always manage these side effects by advising sufficient rest, lots of non-alcoholic fluids, painkillers, and fever-relieving medications. Although extremely rare, COVID-19 vaccine side effects could be more severe or last longer. Contact your healthcare provider right away if you have trouble breathing, chest pain, confusion, loss of speech, or mobility following your vaccination. Vaccines are continuously monitored for the duration of their use to identify and address any uncommon adverse events. THIP MEDIA TAKE: We conclude that because Pfizer is an mRNA vaccine, it is not the cause of the spike in protein concentration in the brain and heart tissues. Additionally, it needs to be emphasized that protein subunit vaccines, rather than mRNA vaccines, can also contribute to an increase in spike proteins, along with viral infection. Myocarditis cases, however, have been linked to the mRNA vaccine, so we deduce that the claim is only half true.

title: Fact Check: Can pinching the fingertips prevent stroke?
claim_text: A Facebook reel with the caption, "If you don't want to have a stroke try it" shares a video where one pinches the fingertips for 5-10 minutes a day. It states that "Pinch gingers can dilate blood vessels, increase blood vessels elasticity"
quick_take: A social media post claims that one can prevent stroke by pinching the fingertips. We fact-checked and found this claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation:
A stroke occurs when part of the brain doesn't get enough oxygen and nutrients. The lack of oxygen occurs because a clot can narrow or block (ischemic stroke) or burst (haemorrhagic stroke) the blood vessels in the brain. This ultimately leads to the death of brain cells. The brain controls the movement and thoughts of a person. So, a stroke can affect a person's ability to think, move and function. It can also affect language, memory and vision. In a few cases, it can even lead to paralysis or death. Blood vessels that are damaged by high blood pressure can narrow, rupture or leak. This can increase the chance of stroke.

Stroke prevention involves several key strategies: managing high blood pressure, controlling diabetes, maintaining a healthy diet low in saturated fats and sodium, engaging in regular physical activity, quitting smoking, limiting alcohol intake, practising stress-reduction techniques, adhering to prescribed medications, maintaining a healthy weight, and attending routine health check-ups. These measures collectively reduce the risk of strokes, which can result from factors like high blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, and obesity. A proactive approach to stroke prevention is crucial for maintaining overall cardiovascular health and well-being.

title: Can Pineapple Juice Help Get Rid of Intestinal Worms?- THIP
claim_text: A social media post by Salatubpune shared a video in which a nutritionist claims that drinking fresh pineapple juice can help eliminate intestinal worms.
quick_take: A social media post suggests that drinking fresh pineapple juice helps get rid of intestinal worms. We fact checked and found the claim to be mostly false.
doctor_explanation:
Dr Sukrit Singh Sethi, Director & Senior Consultant, Gastroenterology, Narayana Hospital, Gurugram, says, 'Pineapple juice cannot treat intestinal worm infections. The idea comes from bromelain, an enzyme in pineapple that can damage parasites in laboratory studies and some animal research. However, in humans, stomach acid breaks down bromelain before it reaches the intestines, so it does not work as a deworming treatment. If symptoms like persistent stomach discomfort, diarrhea, weight loss, or visible worms in stool occur, a stool test and medical consultation are necessary. Doctors usually prescribe antiparasitic medicines such as Albendazole or Mebendazole, which are safe and effective.'

There isn’t good clinical evidence that pineapple juice can cure intestinal worm infections in humans. Here’s why this claim sounds believable: pineapple contains proteolytic (protein-breaking) enzymes, and researchers have explored whether plant enzymes can damage worms. In fact, older observations and later scientific reviews describe fresh pineapple juice/extract having effects against certain parasites under laboratory conditions.

But lab conditions are controlled: worms are directly exposed to concentrated juice or purified enzymes for long periods. In real life, once you drink pineapple juice, it gets diluted, mixed with food, and exposed to stomach acid and digestive processes. That makes 'worm-killing' inside a human intestine far less predictable.

Bromelain is the main reason pineapple gets linked to 'killing parasites.' Bromelain is a group of enzymes found in pineapple (especially the stem and fruit). Scientific work on 'plant-derived cysteine proteinases' (a category that includes enzymes like bromelain) suggests these enzymes can damage the outer surface of some worms, reducing their movement or viability in experimental settings.

Most research showing pineapple's antiparasitic activity has been conducted either in laboratory experiments or in animals such as mice, goats, and poultry. There is currently no strong clinical evidence showing that pineapple juice can reliably eliminate intestinal worms in humans.

Processing can matter a lot. One reason 'pineapple juice kills worms' became popular is the idea that fresh pineapple juice may contain more active enzymes. Heat can reduce enzyme activity, so some sources note that heated/canned pineapple products may not have the same enzyme effect. Even so, 'fresh is better' doesn't solve the bigger problem: we still don't have solid human clinical proof that fresh pineapple juice clears intestinal worms. It's also not clear what amount would be needed, or whether that amount would be tolerable (pineapple can be acidic and may trigger reflux or mouth irritation in some people).

Standard anti-parasitic medicines like albendazole or mebendazole remain the medically recommended treatment. The World Health Organization recommends these medicines for deworming programmes in endemic settings, and the CDC provides clinical dosing guidance for different worm infections.

Dr Anusha Dewan, General Physician at Jeevan Anmol Hospital in Mayur Vihar, New Delhi, explains that intestinal worm infections are best treated with doctor-prescribed antiparasitic medicines such as albendazole or mebendazole, which effectively kill the worms and help the body eliminate them. She adds that good hygiene practices, including regular handwashing, proper cooking of food, and keeping nails short, are essential to prevent reinfection. In some cases, the dose may be repeated after two weeks, especially for threadworms, while more severe infections may require medicines like ivermectin or praziquantel. The World Health Organization also supports deworming programmes, particularly in areas where these infections are common among children.

title: Can placing onion and spices under the feet remove 'toxins'?- THIP
claim_text: Wrapping onion and a mixture of common kitchen spices (onions, ajwain, fenugreek seeds, cumin, turmeric, or pink salt) under the soles of the feet for 5–6 hours can absorb toxins, lower inflammation, and relieve knee or joint pain
quick_take: A social media post suggests that onions, ajwain (carom seeds), fenugreek seeds, cumin (jeera), turmeric, or pink salt placed under the feet can draw out 'toxins' from the body in a few hours. We fact checked and found the claim to be false.
doctor_explanation: Human skin, particularly the skin on the soles of the feet, is designed to protect the body from external substances, not to let them pass through. The outermost layer, called the stratum corneum, is made up of tightly packed dead skin cells and oils that prevent most chemicals or toxins from entering or leaving the body. Some substances, like nicotine or hormone patches, are specially designed to penetrate this barrier. They use medically formulated compounds that can diffuse through skin layers and reach the bloodstream. In contrast, placing raw food items like onion or spices on the skin does not create any pathway for toxins to be 'sucked out.' There is no biological mechanism by which the onion could attract, absorb, or neutralise toxins through the feet. The idea likely emerged from old folk beliefs and visual changes in the onion. When onions are left exposed, they darken or smell foul, which some interpret as 'absorbed toxins.' In reality, this happens because of oxidation and bacterial growth. Onions naturally react to air and moisture, they don't draw out poison or waste from the human body. Regarding joint pain: 'Joint and knee pain are usually caused by inflammation, cartilage wear, poor posture, or other internal issues. Simply placing some spices under your feet cannot influence these deep biological processes.' You may feel a temporary soothing or cooling sensation, especially if the onion is cold or moist, but that's a sensory effect, not true pain relief. This mild comfort might make people believe it is helping, which is known as the placebo effect, when the belief in a treatment makes you feel better even though the treatment itself has no real physiological impact. Real relief from joint pain requires a combination of rest, physiotherapy, anti-inflammatory foods, regular movement, and sometimes medication. Regarding inflammation: Onions, turmeric, and certain spices like fenugreek do contain compounds known for their anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects, but these benefits are seen when they are eaten and metabolised by the body, not when they sit on the skin. When consumed, onions release beneficial molecules such as quercetin and sulphur compounds, which help reduce oxidative stress. However, topical application does not allow these substances to penetrate the skin in meaningful amounts. The epidermis (outer skin layer) blocks such large molecules from entering the bloodstream. Dr. Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition, explains: 'There's no biological mechanism by which an onion under your foot can impact your immune system or circulation. It's an old folk remedy that may give people comfort, but it's not doing what they think it is.' Manasi Banduni, Senior Nutritionist at Clinic Living Plus, Bangalore, adds, 'Onions have antibacterial properties when eaten, not when used topically. The skin is a protective barrier, not a sponge for detox. Believing otherwise can delay people from seeking real treatment when they need it.' The colour and smell changes are due to natural decomposition, not detoxification. When you slice an onion and expose it to air, enzymes inside it react with oxygen. This triggers a process called oxidation, which alters its colour and releases sulphur compounds. If you place an onion under your foot, the warmth, sweat, and bacteria from your skin accelerate this breakdown. Over a few hours, the onion softens, discolours, and smells stronger. People misinterpret this as the onion having 'absorbed toxins' from their body, but it's merely a sign of normal spoilage and microbial activity. There is no proven health benefit, only a placebo or cooling effect. The only possible effect you might experience is a short-lived sense of relaxation, mainly because of the aroma or moisture of the onion. The skin does not function as a detox organ; that role belongs to your liver, kidneys, and digestive system.

The original video was muted and a part of it was used out of context. Loa Loa is a parasitic worm that causes the disease Loiasis or as popularly known African Eye. The website of CDC mentions, the disease is "passed on to humans through the repeated bites of deerflies." The Loa Loa worms reside inside the skin or on the eyes of the infected person. Often surgical removal of adult worms moving under the skin or across the eye can be done as a part of the treatment procedure of Loiasis. There is no scientific evidence that suggests that long use of mobile phones for the purpose of games or studies can cause Loa Loa worms in the body. We talked to Eye Surgeon Dr. Aftab Alam, MBBS, DO (Ophthalmology). He confirms, "Loa Loa is a filarial nematodes disease which means it is a type of roundworm disease. The worm does infect the eye of a patient and hence it is also known as Eye Worm. Using mobile phones has nothing to do with this parasitic infection."

title: Can pomegranate consumption manage kidney stones?
claim_text: A Facebook post titled "Kidney Stones: 2 Ways to Treat It with 1 Fruit" asserts that pomegranate is a definitive solution for kidney stones. It further suggests that both the fruit and its seeds can alleviate this painful condition.
quick_take: A social media post claims that pomegranate is a definite solution for kidney stones. We fact-checked the claim and found that it is mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Pomegranate, also known as Punica granatum, is being studied for its potential to help prevent kidney stone formation. This may be explained by their high antioxidant content and capacity to lessen oxidative stress, a contributing element to the development of renal stones. Pomegranate juice and extracts have also demonstrated encouraging outcomes by lowering reactive oxygen species. However, these results are limited to animal-based studies. Additionally, the fruit has anti-inflammatory qualities that could help lessen renal irritation and lower the risk of stones. Pomegranates are also high in potassium, vitamin C, and polyphenols, all of which may help maintain kidney health. While the fruit helps in reducing oxidative stress and enhancing overall renal function, it is not a definitive treatment option for kidney stones. Dr. Archana Daftardar, Consultant Nephrologist, Hypertension & Transplant Physician, Renova Hospitals, Kompally, Hyderabad, emphasises that the dietary recommendations are usually based on the chemical makeup of the kidney stone. While fruits—especially citrus fruits—can help prevent stones to some extent, they cannot be the mainstay of the treatment. Pomegranates, in particular, are not a therapeutic solution for kidney stones. Fruits should be considered as a beneficial additive to a well-nourished dietary regimen that enhances renal function; however, their ability to dissolve kidney stones has not been demonstrated. Consequently, regulated consumption of pomegranates still has a preventive effect, but their consumption should not bypass the role of evidence-based therapy for kidney stones. Kidney stones, medically referred to as renal calculi, are hard, pebble-like structures that develop in the pelvis and renal calyces. These hard deposits usually accumulate when minerals and salts, such as calcium, oxalate, and uric acid, crystallise in extremely concentrated urine. Men between the ages of 30 and 50 tend to be more vulnerable, as are those who suffer from weight-related problems, hyperparathyroidism, or repeated UTIs. Pomegranates are loaded with antioxidants, fibre, folate, potassium, vitamin K, vitamin E, vitamin B6, and trace amounts of sodium and phosphorus. Given that certain chemicals derived from pomegranates might influence potassium and phosphorus levels, the nephrologist assesses appropriate consumption by considering the type of dialysis and the stage of renal illness. Renal stones are dealt with based on their chemical makeup, structural attributes, and anatomical placement. Dr. Ganesh Srinivasa Prasad P, Consultant Nephrologist at Narayana Health City in Bengaluru, adds that kidney stones cannot be treated with home remedies. The measurement and chemical nature of the stone frequently determine the course of treatment. However, consuming calcium-rich foods, limiting oxalate-rich foods, drinking plenty of water, and limiting salt intake can all help lower the risk of recurrence. Those who are more susceptible should also limit their consumption of meat, sugar, alcohol, and tobacco. Dr. Archana Daftardar adds that there are many misconceptions around kidney stone prevention and therapy. Natural therapies that have not been validated can cause serious problems instead of curing the illness. It is best to get advice from qualified Ayurvedic or allopathic physicians. Such unverified natural remedies may conflict with prescription medications or even provide a false sense of assurance. This could worsen the illness or delay necessary treatment.

title: Fact Check: Can pomegranate cure arthritis?
claim_text: POMEGRANATE Cures Arthritis
quick_take: A social media post claimed that pomegranate cures arthritis. We fact-checked and found the claim to be Half-True.
doctor_explanation: Limited evidence. The available scientific research studies suggest that pomegranate (Punica granatum L.) has antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anticarcinogenic effects that can help with relieving osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. To this Dr Saransh Gupta, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Indian Spinal Injuries Centre, New Delhi, adds, "Current medical treatment is based on reducing the inflammation by using anti-inflammatory medicines. The published studies have shown that the pomegranate fruit is rich in bioactive compounds such as polyphenols, anthocyanin, flavonoids, tannins, puninic acid, etc. These compounds have anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties that can reduce disease activity and inflammatory markers. The published studies have shown that pomegranate fruit extract (PFE) is highly effective in exerting human cartilage sparing effects and is non-toxic to human cartilage cells". Where Dr. Gupta highlighted the benefits of pomegranate against arthritis, Dt. Priyanka, Nutritionist said, "Joint pain is an inflammatory condition. Although pomegranate may be beneficial against arthritis, the condition is a multifactorial disease where some important risk factors that include age, sex, genetics, obesity, and joint injury must be included while deciding the portion size. All these factors need to be considered while managing joint pain like arthritis". During our research, we found that polyphenols in pomegranate can inhibit inflammation. However, they have been widely studied by researchers for their harmful effects. A study shows that pomegranate has high punicalagin which is a type of ellagitannin – a polyphenol. A (2003) study notes, 'The water-soluble ellagitanin punicalagin has been reported to be toxic to cattle'. However, the available evidence cannot establish this polyphenol as 'toxic' to human beings. Hence, 'taking into account the high punicalagin content of pomegranate-derived foodstuffs, safety evaluation should also be carried out in humans with a lower dose and during a longer period of intake'. We also found scientific evidence that shows improperly chewed seeds can cause a medical condition called Phytobezoar. It is a mass formed due to indigestible fibre, skin or seeds, trapped in the gastrointestinal tract. Despite this, there are people who suggest pomegranate juice can cure constipation. But, this isn't true, because it does not have the necessary fibre to help relieve constipation. Some studies also contemplate whether pomegranate can cause food poisoning, and lower blood pressure (BP) in people with already low BP and allergy. It seems there is not enough scientific evidence that has assessed the benefits of pomegranate against arthritis or other bone diseases. To this Dr Gupta further adds, "Unlike the conventional treatment for arthritis (NSAIDs or corticosteroids drugs) which has an associated side effect profile, pomegranate is often considered safe and non-toxic. In view of the identified pharmacological targets and therapeutic potentials of pomegranate, clinical trials are in progress to explore its therapeutic potential for OA treatment, thus pomegranate or pomegranate-derived compounds can emerge as novel therapeutic agents for use in the treatment of OA and other degenerative/inflammatory diseases". In conclusion, we need more studies to understand the optimum dosage of pomegranate that can provide relief from arthritis. Also, studies are needed to understand the role of pomegranate against arthritis due to genetics. Just like this story, we also looked into another claim that says moringa leaves can cure arthritis, but we found it to have a missing context. Similar to pomegranate, moringa surely has all the reasons to be in the 'arthritis management diet'. However, it is an overstatement to say that it 'cures' arthritis completely. THIP MEDIA TAKE: Pomegranate can provide relief to arthritis. However, overdose or indigestion of pomegranate may have serious complications. Hence, the claim remains half-true until proven otherwise.

title: Fact Check: Can pomegranate juice cure constipation?
claim_text: According to a post on Threads you can cure constipation by drinking pomegranate juice everyday. The post further claims that it can help you get rid of gas, bloating and cleanse the gut properly.
quick_take: A social media post claims that pomegranate juice can cure constipation. Our fact check concludes that this claim is False.
doctor_explanation: Pomegranate juice contains very little fibre, which is vital for preventing and relieving constipation. Most of the fibre in the pomegranate fruit comes from the seeds and pulp, which are removed during the juicing process. As a result, pomegranate juice provides negligible fibre, making it ineffective for curing constipation. There is another claim that raw onions can treat constipation, citing its fibre content, but this isn't entirely true. Fibre is essential because it adds bulk to stools, making bowel movements easier. Instead of relying on pomegranate juice, a diet rich in fibre from whole fruits and vegetables, and grains is a more reliable way to address constipation. So, it is advisable to eat the whole pomegranate rather than the juice. Pomegranate juice may help with IBD (Inflammatory Bowel Disease) due to its polyphenols, but it can also cause diarrhoea and allergies in some people. Studies are still investigating its effects on inflammation. Dr Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition, says, "Pomegranate juice is a healthy beverage, packed with antioxidants and vitamins. However, it's not a suitable remedy for constipation, as it lacks the fibre needed to promote bowel regularity. For constipation relief, I always recommend increasing dietary fibre through whole fruits, vegetables, and grains, as well as drinking plenty of water. These are the natural ways to support digestion and improve gut health." Dietician Kamna Chauhan agrees and explains, "While pomegranate juice is beneficial for its nutrients, it doesn't contain much fibre, which is crucial for relieving constipation. Instead of relying on juice, focusing on fibre-rich foods like oats, flaxseeds, and leafy greens is more effective. And don't forget the importance of staying hydrated—water plays a key role in easing digestion and preventing constipation." Regarding gas and bloating: there's no evidence to support the claim that pomegranate juice relieves gas or bloating. In fact, its high sugar content, particularly fructose, could even worsen these symptoms for some individuals, especially if they have fructose sensitivity. Regarding gut cleansing: the idea that pomegranate juice "cleanses the gut" does not have any scientific evidence. The body naturally detoxifies itself through the liver and kidneys. There is no need for specific foods or drinks to perform this function. Ayurvedic practices may recommend certain fruits to support digestion, but they don't suggest that pomegranate juice alone can cleanse the digestive system. Instead, traditional approaches focus on balanced diets and herbal remedies, like ginger or fennel, for digestive health. Regarding excessive consumption: excessive pomegranate consumption may lead to constipation due to the formation of phytobezoars. These are indigestible plant materials that can build up in the gastrointestinal tract. Consuming large quantities of pomegranate seeds may cause blockages and constipation, especially in individuals with digestive issues or prior gastrointestinal surgeries. Additionally, pomegranate juice, which is low in fibre, may not cause constipation directly but could lead to bloating or discomfort when consumed in excess due to its high sugar content and lack of fibre. Therefore, moderation is key to avoiding these digestive complications. Soumam Dutta, PhD Scholar (Nutrition), Department of Endocrinology, ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition, explains, "It is essential for adults to follow 'My Plate' to prevent or treat constipation, as it provides adequate fibre. Including a salad (100g) with breakfast, lunch, and dinner is a healthy and sustainable option. Overall, 400g of vegetables, 100g of whole fruits, and 3-4 litres of water should be consumed daily. Additionally, whole grains, millets, legumes, and nuts can be included in the diet. Bran and/or powdered fibre can be added to cereals, yogurt, or soups. Also, warm water taken early in the morning may help with defecation." Dietitian Anuradha Sharma, M.Sc. Food Science and Nutrition Management (Gold Medalist), Kolkata, says, "Constipation is a common problem that happens when bowel movements become infrequent. It is often linked to three main factors: diet, gut muscle movement (called peristalsis), and the body's natural clock, or circadian rhythm. To avoid constipation, it's important to focus on these areas. A healthy diet is key—eat plenty of fiber-rich foods like fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and lentils, and drink enough water daily (about 2.5–3.5 liters for adults). Avoid too much caffeine, alcohol, and processed foods, as they can make things worse. Regular physical activity is also important. Being active throughout the day is better than just doing one hour of exercise and staying inactive the rest of the time. Additionally, sticking to a consistent sleep schedule and morning routine can help your body's natural rhythm. Late nights and rushing in the morning can interfere with the timing of bowel movements."

title: Fact Check: Can pomegranate unclog arteries? - THIP Media
claim_text: Pomegranate is proven to unclog arteries. Pomegranate has been shown to prevent and even reverse cardiovascular disease.
quick_take: Few social media posts claim that Pomegranate can unclog arteries and reverse cardio-vascular disease. We fact-checked and found that the claim is half true.
doctor_explanation: Arteries carry oxygen-rich blood from the heart to all parts of your body. Wide open arteries allow blood to move quickly and freely in the body. The build-up of fibrous and fatty material inside the arteries make the path narrow and the result is blocked arteries. Dr Amit Bhushan Sharma, Associate Director and Unit Head, Cardiology, Paras Hospitals, Gurugram, says, "Brain stokes, heart strokes, angina, and peripheral artery disease can be caused by blocked arteries. When a particle of plaque breaks off and becomes lodged in the bloodstream, blood flow is reduced, which can result in a heart attack or stroke." Yes. Research has shown that pomegranate can be beneficial in clearing plaque from blood vessels. In fact, research has shown that not only pomegranate but multiple plant based diets can help in stopping the development of plaque in blood vessels. Medical professionals believe a healthy diet of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, lean meats, skinless chicken, seafood, and fat-free or low-fat dairy products can help in preventing the development of plaque in arteries. However, neither pomegranate, nor any other diet is known to be able to cleanse blood vessels completely. It is almost impossible to remove plaque from blood vessels without medical intervention. Preventing development of plaque from arteries needs a combination of healthy diet, losing weight, being physically active, and not smoking. However, once artery blockage has been diagnosed, medical intervention like angioplasty or putting a stent may be the only option depending on the severity of the disease. Dr. Sharma adds, "When plaques grow up inside a person's arteries, they might get clogged, restricting blood flow. Individual foods cannot remove these plaque from the arteries. But a healthy diet can aid in the management and prevention of heart disease. Statins have a pleotropic effect, which means they prevent brain and heart strokes by regressing plaque and transforming it from thin to thick cap, avoiding plaque rupture."
