title: Can rock salt, alum, cloves and mustard oil cure all dental problems?
claim_text: According to a Facebook post, a mixture of powdered rock salt (sendha namak), alum (phitkari), and cloves (laung) mixed with mustard oil (sarson ka tel) can cure all dental problems. The post claims it can treat decayed teeth, toothaches, bleeding gums, pus in the gums, yellow teeth, and pyorrhoea in just 2–3 uses.
quick_take: A social media post claims that rock salt, alum, cloves, and mustard oil can cure all dental problems. We fact checked this and termed it false.
doctor_explanation:
Tooth decay arises due to bacteria producing acids that erode tooth enamel. Some ingredients mentioned in the post might offer temporary relief because they do have mild antiseptic properties. But, they cannot reverse existing decay. A decayed tooth requires professional dental treatment. This can include fillings, crowns, or even extraction, to remove the decay and restore the tooth's structure and function. Ignoring decay and relying on home remedies can lead to the worsening of the condition which can cause more pain and an increased risk for infection.

Bleeding gums and pus are often signs of gum disease (gingivitis or periodontitis), which is a bacterial infection. While some ingredients like cloves have antibacterial properties, they are not potent enough to eliminate the bacteria causing a significant gum infection. Effective treatment for gum disease involves professional dental cleanings to remove plaque and tartar. And, in more severe cases, scaling and root planing or other periodontal therapies. Relying solely on this home remedy can allow the infection to progress, leading to more severe gum damage, bone loss, and eventually tooth loss.

Dr Snigdha, BDS, MDS, from Vananchal Dental College and Hospital, Jharkhand, says that a homemade mix like this cannot treat serious dental issues such as cavities or pus from the gums. "Cavities are permanent damage to the teeth and need proper treatment like fillings. Pus usually means there's a deeper infection, often something like periodontitis, which needs professional care," she explains. Herbal rinses might offer some short-term relief, but they won't fix the underlying problem or stop further damage, she adds.

Dr Pooja Sharma, BDS, MDS, from NIMS University, Jaipur, explains, "Home remedies can sometimes do more harm than good—not because the ingredients are harmful, but because they can give the false impression that professional care isn't necessary. Dental issues like cavities and gum infections don't heal on their own; they require proper diagnosis and treatment. Delaying care can turn a small problem into severe pain, swelling, or even tooth loss. It's always better to consult a dentist early rather than waiting for the situation to worsen."

Some ingredients, like cloves, contain eugenol, which has mild anaesthetic and antiseptic properties that might temporarily ease toothaches. Rock salt might also offer some soothing effects. However, toothaches are often a symptom of underlying dental problems such as decay, infection, or gum disease. So, even though this mixture might provide fleeting relief, it does not solve the root cause of the pain. Plus, the pain will most likely return without proper dental treatment.

Yellowing of teeth can happen due to various factors, including staining from food and drinks, enamel thinning, and poor oral hygiene. Rock salt may have a mild abrasive effect, and might help remove some surface stains. But it is not a substitute for professional teeth whitening treatments or toothpastes that have specific ingredients to break down stains safely. This homemade mixture is unlikely to significantly change the natural colour of teeth.

Pyorrhoea, or advanced periodontitis, is a serious gum infection. It damages the soft tissues and the bone that support the teeth. This condition needs professional treatment from a dentist or periodontist. Management usually includes deep cleaning, medication, and sometimes surgery. A 2021 review mentions Ayurvedic methods for managing periodontitis. These include certain medicinal herbs and practices like oil pulling. However, it does not mention sendha namak, alum, cloves, or mustard oil, the ingredients promoted in the Facebook post.

Dr Annusuiya Gohil, Ayurvedic expert and MD Scholar at the All India Institute of Ayurveda, explains that while classical Ayurvedic texts do cover dental care in detail, the claims made in viral social media posts are often misleading. "There is a full postgraduate specialisation in Ayurveda that focuses on eye, ear, nose, throat, and dental care. But these remedies cannot be applied in a vague or general way. How herbs are prepared and used makes a big difference," she says. Dr Gohil further adds, "It is incorrect to claim that all dental problems, especially serious ones like pyorrhoea, can be treated with a single herbal mix. If someone says the remedy is mentioned in Ayurvedic texts, they must cite the exact reference. That allows trained Ayurvedic professionals to interpret it properly and guide treatment based on individual needs."

Commercial toothpastes are clinically tested and contain ingredients that are scientifically proven to support oral health. Most include fluoride to strengthen enamel and prevent cavities, mild abrasives to remove plaque and surface stains, and detergents to help loosen debris. Some are specially formulated to address sensitivity, tartar build-up, or whitening. While a few products may be overhyped, many are backed by research and approved by dental associations. Replacing them entirely with a homemade mixture like the one suggested could compromise oral hygiene. Brushing twice a day with the right technique and a fluoride-based toothpaste remains the foundation of good dental care.

title: Can rock salt and turmeric permanently resolve mouth ulcers?
claim_text: A combination of rock salt and turmeric can permanently cure mouth ulcers
quick_take: According to a Facebook reel, a combination of rock salt and turmeric can permanently cure mouth ulcers. We analysed the claim and discovered that it is mostly false.
doctor_explanation:
Mouth ulcers, also known as aphthous ulcers or canker sores, are painful, non-contagious lesions that appear in the soft tissues of the mouth. These lesions, which have white or yellow cores and red elevated borders, are usually produced by trauma, hereditary factors, persistent stress, or specific foods. In addition to being uncomfortable, they may tingle, sting, or be irritable. These ulcerative lesions usually appear in clumps of two to four on the inner aspect of the cheeks or lips. They may occasionally form on the gingiva, tongue, or roof of the mouth, suggesting that movements of the mouth when eating or speaking can aggravate the pain. While most mouth ulcers are minor lesions that resolve in one to two weeks, some of these lesions may suggest underlying issues, such as vitamin deficiencies or certain systemic illnesses. If ulcers are severe and last longer than three weeks or are accompanied by additional signs, get medical attention immediately.

Mouth ulcers are prevalent yet distressing; individuals may turn to home remedies for relief. One of them is a home rinse made with salt and turmeric. Given that herbal remedies are deemed safe, however, for the two to be utilised as a mouth rinse necessitates thorough evaluation. First comes salt, a natural antiseptic that may help reduce the oral microbial load while establishing an environment conducive to infection resistance. Next, turmeric, the most widely accepted medicinal ingredient. This could be due to the presence of curcumin, which has well-documented anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antibacterial properties.

While the combination may provide short-term relief by reducing inflammation and the risk of infection, it is not a definitive or permanent solution for mouth ulcers. This is especially true for recurring or persistent lesions, which might indicate underlying concerns such as dietary deficits, gastrointestinal diseases, or autoimmune conditions that call for medical intervention.

Dr. Pooja Siwach, an oral and maxillofacial pathologist, Lucknow warns that even minor mouth ulcers can cause severe suffering. Gentle remedies—saltwater rinses cleanse, honey promotes relaxation, aloe vera hydrates, and a cold pack may help relieve pain—might be beneficial. Limiting irritants along with practising excellent oral hygiene can help prevent recurrence. These basic, natural remedies frequently perform wonderfully, aiding the body's healing process. However, persistent or severe sores may indicate underlying health issues and require professional attention.

Dr. Surya Kiran Mudigonda, Consultant Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeon at Renova Hospitals in Hyderabad, supports this by stating that applying ice, butter, or ghee to mouth ulcers usually offers symptomatic relief while also preserving moisture for wound healing. Nonetheless, they are not the established therapeutic options for mouth ulcers. Never apply turmeric powder, clove oil, or any other irritant to mouth ulcers. They are going to escalate the discomfort and irritation.

While the majority of home cures may provide temporary comfort, the notion that such approaches may permanently resolve mouth ulcers is deceptive. This could be linked to the multifactorial nature of mouth ulcers, which cannot be addressed by unverified home therapies. Moreover, home remedies are not standardised in terms of dosage, safety, or efficacy. It should be noted that evidence-based care of mouth ulcers includes diagnosing underlying deficits, correcting systemic causes, and employing established pharmaceutical medications as necessary. Relying on unreliable remedies may result in delays in the essential evaluation and therapy.

Dr. Gagandeep Singh Sodhi, a Delhi-based dentist, adds that using untested home remedies for mouth ulcers before seeking medical attention can delay critical care, aggravate symptoms, and pose unexpected health concerns. Hence, one should consult a well-qualified dental expert for timely and accurate intervention. Even while certain natural remedies might offer modest benefits when carefully analysed, they should not be relied on solely without expert supervision. These botanical extracts should only be used in combination with conventional therapies, particularly if the mouth ulcers are severe, persistent, or recurring.

As previously noted, minor, non-contagious ulcers usually resolve on their own without the need for special medical intervention. Two of the key approaches to minor mouth ulcer management include: At-home measures - Some at-home remedies that may help relieve oral discomfort and perhaps accelerate the process of healing include utilising warm saline rinses, avoiding hot, spicy, and acidic foods, and taking sufficient amounts of fluids to keep the mouth well-hydrated. Professional intervention - Corticosteroids and topical anaesthetic gels are usually the first choices for pain relief and rehabilitation. Chlorhexidine, an antibacterial mouthwash, can help prevent subsequent infections. In addition, doctors may prescribe systemic therapeutics such as colchicine, dapsone, or thalidomide. Larger, more chronic, and recurring ulcerative lesions require medical attention. Chronic mouth sores can be a sign of an underlying systemic illness, including diabetes, inflammatory bowel disease, HIV/AIDS, Behçet's disease, coeliac disease, and immunological disorders. It is vital to comprehend that, like any other medical condition, mouth ulcers necessitate highly skilled medical care aimed at relieving symptoms, limiting the ulcer's duration, and enhancing the patient's overall well-being.

title: Can consuming Rosemary 'remove sugar from veins' in 10 days?
claim_text: An Instagram post claims that consuming rosemary tea with turmeric and cinnamon can flush sugar out of the veins, promising visible results in just 10 days.
quick_take: A claim circulating on social media suggests that a 10-day course of rosemary, turmeric, and cinnamon tea can remove sugar from the veins. We fact checked and found the claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: This claim is based on a flawed idea of how the body works. Sugar (glucose) in the blood is not waste material or plaque that sticks to the veins. It is a normal and essential fuel that your body constantly uses, especially your brain. Even people without diabetes always have glucose circulating in their blood. In diabetes, the problem is that glucose levels stay too high for too long because insulin is not working properly or is insufficient. This excess glucose does not get flushed out by foods or herbs. Blood sugar improves only when glucose is used by cells more effectively and when the liver reduces excess glucose release. While short-term improvements are possible (if someone reduces sugary foods, avoids sweetened drinks, walks daily, and follows medical advice, daily glucose readings may improve within days), this does not mean diabetes is cured or that blood vessels are suddenly 'clean'. Long-term blood sugar control is measured using HbA1c, which reflects average glucose levels over several months, not days. A 10-day window is simply too short to prove meaningful or lasting improvement. Regarding rosemary: it contains antioxidant compounds and has shown interesting effects in laboratory and animal studies, but evidence in humans is limited and inconsistent. The small amounts of rosemary typically used in cooking are unlikely to have any meaningful effect on blood sugar levels. Rosemary does not act like insulin, does not improve glucose control reliably, and cannot replace diabetes medication or structured lifestyle changes. Regarding turmeric: turmeric contains curcumin, a compound that has been studied for its potential role in improving insulin sensitivity and reducing inflammation. Some research suggests that, when taken consistently over several weeks or months, curcumin may lead to small improvements in fasting blood sugar in certain people with diabetes or prediabetes. However, these effects are modest and vary widely between individuals. Turmeric does not act like diabetes medication, does not 'flush' sugar from the blood, and does not produce rapid or guaranteed results. Regarding cinnamon: 'Cinnamon has been studied for its potential effects on blood sugar, and while some research suggests it may cause a small drop in fasting glucose in certain people, the effect is modest, inconsistent, and highly individual. It does not remove sugar from the blood, it does not clean blood vessels, and it certainly does not reverse diabetes.' At best, cinnamon may slightly improve insulin sensitivity when used regularly over time, but the changes are small and take weeks or months, not days. Many well-controlled studies show no meaningful improvement in long-term markers like HbA1c. Diabetes is a complex metabolic condition, not a blockage that can be cleaned out. Herbs and spices can make healthy food more enjoyable and may offer small supportive benefits, but real blood sugar improvement comes from consistent habits, balanced meals, regular physical activity, good sleep, stress management, and appropriate medical treatment.

title: Fact Check: Can rosemary increase memory by 75%?
claim_text: Scientists found sniffing rosemary can increase memory by 75%. Rosemary helps break down a brain chemical called 'acetylcholine,' which improves communication between nerve cells.
quick_take: A social media post claims that sniffing rosemary can increase memory by 75%. Our fact check reveals this claim is mostly false.
doctor_explanation: While there is some evidence suggesting that rosemary might have cognitive benefits, the idea that it can boost memory by 75% is highly exaggerated. Some studies have found that rosemary can have a small effect on cognitive performance or short-term memory, but the impact is far from dramatic. Research has shown that the scent of rosemary might improve alertness or mental clarity, but nothing close to the dramatic 75% increase suggested in the claim. Dr Sreenivas Meenakshisundaram, Consultant Neurologist, MGM Healthcare, Chennai, says, 'Rosemary has been called a memory herb for a long time. However, there has been little scientific evidence to support this claim. Multiple studies in animals, including rats, mice, and zebrafish, have shown improvements in cognition with regular intake of rosemary.' He adds, 'But, these studies are small, and the effects are subtle. While this is a promising finding, we need to replicate these results in humans to be confident of any meaningful clinical benefit. It's also fascinating that compounds from rosemary can enter the bloodstream through inhalation, but we still need larger, more rigorous research to confirm its true impact. For now, think of rosemary as a pleasant and aromatic herb that might give a small cognitive lift, but it's no substitute for proven methods like staying mentally active, exercising, and eating a balanced diet.' Regarding acetylcholine, rosemary contains compounds like rosmarinic acid, known for their antioxidant properties, which may support brain health. Rather than breaking down acetylcholine (as the claim suggests), rosemary helps prevent its breakdown. Studies show that inhaling rosemary oil may help maintain acetylcholine levels. In one experiment, individuals exposed to diffused rosemary oil performed better on cognitive tasks, with improvements in speed and accuracy linked to longer exposure. A 2022 review of studies found that rosemary extract improved cognitive performance in both healthy and cognitively impaired animals. A 2018 study with 79 students revealed that rosemary enhanced image and numeric memory, while lavender boosted image memory but weakened number recall. However, the small sample size means the findings cannot be applied broadly. In a 2012 study with 28 older adults (average age 75), dried rosemary leaf powder was found to improve memory speed at a low dose (750 mg), while a higher dose (6,000 mg) impaired cognitive function. A 2009 study with 144 participants showed that rosemary essential oil improved overall memory quality and secondary memory factors, although it slowed memory speed. However, these studies are small, so they don't provide strong evidence for the claimed 75% boost in memory. Dr Kunal Bahrani, Director & HOD Neurology, Marengo Asia Hospitals, Faridabad, says, 'To improve memory, it's important to focus on both physical and mental health. Eating a balanced diet with foods rich in antioxidants and omega-3s, along with regular exercise, helps keep the brain sharp. Challenging your brain with activities like reading or puzzles also boosts memory.' He adds, 'Getting enough quality sleep is key, as it helps the brain store memories. Managing stress through techniques like meditation can also protect memory. By combining these healthy habits, you can improve memory and keep your brain healthy over time.'

title: Fact Check: Can rubbing a wet towel make you fair?
claim_text: Soak a towel in warm water and rub it on face. It removes dead skin cells and makes you fairer.
quick_take: A social media post claims that rubbing a wet towel makes you fair. The towel soaked in warm water on the face removes dead skin cells and makes you fairer. We fact-checked and found this claim to be false.
doctor_explanation: Skin colour depends on several factors, primarily genetics, which determine the amount and type of melanin produced by melanocytes in the skin. Melanin is the pigment responsible for the skin's colour, and its production is influenced by genetic inheritance. People with more melanin tend to have darker skin, while those with less melanin have lighter skin. Exposure to sunlight also affects skin colour. Ultraviolet (UV) rays from the sun stimulate melanocytes to produce more melanin, leading to tanning. This natural process helps protect the skin from UV damage. However, excessive sun exposure can lead to skin damage and increase the risk of skin cancer. Hormonal changes can influence skin colour as well. For instance, during pregnancy or certain medical conditions, hormone levels can cause hyperpigmentation or darkening of the skin in some areas. Age is another factor, as the skin can develop age spots or uneven pigmentation over time. Additionally, certain medications and chemicals can affect melanin production and distribution, altering skin colour. Finally, environmental factors, such as pollution and lifestyle choices, including diet and skincare routines, can impact skin health and appearance. Overall, while genetics play a primary role, various external and internal factors contribute to the complexity of skin colour. Can rubbing a wet towel make you fair? No, rubbing a wet towel on your skin cannot make you fair. Skin colour is primarily determined by genetic factors, which dictate the amount and type of melanin produced by melanocytes in the layer of skin. Melanin is the pigment responsible for skin colour, and its production is largely influenced by your genetic makeup, not by external physical actions such as rubbing. While rubbing a wet towel can help clean your skin and remove surface dirt and dead skin cells, it does not affect the deeper layers of skin where melanin is produced. Exfoliation can improve the texture and appearance of your skin to some extent, making it look brighter and healthier, but it does not change your skin's inherent colour. Moreover, the concept of 'fairness' often carries cultural connotations and varies widely around the world. It's important to recognise that healthy skin is more significant than adhering to any particular standard of beauty. Ultimately, while good skincare practices can enhance your skin's health and glow, they cannot fundamentally alter the genetic factors that determine your natural skin colour. Embrace your skin's unique beauty and focus on keeping it healthy and well-nourished. Dr. Jyoti Agarkar, MD (Dermatology), sums it up by stating, 'God has blessed us with a beautiful body and skin, which we should appreciate rather than trying to alter its color. I always advise my patients to follow a healthy diet, exercise regularly, get enough sleep, and stay well-hydrated. This promotes a natural glow that no artificial whitening products can match. Additionally, it's important to choose skincare products that are suitable for your skin type.' What can be the harm of rubbing towels on wet skin? Rubbing towels on wet skin can cause several harmful effects. Vigorous rubbing can irritate the skin, leading to redness, inflammation, and discomfort. This irritation is especially problematic for individuals with sensitive skin, eczema, or other skin conditions, as it can exacerbate symptoms and lead to flare-ups. Excessive rubbing can also damage the skin's protective barrier. The outermost layer of the skin, known as the stratum corneum, acts as a shield against environmental stresses and helps retain moisture. When this barrier is compromised by rough handling, the skin can become dry, itchy, and more prone to infections. Furthermore, rubbing can cause micro-tears in the skin, creating small wounds that are susceptible to bacteria and other pathogens. This increases the risk of infections and can slow down the healing process for any existing skin issues. Rubbing towels on wet skin can also lead to premature ageing. The repetitive friction can break down collagen and elastin fibres, which are essential for maintaining skin's elasticity and firmness. This may cause drooping skin, wrinkles, and fine lines over time. To avoid these problems, gently pat your skin dry with a soft towel instead of rubbing. This method is very soothing to your skin and helps maintain its natural barrier and overall health. Can you get fair easily at home? Certainly not. Achieving fairer skin at home is not easy, as skin colour is primarily determined by genetics and melanin levels. However, you can enhance your skin's natural radiance and achieve a healthier complexion through proper skincare practices and nutrition. Maintain a consistent skincare routine that includes cleansing, exfoliating, moisturising, and sun protection. Use gentle cleansers and exfoliants to remove dead skin cells and improve skin texture. Apply a good moisturiser to keep your skin hydrated and supple. Protect your skin from sun exposure by using a broad-spectrum sunscreen with good SPF. Sun damage can cause dark spots and uneven skin tone, so regular sunscreen application is crucial for healthy skin. Some home remedies, such as aloe vera gel, have been reported to have a protective effect against radiation damage to the skin. Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, which protects against photodamage and helps to improve glow. Also, mulberry and licorice are two common natural extracts that are added to skin whiteners. Some other studies claim natural remedies like honey, lemon juice, and fermented dairy products, such as yoghurt, are known for their healing and brightening properties. But given the paucity of current research, more investigation is necessary to fully evaluate the mechanisms at play as well as the efficacy. Also, be cautious and do a patch test before using any home remedy to avoid adverse reactions. For significant skin concerns, consult a dermatologist for professional advice and treatments. For improving skin appearance, focus on a consistent skincare routine that includes cleansing, moisturising, and sun protection. Sun exposure can lead to tanning and darkening of the skin, so using sunscreen is crucial to protect your skin from UV damage and prevent hyperpigmentation, even indoors under the artificial lights. Maintaining a balanced diet rich in vitamins and antioxidants, staying hydrated, and avoiding harmful habits like smoking can also contribute to healthier, more radiant skin. If you have specific concerns about your skin's appearance or wish to address issues like uneven pigmentation, it's best to consult with a dermatologist. They can provide personalised advice and treatments tailored to your skin type and needs.

title: Fact Check: Can Rubbing Lemon with Vicks and Sugar Permanently Cure Knee Pain?
claim_text: Rubbing Lemon with Vicks and Sugar Permanently Cures Knee Pain. In the reel it is said, 'This is something every child should know. Back pain and knee pain of 100 years will disappear for the next 100 years. What you have to do is take one lemon, cut it in half, apply Vicks on it, and sprinkle sugar over it. After that, rub it on your knee. After 5 minutes, you will see that your knee pain has disappeared for 100 years.'
verdict_original: The claim is FALSE. Hence, the claim is FALSE.
doctor_explanation:
The claim is FALSE. This is a viral home remedy without any backing from clinical studies or medical guidelines. The components may offer temporary comfort but do not provide a cure, let alone a permanent one.

Knee pain refers to discomfort, stiffness, or soreness in or around the knee joint, which may result from injuries, overuse, arthritis, or underlying medical conditions. While some causes of knee pain are temporary and treatable, in many cases it can become chronic, persisting for months or even years.

Vicks VapoRub (VVR) is a medicated ointment formulated with active ingredients such as levomenthol, camphor, eucalyptus oil, and turpentine oil, along with thymol, cedarwood oil, and soft paraffin. It has a petroleum jelly base and is applied to the chest, throat, or back, or sometimes dissolved in hot water for inhalation. VVR is primarily used to relieve nasal congestion and help reduce coughing. There is no scientific evidence that rubbing lemon mixed with Vicks and sugar can permanently cure knee pain.

Lemon is a rich source of vitamin C and is known for therapeutic properties such as anti-inflammatory, antiviral, antioxidant, antidiabetic, and anti-ulcer benefits. However, no reviewed studies provide direct evidence for Vicks VapoRub in knee pain; they focus instead on topical analgesics as treatment options. According to Sheena Derry et al. (PubMed: 28497473), agents like diclofenac and ketoprofen are effective for acute and chronic musculoskeletal pain, including knee pain. Similarly, Jillian Maloney et al. (PubMed: 33534003) notes that topical NSAIDs may help with acute musculoskeletal pain and show some benefit in hand and knee osteoarthritis. However, Vicks VapoRub itself is not specifically studied for this purpose.

Dr Muhammed Nazeer, Senior Consultant & Group Coordinator, Department of Orthopedics & Trauma, KIMSHEALTH, Thiruvananthapuram, said: 'Home remedies can sometimes reduce discomfort, especially in mild or transient knee pain (e.g., after overuse). Products like Vicks (menthol/camphor) may help by creating a cooling/warming sensation, distracting the nerves from pain. Lemon might have some antioxidant effects. Sugar is unlikely to add benefit. But to claim a permanent cure is misleading. If the knee pain arises from arthritis, cartilage loss, ligament tear, meniscal injury, or alignment problems, you need proper medical evaluation—physiotherapy, possibly injections, or in some cases surgery. The home remedy may provide temporary relief of symptoms, but it won't reverse structural damage or halt progression.'

The viral claim that rubbing lemon with Vicks and sugar can permanently cure knee pain is false and misleading. At best, this mixture may provide temporary symptomatic relief due to the menthol and massage effect—but it is not a cure and cannot address underlying joint or tissue problems.

title: Can rubbing oil on the navel treat heart disease and more?
claim_text: The belly button is nature's pharmacy. Applying oils to the navel can treat various health conditions: mustard oil for heart health and eyesight, almond oil for joint pain and male fertility, tulsi oil for diabetes, castor oil for back pain and bone strength, and desi ghee for cracked heels and nerve stiffness.
quick_take: A popular Instagram post has been making bold claims about the healing powers of the belly button. According to this viral content, rubbing oil on the navel can treat heart disease and more. After fact checking, we found that this claim is false.
doctor_explanation:
Dr P. Rammanohar, Research Director at Amrita School of Ayurveda, explains that the idea of curing diseases by applying oils to the navel has no scientific basis and is not supported by classical Ayurvedic texts. He notes that although Ayurveda uses oils in treatments like massage, the belief that the navel serves as a healing centre for all health issues is not part of authentic Ayurvedic practice. The navel is essentially scar tissue from where the umbilical cord was attached before birth. Although some substances can be absorbed through skin, the navel isn't a direct gateway to your cardiovascular system as these claims suggest.

Regarding heart health claims: There's no scientific evidence supporting the claim that applying mustard oil to the navel strengthens the heart or improves blood circulation. While some traditional medicine systems use navel oiling practices, these remain largely anecdotal without clinical proof for treating serious conditions like heart disease.

Regarding joint pain and male fertility: Almond oil applied to the navel cannot reduce joint pain or boost semen and sexual strength. Joint pain ideally requires targeted medical evaluation and treatment, as it can stem from various causes including arthritis, injury, or inflammation. Male sexual health problems involve complex physiological and psychological factors that aren't addressed by topical oil application to the navel.

Regarding lip color: There's no direct scientific evidence that applying mustard oil to the navel makes dark lips pink. Lip color is determined by genetics, blood circulation, and melanin content.

Regarding diabetes: Putting tulsi (holy basil) oil in the navel cannot help control diabetes or reduce blood sugar. Holy basil does contain compounds that may help with blood sugar when consumed orally, but there's no scientific evidence that applying tulsi oil to the navel will manage diabetes. Diabetes is a serious medical condition requiring proper medical care, dietary management, and often medication or insulin therapy. Relying on navel oil application instead of proven treatments could be dangerous.

Regarding back pain and bone strength: Applying castor oil to the navel cannot relieve back pain or increase bone strength. Back pain usually results from musculoskeletal issues, nerve compression, or inflammation that require proper diagnosis and treatment. Bone strength depends on factors like bone density, calcium intake, exercise, and overall nutrition, not external oil application. While castor oil does have some anti-inflammatory properties when used topically, applying it to the navel isn't a recognized method for addressing systemic pain or bone health.

Regarding eyesight: No scientific evidence supports the claim that applying mustard oil to the navel improves eyesight. Vision and eye health involve complex optical and neurological systems. Eye problems require professional diagnosis and treatment by qualified eye care specialists. There's no known physiological mechanism by which oil applied to the navel could influence vision.

Regarding cracked heels and nerve stiffness: Dr Ekansh Shekhar, a Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant in Lucknow, says, "There's no scientific proof that putting desi ghee on your navel can heal cracked heels or stop stiffness in your veins or nerves. Cracked heels usually happen because of dry skin or too much pressure on your feet. The best way to treat them is by applying a good moisturiser directly to the heels. As for stiffness in veins or nerves, that's a medical issue and can't be fixed by oiling your belly button. While desi ghee can be nourishing when used on the skin, applying it to the navel won't send it to other parts of your body. It's always better to treat problems at the source, not through the navel." While ghee is indeed moisturising when applied directly to skin, there's no scientific evidence that navel application will heal cracked heels or address circulatory or neurological issues throughout the body.

title: Fact Check: Can Rubbing Tomato With Sugar Brighten the skin?

Tomatoes are rich in antioxidants like lycopene and β-carotene, carotenoids, phytosterols (β-sitosterol, campesterol, stigmasterol), and minerals, vitamins, proteins, and essential amino acids like leucine, threonine, and lysine. Lycopene has been associated with a lower risk of cancer, heart disease, cognitive disorders, and osteoporosis. The antioxidant compounds help neutralize reactive oxygen species, minimizing oxidative damage to cellular components. Consuming tomatoes may boost antioxidant defenses and reduce oxidative stress-related conditions.

Sugar is a carbohydrate including natural forms (glucose, fructose in fruits/vegetables) and refined forms (sucrose, HFCS). Natural sugars are essential for energy; refined sugars are highly processed and contribute to health concerns when consumed in excess.

Regarding the claim, tomato extracts have been studied for dermatological benefits. A study on tomato seed extract by Mrs. Vaishali Sorte et al. found multiple benefits including anti-aging effects, prevention of hyperpigmentation, regulation of sebum production, and improvement in skin brightness and pore tightness. A study in the Journal of Dermatologic Science and Cosmetic Technology found that continuous intake of tomato extract formulation over eight weeks significantly improved skin hydration and visibly brightened skin — but this was from oral consumption, not topical application. A study in the Journal of Cosmetics, Dermatological Sciences and Applications found that daily consumption (not topical application) of tomato seed extract may help maintain facial skin elasticity.

Dr. Varsha Rangari, Sr. Consultant - Dermatologist & Cosmetologist, Aditya Birla Memorial Hospital, said: "Tomato contains natural acids like citric and malic acid that can mildly exfoliate the skin, while sugar acts as a physical exfoliant. However, there is no scientific evidence that it's a substitute for scientifically formulated skincare products and should be used with caution, especially on sensitive skin. Also, one has to be careful about allergies to any of the ingredients."

Always patch test first, as natural ingredients can still cause irritation or allergic reactions. Further, there is no scientific evidence or medical consensus that it can be used to remove dead skin cells or brighten skin."

While tomatoes consumed orally (dietary intake) have documented skin benefits in scientific literature, the claim specifically refers to topical application of tomato with sugar on the face. No scientific evidence or medical consensus supports the claim that this topical mixture removes dead skin cells or visibly brightens the skin. The exfoliating effect of sugar combined with mild fruit acids may produce a temporary glow, but this is not equivalent to proven skin brightening or dead cell removal.

title: Fact Check: Can rubbing tomatoes naturally shrink pores?
claim_text: Rubbing a raw tomato slice on your face can naturally shrink pores and make your skin glow instantly.
quick_take: A social media post claims that rubbing tomatoes can naturally shrink pores. We did the fact check and found it to be mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Tomatoes cannot shrink pores. Pore size mainly depends on genetics, skin type, and age. Although some skincare products with active ingredients like retinoids or salicylic acid can minimise the appearance of pores, raw tomatoes lack such properties. Tomatoes contain antioxidants like lycopene and a mild acidic content, which may temporarily cleanse the skin or reduce oiliness. However, this effect does not reduce pore size. Dr Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant in Lucknow, says: "While tomatoes may have some minor benefits for the skin, such as being rich in antioxidants and having mild astringent properties, they cannot permanently shrink your pores. Pore size is mostly determined by genetics and other factors like age, and no home remedy, including tomatoes, can drastically change it. At best, applying tomato juice might temporarily tighten the skin, but the effect is short-lived. For long-lasting results or concerns about pores, it's best to seek advice from a dermatologist who can recommend effective treatments tailored to your needs." While tomatoes offer certain health benefits for the skin, exaggerated claims—such as tomato juice preventing heart attacks—lack scientific evidence and should not be taken seriously. For instant glow: while tomatoes contain Vitamin C, which can brighten skin over time, their effect is not instant. The perceived glow after using a tomato slice likely comes from the temporary hydration or residue left on the skin, which reflects light. This fades as the skin absorbs or dries the juice. Home remedies do not effectively reduce pores. Most home remedies, including those involving lemon, baking soda, or tomatoes, do not have scientifically proven effects on reducing pore size. Professional treatments like retinoids, chemical exfoliants, or lasers target collagen production and skin elasticity, which help pores appear smaller. Home remedies like clay masks and exfoliating scrubs can temporarily clean and unclog pores, improving skin texture, but they can't permanently reduce pore size or reverse ageing effects. For long-lasting results, professional treatments such as chemical peels, microdermabrasion, or laser therapy from a dermatologist are more effective options." There are risks in applying raw tomatoes to sensitive skin. The acids in tomatoes, such as citric acid, can irritate the skin, especially for individuals with conditions like rosacea or eczema. Overuse may disrupt the skin's natural pH balance, causing dryness or irritation. Additionally, tomatoes can cause severe allergies in some people. title: Fact Check: Can rubbing Warm Hands, Saliva, and Finger Motions correct Vision?
claim_text: Rubbing warm hands over the eyes, applying saliva, and performing circular finger motions around the eyes can get rid of glasses and correct vision.
quick_take: Eye exercises can reduce strain and improve focus, but actions like applying saliva, rubbing warm hands, or circular motions around the eyes cannot eliminate glasses or correct vision.
doctor_explanation: Saliva is a clear, slightly acidic secretion made up of fluids from both major and minor salivary glands. It plays a crucial role in maintaining oral health by providing lubrication and protection, buffering and clearing harmful substances, maintaining tooth integrity, exhibiting antibacterial properties, and aiding in taste and digestion. Additionally, human saliva can support skin wound healing by promoting the movement and growth of skin cells, reducing stress on damaged areas, and enhancing the inflammation necessary for repair. However, there is no scientific evidence to support the claim that applying saliva can improve vision or eliminate the need for eyeglasses. A study published in the Indian Journal of Ophthalmology found that eating tamarind candy for just 5 minutes can stimulate saliva production, which in turn helps improve tear film function and reduce dry eye symptoms — but the study does not discuss the direct application of saliva or its role in improving vision or helping to remove glasses. Refractive errors are vision problems that make it difficult to see clearly, occurring when the shape of the eye prevents light from focusing properly on the retina. They affect about 2.3 billion people worldwide and are the leading cause of visual impairment globally. Refractive errors include myopia (short-sightedness), hypermetropia (long-sightedness), and astigmatism (distorted vision). Eyeglasses are the most common, cost-effective, and effective method for correcting these errors. Dr Ashwin Santosh Shetty, Consultant – Ophthalmology, Aster CMI Hospital, Bangalore explained: 'There are multiple treatments for someone looking to reduce dependency on glasses and restore well-corrected vision. Refractive surgery is one of the safe and, most importantly corrective procedures, like LASIK, PRK or SMILE, address the reshaping of the cornea for improved visual acuity. In patients for whom laser surgery is not feasible, instead, an implantable contact lens is used, inserted into the patient's eyes in order to correct any kind of refractive error. Non-surgical, temporary orthokeratology, which involves wearing specialized lenses while sleeping at night for reshaping of the cornea, results in visual correction during the day, free of glasses.' He further stated: 'Even though these tricks may assist in easing the pain for a brief period of time, they are not directly meant for solving the underlying refractive errors from which the corrective lenses are required to be made. Indeed, most visual problems like myopia and hyperopia, or astigmatism are the results from the shape of the eyes or cornea, which may have caused malfunction and could not be corrected through external manipulation.' A study published in Risk Management and Healthcare Policy concluded that eye exercises can improve eye focus and reduce visual fatigue in children with myopia but do not reduce the severity of myopia itself. Another study published in the Journal of Indian System of Medicine found that eye and neck exercises effectively reduce eye strain and neck pain, relax eye muscles, and may improve vision and focus — however, it does not provide any evidence that eye-rolling exercises can lead to the removal of glasses. Dr. Sameer Kaushal, Head Ophthalmology, Organ Transplant, Artemis Hospitals, added: 'Science has proven that rubbing warm hands over the eyes, applying saliva, or performing circular finger motions around the eyes does not correct vision or eliminate the glasses requirement. Temporary relief or relaxation may occur, but it does nothing to reverse the conditions that bring about refractive errors, including nearsightedness and farsightedness or astigmatism. Rubbing warm hands across the eyes can stimulate the flow of blood in the eyes and help reduce pressure after prolonged screen time or eye strain. Applying saliva to the eyes, often thought to be a traditional remedy, is not advisable. Saliva carries bacteria that may cause infections or irritate the sensitive tissues of the eye. While such practices could enhance comfort and minimise strain, they cannot act as alternatives for evidence-based treatments, including glasses, contact lenses, or surgical options such as LASIK or PRK.' Dr. Ishan Kataria, MBBS, Medical College Bilaspur, MS Ophthalmology, Dr. Vasantrao Pawar Medical College, Hospital & Research Centre, also shared his views: 'Rubbing gently only helps our muscles to relax and nothing related to refractive error correction. Rather rubbing too frequently can cause a change in the cylindrical correction of particular individuals especially in children.'

title: Fact Check: Can salt cure dizziness, headaches, and brain fog?
claim_text: Salt can resolve numerous health problems including dizziness, lack of energy, headaches, brain fog, and poor focus. A lack of salt in the body affects quality of life.
quick_take: A social media post claims that salt can cure dizziness, headaches and brain fog. However, our fact check says this is false.
doctor_explanation: Salt plays an important role in maintaining overall health. Sodium, a key component of salt, is important for several vital functions. However, salt is not a miracle solution for everything. While it's an essential mineral, it does not act as a cure for the wide range of health problems mentioned in the claim. Conditions like dizziness, brain fog, or fatigue can have many different causes, and salt alone is unlikely to resolve them. Many of these symptoms are often linked to lifestyle factors like poor diet, dehydration, lack of sleep, stress, or underlying medical conditions. Dr Ubaid ur Rahman, General Physician, Holy Mission Clinic, New Delhi, shares his opinion on excessive salt intake: "Excessive salt consumption is a significant risk factor for developing high blood pressure, which can increase the likelihood of heart disease and stroke. Moderation is key to maintaining cardiovascular health." Deepalakshmi Sriram, Registered Dietitian at The Cleft & Craniofacial Centre and Sree Balaji Medical College & Hospital, Chennai, offers her expertise: "Sodium is crucial for vital functions like fluid balance and nerve health, but too much salt can disrupt this balance, leading to issues such as fluid retention and digestive discomfort. Striking the right balance in salt intake is essential for overall health and well-being, helping to prevent complications like high blood pressure and long-term cardiovascular risks." While sodium deficiency (hyponatremia) can cause serious health problems, this condition is relatively rare and usually occurs in extreme cases such as excessive sweating, vomiting, or diarrhoea. The average person is unlikely to suffer from hyponatremia due to low salt intake in daily life. Excess salt intake can be harmful - the World Health Organization advises adults to limit sodium intake to under 2,000 mg per day (approximately 5 grams of salt) to reduce the risk of high blood pressure. A balanced diet with adequate hydration, daily exercise, and stress management is the best approach to improving overall health and well-being. Persistent symptoms should be assessed by a medical professional rather than relying on quick fixes like salt.

title: Fact Check: Can salt cure Keloid scars? - THIP Media
claim_text: Sea salt on keloid scars can help cure it within 3-4 days
quick_take: A YouTube video suggests that sea salt on keloid scars can help cure it. The video claims that sea salt can cure the keloid scars in 3-4 days. We did the fact check and found it to be false.
doctor_explanation: Keloids are abnormal skin formations that occur when skin doesn't heal properly after being injured or inflamed. They develop due to a combination of genetic factors and environmental influences. Individuals with darker skin tones, particularly those of African, Asian, or Hispanic backgrounds, are more prone to keloids. The underlying cause of keloids is an overproduction of collagen and other substances by certain skin cells. Doctors can observe these cells by examining a small sample of skin under a microscope. Keloids typically feel like hard, rubbery lumps at the site of previous skin injury. Unlike regular scars, keloids have the tendency to extend beyond the original injury site. They can also be accompanied by discomfort such as pain, itching, or a burning sensation. While there are various treatment options available for keloids, none of them are universally effective. Using sea salt on keloid scars is not a recommended or proven method. Unfortunately, some home remedies suggest applying sea salt paste for keloid scars to promote healing. But, there is no scientific evidence to support its effectiveness. In fact, applying sea salt directly on keloid scars can cause irritation and may even worsen the condition. Dr Saumya Sachdeva (Dermatologist) for her expert opinion. She says, 'No, sea salt does not cure any hypertrophic scar or keloid scar. Rather, it would irritate the skin leading to a chance for contact dermatitis.' We strongly advise anyone with keloids to consult with a physician for proper treatment. These may include medical interventions such as steroid injections, surgical removal, laser therapy, or silicone gel sheets. Always seek guidance from a qualified healthcare provider before trying any home remedies or alternative treatments for keloids. People may choose home remedies like sea salt paste for keloid scars for various reasons. Some individuals prefer natural or alternative approaches over conventional medical treatments. Home remedies such as aspirin and sea salt paste for keloid scars are still prevalent due to the fact that they are much more easily accessible. DIY methods are often seen as more accessible, affordable, and convenient than seeking professional medical care. Additionally, cultural or familial beliefs may influence someone's decision to use traditional remedies passed down through generations. However, it's important to note that these home remedies may offer temporary relief or symptom management. But, they may not effectively address the underlying cause of keloids or provide long-term solutions. Unfortunately there's no fast way to cure Keloids. Claims like sea salt on keloid scars can treat it in 3-4 days is baseless. But, you can apply one or a combination of following methods for an effective approach: It's important to remember that recurrence rates for keloids are high, regardless of treatment method. Home remedies like sea salt on Keloid scars will make matters worse. Or, in case they do provide a temporary relief it will increase the chances of recurrence really high. So, choose only the medically approved methods to prevent a keloid.

title: Fact Check: Can Sambar prevent colon cancer?
claim_text: Consuming Sambar, a popular South Indian dish, can prevent colon cancer due to its ingredients like turmeric and drumsticks.
quick_take: An article claims that Sambar can prevent colon cancer. Our fact check found no strong evidence to support this claim, so we rate it as Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: Sambar has health benefits, but not as a cure or prevention for cancer. Sambar is a traditional South Indian dish made from lentils, vegetables, and spices like turmeric, which are known for their nutritional value. Lentils are rich in protein and fibre, which support digestion and overall health. Vegetables in Sambar add vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants to the diet. Even though these components contribute to a balanced diet, they do not specifically prevent or cure colon cancer. There is no scientific evidence that consuming Sambar, or any specific dish, can cure cancer. Cancer treatment requires medical interventions such as surgery, chemotherapy, radiation, or targeted therapy. A healthy diet, including dishes like Sambar, can support overall well-being. However, it is not a substitute for professional medical treatment. The spices in Sambar, like turmeric, do contain compounds like curcumin that have been studied for their potential benefits. But, the research is still in early stages, and the quantities you would consume in a serving of Sambar are too small to have a significant impact (poor bioavailability). Colon cancer prevention is more complex, involving a mix of regular screenings, a balanced diet rich in fibre, and other healthy lifestyle habits. A 2016 study suggests that Sambar might offer some protection against colon cancer in a preclinical setting. Researchers found that Sambar reduced certain cancer markers in rats exposed to a chemical that induces colon cancer. However, this was an animal study, not human. We need more research to confirm if these results apply to people. While the findings are interesting, they don't prove that Sambar can prevent colon cancer in humans. Dr Pooja Khullar, Radiation Oncologist from Dharamshila Narayana Super Speciality Hospital, New Delhi says: 'The idea of a dish like Sambar preventing colon cancer is appealing. But, it's important to understand that there's no concrete scientific evidence backing this claim. Turmeric, a key ingredient in Sambar, has been studied for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, and curcumin, the active compound in turmeric, does show some promise in laboratory settings. However, the amount of curcumin you'd get from a serving of Sambar is minimal, and its low bioavailability means your body absorbs very little of it. Cancer prevention is a complex process that involves regular screenings, a balanced diet, and healthy lifestyle choices. Simply eating a particular dish, no matter how healthy, isn't enough to prevent a disease as complex as cancer.' Dr Sharad Malhotra, Senior Consultant & HOD Gastroenterology Hepatology & Therapeutic Endoscopy at Aakash Healthcare, New Delhi states: 'Sambar is a nutritious and wholesome dish that many enjoy as part of a balanced diet, but it shouldn't be seen as a shield against colon cancer. The spices and ingredients in Sambar, such as turmeric, drumsticks, and fenugreek, are certainly beneficial for health in general, contributing to good digestion and providing essential nutrients. However, the claim that Sambar can specifically prevent colon cancer oversimplifies the issue. Colon cancer risk is influenced by a combination of factors, including diet, genetics, and lifestyle. While a diet high in fibre, fruits, and vegetables can help lower your risk, it's important to complement this with regular medical check-ups and screenings, especially if you have a family history of the disease.' Curcumin is a compound found in turmeric. Curcumin has been studied for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. Some research suggests that curcumin may have a role in preventing certain diseases, including cancer. However, the effectiveness of curcumin in cancer prevention is still being studied, and it is not a proven treatment. The bioavailability of curcumin, meaning how well the body can absorb and use it, is also low, especially when consumed in small amounts as part of a dish like Sambar. The amount of curcumin in a typical serving of Sambar is likely too small to have a significant impact. Moreover, curcumin's low bioavailability means that even less of it reaches the bloodstream, reducing its potential effectiveness. Therefore, relying on Sambar or any other food containing curcumin for cancer prevention is not advisable.

title: Can Sanyasi Ayurveda weight gain medicine help with fast and safe weight gain?
claim_text: A Facebook post claims that Sanyasi Ayurveda weight gain medicine can make your digestive system healthy, boost nutrient absorption, and help you gain weight within 15 days, without side effects. It also says that it is safe for everyone, regardless of age and gender.
quick_take: A widely circulated social media post claims that Sanyasi Ayurveda weight gain medicine can improve digestion, help the body absorb all nutrients, and lead to visible weight gain within 15 days, without any side effects. After fact checking, we have rated this claim as mostly false.
doctor_explanation: **What is inside Sanyasi Ayurveda weight gain medicine?** A mix of digestive herbs and salts, but not all are risk-free. The product label and website only mention key ingredients, not a full list, which raises transparency concerns. Based on available information, Sanyasi Ayurveda weight gain medicine contains ingredients like nausadar, baheda, kala namak, lahori namak, narkachoor, kali harar, amla, tej patta, and sanay leaves. Some of these, like amla, baheda, and kali harar, are commonly used in Ayurveda to support digestion and are generally considered safe in moderate amounts. Tej patta (bay leaf) and kala namak (black salt) also have mild digestive benefits. However, others require caution. Nausadar (ammonium chloride), while used traditionally to aid digestion, can cause stomach irritation and affect electrolyte balance if taken in excess. Sanay leaves (senna) act as a strong herbal laxative. Regular or long-term use can lead to dependency and disrupt natural bowel movements. In rare cases, it can lead to liver damage. There is no detailed explanation of quantities, combinations, or scientific testing provided. Without this, it's hard to judge the product's overall safety or long-term effects. Like any Ayurvedic medicine for weight gain, it should not be used without medical advice, especially in people with underlying health conditions. **Is Sanyasi Ayurveda safe for long-term use?** Not always. While some herbs are safe when used correctly, there have been cases where Ayurvedic products were found to contain heavy metals or undeclared steroids. Although promotional videos claim that weight gain medicine is safe for everyone, the website suggests otherwise. It clearly advises against its use in people with heart problems, kidney issues, liver conditions like hepatitis or psoriasis, cancer, asthma, epilepsy, high blood pressure, and in pregnant or breastfeeding women. This indicates that the product may not be as universally safe as advertised. Moreover, the brand also advises people with diabetes, tuberculosis, ulcers, and several other conditions to consult a doctor before use, especially if they have undergone surgery in the past 1 to 1.5 years. These precautions raise valid safety concerns. Yet, no detailed list of ingredients or known Sanyasi Ayurveda side effects is provided on the packaging or website. This lack of transparency makes it difficult to judge whether long-term use is truly safe. **Can Ayurvedic remedies really boost digestion and nutrient absorption?** Sometimes, but not always. Some Ayurvedic herbs may support digestion. For example, trikatu (a mix of black pepper, long pepper, and ginger) is traditionally used to boost appetite and aid digestion. However, this does not mean that everyone who takes it will absorb all nutrients better or gain weight. Nutrient absorption is a complex process, affected by many factors such as gut health, existing deficiencies, food intake, and underlying conditions. No herbal formula has been scientifically proven to fix all these in just 15 days. Dr Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition, says, 'Ayurvedic remedies can support digestion for some people, especially when used alongside healthy eating habits. Herbs like trikatu, ashwagandha and amla have long been used to improve appetite and gut function. Some people do feel better when they use these along with a nutritious diet. But it's important to understand that not all Ayurvedic remedies work the same way for everyone, and we don't have strong scientific studies for many of them yet. So while they may help as part of a holistic routine, they shouldn't replace medical advice or a balanced diet based on individual needs.' **Why does rapid weight gain raise safety concerns?** Because it can harm your body. Gaining weight too quickly, especially through supplements, can stress the liver, kidneys, and heart. Most doctors and nutritionists recommend gradual and healthy weight gain through a balanced diet, protein intake, strength training, and medical guidance if needed. If a product promises visible results in 15 days, it may be using misleading language, or worse, may include hidden steroids or synthetic substances, something seen in many so-called 'herbal' products. Shruti K Bhardwaj, Chief Clinical Nutritionist at Zydus Hospital, Ahmedabad, explains, 'Gaining weight too quickly can put unnecessary pressure on your body. It may seem like a good thing if someone is underweight, but rapid weight gain can lead to fat being stored in unhealthy areas, such as around the liver or abdomen. This increases the risk of insulin resistance, high blood pressure, and poor metabolic health. Even if you're aiming to gain weight, the goal should be to build muscle and improve strength, not just add fat. A healthy, gradual approach supported by a balanced diet, strength training, and proper sleep works much better in the long run.' **What does the Sanyasi Ayurveda weight gain review community say?** Mixed and often unverified. The product's page mentions no reviews. When we searched online, the reviews of Sanyasi Ayurveda weight gain medicine are inconsistent. Some users report feeling more energetic or hungrier, while others say they noticed no changes or developed mild side effects. However, most of these reviews are individual customer opinions, anecdotal and lack medical verification. A proper Sanyasi Ayurveda weight gain review should be based on objective studies, which are currently missing. There are no clearly listed Sanyasi Ayurveda side effects on the official website, which is concerning. Every medicine or supplement, no matter how well tolerated, can have some side effects, and it is important to disclose them for safe use. Similarly, there is another product called Fitness Plus that can guarantee effective weight gain. However this is false. In summary, there is no solid scientific evidence that Sanyasi Ayurveda weight gain medicine can boost digestion, improve nutrient absorption, or help all users gain visible weight in 15 days. The claim that it has no side effects and works for everyone is unverified and medically unsound.

title: Can sauf, ajwain, and dalchini help melt tummy fat in 7 days?
claim_text: An Instagram post suggests that roasting and grinding fennel seeds (sauf), carom seeds (ajwain), and cinnamon (dalchini), then drinking the mixture with lukewarm water each morning, can melt belly fat in just one week.
quick_take: A social media post claims that sauf, ajwain and dalchini can melt tummy fat in 7 days. We fact checked and found the claim to be false.
doctor_explanation: Fat loss doesn't work like that. When the body needs energy, it draws from stored fat, but this only happens if you're consistently burning more calories than you eat. This is known as a calorie deficit. No herb, spice, or drink can override this fundamental rule of biology. Even if you drink litres of cinnamon tea or chew fennel seeds after every meal, you won't shed fat unless your overall diet and activity level create the right conditions. At best, what you may notice is reduced bloating or water retention, which can make your stomach look a little flatter. But that's very different from losing actual belly fat. Fat loss is slow and steady. According to research, a safe and realistic rate is about 0.5 to 1 kg per week with proper diet and exercise, and even that is from the whole body, not just the tummy. Spices simply cannot produce that result alone. Dermatologist Dr Jyothy Kannangath explains that there's no shortcut to losing belly fat - effective options include adopting lifestyle changes or undergoing procedures like liposuction, or exploring cryolipolysis. If you have concerns, always ask your doctor for the correct guidance. Nutritionist Umesh Wadhavani highlights that no single food determines or prevents chronic health issues. Rather, overall health is shaped by a mix of factors like diet, daily habits, work-related stress, relationships, sleep quality, and exercise. Depending on a herbal preparation for fat loss is not recommended. Some research has looked at the effects of spices on metabolism. Cinnamon, for instance, has been studied for its potential to regulate blood sugar and insulin sensitivity. When blood sugar levels are stable, it may help prevent overeating. Ajwain has thymol, which can support digestion and may create a mild warming effect in the body. Fennel is sometimes linked to appetite suppression because of certain essential oils. But these effects are tiny - they might slightly help your body process food better or burn a few more calories, but the impact is so small it's barely noticeable in day-to-day life. One brisk 30-minute walk will burn far more calories than any spice can. There are no scientific trials proving 7-day fat loss with these spices. When researchers test the impact of spices like cinnamon, ajwain, or fennel, they typically look at blood sugar regulation, digestion, or appetite suppression. Even then, results are mixed and usually modest. Some trials suggest cinnamon supplementation over several weeks may help with blood sugar in people with diabetes. Others find fennel extracts can reduce appetite in small groups of women. But none of these studies show rapid belly fat loss, let alone within seven days. Clinical trials that do examine fat loss always combine dietary changes, exercise, and sometimes supplements, not spices alone. Real fat loss takes weeks to months, not days. Dr P. Rammanohar, Research Director at the Amrita Centre for Advanced Research in Ayurveda (ĀCĀRA), explains that Ayurveda considers obesity one of the most difficult conditions to treat. Classical texts even describe it as almost incurable, captured in the saying Karshyameva varam sthaulyat na hi sthoolasya bheshajam meaning it is better to remain lean than to gain extra weight, since effective medicines for obesity are limited. There are no quick fixes, and neither internal remedies nor external therapies can solve the problem on their own. Ayurveda focuses on stress management, lifestyle adjustments, and a personalised diet, with medicines playing only a supportive role. Believing that a handful of seeds or a cup of spiced tea can melt fat often leads people to ignore the basics of health: balanced eating, regular movement, good sleep, and stress management. This is where misinformation becomes dangerous. spices can be part of this overall picture - they can add flavour without extra calories, support digestion, and in some cases curb mild hunger. But on their own, they are not fat-loss solutions.

title: Fact Check: Can saunf, adrak, ajwain, jeera, daalchini drink cure PCOD in 10 days?
claim_text: A drink made from saunf (fennel seeds), adrak (ginger), ajwain (carom seeds), jeera (cumin seeds), and daalchini (cinnamon) can cure PCOD (Polycystic Ovarian Disease) in just 10 days, regulate irregular periods, fix hormonal imbalance, thyroid issues, no egg formation, and support conception — by consuming it daily on an empty stomach for a month.
quick_take: The claim that a drink made from saunf, adrak, ajwain, jeera, and daalchini can cure PCOD in 10 days is entirely false. Some ingredients like cinnamon and fennel seeds may provide minor symptomatic relief, but PCOD is a chronic endocrine condition that needs sustained medical, nutritional, and lifestyle intervention and can be only managed and not cured.
doctor_explanation:
PCOD (Polycystic Ovarian Disease) is a chronic condition primarily caused by hormonal imbalances and genetic factors. In a typical menstrual cycle, the ovaries release mature eggs ready for fertilization. However, in PCOD, the ovaries often release immature or partially matured eggs, which may develop into fluid-filled cysts, causing the ovaries to become enlarged and swollen. PCOD is also associated with an excess production of androgens (male hormones), leading to symptoms such as irregular periods, weight gain around the abdomen, thinning hair in a male-like pattern, and in some cases, infertility. According to UNICEF, PCOD is not curable due to its hormonal and genetic basis; however, its symptoms can be well-controlled through lifestyle changes including a balanced diet, regular physical activity, and stress reduction techniques. While some individual ingredients in the herbal drink may offer minor supportive benefits, there is no scientific evidence that a combination of saunf, adrak, ajwain, jeera, and daalchini can cure PCOD — let alone within 10 days.

Dr Rajni Bagai, Consultant - Gynaecology & Obstetrics, Narayana Hospital, Howrah & Chunavati said: 'Studies done on the effect of cinnamon, fennel, cumin, carom, ginger etc on obesity and PCOS have involved small numbers of patients, which makes the statistical validity dubious. While cinnamon and ginger have been associated with decreased insulin resistance, fennel seeds with increased oestrogen levels, ginger with anti-inflammatory properties and carom (ajwain) with combined hormonal effects, dosages have not been defined and there are no studies showing that these will cure PCOD in a short time such as 10 days.'

Dr Upasana Palo, Consultant, Gynaecologic Oncology and Robotic Surgery, Narayana Hospital RN Tagore Hospital further added: 'PCOD has become one of the greatest concerns in women's life which greatly affects their health and fertility. It may cause several health complications such as irregular menstruation, obesity, infertility, obstructive sleep apnea, acne and cardiovascular diseases. Several factors may contribute to the pathogenesis of PCOD such as insulin resistance, obesity, and sympathetic stimulation. Several studies evidenced that several Indian spices including E. cardamomum play a crucial role in the management of PCOS and associated symptoms. It is suggested that PCOD patient should consume a high protein diet that is present in most of the spices. A balanced healthy diet with regular exercise and lifestyle modification is essential in PCOD. However, it is also suggested that spices may decrease insulin resistance, regulate the menstrual cycle, improve lipid profile, and also decrease weight in PCOS patients. However, they alone cannot cure PCOD in just 10 days as it can be only managed and not cured.'

Emerging research does point to some potential supportive benefits of individual ingredients: A study by Shabnam Omidvar et al. found that fennel seeds (saunf) can effectively help reduce pain and discomfort during periods. A systematic review and meta-analysis by Fatemeh Heydarpour et al. indicates that cinnamon supplementation may help improve metabolic parameters in women with PCOD. However, these individual supportive effects do not constitute a cure, and no combination remedy has been shown to cure PCOD in any timeframe, let alone 10 days.

title: Fact Check: Can saunf, tulsi, laung, elaichi, and gud drink cure piles in a week?
claim_text: "The thing that even surgery couldn't fix, this ₹2 drink cured completely from the root within a week. If someone in your household, family or among your relatives has bawasir (piles) and it is not getting better, then definitely try this remedy. For this, take one cup of water in a pan and add one teaspoon of fennel seeds, a few tulsi (basil) leaves, four to five cloves, two cardamom pods and a piece of jaggery; boil it well for 10 minutes, then strain it and drink it every morning on an empty stomach. This will cure even the most stubborn piles within a week. This is a very effective remedy. It will work 100%."
doctor_explanation:
There is no scientific evidence that a mixture of fennel (saunf), tulsi (holy basil), clove (laung), cardamom (elaichi) and jaggery (gud) can cure piles (hemorrhoids) in just one week. Although fennel, tulsi leaves, clove, and cardamom contain anti-inflammatory properties that may help reduce inflammation, they cannot shrink hemorrhoidal veins or cure piles within a week. According to an article by Dr. Shaikh Mohd Naeem Rafiuddin et al., piles are strongly linked to diet, lifestyle, and medical care. Adopting a fiber-rich diet, proper hydration, and regular physical activity can effectively control mild cases, whereas more severe stages often necessitate medical treatments such as rubber band ligation or sclerotherapy. Of the available options, minimally invasive techniques are generally more effective and preferred, while surgery is usually reserved for the most advanced cases.

Dr. Sanoop Koshy Zachariah, Senior Consultant and Professor, Department of General and Minimally Invasive Surgery, KIMSHEALTH Trivandrum, said: "No, saunf (fennel seeds), tulsi (holy basil) leaves, and elaichi (cardamom) with gud (jaggery) cannot cure piles (hemorrhoids) within a week. Piles are swollen veins in the rectum or anus, usually caused by chronic constipation, straining, or other factors. They do not disappear simply with home remedies in such a short time. Saunf, tulsi, and elaichi with gud may aid digestion, reduce bloating, and mildly ease constipation, which can help relieve some symptoms like burning or discomfort. The patient may feel symptomatically better, but these remedies do not shrink or eliminate hemorrhoids. A proper medical evaluation is necessary, especially to rule out other possible causes, including cancer."

Dr. Manish Dodmani, Consultant, Medical Gastroenterology, KIMS Hospitals, Thanef, further added: "Many people are under the impression that some natural ingredients, like saunf (fennel), tulsi leaves, laung (clove), elaichi (cardamom), and gud (jaggery), will help you cure piles within a week. While some of these or a combination of these natural ingredients may provide some relief, there is not enough time to fully cure a condition like piles. Natural ingredients can help digestion, relieve inflammation, and relieve constipation. It's true that piles can bring some degree of discomfort or pain, and any of the natural ingredients discussed can be of some assistance. Fennel and cardamom help the stomach in digestion; tulsi and clove have soothing elements, and jaggery in moderation can help soften stool. Certainly these ingredients may help to make a bowel movement more pleasant and less straining; but the bulk of issues with piles is typically from long-standing causes including constipation or long periods of sitting. Long-standing lifestyle changes take time and share in prevention and healing of piles, but overall any help or assistance is a net positive to improving comfort. Natural ingredients are helpful in the healing process, and certainly help digestion and comfort. If you want to experience lasting relief and healing from piles the real change is built into the fiber you eat, the amount of water and hydration you have, and then habits you develop over time."
