title: Fact Check: Can Scarf Stretch fix Cervical Pain?
claim_text: A scarf stretch (wrapping a scarf/chunni behind the neck with ends pulled under armpits, applying pressure between shoulder blades) can cure cervical pain and cervical spondylosis with regular practice.
quick_take: While the scarf stretch may provide brief relief for muscular tightness in the neck, there is no scientific evidence or medical consensus supporting its use to cure cervical pain permanently or recommending it as a first-line treatment. In some cases, it could cause harm if used inappropriately.
doctor_explanation:
The claim that a scarf stretch can cure cervical pain is HALF TRUE. While some evidence suggests that neck stretching may help relieve cervical pain, there is no scientific evidence or medical consensus supporting the claim that using a scarf stretch can cure cervical pain permanently. In fact, if used inappropriately, scarf stretching may even cause harm.

WHAT IS CERVICAL PAIN: Cervical pain (Cervical radiculopathy), often referred to as a 'pinched nerve,' occurs when a nerve in the neck is compressed or irritated where it exits the spinal cord. This can lead to pain radiating into the shoulder or arm, as well as muscle weakness and numbness. In most cases, cervical pain is caused by degenerative changes in the spine, such as arthritis, that develop with age. However, in younger individuals, it is typically due to a sudden injury that results in a herniated disc.

LIMITED EVIDENCE FOR STRETCHING: The 'scarf stretch' may offer temporary relief for mild muscular tension in the neck, but there is no scientific evidence that it treats underlying causes of cervical pain, such as nerve compression, disc problems, or chronic conditions. Neck exercises may help reduce cervical pain and improve neck function. In a study by Bryan G. Anderson et. al., young adults who followed a six-week neck stretching and strengthening routine experienced better neck strength, increased movement, and less pain. Further, findings from the study by Seung Kyu Park et. al. demonstrated that cranio-cervical exercises effectively improved muscle function and posture in patients with cervicogenic headaches, which are caused by issues in the cervical spine. Therapeutic interventions may also play a key role in managing cervical spondylosis. Robert Haładaj et. al.'s study found that both therapeutic approaches such as Saunders device and high-intensity laser therapy enhanced functional performance and provided pain relief in patients with cervical spondylosis, both immediately after treatment and over the medium term.

DR. KIRAN LINGUTLA'S ASSESSMENT: Dr. Kiran Lingutla, Clinical Director & Sr. Consultant, Orthopaedic Spine Surgeon, CARE Hospitals, Banjara Hills, Hyderabad, said, 'Well, scarf stretch of upper back can correct the posture for a temporary period and give you some amount of symptom relief. However, it is advisable that you maintain an adequate posture when you are sitting and standing so that your spine is erect and your head is in neutral position. And In this position, there is less amount of stress on the muscles of your upper back and they tend to get tired less easily. So, I would suggest that when you are walking or when you are sitting, you have to maintain an erect posture, maintain your back upright, and keep exercising. One of which is a yoga Surya Namaskar exercise which is very beneficial for your back which provides excellent range of movement exercises in all the segments from the neck to the lower back.'

DR. BRAHMARAJU T J'S ASSESSMENT: Dr. Brahmaraju T J, Sr Consultant - Orthopaedics & Joint Replacement Surgery, Gleneagles, BGS Hospital Kengeri, Bengaluru, added, 'In cervical spondylolysis usually the joint and muscles become inflamed and undergo stiffness. Patient feels stiffness and pain around the neck and shoulder blade region. So the common treatment followed by an orthopedic surgeon is to prescribe medication which reduce the inflammation and relaxes the muscle and once the pain relief is there we ask them to do stretching of the neck joints and strengthening of the neck and shoulder muscles. So, we teach them standard stipulated exercises. If you ask me whether scarf stretching is a relief for cervical spondylosis, this is another form of stretching of the neck muscles, but this is done by another person rather than the patient himself. So, this can give a temporary relief for the patient, but not a permanent relief. And this cannot be done on a day-to-day basis. So, it is better to follow stipulated standard exercises for keeping the muscles and joints stretched rather than depending on scarf stretchers.'

CONCLUSION: It can be concluded that stretching may help relieve cervical pain; however, there is no scientific evidence or medical consensus to support the claim that scarf stretching can cure cervical pain.

title: Fact Check: Can sea buckthorn prevent cancer forever?
claim_text: A social media post claims that consuming sea buckthorn can prevent cancer forever and eliminate all illnesses from the body. The caption reads: 'Willing to prevent Cancer Forever and reverse illnesses in your body????' The post promotes a sea buckthorn juice product as a preventive solution for all diseases, including cancer, immune system issues, and common illnesses like colds and flu.
quick_take: A social media post claims that sea buckthorn can prevent cancer forever and other illnesses too. We fact checked this claim and found it to be false.
doctor_explanation: There is no scientific evidence to support the claim that sea buckthorn can prevent cancer forever. Sea buckthorn is a nutrient-rich fruit packed with antioxidants, vitamins (such as C and E), and omega fatty acids, making it beneficial for health. Antioxidants help neutralise harmful free radicals, potentially reducing cell damage. It also contains quercetin, a flavonoid with anticancer properties, and carotenoids, which may offer some protection against cancer when combined with a healthy lifestyle. A 2018 study found that sea buckthorn has antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer properties. It may support the immune system and help counteract chemotherapy side effects. However, its medicinal and preventive doses are unknown, and no clinical trials have been conducted—only in vivo (on animals) and in vitro (in the lab) studies exist. We need more research to confirm its effects. Despite these findings, no research confirms that consuming sea buckthorn alone can prevent or cure cancer. Cancer is a complex disease with multiple causes, including genetic and environmental factors. Relying on a single food or supplement for prevention is misleading and unsupported by medical science. Dr Pooja Khullar, Radiation Oncologist at Dharamshila Narayana Super Speciality Hospital, New Delhi, says, 'It's important to clarify that no single food, including sea buckthorn, can prevent cancer entirely. Cancer prevention requires a holistic approach, including a balanced diet rich in fruits and vegetables, regular exercise, avoiding carcinogens, quitting smoking and alcohol, limiting long-term sun exposure, and undergoing timely medical screenings. People should focus on overall health and consult medical professionals for expert guidance.' Dr P. Rammanohar, Research Director at Amrita School of Ayurveda, explains, 'Cancer is a complex disease with different types, and no single remedy can prevent or cure it. While some studies suggest that certain herbs or plants may have anticancer properties, there is not enough scientific evidence to use them as treatments or sole preventive measures. Without proper human studies, relying on such claims can be misleading.' Regarding the claim that sea buckthorn can reverse all illnesses: sea buckthorn cannot reverse all illnesses in the body. While it has nutritional benefits, including anti-inflammatory properties and potential support for skin and digestive health, it does not have the ability to reverse all diseases. Claims suggesting that it can eliminate any illness lack scientific credibility. Chronic diseases such as diabetes, cardiovascular conditions, and autoimmune disorders require proper medical treatment and lifestyle management. Scientific studies highlight that sea buckthorn has potential health benefits due to its high content of bioactive compounds. It may support skin health, help in digestion, and contribute to heart health. However, no credible health organisation has endorsed sea buckthorn as a cure or preventive measure for cancer. Misleading health claims like this can be harmful. Promoting a single food as a guaranteed way to prevent cancer may steer people away from proven prevention strategies, such as regular screenings, a balanced diet, physical activity, and avoiding tobacco and excessive alcohol. When people believe in such claims, they may delay or even avoid proper medical treatments, which can have serious consequences for their health. In summary, although sea buckthorn is a nutrient-rich fruit with health benefits, there is no scientific proof that it can prevent or cure cancer.

title: Can sea buckthorn really make you young and beautiful?
claim_text: Sea buckthorn is a powerful fruit that can improve skin, boost immunity, aid weight loss, improve eyesight, support digestion, and make you look younger and more beautiful.
quick_take: A social media post suggests using sea buckthorn for skin. The post claims that it can make you young and beautiful. After fact-checking, we found that the claim is mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Sea buckthorn is a small orange berry found in parts of Europe and Asia. It's rich in vitamin C, vitamin E, flavonoids (plant-based antioxidants), and healthy fats from the seeds and pulp. In traditional Tibetan and Chinese medicine, it's used in some remedies, mainly for skin treatments and digestion. But calling it the "most powerful fruit" is an overstatement. Many fruits like berries, amla, and citrus also offer similar or more nutritional benefits. Sea buckthorn for skin care is becoming increasingly popular, and sea buckthorn oil is sometimes used in skincare products. It contains omega-7 and vitamin E, which may help improve skin hydration and reduce dryness. Some lab and animal studies suggest antioxidant properties that might protect the skin from damage, and there's growing interest in sea buckthorn anti-aging benefits due to its rich nutrient profile. A 2018 study suggests that sea buckthorn seed oil shows promise as a natural ingredient for sun protection, as it helps prevent UV-induced damage to skin cells by improving their antioxidant defenses and lipid metabolism. However, there's no strong scientific proof that eating sea buckthorn or drinking its juice can make human skin glow or look visibly younger. While sea buckthorn for skin health shows promise, a healthy diet and proper skincare matter far more. Research into sea buckthorn and collagen production is still in early stages, though some studies suggest its nutrients may support skin structure. Dr Sachin Gupta, Senior Consultant Dermatologist at Amrita Hospital, Faridabad says, "As dermatologists, we often hear if sea buckthorn juice magically makes skin glow or look younger. The truth is, while it's packed with great nutrients for skin health, like vitamins and good fats, no single juice works miracles. For truly radiant, youthful skin, it's about the whole picture: a balanced diet, sun protection, a consistent skincare routine, and a healthy lifestyle. Think of the juice as a helpful boost to your efforts, not a standalone solution." Regarding eyesight: Sea buckthorn contains vitamin A (beta-carotene), which is crucial for good vision. The post claims it has "3x more Vitamin A than carrots," but this can vary depending on the specific variety and preparation. While vitamin A is essential for eye health and preventing certain vision problems, there's no strong scientific evidence to suggest that consuming sea buckthorn will significantly "improve eyesight" beyond what a balanced diet provides, especially for individuals with healthy vision. Dr Isha Agarwalla, Consultant Ophthalmologist from Drishti Netralaya, Assam explains, "From an ophthalmologist's perspective, while sea buckthorn is beneficial due to its Vitamin A and omegas that support overall eye health and can help with dry eyes, it's not a magical fix for improving eyesight beyond what a balanced diet provides. Maintaining good vision requires a comprehensive approach, including regular eye exams and UV protection, not just one supplement." Regarding weight loss: Although sea buckthorn is a healthy, low-calorie fruit that can be part of a balanced diet, there is no strong scientific evidence to support the claim that it directly causes weight loss in humans. A 2022 study showed that sea buckthorn powder helped prevent obesity in mice fed a high-fat diet, but we need more study in humans. Weight management is a complex process influenced by overall diet, regular exercise, and lifestyle choices. Relying on sea buckthorn for weight loss is not supported by current research. Regarding immunity and digestion: Sea buckthorn is rich in vitamin C, antioxidants, and other beneficial compounds that can support a healthy immune system. The fibre content in sea buckthorn can contribute to healthy bowel function. A 2025 review highlights that sea buckthorn polyphenols are beneficial for gut health by interacting with gut bacteria, improving nutrient absorption, reducing inflammation, and boosting immunity in the digestive system. However, stating it will "boost immunity" and "digestion" dramatically might be an overstatement. Many fruits and vegetables offer similar benefits. Sea buckthorn contains omega-3, 6, 9 and a rare omega-7, but many nuts, seeds, and oily fish offer these fats too. For antioxidants, berries like blueberries and amla (Indian gooseberry) are stronger contenders.

title: Fact Check: Can selenium cure cancer? - THIP Media
claim_text: A Facebook post includes the caption, 'The miracle mineral you're not supposed to know about #selenium #cancer #naturalremedies #holistichealth.' In the video, the narrator claims, 'When selenium is used by itself, there is a dramatic reduction in prostate cancer. It is a remarkable therapeutic agent.' He further explains that since selenium is a naturally occurring substance, it cannot be patented. Consequently, there is no profit margin, and as a result, universities and pharmaceutical companies are not pursuing it.
quick_take: A social media post claims that selenium cure cancer. The post states that the miracle mineral, selenium, when used by itself, dramatically reduces prostate cancer and lung cancer. We fact-checked and found this claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation:
Cancer occurs when there is an uncontrolled cell growth that damages the normal functioning of the affected body part and spreads to other regions. There are many different types of cancer, each with its unique characteristics and treatment options.

Selenium is a mineral that is essential for human health and has been studied for its potential role in cancer prevention and treatment. However, its role as a therapeutic agent for cancer is not well-established, and more research is needed to determine its efficacy. Selenium is an important component of several enzymes that have antioxidant properties and may help protect cells from damage caused by oxidative stress. Some studies have suggested that selenium supplementation may reduce the risk of certain cancers due to its effects on DNA repair, apoptosis, and the endocrine and immune systems. However, other research has not shown a significant protective effect against cancer. A randomized controlled trial concluded that selenium supplementation doesn't prevent prostate cancer.

Dr. Moujhuri Nandi, Consultant Radiation Oncologist at Karkinos Healthcare Pvt. ltd., states, "Selenium (Se) research has focused on its potential chemo-preventive role against cancer, but clinical trials, including the SELECT (Selenium and Vitamin E Cancer Prevention Trial) study, did not confirm its effectiveness in reducing prostate cancer risk. However, Se-containing compounds have gained interest as anti-cancer therapeutics due to their pro-oxidant properties, showing promise in targeting cancer cells. Pro-oxidant Se compounds induce oxidative stress and have demonstrated therapeutic synergy with anticancer drugs in xenograft models. Initial clinical trials combining high-dose SLM with axitinib for renal cell carcinoma showed promising results with manageable toxicity, and further trials are expanding to include immune checkpoint inhibitors. In conclusion, Selenium as a therapeutic drug in cancer is very much still in the trial phases, and though the early results look promising, more clinical studies are being conducted/ need to be conducted on a larger scale to evaluate its efficacy and we will know the results in the near future."

Dr P. Rammanohar, Research Director, Amrita School of Ayurveda, highlights this by stating, "Cancer is not a single disease, and there is no remedy for cancer. Different types of cancer are treated with different procedures of chemotherapy. One drug does not work across all cancers."

The Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center states that no clear evidence to support the use of selenium for cancer prevention. In fact, the long-term use of selenium may increase the risk of certain types of cancer. While selenium is an essential nutrient, taking selenium supplements at high doses can be harmful and may increase the risk of adverse effects. The use of selenium as a cancer therapeutic agent is still under investigation, and any potential benefits cannot prove it to be a therapeutic agent for cancer until research proves it so.

Cancer is a complicated disease that requires more than eating selenium for treatment. Relying on unproven treatments and not seeking proper medical treatment can worsen the condition making cancer incurable. Several people fall prey and believe claims, such as herbal supplements can fight cancer, but that is not true. In extreme instances, such therapies can be unsafe or fatal, possibly hindering conventional cancer treatment. Cancer multiplies quickly and spreads throughout the body in a short span. Any delay in the treatment will make the condition difficult to treat.

title: Fact Check: Can severe autism be reversed?
claim_text: Severe autism can be reversed and symptoms can be reduced to an indistinguishable level, according to a groundbreaking study.
quick_take: A post on X claims that severe autism can be reversed and symptoms can be reduced to an insignificant level. We did the fact check to term it as False.
doctor_explanation: Autism, or Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), is a neurodevelopmental condition that affects how individuals perceive, communicate, and interact with the world. The severity of autism varies, and symptoms can range from mild social challenges to significant communication difficulties and repetitive behaviours. Autism is generally diagnosed in early childhood, and early intervention can improve outcomes. But still, the condition is considered lifelong and currently has no known cure. No, severe autism cannot be reversed. Scientific research consistently shows that autism is a lifelong condition due to differences in brain development. Even though some treatments and therapies can significantly improve skills and reduce symptoms, these improvements do not equate to reversing the condition. The notion that autism, particularly severe autism, can be reversed is not true as per credible scientific evidence. The claim that severe autism can be reversed, based on a case study involving dizygotic twins, is misleading and lacks robust scientific support. The 2024 study describes significant improvements in the twins' symptoms through personalised lifestyle and environmental interventions. However, as a case report, it provides anecdotal evidence without the rigorous controls of larger studies. This makes it impossible to generalise the findings. There is no credible evidence to suggest that environmental modifications alone can reverse it. Although the interventions in the study may help manage symptoms and improve quality of life, they do not constitute a cure for autism. Broader scientific research does not support claims of reversing severe autism based on this study. Yes, individuals with level 3 autism, the most severe form of autism, can experience improvements with intensive and personalised support. Level 3 autism involves severe communication difficulties and significant challenges in daily living. Early and consistent interventions such as behavioural therapy, speech therapy, and educational support can help these individuals develop better coping mechanisms and some degree of independence. However, improvement in certain areas does not mean the condition is cured or reversed; the underlying neurodevelopmental differences remain. Children with severe autism can lead fulfilling lives, though their experience of life may differ from what is usually 'normal.' With the right support and early intervention, children with severe autism can learn to communicate, manage sensory sensitivities, and develop daily living skills. They may require varying levels of support throughout their lives. But, their potential for a meaningful life should not be underestimated. No, there is currently no cure for autism. Treatments and interventions aim to help individuals manage symptoms, improve communication and social skills, and enhance their quality of life. These interventions can include behavioural therapies, speech and occupational therapies. Sometimes, medication may also be necessary for associated symptoms like anxiety. However, these treatments do not cure autism or reverse its effects. Claims that suggest severe autism can be reversed are not only misleading but can also be harmful. Such claims can give false hope to families, leading them to pursue unproven treatments that may be costly, time-consuming, and potentially harmful. Moreover, these claims can contribute to the stigma surrounding autism by implying that individuals with autism need to be 'fixed' or 'cured' to be valued. Dr Shalini Nagori, MBBS, MD, Halol, Gujarat, says, 'Claims that severe autism are misleading and not supported by the broader scientific community. Autism is a complex, lifelong condition, and while interventions can help manage symptoms and improve quality of life, they do not cure or reverse the disorder. It's essential for families to focus on evidence-based treatments that are proven to support individuals with autism.'

title: Can severe headaches be cured naturally in 10 seconds?
claim_text: A Facebook post claims that severe headaches can be cured naturally in just 10 seconds using a combination of salt and grated ginger. The post "10 सेकंड में सिर दर्द गायब" emphasizes that the botanical extract is not only an instant pain reliever but can also be used in place of prescription medications.
quick_take: A Facebook post asserts that excruciating headaches can be effectively managed naturally in just ten seconds. After verifying the claim, we discovered that it is false.
doctor_explanation: Headaches are prevalent pains or discomforts in the head, scalp, or neck that are brought on by the overactivity of pain-sensitive structures in the head and neck rather than the brain itself. They can occur on one or both sides of the head and vary considerably in nature and intensity, from mild pressing pain to throbbing or stabbing pain. Key contributing variables include stress, tense muscles, dehydration, lack of sleep, and certain foods. These triggers might result in various headache types that fall primarily into three categories: tension headaches (most prevalent), migraines (throbbing, excruciating ailments), and cluster headaches (incredibly horrible illnesses that recur in cycles). Dr. Joy Mounica, Consultant Neurologist at Renova Hospitals, Hyderabad, explains that while ginger may exert abortive and prophylactic effects in migraine pain and may help alleviate associated gastric issues, the right amount of salt is key. She underlines that migraine headaches can be brought on by consuming excessive or insufficient salt. Therefore, it is usually suggested that high-risk individuals consume a modest amount of salt. The combination of salt and ginger may provide transient symptomatic relief for mild cases in some individuals, but it cannot address the root cause of the condition. Given that headaches are associated with neurological, vascular, and muscular mechanisms, they necessitate targeted therapeutic intervention. So, the combination should only supplement, not replace, the established treatment for headaches. Dr. Utkarsh Bhagat, Neurosurgeon at Narayana Hospital in Gurugram, clarifies that excruciating headaches such as migraines are a complex neurological disorder characterised by throbbing pain, nausea, and sensitivity to light and sound. The primary contributing factors usually include stress, hormonal fluctuations, certain foods, and environmental factors. While alternative therapies might provide only symptomatic relief, effective preventive measures or medications that reduce the duration and severity of the serious condition can help manage it more proactively. Claims that headaches can be managed and resolved without medication in ten seconds can be highly deceptive because an abrupt or intense headache may occasionally indicate an underlying medical issue. Reliance on such untested solutions might delay the necessary medical evaluation. Hence, frequent headaches necessitate accurate and sustainable pain management that relies on timely and accurate evaluation and management. Medical professionals employ a planned, individualised strategy to handle headaches, considering the patient's medical history, the nature and intensity of the pain, along with the root cause. Pharmacological therapy may include NSAIDs for moderate episodes or preventive measures for severe or recurring occurrences. Non-pharmacological interventions such as cognitive-behavioral therapy, biofeedback, and relaxation methods may help reduce the frequency and severity of headaches.

title: Fact Check: Can sex of an unborn child be predicted using bath soap? - THIP Media
claim_text: Mixing soap with urine of a pregnant lady is a natural way to predict the sex of an unborn child. If the soap fizzes or sizzles in urine, you are having a boy.
quick_take: A YouTube video claims that mixing soap with urine of a pregnant lady is a natural way to predict the sex of an unborn child. We fact checked and found that the claim is False.
doctor_explanation: Such home remedies do not work. They have no scientific basis. The proponents of the theory believes that the human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG), a hormone that a woman's body produces during pregnancy and is often detected in urine, reacts with the compounds of a soap to reveal the gender of the unborn baby. There is some research that have shown that hCG amount in urine varies as per the sex of the unborn baby. But since the compounds of a soap varies greatly from one brand to another, there is no guarantee to have any consistent reaction between urine of a pregnant woman and soap. We checked with our expert Dr Anita Gupta, Gynecologist and Associate Director at Fortis La Femme, New Delhi, can home-based ingredients predict the gender of an unborn baby at home. She replied, "No. Home-based ingredients like toothpaste, baking soda, soap, urine fizz etc., cannot help predict the gender of an unborn baby at home. There exists a lot of myths and false claims around gender prediction using such ingredients. Medical fraternity practicing modern medicine does not promote such practices at home. These claims lack scientific evidence. Also, pre-natal sex determination testing is illegal in India since 1994." The NIPT (Non-invasive prenatal testing) test is a noninvasive blood test for a pregnant woman after 10 weeks of pregnancy. It can determine the gender of your unborn child and various chromosomal abnormalities, such as down syndrome (if present). NIPT checks for the presence or absence of the Y chromosome. The presence of the Y chromosome indicates that you're having a boy, and its absence indicates that your baby's sex is female. An ultrasound is the only way other than a blood test for gender determination. After 14 weeks of gestation, the baby's genitals can be seen in an ultrasound. It is non-invasive and up to 90% accurate in visualizing the gender of the fetus when the test is performed after the 16 weeks of gestation.

doctor_explanation: Does this mixture whiten skin in one use? No, this combination cannot significantly whiten skin, let alone in one use. There is no scientific proof that this mixture can dramatically whiten skin. Skin colour is mainly determined by melanin, and applying these ingredients cannot change the genetic factors that control skin tone. Can any product make skin fair permanently for 150+ years? No, it cannot. The idea of permanent skin whitening through a home remedy is biologically impossible. Skin colour depends on genetics, melanin production, and environmental factors like sun exposure. Even if a product temporarily lightens the skin, it cannot permanently stop melanin production. The claim of 150 years is absurd—far beyond a human lifespan. The skin renews itself every 28–30 days in young adults and 45–50 days in older adults, meaning any temporary lightening effect would fade. No product can stop this natural process. The stratum corneum, the skin's outer layer, is made of dead cells that protect the body. These cells constantly shed and renew, but this process slows with age. Will this mixture prevent skin from darkening forever? No, not at all. Skin darkening occurs due to sun exposure, which triggers melanin production. This mixture does not provide any sun protection—none of the ingredients contain SPF. In fact, lemon juice can make skin more sensitive to sunlight, increasing the risk of burns and hyperpigmentation. Without sunscreen, skin will naturally darken when exposed to UV rays. Is this mixture safe to use on the skin? Not recommended. While some ingredients like lemon and baking soda are popular in DIY skincare, they can be harsh and damaging. Dr Iram Qazi, Dermatologist, Life Medical Centre & Clinic, UAE, clarifies: "Toothpaste is designed for cleaning teeth, not for skin use. Its strong ingredients can cause irritation, burning, and redness. I do not recommend using toothpaste for skin treatment, as it may worsen the condition." Dr Swati Watwani, Medical Director at Persianlly Clinic, explains: "Baking soda is too alkaline for the skin and can upset its natural balance. This may cause irritation, dryness, and sensitivity. Since it is rough in texture, it can over-exfoliate the skin, leading to dryness, rashes, and dark spots." Dr Rashi Soni, Co-founder and Consulting Dermatologist, Aesthetician, and Hair Transplant Surgeon at Rashi Hospital in Mumbai, states: "Shampoo is formulated for the scalp and hair, not for facial or body skin. Many shampoos contain surfactants and fragrances that can strip the skin of its natural oils, leading to dryness, irritation, and even allergic reactions. Using shampoo on the skin regularly may disrupt its protective barrier and cause sensitivity." Dr Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant in Lucknow, warns: "Lemon juice is highly acidic and can irritate the skin, especially for those with sensitive skin. It can cause redness, burning, and dryness. Additionally, when exposed to sunlight, lemon juice can trigger phytophotodermatitis, a reaction that leads to painful burns and dark spots. It is not a safe or effective skincare remedy." Using such harsh ingredients together can increase the risk of irritation, redness, or allergic reactions, especially for sensitive skin. title: Can Sheesham leaves in oil cure paralysis in just 3 days?

doctor_explanation: Paralysis cannot be cured at home using oils. Paralysis happens when communication between the brain and muscles is disrupted—this can be due to a stroke, spinal injury, nerve damage, or other medical conditions. Oil for paralysis treatment, whether herbal or not, may help with massage and muscle stiffness, but it cannot repair nerve damage or restore movement on its own. Dr Mohit Sandhu, Ayurvedic Practitioner at AgniShalya Ayurvedic Hospital and Research Centre, Hamirpur, firmly dismisses the idea to cure paralysis in just 2 or 3 minutes of oil massage, or even a few days, by applying oil, whether it contains sheesham leaves in oil for paralysis or not. 'That's not how paralysis works, not even according to Ayurveda,' he says. Dr Sandhu explains that while certain medicated oils like Mahanarayan tailor Ksheerabala tail may be used in Ayurvedic treatments, their role is to support recovery by improving circulation and easing stiffness when combined with massage (Abhyanga) and steam therapy (Swedana). In very rare and early-stage cases, such as mild Bell's palsy or functional paralysis, some minor movement may return temporarily, but this is only short-term relief, not a cure. He adds that Ayurveda approaches paralysis through a structured, long-term protocol involving internal and external oleation (Snehana), medicated enemas (Basti), nasal therapy (Nasya), and calming treatments like Shirodhara and Shirobasti. Therapies such as Rasayana for nerve regeneration and procedures like Marma Chikitsa or Agnikarma may also be included. 'These treatments aim to manage symptoms and support nerve function over time. Claims of instant or three-day cures are misleading and have no basis in classical Ayurvedic texts or clinical practice,' Dr Sandhu concludes. Dr Muskan Thakur, Ayurvedic Practitioner from Indore, also denies this, stating, 'Classical Ayurvedic texts and scientific evidence do not support such claims.' According to her, paralysis, or Pakshaghat in Ayurveda, is a serious condition caused by an aggravated Vata dosha, which affects the nervous system. Treatment involves a gradual, multi-step process including medicated oil massages (Abhyanga), internal herbal medicines, Panchakarma therapies like Pizhichil and Basti, and appropriate lifestyle changes. Oils such as Mahanarayan Tail and Dhanwantaram Tail can help support nerve function over time, but they cannot provide an instant cure. Dr Thakur stresses that the idea of one oil curing all types of paralysis contradicts the core Ayurvedic principle of personalised treatment, which considers a person's dosha, dhatu, and roga (imbalance, tissues, and disease). 'Such one-size-fits-all claims are misleading and go against the very foundation of Ayurveda.' There is no scientific proof that sheesham leaves in oil for paralysis work as a cure. While Sheesham leaves benefits are known in Ayurveda for managing pain and inflammation, this is not the same as curing or reversing paralysis. A 2021 animal study showed that extracts from Sheesham leaves might help improve memory and reduce brain inflammation in rats with Alzheimer's-like symptoms, but this has no connection to paralysis. So far, no clinical research supports the idea that Sheesham leaves, whether raw or boiled in oil, can heal nerve damage or restore lost muscle control. Dr Kunal Bahrani, Director and HOD of Neurology at Marengo Asia Hospitals, Faridabad, explains, 'Paralysis, particularly due to stroke, is a critical condition that demands immediate and structured care. It results from a sudden interruption in blood flow to the brain, which can damage the regions responsible for movement. Managing it requires timely diagnosis, medical support, and regular rehabilitation. False information about quick fixes can be harmful as it may lead patients to skip essential treatment during the most crucial recovery window.' Gentle massage with warm oil may improve blood flow, reduce stiffness, and offer emotional comfort, but these are part of a broader treatment plan and on their own are not enough to cure paralysis.

title: Fact Check: Can simple exercises cure heart failure at home?

Can exercises alone cure heart failure? No, simple exercises cannot cure heart failure. Heart failure is a chronic, progressive condition where the heart does not pump blood as effectively as it should. Exercise can help improve heart health, manage symptoms, and even prevent heart problems, but it is not a cure. Treatment usually involves a combination of medication, lifestyle changes, and sometimes surgery, depending on the severity of the condition. Regular physical activity can support heart function and enhance quality of life. However, it must be done under medical supervision, especially for those with heart issues. Ignoring proper treatment could lead to severe complications. Some also promote drinking kishmish water to prevent heart attacks, but this is not a sure shot method for prevention.

Dr Subhaargh Kumar, Consultant Cardiologist, The Five Elements Medical Centre, Gurugram states: "No, exercise alone cannot cure heart failure. Regular physical activity can strengthen the heart and improve circulation, but it isn't enough on its own. Managing heart failure effectively usually involves a mix of medication, lifestyle changes, and medical supervision. Patients should talk to their doctors to create a personalised care plan."

How does exercise impact heart failure? Exercise benefits heart failure patients but does not reverse the condition. For those diagnosed with heart failure, supervised exercise programmes improve endurance, reduce symptoms, and enhance overall well-being. Healthcare professionals often recommend cardiac rehabilitation, which combines monitored exercise, education, and lifestyle counselling. They design these programmes carefully, assessing individual capacities and risks. Random, unsupervised exercises could be harmful, especially for those with advanced or unstable heart conditions.

Dr Almas Fatma, MBBS, Diploma in Family Medicine, PG in Digital Health, General Physician from Navi Mumbai says: "Heart failure is a chronic condition where the heart can't pump blood effectively, requiring lifelong care through medications, lifestyle changes, and sometimes surgery. While treatments can manage symptoms, there's no cure. Exercise can help improve heart function and quality of life for those with stable heart failure, but it should be part of a comprehensive treatment plan that includes medication, diet, and regular check-ups. Supervised exercise, like cardiac rehabilitation, is often recommended, but unsupervised or excessive activity can be harmful. Cold weather doesn't cure heart failure and may even worsen symptoms. Misleading claims suggesting that exercise alone can cure heart failure can delay proper medical care, so it's important to consult a healthcare professional before starting any exercise regimen."

Are there risks in exercising without medical advice for heart failure? Yes, exercising without proper guidance can be dangerous for heart failure patients. The type, intensity, and duration of exercises need to be customised based on the patient's condition. Sudden or intense physical activity might strain the heart, increase blood pressure, or even lead to life-threatening events. Heart failure patients may experience symptoms such as shortness of breath, chest pain, and palpitations. Pushing through these signs without understanding their implications could worsen the condition.

Why is it important to have a medical treatment plan for heart failure? A comprehensive treatment plan is essential because heart failure affects multiple body systems. Managing heart failure generally involves medications to reduce fluid build-up, lower blood pressure, and improve heart function. Lifestyle adjustments like reducing salt intake, maintaining a healthy weight, and monitoring fluid levels are also essential. These strategies work together to manage symptoms and slow disease progression. Over-reliance on non-medical interventions, such as unsupervised exercise, might cause patients to neglect the critical elements of care which can likely worsen their health outcomes.

THIP Media Take: The claim that simple exercises can cure heart failure at home is false. While exercise is beneficial as part of a treatment plan, it is not a cure. Heart failure requires a multifaceted approach, including medication, lifestyle changes, and regular medical check-ups. Patients should always consult healthcare professionals before starting or modifying any exercise routine.

Additionally, engaging in yoga classes or group sessions can provide social support and a sense of community, which can further contribute to improved mental health. Sirsasana, also known as the headstand pose in yoga, is a challenging inversion posture that involves balancing your body upside down with the support of your forearms and head. While yoga and specific yoga poses like Sirsasana can have numerous physical and mental health benefits, claiming that a single pose can cure diseases like depression and anxiety is an oversimplification. Regular practice of yoga can contribute to stress reduction, improved mood, increased mindfulness, and overall well-being. These benefits may indirectly help manage symptoms of depression and anxiety for some individuals, especially when combined with other therapeutic approaches such as counseling or medication if needed. However, it is essential to remember that depression and anxiety are complex mental health conditions that typically require a multifaceted approach to treatment. While yoga and other mind-body practices can be valuable components of a holistic wellness plan, they are not a substitute for professional medical or psychological treatment when needed. Depression and anxiety are complex mental health conditions influenced by a combination of genetic, environmental, psychological, and neurological factors. While yoga and physical activity, in general, can contribute positively to mental well-being, they are usually considered complementary practices to traditional medical treatments. Dr Rahul Bansal, Consultant Psychiatrist in an interview with THIP adds, "Any delay in treatment will worsen the health." The idea that any one remedy can prevent depression is an oversimplification of a complex condition, and it is essential to approach depression treatment with a comprehensive and individualized approach. Psychologist Dr Binda Singh states, "Depression is a disease and needs proper treatment. It can happen due to a variety of reasons, such as situational, trauma, physical health issues, etc. Depression needs intervention, which might include medication, counselling, positive thoughts, communication, etc." Dr Sameer Kalani, Consultant Psychiatrist, Fortis Gurgaon, in an interview with THIP MEDIA informs that home remedies alone cannot treat the root cause of depression. It is important to note that yoga cannot cure depression and anxiety for everyone. It is crucial to seek guidance from a qualified healthcare provider who can offer personalized recommendations and support tailored to your individual needs. They can help you develop a comprehensive treatment plan that may include a variety of approaches, potentially including yoga and other forms of exercise, therapy, medication, and lifestyle adjustments. title: Fact Check: Can skin absorb chlorine from water? - THIP Media
claim_text: drinking and swimming chlorinated water coming from the faucet harms people and within 60 seconds skin absorb chlorine
quick_take: A social media post claims that drinking tap water or directly from the faucet contains chlorinated water is absorbed by the body and may cause harm to the body. We fact checked and found the claim to be Half True.
doctor_explanation:
The claim that skin absorbs chlorine from water is partially true but exaggerated. Chlorine is a highly reactive chemical element used as a disinfectant in water treatment. It kills harmful pathogens and makes water safe for drinking and swimming. However, chlorine is toxic and can cause health issues if not handled properly.

How chlorine affects the body and skin:
1. Respiratory System: Inhalation of chlorine gas can irritate the respiratory tract, causing coughing, throat irritation, and shortness of breath. In severe cases, high-level exposure can lead to pulmonary edema.
2. Digestive System: Consuming small amounts of chlorine in drinking water is generally safe at low concentrations. Higher concentrations can cause nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain.
3. Circulatory System: Chlorine can form trihalomethanes (THMs) when reacting with organic matter in water. Long-term exposure to THMs through drinking water has been linked to increased cancer risk and adverse reproductive outcomes.
4. Skin Effects: Chlorine can strip natural oils from skin, causing dryness, itching, irritation, rashes, redness, and in some cases eczema or dermatitis.

Does skin absorb chlorine? Yes, but in very very small quantities. When skin contacts chlorinated water, chlorine can penetrate the outer layers. Small amounts can pass through the skin barrier into the body, though the amount absorbed is generally low. Prolonged or repeated exposure can increase absorption. The absorbed chlorine can contribute to skin irritation, dryness, and eczema.

Expert Opinion from Dr Sachin Gupta, Dermatologist, Amrita Hospital, Faridabad: "The idea that skin absorb chlorine during showering or swimming is not strongly supported by evidence. Chlorine in water mainly exists in forms that do not easily penetrate the skin, which acts as a strong barrier. Small amounts can pass through, but the body quickly gets rid of them." Most chlorine exposure happens through inhaling chlorine gas that evaporates from water, especially in indoor pools or hot showers, which can irritate lungs and airways. Skin exposure effects are due to chlorine interacting with the skin's surface rather than being deeply absorbed. For most people, this exposure is minimal and not a major concern. However, for swimming instructors, pool staff, and competitive swimmers, effects might be more significant. Recommendations include using shower filters, showering before and after swimming, and keeping skin moisturized.

title: Can skin be effectively whitened with whipped coffee foam?
claim_text: According to an Instagram post with the caption 'गोरा होने के लिए घरेलू उपाय', whipped coffee foam – prepared with coffee, sugar, milk, and hot water – is a highly effective home remedy for skin whitening.
quick_take: An Instagram post suggests that whipped coffee foam can make skin whiter. We analysed the claim and found it to be completely false.
doctor_explanation:
Skin colour specifically the skin's perceived tone or shade, which frequently depends on the type and concentration of melanin, the primary skin pigment. Variations in skin pigmentation are caused by melanocytes, carotene, oxygenated haemoglobin, and local blood flow. Skin pigmentation, which fundamentally establishes an individual's constitutive or baseline skin colour, is influenced by approximately 150 genes. The equilibrium of the pigments is maintained by genes such as MC1R, SLC24A5, and TYR that regulate melanin concentration and dispersion. Ageing and hormonal imbalances are also significant contributors. External triggers may have a major impact on skin appearance via influencing the quantity of melanin produced. Out of all the external elements that affect skin tone, UV radiation from sunshine frequently has a significant influence. Furthermore, several medications and compounds may alter pigmentation by inhibiting melanocyte activation.

Whipped coffee foam prepared by combining coffee, milk, sugar, and boiled water is being touted as a skin-whitening formulation, but it lacks scientific validation. This lack of evidence could be attributed to the fact that skin colour is primarily determined by melanin production – regulated by genetics and biological pathways.

COFFEE: The caffeine-rich component is packed with polyphenols such as chlorogenic acid, which may exhibit antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and modest photoprotective benefits; however, topical coffee application does not demonstrate skin whitening effects.

MILK: Even though it is utilised in regulated dermatological compositions, because it provides the alpha-hydroxy acid, lactic acid, which might improve skin texture and encourage mild exfoliation instead of actual whitening.

SUGAR: The common culinary ingredient can be used as a physical exfoliator, but if applied vigorously, it may result in micro-abrasions, which might worsen pigmentation, particularly hyperpigmentation caused by inflammation. Additionally, none of the aforementioned ingredients, either by themselves or in combination, can either inhibit tyrosinase or reduce melanin synthesis, essential for skin whitening. Therefore, depending too much on the skin-whitening therapy could lead to unrealistic expectations and delay the required evidence-based therapy.

Dr. Sachin Gupta, MBBS, MD (Dermatology and Venereology from AIIMS Delhi) of Amrita Hospital, emphasises that 'natural components are not always equivalent to safety or efficacy, and what might seem harmless can actually be detrimental.' The safest and most efficient method to address skin-related issues is to consult a dermatologist. Brightness brought on by enhanced skin health should not be mistaken for reduced natural pigmentation. Although these compounds may help address skincare issues, there is no scientific evidence that they can effectively or safely whiten skin.

Dr. Annusuiya Gohil, MD Scholar at the All India Institute of Ayurveda, adds that skin pigmentation is primarily brought on by genetic makeup and environmental factors. Skin pigmentation cannot be changed; it can only be enhanced. However, there are several approaches to make the skin more luminous. More specifically, it can be achieved to restore the natural skin pigmentation that may have been lost over time due to ageing, exposure to harsh environments, and other factors like food and medication. Topical treatments cannot change the colour of the skin.

Social media platforms promote instant skin-whitening remedies using baking soda, milk, coffee, and lemon. These claims align with the urge for rapid cosmetic enhancements but lack scientific credibility. Skin colour is primarily determined by melanin biology and genetics rather than topical food additives. Additionally, excessive use and improper application may negatively impact the skin barrier, alter pH, result in hyperpigmentation rather than lightening, and induce irritant or allergic contact dermatitis. Unregulated internet skin-whitening products lack clinical validation and are risky and unreliable substitutes for scientifically supported skin care practices.

title: Fact Check: Can skipping breakfast lead to gradual brain damage and an increased risk of memory loss?
claim_text: Skipping breakfast can lead to gradual brain damage and an increased risk of memory loss. People who do not have breakfast in the morning experience brain damage slowly, and skipping breakfast for a long time leads to reduced brain capacity and leads to brain damage, which leads to serious problems like increased risk of memory loss.
verdict_original: This claim is MISLEADING. — Hence, to claim that skipping breakfast can lead to brain damage and increased risk of memory loss in the long run is MISLEADING.
doctor_explanation:
The Medical Dialogues Fact Check Team spoke with Dr. Rahul Chawla, Associate Consultant, Neurology, PSRI, New Delhi, who said: "Skipping breakfast has been shown to negatively impact memory functions, especially in children, in some low-powered studies. However, the claim that it may lead to 'memory loss' in the long term cannot be made based on these studies and high-powered studies with larger sample sizes are needed. Having said that, breakfast is an important meal of the day and should not be missed. Skipping breakfast is a known trigger factor for migraine. It is also associated with lowered immunity. While the importance of eating a healthy breakfast daily cannot be overemphasized, such scaremongering should be curtailed."

Dr. Anshu Rohatgi, Senior Consultant Neurologist at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, New Delhi, responded to the claim: "Skipping breakfast can have some effects on memory and cognitive function. Research indicates that missing breakfast may lead to lower energy levels and reduced mental focus, which can impact memory performance. The brain relies on glucose for optimal functioning, and breakfast often provides a significant portion of this energy. However, it's important to note that while skipping breakfast might cause temporary memory issues, it doesn't necessarily lead to long-term memory loss or conditions like dementia. Consistently maintaining a balanced diet and healthy eating habits is crucial for overall brain health."

The article explains that memory loss can arise from multiple factors including neurodegenerative conditions such as Alzheimer's Disease, Stroke, Vascular Cognitive Impairment, traumatic brain injury, structural lesions, nutritional deficiencies, lifestyle habits, and psychological factors such as depression.

Regarding the scientific evidence, the article cites multiple studies: A study published in Nutrients by Humberto Peña-Jorquera et al. found that skipping breakfast regularly was negatively linked with lower cognitive performance, especially in adolescents living with overweight/obesity — those who had breakfast immediately before a cognitive task performed better, especially with high-quality components such as dairy products. [3]

A study published by Masato Kawabata et al. in Nutrients observed that combining morning breakfast with exercise enhances adolescents' short-term performance and speed on mathematical tasks; those who consumed a low glycemic index breakfast and participated in 30 minutes of aerobic exercise showed improvements in mathematics scores and reaction times, compared to those who fasted during the morning. These improvements were noted as significant for short-term academic performance in youth but limited in scope. [4]

A 2022 study published in Innovation in Aging found that for people with diabetes, skipping breakfast is a risk factor for obesity and dyslipidemia, which are further associated with dementia. However, the study did not find any direct correlations between dementia and skipping breakfast. [6]

A study published in the Journal of Geriatric Psychiatry and Neurology by Rika Ishizuka et al. found that breakfast skipping is longitudinally associated with declines in cognitive scores among older adults. [7]

However, a 2013 study noted that skipping breakfast, which has been argued to have universally negative cognitive consequences, is a "presumption" unsupported by scientific evidence. [5] No study could be located that supported the claim that skipping breakfast can lead to brain damage in the long run.

Further, a study by Alby Elias et al. published in Nutrition Reviews found that intermittent fasting (a dietary pattern that alternates between periods of voluntary fasting and eating, which includes generally delaying or skipping breakfast) over the years may potentially reverse or delay the pathological process of Alzheimer's disease. [8]

The overall consensus: The majority of studies hint at short-term effects of skipping breakfast on cognitive function, but the long-term effect of skipping breakfast has not been established. There is scientific evidence related to positive impacts of intermittent fasting, including delaying or skipping breakfast, on cognitive functions. To establish a direct connection between skipping breakfast and linking it to brain damage and memory loss is misleading.

While consuming breakfast offers various benefits including cognitive advantages, no scientific evidence or medical consensus supports the claim that skipping breakfast can cause brain damage and increased risk of memory loss in the long run. Numerous studies have demonstrated that breakfast can enhance concentration, attention, and overall cognitive performance, particularly in school-aged children and adolescents. However, these studies do not conclusively link the absence of breakfast to any long-term cognitive deficits such as memory loss.

title: Fact Check: Can skipping breakfast reverse ageing? - THIP Media
claim_text: Hard to believe, but skipping breakfast can reverse ageing. Calorie restriction and intermittent fasting can help increase growth hormones and lower your insulin levels
quick_take: A social media post claims that skipping breakfast can reverse ageing. We did a fact-check and found the claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: Ageing is a gradual decrease in physical and mental health that may increase the risk of disease and ultimately death. The World Health Organization (WHO) suggests that ageing at the biological level is the accumulation of molecular and cellular damage over time. Ageing reduces elasticity to cause wrinkles, rough-textured and saggy appearance. Research notes, "This ageing process is accompanied with phenotypic changes in cutaneous cells as well as structural and functional changes in extracellular matrix components such as collagen and elastin". The natural process of ageing cannot be reversed. There are factors such as genes, environment and lifestyle choices on which ageing mostly depends. The damage already made by these factors are irreversible. But we can slow the natural process of ageing. The National Institute on Aging (NIA) website claims, "Studies have demonstrated that the rate of ageing can be slowed, suggesting that targeting ageing will coincidentally slow the appearance and reduce the burden of numerous diseases to increase the portion of life spent in good health". The American Academy of Dermatology Association (AAD) website suggests ways to reduce premature skin ageing. However, the website strongly recommends you see a dermatologist. No. Diet cannot stop or reverse ageing. Dr Saurabh Gaba, Associate Consultant, Internal Medicine, Paras Hospitals, Panchkula, says, "There is no scientific evidence for it. However, it is a healthy practice to limit overall food intake to maintain an ideal body weight." A nutritional diet is closely associated with skin health right from youth to ageing or disease. A study has shown that it is important to eat a diet that meets your nutritional demand as eating habits can either repair damaged skin or cause damage to the skin. But researchers note that, "Only oral supplementation is not enough to improve the skin" and "Improvement in skin aging through diet should not be rushed, because skin aging caused by diet and improvement of aging performance by diet are long-term processes." There is also a popular saying that the human body regenerates itself every seven years, and then you become a completely new person. But, this isn't scientifically correct. No. Calorie restrictions or fasting cannot reverse ageing. Some studies show that calorie restriction can "reduce aging-associated biomarkers in humans," but there is no research that establishes that the process of ageing can be reversed. On the topic of Intermittent fasting being helpful to overall health, Dr Smriti Naswa, Consultant Clinical, Pediatric & Cosmetic Dermatologist, Fortis Hospital, Mulund, Mumbai, says, "The meal timings are equally important for health as the quality & quantity of food. Dr Sujata Chakravarti, Consultant-General Medicine, Hiranandani Hospital, Vashi-A Fortis Network Hospital further adds, "Skipping breakfast can actually be harmful, and can increase risk of Diabetes, weight gain, Acid Reflux, and Migraines. title: Can skipping roti and rice shrink belly fat in 15 days?
claim_text: A social media post suggests that cutting out rice and roti can shrink belly fat and cure all diseases within just 15 days.
quick_take: A social media post suggests that avoiding carbs such as roti and rice can completely shrink belly fat or even fix major health problems in just 15 days. We fact checked and found the claim to be Mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Not really. While reducing these carbs might help shed a few kgs initially, it doesn't specifically target or "shrink" belly fat in a miraculous way, especially not in 15 days. Think about it like this: roti and rice are rich in carbohydrates, which your body turns into energy. When you cut them out suddenly, your system dips into stored glycogen, a form of sugar held in muscles and the liver, bound up with water. Losing that glycogen means you also lose water weight, which can make the scales drop quickly, sometimes by a kilo or two in the first week. But that's not actual fat melting away; it's mostly fluid. Studies show low-carb diets can lead to more short-term weight loss than low-fat ones, but after a year or so, the results even out. Belly fat, or visceral fat, is stubborn. It wraps around organs and links to health risks like heart disease. True fat loss happens through a calorie deficit, burning more energy than you consume, combined with exercise. One trial found that low-carb eaters lost a bit more body fat overall, but not magically from the belly. In 15 days? Unrealistic. Your body needs time to adapt, and spot-reduction myths have been debunked for years. If you're hoping for a flat tummy fast, this isn't the shortcut. Hakim Bharmal, Master Trainer and Contest Prep Coach, explains that belly fat loss relies on a few core principles. A calorie deficit helps the body tap into stored fat, while balanced meals with protein, carbs, and healthy fats support energy and recovery. Cardio activities such as walking, running, or cycling increase calorie burn, and strength training builds muscle, which naturally boosts fat burning even at rest. Equally important are quality sleep and stress management, since poor rest and high stress can raise cortisol a hormone tied to belly fat. Still, results don't happen overnight; it won't melt away in just 15 days. Staying consistent with diet, exercise, and healthy routines is what truly drives long-term progress and a fitter body. Can eliminating roti and rice cure diseases within 15 days? No. There's no evidence that skipping these foods alone can cure any disease, let alone in such a brief period. Diseases like diabetes, high blood pressure, or even digestive issues don't vanish because you avoid carbs. Low-carb approaches, like the ketogenic diet, have shown promise in managing certain conditions, for instance, helping control blood sugar in type 2 diabetes by reducing insulin spikes, or easing symptoms in epilepsy through ketosis, where the body burns fat for fuel instead of carbs. A small study even suggested keto might stabilise mood in severe mental illnesses by altering brain energy use. But "cure"? That's a bluff. These benefits build over months, not days, and require medical supervision. Suddenly dropping roti and rice could backfire. Your body might rebel with fatigue, headaches, or constipation from lacking fibre, roti, especially wholewheat, provides that gut-friendly stuff. Bottom line: no quick miracle. Consult a doctor for real disease management. Dr Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition, said, "As a dietitian, I want to clarify that eliminating roti or rice will not magically cure any disease within 15 days. Health conditions like diabetes, thyroid imbalance, or heart disease are complex and cannot be reversed so quickly by cutting out a single food. What truly matters is an overall balanced diet, portion control, physical activity, stress management, and regular medical care. Whole grains like roti and rice, when eaten in moderation, can be part of a healthy diet. Quick fixes often lead to disappointment. Sustainable lifestyle changes are the real path to long-term health." Mixed. You might feel lighter at first, but there are downsides that could leave you sluggish. On the plus side, cutting refined carbs like white rice or plain roti can stabilise blood sugar, reducing energy crashes and cravings. One woman who tried it for a month reported clearer skin and less bloating, thanks to lower inflammation. Weight dips happen because carbs hold water, lose the carbs, lose the bloat. But go too extreme, and "keto flu" hits: dizziness, irritability, even bad breath from ketosis. Without balanced swaps, you risk missing B vitamins, magnesium, or fibre, leading to tiredness or gut woes. It's not all doom; if done right, with veggies and proteins, it can boost satiety and aid steady weight control. Just don't expect 15-day wonders. Yes, moderation works, but cutting carbs out completely for 15 days makes little sense. What happens on day 16? Carbohydrates aren't the enemy; they're the body's main source of energy. Wholegrain options like roti or brown rice provide fibre that supports heart health and keeps digestion regular. Removing them for too long can create nutrient deficiencies for instance, poor calcium absorption may weaken bones, and reduced serotonin production can affect mood, since carbs help make this "feel-good" chemical. Studies also suggest that very low-carb diets may even raise the risk of diabetes in some people. Most importantly, sustainability counts. Once carbs are reintroduced, many end up regaining weight because such strict diets are difficult to maintain socially and culturally. A balanced approach always works better than complete restrictions. In wrapping up, this claim preys on our desire for fast results, but science says patience is the key. By understanding your body's needs, you can make informed choices that last. Stay curious, eat mindfully, and your belly and health will thank you.

title: Fact Check: Can sleeping on the right side cause heart attacks?
claim_text: The leading cause of heart attack-related deaths during sleep is sleeping in the wrong position—on the right side instead of the left. It states that sleeping on the left side is essential for heart health and digestion. Additionally, it warns that waking up suddenly or getting up too quickly can put excessive pressure on the heart, potentially leading to heart attacks or strokes.
quick_take: A social media post claims that sleeping on the right side causes heart attacks during sleep. We fact checked this claim and found it to be mostly false.
doctor_explanation: No, sleeping on your right side does not cause heart attacks. In fact, some studies suggest that sleeping on the left side may change how the heart appears on an ECG due to a slight shift in position. However, these changes are simply a result of how the machine records the heart's activity and do not mean that left-side sleeping is harmful. For healthy people, the side you sleep on doesn't affect your heart's performance. For some people with certain heart conditions (like consecutive dilated cardiomyopathy), sleeping on the right side might actually feel more comfortable because it helps keep the heart steady. Experts advise pregnant people to sometimes try left-side sleeping to ease pressure on the liver, but overall, both sleeping positions are safe. Dr Ubaid ur Rahman, General Physician at Holy Mission Clinic, New Delhi, says, "Sleeping on your right side doesn't cause heart attacks. There's no scientific evidence linking it to heart problems. Your heart is well-protected by your body, and sleeping positions generally don't harm it. If you have existing heart conditions, certain positions may cause discomfort. Maintaining a healthy lifestyle—regular exercise, a balanced diet, and stress management—is key. Always consult your doctor for personalised heart health advice." Regarding left side sleeping: There isn't strong, conclusive research proving that sleeping on the left side improves heart function or circulation in healthy individuals. However, it may help in digestion and reduce acid reflux. There is also no strong evidence that sleeping on the right side is harmful. In fact, a 2011 study suggests that sleeping on the right side can help you sleep better and may prevent breathing issues if you have respiratory problems. People with heart failure may feel better sleeping on their right side, while those with acid reflux (GERD) or pregnant women may benefit from the left side. If you have sleep apnea, avoiding back sleeping can help. The best sleep position is the one that lets you rest well. Regarding waking up too quickly: Not directly, but sudden movements can affect blood pressure. Waking up too quickly from deep sleep may cause a sudden drop in blood pressure, leading to dizziness or lightheadedness—a condition called orthostatic hypotension. This is more common in older adults and people with certain health conditions, but it does not directly trigger heart attacks or strokes in healthy individuals. Severe orthostatic hypotension may increase the risk of a stroke, but this is rare. Also, getting up at night to urinate has no proven link to sudden cardiac arrest or changes in ECG readings. Dr Almas Fatma, MBBS, Diploma in Family Medicine, PG in Digital Health, General Physician from Navi Mumbai, says, "There's no scientific evidence to support that waking up suddenly or standing up too quickly causes heart attacks or strokes. Waking up to urinate, known as nocturia, may signal underlying health issues like heart disease or high blood pressure, but it doesn't directly cause heart problems. If you feel dizzy when standing up, sitting on the edge of the bed for a moment can help. The key to heart health is regular checkups and managing risks, not following viral myths." The primary factors that contribute to heart attacks include underlying health conditions, not sleep position. In summary, the claim that sleeping on the right side causes heart attacks is mostly false. While sleep position can influence heart function in some cases, it is not a major cause of heart attacks. Similarly, waking up slowly is a good habit to prevent dizziness, but it does not directly prevent heart attacks or strokes. The real key to heart health is managing risk factors like diet, exercise, and medical conditions rather than worrying about sleeping position.

title: Fact Check: Can Sleeping with Onion Detox your whole body overnight?
claim_text: If you sleep with onions on your feet, you will detox your whole body overnight. It's also one of the best ways if you want to improve your immune system. It's one of the best ways to get rid of physical pain and inflammation in your body.
quick_take: The claim that sleeping with an onion on feet detoxifies the body overnight is completely FALSE and not supported by scientific evidence or medical consensus. Detoxification is an internal process handled by the liver, kidneys, and other organs. While onions are nutritious when consumed as part of a balanced diet, placing them on the body provides no proven health benefit.
doctor_explanation:
The claim that sleeping with an onion can detox your whole body overnight is false. Onions have certain benefits but there is no scientific evidence or medical consensus supporting the claim that placing onions on feet has any detoxifying effect. Detoxification is a complex biological process managed primarily by the liver and kidneys—not by vegetables placed on the skin.

How does the human body Detoxify?
The human body naturally detoxifies itself through several organs and systems. The liver plays the central role by breaking down toxins into less harmful substances that can be excreted. The kidneys filter blood to remove waste and excess fluids, which are expelled as urine. The lungs expel carbon dioxide and airborne toxins, while the skin eliminates waste through sweat. The digestive system also contributes by flushing out undigested food and harmful substances via the colon. Together, these systems work continuously to neutralize and remove toxins, maintaining internal balance and health without the need for external detox products.

Nutritional Benefits of Onion:
Onions are low in calories—just 45 per serving—and contain no fat or cholesterol. They are a good source of dietary fiber, vitamin C, vitamin B6, potassium, and essential nutrients like folate, calcium, and iron. Onions are also rich in organosulfur compounds, which have been associated with reducing blood pressure and cholesterol. One of the most beneficial compounds in onions is the flavonoid quercetin. It has anti-inflammatory properties, helps prevent the oxidation of low-density lipoprotein (LDL), supports vitamin E regeneration (a vital antioxidant), and may contribute to cancer prevention.

Scientific Evidence on Onions:
A study published in the Iranian Journal of Basic Medical Sciences concluded that onions may aid in preventing and managing components of metabolic syndrome—including dyslipidemia, hypertension, diabetes, and obesity— thereby reducing the risk of cardiovascular diseases. This is attributed to their antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and vasodilatory effects, as well as their ability to enhance insulin secretion and sensitivity, lower the absorption of cholesterol and glucose, regulate lipid and carbohydrate metabolism, and inhibit fat cell formation (adipogenesis). PMID: 33643564.

A study published in the International Journal of Molecular Sciences identified quercetin, a flavonoid present in onions, as possessing potent anti-inflammatory properties. These effects may help reduce inflammation associated with conditions, suggesting a potential therapeutic role for onions in managing inflammatory disorders. PMID: 33488935.

Dr. Pooja Pillai, Consultant - Internal Medicine, Aster CMI Hospital, Bangalore said: "Placing onions in your socks while you sleep is a popular home remedy said to 'detox' the body but there's no scientific proof it works. While onions do have antibacterial properties and can absorb odors, the idea that they pull toxins from your body through the feet is more folklore than fact. That said, if it helps you relax or sleep better, there's no harm in trying. Just remember, true detox comes from staying hydrated, eating well, and supporting your liver and kidneys. The body's real detox powerhouses."

Dr. Brunda M S, Consultant – Internal Medicine, Aster CMI Hospital, Bangalore said: "Sleeping with onions in your socks is an old folk remedy that's gained attention for its supposed detox benefits. The idea is that onions can draw out toxins through the soles of your feet while you sleep. While it's a comforting ritual for some, there's no scientific evidence proving it actually detoxifies the body. Onions do have natural antibacterial properties, but your liver and kidneys do the real detox work. Still, if it helps you feel better or sleep more soundly, there's no harm—sometimes wellness is as much about what comforts the mind as it is about science."

title: Fact Check: Can smartphone vision syndrome lead to blindness?
claim_text: Using smartphone in the dark can lead to smartphone vision syndrome or digital eye strain, and this can eventually lead to blindness.
quick_take: An Instagram post claims that smartphone vision syndrome can lead to blindness. We did a thorough fact check to term it as Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: Smartphone vision syndrome is also called digital eye strain or Computer Vision Syndrome (CVS). It is an amalgamation of eye and vision-related issues developing from the extended use of digital screens, such as smartphones, computers, and tablets. The smartphone vision syndrome symptoms include eye discomfort, headaches, blurred vision, dry eyes, and pain in the neck and shoulders. These problems are mostly due to glare from the screen, lighting, wrong viewing distance, plus prolonged use of the screen without breaks. Prolonged use of smartphones can affect your eyesight, but not in the way claimed. All these symptoms are generally temporary in nature and do not have a potential to cause permanent damage. There is no scientific evidence to suggest that smartphone vision syndrome can lead to permanent vision loss or blindness. Digital eye strain can cause temporary discomfort and visual disturbances, but it does not result in permanent damage to the eyes. The symptoms of digital eye strain are generally reversible with proper eye care, reduced screen time and lifestyle adjustments. A 2022 review on artificial blue light safety highlights that while blue light from digital devices can cause photochemical damage to the retina under certain conditions, the levels emitted by these devices are generally below safe viewing limits. The long-term effects of chronic exposure to low-illuminance blue light remain uncertain, with ongoing debate about its impact on eye health and circadian rhythms. Studies suggest that blue light may influence eye strain and sleep patterns, but more research is needed to understand the cumulative effects and develop appropriate safety guidelines. Dr Isha Agarwalla, an Ophthalmologist from Drishti Netralaya, Dibrugarh, Assam, states: "While prolonged exposure to blue light from smartphones and other digital devices can cause discomfort and contribute to digital eye strain, it does not lead to permanent vision loss or blindness. The symptoms of digital eye strain, such as headaches, dry eyes, and blurred vision, are generally temporary and can be managed with proper eye care and lifestyle adjustments. It's important to take regular breaks, use proper lighting, and adjust screen settings to reduce eye strain." Dr Aftab Alam, an Ophthalmologist, says: "Blue lights from most modern day gadgets do not harm eyes. So, blue cut lenses don't provide any extra benefits. However, continuous exposure to blue lights may disturb our sleep cycle. From that perspective, using blue cut lenses may help you stay protected or sleep better." Blue light, particularly between 415 and 455 nm, can penetrate the eye and cause damage to the retina, leading to visual fatigue and other symptoms. Sunlight is the largest source of blue light, while screens, fluorescent lights, and LED bulbs provide much less. The blue light from screens is not more harmful than the blue light from the sun. Research from The University of Toledo, conducted in vitro, found that blue light exposure causes retinal molecules to generate toxic chemicals that kill photoreceptor cells, which are essential for vision. However, the author of the study also said that the study does not show that light from mobile devices or other digital screens causes blindness. And, whether blue light from these sources induces similar toxicity levels is still unanswered.

title: Can using drumstick for pigmentation remove years of dark spots?
