quick_take: A social media post claims that using drumstick for pigmentation, especially by drinking soaked drumstick water, can remove years of dark spots. We fact checked it and found the claim to be mostly false.
doctor_explanation: There is no proof this works so quickly. There is no scientific study or dermatological guideline that supports the idea of soaked moringa water clearing years-old pigmentation overnight. Drumstick for pigmentation is a trending natural remedy online, but its effectiveness is exaggerated. Moringa does have skin-friendly nutrients like vitamin C and antioxidants, but changes in skin pigmentation take time. Years of sun damage or hormonal pigmentation cannot disappear in a day just by drinking herb-infused water. Pigmentation builds up deep within the skin over time. Removing it, even with clinical treatments, usually takes weeks or months. Claiming that a natural drink can reverse it instantly is misleading and medically inaccurate. We asked Dr Ekansh Shekhar, a Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant in Lucknow, about what causes skin pigmentation. He said, "Long-term pigmentation on the face often develops because of repeated sun exposure, hormonal changes, or skin inflammation like acne. When the skin gets injured or irritated, it can produce more melanin, which leads to dark spots or patches. Conditions like melasma or post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation are common examples. It's also important to remember that pigmentation can worsen without proper sun protection. Understanding the cause helps us choose the right treatment and prevent it from coming back." Moringa is rich in vitamin C, beta-carotene, polyphenols, and other antioxidants. These nutrients may help protect skin cells from environmental stress and support skin healing. Some studies support moringa for skin benefits. For example, a 2022 study suggests that moringa extracts in creams or oils may help with dry skin or inflammation. However, soaking moringa in water overnight and drinking it provides only a diluted amount of these nutrients. It's not concentrated enough to cause any noticeable change in pigmentation. To benefit from moringa, it needs to be part of a balanced diet or used in skincare products in effective formulations, not in water form alone. For expert insights, we spoke with Dr Rashi Soni, Co-founder and Consulting Dermatologist at Rashi Hospital, Mumbai. She says, "When it comes to stubborn pigmentation, we usually take a layered approach. The first and most important step is daily sun protection, because UV rays make pigmentation worse. Then we use creams that contain active ingredients like vitamin C, retinoids or niacinamide, which help lighten dark spots over time. In some cases, we recommend chemical peels or laser treatments to target deeper pigmentation. It's not a one-size-fits-all process, and it does take patience, but with the right plan, we can achieve noticeable and lasting results." The claim that using drumstick for pigmentation, especially by drinking soaked drumstick water, can remove years of pigmentation is mostly false. While moringa is a nutritious plant and may support general skin health as part of a healthy diet, there is no scientific evidence that drinking Moringa detox water clears old pigmentation, especially not overnight. For long-standing pigmentation, seek medical advice and follow proven treatments. Social media remedies may sound magical, but skin healing rarely happens that fast. Also, while drumstick benefits for skin are known in traditional medicine, they are best used in combination with clinical care, not as a stand-alone cure.

title: Fact Check: Can soaked raisins cure hemoglobin deficiency?
claim_text: eating soaked raisins cures anemia which is the deficiency of hemoglobin in the body
quick_take: A social media post claims that eating soaked raisins cure hemoglobin deficiency. We fact-checked and found the claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: Hemoglobin deficiency arises when there is an insufficient level of hemoglobin in red blood cells. Hemoglobin is vital for transporting oxygen from the lungs to the body's tissues and organs. Iron deficiency is a prevalent cause, impacting hemoglobin production. Common symptoms of anemia encompass fatigue, weakness, pale skin, shortness of breath, dizziness, and cold extremities. Treatment varies based on the underlying cause and may involve dietary adjustments, supplementation, blood transfusions, or addressing the primary medical condition. Hemoglobin is a protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen throughout the body. Iron deficiency can lead to low hemoglobin levels which can cause anaemia. While hemoglobin deficiency is a common cause of anemia, it does not necessarily mean that every instance of low hemoglobin levels will result in anemia. Hemoglobin deficiency can occur for various reasons, including nutritional deficiencies (such as iron, vitamin B12, or folic acid), chronic diseases, genetic conditions affecting hemoglobin structure or production, and blood loss. Raisins are dried grapes, and they are known for their sweet flavour. Raisins are a good source of antioxidants and may safeguard against iron deficiency. There is no scientific evidence of soaking raisins before eating. Eating raw dry fruits are also healthy. They provide essential vitamins, minerals, and fiber. While they are energy-dense, their natural sugars come with valuable nutrients. Soaking may help soften raisins, making them plumper and juicier. Soaking can rehydrate raisins that have become too dry or hard due to prolonged storage. Raisins are a source of iron, which is essential for hemoglobin production. However, while raisins contain iron, they might not be sufficient on their own to cure haemoglobin deficiency. Also, no evidence confirms that soaked raisins are much healthier than normal raisins. Evidence only suggests that eating soaking raisins overnight might make them easier to digest. Soaking may easily release some nutrients, making them more available for absorption by the body. So, soaked raisins might contribute to increasing iron intake for better haemoglobin levels. It is essential to have a balanced diet that includes various sources of iron along with vitamin C-rich foods that can enhance iron absorption. If someone has low haemoglobin or iron deficiency anaemia, it is crucial to consult a healthcare professional for proper evaluation and advice. They might recommend iron supplements or dietary changes tailored to the individual's needs. While soaked raisins can be a part of a balanced diet to support iron intake and potentially aid in managing haemoglobin deficiency, they may not be a standalone cure. Dr Kashyap explained that, 'determining the cause is crucial in the overall management of hemoglobin deficiency. Some of the common causes of hemoglobin deficiency include – blood loss, nutritional inadequacy, impaired red blood cell production, faulty red blood cell destruction, advanced diseases, chronic infection, renal or autoimmune disease, and thalassemia. Therefore, the main part of treatment is finding the underlying cause. For the treatment of anemia due to nutritional deficiency, iron, vitamin B12, or folic acid are used. Patients with severe iron deficiency may require blood transfusions to correct low hemoglobin levels.' Dietary modifications are fundamental in managing haemoglobin deficiency. Haemoglobin deficiency, often leading to anaemia, necessitates tailored treatment based on its cause and severity. Addressing this condition involves several approaches. So, a well-rounded diet rich in iron, vitamins, and minerals can prevent and combat anaemia. A doctor can prescribe iron supplements for individuals experiencing iron deficiency or absorption issues. Precision in dosage is crucial to avoid adverse effects. Vitamin supplements, particularly B12 and folate, play a pivotal role in red blood cell production. Deficiencies in these vitamins can contribute to anaemia, warranting supplementation. Treating underlying health conditions contributing to anaemia is vital. Conditions such as chronic kidney disease or internal bleeding require targeted treatment to improve haemoglobin levels. In severe cases with critically low haemoglobin levels, blood transfusions may be necessary for an immediate boost. However, this is typically reserved for emergencies. For specific scenarios like chronic kidney disease, erythropoietin-stimulating agents (ESAs) might be prescribed to stimulate red blood cell production. Lastly, bone marrow stimulants or transplants may be considered in rare, severe cases to enhance red blood cell production.

Moreover, some components of soursop have been associated with neurotoxicity, which could cause nerve damage. Parts of the plant, like the leaves, fruit, and seeds, are used as natural remedies in some tropical regions. Consuming these seeds, especially in large amounts, can cause nerve damage and has been linked to symptoms similar to Parkinson's disease. This risk is higher in areas where soursop is regularly eaten, as the neurotoxin affects the nervous system, potentially leading to motor issues. For cancer patients, depending on soursop alone can delay proper treatment, allowing cancer to worsen. title: Fact Check: Can Spit (Thook) Cure Pimples?
claim_text: Applying spit (thook) on the face can help cure pimples. Morning spit, especially before brushing, has antibiotic properties that can dry up and cure acne.
doctor_explanation: There is no scientific evidence or medical consensus supporting the claim that human saliva (spit or 'thook') cures pimples. Although saliva does contain certain mild antimicrobial properties that help inside the mouth, applying it to acne-prone skin can introduce harmful bacteria and potentially aggravate the condition. Doctors have cautioned against this practice and highlighted several possible side effects. In a video posted in December 2024, AIIMS dermatologist Dr. Gargi Taneja debunked the myth that saliva can treat acne. She explained: 'This is a common misconception that application of saliva on your pimples as well as rubbing it on your face can result in healthy and glowing skin as well as can decrease the acne. It should not be done because it can result in lots of side effects compared to benefits. Because in our saliva because of unhealthy oral condition, poor dental hygiene, lots of unhealthy bacterial proliferation, the pH of the saliva is acidic instead of being alkaline. So, when we apply this acidic saliva on the face, it can worsen your acne and damage your skin barrier and then can destroy your healthy skin also. Also, since the bacteria are not commensals, but are harmful bacteria, it can result in a lot of infection on your skin also.' Regarding acne pathophysiology, pimples (acne) occur when oil glands connected to hair follicles become inflamed. Sebaceous glands produce sebum (oil), which travels through pores to reach the skin's surface. In acne, sebum, dead skin cells, and hair become trapped in the pore, creating an ideal environment for bacteria to grow, triggering inflammation. Saliva is primarily made up of water along with vital proteins; its composition varies based on oral health status. Evidence-based first-line treatments for acne include topical retinoids, benzoyl peroxide, and azelaic acid (per Dawn Z. Eichenfield et al., PubMed: 34812859), along with salicylic acid, antibiotics, hormonal therapies, antiandrogens, sulphur, sodium sulfacetamide, and alpha hydroxy acids. Severe cases may require oral antibiotics, hormonal therapy, or isotretinoin. The claim by actress Tamannaah Bhatia that morning spit has 'enough antibiotic' properties is not supported by any medical evidence.

It is known for its numerous health benefits, including potential effects on hair health. One can consume fenugreek seeds in various forms, including as sprouts, which can potentially enhance their nutritional value. Sprouted fenugreek has possible benefits for hair health due to its rich nutrient profile and traditional use. However, there is little scientific evidence supporting its effectiveness in promoting hair regrowth or regeneration. We need more research to come to a conclusion. Numerous anecdotal reports suggest that applying fenugreek seed paste or consuming the seeds promotes hair growth. However, there aren't enough scientific studies to back these claims. Proponents of using sprouted fenugreek for hair regeneration argue that its high content of vitamins (such as vitamin A, C, and B-complex), minerals (including iron and zinc), and plant compounds (like flavonoids and saponins) can stimulate hair follicles, improve scalp health, and promote hair regrowth. But the scientific evidence is insufficient and not conclusive. Also, fenugreek alone cannot guarantee regeneration of lost hair or hair regrowth. Hair loss happens due to multiple factors and a professional can help better with the correct diagnosis and treatment. Fenugreek seeds are rich in nutrients essential for hair health. Iron helps in maintaining proper blood circulation to the scalp, while vitamins A and C are crucial for maintaining the health of hair follicles. Fenugreek has anti-inflammatory properties that can help reduce scalp inflammation, a factor that can contribute to hair loss. Fenugreek has phytoestrogens, which are likely to balance hormone levels and could possibly address hair loss related to hormonal imbalances. Some experts acknowledge the traditional use of fenugreek in promoting hair health. But they emphasize the lack of solid clinical trials to prove its effectiveness. Dr Sachin Gupta, Dermatologist at Amrita Hospital, Faridabad states: 'Fenugreek has properties that theoretically could support hair health, but we need more rigorous scientific studies to establish its efficacy in hair regrowth. Its use in hair care includes making pastes from the seeds or consuming the sprouts for their nutritional benefits. To conclude, current evidence on the effectiveness of sprouted fenugreek in promoting hair regrowth is largely anecdotal and based on traditional practices. Fenugreek seeds are nutritious and have properties that could possibly support hair health. But there is a significant gap in clinical research directly linking their consumption to hair regrowth. People interested in using fenugreek for hair health should approach it as a complementary method. We recommend consulting healthcare professionals before making any significant changes to your diet or hair care routine, especially in cases of severe hair loss.

title: Can stage IV cancer be eradicated with a miracle cure?
claim_text: Stage 4 cancer can be completely eradicated by boiling two cloves, one cardamom pod, one tablespoon of fenugreek seeds, and cinnamon powder in a glass of water.
quick_take: A social media post asserts that an Ayurvedic concoction may successfully cure cancers at advanced stages. After verifying the claim, we discovered that it is mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Cancer develops when normal cells undergo genetic and molecular alterations, resulting in their unregulated growth and proliferation and impairing physiological processes. Cancer staging is the process of determining the extent to which the disease has spread throughout the body. It serves to provide consistent communication among the specialists involved in cancer management, determine prognosis, and inform therapy options. The TNM staging system is the widely used approach for the classification of the condition. According to the TNM criteria, cancer is categorised into four stages. Stage I cancer is small, localised, and free of metastases or nodal involvement. Stage II includes locally progressed tumours or early nodal involvement. Stage III denotes the later stages of locally advanced cancer with more extensive nodal involvement. The hallmark of stage IV, however, is distant metastases, which indicates the cancer cells may spread to other organs. The fourth stage is the most lethal of all. This may be because of its propensity to spread, which compels the treatment into a palliative framework that aims to relieve symptoms and impede the progression of the disease. Furthermore, systemic dissemination puts patients at risk for consequences that could significantly lower survival rates, organ dysfunction, and malnutrition. Ayurvedic texts acknowledge Stage IV cancer as Arbuda, a massive, systemic tumour where a dosha imbalance has overwhelmed the body's defence and metabolic systems. The key objective of Ayurvedic therapy is to determine the root cause of an illness, and its four treatment pillars are as follows: Prakritisthapani chikitsa or overall maintenance of health, Rasayana therapy for the restoration of normal function, Roganashani chikitsa for managing the disease, Naishthiki chikitsa or the spiritual approach. Popular medicinal blends found in Ayurveda are composed of several herbs that have been shown to have significant cancer-curing potential; from a scientific standpoint, these formulations affect various organ systems, participate in various biochemical reactions, and support the body's defence mechanisms. Dr. P. Rammanohar, Research Director at Amrita School of Ayurveda, states that cancer is a complicated illness that cannot be easily cured. Every type requires a different course of treatment, which frequently includes radiation, chemotherapy, or targeted medications. There is no single herb or natural remedy for all types of cancer. While several herbs have shown potential in preliminary laboratory research, there isn't enough conclusive data from human trials to regard them as effective medicines. It is critical to consult qualified medical professionals and rely on established therapies before implementing anything else. Ayurveda employs a tailored, multimodal approach for addressing the metastatic stage, even when curative treatment is no longer viable. This approach seeks to restore metabolic equilibrium, strengthen immunity, enhance resilience, facilitate symptomatic relief, or cleanse tissues while also enhancing quality of life. As per scientific evidence available, malignancy should never be taken lightly. It is important to note that there is rarely a cure at this stage; instead, contemporary medicine seeks to manage the progression of the illness, relieve symptoms, and improve quality of life. This is often accomplished by a team of oncologists, surgeons, radiologists, palliative care specialists, and allied health workers using a carefully crafted interdisciplinary approach. Medical oncologists lead the systemic therapy, which includes immunotherapy, targeted medicines, and chemotherapy. The treatment plan is influenced by the type of cancer, biomarkers, and previous therapies. Isolated masses may be removed using radiation therapy and surgery. People in stage IV frequently suffer from malnutrition and muscle loss. Therefore, individualised nutrition plans could be utilised to support ongoing cancer therapy. Furthermore, the patient undergoing therapy may seek psychosocial support that tackles existential concerns, anxiety, depression, and fatigue. Additionally, palliative therapy may aid in the management of symptoms or complete pain alleviation. Stage IV cancer is therefore not a passive condition; rather, it requires planned, scientifically backed interventions aimed at prolonging a good quality of life. It is important to note that there is no such thing as a 'miracle cure', and relying on such unproven remedies can be completely fatal because they have not been subjected to scientific examination, clinical validation, or approval by global cancer treatment protocols. One such unverified Ayurvedic preparation composed of fenugreek, cinnamon, cloves, and cardamom has been asserted in the post. Since the mentioned ingredients are being considered for the eradication of advanced-stage cancer, it becomes critical to understand the rationale behind these claims: Despite their preclinical indications, none of the spices—fenugreek, cinnamon, cardamom, and clove—have been proven to be effective treatments for stage IV cancer in clinical trials; depending on them as the sole option could be extremely risky, leading to toxicity, contamination, postponed treatment, or even exacerbating the ongoing condition. Dr. Rakesh Sharma, Senior Consultant and HOD Medical Oncology, SHALBY Sanar International Hospital, Gurugram, who suggests that while these spices contain bioactive compounds with reported antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-proliferative effects, claims that they can cure cancer, especially late-stage cancer, are false and not supported by scientific evidence. It's crucial to rely on established cancer treatments and consult with healthcare professionals. Treatment with ethanolic extracts of clove, cardamom, and fenugreek results in a marked decrease in total protein content. This suggests that these extracts may induce proteolytic activities or inhibit protein synthesis, contributing to their anti-cancer effects. There is ongoing research on combining these agents with cancer therapy. Patients with stage IV cancer may be considered clinically cancer-free if there are no visible cancerous symptoms based on available diagnostic tools. This may not necessarily imply a cure because the disease may still be present at levels too low to detect even with ongoing oncological treatment. Dr. Rakesh Sharma explains that patients with stage-IV cancer can be completely cancer-free in certain scenarios. Patients with stage-IV lymphoma, breast cancer with limited metastasis and germ cell tumours can be cured with proper treatment with a multi-disciplinary approach. However, it is crucial to stress that recurrence is always a possibility, especially in cases with advanced-stage cancer, even when the disease appears to be undetectable.

title: Fact Check: Can storing potatoes and onions together kill a child?
claim_text: According to an Instagram post, keeping potatoes (aloo) and onions (pyaaj) together can be extremely harmful and even kill a child. The video shows a child having a seizure and claims the child died because these vegetables were stored together. It says this is not a rumour but a scientific fact. The post claims onions release a chemical that makes potatoes sprout early, leading to the formation of toxic substances called solanine and chaconine. It warns that these can make the entire family sick, causing symptoms like stomach pain, vomiting, nausea, weakness, diarrhoea, fever, headache, breathlessness, coma, or even death. The video also claims that this is often the hidden reason behind sudden deaths in children.
quick_take: A social media post claims that storing potatoes and onions together can kill a child. Our fact check concludes that this is false.
doctor_explanation: Can onions really make potatoes toxic? No, onions don't make potatoes toxic. It's true that storing onions and potatoes together can lead to faster spoilage, but not because onions release any toxic chemical. Both vegetables release moisture and gases that encourage each other to sprout or rot more quickly. However, this is about food quality and shelf life—not toxicity. The claim that onions trigger a chemical reaction that makes potatoes harmful is untrue. No research supports this. Do sprouted potatoes contain harmful substances? Yes, but only if eaten in large amounts or when clearly spoiled. Sprouted potatoes can contain natural chemicals called glycoalkaloids—mainly solanine and chaconine. These are part of the plant's defence system. In high amounts, they can cause mild poisoning. Symptoms may include stomach pain, vomiting, or diarrhoea. But the risk of serious illness or death from eating a small amount at home is extremely low. In 2022, a case report from Saudi Arabia described an 11-year-old boy who became sick after eating raw, sprouted potatoes. He had stomach pain, vomiting, and later developed slow heart rate and breathing issues. Doctors suspected solanine poisoning. The boy was treated in hospital and made a full recovery. The report did not mention onions or say that storing onions with potatoes caused the problem. It also said that solanine poisoning is rare and usually happens only when a large amount is eaten. Shruti K Bhardwaj, Chief Clinical Nutritionist at Zydus Hospital, Ahmedabad, explains, 'Yes, sprouted or green potatoes can develop natural compounds called glycoalkaloids, mainly solanine, which are the plant's way of defending itself. These chemicals are found in higher amounts when potatoes are exposed to light, stored for too long, or begin to sprout. If eaten in large quantities, they can irritate the stomach and, in rare cases, cause more serious symptoms. But the key thing to remember is this: the average person isn't likely to get sick from eating one or two sprouted potatoes by mistake. Just look out for green skin or deep sprouts, and if in doubt, throw it out. It's more about food quality and taste than a serious health hazard in everyday situations.' If a potato has green patches or deep sprouts, it's safest to throw it away. But keeping it near onions won't make it toxic. Can solanine poisoning kill a child? Extremely unlikely, especially from household vegetables. Severe solanine poisoning is very rare. For it to become deadly, a child would need to eat a large quantity of highly spoiled or green potatoes. The idea that one or two sprouted potatoes—caused by storing them near onions—could kill a child is scientifically baseless. The symptoms shown in the video, like seizures or coma, are not typical of common food spoilage. Is the video showing a real cause-effect situation? No, the video is misleading with unrelated visuals. The video shows a child having a seizure and connects it to storing onions and potatoes together. However, seizures in children can be due to many medical conditions, like epilepsy, high fever, or infections. There is no evidence that food spoilage which arises due to co-storage of vegetables can lead to such a reaction. The video uses fear tactics and emotional manipulation without any scientific backing. Is there any merit to keeping onions and potatoes apart? Yes, but only to reduce spoilage—not for safety reasons. Onions and potatoes should ideally be stored separately. Onions prefer dry, ventilated conditions. Potatoes last longer in cool, dark places. Storing them together may make them spoil faster, but it won't create harmful toxins. It's more about reducing food waste, not preventing illness. Dr Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition, states, 'Yes, there's good reason to store onions and potatoes separately. Onions naturally release ethylene gas, which can speed up sprouting and spoilage in potatoes. At the same time, potatoes release moisture, creating a damp environment that can cause onions to soften and develop mould. When kept together, this exchange makes both spoil faster. To help them last longer, store onions and potatoes in separate, cool, dry, and well-ventilated spots.' THIP Media Take: The claim that storing potatoes and onions together can kill a child is false. There is no scientific evidence to support it. While it's true that these vegetables should be stored separately for better shelf life, they do not release toxic chemicals that can kill. The post uses scary visuals and unverified science to spread fear. Always check facts before believing or sharing health claims online.

title: Fact Check: Can strawberries be used to treat tooth discoloration? - THIP Media

doctor_explanation: Tooth discoloration is a common dental observation associated with both clinical and cosmetic issues. It varies in underlying cause, appearance, composition, location, severity, and firmness of adherence to the tooth surface. The discoloration could be caused by both external and internal factors. Intrinsic discoloration is usually caused by a congenital or systemic condition, while external variables such as coffee, tea, tobacco, and medications, as well as aging, can cause external discoloration. Strawberries are thought to have teeth-whitening characteristics, but these properties are ineffective and short-lived. However, citric acid is known to expedite tooth demineralization, which eventually weakens the tooth enamel, making it susceptible to sensitivity and even tooth decay. Citric acid breaks down your tooth enamel, making any benefit of whitening negligible. Also, strawberries don't contain any ingredients that can actually lift stains to whiten your teeth. It dissolves your enamel which brushes away while brushing. Hence, harming the tooth. In cases of intrinsic stains, strawberries are of no help. Any visible whitening effect from using strawberries is temporary, leaving the enamel demineralized. Dr. Paridhi Garg, Endodontist, Noida, says, 'Strawberries don't whiten the teeth. Strawberries have citric acid which will harm and demineralize the enamel on the contrary, causing hypersensitivity. Strawberries also have a high sugar content which will make the teeth more prone to decay and the probability of cavities also increases.'

title: Can strict diet and lifestyle change reverse Stage 4 Cancer?

Various social media users are sharing reels created from a part of interview claiming that stage 4 Cancer can be reversed in just 40 days. Our fact-check reveals this claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: The claim that stage 4 cancer can be reversed in 40 days through diet alone is medically implausible and false. Dr Pooja Khullar, Radiation Oncologist at Dharamshila Narayana Super Specialty Hospital, New Delhi explains that while fasting may have some benefits for people undergoing Cancer treatments like Chemotherapy, it is not a cure for cancer. Cancer cells cannot be isolated separately and treated with fasting - the effect of fasting is uniform on the body. Curcumin (found in turmeric) has shown promise in laboratory studies for anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, but these findings do not equate to a cure, especially for advanced cancer. Neem leaves may have health benefits, but being able to treat and completely cure Stage 4 Cancer is not supported by any medical research. While lemon juice has some anti-cancerous properties, it is a gross exaggeration to say that drinking lemon water will cure Cancer. Dr P Rammanohar, Research Director at Amrita School of Ayurveda states, 'Cancer is not a single disease and there is no remedy for cancer. Different types of cancer are treated with different procedures of chemotherapy. One drug/herb does not work across all cancers. Even though some studies have shown that some plant/herbs may have anticancer benefits, they cannot be used to treat patients.' Dr Mohit Sandhu, Consultant Ayurveda Professional explains that while Ayurveda can work with regular Cancer treatments to enhance effectiveness or manage side effects, promoting Ayurveda as a sole replacement for Chemotherapy is misleading. Dr Sukrit Kumar, Medical Director at Rainbow Children's Hospitals emphasizes that 'Cancer's complexity demands interventions targeting specific mutations, cellular pathways, or immune responses—areas where Ayurveda lacks the precision of modern medicine.' Dr Sarthak Moharir, Chief Radiation Oncologist at Apollo Cancer Centre states, 'In the case of cancer medicine and Oncology, no drug has been proven to cure cancer. Hence, no herb/herbal drug/herbal drug cocktail is used in any treatment algorithm for any kind of cancer.' Stage 4 cancer is the most advanced form, with treatment goals typically focused on extending life, managing symptoms, and improving quality of life rather than achieving a cure. The Tata Memorial Hospital released a statement signed by 262 oncologists urging people 'not to get fooled' and to continue with evidence-based care. Mr. Sidhu himself accepted in the interview that his wife was undergoing proper Cancer treatments - something social media users ignored and credited the entire recovery to strict diet regime.

title: Fact Check: Can sugarcane juice manage diabetes in just 10 days?
claim_text: According to a widely shared Instagram post by Sehatmantarna, consuming freshly made sugarcane juice (without any additives) regularly is effective for managing diabetes in 10 days. (Hindi caption: गन्ने के जूस से करें 10 दिन में शुगर खत्म)
quick_take: An Instagram reel asserts that consuming sugarcane juice can manage diabetes in just ten days. After verifying the claim, we determined that it is completely false.
doctor_explanation:
Blood glucose regulation, also known as glucose homeostasis, is a mechanism used by the body to maintain stable blood sugar levels within an established range, often between 70 and 140 mg/dL. This precise equilibrium is necessary to keep cells' energy supply constant and prevent the harmful effects of both high and low blood sugar. Diabetes impairs this regulatory mechanism.

Sugarcane juice is a natural liquid made from compressed sugarcane stalks. While it is rich in carbohydrates, vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants, it should not be consumed by individuals with diabetes due to its moderate to high glycaemic index, which is mostly brought on by its high sucrose content, which may raise blood glucose levels. The advantages—hydration, vitamin provision, and antioxidant activity—do not outweigh the concerns of high blood glucose levels. Furthermore, the available data does not justify its inclusion in the overall diabetes management plan. Therefore, sugarcane juice is not a therapeutic choice for controlling diabetes.

While a well-crafted, customised diet is essential for managing diabetes, it cannot replace evidence-based diabetes therapy. Healthy dietary options may complement insulin therapy in type 1 patients and, in certain cases, may help reduce the reliance on medication for those with T2D. Nonetheless, patients still need insulin or prescription medications to attain optimal glycaemic control. All medications, including those used for controlling diabetes, undergo extensive clinical testing to ensure their efficacy and reliability.

Dr. Ritesh Bansal, the founder and senior consultant diabetologist of Delhi's Saroj Diabetes & Research Centre, explains that while dietary changes can help in the management of diabetes, they shouldn't be seen as a practical substitute for prescription diabetic medications. Consequently, dietary changes could be an advantageous supplement that may reduce the need for high medication doses. Dr. Bansal advises seeking expert advice before implementing any nutritional changes as part of a therapy regimen.

Diabetes is a persistent illness that exhibits gradual progression. Type 1 diabetes is autoimmune in origin, caused by immune cells accidentally damaging the beta cells of the pancreas that create insulin, necessitating long-term prescribed insulin therapy. Type 2 diabetes is caused by insulin resistance and progressive beta-cell dysfunction brought on by heredity, obesity, and a sedentary lifestyle. Supervised diet and exercise regimens may temporarily improve glycaemic control in certain T2D patients; nevertheless, this is not a substitute for therapy. From a scientific viewpoint, diabetes, especially Type 1, is currently considered incurable. Although some early-stage patients may achieve remission through significant lifestyle changes or therapeutic intervention, type 2 diabetes does not qualify for a permanent cure.

Dr. Naseemuddin N. Shaikh, Consultant Endocrinologist at Renova Century Hospitals, Banjara Hills, Hyderabad, explains the primary distinction between cure and remission. The cure is when the illness is totally eradicated and won't recur, like when prescribed medicines are used to treat a bacterial infection. On the other hand, remission is a stage in which the disease is under control and does not require treatment; however, it may return. Diabetes is a progressive disease that calls for adherence to evidence-based medical therapies. This is particularly true for type 1, which requires insulin therapy for the rest of one's life. Early-stage type 2 diabetes can undergo remission with a multifaceted strategy that includes prescribed medications, low-glycaemic foods, and 30 to 45 minutes of aerobic exercise each day. Therefore, it is not advised to forego treatment based on unsubstantiated assertions made online.

Hyperglycaemia necessitates a multimodal strategy. Along with a healthy lifestyle, prescribed medications such as insulin therapy for Type 1 and oral hypoglycemics for Type 2 diabetes are usually employed to manage unregulated blood glucose levels. This is supported by psychological counselling, timely patient education, and three- to six-monthly HbA1c level monitoring. Failure to comply with diabetic medication as prescribed might worsen blood glucose levels and exacerbate its consequences. The persistent rise may cause damage to blood vessels and nerves, leading to cardiovascular illness, renal impairment, vision loss, and neuropathy.

title: Fact Check: Can sunscreens cause melanoma? - THIP Media
claim_text: Sunscreen is a MASSIVE scam 🚨 Sunscreen users have the highest rates of melanoma. This is because it's inhibiting their body from producing melanin, the hormone to help you tan! Sunscreen also contains many harmful chemicals which are heavily linked to cancer.
quick_take: A social media post claims that sunscreens are a massive scam and that sunscreens cause melanoma. We did the fact check and found out the claim to be false.
doctor_explanation:
Melanoma, a type of skin cancer, starts in melanocytes. These are the cells that make melanin, the pigment that gives skin its color. Uncontrolled growth of these cells can cause tumours, leading to melanoma. Early detection is important because untreated melanoma can spread to other body parts. Regular checkups for skin and protecting skin from the sun are essential for preventing melanoma.

It is not true that sunscreens cause melanoma. In fact, sunscreen is an important tool which helps protect the skin from harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation. The UV rays are a major risk factor for developing melanoma and other types of skin cancer. Sunscreens work by absorbing or reflecting UV rays, reducing the skin's exposure to them. Using sunscreen, along with other sun protection measures like wearing protective clothing and seeking shade, can help lower the risk of melanoma and other skin cancers.

Dr Aseem Sharma, Director and Chief Dermatologist at Skin Saga Centre for Dermatology, Mumbai, for his opinion on sunscreens causing cancer. He says, "4-MBC, also recognised as enzacamene, is a chemical component found in sunscreens. While certain studies indicate its potential to disrupt the endocrine system, there's insufficient direct evidence linking it to cancer in humans. It's essential to weigh these concerns against the established advantages of sunscreen in shielding against skin cancer. Opting for physical sunscreens containing zinc oxide or titanium dioxide may offer a safer choice for individuals wary of chemical sunscreen ingredients."

Sunscreen is generally safe and effective when used as directed. Some individuals may experience long-term side effects, although they are relatively rare. There's an ongoing debate around sunscreen usage and Vitamin D deficiency, but we did not find any studies linking both. Regular sunscreen use does not cause Vitamin D deficiency.

The benefits of using sunscreen in protecting against sunburn, skin cancer, and premature ageing generally outweigh the potential risks associated with long-term use. Individuals concerned about possible side effects can opt for mineral-based sunscreens containing zinc oxide or titanium dioxide. These are considered safe and less likely to cause skin irritation or systemic effects. Additionally, consulting with a dermatologist can provide personalised recommendations for sunscreen use based on individual skin type.

title: Can supplements stop weight from coming back? - THIP Media
claim_text: A social media video features a claimant stating that taking a combination of Water Out, Super Cut, Gold Capsule, and Yohimbine supplements for six weeks can tone the body and give it a glowing appearance without the need for exercise. He claims that after completing the six-week course, the fat will never return.
quick_take: A social media video claims that combining Water Out, Super Cut, Gold Capsule, and Yohimbine supplements can prevent fat from returning. We fact checked and found the claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: Are these featured supplements truly natural? No. The term "natural" is frequently misused in the supplement industry, often creating a false sense of safety and effectiveness. While some ingredients in these supplements originate from plants, many others are either synthetic, pharmaceutical-grade, or even chemically altered from their natural sources. For instance, Water Out contains diuretic herbs like dandelion and juniper berry. While these are natural, Gold Capsule includes Swarn Bhasma (gold ash) and Makardhwaj, which are traditional Ayurvedic ingredients but may contain heavy metals such as mercury. Super Cut contains synthetic compounds like Liothyronine (T3), a pharmaceutical thyroid hormone, and Clenbuterol, a potent bronchodilator with strong metabolic effects and it is banned by WADA. These ingredients are not natural in any safe or health-promoting sense. Similarly, Yohimbine, although extracted from tree bark, is highly potent and can have severe side effects, including increased heart rate, heightened anxiety, and potential cardiovascular risks. Despite some of these components originating from natural sources, the overall composition of these supplements is far from "natural" in the way the term is often understood. The presence of pharmaceutical drugs, potent stimulants, and potentially toxic metals makes it clear that these products cannot be classified as purely natural or inherently safe. Can these supplements burn fat without exercise? No. The fundamental principle of fat loss revolves around creating a calorie deficit, burning more calories than consumed. No supplement can make the body burn significant amounts of fat without proper diet and physical activity. While Super Cut and Yohimbine may slightly enhance fat oxidation, their effects are marginal without a structured diet and exercise plan. Water Out only results in temporary weight loss due to dehydration rather than actual fat reduction. Ultimately, these supplements cannot substitute for the metabolic effects of physical activity, which remains the most effective and sustainable way to lose fat. Hakim Bharmal, Master Trainer and Contest Preparation Coach from Maharashtra, said that many supplements claiming rapid weight loss are often ineffective and a waste of money. He cautioned against the use of products like water cut, which is essentially a diuretic supplement. These products work by flushing out essential electrolytes like magnesium and potassium from the body, leading to excessive water loss. While this may result in a temporary drop in weight, it is not fat loss but rather the loss of water weight. He emphasized that although water cut supplements are in high demand, particularly in the bodybuilding and sports community for quick weight reduction before competitions, they come with severe risks. Depletion of vital electrolytes can lead to dangerous health conditions, including heart issues, dehydration, and even diarrhea. In extreme cases, the side effects could be life-threatening. Can these supplements prevent fat regain? No. Fat regain occurs due to a combination of metabolic adaptation, caloric intake, and hormonal regulation. After weight loss, the body naturally slows its metabolism to conserve energy, making fat regain easier. Additionally, without maintaining a proper diet and lifestyle, any weight lost—whether through natural means or supplements—will return over time. These supplements do not address the biological mechanisms of long-term weight maintenance. They may cause short-term changes, but without sustained healthy habits, they offer no long-term solution to preventing fat regain. Hakim Bharmal strongly advised against the use of such supplements, especially for the general population looking to lose 5-10 kgs quickly, as the risks associated with these products far outweigh any potential benefits. Are these supplements safe without expert guidance? No. Several ingredients in these supplements are associated with serious health risks when taken without proper supervision. Without professional guidance, the risks of these supplements far outweigh their potential benefits. When asked Dr Varsha Kachroo, Consultant Endocrinologist, Yatharth Superspeciality Hospital, Noida, she answered, "No, these substances when consumed as stimulants, without medical supervision can definitely lead to metabolic issues. Usually these are co-ingested along with anabolic steroids. Thyroid hormones when used as stimulants without a definitive therapeutic indication can lead to thyrotoxicosis, tachyarrhythmias, thyroid storm, osteoporosis, psychological problems, hypokalemic periodic paralysis and other hormonal disruptions. Clenbuterol is mainly used as a bronchodilator for treatment of asthma in animals. WADA classifies it as an anabolic agent rather than for medicinal purposes. It also leads to tachyarrhythmias, hypokalemia, hyperglycemia, palpitations and chest pain, thyroid dysfunction, heart failure and myocardial ischemia." So the bottom line is to use these medications if and only when prescribed by your health care professional. What are the health risks? Significant and Dangerous. The ingredients in these supplements can have severe and even life-threatening side effects. Many of these substances are banned or require prescriptions in regulated countries due to their potential harm.

title: Fact Check: Can sweet potatoes help to decrease labor pain? - THIP Media

quick_take: A number of Facebook and Instagram posts claim sweet potatoes can decrease labor pains and hence implying expecting mothers should eat a lot of sweet potatoes before delivery. We fact-checked the claim and found it to be mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Endorphins are a group of hormones that have varied physiological functions. They are produced and stored in the pituitary gland. Endorphins belong to a group of hormones that are generally referred to as "Happy Hormones." They are produced when we do something or eat something that makes us satisfied. Other hormones in this group are dopamine, serotonin, and oxytocin. There are a number of studies that have related endorphins to the body's ability of pain management. Researchers note that opioid medications (that are often prescribed for pain endurance in a post-operative scenario) work by mimicking natural endorphins. There are studies that have linked endorphin deficiency to chronic headaches and fibromyalgia. Endorphins are also believed to have a role to play in handling labor pain. In a study done on pregnant women, researchers have noted endorphin "may increase the ability of women to tolerate acute pain." In another small study done on a small group of 45 healthy women giving birth, scientists found that the endorphin levels are low post-delivery thereby raising the need for pain treatment medications. However, further studies are required to conclusively deduce that endorphins can reduce labor pain significantly. No conclusive evidence. We have found no specific research that suggests sweet potatoes can produce endorphins. No conclusive evidence. A study done on mice in 2017, showed that extract of purple sweet potato color may help reduce the risk of inflammation and obesity. But this does not necessarily translate into the same effect on humans. Dr. Arpita Chakraborty, MS (OBGY) says, "Sweet potato cannot potentially reduce the labor pains at the time of delivery. Labor pains rank very high on pain levels and have been classified as the most severe form of pain that the human body can tolerate. Eating a few sweet potatoes just before your delivery may not cause a huge difference. Rather, Solid food during active labor is not advised due to the risk of vomiting which very remotely carries the risk of aspiration, which could be very dangerous. Moreover, a normal labor pain doesn't always culminate in normal vaginal delivery due to numerous obstetrical causes and the only option that remains is a cesarean section for which we require a fasting/empty stomach status for uneventful anesthesia induction and maintenance. Dr. Chakraborty puts in a word of caution, "females in the latent phase of labor can have any kind of nutritious food that they prefer or like. However, if you have gestational diabetes, sweet potato is not recommended for you."

Therefore, even though vitamin D supplements can reduce the risk of respiratory infection, there is not enough data to state that it reduces the respiratory infection exactly by 42%. title: Fact Check: Can tamarind seeds cure arthritis?
claim_text: According to an Instagram video, tamarind seeds can cure arthritis. The woman in the video says her mother suffers from joint pain and that "even western medicine cannot cure arthritis." The video suggests consuming tamarind seeds, either roasted, soaked, or powdered in dishes like dosa or porridge.
quick_take: A social media post claims that tamarind seeds can cure arthritis and relieve joint pain. We did the fact check to term this claim as false.
doctor_explanation: Do tamarind seeds have healing properties for arthritis? Not really. Even though tamarind seeds contain some compounds that might have health benefits, there is no scientific proof that they can cure arthritis. Arthritis is a chronic condition that usually requires long-term management, including medical treatments. Tamarind seeds alone will not cure it. A 2019 study tested a combination of tamarind seed extract and turmeric to relieve knee pain and improve joint function. The study showed that after 90 days, participants who took the extract had less pain and better mobility compared to those who took a placebo. A 2015 study showed that tamarind seed extract helps protect cartilage and bone by reducing harmful enzymes and inflammation linked to arthritis. It also helped balance antioxidant levels in the body, showing promise as a treatment for arthritis symptoms. In short, tamarind seed extract might help some people with joint pain and arthritis, but we need more studies to prove how effective it really is. Also, the studies use extracts in specific dosages for pain relief, which can be difficult to replicate in real life by consuming the seeds directly. Can tamarind seeds really cure arthritis? No, tamarind seeds cannot cure arthritis. In fact arthritis has no cure, yet. Tamarind seeds contain antioxidants and anti-inflammatory compounds, which are helpful for general health and may offer some minor relief from inflammation. However, there is no strong evidence to suggest that consuming tamarind seeds can significantly reduce arthritis pain. The effects, if any, are very mild. Arthritis requires much more than just eating tamarind seeds for effective symptom relief. Dr Aryan Kumar Mohanty, Senior Resident, Department of Orthopaedics, MKCG Medical College & Hospital, Berhampur, Odisha, says: "Arthritis is a chronic condition, meaning it cannot be cured, but its symptoms can be managed. Tamarind seeds are thought to contain nutrients that might help reduce inflammation, but they cannot address the underlying causes of arthritis, such as joint wear and tear or autoimmune issues. It's important to focus on treatments that are proven to slow progression and improve mobility, like prescribed medication and regular exercise." Dr Almas Fatma, MBBS, Diploma in Family Medicine, PG in Digital Health, General Physician from Navi Mumbai, explains: "Arthritis, unfortunately, has no complete cure. It's a condition that causes joint inflammation and damage, which cannot be reversed. While tamarind seeds have some anti-inflammatory properties, they cannot repair joint tissues or stop arthritis from progressing. Effective management requires a combination of medical treatments, physical therapy, and lifestyle adjustments. Relying solely on tamarind seeds or similar remedies can delay proper care." Can tamarind seeds help with inflammation? Maybe, but not enough to cure arthritis. Tamarind seeds do contain flavonoids and other antioxidants, which are known to help fight inflammation. In some cases, eating foods with anti-inflammatory properties can help manage symptoms. However, it's important to remember that arthritis is more than just inflammation. It's a complex disease that affects joints in ways tamarind seeds alone can't fix. Can tamarind seeds replace traditional arthritis treatments? No, tamarind seeds should not replace proper medical treatments for arthritis. Arthritis is a serious condition, and while some natural remedies may provide mild relief, they cannot cure or fully manage the disease. Treatments such as medications, physical therapy, and lifestyle changes are necessary for effective management.

title: Fact Check: Can tartar be removed using foaming agents? - THIP Media
claim_text: A Facebook post promoting a teeth-whitening foaming toothpaste claims that it can remove plaque and tartar.
quick_take: A social media post claims that a teeth whitening foaming toothpaste can remove tartar. We fact-checked and found this claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation:
## What is tartar?
Calculus, also referred to as tartar, is essentially an accumulation of plaque and minerals from the saliva that solidifies. Tartar is formed by the precipitation of calcium phosphate on dental plaque, particularly in an alkaline environment. The surface of teeth gets covered in tooth tartar, which in severe cases can be seen below the gum line. The tartar covers the teeth like a crust. Due to its high porosity, it is vulnerable to stains from food and drinks.

## Is it advisable to get rid of dental tartar at home?
No, definitely not. Plaque and tartar pose a significant risk to the health of your teeth. The removal of this dental tartar is crucial because its persistence can worsen gum disease, damage enamel, and cause bad breath. Unfortunately, it is unlikely that a toothbrush and floss will be able to remove plaque once it has hardened into tartar. It is not a good idea to use at-home tools to scrape tartar off of yourself. This is due to the possibility of damaging one's smile through improper use of electric tartar removal devices, which necessitates special training. If misused, they might cause gum damage and infection. Furthermore, harsh devices can wear down the enamel on your teeth, causing sensitivity and caries. Remember that once lost, the enamel—the outer, protective layer of teeth—cannot be replaced.

## Can tartar be removed using foaming agents?
Not exactly. While there are many products on the market that claim to help remove tartar, most dental professionals agree that the only effective way to remove tartar is through a professional cleaning by a dentist or dental hygienist. Foaming agents such as toothpaste, mouthwash, and other oral care products can help to prevent tartar buildup by reducing the amount of plaque on teeth. However, once tartar has formed, it cannot be removed by foaming agents alone. Tartar is too hard and firmly attached to teeth to be removed by brushing or other at-home methods.

## How can tartar and plaque buildup be prevented at home?
Plaque can quickly calcify into tartar. Therefore, maintaining good oral hygiene is essential for preventing the development of dental tartar and plaque. The best way to control plaque is to brush your teeth for two minutes at a time, twice daily, with a prescription toothpaste. Brushing should be done at a 45-degree angle with a soft bristle brush so that the bristles can reach the areas between the teeth and gums. Along with brushing, eating fresh fruits and vegetables and using alcohol-free mouthwashes can also help reduce plaque and tartar buildup.

This technique is an established method to enhance dental appearance by reducing tooth discolouration brought on by lifestyle choices, dietary intake, and even heredity. The most prevalent factors contributing to tooth discolouration include tobacco use and the consumption of dark-coloured foods and drinks, such as tea, coffee, and red wine. In addition, staining can result from poor dental hygiene because discolouring chemicals can be trapped by plaque accumulation. Certain medications, such as tetracycline, can also discolour teeth, particularly if administered to a child. Ageing is another factor; as enamel thinning occurs, the yellowish dentin underneath becomes exposed. Hence, knowing about these factors is essential when determining a treatment plan for dental discolouration. Traditionally, neem leaves—also known as Azadirachta indica—have been used in oral hygiene practices. For centuries, thin neem branches have been used as natural toothbrushes, known as datun. This could be attributed to its antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant characteristics, which are considered beneficial for dental health. Neem-based preparations have therefore been used to reduce oral microbial loads, dental plaque, and gingival inflammation. Furthermore, neem leaf extracts have demonstrated high efficacy against oral pathogens such as Streptococcus mutans and Lactobacillus. Despite these benefits, it is critical to acknowledge that there is no concrete scientific evidence that establishes that neem leaf paste is an effective remedy for whitening teeth. Dr. Ketan Rajput, Periodontist, and Oral Implantologist, Dhule, Maharashtra, adds more credence to this by recommending that neem leaves be included in routine oral care regimens. This could help with plaque reduction and gum health. It is not, however, a reliable teeth-whitening solution. People should consult dental professionals while seeking safe and reliable teeth-whitening procedures. Even though long-term neem use is thought to be safe, it should only be used as part of a comprehensive oral hygiene routine that also comprises regular brushing and expert follow-up. It is usually best to see a dentist before incorporating neem-based products into a daily care routine, particularly for people who have specific dental conditions or allergies. Despite being extensively promoted on social media as natural teeth-whitening measures, a number of home remedies—including baking soda, lemon juice, strawberries, and activated charcoal—lack strong scientific backing. Furthermore, it has been shown that these natural remedies have a limited ability to whiten teeth. Most significantly, ingredients such as baking soda and activated charcoal have a high abrasive potential; their prolonged application can lead to enamel erosion. Likewise, applying lemon juice to teeth may increase enamel microporosity, which could cause discolouration rather than teeth whitening. Their regular use may therefore be more detrimental than helpful. Another important factor to take into account is that dental stains may also be intrinsic, which calls for expert cosmetic dentistry care. Dr. Gagandeep Singh Sodhi, Delhi-based Dental Surgeon, cautions that using unproven at-home teeth-whitening techniques before visiting a dentist can delay vital care and pose unforeseen health risks. Some of these natural remedies can be used as adjuncts to professional teeth-whitening procedures, but they cannot completely replace them. When it comes to teeth whitening, dental experts first assess your teeth's condition, remove any cavities, tartar, or surface stains, and then decide on the teeth whitening procedure. Even while neem leaf paste has traditionally been used as a natural remedy for maintaining oral hygiene, its role as a natural teeth whitening agent is questionable. This is because neem may help with gum inflammation and dental plaque reduction; teeth whitening, being a cosmetic issue, necessitates professional intervention.

title: Can testing hair porosity with water determine the right oil for your hair?
claim_text: A viral Facebook video claims that to test hair porosity, one should place a strand of hair in water and wait for five minutes. According to the video, if the hair floats, it indicates low porosity, and you should use almond oil. If it sinks halfway, it suggests medium porosity and neem oil is recommended. If it sinks completely, it signals high porosity and coconut oil should be used. This process is purported to prevent hair fall.
quick_take: A social media post suggests that testing hair porosity with water can determine the right oil for your hair. We fact checked this and found it to be mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Hair porosity isn't determined by how a strand behaves in water. Porosity refers to how well hair absorbs and holds moisture, which depends on the structure of the hair cuticle. The water test doesn't accurately reflect this and can lead to incorrect results. Due to surface tension, water molecules stick together, making light objects like a hair strand float. Since dry hair is buoyant, it can float in water, regardless of its porosity. This makes the water test unreliable for assessing hair porosity. The belief that low porosity hair floats is a common myth. While it's true that low porosity hair has tightly packed cuticles that resist moisture, floating in water doesn't reliably indicate this. Hair can float due to surface tension or natural oils, regardless of its porosity. A more accurate way to check porosity is to see how quickly your hair absorbs water or products when damp. Almond oil is often recommended for low porosity hair because it is lighter than some oils and may help moisturise the hair without weighing it down. However, managing low porosity hair is more about using heat to open the cuticles and using products designed for this hair type, rather than solely relying on almond oil. Neem oil is known for its antimicrobial properties, but it is not a one-size-fits-all solution for medium porosity hair. Medium porosity hair can generally handle a variety of oils, including lighter ones like argan oil or heavier oils like olive oil. The choice of oil should depend on individual hair needs, such as dryness, damage, or scalp conditions, not just the porosity. Coconut oil is commonly recommended for high porosity hair because it penetrates the hair shaft and helps retain moisture. However, this doesn't mean it can prevent hair fall. High porosity hair may be more prone to breakage due to moisture loss, and while coconut oil can help with hydration, it doesn't address deeper causes of hair fall such as poor nutrition, hormonal imbalance, or scalp issues. Dr Rashi Soni, Dermatologist and Co-founder of Rashi Hospital in Mumbai, states, "Coconut oil can help high porosity hair retain moisture, which may reduce breakage; but it doesn't stop hair fall altogether. Hair fall is often caused by internal factors like stress, nutritional deficiencies, or hormonal changes. While coconut oil nourishes the hair shaft and improves manageability, it won't address the root causes. It's a useful part of a hair care routine, but not a standalone solution for preventing hair loss." Oils can condition, strengthen, and protect hair, but there's no scientific evidence that matching oils to porosity levels can prevent hair fall. Hair loss is often influenced by factors like genetics, diet, stress, and scalp health. Dr Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant in Lucknow, says, "Choosing hair oils based on porosity sounds appealing, but it oversimplifies a much more complex issue. Porosity tells us how your hair absorbs moisture, but hair fall isn't just about moisture. It can stem from stress, poor diet, hormonal changes, or scalp conditions. Oils like coconut, almond, or neem can improve texture and hydration, but they won't treat the root cause of hair loss. Think of oils as support for hair health, not a cure. For long-term results, we need to look at the bigger picture, including lifestyle, nutrition, and scalp care."

The outcomes being measured (subjective improvements in gas and bloating) are subjective - placebo effect can influence responses, and gas/bloating naturally fluctuate. Measuring over just 14 days doesn't prove much. Dr Sharad Malhotra, Head of Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Therapeutic Endoscopy at Aakash Healthcare, New Delhi, explains, 'Just because a clinical trial is registered doesn't mean a product works. A strong trial needs good design, enough people, clear results, and public data. In this case, the study is small, short, and unpublished. So, when a brand says clinically proven without sharing the full picture, it's important to stay cautious. Also, no drink can truly detox or cleanse your gut. Your body already has a natural system for that, like, your liver, kidneys, and gut do the job every day. Good gut health comes from time, fibre, water, rest, and movement, not a quick fix over 14 days.' Dr Almas Fatma, Diploma in Family Medicine, PG in Digital Health, General Physician from Navi Mumbai, says, 'The idea of a drink cleansing your gut sounds appealing, but it's not how the body works. Your gut doesn't need a cleanse the way a dirty pipe might. Our digestive system is designed to manage waste and toxins on its own, with help from the liver, kidneys and regular bowel movements. What really supports gut health is a balanced diet with fibre, staying hydrated, getting enough sleep and staying active. A 14-day drink might help you feel lighter for a while, but it's not a deep clean.' The THIP Media Take states the product may include harmless and mildly beneficial ingredients, but marketing greatly exaggerates its effects. Bold statements like 'clinically proven 70% less bloating' are not backed by publicly available data.

title: Fact check: Can the consumption of smoothies aid in weight loss? - THIP Media
claim_text: A Facebook video reel featuring an obese woman claims she lost 105lbs (7 stone) within 3 weeks after consuming a weight loss smoothie, presenting it as an effective way to lose weight.
quick_take: A Facebook video claiming that drinking smoothies is an effective way to lose weight has been fact-checked and found to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation:
Smoothies are a popular and convenient way to increase daily intake of fruits and vegetables. They are made by combining whole fruits and vegetables, which helps maintain nutritional value. Fruits and vegetables are important for a healthy diet as they contain essential nutrients and reduce the risk of chronic diseases like heart disease and certain types of cancer.

Theoretically, smoothies can help with weight loss. However, experts are challenging popular beliefs about weight loss. Small lifestyle changes may not prevent or reduce obesity. A 2017 study found that dietary change and exercise were better predictors of weight loss than juice/liquid diets or diet pills. Obese adults who ate less fat and exercised more were more likely to achieve meaningful weight loss - 41% lost 5% of body weight, and an additional 20% lost 10% of body weight, in line with NIH recommendations.

The paradoxical effects of fruit on obesity were observed in a 2016 study - while consuming fruits is generally healthy and can help prevent obesity, there are instances where it may actually contribute to weight gain if consumed in large amounts or as sugary drinks, leading to increased calorie intake. Some fruits have a high glycemic index, causing rapid blood sugar increases, increased hunger, and potential overeating.

Nutritionist Kamna Chauhan states: "Smoothie diets are part of those weight loss plan that involve replacing meals with fruit and vegetable juice. It helps dieters have great control over calories. There are several allegations of a smoothie diet, as we are only drinking smoothies instead of consuming meals. As a short-term measure, there is reduction in carbohydrate and fat. Smoothie diets could lead to weight gain. If we think smoothies help in weight loss then it also can be the reason for weight gain. As consuming so many fruits lead to excess in overall calorie intake and promote weight gain."

Nutritionist Pariksha Rao says: "To achieve permanent and healthy weight loss, it is essential to adopt a combination of a reduced calorie diet, regular physical activity, and a disciplined lifestyle and behavioural change. There are also additional factors that can assist in weight loss, such as pharmacotherapy and bariatric surgery. It is important to note that any weight loss regimen combined with physical activity will prevent weight regain."

Clinical Dietitian Melanie Dsouza says: "To ensure a healthy and sustainable weight/fat loss, it is important to integrate a balanced diet that takes into consideration an individual's medical history. Quick-fix solutions should be avoided, and a balanced diet should be prioritised instead. It is important to understand that excessive consumption of anything may have negative effects on the body, and moderation should be practised."

Regarding safety: A 2018 study documented a 65-year-old woman who developed kidney failure after drinking a green smoothie juice "cleanse" made from oxalate-rich leafy vegetables and fruits. She had previously had stomach surgery and been on antibiotics. Drinking juices like this can increase oxalates in the body, causing kidney damage in people at risk. Fruit juices can also have negative effects on tooth structure due to acidic content, leading to dental erosion.

A 2008 study published in Diabetes Care Journal found that higher consumption of whole fruits and green leafy vegetables was associated with a lower risk of developing type 2 diabetes, while higher consumption of fruit juices was associated with a higher risk. Although smoothies can contribute to a healthy diet, they don't provide the same amount of fibre as whole fruits and contain relatively high amounts of sugar, which can be detrimental to dental health and provide excess energy.

The Smoothie Diet program shown in the video was created by Drew Sgoutas, a self-proclaimed health coach and author, but little information about him exists online. The program involves replacing two meals per day with smoothies. A video testimonial on the website featuring a woman appears in multiple videos under different names on YouTube, raising questions about credibility. Testimonials may have been paid.

title: Can the daily application of vitamin E make skin wrinkle-free?
claim_text: Daily application of a vitamin E capsule can permanently remove wrinkles and make the skin wrinkle-free.
quick_take: According to a Facebook post, daily application of vitamin E is sufficient to make the skin wrinkle-free. We fact-checked the assertion and found that it is mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Wrinkles are natural, time-dependent, or genetic phenomena that commonly develop as lines or creases on the face, neck, and hands. These primarily result from a confluence of environmental factors and ageing. As we age, our skin lacks elastin, collagen, and hydration, which makes it less elastic and more prone to creases. With the decreasing thickness of the epidermis, the dermal support structure is compromised. Furthermore, a combination of elevated oxidative stress and a reduced rate of cellular regeneration could result in an additional layer of cells. Because of all of this, the skin eventually becomes more fragile, sags, and acquires permanent creases and lines. The ageing process is facilitated by environmental variables, such as smoking, contaminants, UV exposure, dehydration, and repetitive facial motions. Vitamin E is frequently conceived of as a wrinkle remedy due to its potent antioxidant qualities, which can counteract free radicals. Vitamin E has been suggested to have the ability to shield the skin from oxidative stress, which can greatly speed up the breakdown of collagen and elastin, resulting in wrinkles and fine lines. Several topical formulations based on vitamin E are designed to improve skin hydration, barrier function, and short-term skin smoothness. When combined with vitamin C, vitamin E may also exhibit modest benefits in skin texture. Moreover, its oral supplementation is associated with wrinkle reduction. Dr. Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Cosmetician, Trichologist, and Consultant in Aesthetic Medicine in Lucknow, explains that vitamin E may provide some protection against dryness and early signs of ageing while also keeping the skin hydrated. Since wrinkles are caused by deeper structural changes in the skin over time, they often respond to more specialised skincare solutions that contain tried-and-true chemicals, including retinoids, peptides, and sunscreen. While vitamin E can be incorporated in a moisturising regimen, it shouldn't replace dermatologist-recommended therapies or an appropriate sunscreen formulation. Despite these advantages, there is limited and conflicting scientific evidence supporting its ability to significantly diminish wrinkles. While vitamin E might enhance skin health and address transient cosmetic concerns, it is not an established remedy for wrinkles. Dr. Sachin Gupta, Consultant Dermatologist at Amrita Hospital in Faridabad, emphasises that it is advisable to opt for treatments with proven efficacy and established clinical benefits, given the limited and inconclusive nature of studies backing such remedies. There is no remedy that can remove wrinkles entirely as they are an inevitable consequence of ageing, hormonal shifts, and hereditary traits. While they cannot be completely removed, scientifically proven therapies, including topical retinoids, antioxidants, chemical peels, laser treatments, and botulinum toxin, can significantly reduce their appearance. Dr. Rashi Soni, Co-founder and Consulting Dermatologist, Aesthetician, and Hair Transplant Surgeon at Rashi Hospital in Mumbai, explains that using a high-quality sunscreen every day is one of the best methods to prevent further damage. Retinoids aid by promoting cell turnover and collagen synthesis. Skin-plumping moisturisers with ceramides or hyaluronic acid preserve the skin's protective layer. Lifestyle decisions are also crucial; eating a balanced diet, getting enough sleep, and quitting smoking can all have a significant impact.

title: Fact Check: Can the drug Fenbendazole cure cancer?
claim_text: In a video posted on Facebook, a man says, "I got a call from an animal veterinarian in western Oklahoma, who is a college friend and a family friend. He told me this crazy story about a scientist who has been doing cancer research on mice. She had hundreds of mice, and some had cancer all over the body. Her mice population was down within intestinal parasites and she had no choice but to save her research. She gave all of her mice fenbendazole. If you go to any zoo in the world, they bring in fenbendazole by a truckload front-end loader, head-high piles in bays because they give them to every single animal. And she did, and unfortunately or fortunately for all of us, she she accidentally killed all the cancer."
quick_take: A social media post claims that the deworming drug Fenbendazole can cure Cancer. We fact-checked and found this claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: Fenbendazole is a broad-spectrum anthelmintic medication, which means it is effective against a wide range of parasitic worms. It is commonly used to treat and prevent intestinal parasites in animals, including dogs, cats, horses, and livestock. Fenbendazole works by disrupting the energy metabolism of parasites, specifically by inhibiting the formation of microtubules, which are essential for cell division and nutrient uptake. As a result, the parasites are unable to survive and eventually die. Can Fenbendazole cure cancer? No. Fenbendazole is a broad-spectrum antiparasitic medication primarily used to treat parasitic worm infections in animals. While some preliminary research has shown potential anti-cancer properties of fenbendazole in laboratory settings, there is currently no conclusive evidence from rigorous clinical trials to support the claim that fenbendazole can cure cancer in humans. The existing evidence is limited to in vitro (test tube) and animal studies, which have shown that fenbendazole can inhibit the growth of certain types of cancer cells. However, these findings have not been translated into effective treatments for cancer in humans. Furthermore, another research has concluded that it has no value in cancer therapy. Dr P. Rammanohar, Research Director, Amrita School of Ayurveda, highlights this by stating, "Cancer is not a single disease, and there is no remedy for cancer. Different types of cancer are treated with different procedures of chemotherapy. One drug does not work across all cancers." Moreover, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has not approved fenbendazole for the treatment of cancer. Using fenbendazole for cancer treatment is considered an off-label use, meaning it is not approved for that specific purpose. Cancer treatment depends on various factors, including the type and stage of cancer. It often involves a combination of treatments such as surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy. These treatments have been extensively researched and proven effective in managing and sometimes curing certain types of cancer. Shivashankar T., Chief Clinical Nutritionist and Dietician at Tata Memorial Cancer Hospital, Mumbai further informs that a good diet is important in cancer treatment. He further explains that "A healthy diet plays an important role in supporting overall health and well-being during cancer treatment. A diet high in good protein and no simple carbohydrates as well as inflammatory proteins can be beneficial for the cancer patients. However, this diet advice needs to be altered for every patient according to the requirements of their body." Our research further shows that cancer treatment typically involves a multidisciplinary approach, including medical interventions like chemotherapy, radiation therapy, surgery, and targeted therapies. It is important to note that self-treating with fenbendazole for cancer can be dangerous. Fenbendazole can have side effects, including liver damage, and may interact with other medications. It is crucial to consult with a healthcare professional before considering any off-label use of fenbendazole or any other medication. Currently, there is no definitive evidence to support the claim that fenbendazole can cure cancer in humans. More rigorous clinical trials are needed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of fenbendazole for cancer treatment.
