title: Fact Check: Does Irradiated food cause cancer? - THIP Media
claim_text: Food irradiation, another disturbing fact in your diet that causes cancer
quick_take: According to a YouTube video, food irradiation is a key factor in the development of cancer. We verified the accuracy of the claim. Analysis revealed that the assertion is Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: Food irradiation slows the pace at which food ages. This includes the sprouting of fruits and vegetables and the preservation of grains and spices for a longer time. This helps the shipping of grains and spices over great distances. Thus, it has been developed to address the major issue of food storage. There are three types of radiation that can be used to irradiate food. These include gamma rays, electron beams, and x-rays. The same principle governs the three approaches. Food is transported on a conveyor belt while being passed through a radiation chamber and a radiation beam. Ionizing radiation emits enough energy to cause the chemical bonds of bacteria or molds to disintegrate by destroying the bacteria or preventing them from proliferating. Thus, the procedure reduces rotting and even food-borne sickness. However, it must be emphasized that irradiating food does not make it radioactive. Yes, but only when employed within authorized parameters. Thorough research has been done on the procedure's safety more than on any other food industry technology. Irradiation has a greater impact on living things that include DNA and/or RNA but has little effect on items that contain macronutrients. Irradiation has no impact on the nutritional value of proteins, lipids, or carbohydrates. However, evidence exists that suggests vitamins may be both vulnerable and sensitive to irradiation. A few of these vitamins, such as biotin, pyridoxine (B6), and riboflavin (B2), are frequently stable, although others, such as thiamin (B1) and vitamins A, C, and E, are unpredictable. Please remember that irradiation should not be used in place of proper food control practices. Irradiated food needs to be handled, stored, and prepared the same way as organic food. If safeguards are not taken, they could still become contaminated with pathogens. No, not for now. Though it has been claimed that irradiation alters food unfavorably and can also damage important minerals like vitamins. Radiolytic products, also known as novel compounds, are produced as a result of food irradiation. These byproducts might cause mutations and may consequently have a role in the development of cancer. Additionally, it is thought that irradiation of foods alters and even damages foods' flavor, odor, look, and texture. Additionally, the authorized bodies always regulate the irradiation parameters. Our research, however, was unable to uncover any evidence to back up these allegations. Dr Sarthak Moharir, Radiation Oncologist, HCG Cancer Centre, Vadodara, responded that, 'Packaged goods and medical equipment like needles are actually sterilized by extraordinarily high radiation doses. As a result, radioactivity is not retained in irradiated foods or plastics. So, consuming irradiated food won't make one develop cancer.' THIP MEDIA TAKE: Food irradiation is a versatile approach. The method involves eliminating potentially dangerous biological organisms from food. By prolonging shelf life, food irradiation offers the opportunity to improve food quality and microbiological safety. As a result, we draw the conclusion that the assertion is mostly false.

title: Fact Check: Does Ivermectin cause infertility?
claim_text: A post circulating on Instagram features Dr Mike Yeadon, an ex-Pfizer scientist and anti-vaccine activist, claiming that ivermectin is "one of the most violent fertility toxins" and reduces the ability to conceive and carry pregnancies to term.
quick_take: A social media post claims that Ivermectin causes infertility. We did a thorough fact check to determine the claim as false.
doctor_explanation: Dr Almas Fatma, MBBS, Diploma in Family Medicine, PG in Digital Health, General Physician from Navi Mumbai, says, "Ivermectin has been used safely for over 30 years to treat parasitic infections, and there's no reliable evidence linking it to fertility problems in men or women. If it did affect fertility, we'd have seen clear signs in the millions of people who've taken it worldwide." There is no solid scientific evidence that ivermectin harms fertility in humans. Ivermectin is an antiparasitic drug widely used to treat infections like river blindness, scabies, and strongyloidiasis. It has been safely administered to millions of people worldwide for decades, particularly in mass drug administration programmes in Africa and South America. No well-designed human studies show that ivermectin causes infertility. Regulatory bodies, including the World Health Organization (WHO), the US FDA, and the European Medicines Agency (EMA), have not identified infertility as a known side effect. Post-marketing surveillance data also do not report fertility issues linked to ivermectin use. While ivermectin is approved for treating parasitic infections, the FDA has not approved it for COVID-19 treatment. Additionally, claims that ivermectin is the future of cancer treatment are misleading. It is only being studied in early lab and animal research, with no proven effectiveness or approval for use in humans. Studies in rats and mice have shown that extremely high doses of ivermectin can affect reproductive health, including reduced sperm motility and changes in ovarian function, but only at doses much higher than those prescribed for humans. Animals process drugs differently from humans, so these results don't directly apply to people. In a 2020 study, researchers reviewed six studies from African countries, involving 893 pregnant women. Some women took ivermectin by accident during mass drug campaigns, while others received it as part of a clinical trial. There were no reported cases of newborn deaths, pregnancy complications, premature births, or low birth weight. However, it's still unclear if ivermectin increases the risk of miscarriage, stillbirth, or birth defects due to limited and uncertain data. Any negative effects seen in animal studies were often reversible once the drug was stopped. Dr Mike Yeadon's claim that ivermectin is "one of the most violent fertility toxins" has no scientific backing. If a medicine posed serious fertility risks, it would come with strict warnings, but that's not the case with ivermectin. It's not listed as a reproductive toxin in medical references or official safety guidelines. Dr Ubaid ur Rahman, General Physician, Holy Mission Clinic, New Delhi, explains that "Ivermectin is generally safe when used as prescribed for conditions like parasitic infections. Health risks usually arise when people take it in the wrong dose, too frequently, or use versions meant for animals. This can lead to side effects like nausea, dizziness, or even serious issues like seizures in extreme cases." Taking high doses of ivermectin can be dangerous and put your health at risk. It can interact with other medicines, like blood thinners, leading to harmful side effects. An overdose may cause symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, low blood pressure, skin rashes, dizziness, balance problems, seizures, coma, and even death.

title: Does jaggery and ajwain prevent period pain? - THIP Media
claim_text: Consuming jaggery with ajwain can significantly lessen the intensity of period pain
quick_take: A social media post suggests that drinking tea made with jaggery and ajwain can provide relief from period pain. We fact checked and found the claim to be mostly false.
doctor_explanation:
There is no medical or scientific evidence showing that drinking tea made with jaggery and ajwain can prevent menstrual pain. Period pain, known medically as dysmenorrhoea, is primarily caused by hormone-like substances called prostaglandins. These chemicals trigger the uterus to contract so it can shed its lining during menstruation. In some people, prostaglandin levels are higher, leading to stronger contractions, reduced blood flow to the uterine muscle, and pain. A drink made of lukewarm water, jaggery, and ajwain might help but it does not affect prostaglandin production or uterine muscle activity in any proven way. While warmth and hydration may make someone feel temporarily soothed, that is very different from preventing or treating the biological process behind cramps.

Regarding ajwain: Partly, but very mildly. Ajwain contains compounds such as thymol, which have antispasmodic properties. In laboratory and animal studies, these compounds have been shown to relax smooth muscles, including those in the gut. This is why ajwain is commonly used to ease bloating, gas, and indigestion. However, menstrual cramps are not the same as digestive spasms. The uterus is a specialised muscle influenced mainly by hormones, not by the same mechanisms that control gut movement. There is no high-quality human study showing that consuming ajwain can meaningfully relax uterine contractions or reduce menstrual pain. At best, ajwain may reduce accompanying digestive discomfort, such as bloating or heaviness, that some people experience during periods.

Regarding jaggery: Jaggery is a form of unrefined sugar that contains small amounts of minerals like iron, potassium, and magnesium. However, the quantities of these minerals in a typical spoon of jaggery are too small to influence menstrual pain. Some people feel more energetic after consuming jaggery because it provides quick carbohydrates, which may help with fatigue or low mood during periods, but it does not reduce uterine contractions or inflammation. There is also no scientific evidence that jaggery improves pelvic blood flow in a way that reduces cramps.

One key concern is that relying on this remedy can delay proper pain management. If someone experiences moderate to severe period pain, especially pain that interferes with work, sleep, or daily activities, relying solely on home remedies can delay proper evaluation and treatment. Persistent or worsening cramps may be linked to conditions such as endometriosis, fibroids, or adenomyosis, which require medical attention. Effective, evidence-based options for managing period pain include non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), hormonal treatments when appropriate, regular physical activity, adequate sleep, and stress management.

title: Fact Check: Does jaggery clean your lungs? - THIP Media
claim_text: Jaggery (gur) is a natural lung cleanser that can protect against air pollution and clean your lungs
quick_take: A social media post suggests that jaggery (gur) is a natural lung cleanser. We fact checked and found the claim to be mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Can jaggery protect the body from the effects of air pollution? Partly yes, but not in the way many social media posts suggest. Jaggery naturally contains small amounts of minerals and antioxidants. These compounds may help neutralise free radicals and reduce the oxidative stress that rises when your body is exposed to pollutants. So, in a broad sense, jaggery can support general health and may help your body cope marginally better with everyday environmental stress. But the popular idea that 'jaggery is a natural cleanser for your lungs' has no scientific backing. The antioxidant effect is helpful, but it is not powerful enough to shield the lungs from the complex mix of chemicals, particulate matter, and toxins in today's air pollution. Using jaggery as a protective shield against smog or severe pollution simply oversells what the ingredient can realistically do. Where does the belief come from? Surprisingly, this claim traces back to a small set of animal experiments. In one well-known study from 1994, researchers exposed rats to coal dust and then fed some of them jaggery for three months. The jaggery-fed rats showed [results]. These results looked encouraging and hinted that jaggery might help minimise the impact of regular dust exposure, especially for workers in mines or industries. However, the limitations matter: So while the research is interesting, it's nowhere near enough to recommend jaggery as a lung-cleaning remedy for the general public. Does jaggery literally pull out carbon or PM2.5 from the lungs? Absolutely not. There are no human trials proving that jaggery can extract fine particulate matter from alveoli (the tiny air air sacs where oxygen exchange happens). PM2.5 and carbon particles embed deep into lung tissue and cannot simply be 'washed out' by any food including jaggery. The rat study is often quoted as proof, but at best it suggests a possible mechanism in animals. Human lungs are far more complex, and pollution exposure is continuous and long-term. So interpreting that rat study as evidence that jaggery can 'clear your lungs' is a major overreach. Dr Saket Sharma, MD, DM, Senior Consultant, Pulmonary Medicine, JayPrabha Medanta Hospital, Patna said, 'There's nothing wrong with having a little jaggery—we all do—but don't expect it to replace air-pollution control measures or give unrealistic results. Scientifically, I cannot think of any mechanism through which jaggery could pull out carbon particles from the lungs.' Is jaggery a safe replacement for proper pollution protection or medical care? No and depending on your health, it might even be harmful in excess. Jaggery is not a medical treatment. It is not a substitute for [proper medical care]. While jaggery is fine in moderation, it is still a concentrated sugar. Large quantities can spike blood sugar levels and are unsuitable for people with diabetes or those advised to limit sweets. If you enjoy jaggery, have it in small amounts for taste or seasonal comfort. But for genuine lung protection, rely on steps that are scientifically proven quality masks, cleaner indoor air, and timely medical attention when needed. Food can support health, but it cannot undo the damage caused by the air we breathe.

title: Fact Check: Does jalebi with milk help relieve joint pain?
claim_text: Having jalebi soaked in warm milk can cure back and joint pain.
quick_take: A social media post suggests that eating milk and jalebi help relieve body and joint pain. We fact checked and found the claim to be false.
doctor_explanation: Dr. Sushant Srivastava, Orthopaedic Surgeon, stated: 'No, it does not provide any proven pain relief.' There is no medical research showing that this sugary, deep-fried sweet dipped in milk has anti-inflammatory or analgesic (pain-reducing) effects. Jalebi is made from refined flour and sugar, both of which have zero nutritional role in reducing any type of joint discomfort. Milk does contain nutrients like calcium and protein, but these support long-term bone health, not immediate joint pain relief. Many studies also talk about dairy and inflammation connection. The idea that mixing the two creates a healing remedy mostly comes from traditional beliefs, not scientific evidence. At best, the warm milk may give a temporary sense of comfort, but comfort is not the same as healing. Regarding milk alone: Milk offers calcium, protein and sometimes added vitamin D, nutrients that help keep bones strong over time. Some studies suggest that regular consumption of low-fat dairy may be linked to slower progression of certain joint conditions like osteoarthritis in some people. But this benefit is mild, long-term and not guaranteed. Milk does not work like a painkiller, nor does it treat inflammation or cartilage wear directly. It certainly does not produce instant relief, which is what the viral claim implies. Regarding sugar: Excessive sugar intake can increase inflammation and worsen pain. Jalebi is made by deep-frying refined flour and then soaking it in sugar syrup, a combination known to cause sharp spikes in blood sugar and promote low-grade inflammation in the body. Inflammatory processes can make joint pain feel worse, especially for people with arthritis or chronic joint problems. Additionally, frequent consumption of calorie-dense sweets may lead to weight gain, which puts extra pressure on weight-bearing joints like the knees and hips. Dr. Mohit Sandhu, Ayurvedic expert, stated: 'It may offer relief only in very specific situations and certainly not because of the jalebi. Any benefit comes from the ghee, the warmth, and the pacification of Vata-Pitta, not the sugar. Avoid jalebi with milk if your joints show swelling, heat, or redness, if you have diabetes, if you experience indigestion or acidity, or if your pain is due to Aamvat or rheumatoid arthritis.' Jalebi with milk is a tasty indulgence, not a therapy. There is no scientific mechanism by which it can heal joint pain, reduce inflammation or help manage arthritis. title: Fact Check: Does Kalanchoe pinnata plant with honey treat gallstones? - THIP Media
claim_text: Mixing Kalanchoe pinnata plant with honey can treat gallstones
quick_take: A social media post claims mixing Kalanchoe pinnata plant with honey treat gallstones. We fact checked and found the claim has missing context, hence Half True. There is scant scientific evidence that shows the Kalanchoe pinnata plant treats gallstones. Whereas honey might have a positive impact against gallstones.
doctor_explanation:
Kalanchoe pinnata plant (or pattharchatain Hindi) is a succulent native to Madagascar. In India, the plant is recognized for its curative properties to treat eye pain, stomach disorder, jaundice, cuts, wounds, pain, fever and diarrhoea. Advocates claim that the Kalanchoe pinnata plant can treat fatal diseases, including cancer. We could not find credible medical papers for such a claim. We even found a social media post that seems to have a missing context as it claims the Kalanchoe pinnata plant can treat cancer.

Gallstones are hardened digestive fluids deposits that look like stones formed in the gallbladder. The gallbladder holds a digestive fluid called bile between the meals when there is no fat to be digested. However, when we eat food, gallbladder contracts to squeeze out the bile through the bile duct into the small intestine. Besides bile, the gallbladder also stores cholesterol and bilirubin (which makes urine yellow and stool brown). Due to some chemical imbalance, these stored compounds in the gallbladder produce stones.

Yes. Gallstones stuck in the gallbladder can only be treated through surgical procedures including endoscopy, laparoscopy, cholecystectomy or open surgery.

But gallstones range from the size of a sand grain to a golf ball. So, small gallstones may leave the gallbladder and pass into the bile duct to reach the small intestine and stool.

We asked Dr Sharad Malhotra, Gastroenterologist, to suggest if doctors recommend natural remedies as stated in the claim along with the treatment. To this, he said "Gallstones occur because of supersaturation of cholesterol or infection in bile. Since no food elements will change the bile composition, no food can be offered as a cure for gallstones".

Maybe. There is some available research that shows the plant contains essential nutrients and properties with no known adverse reactions or toxicity to humans and can reduce the severity of the condition. But we have no studies that can show optimal dosage safe for regular human consumption.

Dr Malhotra explains, "Gallstones can range from the size of a sand grain to a golf ball. So, small gallstones may leave the gallbladder on its own and pass into the bile duct to reach the small intestine and stool. So, with the available evidence, it is difficult to confirm whether the plant is effective against all sizes of gallstone."

In context with honey, we found a research published in 2020 that shows honey can break the Salmonella typhi biofilm to expose the gallbladder for treatment or to be passed through the stool on its own. But we also found another research published in 2014 that shows eating too much honey can cause food poisoning to cause dizziness, vomiting, nausea, convulsions, palpitations, headache or even death.

Gallstones often do not cause symptoms and won't necessarily cause any problem to most people. However, gallstones often block the tubes that carry bile. This scenario can be life-threatening as it can cause infection in the bile duct, pancreas or liver. Also, once people have had gallstones, they are at a higher risk of having them again. In this case, it can be dangerous to not seek medical attention and keep trying out home remedies.

Dr Malhotra further informs, "Trying to treat gallstones with home remedies without understanding the underlying cause can leave the condition untreated. This can cause cholecystitis and induce potentially life-threatening complications, including spread of infection throughout the body and build-up of pus."

title: Does Kangen water prevent diseases and slow ageing? - THIP
claim_text: Drinking alkaline ionised Kangen water can prevent diseases, slow ageing, improve memory, prevent cancer, manage diabetes, and cure multiple conditions.
quick_take: A social media post claims that Kangen's Alkaline Ionised water works as a miracle drink and prevents diseases and ageing. We fact checked and found the claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation:
IS KANGEN'S ALKALINE IONISED WATER FREE FROM DISEASE-CAUSING RISKS?: No, there is no evidence that Kangen water prevents diseases. The idea that alkaline ionised water can protect you from illness sounds appealing. But here's the reality: diseases are caused by bacteria, viruses, lifestyle, genetics, or environmental factors — not by the pH of the water you drink. Multiple studies, including research published in The Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition, have shown that while alkaline water may slightly affect urine pH, it has no role in preventing or curing diseases. The body already has an incredible acid-base balancing system. Your kidneys and lungs maintain your blood pH at a steady level. Drinking alkaline water doesn't magically change that. In simple words, your body's chemistry is not so easily influenced by what's in your glass.

DOES KANGEN WATER SLOW DOWN AGEING?: No, it does not slow aging, neither any studies done on humans! Ageing is a complex natural process. It's influenced by genetics, cell damage, lifestyle, and environmental exposure. No water whether it's detox or alkaline or ionised can reverse or slow this down. Although some studies indicate that alkaline ionized water might have positive effects on longevity, such as a 2016 mouse study showing improved survival rates, the evidence supporting its ability to extend lifespan is still limited and needs further investigation.

CAN ALKALINE IONISED WATER CURE JOINT PAIN OR KIDNEY PROBLEMS?: No, there is no medical backing for these claims. Joint pain, arthritis, or kidney issues are complex medical conditions. Drinking alkaline water will not act as a magical cure. The Arthritis Foundation said there is little to no evidence that higher pH water can help with joint pain. In fact, kidney experts warn that patients with chronic kidney disease should avoid excessive alkaline water, as it can disturb electrolyte balance and worsen their condition. A study was published clearly mentioning in bold letters that alkaline water does not prevent kidney stones. According to the Harvard Health, people with impaired kidney function should be very cautious with high-mineral or altered pH water. So, not only is this claim unsupported — it could even be dangerous.

DOES KANGEN WATER REGULATE SUGAR LEVELS OR PREVENT CANCER?: No, these are false claims. This is perhaps the most misleading part of the advertisement. Diabetes management relies on diet, exercise, medication, and medical supervision — not the pH level of your water. The American Diabetes Association makes no mention of alkaline water in diabetes care guidelines. And what about cancer prevention? The American Institute for Cancer Research and Cancer Research UK have made it very clear — cancer cells do not thrive or die based on the pH of what you drink. Your stomach acid neutralises any water you consume, and your blood pH is tightly regulated. There is zero scientific evidence that alkaline water can prevent or cure cancer.

CAN ALKALINE WATER IMPROVE MEMORY AND EYESIGHT?: No. There's no scientific evidence that alkaline water can improve memory or eyesight. Alkaline water has a higher pH than regular water and is often marketed with health claims, but research does not support cognitive or vision-enhancing benefits. Memory and eyesight are influenced by factors like nutrition, sleep, exercise, and overall health. Nutrients such as omega-3 fatty acids, antioxidants, and vitamins A, C, and E play a more proven role. Staying hydrated is essential, but alkaline water offers no special advantage for brain or eye health.

CAN DRINKING ALKALINE WATER REDUCE URIC ACID?: May be. A 2024 study presents a new perspective on non-drug methods for managing uric acid-related issues and discomfort. It suggests that alkaline water may help in reducing serum uric acid levels, easing pain, and improving overall quality of life for patients. However, more extensive research is necessary to verify these initial findings and to better understand the long-term safety and effectiveness of using alkaline water for managing uric acid concerns.

IS KANGEN'S ALKALINE WATER SAFE FOR DAILY USE?: Yes, but it's unnecessary and expensive. At the end of the day, alkaline ionised water is generally safe for healthy individuals in small amounts. But spending thousands on a machine for ordinary drinking water makes little sense. Your body is perfectly capable of balancing pH on its own. In fact, plain clean drinking water, eaten with a balanced diet, does the job just fine. The World Health Organization guidelines recommend safe, potable water without contamination but do not endorse ionised water.

title: Fact Check: Does kicking a man's testis produce pain of 9000 dels? - THIP Media

quick_take: A social media post claims kicking a man's testis causes 9000 del pain. We fact-checked and found this post to be False.
doctor_explanation: The del was proposed in the 1940s by James Hardy, a physiologist at Cornell University. He developed the scale to measure the pain of childbirth, and he estimated that the pain of a kick to the testicles was equivalent to 10 dels. However, the del was never officially adopted, and there is no scientific consensus on how to measure pain. Also, a research paper showed the unit of measuring pain is 'dol' which is measured using a dolorimeter. There is no evidence that proves that kicking a man's testis produces pain of 9000 dels. A del is a unit of pain measurement that is never officially adopted, and there is no evidence that a kick to the testicles would produce such pain. The Harvard Medical School has developed a 10-point pain scale to analyze the severity of pain. 0 means no pain whereas 10 means extreme pain. This scale is often used by doctors and other healthcare professionals to document and monitor the extent of pain and prescribe treatment accordingly. However, even this method does not seem efficient enough because the extent of pain can be at different rates on the same value. In fact, the pain of a kick to the testicles is likely to vary depending on the individual and the severity of the kick. Some men may experience excruciating pain, while others may only experience mild discomfort. There is no way to know for sure how much pain a man would experience from a kick to the testicles without actually kicking him. So, while a kick to the testicles can certainly be painful, it is unlikely to produce pain of 9000 dels. Pain is a highly subjective experience, and its perception can vary significantly among individuals. The intensity of pain can depend on various factors, including an individual's pain tolerance, the force of the impact, and other personal factors. However, it is generally agreed upon that a direct blow to the testicles can cause intense pain. The unit of measurement 'dels' being referred to is not a recognized standard for quantifying pain. It is not a widely accepted or used scale in the medical or scientific community. Therefore, it is not possible to determine whether kicking a man's testicles would produce a pain level of 9000 dels or any specific numerical value.

doctor_explanation: Every new invention in the history of humankind has faced resistance, criticism, and conspiracy theories upon its launch. Electronic gadgets and technology have been the latest targets of this ongoing scrutiny. What are the potential causes of miscarriage? Miscarriages, or the loss of a pregnancy before 20 weeks, can occur due to various reasons. Common causes include drug or alcohol use, blood clotting disorders, exposure to environmental toxins, hormone imbalances, infections, obesity, physical abnormalities in the mother's reproductive organs, immune system irregularities, and serious systemic diseases like uncontrolled diabetes. Additionally, smoking during pregnancy heightens the risk. Nearly half of all fertilised eggs are spontaneously lost before the woman knows she is pregnant, and among recognized pregnancies, 10% to 25% end in miscarriage (as of October 2022), primarily within the first 7 weeks. Risk escalates with the mother's age, particularly after 30 years, peaking after age 40, and among those who have previously experienced a miscarriage. While early miscarriages often go unnoticed, their prevalence may be significantly higher in low- and middle-income countries. Recent findings from the National Family Health Survey (NFHS), conducted in India between 2019 and 2021, indicate that around 7% of pregnancies result in miscarriages. Can laptop usage by pre-teen and teen girls really cause miscarriages later in life? No, this is not true. There is currently no scientific evidence supporting the claim that laptop usage by pre-teen and teen girls can directly cause miscarriages later in life. Miscarriages result from a variety of factors, such as genetic abnormalities, health conditions, lifestyle choices, and environmental factors. While prolonged laptop usage may contribute to discomfort or strain, leading a balanced lifestyle with regular breaks and proper ergonomics can help mitigate any potential risks. It's essential to rely on credible sources and consult healthcare professionals for accurate information regarding pregnancy and reproductive health. Who is the person in the video? The woman in the video is Barbara O'Neill. A simple Google search is enough to conclude that she is an infamous healthcare promoter who perpetuates dangerous and unsupported health claims. In 2019, the Health Care Complaints Commission in New South Wales issued a ruling prohibiting her from providing any health-related services. This decision came after receiving multiple complaints from both the public and healthcare professionals. She further mentions in the video that there are over 8000 studies which show laptop usage is responsible for miscarriages in women. According to current scientific findings, using laptops is generally considered safe. Like many other electrical devices, laptops generate electric and magnetic fields, but these are mostly in the extremely low frequency range. The WHO assures that the strength of these fields remains well below international exposure limits. Scientific studies affirm that the low level of exposure to these fields from laptops over the long term is safe for individuals. The electromagnetic fields emitted from laptops fall under the category of non-ionizing radiation. These are considered non-harmful for humans because they cannot damage our cells. In their 2020 revised guidelines, the International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection (ICNIRP) asserted that no harmful impacts of radiofrequency electromagnetic field (EMF) exposure on fertility, reproduction, or development relevant to human health have been confirmed. What is the impact of laptop usage on fertility? The external heat generated by laptops presents a minor concern for men's reproductive health. While it's unlikely to be the primary cause of fertility issues, men concerned about their sperm count may consider refraining from placing laptops on their laps and using a desk instead. Although a study has indicated that frequent exposure to high temperatures, such as in hot tubs, can decrease sperm viability, laptops generally do not reach such extreme temperatures. Hence the medical fraternity downplays concerns about the heat emitted by laptops. In contrast, women's ovaries are situated internally (thus, well protected) and are less sensitive to external heat, alleviating immediate concerns in this regard. Therefore, women may not need to modify their laptop usage habits. For men, using a desk instead of placing laptops on their laps could be a cautious approach, but it is not necessarily required unless specific fertility concerns arise. Is there a link between laptop usage and women's reproductive health? According to Dr Saumya (MBBS, DNB Obstetrics and Gynecology), 'No. Sitting on the sofa with your laptop or working with your laptop in bed won't lead to female infertility or future miscarriages. The heat emitted by laptops is generally minimal in terms of its impact on a woman's reproductive system.' She further explains, 'It's important to note that even women who frequently use laptops or rest tablets and similar devices on their laps are not at an increased risk of infertility or pregnancy issues in future. So, whether it's for work or leisure, using your laptop in these ways is unlikely to have any adverse effects on your fertility.'

title: Does Lemon Peel Tea remove heavy metal toxins from the body?
claim_text: An Instagram post claims that boiling lemon peels into a tea can 'flush out' heavy metals, cleanse the blood, and detox organs naturally.
quick_take: A social media post suggest that lemon peel tea remove heavy metal toxins from the body. We fact checked and found the claim to be false.
doctor_explanation: Heavy metals do not behave like everyday waste products that can be washed out with fluids or herbal drinks. Once these metals enter the body, they bind strongly to proteins, bones, and organs such as the liver, kidneys, and brain. Drinking lemon peel tea does not break these bonds or remove stored metals. Some laboratory studies show that citrus peels contain fibre (like pectin) and plant compounds that can bind metals outside the body, under controlled conditions. However, the human digestive system is far more complex. During digestion, these compounds are broken down, absorbed, or excreted long before they could meaningfully attach to heavy metals in tissues. At present, there are no human clinical trials proving that lemon peel tea reduces heavy metal levels in blood or organs. Dr Divya Chauhan, Senior Ayurveda Researcher at Pratha Ayurveda, said 'In Ayurveda, lemon peel may support digestion and metabolism, but it is not described as a treatment for metal toxicity. Such conditions require proper assessment and intervention.' Dr Shalin Nagori, Consultant Pathologist and Industrial Physician, said 'Heavy metal detoxification requires specific chelating agents. There is no clinical evidence that foods or teas can remove metals already stored in human tissues.' Antioxidants and detoxification are often confused, but they are not the same thing. Lemon peel contains vitamin C and flavonoids, which help reduce oxidative stress, damage caused by unstable molecules in the body. This may support overall health, but it does not equate to removing heavy metals. title: Does mixing curd, black salt, and black pepper quickly melt body fat?

doctor_explanation:
## Does consuming curd help melt body fat quickly?
No. Curd is a nutritious food, rich in protein and calcium. Protein can help in weight management by increasing satiety, meaning it helps you feel fuller for longer, potentially reducing overall calorie intake. Calcium has also been studied for its potential role in metabolism, but the effect on rapid fat loss is negligible and not supported by robust evidence. Curd is part of a healthy diet but does not possess properties that cause fat to "melt" rapidly on its own.

Some social media claims also warn against eating curd at night, calling it harmful. But these claims are not backed by science and are largely untrue.

## Does adding black salt contribute to quickly melting body fat?
No. Black salt, also known as kala namak, is primarily sodium chloride with trace minerals giving it a distinct flavour and colour due to sulphur compounds. Although it's used in cooking and traditional medicine for minor digestive issues, it has no scientifically proven ability to melt body fat or significantly contribute to rapid weight loss. Excessive salt intake, regardless of the type, is generally discouraged for overall health, particularly concerning blood pressure.

## Is it true that black pepper quickly melts body fat?
No. Black pepper contains a compound called piperine. And, some studies suggest it has metabolism-boosting effects and could potentially interfere with fat cell formation in animal studies. However, these effects are modest, and the amount of black pepper usually consumed as a spice is far too small to induce rapid fat loss in humans. It is a healthy addition to food for flavour and potential minor benefits, but it is not a fat-melting agent.

## Can mixing curd, black salt, and black pepper cause body fat to melt quickly?
No. There is no scientific evidence to suggest that combining these three ingredients creates a synergy that leads to the rapid melting of body fat. Weight loss is a complex process that requires consuming fewer calories than the body uses. This can be achieved through dietary changes and exercise. Even though these ingredients can be part of a balanced diet, especially curd, their combination does not have a unique fat-melting effect. Claims of specific food combinations causing rapid fat loss are generally not supported by nutritional science. Focusing on overall dietary patterns and lifestyle changes is the effective and evidence-based approach to weight management.

Dr Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition, explains, "There's no magical mix of curd, black salt, and black pepper that can melt body fat quickly. Curd is nutritious and provides protein and calcium, while black pepper may support digestion in small ways. But mixing them won't lead to rapid fat loss. Sustainable weight loss comes from balanced eating, regular exercise, and healthy lifestyle habits. These ingredients can support your diet, but they aren't a shortcut to burning fat."

Believing in such quick fixes can lead to disappointment. For real and lasting weight loss, it is important to eat mindfully, stay active, and follow a consistent routine."

## THIP Media Take
The claim that mixing curd, black salt, and black pepper quickly melts body fat is false. This post is not supported by strong scientific evidence. While the individual ingredients can be part of a healthy diet, this specific combination does not possess any magical fat-melting properties. Effective weight loss requires a calorie deficit achieved through diet and exercise.

title: Fact Check: Does more CO2 improve global food production?
claim_text: According to a Facebook post, "More CO2 helps to feed more people worldwide." The post includes a graph showing a link between rising CO2 levels, higher temperatures, and increased crop production. It claims that the steady rise in global food production is due to mechanisation, agricultural innovation, CO2 fertilisation, and warmer weather. The post argues that climate change has only had positive effects on crop yields so far, with no clear negative impacts. It also suggests that higher CO2 levels and warmer temperatures will keep boosting food production, describing carbon dioxide as beneficial because "carbon is plant food."
quick_take: A social media post claims that more CO2 improves global food production. We did the fact check and found out it's mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Is CO2 the primary driver of increased food production? Not entirely. Increased crop yields are primarily a result of advancements in agricultural practices, mechanisation, and irrigation techniques rather than CO2 levels alone. Modern agriculture has transformed food production through improved fertilisers, genetically enhanced crop varieties, and better pest control. While CO2 does play a role in photosynthesis, its effects on yields are limited. Studies indicate that other factors, such as soil quality, water availability, and extreme weather events (exacerbated by climate change), are more influential. Additionally, elevated CO2 can reduce the nutritional value of staple crops like wheat and rice by lowering protein, zinc, and iron content. We have previously debunked a similar claim that says 'CO2 leads to more plants and more oxygen, which is good for the planet.' However, this is not scientifically accurate. Does warmer weather improve crop production? Not always. While moderate temperature increases can benefit some crops in certain regions, extreme heat and unpredictable weather patterns often harm agricultural output. Global warming causes changes in precipitation patterns and increases the frequency of droughts, floods, and storms, which negatively affect farming. For example, heat stress reduces yields of maize and sorghum, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions. Prolonged heat waves also damage soil fertility, leading to long-term productivity losses. How does climate change affect crop yields? Climate change affects crop yields in several ways: Efforts like using climate-resilient seeds, adjusting planting schedules, and improving irrigation can help mitigate some effects, but challenges persist. Despite the visible impacts of climate change, some people still claim that the CO2 levels in our atmosphere are negligible. Are current food production trends sustainable with rising CO2 and temperatures? Unlikely. The initial gains from CO2 fertilisation and temperature changes are offset by long-term risks like extreme weather events, reduced soil health, and water scarcity. Climate change worsens challenges like desertification, water shortages, and pest infestations. For instance, a NASA study suggests that climate change could impact maize and wheat production by 2030 if greenhouse gas emissions remain high. Maize yields may drop by 24%, while wheat yields might increase by 17%. Over-reliance on CO2 fertilisation fails to account for these broader environmental impacts, which could undermine future food security. Does the graph in the claim provide complete context? No, it oversimplifies the relationship between CO2, temperature, and crop production. The graph assigns rising yields solely to increased CO2 and temperature without considering critical factors like technological advances and policy changes. For example, Green Revolution initiatives in the mid-20th century significantly boosted food production. The graph also ignores the regional disparities in climate impacts—while some areas may benefit from warmer conditions, others face declining productivity. THIP Media Take: The claim that more CO2 improves global food production is mostly false. While CO2 fertilisation and warmer weather can provide short-term benefits to crop yields in specific contexts, their overall impact is minor compared to agricultural innovations. Moreover, the adverse effects of climate change, including extreme weather, threaten long-term food production. A balanced approach focusing on sustainable farming and climate resilience is essential for global food security.

title: Does muskmelon tea dissolve kidney stones in 30 mins? - THIP
claim_text: Drinking muskmelon peel boiled with sugar as a tea can dissolve kidney stones within just 30 minutes and flush them out naturally
quick_take: A social media post claims that drinking muskmelon peel boiled with sugar as a tea can dissolve kidney stones within just 30 minutes. We fact checked and found the claim to be false.
doctor_explanation: Can a kidney stone dissolve within 30 minutes after drinking muskmelon tea? No. Kidney stones are hard crystalline structures formed when minerals in urine become concentrated and stick together. The most common type is calcium oxalate, but stones can also be made of uric acid, calcium phosphate, or other substances. These stones develop over weeks or months. They are compact, solid, and often quite dense. For a stone to dissolve, the chemical environment in the urine must change significantly and remain altered for a sustained period. This does not happen within minutes. Even in medical settings, when doctors intentionally try to dissolve certain uric acid stones, the process takes days to weeks under supervision. A single cup of herbal tea cannot realistically change urine chemistry that quickly or dramatically. In short, a stone that took months to form cannot disappear in half an hour. While certain home remedies may offer temporary support for digestive or urinary comfort, Dr Sharad Malhotra, HOD – Gastroenterology, Hepatology & Therapeutic Endoscopy at Aakash Healthcare, New Delhi, advises against relying on them as a long-term solution for kidney stones. He emphasises that these approaches lack strong scientific evidence and should not replace established, evidence-based medical treatments for renal calculi. Is there any scientific research supporting muskmelon tea for dissolving stones? No. There are no high-quality human clinical trials demonstrating that muskmelon tea dissolves kidney stones, let alone within 30 minutes. While some fruits, including melons, contain water, potassium, and small amounts of natural compounds, none of these are known to chemically break apart established kidney stones in the human body. Occasionally, laboratory or animal studies explore plant extracts and their potential effects on urine composition. However, laboratory findings are not the same as proven clinical treatments. More importantly, none of the available evidence supports the dramatic and time-bound claim circulating online. Dr. Archana Daftardar, Consultant Nephrologist, Hypertension Specialist, and Transplant Physician at Renova Hospitals, Kompally, Hyderabad, highlights that kidney stone care and prevention are often surrounded by myths. She cautions that relying on unproven natural remedies may do more harm than good and could potentially worsen the condition. Seeking guidance from a qualified allopathic physician remains the safest and most appropriate approach. Could muskmelon tea help in passing small stones indirectly? Yes, but only through improved hydration. Muskmelon tea is essentially flavoured water. Increased fluid intake leads to increased urine output. When urine volume rises, it can help flush out tiny stones or small crystal fragments, especially if they are already on the move. However, passing a small stone still takes time. The stone must travel from the kidney, through the ureter (a narrow tube), into the bladder, and then out through urine. This journey is often painful and can take days or weeks. Hydration supports this process; it does not accelerate it to a 30-minute event. It is also worth noting that if a stone is too large, no amount of tea will push it through safely. Medical intervention may then be required. Are there any stones that can actually be dissolved medically? Yes, but only specific types, and not instantly. Uric acid stones can sometimes be dissolved by making urine less acidic using prescribed alkalinising medication. This treatment requires monitoring of urine pH and is carried out under medical supervision. Even then, dissolution takes time. Most kidney stones, particularly calcium oxalate stones, do not dissolve with diet or herbal drinks. They either pass naturally if small enough or require treatments such as shockwave therapy or minimally invasive procedures. Therefore, the idea of a quick herbal solution does not align with current medical understanding. So muskmelon tea does not dissolve kidney stones in 30 minutes. At best, it contributes to hydration, which may support the natural passage of very small stones over time. Kidney stones are solid mineral deposits that require patience, monitoring, and sometimes medical treatment.

title: Does one who eats holy basil never get Malaria? THIP Media
claim_text: Malaria never occurs in those who consume two leaves of Holy basil daily. Tulsi (Holy basil) should not be chewed. Rather, small pieces should be broken and swallowed with water.
quick_take: A social media post claims that a person who consumes 2 leaves of holy basil each day would never get Malaria. We fact-checked and found this claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: Malaria is a potentially life-threatening infectious disease caused by parasites of the Plasmodium genus. It is primarily transmitted to humans through the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes. Malaria is a significant global health concern, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions. During the rainy season, there is humidity in the air, which is a good environment for mosquito breeding. Once there is a diagnosis of malaria, the appropriate antimalarial treatment must begin as soon as possible. It is most often characterised by fever. Chest pain, headache, muscular pains, nausea, and vomiting are additional frequent symptoms. Malaria patients can also exhibit diarrhoea, and abdominal pain occasionally. No, eating holy basil does not guarantee that you will never get malaria. Malaria is a serious mosquito-borne disease that requires proper medical treatment and preventive measures. While holy basil has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, including its antimicrobial properties, it is not a substitute for proven methods of malaria prevention as there is no conclusive scientific evidence to support its effectiveness as a preventive measure or cure for malaria. Remember, it is primarily transmitted through the bite of infected mosquitoes, which cannot be prevented by consuming these leaves. General Physician Dr. Atul Vashishta further confirms this by stating, "No. Malaria prevention primarily relies on various strategies and interventions related to mosquito control and personal protection, as well as, in some cases, antimalarial medications. While having a healthy diet is important for overall health and can support your immune system, diet alone is not a reliable or sufficient method for preventing malaria. Holy basil may have potential health benefits and can be a part of a healthy diet, it should not be considered a sole or primary means of preventing malaria. it cannot be ascertained for use as an antimalarial drug or prevention as there are no research papers that base this remedy yet. It's important to rely on proven and recommended methods for malaria prevention if you are in an area where the disease is prevalent or are at risk of exposure. If you have malaria prevention concerns, consult a healthcare professional for guidance and appropriate interventions." Relying solely on holy basil for malaria prevention can be dangerous and could lead to delayed diagnosis and treatment, potentially increasing the severity of the disease. It is crucial to consult a healthcare professional for proper diagnosis and treatment if you suspect malaria. Preventive measures like using mosquito nets, insect repellents, and wearing protective clothing are more effective in reducing the risk of contracting malaria. Additionally, many vaccines against malaria are currently being developed. The World Health Organization strongly recommends that children in sub-Saharan Africa and other regions with moderate to high P. falciparum malaria transmission use the RTS,S /AS01 (RTS,S) malaria vaccine.

title: Does onion, ginger, and cardamom cleanse liver in just 3 days?
claim_text: An Instagram post claims that a blend of onion, ginger and cardamom when boiled in a tea, or soup, can flush out liver toxins, and restore full function in as little as three days.
quick_take: A social media post suggests that some kitchen ingredients will help you clean your liver in just 3 days. We fact checked and found the claim to be False.
doctor_explanation:
No. There's no strong scientific backing for these spices performing a true 'cleanse' on your liver. Sure, each has been studied individually for potential benefits, but combining them doesn't suddenly unlock detox superpowers. For instance, onions contain quercetin, an antioxidant that might help reduce oxidative stress in the liver, as shown in some animal research where it prevented fat buildup in rats fed high-cholesterol diets. Ginger's active compounds, like gingerols, have shown promise in lowering inflammation markers in people with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) through small human trials, potentially easing liver strain. Cardamom, meanwhile, has been linked to improved liver enzymes and reduced inflammation in overweight individuals with NAFLD, based on a double-blind study involving daily supplementation. Yet, these effects are subtle and supportive, not a full purge of toxins. Many experts encourage that liver cleanses lack proof and can sometimes do more harm, especially if they replace medical advice for real issues like fatty liver or hepatitis. In short, while these ingredients might add a gentle boost when part of a varied diet, they don't scrub your liver clean like a dishwasher cycle.

Is detoxing the liver in just 3 days even possible? Definitely not. The liver's natural repair process is gradual, often taking weeks or months, depending on the damage. If you've overloaded it with alcohol, for example, minor recovery might begin in days, but full healing requires sustained changes, like quitting alcohol entirely, and could span months. Viral claims of three-day miracles ignore basic biology: toxins aren't flushed out in a flash; the liver processes them continuously through enzymes and bile. Short-term 'detoxes' might make you feel lighter from reduced calorie intake or hydration boosts, but that's not true cleansing, it's often just temporary water loss or placebo effect. Studies on detox diets show no lasting detox benefits, and extreme versions can strain the kidneys or cause nutrient gaps.

They offer some supportive advantages, but nothing revolutionary or combo-specific. Onions, rich in sulphur compounds and flavonoids, can combat inflammation and support antioxidant defences, potentially lowering liver fat in those at risk of NAFLD, per human and animal data. Ginger shines in easing nausea and reducing oxidative stress, with trials indicating it might drop liver enzymes like ALT in NAFLD patients after consistent use over weeks. Cardamom's essential oils have anti-inflammatory effects, helping with lipid profiles and liver stress in small clinical groups. Together in meals, like a warming curry or tea, they could enhance digestion and provide mild anti-inflammatory vibes, indirectly benefiting the liver by promoting overall gut health. But no research tests this exact trio for liver detox, and benefits emerge from long-term habits, not a quick binge.

Dr. Sharad Malhotra, Senior Consultant and Head of Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Therapeutic Endoscopy at Aakash Healthcare in New Delhi, made it clear that no magic drink can actually detox your liver. This vital organ is a natural powerhouse, constantly filtering out toxins on its own without any need for fancy juices or special concoctions. Sure, ingredients like ginger and cardamom can be great, nutritious boosts to your everyday meals, but they're far from a miracle fix. As he pointed out, genuine progress for liver health stems from steady, ongoing lifestyle choices - things like enjoying well-rounded, nutritious foods, drinking plenty of water, cutting back on alcohol and junky processed snacks, keeping stress in check, and making time for regular physical activity.

Dietician Kamana Chauhan pointed out that while the blend of beetroot, carrots, and ginger is helpful, it shouldn't be relied on as the only remedy for fatty liver. Instead, a well-rounded diet, staying hydrated, and maintaining a healthy lifestyle are all crucial for truly and thoroughly detoxing the liver.

Risks: Overconsuming these spices might irritate the stomach, leading to heartburn or bloating, especially if you have acid reflux. More worryingly, believing in a fast fix might delay seeing a doctor for symptoms like fatigue or jaundice, which could signal serious conditions.

title: Does Onion Peel Spray Really Help in Hair Regrowth?- THIP Media
claim_text: Boiling onion peels in water and using the liquid as a spray on the scalp can stimulate hair growth, stop hair fall, and even regrow lost hair.
quick_take: A social media post suggests that onion peel spray helps in hair regrowth. We fact checked and found the claim to be mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Dr. Bhavna Sandhu B.A.M.S. Ludhiana explains: "Ayurvedically, onion is described as having Katu and Madhur ras with Ushna virya, which means it can help improve blood circulation and stimulate hair follicles. Onion peels are also rich in compounds like quercetin and sulfur, which have antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. These may support scalp health by improving local circulation, reducing micro-inflammation, and strengthening hair roots. However, in Ayurveda, onion peel spray is not considered a classical primary treatment for hair loss. It may act only as a supportive external remedy rather than a standalone cure." Onions contain compounds such as sulphur, flavonoids and antioxidants, which are known to support general skin and hair health. Because hair is largely made of a protein called keratin, and sulphur is involved in keratin formation, people often assume that applying onion-based products will stimulate hair growth. However, hair regrowth is a complex biological process. It depends on factors like genetics, hormones, scalp health, nutrition, and medical conditions. A simple homemade spray made from onion peels does not address these underlying causes. Scientific studies that have examined onion juice for hair loss have been very small and limited, and they used fresh onion juice directly on the scalp, not onion peel spray. Even those studies cannot be considered strong evidence. Dr Rashi Soni, Co-founder and Consulting Dermatologist at Rashi Hospital, Mumbai, emphasises that a balanced diet rich in proteins, vitamins and essential minerals plays an important role in reducing hair fall and strengthening hair. She also highlights the importance of gentle hair care practices, such as avoiding harsh chemical treatments and limiting the use of heat-styling tools. Using mild shampoos and conditioners that suit your hair type can further help maintain scalp and hair health. However, if hair loss is related to hormonal imbalances or genetic factors, treatments such as minoxidil or other dermatologist-prescribed medications may be required. She advises seeking guidance from a qualified dermatologist to receive personalised treatment and care. Regarding onion peels containing nutrients that benefit the scalp: onion peels do contain beneficial plant compounds like quercetin and other polyphenols with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. However, the presence of beneficial nutrients does not automatically translate into hair regrowth when applied topically. The scalp acts as a protective barrier. Many compounds in plant extracts do not penetrate deeply enough to affect the hair follicle, which sits under the skin. Without reaching the follicle, the hair growth cycle cannot be significantly influenced. Regarding whether onion peel spray can reduce hair fall or improve hair quality: possibly in minor ways, but the effect is likely small and temporary. Using onion-based rinses may sometimes make hair appear slightly shinier or smoother, mainly because natural plant extracts can condition the hair shaft. Some people also report less hair breakage, which may give the impression of reduced hair fall. However, it is important to understand the difference between hair breakage and true hair loss. Hair loss occurs when hair follicles stop producing healthy hair. This can happen due to conditions such as hormonal changes, nutrient deficiencies, stress, or genetics. A topical spray made from onion peels cannot correct these deeper causes. What actually helps with hair regrowth according to science: evidence-based treatments and addressing the root cause are what truly help. Medical research shows that hair regrowth depends on treating the underlying reason for hair loss. This may involve improving nutrition, managing hormonal conditions, reducing stress, or using treatments recommended by doctors. Nutrients such as protein, iron, zinc, vitamin D and biotin play an important role in maintaining healthy hair growth. In some cases, dermatologists may recommend clinically tested treatments if hair loss is significant. Lifestyle factors also matter. Adequate sleep, a balanced diet, and gentle hair care practices can support overall hair health much more effectively than unproven home sprays. The idea that onion peel spray can regrow hair is largely a myth. While onion peels contain antioxidants and plant compounds, there is no reliable scientific evidence showing that spraying onion peel water on the scalp can stimulate hair follicles or reverse hair loss. At most, it may act as a simple herbal rinse with mild conditioning effects.

title: Does only cholesterol plaque cause ED? - THIP Media
claim_text: A Facebook post claims that there is only one cause of erectile dysfunction, i.e., sticky cholesterol plaque that clogs the blood flow to the penis. It is unrelated to stress, fatigue, psychological reasons or low testosterone levels. It further states that it is not a normal part of aging.
quick_take: A social media post claims that no amount of pills can help with erectile dysfunction as it is unrelated to stress, fatigue, psychological reasons or low testosterone levels and is caused by a buildup of a sticky cholesterol plaque. We fact-checked and found this claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation:
Erectile dysfunction or ED is the inability to get or keep an erection firm enough for sexual intercourse. It is a common male sexual problem that can affect men of all ages, but it is more common in older men. It is frequently described as an ongoing issue that lasts at least six months.

Dr Rupin Shah, consultant Andrologist and Microsurgeon, clarifies that it's not a label, a diagnosis or a stigma. He adds how somebody who has no problem otherwise, can also have ED. Dr Shah explains, "We need to start by understanding that it's nothing to be ashamed of or worried about, and neither does it necessarily mean that there is something wrong. A problem with erection, which is what it is, could happen in any young person, just because he was anxious or tense or misinformed or was trying to impress a new partner so could have ED due to performance anxiety."

No. ED can be caused by a variety of factors and even though cholesterol plaque can be a factor, it can't be the only one factor. Cholesterol plaque can cause ED by narrowing or blocking the arteries that supply blood to the penis. This can reduce blood flow to the penis, making it difficult to get or keep an erection. The condition is called as Arteriogenic ED or arterial ED when atherosclerosis (buildup of cholesterol plaque in arteries) causes a blockage in one more of the arteries that supply blood to the penis. However, it is important to note that not all men with cholesterol plaque will develop ED. Conversely, not all men with ED have cholesterol plaque.

Dr Raman Tanwar, Andrologist and Urologist at Urocentre, Jyoti Hospital, Gurugram, says, "It is a complex problem as it arises from the faulty interplay of the mind, the nerves, the arteries, the corporal sponge, the veins, and the influence of hormones. It can be both physiological or organic as well as psychological."

The factors which may cause ED can be medical, psychological, or lifestyle-related. Lifestyle factors, such as smoking, excessive alcohol use, and drug use can lead to this condition. Additionally, certain medical conditions, like cardiovascular risks, could restrict blood flow to the penis, making it difficult to achieve or maintain an erection. Moreover, neurological disorders such as multiple sclerosis and Parkinson's disease can interfere with the nerve signals needed for normal sexual function. Hormonal imbalances, particularly low testosterone levels, can also contribute to erectile dysfunction. Additionally, some medications, like antidepressants, antihypertensives, and antipsychotics, may cause ED as a side effect. Lastly, nutritional insufficiency, such as Vitamin D deficiency can also increase the risk of ED by promoting endothelial dysfunction.

Also, Dr Shah comments on this by stating, "It could happen in middle-aged men who again don't have a real problem, but they're stressed out, have work-related tension, work pressure, and come home very tired. It could happen in older men who have actual physical problems because of diabetes, hypertension, high cholesterol, and smoking, all of which compromise the blood flow."

Another important factor which puts the male at an increased risk of ED is obesity. It causes insulin insensitivity in the body which leads to high blood glucose levels. Over a period of time, high glucose levels cause damage to blood vessels that carry blood to the penis. It can also cause damage to the nerves that innervate the penis. It sometimes leads to abnormal testosterone levels which can also cause erectile dysfunction.

Additionally, stress can be a cause of psychological erectile dysfunction. Factors involved in an erection include blood vessels, the nervous system, muscles, and emotions. Chronic stress can affect the way the brain signals the physical response of the body. At the time of erection, the penis gets an extra flow of blood. When a person is stressed, the flow of blood gets interrupted.

Boston-based Dr Anita Shyam, Psychiatrist, Clinical Sexologist, and Sex and Intimacy Coach, often meets patients who come to her after having met other doctors and have long-term ED "Stress plays a major role in an individual's relations causing a lot of relationship problems that go on to cause a lot of sexual problems."

title: Fact Check: Does oregano prevent cancer? - THIP Media
claim_text: An article titled 'Oregano Oil Health Benefits, Uses And Its Side Effects' published on Lybrate claims that organic oregano seed oil can prevent potential harm from free radicals and actively repair damage. This will entirely eliminate the risk of cancer.
quick_take: An article published by a healthcare online platform claims that oregano prevents cancer. We fact checked it and found the claim to be Half True.
doctor_explanation: Is oregano healthy? Yes, oregano is a healthy herb. Packed with antioxidants, it possesses anti-inflammatory properties that can contribute to overall well-being. Oregano also contains essential nutrients, including vitamins and minerals. Incorporating this aromatic herb into your diet, whether in fresh or dried form, may provide potential health benefits. However, it's important to view oregano as part of a diverse and balanced diet for optimal nutrition. Oregano has nutritional richness and health benefits. But it is important to note that not all varieties offer the same effects. Specific species of oregano, such as Origanum vulgare, have health-promoting properties. Rich in antioxidants, oregano contains phenols like carvacrol and thymol, which possess antimicrobial properties. These compounds contribute to its ability to combat bacteria and other microorganisms. Additionally oregano is a source of essential vitamins, including A, C, and K, and minerals like calcium, iron, and manganese. Cancer is a complex disease that happens due to uncontrolled cell growth. Below we have written how diet can influence this process and potentially reduce the risk of cancer: DNA damage: Free radicals (reactive molecules) generated from internal processes or external sources like pollution and UV rays may damage DNA. This can lead to mutations. Some dietary antioxidants can scavenge these free radicals, protecting DNA from damage. Inflammation: Chronic inflammation creates an environment conducive to cancer growth. Certain dietary components like sugar, processed meats, and unhealthy fats may promote inflammation. Conversely, foods rich in anti-inflammatory compounds can suppress inflammation. Hormonal imbalance: Hormones like estrogen and insulin can influence cell growth, and diet can affect their levels. For example, excessive red meat consumption is linked to elevated estrogen levels. This potentially increases the risk of hormone-sensitive cancers like breast cancer. Conversely, fiber-rich foods can help regulate hormone levels. Metabolic abnormalities: Obesity and metabolic syndrome may cause an increase in insulin resistance and chronic inflammation. Both of them may promote cancer development. A healthy diet can help regulate metabolism and reduce these risks. Gut microbiome: The trillions of bacteria in the gut play a crucial role in digestion, immune function, and inflammation. Disruptions in the gut microbiome (dysbiosis) may increase cancer risk. Dietary fiber feeds beneficial gut bacteria, promoting a healthy microbiome and potentially reducing cancer risk. Can be. The claim has some accuracy. But crucial details such as the specific type of oregano, the type and stage of cancer, and individual factors influencing cancer growth are unclear. Not all commercially available oregano, as found in pizza shops or grocery shelves, may have the properties required for cancer treatment. Our research shows that including oregano in diet can work against certain cancers. Oregano contains compounds like carvacrol and thymol, which have demonstrated antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties in laboratory studies. Oregano is also linked to a lower risk of colon cancer. While its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial benefits are known, its specific role in cancer prevention, particularly the mechanism involved, is less studied. Another study was also conducted for its effects on skin cells and melanoma (a type of skin cancer). The oregano extract was found to have a unique chemical makeup and could stop the growth of melanoma cells. It did this by causing these cancer cells to undergo a kind of self-destruction process. Importantly, the oregano extract seemed to affect cancer cells more than normal cells. This discovery suggests that oregano, with its natural compounds, could be a promising candidate for developing new drugs to treat melanoma. However, translating these findings to human health requires more comprehensive research, including clinical trials. So, including oregano in a varied and balanced diet may offer nutritional benefits. But it is premature to definitively state that oregano can protect against cancer. We need more research to establish a clearer link between oregano consumption and cancer prevention. The same statement is also supported by Dr. Moujhuri Nandi, Consultant Radiation Oncologist at Karkinos Healthcare Pvt. Ltd. Moreover, the American Society of Cancer website informs that diet is just one element influencing cancer risk. Genetics, lifestyle choices like smoking and exercise, and environmental factors also play substantial roles. While a healthy diet cannot entirely prevent cancer, it substantially decreases the risk. Individual needs vary, emphasizing the importance of personalized dietary advice from healthcare professionals. By comprehending the underlying mechanisms and embracing a healthy dietary pattern, individuals actively contribute to cancer prevention and overall well-being. Shivashankar T. is the Chief Clinical Nutritionist and Dietician at Tata Memorial Cancer Hospital, Mumbai informs, 'Eating a balanced diet that includes plenty of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and lean proteins can help maintain a healthy weight and provide the necessary nutrients to support the immune system. Some studies suggest that certain foods, such as cruciferous vegetables (e.g. broccoli, cauliflower), berries, and turmeric, may have anti-cancer properties. The best anti-cancer diet is the Mediterranean diet. In this diet, there is less red meat and good amount of white meat'. What are the dangers of attempting to treat cancer through diet without seeking medical advice? Relying solely on dietary changes to cure cancer without consulting medical professionals can be highly risky. Cancer is a multifaceted disease that requires comprehensive medical intervention beyond dietary adjustments. Depending solely on home remedies may worsen the situation, making the cancer more difficult to treat or possibly incurable. Cancer cells can rapidly multiply and spread. So, any delay in seeking professional medical treatment may intensify the severity of the condition. This can make it harder to manage and treat the cancer effectively. Voomika Mukherjee, Health & Nutrition Life coach, emphasises that while no specific food or food group can guarantee the prevention of cancer, avoiding certain items won't necessarily reduce the risk. In the context of cancer treatment, maintaining a healthy body weight, particularly minimising visceral fat and enhancing muscle strength, alongside a balanced diet, is crucial. Mukherjee recommends a well-rounded diet that includes beans, lean proteins, fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and low-fat dairy while reducing the intake of sugar, caffeine, salt, and alcohol. She underscores that consuming meals of adequate quality and quantity plays a role in lowering the risk of cancer and other chronic diseases. However, it's essential to note that no single food can serve as a cure for cancer. Dr. Sarthak Moharir, Chief Radiation Oncologist Apollo Cancer Centre, Bilaspur further adds, 'Special diet or diet modifications do not cure cancer. Diet is very important for patients undergoing cancer treatment. So, patients must take a balance meal with all macros and micronutrients as prescribed by their dietary counsellor.'

title: Does palm oil increase cholesterol and diabetes levels? - THIP
claim_text: Palm oil makes the body prone to cardiovascular disease and diabetes
quick_take: A video on social media about palm oil increase cholesterol and linked to diabetes is likely an exaggeration or a misconception. We fact checked the side effect and found the claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation:
Regarding diabetes: A 2020 study highlighted that palm oil contains a diverse array of antioxidants, which are believed to shield the body from oxidative stress-induced cellular damage, making it potentially beneficial for individuals with diabetes. While red palm oil has been extensively studied for its nutritional advantages, such as its antioxidant properties, ability to lower cholesterol, protection against atherosclerosis, and potential anticancer effects, there remains a scarcity of data specifically examining its effects on diabetes. This review thus centres on exploring the potential of palm oil to alleviate diabetes mellitus.

Regarding cholesterol and cardiovascular disease: The relationship between palm oil consumption and heart attacks is mixed, as numerous studies have not definitively identified the primary cause. A 2015 study on humans found palm oil to have a neutral or even favorable impact on cholesterol levels compared to other oils. For instance, a study in Nigeria showed lower cholesterol levels in subjects using palm oil exclusively compared to Americans. In a 2003 Chinese study, palm oil reduced cholesterol in individuals with normal levels but had varying effects in those with high cholesterol, improving the TC/HDL ratio more than peanut oil.

A 2014 rat study found no significant difference in blood cholesterol levels between rats fed palm oil and those fed sunflower oil, despite the latter having less saturated fat. However, rats consuming palm oil had more liver fat accumulation, suggesting potential liver health effects and the need for moderation. A 2010 study revealed diets with corn oil, butter, animal fat, or margarine increased serum triglycerides, while diets with soybean oil, palm oil, olive oil, or sunflower oil resulted in lower triglyceride levels.

A 2021 study on rats examined the cardiovascular effects of fresh versus thermally oxidized palm oil. Rats consuming thermally oxidized palm oil had lower triglyceride, VLDL, and HDL levels but higher total cholesterol and LDL levels, indicating potential negative cardiovascular effects due to lipid peroxidation from vitamin E destruction. A 2022 study highlighted palm oil's vitamin E content, which can improve heart health by slowing or preventing heart disease progression and reducing plaque buildup and ischemic damage. When consumed as part of a balanced diet, palm oil does not pose an additional risk for cardiovascular disease.

Why Indian food companies and street vendors prefer palm oil: Palm oil is favoured by both Indian food companies and street vendors for its cost-effectiveness, versatility, and stability. Its economic viability makes it ideal for food production, while its neutral taste and high smoke point allow extensive culinary use, particularly in frying. Additionally, palm oil's resistance to oxidation ensures extended product shelf life, contributing to its widespread adoption in the food industry across India.

Why palm oil is in controversy: Palm oil is contentious due to deforestation and health worries, yet it remains a dietary staple in tropical areas such as Africa, Southeast Asia, and parts of Brazil. Despite their regular usage, Russia tops the list for heart attacks, and the USA has high obesity rates. Vendors use palm oil for its cost-effectiveness, flavour enhancement, and popularity in foods like samosas and namkeens. Natural foods aren't inherently harmful; tackling overconsumption and making informed decisions is essential.

Dr Swati Dave's conclusion: 'A healthy lifestyle is not about deprivation, it's about balance. It's about finding harmony between the food you eat. As a dietician, I've seen people try to cut out entire food groups or restrict themselves to fad diets, only to end up feeling deprived and eventually giving up. That's not sustainable. That's not living.' And let's be real, palm oil isn't the devil. It's a complex issue with multifaceted solutions. The problem isn't the palm oil itself, but our relationship with it. We overindulge in processed foods, we over consume unhealthy fats, and we neglect our physical activity. So, instead of demonising palm oil, let's focus on teaching ourselves and our children moderation. Let's teach them that it's okay to have a cookie or two, but it's also important to balance that with healthy habits like regular exercise and mindful eating.
