title: Fact Check: Is a DIY shampoo reliable for lice treatment at home?
claim_text: Take neem leaves, garlic, one spoon of turmeric, and half a cup of water. Then, boil this mix for ten minutes, strain it, and add your favourite shampoo and lemon. Use this mix two to three times a week to get rid of dandruff and lice, like they were never there before.
quick_take: A viral social media post suggests a lice treatment at home. The video claims that neem leaves, garlic, turmeric, and water, along with shampoo and lemon, can treat dandruff and lice in just a few uses. After fact checking, we found this claim to bemostly false.
doctor_explanation: How effective is a neem remedy for lice? Not really. Neem and garlic do have insect-repelling and antimicrobial properties, but using them in a home remedy isn't enough for effective lice treatment at home. A 2012 study showed that a specially made shampoo with neem seed extract (Licener®) killed all lice and prevented eggs from hatching, after just one use. But this was a standardised neem product, not boiled neem leaves. So, a simple neem remedy for lice, like boiling the leaves at home, is unlikely to work the same way. Similarly, a 2010 study found that a 25% garlic extract killed lice in just 4 minutes and 35 seconds by disrupting their nervous and breathing systems. But again, this was a lab-made extract. Raw garlic or homemade pastes are not proven to be effective. There is no strong evidence that combining boiled neem and garlic water with shampoo can completely remove lice and nits. Lice are parasites that live close to the scalp and lay eggs near the hair roots. Fully treating an infestation usually requires clinically tested products, not DIY mixes like ginger, lemon or neem. Natural or home remedies may help with itching but won't clear lice on their own. Dr Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant in Lucknow, says, 'Neem has some insect-repelling properties, but when it comes to treating head lice, we need something more reliable. The correct approach involves using clinically tested anti-lice shampoos or lotions that contain ingredients like permethrin or malathion. These are designed to kill both adult lice and their eggs. Along with that, regular combing with a fine-toothed lice comb helps remove dead lice and nits. Home remedies may give some relief, but they don't guarantee complete removal. For best results, it's always better to follow a targeted, medical treatment.' Does turmeric help with dandruff? Only in theory. Turmeric contains curcumin, which has anti-inflammatory and antifungal properties. Some small studies suggest it may help reduce skin inflammation or dryness. However, there's no clinical proof that turmeric alone, or in a shampoo mix like this, can cure dandruff. Dandruff is usually caused by a fungus called Malassezia, excess oil on the scalp, or skin sensitivity. Medical shampoos containing ingredients like ketoconazole, zinc pyrithione, or salicylic acid are proven to work better than DIY home remedies. For instance, some suggest methi, clove, kalonji and onion to cure dandruff at home, but this is misleading. Can lemon and shampoo boost the effect of lice treatment at home? No. Lemon juice is acidic and may offer a slight cleansing effect, but it can also irritate the scalp, especially if used frequently. A 2022 study looked at limonin, a compound found in citrus fruits like lemon, for its potential to help with hair growth, not lice or dandruff. The study showed that limonin may help hair cells grow by affecting certain pathways in lab tests on rats. But it did not show any effect on lice, nits, or dandruff. Furthermore, mixing it with shampoo doesn't make it stronger. In fact, such combinations can sometimes cause more dryness or itching, especially if someone already has a sensitive scalp or skin issues like eczema. Shampoo alone is made to clean the scalp, but diluting it with boiled herbal water does not increase its power to cure dandruff or lice. So while the mix may sound like a natural option for lice treatment at home, it doesn't hold up scientifically. Why do dandruff and lice need targeted treatment? Because causes are different and need specific solutions. Dandruff and lice may both cause itching, but they are very different problems. Dandruff is linked to scalp skin and oil imbalance, while lice are living insects. That's why treating both requires different kinds of products. There are no shortcuts or all-in-one natural cures. While home remedies may offer mild relief, only properly tested treatments can fully manage or remove the problem. For a reliable solution, one should choose products that are clinically tested. Dr Rashi Soni, Consultant Dermatologist, Rashi Hospital, Mumbai, explains, 'Dandruff and lice may both cause itching, but they are completely different problems and need different treatments. Dandruff is often linked to scalp irritation or an overgrowth of a yeast-like fungus, while lice are tiny insects that live and lay eggs in the hair. You can't treat both with the same shampoo or home remedy. Lice need specific anti-parasitic treatments to kill the bugs and their eggs. Dandruff, on the other hand, needs antifungal or scalp-calming products. That's why it's important to know the cause before choosing the treatment.' In summary, the viral claim that a homemade mix of neem, garlic, turmeric, lemon, and shampoo can cure dandruff and lice is mostly false. While some of the ingredients have natural properties that may offer temporary relief, there is no medical or scientific proof that this remedy can treat lice or dandruff effectively. For proper care, it's best to use proven antifungal or anti-lice shampoos and consult a healthcare provider if symptoms persist. When it comes to lice treatment at home, make sure the method is safe, reliable, and backed by evidence.

title: Fact Check: Is a homemade drink to cure cancer really effective?
claim_text: Boiling cucumbers, carrots, ginger, mint, coriander, and amla (or lemon) in a clay pot for 10 minutes and leaving it to soak overnight creates a powerful healing drink. Drinking one glass of this water on an empty stomach cleans the kidneys, liver, stomach, and blood, flushes out cholesterol and triglycerides, removes major diseases, prevents cancer completely, and cures cancer from the roots.
quick_take: A social media video suggests a homemade drink to cure cancer and cleanse all the internal organs and the blood. After fact-checking, we found this claim to be false.
doctor_explanation: The claim that this boiled veggie detox drink can clean internal organs is not backed by science. The kidneys and liver already work hard to remove waste and toxins from the body. Drinking water is important, but no one food or drink can magically 'clean' these organs. The idea of 'detoxifying' organs through a specific drink is not backed by science. A balanced diet, regular movement, and staying hydrated support organ health, not this kind of shortcut. Boiling ingredients like cucumber, carrot, ginger, and mint in water may allow some vitamins or plant chemicals to seep into the water, but most of their benefits come from eating them whole, not just drinking their boiled water. Heat-sensitive nutrients like vitamin C may be lost during boiling. There is no strong evidence that this drink alone can reduce cholesterol or triglycerides in the blood. Ingredients like ginger and amla do have some heart-friendly compounds, but controlling cholesterol needs bigger lifestyle changes like eating less saturated fat, quitting smoking, exercising, and sometimes taking prescribed medicines. This drink is not a substitute. Dr Pooja Khullar, Radiation Oncologist at Dharamshila Narayana Super Speciality Hospital in New Delhi, says, 'No homemade drink or herb, no matter how healthy it seems, has been scientifically proven to cure cancer. Some plant ingredients may show benefits in lab settings, but that doesn't mean they work the same way in real patients. Cancer is a complex disease that usually needs a proper combination of treatments like surgery, chemotherapy, radiation, or targeted therapy. Depending only on home remedies without medical advice can delay the right treatment and reduce the chances of recovery. If someone wants to use natural options along with medical care, they must speak to their doctor first.' Dr P. Rammanohar, Research Director at Amrita School of Ayurveda, stated, 'Cancer is a group of many different diseases, each needing specific approaches to treatment. There is no one-size-fits-all cure. Some herbs have shown anticancer effects in laboratory studies, but that does not make them proven treatments for patients. Without strong clinical evidence in humans, no single herb or home remedy can be relied on to treat or cure cancer.' Dr Muskan Thakur, Ayurveda Consultant from Indore, also cautions against relying on such remedies alone. She explains, 'Cancer is a disease which needs proper medical treatment — whether it's chemotherapy, radiation, immunotherapy, or other clinical approaches. Depending only on homemade or Ayurvedic drinks or diets to cure cancer isn't backed by scientific evidence. That said, Ayurveda can support recovery by helping manage symptoms, reduce side effects, and improve overall well-being. Herbal diets, fresh juices, and immunity-boosting foods may complement standard treatment, but they should never replace it. Patients should always work with both an oncologist and an experienced Ayurvedic doctor to ensure safe and balanced care.'

title: Fact check: Is a homemade recipe effective for cavities in children?
claim_text: A homemade preparation made of garlic, Eno, toothpaste, lemon juice, and shampoo is a multipurpose natural remedy that whitens teeth effectively and is beneficial for oral issues like bad breath and dental cavities in both adults and children.
quick_take: A social media post claims that a homemade preparation is a natural solution for cavities in both children and adults. We fact-checked the claim and found that it ismostly false.
doctor_explanation: Cavities in the primary dentition of young children are known as early childhood caries, or ECC. Dental caries is one of the most prevalent, albeit preventable, diseases that affect kids less than six years of age. It is a dynamic, multidimensional, biofilm-mediated, sugar-driven condition that is influenced by biological, behavioural, psychological, and economic factors in an individual's environment. In an interview with THIP Media, Dr. Gauri Kalra, Professor, Department of Paediatric Dentistry, Manav Rachna Dental College, Faridabad, explains that while milk teeth are not permanent and they eventually fall off at a predesigned time as the baby grows and becomes an adolescent, maintaining their wellness is equally significant. Healthy baby teeth are a sign of a healthy child. Milk teeth are important as they are the natural space keepers for permanent teeth. If primary or milk teeth are neglected, ECC can have serious repercussions, such as poor permanent tooth growth, excruciating pain, infections, cognitive problems, and trouble speaking and eating. These problems can eventually affect a person's ability to succeed in school, their self-confidence, and their overall wellness. Routine follow-ups, parental education, and early professional intervention are essential for preventing ECC and promoting long-term dental health. The post made unsubstantiated claims regarding the use of toothpaste, shampoo, lemon juice, garlic, and Eno to treat dental cavities in children. Since children are more prone to tooth decay than adults, it becomes imperative to analyse these ingredients. Beginning with garlic: the primary ingredient, allicin, has antibacterial characteristics that could help reduce the oral bacterial load; nevertheless, there is conflicting scientific proof about its direct application for the treatment of paediatric carious lesions. Toothpaste, when appropriately formulated for children (with a correct fluoride content of 1000 ppm for children above 3 years), may facilitate cavity prevention but cannot manage tooth decay. Eno, an antacid that contains citric acid and sodium bicarbonate, is not intended for oral use by children because it may upset the pH balance in the mouth, which could further exacerbate the demineralisation of paediatric enamel. Likewise, the high acidity of lemon juice can damage tooth enamel and make cavities worse. Most concerning of all, shampoo or hair cleanser is a chemical-based cosmetic product that is not edible and is not thought to be safe for oral exposure or ingestion, especially by children. There is no medical literature to support the ingestion of this hazardous ingredient by children. Dr. Laresh Mistry, Senior Consultant and Associate Professor, Department of Paediatric Dentistry, Bharati Vidyapeeth Dental College, Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra, strongly advises that the use of lemon juice, ENO and shampoo to treat early childhood caries is not only ineffective but potentially harmful. Children under the age of 6 (ECC susceptible) often lack the ability to spit properly, making ingestion likely—and ingredients like shampoo are toxic if swallowed. Acidic agents like lemon juice can erode enamel, while ENO and garlic offer no proven benefit against cavity-causing bacteria. Such remedies may create new problems without addressing the real issue. The only safe and effective approach is professional care guided by a paediatric dentist and a personalised prevention plan. Parents should understand that the homemade recipe suggested in the claim lacks substantial scientific support. As a result, unsupervised use of the untested formulation could cause toxicity, enamel erosion, or burns to the mouth. Parents should always seek professional dental advice for the handling of dental cavities in children. Some products that are deemed safe for adults may be entirely unsafe for children due to notable physiological disparities. Children are especially susceptible to some toxins because they often have larger pulp chambers, thinner enamel coatings, and developing immune systems. Any mixture containing acidic, alkaline, and detergent-based ingredients, such as the one recommended in the claim, has the potential to irreversibly impair systemic and oral wellness. Tobacco stains and dental cavities are two distinct oral conditions, each necessitating specific interventions. Tobacco stains are external discolourations on the tooth surfaces that are usually brought on by tar and nicotine depositions. Generally, these external stains are addressed with counselling for quitting the addictive habit, professional scaling, and teeth-whitening procedures. Conversely, no home cure has been proven to successfully halt or reverse the development of dental cavities in either adults or children, which are caused by bacterial activity leading to tooth tissue loss. Dr. Ketan Rajput, BDS, MDS, Periodontist and Oral Implantologist, Dhule, Maharashtra, advises consulting a dentist before trying any new oral hygiene methods, especially for cavities in children, which can become problematic if ignored. The evidence-based methodology for addressing cavities in children includes: Early, non-cavitated lesions generally respond well to fluoride treatments since they can help halt or even reverse the existing demineralisation. For cavitated lesions, restorative techniques, including GIC and composite resin fillings, can be applied. ART utilizing high-viscosity glass ionomer and hand tools works well with young or nervous children. In more severe situations, stainless steel crowns and pulp therapy may be used to save the tooth. Dental care for kids is always supported by behavioural modification and nutritional counselling. When prevention-focused therapy is combined with minimally invasive procedures, caries development and the need for complex therapies are greatly reduced.

title: Fact Check: Is a PCR test covertly vaccinating people?
claim_text: Johns Hopkins University Confirms: You can be 'Vaccinated' with a PCR Test, Even Without Knowing. The claim suggests that PCR tests used for COVID-19 testing secretly contain micro-devices called 'theragrippers' that can vaccinate people without their knowledge.

doctor_explanation: Theragripper is a microdevice invented by Johns Hopkins University that can slowly release drugs into the body through the gastrointestinal tract. The 'theragrippers' are made of metal, each roughly the size of a dust speck, can potentially carry any drug and release it gradually into the body. John Hopkins published about the technology in March 2020. Yes, as per the initial reports published the technology can be used to deliver drugs inside our bodies. However, the tests are done on animal models at the moment and there is no reports about the technology being used currently in any medical applications. PCR is an abbreviation for Polymerase Chain Reaction. PCR test is widely used to detect covid positive people as the test can trace viruses in the earliest stages of infection. During the PCR test, the sample DNA is copied multiple times to detect the virus. However, the covid virus is made of RNA for which Reverse Transcription PCR (rtPCR) test is done. During rtPCR, the sample RNA is converted into DNA before copying using PCR equipment. No evidence proves PCR testing can secretly vaccinate people against the Covid virus. The claim has been circulating since 2021 with the intent to spread misinformation on social media. The press release by the university about the theragrippers was published in 2020 and is not a new confirmation. The report clearly mentioned that Theragrippers have been tested only on animals to deliver pain-relieving drugs. There have been no recent communication from John Hopkins about theragrippers being put to production for real life use. Moreover, theragrippers have not been approved by any agency worldwide for delivering drugs to humans. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration website and the Indian Ministry of Health and Family Welfare website have set guidelines to avoid tampering with the covid sample.

title: Fact Check: Does a sauna blanket let you lose inches quickly? - THIP Media
claim_text: Sauna Blanket treatment rejuvenates muscles while gets rid of harmful toxins! #detox #musclerecovery #bodysculptingtreatment #saunablanket #loseinches #sweatchallenge

Along with the video, the post claims the treatment rejuvenates muscles and removes harmful toxins along with #loseinches. We fact-checked and found the claim to have a missing context and is Half True.
doctor_explanation: A sauna blanket is a portable device which uses Far Infrared Radiation (FIR) to warm the body while zipped up in a blanket. Unlike steam saunas, FIR sauna blanket operates at a lower temperature. The available evidence shows that 'FIR therapy uses a certain wavelength of light to restore, repair, and protect cellular tissue. Also, FIR can affect bodily cells by increasing their mitochondrial function and producing more cellular energy'. The Heliotherapy Research Institute website has shown that the temperature can exist between 70 to 180°C. Relaxing inside the sauna blanket for a short period helps people experience an intense sweat session and increased heart rate that can release toxins and speed up muscle recovery. Sauna blankets can improve blood circulation, release the happy hormone, improve skin appearance or de-stress and improve sleep. However, dry saunas like sauna blankets are considered for weight loss. It does not seem so. Sauna blankets cannot lose inches in one sitting. But, regular use can induce weight loss which might temporarily reduce a few inches. Sauna blankets cannot lose fat. Any kind of sauna can target weight content by reducing water retention in the body by releasing sweat. However, the weight gets replenished by one's dietary preferences. Fat loss is induced by increasing the metabolic rate which any kind of sauna does not seem to do. Metabolic rate can be increased by regularly eating a healthy diet and doing exercise which is a significant metabolism booster. This has been further confirmed by Dr. Kashyap Dakshini, General Physician, who said, "Using Sauna blankets will remove the 'easily replaceable water' from the body, as the heat makes one sweat, it will lead to fluid loss. The water/fluid loss is the reason for a lower weight on the scale after a sauna session, which will be regained upon consumption of fluids/liquids. Sauna blankets, if used with clothes on, should not impose any risk, except for those who are insensitive to heat". To a certain extent. The heat from the sauna blanket may cause temporary symptoms such as headache, rash, heat exhaustion, dizziness or even dehydration. These symptoms recover within a short span. The use of a sauna blanket is mostly considered non-harmful. Dr. Kashyap Dakshini recommends that "one should drink sufficient water/liquids to avoid dehydration, low blood pressure, light-headedness at the end of a sauna session. THIP Media analysed the video and found that the person on the bed was wrapped in three different layers. The videos of sauna blankets on YouTube do not seem to follow the same process. Social media can often provide conflicting and inaccurate guidance when it comes to weight loss. The diverse opinions and information shared on social platforms can make it challenging to discern what is truly effective and safe. This presents a significant issue, as individuals may end up adopting practices that are detrimental to their health. THIP MEDIA TAKE: Sauna blanket can rejuvenate muscles and remove harmful toxins if used under proper guidance. But a single sitting or not following the correct procedure can cause side effects. Also, no evidence confirms sauna blankets can induce weight loss. Hence, the claim has a missing context and is half true until proven otherwise.

title: Fact Check: Is a woman thrown into prison for abortion in Alabama? - THIP Media
claim_text: In Iran if a 12-year-old girl is raped and impregnated by her father, she must carry the baby to term, or be thrown in prison for life. Wait, sorry, no. That's Alabama.

Infants and Incompetents § 26-23A-4, 'Except in the case of a medical emergency, no abortion shall be performed or induced without the voluntary and informed consent of the woman upon whom the abortion is to be performed or induced.' Nothing in this section shall be construed to make an abortion legal which is not otherwise authorized by law.' In 2019, Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey signed into law House Bill 314, The Human Life Protection Act (HB 314), also known as the Alabama abortion ban, which was set to impose a near-total ban on abortion in the state starting in November 2019. Section 5 of HB314 states that 'No woman upon whom an abortion is performed or attempted to be performed shall be criminally or civilly liable. Additionally, the act is not enforced in Alabama at the time of writing, as it was blocked by a lawsuit in 2019. Furthermore, the Supreme Court decision Roe v. Wade stated that abortion is a constitutional right. As per this decision, the state laws that completely ban abortion are considered unconstitutional.

title: Fact Check: Is adding turmeric to chai poisonous or potentially fatal?
claim_text: A Facebook video by the name Jay Maa Durga asserts that adding turmeric to your chai can be extremely hazardous, to the extent that there wouldn't be enough time to even reach the hospital before facing fatal consequences.
quick_take: There's a long 17-minute video on Facebook claiming that drinking chai with turmeric can be poisonous and even deadly. We fact checked the claim and found it to be False.
doctor_explanation: The addition of turmeric to milk tea does not typically render it poisonous or harmful. Turmeric is a widely used spice known for its vibrant colour and potential health benefits. When added to milk tea, it imparts a subtle earthy flavour and a rich golden hue. While some concerns have been raised about the potential interaction between turmeric and certain medications or health conditions, consuming turmeric in moderation as part of a balanced diet is generally considered safe for most people. However, excessive consumption of turmeric daily or any substance can lead to adverse effects. Additionally, individuals with specific allergies or sensitivities to turmeric should exercise caution. Curcumin, found in turmeric, can change how certain medications work in your body by affecting their levels and how they're processed. When taken with drugs like those for heart health, depression, blood thinners, antibiotics, cancer treatments, and allergies, curcumin can alter their effectiveness. This happens because curcumin can block certain enzymes and proteins in the body that help process medications. While there's only limited evidence from one study showing significant changes in drug levels when curcumin is taken with other medications, more research in humans is needed to fully understand these interactions. The recommended daily intake of turmeric varies, but a typical suggestion is around 1 to 3 grams, equivalent to roughly 1/2 to 1.5 teaspoons of ground turmeric. This amount offers a moderate dose of curcumin, the active compound, which may provide health advantages. Nonetheless, excessive doses or concentrated supplements could lead to adverse effects or interfere with medications. Dr. Swati Dave dismisses the notion, highlighting the historical practice of consuming turmeric tea with milk or water without any signs of harm. She points out that the real risk comes from consuming stale tea, and warns against the dangers of regularly drinking sugary tea and leading a sedentary lifestyle, which can lead to several health issues. Additionally, she advises against consuming tea with meals or in close proximity to them. The presence of anti-nutrients in tea can impede the absorption of micronutrients, particularly iron, affecting their availability in the body.

title: Fact check: Is Almond mixed with butter a natural cure for stammering?
claim_text: Almond mixed with butter is a natural cure for stammering. In the video, the user explains that one should take 5-7 almonds and soak them in water overnight. These almonds should be ground in butter, and licking them every day can benefit those who are stammering or stuttering.
quick_take: No. almonds mixed with butter, or even alone, cannot cure stammering. No scientific evidence supporting this claim is found. Hence, the claim eating soaked almonds mixed with butter everyday naturally cures stammering is False.
doctor_explanation:
There is no scientific evidence, or medical research that supports almonds having any effect on curing or directly improving stammering and stuttering.

What is stammering? Stammering is a speech disorder affecting fluency and timing. It is characterized by repetitions, pauses, unnecessary vowel production, unintentional breaks, spasms, and emotional swings during speech production, making it difficult to communicate effectively. Stammering can occur at any age, although it typically starts in preschool years, suggesting that factors during child development are involved.

Is there a cure for stammering? There is no definitive 'cure' for stuttering (also known as stammering), as it varies greatly from person to person and can be influenced by multiple factors, including genetic, developmental, and neurological components. However, there are effective treatments that can help manage and reduce the symptoms of stuttering. The three types of stuttering are developmental, neurogenic, and psychogenic. Some of the measures used to treat stammering include speech therapy and cognitive behavioural therapy.

Benefits of almonds: Almonds are high in antioxidants, vitamin E, protein, and fibre. They may have health benefits, including supporting heart health and reducing blood pressure. However, there is no evidence of their curing speech disorders.

Does almond butter really cure stammering? No almond butter does not cure stammering. According to American Speech-Language-Hearing Association, Stammering can only be managed with the help of a speech-language pathologist (SLP), making people feel less tense and speak more freely in school, at work, and in different social settings.

Tania Solanki, a speech-language pathologist from Meenakshi Speech and Hearing Clinic, said: 'Almonds do not affect stammering. Eating almonds may help in overall Brain functioning; it is good for health but has no relation directly to curing stuttering (stammering).' She further quoted an article published by Singh et al. (2022) regarding the same issue, where eating almonds was one of the psychological beliefs of the clients, which was mentioned under the label 'superstitious beliefs.' She added: 'For example, doctors won't support the use of mustard oil for middle ear infections or pain, but most people do it anyway. We ASLPs (Audio and Speech-Language Pathologists) do not recommend using almonds to cure stuttering. There is no scientific research to authenticate this relationship.'

Dr. Chanchal Pal, Senior Consultant, Department of ENT and Head & Neck Surgery, Indraprastha Apollo Hospital, New Delhi, said: 'Stammering is purely a personality disorder mostly occurring in people, especially children, due to deep-seated social fears and hesitation. It may also happen due to family, school, or workplace atmosphere. The more we make them conscious of it, the more it becomes dominant. Treatment includes psychological support of family and friends, help in confidence building, and speech therapy. Almond, since ages, has been considered good for brain and memory so it may have some credibility in neural function, but it does not specifically relate to the treatment of stammering.'

title: Fact Check: Is Alopecia Areata just another name for male or female pattern baldness? - THIP Media
claim_text: Jada Pinkett Smith has Alopecia. Per google it literally means male or female pattern baldness. Hair loss. Jada started going bald.
quick_take: A social media post is claiming that "Jada Pinkett Smith has Alopecia. Per google it literally means male or female pattern baldness. Hair loss. Jada started going bald." We fact-checked and found this claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: Pattern hair loss is a progressive, nonscarring form of hair loss characterised by gradual loss of terminal hair and follicle miniaturisation to vellus hair fibres on the scalp in a characteristic distribution. In male-pattern baldness, hair loss starts at the front of the head and recedes to the back until the person goes bald. But female-pattern baldness starts at the part line, sometimes appearing all over the head. Here, the hair at the temples may also recede. Dr. Nilam Jain Kothari, Consultant Dermatologist at Masina Hospital in Mumbai explains "Androgenetic alopecia or male pattern baldness and female pattern baldness (hair loss) is the commonest form of alopecia, affecting 58% men in 30 to 50 years age group and around 6% to 38% in women across all age groups. Patients may manifest symptoms as early as puberty. This pattern of alopecia can be genetic or hormonal in aetiology." The National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases states, "Alopecia areata is a disease that happens when the immune system attacks hair follicles and causes hair loss. Hair follicles are the structures in the skin that form hair. While hair can be lost from any part of the body, alopecia areata usually affects the head and face. Hair typically falls out in small, round patches about the size of a quarter, but in some cases, hair loss is more extensive. Most people with the disease are healthy and have no other symptoms." The National Alopecia Areata Foundation further states that it is a "common autoimmune skin disease" and as many as 6.8 million people in the U.S. are affected by alopecia areata. Dr. Kothari further explains this by stating that "There are other common forms of alopecia like alopecia areata and lichen planopilaris which are autoimmune in nature, trichotillomania, which is due to compulsive habit of hair pulling, fungal or bacterial infections of the scalp and many more. Patchy form of alopecia is most commonly due to alopecia areata or localised scalp infections." No. The National Institute of Health states, "In alopecia areata, the immune system mistakenly attacks hair follicles, causing inflammation. Researchers do not fully understand what causes the immune attack on hair follicles, but they believe that both genetic and environmental (non-genetic) factors play a role." On the contrary, the hair loss due to male or female pattern baldness is not caused due to an autoimmune disorder. It can be due to hormones, ageing, and genetics. Dr. Kothari concludes by stating that, "Alopecia is a broad term coined for hair loss. It can be seen in all age groups and can be due to multiple causes. Accurate diagnosis is the key, as most patchy alopecias can recover completely if treated timely, except scarring alopecias. Male and female pattern alopecia is mostly associated with extensive hair loss. In men, it is localised to the crown area, whereas in women it is mostly seen as global hair loss affecting all the areas. Pattern alopecia is generally progressive in nature and can be controlled with treatment. Diagnosis is generally clinical and a scalp and hair analysis using a trichoscope or skin biopsy can help in complex cases. A board certified dermatologist can accurately diagnose and guide with management. Most alopecias give satisfactory responses if treated promptly."

claim_text: Aluminum is the primary cause of Alzheimer's disease
quick_take: A social media post claims that aluminum is the biggest cause of Alzheimer's disease. We fact-checked and found the claim to be False. Age, not aluminum is the biggest cause of Alzheimer's disease.
doctor_explanation: No evidence confirms that aluminum is the biggest cause of Alzheimer's disease. The National Institute on Aging website informs that age is the most important known risk factor of Alzheimer's disease. The exact cause of Alzheimer's Disease is still unknown. The current research suggests that a combination of factors including age, genetics, environmental influences, and lifestyle choices causes Alzheimer's disease. There is no established direct link between dietary intake of aluminum and Alzheimer's Disease. For instance, we do not know whether individuals who regularly consume aluminum through certain medications are at a higher risk of developing the disease. The Alzheimer's Society website informs that we need better studies to support concerns that exposure to metals through equipment use, food, or water contributes to a higher risk of developing Alzheimer's disease. In their extensive research, THIP MEDIA thoroughly investigated cooking in Aluminum foil cause Alzheimer's disease. The findings revealed a lack of clinical trials to substantiate the claim as accurate. Additionally, the findings also highlights that consuming excessive amounts of aluminum through the diet may have some association with the development of the disease. But further research is needed to fully understand this relationship. Neurologist Dr. Pawan Raj explains that 'there is some indirect evidence linking elevated levels of aluminum to the development of dementia, particularly Alzheimer's dementia. Studies conducted on rats and mice have demonstrated that aluminum tends to accumulate in specific regions of the brain, including the cortex, hippocampus, and cerebellum.' In conclusion, we need more evidence to understand whether consuming aluminum through regular diet can cause Alzheimer's disease.

title: Fact Check: Is Alzheimer's disease made by physicians? - THIP Media
claim_text: Alzheimer's disease is a physician-caused disease. The inefficiency of myelin which is a part of neurons is responsible for Alzheimer's disease. Myelin is made of cholesterol and when doctors recommend their patients to a cholesterol-restricted diet and give cholesterol-lowering drugs, this worsens the myelin functioning to induce Alzheimer's disease.

doctor_explanation: Alzheimer's disease is a form of dementia that is characterised by a gradual decline in memory and thinking. We even found no evidence of who the speaker was, his credentials, or where and to whom he was presenting the information. title: Fact Check: Is Amitabh Bachchan in ICU with critical liver damage?
claim_text: Sad News for Bachchan Family as Amitabh Bachchan admitted to ICU after 75% Liver damage, and is critical.
quick_take: A viral social media post on Facebook claims that Amitabh Bachchan is in the ICU with critical liver damage. After a thorough review, we found this claim to be false.
doctor_explanation:
The claim that Amitabh Bachchan is currently in ICU with critical liver damage is FALSE. Here is the detailed fact-check:

## Is Amitabh Bachchan currently in ICU?
No. There is no credible evidence from reliable news sources or official statements confirming that Amitabh Bachchan is currently admitted to the ICU. Recent reports from 2024, including a fact-check by India TV, debunked similar claims about his health deteriorating or being hospitalised. These claims often rely on outdated or manipulated images, like those from 2005, to mislead the public. Bachchan has been active on social media, sharing updates about his work and public appearances, with no mention of recent hospitalisation. To further verify the visuals used in the post, we conducted a reverse image search. Out of all the images, we could confirm the origin of one: the photo of Aishwarya Rai, which is from her father's funeral held on 19th March 2017, as reported by multiple news outlets and visible in archived news footage on YouTube. Similarly, there were false claims stating that Bharti Singh is hospitalised in the ICU, and that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is on a ventilator in a hospital. These are equally false.

## Does Amitabh Bachchan have 75% liver damage?
Yes, but this is not new. Amitabh Bachchan has publicly shared that he contracted Hepatitis B during a blood transfusion after a near-fatal accident on the set of his film Coolie in 1982. This led to liver cirrhosis, a condition where scar tissue replaces healthy liver tissue, reducing its function. He has stated that 75% of his liver is damaged, leaving him with 25% functionality. However, this information dates back to at least 2019, when he discussed it during a Hepatitis B awareness campaign. There is no evidence suggesting his condition has recently worsened to a "critical" state. Such misleading narratives about Amitabh Bachchan are not new. Social media platforms are often flooded with false claims, ranging from fabricated health updates to AI-generated videos showing him endorsing miracle cures for conditions like prostate issues. These are entirely fake and designed to deceive fans and boost engagement.

## Can someone survive with 25% liver function?
Yes. The liver is a remarkable organ that can function even when significantly damaged. Medical experts note that a person can survive with as little as 10-20% of liver function, as the liver can regenerate and adapt over time. Bachchan himself has highlighted the importance of regular check-ups, which have helped him manage his condition for decades. Cirrhosis, while serious, does not automatically mean a critical state or immediate need for ICU care, especially if managed properly with medical guidance.

## What are the general symptoms of severe liver damage?
Symptoms of severe liver damage, often seen in advanced stages like decompensated cirrhosis, can include jaundice (yellowing of the skin and eyes), swelling in the legs, ankles, and abdomen (ascites), easy bruising or bleeding, fatigue, nausea, loss of appetite, and confusion or memory problems (hepatic encephalopathy). It's important to remember that early liver damage may not show any noticeable symptoms, which is why regular check-ups are crucial, especially for those at risk.

## THIP Media Take
The claim that Amitabh Bachchan is currently in the ICU with critical liver damage is false. While Bachchan has a known history of liver damage due to Hepatitis B, this is not a recent development, and there is no evidence of a current ICU admission. His condition has been managed for years, and recent fact-checks confirm he is not in critical health. Fans should rely on verified news and official statements to avoid falling for misleading social media posts.

title: Fact Check: Is Amla, dried plums and tamarind water in 15 days a permanent solution for fatty liver?
claim_text: Consuming a mixture of Indian gooseberry (amla), dried plums (aloo bhukhara), and tamarind water can provide a permanent solution for fatty liver in just 15 days, with results visible after soaking 4 pieces of each in water and drinking it on an empty stomach after straining.
verdict_original: The claim that Indian gooseberry, dried plums and tamarind water in 15 days is permanent solution for fatty liver made by an Instagram user is FALSE. Thus, the claim is FALSE.
doctor_explanation:
Dr. Rajiv Kovil, Head of Diabetology, Zandra Healthcare and Co-founder of Rang De Neela initiative, explained: 'Fatty liver disease happens when fat tends to build up in the liver, which can damage it over time. The two main types of fatty liver disease are nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and alcoholic fatty liver disease which will require timely intervention. Today NAFLD has a new name and is called as MASLD (Metabolic Dysfunction Associated Steatotic Liver Disease). The causes behind fatty liver disease are obesity, type 2 diabetes, high cholesterol, a diet loaded with fats, and alcohol, and eating carbohydrates in large quantities. Fatty liver occurs because of wrong deposition of fat in the liver and sometimes it's the harbinger for Type 2 Diabetes and Cardiovascular disease. Fatty liver is a common occurrence in the age group 25-45 now. Hence, it is better to initiate prompt treatment after the symptoms are seen. Delaying treatment can worsen one's condition.'

Dr Uday Sanglodkar, Senior Consultant Hepatologist and Clinical lead liver and transplant ICU, Gleneagles Hospital Parel Mumbai, highlighted: 'There are several stages: Simple fatty liver (steatosis) — during this stage, there is a build-up of fat in the liver cells that will be detected during tests; Non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) — it is a form of fatty liver disease wherein liver inflammation is seen in patients; Fibrosis — the constant inflammation causes scar tissue to form around the liver and nearby blood vessels, however, the liver can function in a normal way.'

Dr Uday Sanglodkar responded to the claim: 'Indian gooseberry is known to be loaded with antioxidants and vitamin C that protect the liver from damage and oxidative stress, it is believed to help the liver filter toxins and it is anti-inflammatory and helps control inflammation and prevent conditions like fatty liver disease and claims to cure jaundice. Moreover, dried plums and tamarind water are claimed to cure fatty liver disease and liver fibrosis. Don't believe any magical drink such as gooseberry, dried plums, and tamarind water is promoted on social media. This is not at all a permanent solution for fatty liver. Fatty liver treatment will require a multidisciplinary approach including a well-balanced diet, exercise, stress-free techniques, and weight management. Don't rely on any home remedies and follow the advice given by the doctor only. These ingredients if taken regularly and in large quantities can do more harm than good.'

Dr. Rajiv Kovil further added: 'Indian gooseberry, dried plums and tamarind water none of them are to be used for NAFLD. Resmetirom, is a thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonist for the treatment of adults with noncirrhotic non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) with moderate to advanced liver scarring (fibrosis), to be used along with diet and exercise. It is the only approved treatment for NAFLD. Pioglitazone which is an insulin sensitiser and GLP1 Analogues are the other drugs used in NAFLD.'

No scientific evidence supports the claim that Indian gooseberry, dried plums and tamarind water in 15 days is a permanent solution for fatty liver. Fatty liver can be reversed but it cannot be cured. A paper published in Advances in Nutrition outlines five key dietary recommendations for preventing and managing fatty liver disease: adopting traditional diets like the Mediterranean diet; reducing excess fructose intake and avoiding processed foods and drinks with added fructose; replacing saturated fats (SFAs) with polyunsaturated fats (PUFAs), especially long-chain omega-3s, and monounsaturated fats (MUFAs); swapping processed and fast foods, commercial bakery items, and sweets for high-fiber, unprocessed foods such as whole grains, vegetables, fruits, legumes, nuts, and seeds; and limiting alcohol consumption. Tiziana Fernández and colleagues concluded that lifestyle modifications are effective in treating NAFLD, with the combination of diet and exercise proving more beneficial than either intervention alone in improving liver enzyme levels and HOMA-IR (a marker of insulin resistance).

title: Is amla the secret to glowing skin and a stronger immune system?
claim_text: Amla (Indian gooseberry) is good for skin and helps increase immunity
quick_take: A social media post suggests that amla (Indian gooseberry, Emblica officinalis) can magically enhance skin health and dramatically boost immunity. We fact checked and found the claim to be Half True.
doctor_explanation: Amla can improve skin health to a limited extent but cannot magically boost immunity. SKIN HEALTH: Amla has been used in traditional Indian medicine (Ayurveda) for promoting youthfulness and radiant skin. Scientific evidence shows limited but promising results due to antioxidant and collagen-protective effects. Dr. Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant in Lucknow said: "Amla is a wonderful natural ingredient that supports healthy, youthful skin. Its rich antioxidant content helps protect collagen and improve skin texture over time. While it's not a miracle cure, regular use alongside good skincare and sun protection can noticeably enhance skin health and radiance." A laboratory study published in the Journal of Ethnopharmacology (2008) found that amla extract stimulated procollagen production in human skin fibroblasts while inhibiting MMP-1 (an enzyme that breaks down collagen), suggesting it may help slow collagen degradation. A human trial published in Clinical, Cosmetic and Investigational Dermatology (2019) tested amla and lingonberry extracts in 99 healthy women over 12 weeks, showing measurable improvements in skin elasticity, hydration, and wrinkle depth - but effects were subtle, not dramatic, and came from a combination formula. A small study in Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology (2021) tested 0.1% amla branch extract gel on 20 volunteers for 84 days, showing increased skin elasticity, smoother texture, and reduction in fine lines. IMMUNE SYSTEM: The phrase "boosting immunity" is scientifically vague - the immune system is a complex network that cannot be simply "boosted" by one food. Dr. Sai Praveen Haranath, Intensivist and Pulmonologist at Apollo Hospitals, Hyderabad, explains that the immune system is a complex, multi-layered defence network of specialized cells and proteins like antibodies that protect from harmful pathogens, depending on essential nutrients like vitamins and zinc. He cautions that no single medicine or supplement can truly "boost" immunity as there is no solid scientific evidence. Amla contains natural vitamin C which plays a role in maintaining skin barrier, enhancing wound healing, and supporting immune response by stimulating white blood cells. Clinical Nutritionist Nidhi Sarin emphasizes that true immunity develops gradually through consistent healthy practices - balanced diet, physical activity, good lifestyle habits, and adequate sleep. Beyond vitamin C, amla contains polyphenols, tannins, and flavonoids with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects that may modulate immune activity. A mouse study in Toxicology and Industrial Health (2013) found amla extract protected thymocytes from arsenic-induced oxidative damage. A human trial in Japan gave 15 healthy adults 500 mg amla extract daily for 18 weeks, showing reduced oxidative stress markers and improved blood fluidity, but no direct immune parameters were measured. A systematic review in Nutrients (2023) evaluated 19 clinical studies finding improvements in cholesterol, blood sugar, and inflammation markers like CRP, but no consistent evidence for enhanced immunity in terms of infection resistance or immune-cell counts. SAFETY: Generally safe but high-dose supplements may cause digestive discomfort, acid reflux, or interactions with blood thinners and diabetes drugs. Amla can slightly lower blood sugar and cholesterol, so people on related medications should consult their doctor.

title: Fact Check: Is an at-home formulation an effective remedy for a toothache?
claim_text: A toothache could be managed by applying turmeric and asafoetida to the affected area.
quick_take: An Instagram post asserts that an at-home formulation can effectively manage a toothache. We fact-checked and found that it's mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Toothache, also referred to as odontogenic discomfort, is the body's signal that the teeth require professional intervention. The unpleasant sensation originates from the teeth or adjacent supporting structures, such as the periodontal ligament and alveolar bone. A toothache results from an irritated dental pulp brought on by deep cavities, fractured teeth, and dental infections. Based on its origin, dental pain varies in terms of severity. Even if the discomfort might not be permanent, it is crucial to get the underlying cause assessed. Furthermore, transient alleviation should not be mistaken for dental sensitivity. Dental sensitivity is a momentary, intense pain that arises as gums recede or enamel wears off, exposing the dentine underneath. The primary contributors include cold water, hot tea, and even sugary foods. The discomfort, however, subsides when the stimulus is removed. It is critical to acknowledge that a toothache that doesn't go away on its own typically throbs, lasts, or gets worse over time, which is usually a sign of an infection. The aforementioned combination is being promoted on social media for managing toothache; it lacks sufficient scientific evidence. Given that a toothache is associated with a specific condition, it is critical to understand the benefits and drawbacks of the ingredients in the recipe. Turmeric has well-established antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and analgesic properties. This may be due to curcumin, which is its active component. Furthermore, curcumin has been linked to the inhibition of oral pathogens such as Streptococcus mutans, which are principally responsible for the development of tooth cavities and the associated pain. Asafoetida, also called hing, has antibacterial and antifungal effects. It is therefore advised as a topical therapy for mild oral discomforts. Even while both of these components provide short-term relief by lowering the microbial load and inflammation, they cannot be considered as a permanent solution for toothache. This is due to the fact that tooth-related pain is often linked to an underlying ailment, such as advanced gum disease, pulpitis, or deep cavities, which calls for evidence-based therapy. Clinical dentistry emphasises that while natural therapies can be used as supplements, they cannot replace conventional dental interventions. A tooth-related pain should be assessed and managed by a qualified dental practitioner. People usually opt for herbal or alternative remedies rather than prescription analgesics because of their perceived organic nature, accessibility, and safety profile. However, as previously stated, they only temporarily relieve tooth-related discomfort; they are not a permanent solution. Some of these natural therapies are clove oil, salt water rinses, and herbal pastes. The actual risk of depending on such unverified solutions is the presumption that the transient comfort equates cure. Most importantly, delaying the necessary intervention might conceal the symptoms and permit the underlying infection to progress silently. This may lead to a more intrusive and expensive dental treatment. Dr. Pooja Sharma, BDS, MDS, of NIMS University in Jaipur, warns that adopting at-home remedies for tooth discomfort might often lead people to believe they don't need professional care. title: Fact Check: Is antineoplaston therapy an effective cancer cure?
claim_text: Antineoplaston therapy developed by Dr. Stanislaw Burzynski is an effective cure for cancer
quick_take: Various social media posts claim that antineoplaston therapy developed by Dr. Stanislaw Burzynski is an effective cure for cancer. We fact-checked and found this claim to be Half true.
doctor_explanation: Antineoplastons are chemical compounds found normally in blood and urine. They are made up of amino acids and peptides. Amino acids are the building blocks of protein. Two or more amino acids form a peptide. In 1976, an experimental cancer therapy was found by Dr. Burzynski that is purported to provide a natural biochemical substance (antineoplastons) that is excreted and, therefore, lacking in people with cancer. He believed that by providing cancer patients with supplemental doses of these compounds, he could help to 'reprogram' cancer cells so that they stop dividing and eventually die off and prevent abnormal cell growth. Initially, these antineoplastons were isolated from human urine but are now synthesized from readily available chemicals in the developer's laboratory. Dr. Moujhuri Nandi, Consultant Radiation Oncologist at Karkinos Healthcare Pvt. Ltd. opines her view by stating, 'Antineoplastons refer to a group of drugs that contain naturally occurring chemical compounds found in human blood and urine. These drugs consist of a combination of amino acid derivatives, peptides, and amino acids. However, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has not approved them for the prevention or treatment of any disease. To date, no randomized controlled trials have been published in the scientific literature to demonstrate the effectiveness of antineoplastons as a form of anti-cancer therapy. Furthermore, the potential adverse effects of antineoplaston therapy range from mild and short-lasting symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, fever, chills, abdominal gaseous distention, and maculopapular rash to severe neurologic toxicity that may require discontinuation of therapy for some patients.' There is currently no evidence to support the effectiveness of antineoplaston therapy in treating cancer. Antineoplaston therapy is an investigative cancer treatment. No randomized controlled trials showing the effectiveness of antineoplastons have been published in the peer-reviewed scientific literature. Decades after development, it still lacks FDA approval for general use. A document by the FDA also cites various cases in which the patients undergoing this treatment experienced adverse symptoms. Additionally, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center also states that there is no conclusive evidence to support the antineoplaston theory. There are various side effects associated with its use. The adverse effects range from mild ones, such as nausea, vomiting, fever, dizziness, high blood pressure, dry skin, etc., to severe ones, like sleepiness, confusion, seizures, and swelling near the brain. Furthermore, no phase III, randomized, controlled trials of antineoplastons as a treatment for cancer have been conducted.

Although baking soda is naturally alkaline, it is possible that it helps relieve the burning sensation brought on by canker sores that have already appeared. However, baking soda is not a cure-all for the lesions themselves and may even be harmful. This might be explained by the lesions' multifactorial etiology. Home remedies are, therefore, not advised for these conditions. Additionally, there are not sufficient credible studies discussing baking soda mouthwash's effectiveness in treating aphthous ulcers. However, avoiding triggers that lead to ulcers is best, particularly if the patient in question has noticed a connection. Besides, one with canker sores should stay away from hard, acidic, and spicy foods and drinks like fruit juices, tomatoes, citrus fruits, pepper, paprika, and curry, as well as alcoholic and carbonated beverages. Dr. Pooja Bhardwaj, BDS advised against using baking soda because doing so might be harmful, even though it lowers oral acidity and bacterial activity and may speed healing. Additionally, different people may develop this condition for a variety of reasons, such as stress, hormonal issues, genetics, eating foods high in acid, etc. Therefore, it might not work in every situation. She further recommended that cases of canker sores that recur frequently should be treated with a combination of prescribed corticosteroids and a mild antiseptic like hydrogen peroxide or benzocaine. With the proper topical therapy, patients who occasionally experience minor ulcer episodes significantly feel better. Preventive measures include drinking lots of water, keeping your mouth clean, using warm saline rinses, and avoiding foods that are hot, spicy, or acidic. doctor_explanation: Kidney stones—medically referred to as renal calculi—occur when components such as calcium, oxalate, and uric acid precipitate and aggregate as hard pebbles in the renal urinary or Bowman's space. While renal aggregates are highly prevalent, certain variables may enhance an individual's risk. Since kidney stones often serve as symptoms of underlying medical conditions, examining urine chemistry and kidney stone composition may provide a window into determining it. Once the evaluation is completed, the condition is addressed accordingly. Traditional Ayurvedic literature asserts that banana stem, or Vazhaithandu, has several health benefits. Furthermore, the mild diuretic activity may indirectly enhance renal function by enhancing toxin elimination and maintaining fluid homeostasis. Additionally, Ayurveda views it as a body cooling diet that could aid in cleansing by balancing excess pitta. Researchers are also looking into the possibility of using banana stems to help control weight and reduce cholesterol levels. Even while it is still a functional food, its use for kidney stones is still supportive rather than remedial. The aforementioned preparation of banana stem juice is being advertised as a treatment for renal calculi; nevertheless, it is not an effective solution for their dissolution because: While these components may help with digestion, hydration, and overall urinary tract health, they cannot replace conventional kidney stone treatment. Dr. Sharad Malhotra, HOD Gastroenterology, Hepatology & Therapeutic Endoscopy, Aakash Healthcare, New Delhi, warns against utilizing them as a long-term treatment for kidney stones. Additionally, he stressed that there is no compelling evidence that these remedies may remove or cure kidney calculi. It is never advisable to substitute these unsubstantiated alternatives for proper medical care. Dr. Archana Daftardar adds that there are a lot of fallacies regarding renal stone management and prevention. Unverified natural remedies might not help the condition; they might make it worse. Consulting with qualified allopathic or Ayurvedic physicians is the recommended course of action. It is critical to acknowledge that the banana stem juice preparation could enhance metabolic health and urinary function rather than acting as a definitive cure for existing renal stones. Individuals who have renal calculi should seek evidence-based medical therapy; online options should only be utilized as adjuncts. Even though these foods have significant health benefits, it is not advised to consume them in large amounts for an extended period of time without medical supervision. Usually, renal stones are treated based on their structural characteristics, anatomical location, and chemical makeup. Even though asymptomatic stones are prevalent, symptomatic calculi can be handled by a multifaceted approach that seeks to address both the short-term discomfort and the prospective risk of kidney stones.

Beer contains small amounts of B vitamins and minerals but far less bioavailable, and alcohol has detrimental effects that neutralize any small benefits. 4) Milk causing diseases: No strong evidence suggests milk directly causes obesity or cancer. Research suggests dairy consumption might help reduce bowel cancer risk. Dr. Amit Harshana cautions: 'I strongly advise my patients against starting to drink alcohol in the belief that it has health benefits. The myths surrounding alcohol's positive effects are often exaggerated and lack strong evidence to justify drinking, especially given the risks of abuse and addiction. The negative impacts of alcohol far outweigh the minor benefits suggested by some studies.' Aditi Prabhu adds: 'While there is no definitive evidence linking milk directly to diseases such as obesity, diabetes, and cancer, most research suggests that milk may not be the sole cause. In relation to the studies mentioned in the PETA video, one study specifically targets the Swedish population, which means its findings may not be universally applicable to people from other backgrounds. Additionally, this study does not account for overall dietary habits or lifestyle factors, and it has several other limitations.'

title: Fact Check: Does being a Gay or Lesbian refer to neurological disorder? - THIP Media
claim_text: Gay is neurological disorder that needs to be curb and not find an excuse for. What is bad is bad!; I identify LGBT as abnormality in brain
quick_take: Some online voices are asserting that being LGBTQIA+ is a neurological disorder. We fact-checked and found this claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: There is no scientific evidence to support the claim that being LGBTQIA+ is a neurological disorder. Sexual orientation, gender identity, and diverse expressions of gender are natural and expected variations of human sexuality and identity. They are not considered illnesses, disorders, or abnormalities. A study investigated the structural differences in the brains of homosexual and heterosexual people. They found that homosexual men had significantly larger volumes of the right amygdala and hippocampus. While homosexual women had significantly larger volumes of the left amygdala and hippocampus. However, more research is needed to confirm these findings and to understand the mechanisms by which these differences in brain structure may influence sexual orientation. Despite this, the study does not indicate a neurological defect, rather structural changes. Numerous scientific studies have supported the understanding that sexual orientation and gender identity have biological, psychological, and social underpinnings. Many factors contribute to a person's sexual orientation and gender identity, including genetics, environment, and personal experiences. However, there is no single factor that can definitively explain why someone is LGBTQIA+. Being LGBTQIA+ is not a choice. People do not choose to be LGBTQIA+, just as they do not choose their eye or hair color. LGBTQIA+ people are simply born this way. Research suggests these aspects of identity have complex origins involving a combination of genetic, hormonal, and environmental factors. Historically, there have been misconceptions and stigmatization of LGBTQIA+ individuals, including attempts to pathologize their identities. However, these perspectives have been widely discredited. Currently, scientific and medical communities have made significant progress in recognizing the natural and diverse spectrum of human sexual and gender identities. The World Health Organization declassified being transgender as a mental disorder and now recognizes the importance of affirming gender diversity and providing appropriate healthcare support. The American Psychiatric Association (APA) has removed homosexuality from its list of mental disorders since 1973. Dr Abhishek Juneja, Consultant Neurologist in Delhi informs, 'LGBTQIA+ is a part of the spectrum of sexual inclination and desires. This generally has no bearing on the manifestations and treatment of neurological disorders among patients. It's not a disease but a normal variation from established socio-cultural standards in our society. I, as a practicing clinician, do not give much importance to the gender/sexual inclination of the patient while providing the treatment.' Many studies have shown that people from LGBTQIA+ community are just as mentally healthy as heterosexual and cisgender people. But, they experience significant emotional distress and mental health challenges due to stigmatization, victimization, discrimination and barriers to accessing mental healthcare services which negatively impact their mental health. Psychologist Dr Binda Singh emphasized that being part of the LGBTQIA+ community is not a psychological disorder. It is considered normal and natural by reputable psychiatric associations and the World Health Organization. However, counselling can be beneficial for individuals within the community who may be facing behavioural issues, experiencing gender dysphoria, or struggling with their sexual identity. It can provide support and guidance to navigate these challenges and address the psychological impact of societal stigmatization and myths that often affect the mental health of LGBTQIA+ people.

title: Fact Check: Is being transgender a mental disorder in kids?
claim_text: Transgenderism, especially in kids, is a mental health disorder
quick_take: In a widely circulated social media video, entrepreneur Vivek Ramaswamy made a clear statement during his appearance at the second Republican presidential primary debate, asserting that transgenderism, especially in kids, is a mental health disorder. We fact-checked and found the claim made to be False.
doctor_explanation:
Transgenderism refers to the experience of individuals whose gender identity doesn't align with the sex they were assigned at birth. It involves a person's deep-seated sense of being male, female, a blend of both, or neither, which may not match their physical characteristics. Transgender individuals may pursue various steps, such as hormone therapy or gender-affirming surgeries, to align their bodies with their gender identity. It's important to respect and support transgender people, using their preferred pronouns and acknowledging their gender identity.

Gender dysphoria is a term used in psychology and healthcare to describe the distress or discomfort that some individuals may experience when their gender identity doesn't align with the sex they were assigned at birth. This disconnect between their internal sense of self and their physical characteristics can cause emotional and psychological distress. Children and adolescents who experience gender dysphoria may feel distressed or anxious about their gender identity. They may also have difficulty accepting their assigned sex or expressing their gender identity in a way that feels authentic to them.

It is important to note that gender dysphoria is not the same as being transgender. Not all transgender people experience gender dysphoria, and not all people who experience gender dysphoria are transgender. There is no consensus on the causes of gender dysphoria. Some experts believe that it is caused by a combination of genetic and environmental factors. Others believe that it is caused by a neurological difference in the brain.

No. Being transgender is not a mental disorder in kids. In the past, the term 'disorder' was historically associated with the experience of being transgender. However, experts have evolved their understanding and are actively working to remove stigma while ensuring access to gender-affirming healthcare.

In 2019, the World Health Organization (WHO) updated its International Classification of Diseases, renaming the diagnosis from transsexualism to gender incongruence and relocating it from the mental health disorders section to a new section called conditions related to sexual health.

According to the American Psychiatric Association (APA). In 2013, the APA removed gender identity disorder from the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5), the standard reference book for the classification of mental disorders. The DSM-5 now classifies gender dysphoria as a condition that can occur in children and adolescents. When this manual was revised, the term 'gender identity disorder' was changed to 'gender dysphoria' to emphasize that being transgender is not an illness. Just like being transgender, being part of the LGBTQIA+ community as a whole is not connected to mental disorders. This also means that being gay or lesbian is not a neurological disorder.

title: Fact Check: Is Bhut Jolokia the hottest chilli in the world? - THIP Media
claim_text: Bhut Jolokia (Ghost Pepper) is the world's hottest chili pepper that is cultivated in northeast India
quick_take: A lot of people believe that Bhut Jolokia (Ghost Pepper), a chilli that grows in North East India, is the hottest and spiciest chilli in the world. We fact-checked and found that Bhut Jolokia was the hottest chilli at one point of now, but no more. We rate this claim as MostlyFalse.
doctor_explanation: The hotness in chilli is measured by a unit called Scoville ratings. The scale is used to measure the amount of capsaicin in a particular chilli. Capsaicin is the chemical compound that gives the chillies their hotness and creates that burning sensation on our tongues. The Scoville rating is given by human taste testers (people who eat the chilli and rate its hotness) and hence is believed to be very subjective. A modern method called high-performance liquid chromatography can detect capsaicin content even more exactly, but still, the Scoville rating is the most accepted measurement of hotness in chillies chefs, foodies and experts. Bhut Jolokia (also known as Ghost Pepper) is NOT the hottest chilli anymore in the world currently in 2021. Bhut Jolokia, found in the northeastern state of Assam in India, entered the Guinness Book of World Records in 2007 as the hottest chilli in the world. But it was dethroned of its position in 2011 first by the Infinity, then by the Naga Viper Pepper and then by the Trinidad Scorpion Butch T Pepper. As per the Guinness Book of Records list, Carolina Reaper is the hottest chilli in the world since 2013. Two other chillies that were measured to have a higher Scoville score than Carolina Reaper – the Dragon's Breath in 2017 and the Pepper X in 2019 – are still not verified and entered into the Guinness Book. Bhut Jolokia has a Scoville rating of 1,041,427. To put it in comparison, a regular Green chilli (Thai Chilli) in the market will be around 10,000 in Scoville rating. Taking Dragon's Breath and Pepper X into account (both are still not in Guinness Book of World Records as of date), Bhut Jolokia is probably the sixth hottest chilli in the world. Professor Paul Bosland, Director of the Chile Pepper Institute, who was responsible for finding the Bhut Jolokia mentioned in media interviews that theoretically it is possible to die from eating chillies but our bodies will revolt before we reach that point. A research done in 1980 shows that it will take a person weighing 150 pounds (approx. 68KG) to eat 3 pounds (1.3KG) of Bhut Jolokia at one sitting to die from capsaicin toxicity. The same amount of chillies eaten over a period of time will not lead to any major health problems.

title: Is the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation not in India anymore?

Further stating that this resulted in the expulsion of the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation from India. We researched and found that this information is misleading. The Gates Foundation continues its operations in India. Also, there is no published evidence to support the claim that thousands of girls participating in an HPV vaccination project suffered injuries or disabilities. A committee established by the Indian Government investigated the deaths of seven girls who had received HPV vaccines and concluded that these deaths were most probably unrelated to the vaccine. Nevertheless, the committee identified issues with the reporting of adverse events following immunization. Vaccines utilized in the project had received approval for use in India, and the US Food and Drug Administration confirmed the safety of these vaccines through extensive studies involving tens of thousands of women. Regarding the claim that the Gates Foundation was kicked out of India, this may be a distortion of news from 2017 when the Indian government announced partial funding for an immunization program in New Delhi, previously supported by the Gates Foundation. However, the Indian government denied expelling the foundation. The Gates Foundation maintains an office in India and collaborates with various stakeholders, including government entities, community groups, non-profits, academic institutions, the private sector, and development organizations in the country. The Gates Foundation has refuted claims that the Indian Government issued any directive to halt or cease its work in India. The origin of these claims can be traced back to a project in which around 24,000 girls in India aged 10 to 14, including those from tribal communities, received the HPV vaccine. This project was conducted by the non-profit organization Programme for Appropriate Technology in Health (PATH) in collaboration with the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and state governments in Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat from 2007. It was suspended in March 2010 following public outcry and news reports of some girls who received the vaccine having died. The project received funding from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. The committee established by the Indian Government in 2011 determined that the reported deaths among vaccinated girls were most probably unrelated to the vaccine, although the exact causes of these deaths could not be conclusively established. The deaths were attributed to causes such as ingesting poisonous substances, snake bites, malaria, drowning, probable brain hemorrhage, and viral fever, which the report stated were unlikely to be linked to the vaccines. The report did mention three serious adverse reactions following vaccination but also highlighted significant underreporting of non-serious adverse events, casting doubt on the accuracy of reporting serious adverse events. It further emphasized the inadequacy of monitoring adverse events in the program. Disseminating misinformation about vaccines can have a direct, detrimental impact on individuals' physical and psychological health, as well as on specific communities. Such misinformation can also erode trust in healthcare professionals, divert attention from established medical consensus, and undermine public health messaging.

title: Fact Check: Is Bill Gates integrating HIV into Mpox vaccines?
claim_text: Bill Gates is planning to cause a monkeypox pandemic by releasing a lab-created version of the bioweapon and then releasing a vaccine for the virus that is even deadlier than the disease. The vaccines being developed contain HIV antigens which could lead to full-blown AIDS. The video also claims that chemtrails are seeding the virus in major cities.
quick_take: A post on X claims that Bill Gates is integrating HIV antigens into Mpox vaccines. We did a fact check to term this as False.
doctor_explanation: Mpox, previously known as monkeypox, is a viral disease caused by the monkeypox virus. This pathogen is a member of the orthopoxvirus genus. It shares similarities with smallpox but is generally less severe. Symptoms include fever, headache, muscle aches, and a distinctive rash that often progresses to blisters. Vaccines like the Modified Vaccinia Ankara (MVA), initially developed for smallpox, are effective against Mpox. Regarding the claim that Bill Gates is planning to cause a monkeypox pandemic using a lab-created virus as a bioweapon: There is no evidence to support this claim. The notion is a conspiracy theory without any scientific backing. The monkeypox outbreaks in the past have been naturally occurring, traced to zoonotic transmission, not to any intentional release of a bioweapon. Bill Gates and his foundation focus on global health initiatives, which include the prevention of pandemics, not causing them. Regarding chemtrails: The idea that Mpox is being spread via chemtrails is a conspiracy theory. Chemtrails are a myth. The trails seen behind aircraft are contrails, made up of water vapour and harmless. There is no scientific basis for the claim that viruses are being disseminated through these trails. Mpox mainly spreads through close contact with an infected person or animal or by touching an infected object. It does not spread through the air in the form of chemtrails. Regarding HIV antigens in Mpox vaccines: HIV antigens are specific to the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and are not used in vaccines for other diseases, such as Mpox. Vaccine development follows stringent regulatory guidelines to ensure safety and efficacy. Any claims to the contrary lack scientific evidence. People with HIV-associated immunosuppression may face higher risks with Mpox. The JYNNEOS vaccine does not contain any HIV antigens - it is clear from the ingredients list that Mpox vaccines are devoid of HIV antigens. Regarding the multi-phase plan: The concept of a multi-phase plan involving the intentional seeding of a virus followed by the release of dangerous vaccines is a common narrative in conspiracy theories. Public health agencies globally, including the World Health Organization (WHO), monitor and regulate the development and distribution of vaccines. They make sure that the vaccines are safe and effective. Claims of a coordinated effort to cause harm through vaccines are not true. Mpox spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids, sores, or respiratory droplets of an infected person or animal, or through contact with contaminated materials. It does not spread easily through casual contact or air over long distances. HIV spreads through certain body fluids including blood, semen, vaginal fluids, rectal fluids, and breast milk through unprotected sexual contact, sharing needles, or from mother to child during childbirth or breastfeeding. HIV does not transmit through air, water, or casual contact. Mpox vaccines such as the Modified Vaccinia Ankara (MVA) vaccine are safe and effective, developed following rigorous testing to protect against orthopoxviruses including Mpox.

title: Fact Check: Is Black Salve a viable cancer treatment option?

doctor_explanation: The claim is not credible. Black Salve has a history of being used as a substitute for conventional cancer treatment, dating back to the middle of the 1800s when American surgeon Jesse Weldon Fell proposed using herbs to treat skin cancer.
