title: Fact Check: Should fluoride not be used as it is toxic? - THIP Media
claim_text: Only 8 countries in the world use fluoride, and it shouldn't be used as it is ineffective and toxic.
quick_take: A social media post claims that one should not use fluoride as it is ineffective and toxic. We fact-checked and found this claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: Fluoride is a naturally occurring mineral. It is added to drinking water as a public health measure. Fluoride in drinking water helps to prevent tooth decay. It has been shown to improve oral health by reducing the number of cavities and tooth decay, especially in children. Using fluoride is a cost-effective way to prevent tooth decay, especially in communities where access to dental care is limited. Even though fluoride in drinking water provides these benefits, excessive exposure to fluoride can lead to fluorosis. Fluorosis is a condition that causes discoloration and mottling of the teeth. Dr. Kashyap Dakshini, General Physician, further clarifies by stating, "Drinking fluoridated water reduces the incidence of dental cavities and keeps the teeth strong. The WHO has stipulated the upper limit of fluoride in drinking water. However, excess of fluoride in drinking water is bad. It can cause dental & skeletal fluorosis, arthritis, osteoporosis, muscle damage, and fatigue. Higher than upper limits consumption could also cause toxicity and damage the heart, arteries, kidney, liver, endocrine glands, neuron system, and several other delicate parts of a living organism." The safety and effectiveness of fluoride have been extensively studied for many years. Fluoride is safe and effective in preventing tooth decay when used in the recommended amounts. The American Dental Association, the World Health Organization, and many other reputable health organizations endorse the use of fluoride as a safe and effective way to prevent tooth decay. While it is true that excessive amounts of fluoride can be toxic, the amount of fluoride used in dental products is carefully regulated to ensure safety. Excessive long-term exposure to fluoride can have adverse effects, which include osteoporosis, dental fluorosis and damage to bones, kidney, reproductive organs, nerve and muscles. However, fluoride in low concentration maintains and solidifies bones and prevents dental caries. Therefore, countries have set parameters to limit the levels of fluoride in water. The IndiaWaterPortal.org website informs the limit is 1.5 mg/L. Also, even without fluoridation, the natural levels of fluoride in water in some places can be higher than 4 mg/L. Government regulates fluoride in drinking water to ensure safe levels. Therefore, there is no evidence to suggest that fluoride is ineffective or toxic when used in the recommended amounts. In fact, not using fluoride as part of a comprehensive oral hygiene routine can increase the risk of tooth decay and other dental problems. If you have concerns about fluoride use, it is best to consult with your dentist or healthcare provider for personalized advice and dosage recommendations.

title: Fact Check: Should one depend on ACV for kidney stones?
claim_text: According to an Instagram post by drsaleem4u, five drinks would naturally address kidney stones. As per the claim, consumption of diluted ACV twice daily breaks down kidney stones for their easy passage.
quick_take: A social media post claims that kidney stones can be instantly resolved by consuming apple cider vinegar. We verified the claim and found it Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: Kidney stones—medically referred to as nephrolithiasis or urolithiasis—occur when substances such as calcium, oxalate, and uric acid precipitate and aggregate as crystals in the renal urinary space. The incidence of nephrolithiasis has been increasing, and the following factors may predispose individuals to the formation of kidney stones. Given that kidney stones often serve as indicators of underlying medical conditions, analysis of urine chemistry and stone composition may provide a window into determining the root cause. Therefore, an interdisciplinary team of urologists, nephrologists, and interventional radiologists should address the issue along with input from endocrine surgeons, endocrinologists, and dietitians. While natural remedies such as apple cider vinegar (ACV) are receiving a lot of attention for their potential to treat kidney stones, they cannot replace the conventional kidney stone treatment. However, ACV may support kidney stone management by reducing stone development. The high acetic acid content of the fermented ACV is believed to aid in the dissolution and softening of renal calculi. The acidic component is also thought to have the capacity to reduce the size of the stones by facilitating their passage through the urinary system via a chemical interaction. This has been further substantiated by a pilot clinical trial that showed that regular consumption of ACV may considerably lower the recurrence of renal stones by lowering urine calcium levels and increasing urinary citrate. It is important to note that these findings are based on preliminary or small-scale research and should not be interpreted as a cure-all for kidney stones. There are no reliable, comprehensive clinical studies that demonstrate that ACV eliminates kidney stones in all patients. Above all, excessive use of vinegar is discouraged because of the associated adverse outcomes. Before depending entirely on such measures, patients should speak with their healthcare providers, especially if their symptoms intensify or continue. Dr Sharad Malhotra, HOD Gastroenterology, Hepatology & Therapeutic Endoscopy, Aakash Healthcare, New Delhi, advises against using home remedies as long-term therapy for kidney stones, even though they may be beneficial for digestive or urinary health. He also emphasised that there is no definitive evidence that such ingredients can cure or dissolve kidney stones. Appropriate medical care should never be substituted with these unverified remedies. Dr Ganesh Srinivasa Prasad P, consultant nephrologist at Narayana Health City in Bengaluru, supports this further by stating that kidney stones are common in tropical nations because of dehydration, and the stone composition usually determines their management. While kidney stones cannot be managed by home remedies, the risk can be decreased by drinking sufficient water, limiting salt intake, consuming foods high in calcium, and avoiding foods high in oxalate. The risk of uric acid stones can be reduced by limiting meat, sugar, alcohol, smoking, and carbohydrates. Delaying treatment for kidney stones, especially those that require surgery, may result in significant and sometimes fatal complications. An untreated stone obstructing the urinary tract can cause kidney damage, urinary tract infections, and persistent discomfort. Infection can be a critical risk associated with untreated blocking stones. When blockage coexists with a urinary tract infection (UTI), the infection can quickly progress to sepsis, a potentially lethal systemic illness. Furthermore, long-term blockage can also result in hydronephrosis, a disorder in which the kidney expands as a result of urine accumulation. If this pressure fails to be addressed promptly, it might eventually impede renal function and result in irreparable kidney damage or even kidney failure.

title: Should one rely on a natural recipe for all dental issues?

Dr. Annusuiya Gohil, MD Scholar at the All India Institute of Ayurveda and an expert in Ayurveda, explains that the assurances stated in extensively shared social media posts are usually deceptive. Moreover, the traditional medicine provides extensive postgraduate training in dental, ear, nose, throat, and eye care. These therapies, however, cannot be applied in a vague or general way. Dr. Gohil further clarifies that one herbal combination is not sufficient to heal all dental issues, particularly severe ones like pyorrhoea. If someone claims that a certain medication can be found in Ayurvedic manuscripts, they have to provide the specific source. This may enable qualified Ayurvedic physicians to appropriately evaluate it and tailor treatment to each patient's needs. Dependence on unverified organic options may not only delay the required treatment but may also delay the existing issue.

While the combination of mustard oil, salt, lemon juice, and turmeric is being touted as a powerful remedy, its role is confined to being used as an adjunct at best. Despite these benefits, there is insufficient scientific evidence that the four components are effective in addressing significant dental diseases, including bone loss, deep cavities, periodontal disease, or abscesses. Conversely, using the natural formula excessively or incorrectly could erode dental enamel, which could make sensitivity worse.

Dr. Snigdha, BDS, MDS, of Vananchal Dental College and Hospital in Jharkhand, maintains that major dental problems, such as cavities or gum infections, cannot be resolved by a homemade natural remedy for dental problems like the one described. Cavities may result in tooth damage that cannot be repaired and require professional procedures such as fillings. Gingival pus often signals a serious infection, such as periodontitis, that needs to be handled by a specialist. Although herbal remedies may offer short-term relief, they are unable to address underlying issues or prevent further damage. Even though the herbal composition may help some people with their symptoms, it should not be utilised as the main therapeutic approach.

Dr. Pooja Sharma, BDS, MDS, of NIMS University in Jaipur, explains that since gum infections and cavities cannot be cured on their own, they need to be evaluated and managed professionally. She contends that depending on online quick solutions for more severe oral health issues might delay the required intervention, thereby escalating minor problems into more serious ones, such as excruciating pain, swelling, or tooth loss. Seeking early intervention is recommended to stop the symptoms from getting worse.

The article also states that prevalent dental concerns like cavities, gum disease, tooth mobility, and recurring oral infections are more common in high-risk people, especially those with diabetes, chronic gum inflammation, those who smoke, and those dealing with the effects of ageing. One may resort to unregulated web-based home cures because of a fear of dental procedures, financial constraints, or the conviction that natural solutions are safer or chemical-free. Additionally, reliance on such options may create a false sense of security. Even while such unverified online alternatives may offer mild antibacterial or anti-inflammatory effects, they cannot replace the evidence-based treatment of such dental problems. If neglected, dental conditions such as extensive carious lesions, advanced gum disorders, abscesses, and spreading infections can pose serious risks. Ignorance of these conditions can exacerbate bone loss and even result in irreversible pulp damage.

title: Fact Check: Should one rely on alum and black pepper for toothaches?
claim_text: A well-shared Instagram post with the caption "सबको पता होना चाहिए शेयर जरूर करे" claims that massaging the tooth roots with a combination of alum and black pepper can successfully resolve toothaches.
quick_take: According to an Instagram post, alum and black pepper can effectively address toothaches. We fact-checked the assertion and found it to be false.
doctor_explanation:
A toothache or tooth-related discomfort is essentially a symptom that originates from the tooth or the tissues around it. Even though they are uncomfortable, toothache symptoms are more than just a medical issue. On the other hand, they frequently indicate underlying oral or systemic issues. The discomfort generally comes from the deepest layer of the dental pulp. Dental caries is the most prevalent root cause, where the infection reaches the pulp owing to enamel degradation induced by bacterial acids. Additional contributors include gum disease, exposed tooth roots, and sinus-related referred pain. In certain cases, bruxism—the habit of grinding one's teeth—and trauma may also be influences. Given that the oral discomfort originates from a root cause, it should not be ignored, or it can progress to abscess formation and systemic spread of bacteria. Moreover, persistent pain can affect nutritional intake, speech, and quality of life. Therefore, timely identification and management of toothaches can preserve oral health and prevent broader health implications.

Can a toothache be managed with alum and black pepper? No, absolutely, not. While black pepper and alum have been promoted as toothache remedies, these claims are confined to social media due to the dearth of supporting scientific evidence.

Alum (potassium aluminium sulphate), also known as fitkari, is valued for its astringent and antimicrobial effects. It is believed that the ingredient may help reduce inflammation and limit bacterial growth.

Black pepper, the most frequently employed folk medicine, is usually taken into consideration due to its bioactive component, piperine. The alkaloid is well-known for its anti-inflammatory, digestive-supporting, antioxidant, and mild analgesic properties that may temporarily alleviate pain.

Although the aforementioned ingredients may offer short-term superficial relief, their benefits are limited to the tissues surrounding the tooth and may not be able to completely eliminate the pain. This could be attributed to the fact that it is multifactorial in origin; a single home remedy, such as the combination of alum and black pepper, may not be able to address it.

Another important factor to take into account is that the cementum, the periodontal ligament, and the jawbone are the main protectors of the tooth root, with dentin situated beneath the cementum. This external covering makes it impossible for any surface or topical applicant to reach the actual source of pain, proving that natural remedies are unable to treat the underlying cause of toothaches, which can be highly specific and individualistic.

Dr. Pooja Sharma, BDS, MDS, of NIMS University in Jaipur, Rajasthan, clarifies this further and urges anyone experiencing a toothache to seek immediate dental care. Dental pain usually implies more serious conditions, including gum disease, infections, or decay, which call for therapy. Neglecting the dental visit might lead to more major issues, including abscesses or tooth loss. While home cures could offer short-term relief, only a dentist can identify the problem's root cause and manage it to preserve prolonged oral health. Even while some home cures may provide temporary symptomatic relief, they cannot replace clinically validated dental care. If alum and black pepper are used for alleviating toothaches, the actual issue may worsen silently and cause severe complications.

Dr. Gagandeep Singh Sodhi, a dentist from Delhi, adds credence to this by pointing out that the majority of internet shortcuts have no proven scientific foundation. Dependence on do-it-yourself fixes may cause irreversible damage and delay a professional assessment. As a result, every toothache condition needs to be evaluated by a licensed dentist.

Toothaches are usually dealt with by dental practitioners using a carefully thought-out strategy. They begin by determining the root cause via pulpitis, dental caries, periodontal disorders, and damaged teeth. Once the exact cause has been identified, the appropriate course of action may be tailored. In early-stage cavities, dentists frequently remove the compromised tooth portion and replace it with the appropriate dental filling material. If the carious lesion has progressed to the pulp and resulted in pulpal irritation or infection, root canal therapy would be beneficial. However, there may be instances where the tooth is severely damaged structurally or cannot be recovered; in these cases, the infected tooth must be removed and replaced with options such as bridges or implants. If the pain is brought on by gum disease, periodontal therapy—such as scaling, root planing, or surgery—might be suggested. Severe toothache and infections may be supported with prescribed analgesics and antibiotics– temporary relievers. In addition to proactive supervision, dentists may place a high priority on patient education, regular dental exams, dietary changes, and continuous oral hygiene maintenance. In cases of persistent dental discomfort, evidence-based dentistry emphasises the necessity of timely, accurate examination and management by a qualified practitioner.

title: Should one rely on an online product for vitiligo patches?
claim_text: सफ़ेद दाग़ के मरीज़ों के लिए अब उम्मीद है – 3 महीनों में आराम, वरना दवा मुफ़्त (A Facebook post promoting Leugo Kit Ayurvedic topical therapeutic for vitiligo-related white skin patches, claiming it has been able to handle cases with generalised skin depigmentation and offers relief in 3 months or money back)
quick_take: A well-known Facebook post suggests that an online product is highly effective in managing vitiligo patches. After verifying the claim, we discovered that it is completely false.
doctor_explanation: Vitiligo is a condition marked by depigmented areas of the skin brought on by melanocyte loss or dysfunction. Melanocytes are essentially the cells that synthesise melanin, the pigment that gives skin its colour. These symmetrical depigmented lesions can appear anywhere on the body and have the potential to grow over time. While the condition is painless, it is more than a cosmetic concern. This is due to the fact that it can have a substantial impact on one's social, psychological, and physical well-being, particularly when lesions are visible on exposed parts like the face and hands. Moreover, the sickness may be associated with autoimmune diseases like diabetes, pernicious anaemia, and thyroid-related conditions. The claim promotes the use of an Ayurvedic intervention known as the Leugo Kit for vitiligo, which is alleged to reduce or repigment the white patches (safed daag) associated with the condition. The product's claimed ingredients include bakuchi, tulsi, panvad beej, bakayan, calaguala, reetha, rosemary, tea tree, and gandhak. However, for any Ayurvedic product to be sold in the market, it needs to reveal the exact quantity, standardisation, and purity tests of its ingredients. As the exact chemical composition of Leugo Kit has not been reported, claims that the product is completely herbal are questionable. We were unable to locate any reliable evidence that the kit is approved by the Ministry of AYUSH, including the QCI and IMPCL list, which casts doubt on its credibility. Upon searching the PubMed-indexed clinical trials for the effectiveness and safety of the Leugo Kit for vitiligo, we were unable to come across any peer-reviewed, randomised controlled trials. Considering the paucity of scientific studies substantiating the notion that vitiligo patches can be repigmented with Leugo Kit, the product is unreliable. Bakuchi (scientifically known as Psoralea corylifolia), one of the product's herbal ingredients, has been thoroughly investigated for its melanogenic properties. However, these studies remain limited to a small scale. Conversely, the management of vitiligo relies on clinically tested therapies, including phototherapy, corticosteroids, and topical calcineurin inhibitors, supported by both large-scale trials and dermatological guidelines. Dr. Pallav Prajapati, BAMS, Founder of Chetanya Ayurveda, Varanasi explains that Ayurvedic tradition describes vitiligo as a skin condition that results from an imbalance in the three doshas (Pitta, Kapha, and Vata), with a particular impact on the Pitta dosha, and offers a highly specific and comprehensive approach focusing on the root causes. However, random online Ayurvedic remedies may not be beneficial to everyone. Dr. Swati Watwani, Chief Consultant and Medical Director of Persian Lily in Maharashtra, an Aesthetic Dermatologist and Cosmetologist, informed THIP Media that vitiligo cannot be completely cured because of its genetic basis. Even with the incredible results of the latest procedures and state-of-the-art medications, it could happen again at any time. Dr. Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Cosmetician, Trichologist, and Consultant in Aesthetic Medicine from Lucknow maintains that currently, there is no permanent solution for vitiligo. Conventional therapy can help control it, restore some skin pigmentation, and prevent it from spreading. It is highly discouraged to use products bought online to manage vitiligo, a chronic autoimmune condition, because white skin lesions can be caused by a variety of conditions including vitiligo, eczema, fungal infections, and post-inflammatory hypopigmentation. Inadequate assessment could result in misidentification and ineffective therapy. Online self-medication products expose consumers to potentially hazardous substances, raise the possibility of diagnostic errors, and delay access to essential medical care. Dr. Gurman Singh Bhasin, Director & Chief Dermatologist, Skinclarity Clinic, Nagpur, states that vitiligo is a complicated autoimmune condition that requires a medical diagnosis and tailored care. Despite their extensive marketing, online products frequently lack stability evaluations, scientific validation, and formulations suitable for vitiligo phases. He strongly cautions against using these products exclusively. Protocols based on data, not internet fads, should direct management of a sensitive skin condition such as vitiligo.

title: Fact Check: Should one rely on self-diagnosis for cancer?
claim_text: According to Aaharhidavahai's Instagram reel, some symptoms such as persistent drops in blood haemoglobin levels, inexplicable weight loss, and an increase in lump size are early warning indicators of cancer. The claim suggests that being aware of these clinical symptoms can help in self-diagnosing cancer.
quick_take: According to a well-circulated Instagram post, being aware of early warning signs might be helpful in self-diagnosing cancer. After verifying the claim, we found that it is mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Cancer is the leading cause of mortality in several countries across the world. This could be explained by the delayed onset of the medical condition. Consequently, recognising the early warning signs of cancer could help in its timely detection and effective treatment. Some of the most frequently reported symptoms include unexplained weight loss, non-healing sores, unusual bleeding, changes in bowel or bladder habits, persistent coughing or hoarseness, and the presence of lumps or thickened areas beneath the skin. Additionally, skin-related modifications, difficulty in swallowing, or chronic indigestion may point towards an underlying malignancy. As a chronic, progressive condition, cancer may not always be detected by early clinical indications; however, they may suggest further confirmatory examinations. It is vital to emphasise that while warning signs such as unexplained weight loss, persistent weakness or fatigue, outgrowths or tumour masses, and even bleeding do trigger suspicions, they are not conclusive in determining whether a patient has cancer. This is because these symptoms may overlap with many benign medical illnesses. Therefore, even though early clinical indicators are helpful, a skilled medical specialist should always confirm these findings. Self-diagnosis is the practice of identifying a medical condition based on personal symptomatic observation without any medical intervention. While self-awareness and body vigilance are important, relying solely on self-diagnosis for cancer is neither reliable nor safe. This is due to the fact that a lot of cancer symptoms are nonspecific and might even resemble non-cancerous illnesses, which can produce unnecessary panic or false reassurance. Self-examinations, such as those for breast lumps, can be beneficial, although their sensitivity and accuracy are limited. Furthermore, not all tumours may exhibit obvious clinical signs, and some lumps may be misconstrued. Early-stage ovarian cancer, colorectal cancer, and pancreatic cancer can all be completely asymptomatic in their early stages, making them invisible. While awareness of the physical changes is vital, relying solely on self-examination may delay the required management of the issue. Dr. Nishith Vaddiboina, Senior Consultant Medical Oncologist, Renova Century Hospital, Road No. 12, Banjara Hills, Hyderabad, advises that as an oncologist, he often comes across people who try to self-diagnose cancer based on their symptoms, like unexplained weight loss or low haemoglobin. While these signs can be worrisome, they are not specific to cancer and could be linked to many other conditions. Googling symptoms often leads to unnecessary panic. The real danger lies in delaying proper diagnosis and taking unnecessary self-medication. As a result, people may either ignore the symptoms, thinking they're not serious, or assume the worst and avoid medical help out of fear. Either way, precious time is lost, and in cancer, early detection makes a big difference. Hence, Dr. Vaddiboina cautions against self-diagnosis. He urges people to consult a specialist for any concerning symptoms. This may foster mental calm and clarity. Let's trust medical expertise and not Google. When it comes to cancer, people may attempt to recognise the early symptoms, and assuming a diagnosis on their basis should be avoided. Oncologists and other medical professionals are educated to recognise these subtle changes or indicators, provide the right follow-up diagnostic procedures, and then correctly interpret the findings. A comprehensive clinical examination, an exhaustive medical history, and focused investigations—such as imaging and biopsies—are necessary for the conclusive diagnosis of cancer. False health-related information thrives on the internet, particularly on social media sites. After reading the web information, people who are suffering from bloating, exhaustion, or even weight loss may mistakenly believe that these symptoms are indicative of cancer. This could result in excessive anxiety or deceptive assurance, both of which are perilous. Another vital aspect to take into account is misdiagnosis, which can cause a major delay in necessary medical care. Additionally, some people may turn to unproven home cures or miracle treatments because they think they are the only effective ways of dealing with their ailments. Furthermore, deceptive online comparisons may cause people to ignore nebulous symptoms that would point to early-stage cancer, which might lead to the silent progression of the life-threatening condition. Therefore, health literacy is necessary to steer patients in the right direction. An individual who is more health literate is more likely to participate in preventive screenings, follow medical advice, and seek care as soon as possible. Health literacy, according to Delhi-based Senior Homoeopathic Consultant at Aggarwal Homeo Clinic, Dr. Pankaj Aggarwal, is basically taking charge of your health by being knowledgeable enough to make wise choices. However, there is a prevalent misconception that any medical condition can be managed on its own, which could delay getting the proper treatment. Hence, Dr. Aggarwal suggests that people should be wary of health information they find online and should confirm it with a licensed medical professional before accepting or acting upon it. Please understand that there is a very thin line between self-diagnosis and self-awareness. While awareness enables people to effectively communicate symptoms, diagnosis necessitates lab testing, clinical knowledge, and contextual awareness. Health outcomes may be compromised if one is mistaken for the other. Being informed is therefore essential, but it is never a good idea to substitute assuming for a doctor's assessment. Always seek professional advice.

title: Should one stare at a solar eclipse only with their eyes?
claim_text: Black people were Egyptians and used to celebrate solar eclipses! Only White people need special glasses! Everyone else should experience it with their bare eyes, the natural way!
quick_take: A popular social media post claims to see a solar eclipse with bare eyes. After verifying the assertion, we discovered that the claim was mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Dr. Nikita Chauhan, an obstetrician and gynaecologist, advises against relying only on someone or an organisation's medical information unless you have confirmed their qualifications. Dr. Nikita further explains that people are usually not the best sources of information if their credentials aren't very clear. According to the American Academy of Ophthalmology, even a short while in the sun without the appropriate eye protection might damage your retina irreversibly. In extreme cases, exposure to these solar flares may result in solar retinopathy or blindness. Solar or photic retinopathy is characterised by retinal damage. This could be brought on by prolonged exposure to strong light sources. This intense light is visible when arc welding, during solar eclipses, or even when one is simply staring directly at the sun. The retina, which is sensitive to light and is usually found in the rear of the eye, is responsible for converting light into neural signals. These signals are received by the brain, allowing us to perceive images. As a result, extended exposure to light might eventually harm the retina's photoreceptor cells by overwhelming them. This phenomenon may be especially noticeable in the macula, the area of the retina in the centre that is responsible for crisp central vision. In addition, solar retinopathy has the potential to generate acute foveal damage, hence giving rise to abnormalities in the outer retina. The sun's radiation damages the retina's sensitive cells, resulting in blurred vision, blind spots, altered coloured vision, and difficulty in discerning fine details. Most of the time, the issue resolves itself, but prolonged exposure to intense light may result in irreversible vision loss. Consequently, it is advised to see an ophthalmologist for early identification. Dr. Aditya Sethi, Ophthalmologist at Arunodaya Deseret Eye Hospital, Gurgaon stated: "As an ophthalmologist, my primary concern during a solar eclipse is ensuring the public's eye health and safety. It's crucial to recognise that looking directly at the sun, even during an eclipse, can lead to permanent eye damage or blindness. Therefore, one of the absolute 'dos' is to use ISO-certified eclipse glasses or handheld solar viewers that meet the ISO 12312-2 international standard for safe viewing. Looking at the sun with regular sunglasses—even the very dark ones—is not safe. Another important 'do' is to use indirect viewing methods, such as a pinhole projector, to observe the eclipse safely. On the 'don'ts' side, never look at the sun through an unfiltered camera, telescope, binoculars, or any other optical device, as concentrated solar rays can damage the filter and enter your eye, causing serious injury. Also, don't use homemade filters or wear eclipse glasses with scratches or damage, as their protective capabilities might be compromised. Ensuring your viewing equipment is in perfect condition and adhering to safety guidelines can make a solar eclipse a memorable and safe experience for everyone involved." Dr. Vaibhav Sethi (MBBS, DNB, FICO), Vitreoretinal specialist at Arunodaya Deseret Eye Hospital in Gurgaon, advised: "It is not safe to observe a solar eclipse with bare eyes; doing so can cause serious damage to your eyesight. It's essential to use proper eye protection, such as solar viewing glasses or specially designed solar filters for telescopes or binoculars that block harmful ultraviolet radiation." According to the American Astronomical Society, using filters—like those found in eclipse glasses or handheld solar viewers that adhere to ISO 12312-2—is the only safe way to view the sun directly during an eclipse in a safe manner. During a total eclipse, one may remove their safety glasses only when the moon completely covers the sun's bright face, but must use their solar viewer again as soon as the sun begins to shine again. The use of solar filters is not necessary only during totality. Binoculars, telescopes, unfiltered cameras, or other similar instruments should never be used to see the uneclipsed or partly eclipsed sun.

title: Should parents consider home-made baby food formula?- THIP
claim_text: Baby formula from 1960, 20oz of boiled water, 1 can of evaporated milk and 2 level tablespoons of Karo syrup. This is formula for babies in case you can't find any.
quick_take: A social media post shares a recipe to claim that baby formula can be made at home if people cannot find any at stores. We fact-checked and found the claim to be MostlyFalse.
doctor_explanation: The formula includes three ingredients – boiled water, evaporated milk and Karo syrup. While milk and water are harmless, Karo syrup is a debated ingredient to be administered to babies. Karo syrup is a commercial corn syrup derived from the starch of maize. It is true that, medical professionals in past may have recommended administering corn syrup to kids for multiple ailments. One of the popular belief was corn syrup may help relieve constipation in kids. However, the popular home remedy, has little scientific evidence to back it up. Rather, corn syrup raises the concern of dental cavities in kids. Also, medical professional believe that commercial corn syrup like Karo syrup can be made genetically modified corn which may be harmful to babies. Also, commercial corn syrups are not sterilised products that can be administered to a new born. It increases the risk of bacterial infection in the babies. Dietitian Priyanka explains, 'Although this formula does not contain all the vitamins and minerals but may help in the growth and development of malnourished babies. Milk contains all the nutrients needed for growth and development of babies. Corn syrup can be an important energy source that can provide extra calories required for the growth and development of under nourished babies. Since it is gluten free, it may not cause allergic reaction among children. But less research is available on Karo syrup.' Home-made formulas should not be considered as an alternate to commercially manufactured baby formulas. Home-made formulas are discouraged by all authority health bodies. Research suggests, nutrition is important in early days for a baby's physical and mental growth. Home-made formulas exposes the baby to a chance of contamination, leading to infections. It may even cause serious problems with high or low levels of minerals like calcium or electrolytes such as sodium. Both the American Academy of Pediatrics and the US Food and Drug Administration do not recommend making baby formula at home. Because the homemade formula recipes are not evaluated by governing authorities, it is tough to say if a homemade recipe has all essential nutrients. If not, then the lack of vital nutrients may negatively affect the growth of a baby. There are also concerns of water intoxication for infants who are fed anything other than breast milk or approved formula. Baby formulas are also prepared under strong guidelines from health authorities. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has recently drafted a regulation called Food Safety Standards (Food for Infant Nutrition) Regulations (2019) to provide manufacturers with a comprehensive guidelines and set of standards for producing quality baby food in India. This regulation aims to protect the nutritional demands of the infants, including those with inborn Errors of Metabolism (IEM). In India, it is essential for a baby food manufacturer to obtain the FSSAI registration before selling the product. Dr Vikalp Tomar, Pediatrician, Max Hospital, Dehradun, says, 'Home-made baby formula is not at all recommended by doctors. As of now, the practicing guidelines for doctors and available research considers homemade baby formula unsafe. This area requires detailed analysis using scientific methods. We do not have a standard recommendation on this formula and whether it can be prescribed to babies without significant research. Also, the age of a baby is a crucial deciding factor because you cannot universally give this recipe to every age group.' Cow's milk is not recommended for babies below 12 months. However, the American Academy of Pediatrics recommends cow milk in urgent situations for kids above 6 months old. However, 'This is not ideal and should not become routine,' reads the website of AAP. In a similar note, though plant based milk is not a recommended option for infants, AAP suggests, 'Soy milk may be an option to give babies who are close to a year of age for a few days in an emergency, but always buy the kind that is fortified with protein and calcium. Make sure to change back to formula as soon as some is available.' The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) on its website clearly advice against home made formula. In an advisory issued during baby food shortage in US, the website of HHS says, 'Call your OBGYN or paediatrician to see if they have in-office samples or can suggest a similar formula that may be more readily available in stores and is nutritionally similar to your infant's typical formula. You should not water down formula, try to make formula at home, or use toddler formula to feed infants.'

title: Fact Check: Should people with diabetes follow the MRPS rule?
claim_text: People with diabetes should avoid all foods that fall under the MRPS rule (Meat, Refined oils, Packaged foods, Sugar and Salt) because these foods are acidic, hard to digest, and harmful for people with diabetes, suggesting they should never be consumed.
quick_take: A social media post claims that people with diabetes should follow the MRPS rule. After fact checking, we found it to be mostly false.
doctor_explanation:
Can people with diabetes not eat meat or milk at all? No, not necessarily. There's no scientific guideline that completely bans meat or milk for people with diabetes. Lean meat (like chicken or fish) can be part of a healthy diabetic diet, especially when grilled or baked without excess fat. Red and processed meats, however, are best limited due to links with heart disease. Milk and dairy can also be safe in moderation. Low-fat milk, curd, and paneer (cottage cheese) provide calcium and protein. The concern with packaged milk being acidic or hard to digest lacks strong evidence. People without lactose intolerance or a milk allergy don't need to completely avoid milk. Malvika Fulwani, Founder and Chief Dietician at Healthitude, says, People with diabetes can eat meat and milk, but it's important to choose wisely and watch portions. Lean meats like chicken or fish are better than red or processed meats, which can raise the risk of heart disease. Milk and dairy can be part of the diet too, but low-fat options are preferred to manage calories and saturated fat. The goal is to keep blood sugar stable while supporting overall health.

Should refined oils and processed foods be completely cut out? Mostly yes, but not all need to be avoided entirely. It is best to limit refined oils and heavily processed foods. They often contain unhealthy fats, additives, or hidden sugars and sodium. However, saying all refined oils are harmful ignores nuance. For instance, cold-pressed or heart-healthy oils like olive or mustard oil (used in moderation) can be a part of many diabetic diets. Similarly, not all processing is harmful. Cleaning, cooking, or pasteurising are also processing methods. The problem lies in ultra-processed foods, like chips, fried snacks, sugary cereals, not in all items that undergo human handling.

Are all packaged foods bad for people with diabetes? No, not all packaged foods are harmful. Blanket avoidance of packaged foods isn't practical or accurate. Many healthy items, including oats, wholegrain bread, nuts, and yoghurt, come in packages. What matters is what's inside the packet. We advise people to read labels carefully to check for added sugars, trans fats, or high sodium levels. Some diabetic-friendly packaged foods are designed with nutrition in mind and can be part of a balanced plan.

Should all sugar and salt be removed from a diabetic's diet? No, but moderation is key. Refined sugar should be strictly limited for people with diabetes, as it raises blood sugar quickly. Natural sugars from fruits or complex carbohydrates may sometimes be a better option. However, they are still sugars and will ultimately raise your blood sugar levels. Some people prefer jaggery over sugar, thinking it is healthier, but people with diabetes should be cautious. Even so, occasional use of small amounts in controlled diets is not harmful for everyone. Salt intake should be limited, especially for people with high blood pressure. This is because all common salts, including pink and rock salt, contain similar sodium levels that affect blood pressure. Relying solely on non-iodised salts like rock or pink salt can raise the risk of iodine deficiency, which is essential for thyroid health. Because iodine deficiency still exists in some areas, using iodised salt is important to prevent thyroid problems such as goitre and hypothyroidism. Dr Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition, explains, People with diabetes don't need to cut out all sugar and salt, but they should manage their intake carefully. Natural sugars from fruits can be included in moderation, while added sugars should be limited. Similarly, reducing salt helps control blood pressure, which is important because diabetes increases the risk of heart disease. It's all about balanced eating and mindful choices.

According to the latest guidelines, people with diabetes do not need to completely avoid food groups like milk, meat, or even small amounts of sugar and salt. Instead, the focus is on balanced eating, moderation, and choosing healthier alternatives where possible.

THIP Media Take: The claim that people with diabetes should follow the MRPS rule is mostly false. The MRPS rule, as presented in the video, oversimplifies diabetes management and promotes fear around many foods unnecessarily. Although avoiding highly processed and sugary items is sound advice, completely cutting out milk, meat, and all packaged or refined foods is not backed by scientific evidence. People with diabetes should follow a personalised, balanced diet based on their individual needs, ideally planned with a certified dietitian or medical doctor.

title: Fact Check: Should scarlet fever be treated without antibiotics? - THIP Media
claim_text: To the parents, PLEASE don't live in FEAR (it's bad for your immune system and will suppress it). Scarlet fever and Strep A is very treatable and don't need antibiotics. It's very easy for people to ask for them and think it's a quick FIX, but it will damage your gut and immune for a long time. You won't want that. Antibiotics should be GIVEN when it's a life and death situation, not for something simple like these illnesses, when it can be treated with natural remedies.
quick_take: A social media post claims Scarlet fever and Strep A are treatable and don't need antibiotics. In fact, the consumption of antibiotics can damage the gut and immune system. We fact-checked and found this claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation:
Scarlet fever is a contagious bacterial illness that mostly affects children. The causative agent is a bacteria called group A Streptococcus (group A strep). The same bacteria is also the causative agent of strep throat. The bacteria sometimes make a toxin (poison), which causes a distinctive pink-red rash, the 'scarlet' of scarlet fever. The rash can spread over the body and is also bumpy, so it's sometimes called a sandpaper rash. It is also accompanied by fever, a white-coloured coating on the tongue, chills, stomach pain, nausea, etc. Lastly, scarlet fever is also known as Scarlatina.

An antibiotic treatment regime is the ideal treatment recommended for Scarlet fever. The choice of drug is penicillin or amoxicillin and cephalosporins (in case of penicillin allergy). These medications are given to shorten the duration of symptoms, reducing the likelihood of transmission and preventing complications. The CDC recommends that if a child has scarlet fever, antibiotics can help the child feel better faster and prevent long-term health problems. The NHS also puts why antibiotics are necessary by stating that scarlatina is a serious illness, but with the use of antibiotics, it becomes easily treatable. It must be noted here that antibiotics are not just used to treat the patient but also help protect others from getting sick. Antibiotics kill bacteria or prevent them from reproducing and spreading.

Dr. Kashyap Dakshini, General Physician practicing in Mumbai, further elaborates on this by stating, "Scarlet fever is treated by a course of antibiotics for 10 days. There is no documented scientific evidence published in any reputed journal with respect to the treatment of scarlet fever without antibiotics with success."

If timely treatment is not given, the patient is put at risk of various complications, such as ear infection, sinusitis (inflammation of the sinus), throat abscess (a painful collection of pus), pneumonia (inflammation of the lungs) and in rare cases can cause life-threatening complications, such as bacteremia, septic arthritis, meningitis, necrotizing fasciitis and streptococcal toxic shock syndrome. Researchers state that around 5% of those with untreated streptococcal infection, such as strep throat or scarlet fever, will develop rheumatic fever.

It is true that fever is a part of the body's immune response, but high temperatures should always be treated as per medical advice. In general, antibiotics are considered safe if used correctly, and serious side effects are rare. However, overprescribing antibiotics is associated with an increased risk of adverse effects.

title: Fact Check: Should toothaches be managed with yoga mudras?
claim_text: Apan Vaayu and Vaat Nashak yoga mudras are particularly effective in managing toothaches
quick_take: According to a widely shared Facebook post, two specific yoga mudras are particularly effective in addressing toothaches. After verifying the claim, we determined that it is false.
doctor_explanation:
A toothache is usually referred to as discomfort in and around the jaws and teeth. It is one of the most prevalent signs of dental deterioration or caries. Gingivitis, periodontitis, impacted wisdom teeth, ulcers, sinusitis, or dental abscesses can all cause dental discomfort. The dental pain is most frequently associated with tooth decay. Bacterial activity in dental plaque usually initiates the carious lesion by producing acids that have the potential to demineralise enamel. When degeneration reaches the dentin and exposes the pulp, pulpitis results. This inflammation results in enhanced blood flow and pressure inside the hard tooth structure, which causes sharp or throbbing pain. If treatment is not received, pulpal necrosis may affect the surrounding bone and soft tissue, potentially resulting in pus-filled pockets. Determining the precise cause of the toothache facilitates timely and accurate intervention.

Both the Apan Vaayu Mudra and the Vaat Nashal Mudra are conventional hand gestures. These are considered to alleviate various facets and influence the body's elemental equilibrium. The Vaat Nashak Mudra frequently combines Vayu mudra, which decreases the air element, and Shunya mudra, which lessens the space element. When taken together, they have been suggested to be beneficial with the exacerbated Vata dosha, which is associated with restlessness, numbness, and pain. The Apan Vayu Mudra is also referred to as the "life-saving manoeuvre". Generally speaking, this mudra is said to enhance heart function and circulation, which reduces chest pain and discomfort. While it is commonly known as the Mrita Sanjivani Mudra, which translates to "one that brings life from death," the mudra's role is confined to serving as an adjunct to professional medical care rather than a viable substitute for it. Despite being widely employed in traditional medical systems, there is conflicting empirical evidence regarding the efficacy of these yoga mudras in managing toothaches. As a result, they should not be used instead of evidence-based dental procedures.

Yoga therapy may help reduce pain associated with temporomandibular joint issues, stress, or muscle tension. In patients receiving root canal therapy, yoga relaxation techniques may also considerably reduce anxiety, suggesting the potential benefits for dental pain management. Additionally, dental practitioners may be able to prevent musculoskeletal issues by following a disciplined yoga regimen. Despite these benefits, it is not recommended to implement yoga therapy for the management of toothaches. Dental discomfort is a symptom that results from underlying dental conditions, including cavities, infections, or gum diseases that call for professional dental evaluation and therapeutic intervention.

Dr. Pooja Sharma, BDS, MDS, of NIMS University in Jaipur, Rajasthan, strongly advises anyone with a toothache to seek medical attention right away. Dental discomfort usually indicates more serious diseases that call for clinical attention, such as infections, decay, or gum disease. Delaying a dental appointment may result in more serious issues, such as tooth loss or abscesses. Home remedies could provide temporary relief, but only a dentist can determine the source of the issue and manage it to maintain long-term oral health.

This is further supported by Dr. Gagandeep Singh Sodhi, a dental expert from Delhi, who notes that most online shortcuts lack an established scientific basis. Reliance on do-it-yourself solutions could result in irreparable harm and delay a professional evaluation. Therefore, every toothache case should be examined by a qualified dentist. Given that yoga therapy may help alleviate anxiety brought on by toothaches, it is crucial to comprehend that dental pain is a sign of an underlying issue that calls for evidence-based management. Therefore, yoga and the previously mentioned mudras should be an integral component of an all-encompassing strategy for tooth management rather than the primary therapy for dental issues.

Managing toothaches necessitates a multimodal approach. Dental professionals usually perform a comprehensive clinical examination and radiographic evaluation. Patients get recommended NSAIDs or prescription analgesics with an established safety and efficacy profile to relieve their pain. In case of an infection, antibiotics may be given to halt the rapid spread of the infection. Definitive intervention depends on the underlying cause. Dental experts usually employ restorative filling, prosthetic crowns, endodontic therapy, and surgical intervention for abscess drainage. While these unsubstantiated remedies are becoming more and more popular on social media, they don't work to relieve the excruciating toothache. Reliance on them can be detrimental and could interfere with your existing pharmacological regimen.

title: Fact Check: Should toothpaste never be used?
claim_text: We have been brainwashed into using toothpaste and it should never be used as it contains various chemicals, such as fluoride and is made by secret individuals in the lab. It further states that can hamper the brain, making it function at low levels and develop conditions, such as dementia.
quick_take: A social media post claims that toothpaste should never be used as it contains various chemicals, such as fluoride and is made by secret individuals in the lab. It further states that can hamper the brain. We fact-checked and found this claim to be False.
doctor_explanation: Brushing your teeth is essential for maintaining good oral hygiene and promoting overall health. Toothpaste is generally recommended and should be used as a part of your daily oral hygiene routine to maintain good oral health. It removes plaque which is a sticky film of bacteria that can lead to cavities and gum disease. Brushing also freshens breath by removing food particles and bacteria to avoid bad breath. Poor oral health can cause various health problems, including heart disease, stroke, and diabetes, so regular brushing is essential. However, it's important to use it in moderation, choose toothpaste with appropriate ingredients for your needs, and brush gently to avoid damaging your teeth or gums. The choice of toothpaste can depend on your individual dental needs, such as sensitivity, cavity prevention, or gum health. Remember, it is advisable not to swallow toothpaste as it contains certain chemicals, such as fluoride. If you have any doubts or concerns about which toothpaste to use or if you should use toothpaste at all, it's best to consult with your dentist or dental hygienist for personalized guidance based on your specific oral health needs. Regarding fluoridated toothpastes: Rarely. Fluoride toothpaste strengthens tooth enamel, which can prevent cavities. It also prevents gum disease by removing plaque and bacteria that can cause inflammation and infection in the gums. It can be harmful only in a certain scenario. Many dentists recommend the topical use of fluorine because of its cariostatic effect that prevents the formation of dental caries. The Indian dental Association (IDA) website states that the topical use of fluorides is 'the most effective and economical method of protecting the teeth against decay'. Dr. Paridhi Garg, Endodontist, adds, 'Fluoride makes the tooth enamel stronger by remineralizing the lost enamel and by disrupting the cavity-causing bacteria. Fluoride can be incorporated into our teeth by adding it to our diet, drinking water and toothpaste. But in excess, fluoride can be harmful for your teeth and bones so a dentist's guidance becomes imperative'. For the body, excessive long-term exposure to fluoride can have adverse effects which include, osteoporosis, tooth decay and damage to bones, kidneys, reproductive organs, nerves and muscle. However, fluoride in low concentration maintains and solidifies bones and prevents dental caries. That being the case, fluoride is widely used in toothpaste because it prevents tooth decay. Dr. Sandeep Sharma, Dental Surgeon in Delhi, said, 'Fluoride is good for teeth because it hardens the enamel to prevent demineralization and cavities. However, the fluoride should be used in moderate amounts. Chronic and regular consumption of high levels of fluoride results in white flecks and yellow or brown areas scattered over the tooth surface.' Addressing brain harm claims: There is no credible scientific evidence to suggest that using toothpaste as directed can harm your brain. Toothpaste is specifically formulated for oral use and is not designed to have any adverse effects on the brain or neurological system when used as intended. Toothpaste is primarily composed of mild abrasives, fluoride, detergents, flavorings, and other ingredients that are safe for oral hygiene. The fluoride in toothpaste, for example, is beneficial for strengthening tooth enamel and preventing tooth decay when used properly and in appropriate quantities. The ingredients in toothpaste are not known to have any harmful neurological effects. It's important to use toothpaste in the recommended manner, which includes applying a small amount (about the size of a pea) to your toothbrush, brushing your teeth gently, and spitting out the toothpaste after brushing. Swallowing small amounts of toothpaste during brushing is generally not harmful for adults, but it should be minimized, especially in the case of young children, to avoid excessive fluoride ingestion and in case of overdosage, contact the doctor immediately. In conclusion, it is better to brush your teeth twice a day with toothpaste for at least two minutes each time. Just remember to use a gentle technique, a good quality toothbrush, and follow a consistent oral care routine to keep your teeth and gums in the best possible condition. Also, it is beneficial to visit your dentist regularly for professional cleanings and check-ups.

title: Fact check: Should we reconsider using paracetamol to control fever?
claim_text: A widely shared Facebook Reel claims that taking an antipyretic like Paracetamol can harm various organs, and recommends ingesting Kadha, an Ayurvedic medicated preparation, rather than the conventional allopathic antipyretic. Additionally, some posts express worry about the negative effects of paracetamol and the possibility that the Machupo virus is present in the paracetamol tablets.
quick_take: There is a circulating Facebook reel that claims paracetamol is dangerous and should not be used to control fever. We have conducted thorough research to verify this claim and found it to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation:
Fever is a natural defence mechanism that occurs when the body's temperature rises above 98.6 degrees Fahrenheit (37 degrees Celsius). It frequently occurs as a result of trauma, inflammation, or infections. There are two main types of fevers: acute, which last for a short duration, and chronic, which persist for a longer period and may indicate underlying health issues such as autoimmune disorders or certain cancers. Fever is often accompanied by common symptoms such as sweating, chills, and an elevated heart rate. To manage fever and alleviate discomfort, antipyretic medications are commonly used. Paracetamol (acetaminophen) works by inhibiting the production of prostaglandins, which are chemicals in the body responsible for the fever response. By reducing prostaglandin levels, paracetamol effectively lowers body temperature and provides relief from fever and its associated symptoms. However, it is important to use paracetamol under medical guidance and adhere to recommended dosages.

Paracetamol is a widely used over-the-counter medication known for its effectiveness in reducing fever and managing mild to moderate pain. However, improper use can pose risks, particularly in terms of liver damage. Paracetamol is metabolised by the liver, and an overdose, especially when combined with regular alcohol consumption, can result in severe liver toxicity. Accidental overdoses can also occur when individuals unknowingly take multiple medications that contain paracetamol, which is a common ingredient in cold and flu remedies. Although paracetamol does not have anti-inflammatory properties, which makes it less suitable for certain conditions like arthritis, its widespread use can be attributed to several factors. Paracetamol is known for its minimal impact on the gastrointestinal system. However, excessive and uncontrolled intake of paracetamol may result in abdominal pain, discomfort, heartburn, nausea, or vomiting. Additionally, it is well-tolerated across different age groups, from children to older people, and has few interactions with other medications, making it compatible with various treatments. Paracetamol is considered safe during pregnancy under medical guidance.

In rare cases, paracetamol can cause adverse skin reactions such as rashes, itching, hives (urticaria), and, extremely rarely, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN). These skin reactions emphasise the importance of monitoring for unexpected symptoms and promptly discontinuing the use of paracetamol, especially for individuals with a history of skin sensitivity or allergies.

Dr. Kashyap Dakshini, General Physician, Mumbai, explains that paracetamol is considered the safest antipyretic for treating fever. While other drugs like ibuprofen and NSAIDs also have antipyretic effects, it is important to use them with caution. He advises exercising caution when taking these drugs for prolonged periods, as they may have adverse effects on the stomach, liver, and kidneys. It is not recommended to use NSAIDs in individuals with kidney problems, stomach ulcers, liver conditions, or cardiac issues.

Regarding Ayurvedic Kadha: Ayurveda offers a comprehensive approach to managing fever by emphasising the traditional herbal remedy known as 'kadha'. According to Ayurvedic philosophy, fever is seen as a doshic imbalance that needs to be restored for overall harmony. Kadha, a time-honoured infusion, combines tulsi, ginger, black pepper, and cinnamon, which are renowned for their immune-boosting, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and overall wellness properties. However, it is essential to note that kadha plays a significant role in Ayurvedic fever management, but it is considered complementary and not a substitute for conventional medications such as paracetamol. Paracetamol, a pharmaceutical fever reducer, is specifically designed for symptom relief. Even though kadha can enhance treatment regimens, caution must be exercised and medical professionals should be consulted, especially in cases of severe or persistent fever.

title: Fact Check: Should you clean your baby's ear with a toolset?
claim_text: A Facebook post advertising an earwax removal toolkit displays a video which starts with a baby with earwax and then shows how the toolkit works. Its caption also reads, "Safe and efficient deep cleaning of ears, prevent infection, and relieve itching. The perfect personal care tool for your family."
quick_take: A social media post claims that earwax can be removed with a toolset even in babies. We fact-checked and found this claim to be Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: Earwax, or cerumen, serves essential functions in ear health. It acts as a natural barrier, safeguarding the ear canal from debris and insects. The natural oils in earwax moisturize the ear canal, preventing dryness and discomfort. Furthermore, earwax possesses antibacterial and antifungal properties, shielding against infections. The ear's self-cleaning mechanism pushes earwax from the ear canal to the outer ear, facilitating natural, maintenance-free cleaning. Earwax primarily consists of sebum from the glands, deceased epithelial cells, keratin, and fatty acids. The color of the wax tends to turn black when there is a higher concentration of keratin and dead cells, often associated with dirt and commonly observed in older individuals. On the other hand, if the wax contains a larger proportion of fatty acids, it appears yellowish, which is typically seen in children and is more common in older people. Earwax (cerumen) does not typically require regular removal. The ear has a self-cleaning mechanism that usually keeps the ear canal clean without the need for intervention. As you engage in everyday activities such as talking and chewing, the movement of your jaw helps to naturally move earwax from the ear canal toward the outer ear. Eventually, the earwax dries up and flakes off or falls out on its own. This process ensures that the ear canal remains clean and free from excessive earwax buildup. In most cases, the earwax that is produced naturally by your body will not cause problems and does not need to be removed. However, some individuals may experience earwax buildup or impaction, which can lead to symptoms such as hearing loss, pain, or discomfort. It is not recommended to use a wax cleaner toolset to clean your baby's or your own ears. In fact, doing so could cause permanent hearing damage. Earwax is a natural substance that helps to protect the ear canal from dust, dirt, and other foreign objects. A baby's ear does not need to be cleaned more than 2-3 times a week with a washcloth or cotton wool and warm water. Wax cleaner toolsets can push earwax further into the ear canal, where it can become lodged and cause a blockage. It can also introduce new bacteria, dust, or dirt. Furthermore, babies' ear canals are very small and delicate. It is easy to damage the ear canal or eardrum when using earwax tools, especially in babies. Some online toolkits may be made with cheap, low-quality materials that could irritate or damage the ear canal. In fact, some online toolkits may not be effective at removing earwax. If you or your baby has excessive earwax buildup or blockages, see a doctor for professional cleaning. A doctor can use a special ear irrigation device to gently flush the earwax out of the ear canal. It's essential to strike a balance between maintaining ear health and avoiding excessive earwax removal, as removing too much earwax can lead to dryness and irritation of the ear canal. Some people also use earwax removal spray, which is also not safe. If you have concerns about earwax or experience symptoms related to earwax, consult a healthcare provider for guidance and appropriate care.

title: Should you eat onions to control blood sugar? - THIP Media
claim_text: An article titled, 'Control diabetes with raw onions!' was published on a media website named hariome.com. The article recommends people eat 50 grams of onion daily as it is equivalent to 20 units of insulin.

doctor_explanation: There is limited scientific evidence to suggest that onions can regulate blood sugar levels. Onions are a low glycemic index food, meaning they release sugar into the bloodstream more slowly than high glycemic index foods, which helps prevent sudden spikes in blood sugar levels. However, more research is needed to fully understand the potential benefits of consuming raw onions for blood sugar control. The relationship between onions and diabetes is complex. Many factors contribute to the prevalence of diabetes in India which mere eating onions cannot resolve, including genetic predisposition, lifestyle changes (sedentary habits and unhealthy diets), obesity, gestational diabetes, socioeconomic factors, and an aging population. Diabetologist Dr Ritesh Bansal explains, "Onion has a low glycemic index, low carbohydrate content, and high in antioxidants. All those complement sugar control. Also, onions contain quercetin, a flavonoid that improves insulin sensitivity, a major factor in diabetic patients. So onion though not behaving like insulin certainly have a positive impact in controlling sugar level". While there is some limited evidence suggesting that consuming raw onions may help regulate blood sugar levels due to their low glycemic index, it is not a guaranteed solution for blood sugar control. Managing blood sugar levels involves a comprehensive approach that includes a balanced diet, regular physical activity, and potentially medication or insulin as prescribed by a healthcare professional. Referencing findings from The Endocrine Society's 97th annual meeting, an extract derived from onion bulbs, when administered alongside the anti-diabetic drug Metformin in rats, exhibited a significant ability to reduce high blood sugar and total cholesterol levels. This study suggested onions could potentially lower blood sugar levels by approximately 50 percent, but it is important to note that it is not yet ready for widespread implementation in diabetes treatment. The study specifically investigated the effects of onion extract in combination with existing medication, rather than relying solely on onions for blood sugar normalization. Moreover, the study was relatively small in scale, underscoring the need for further research. Nutritionist Kamna Chauhan informs, "Eating raw onion can help to control blood sugar level. In the absence of proper care, erratic blood sugar levels may lead to kidney failure, heart complications, and obesity. Some studies have shown that raw onion can help to control our blood sugar level as it contains multiple flavonoids which is a class of antioxidants. Besides this, onions are high in fiber, low in carbohydrates as well as glycemic index. However, people must not replace it with their prescribed medical treatment". Additionally, consuming large amounts of raw onions may cause digestive discomfort in some individuals. Not seeking medical advice while trying to maintain blood sugar levels at home can be dangerous, leading to inadequate monitoring, misinterpretation of results, improper medication management, delayed detection of complications, lack of individualized treatment, and missed educational opportunities.

title: Fact Check: Should you perform CPR by watching social media videos? - THIP Media
claim_text: A Facebook video showing a person performing CPR on an unconscious individual, claiming it demonstrates the correct lifesaving procedure for heart attack emergencies
quick_take: A video on social media claims cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is lifesaving in case of a heart attack. The video shows a person giving CPR to an unconscious individual. We fact-checked and found the claim is False. The way CPR is done in the video is incorrect.
doctor_explanation: What is CPR? Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is a procedure to restart a heart that has stopped beating. This condition is called cardiac arrest as the heart's electrical system stops sending signals for the heart to beat. Heartbeat can also stop in case of a heart attack. During a heart attack, blood flow to the heart gets significantly reduced due to a blocked artery. In the case of a heart attack, CPR is no use as long as the person having a heart attack is alert and breathing. Also, CPR does not work on all unconscious people with a heart attack. Is the method shown in video correct? No. We referred to the CPR steps provided by the American Red Cross Training Services and found that the person in the Facebook video is performing the wrong CPR. The fingers while giving chest compressions must be interlocked. Also, the body posture of the unconscious person must remain straight, which was not followed in the video as the unconscious individual's neck was tilting throughout the video. Also, the process does not require a handkerchief to give breaths, as shown in the video. The video also does not talk about compressions to ventilations ratio. After performing 30 chest compressions, two rescue breaths must be administered mouth to mouth, mouth to mask or through stoma, as appropriate. For children and infants, if two rescuers are performing CPR, this ratio changes to 15:2. No. Most social media videos do not give the correct picture of the process. From the Facebook video, it is evident that CPR must be given only by experienced healthcare professionals. A layman should only watch the video to understand the basic steps involved in giving CPR as well as when and why CPR should be done. Mere watching social media videos will never provide hands-on experience, which is essential to follow the correct procedure. The same has been confirmed by a research published in 2022 that informs no video presents 100% compliance with the American Heart Association guidelines. Also, there is no method to supervise and control health-related contents that allow people to post mistaken videos, which are used as learning material by many people. Doing CPR is not as easy as it looks in videos. Regular practice of CPR gives an idea of strength and ability to continue doing CPR along with an understanding of the depth needed for each chest compression. Good CPR requires an in-person class with mannequins which is monitored by a good instructor.

title: Fact Check: Should you trust social media for your parasitic wounds? - THIP Media
claim_text: A Facebook Video shows an ASMR video simulation of a procedure to remove parasitic wounds and snail infestations to disinfect the soles of the feet.
quick_take: A Facebook video, which is actually an animated video, claims to show a procedure to remove parasitic wounds and snail infestations. The process depicted in the video is medically inaccurate and False. Despite it being an animated video, we believe it can be bothersome, confusing, and deceiving. The video can affect any person who has little or no idea about real-life snail infestation and sole disinfectant procedures.
doctor_explanation: Why is this video deceptive? Despite being an animated video, the video does not clearly mention that its content is only for entertainment purposes. People can perceive the claimed video as an actual simulation of a procedure to remove parasitic wounds and snail infestations. The highly inaccurate nature of the video creates a wrong notion about how the procedure is performed. The overall video creates a wrong image of a crucial medical procedure with only a disclaimer of being an ASMR video. The video could be misleading for someone who is uninformed about these conditions. Even, considering this as an entertainment video, the content is medically inaccurate. What is an ASMR video? ASMR (Autonomous Sensory Meridian Response) videos are a type of content that aims to trigger a tingling or relaxing sensation in the viewer's body. The tingling sensation often begins at the scalp and moves down the neck and spine. These videos typically feature sounds such as tapping, whispering, or other soft noises that some people find soothing or calming. Some people experience ASMR responses from videos like the one in question. However, others may find the images unsettling and uncomfortable. Those who are uncomfortable may also have trypophobia, a fear of holes. Should you trust social media for your parasitic wounds? No. People must not trust social media videos for their parasitic wounds. Most social media videos do not give the correct picture of the process. The claimed social media video does not provide a clear picture of what parasitic wounds and snail manifestations are, what they look like, and how they are treated. The claimed video is a complete distortion of the parasitic wounds and snail infestation procedures (even if we consider the video as entertainment). To clarify, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) defines snail infestation as Schistosomiasis. This condition is an infection that transmits to humans through infected water. No evidence shows that schistosomiasis looks the way shown in the claimed Facebook video. Additionally, while different parasites can cause wounds, none of them resemble the portrayal in the video. Dr Kunal Gupta, MD, Emergency Physician at Accord Superspeciality Hospital, Faridabad, informs, "Treating parasitic wounds and snail infestations as shown in these videos are not so easy . They are very difficult to treat and may take a number of surgical procedures repeatedly". Dr Kashyap Dakshini, General physician practicing in Mumbai explains, "Snail/worm infestation requires medical expertise to determine the type of worm/parasite, use of antibiotic or anthelmintic with specific sensitivity, appropriate dosage and duration of treatment. One should avoid being carried away with random posts in social media which may not have scientific basis or clinical trial and evidence to support the claim." Upon further research, we found that the claimed video has been shared by a Facebook group called SRBD Gaming. This group specializes in live streaming of various games. Upon review, we found that they have other videos that are similar in nature to the claimed video.

title: Can you trust social media on aluminum leaching?
claim_text: An Instagram video claims that aluminum utensils leave black residue when cleaned with a scrubber, demonstrating that aluminum leaches into food. The video shows a steel utensil leaving no residue when cleaned, while the aluminum utensil leaves black liquid residue, suggesting aluminum is harmful and leaches into food during cooking.
quick_take: A video circulating on social media presents an experiment suggesting that aluminum leaches into food when using certain utensils. While the claim itself seems valid to a certain extent, the experiment showcased in the video lacks credibility. Hence, we rate the video as Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: Cookware and utensil manufacturers frequently employ aluminum as a common material. Also, evidence shows that under certain conditions, small amounts of aluminum can leach into food. However, no evidence proves that the experiment conducted in the claimed Instagram video is a correct way to confirm aluminum leaching. When it comes to aluminum leaching from utensils, it is a topic that has been studied by various researchers. Dr Sumit Aggarwal, Scientist D and Program officer, Division of Epidemiology & Communicable Diseases at the ICMR, Department of Health Research, Ministry of Health and family welfare, GOI, confirms the same. He informs, "We do have studies on aluminum leaching from utensils into food done in India as well as abroad. The results demonstrated that there is no direct significant negative effect on the human body. However, toxicity manifests whenever there is an elevation in some influencing parameters like in acidic pH range 4-8." Dr Aggarwal further explains, "The water turns black due to the presence of aluminum oxides (Al2O3). Using an abrasive paper, removes the oxide layer. However, a new one develops instantly, adding to the pile of oxides. The apparent black color is a result of the very fine particle size of the oxide 'powder', which does not reflect light effectively. Fretting corrosion on metals, including aluminum and copper, appears black for this reason. A bare aluminum surface cannot withstand exposure as it is highly reactive to oxygen, resulting in the formation of a stable oxide compound through a reaction with O2". The article also references a previous fact-check on cooking in Aluminum foil causing Alzheimer's Disease, noting that while aluminum leaches into food, the available evidence is not enough to confirm whether it is a proven risk factor for Alzheimer's disease. Social media users also pointed out flaws in the experiment: one user noted they never experienced black residue after cleaning an aluminum utensil but did notice residue when cleaning an iron utensil; another mentioned that vigorously scrubbing aluminum utensils or using a new scrub can result in a black color; a third commented that the person in the video was scrubbing a dirty aluminum utensil; and another observation was that the scrubber used for steel utensils appeared clean while the scrubber used for aluminum utensils seemed to have soap or dirt on it.
