Dr. Pawan Raj, Associate Professor & Consultant Neurologist at Father Muller Medical College, says, 'No it is not a valid test for diagnosing Alzheimer's disease.'

Shallu Joon, Clinical Neuropsychologist at National Brain Research Centre, echoes the same answer: 'Many messages like this circulate on social media claiming to test/screen various psychiatric or neurological disorder. I have also seen these random Images claiming to test intelligence or personality types or memory capabilities etc. We only rely on reliable and valid neuropsychological tests with research based evidence backing those. So I don't find this as a test to detect Alzheimer's disease.'

The US National Department of Aging defines Alzheimer's disease as 'an irreversible, progressive brain disorder that slowly destroys memory and thinking skills, and, eventually, the ability to carry out the simplest tasks. Scientists don't yet fully understand what causes Alzheimer's disease in most people.'

Dr. Raj points out to a recent study published in Neurology (a peer-reviewed neurology journal) in June 2020, which states that combination of healthy lifestyle choices may cut the dementia risk by up to 60%, which includes 'engagement in late-life cognitive activities' — but solving a single puzzle is not a diagnostic test.

On self-testing, Dr. Raj states: 'You cannot diagnose yourself. The diagnosis of Alzheimer's has to be done by a physician after interviewing and examining the patient with memory loss. There is no gold standard test to confirm Alzheimer's disease but some tests are being developed. However if you have a strong suspicion, you can screen yourself by administering various validated self assessment tests which can assess your memory and cognitive function. Eg: SAGE questionnaire, MMSE, miniCog assessment etc. A set of validated online tools are available.'

Shallu Joon adds: 'Every memory problem is not indicative of having Alzheimer's Disease. So only a person of knowledge can differentiate and go to actual reasons of the issue. A person who is in initial stage facing memory problems and other cognitive issues might indicate towards mild cognitive impairment (MCI) should seek professional help only.'

Dementia Central has a list of scientifically approved tests for Alzheimer's disease, and 'Find the camel' test is not one of them. The claim refers to a product from a company that is no longer in operation and had no partnership or involvement with Gates or his foundation. Entomophagy (the practice of eating insects) is common in many cultures around the world; insects have been consumed by humans for centuries and are considered a sustainable and nutritious food source. They are rich in protein, vitamins, and minerals and have a lower environmental footprint compared to traditional livestock. Insects like crickets, mealworms, and locusts are popular choices due to their high nutritional value. According to the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), the average person unintentionally eats around 500 grams of insects per year through processed foods like chocolate, peanut butter, and canned fruits. Insects are an excellent source of protein, often containing more protein per gram than traditional meat sources. They are also rich in essential amino acids, vitamins (such as B12 and riboflavin), minerals (like iron, zinc, and magnesium), and healthy fats including omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids. Insect farming requires significantly less land, water, and feed compared to traditional livestock farming, and insects produce fewer greenhouse gases. Potential risks include pathogens or parasites if insects are not properly cooked or processed, and allergic reactions similar to shellfish allergies.

title: Fact Check: Has the Indian government enforced lockdowns to control Mpox?
claim_text: The Indian government has enforced lockdowns to curb the Mpox outbreak in India. There are over 2,00,000 cases and 400+ deaths in India. People are advised to wear masks and follow COVID protocols to protect themselves from Mpox.
quick_take: A social media post claims that the Indian government has enforced lockdowns to curb the Mpox outbreak in India. We did the fact check and found it to be False.
doctor_explanation: The Indian government has NOT ordered any lockdowns due to Mpox. As of now, there is no official announcement from the Indian government, the Ministry of Health, or any other reliable source regarding lockdowns to control Mpox cases. Lockdowns are usually implemented for highly contagious diseases with widespread community transmission, like COVID-19. Mpox does not currently pose such a significant threat in India to enforce this extreme measure. The recent Mpox case in India is a travel-related infection of the West African clade 2. It is the 31st case since July 2022. The patient, a young male, is stable and in isolation. Moreover, contact tracing is ongoing. Currently, there is no public health risk in India. Dr Meinkaa Aakash, Senior Manager at the Office of Public Health & Research, Max Healthcare, New Delhi, explained: "India is taking proactive steps to protect its citizens, especially after the World Health Organization (WHO) raised global concerns. The government has strengthened surveillance at airports and entry points to detect and isolate suspected cases early, which is crucial for preventing the virus from spreading." Dr Aakash emphasised the role of public awareness campaigns in educating people about Mpox symptoms and transmission, urging quick action if symptoms appear. "Hospitals and clinics across the country are well-equipped to diagnose cases quickly, and healthcare workers are trained to provide safe care," she added. She also reassured: "India's healthcare system is more resilient now, having learned valuable lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic. With improved infrastructure and systems in place, and collaboration with international bodies like the WHO, we are well-prepared to manage any potential outbreaks effectively." Regarding the claim of 2,00,000 cases and 400+ deaths in India: These numbers are inaccurate. As per the latest data from official health agencies, India has recorded just 31 Mpox cases since the WHO declared it a PHEIC in 2022. Although Mpox is a viral disease, it has not caused such an overwhelming number of infections or deaths in India. Regarding COVID protocols for Mpox: Mpox and COVID-19 are two different viruses with distinct transmission patterns. Mpox primarily spreads through close contact with infected persons, including skin-to-skin contact or exposure to contaminated materials like bedding or towels. Unlike COVID-19, it does not spread easily through the air, and hence Mpox is not airborne. Wearing masks is not a standard precaution for Mpox prevention. Instead, avoiding close contact with infected individuals and practising proper hygiene is more effective. Public health guidelines for Mpox do not strictly require COVID protocols like wearing masks or maintaining physical distance. Regarding whether lockdowns can prevent Mpox spread: Not necessarily, since Mpox does not spread in the same way as highly contagious respiratory viruses like COVID-19. The virus requires close physical contact for transmission. Most cases can be controlled with isolation of infected individuals and targeted public health measures. Lockdowns are not a recommended strategy for controlling Mpox outbreaks. India's health authorities, including the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), have designated 35 laboratories nationwide for Mpox testing, including AIIMS Nagpur. Health experts such as Prof. Dr Prashant Joshi from AIIMS Nagpur have advised the public not to panic but to take precautions, especially for high-risk groups like children, pregnant women, and immunocompromised individuals. THIP Media Take: The claim that the Indian government has ordered lockdowns due to Mpox is false. There are no such orders, and the figures related to cases and deaths mentioned in the post are incorrect. Mpox is not highly contagious, and public health measures such as isolation and hygiene practices are sufficient to control its spread. There is no need to follow COVID-19 protocols for Mpox prevention.

title: If alcohol kills coronavirus, it will be party time for many. But is it true?
claim_text: Alcohol Kills Coronavirus. When coronavirus can be removed by washing hands with alcohol, then drinking alcohol will surely remove virus from the throat.
quick_take: A social post is doing rounds which claims that alcohol can actually kill coronavirus. The post, for obvious reasons, found many supporters. We fact check the claim and found it to be half true.
doctor_explanation: Yes, 70% of alcohol concentration can kill many pathogens including coronavirus. Hence alcohol based hand sanitizers are recommended to be used to keep your hands free of virus. But 'drinking alcohol' doesn't kill Coronavirus inside your body. One of the fake posts talks about a press release from Saint Luke's Hospital of Kansas City suggesting that extensive research has shown that Vodka can kill novel Coronavirus. For alcohol to be effective against any kind of pathogens (virus, bacteria) it needs to be 60% to 70% pure. Most hand sanitizers have around 70% alcohol content. A solution that is around 70% alcohol can effectively kill pathogens by breaking apart proteins in a pathogen, splitting cells into pieces or messing with a cell's metabolism. The alcohol content in hard drinks (whisky, vodka etc.) are much milder with average alcohol content around 40%. At this proportion, alcohol is mostly ineffective against any virus. This is exactly why regular alcohols like Vodka will not be an effective hand sanitizer. To prove the point, Vodka maker Titos Vodka has put out a tweet saying their product is not effective to be used as hand sanitizer or killing any viruses. Per the CDC, hand sanitizer needs to contain at least 60% alcohol. Tito's Handmade Vodka is 40% alcohol, and therefore does not meet the current recommendation of the CDC. Absolutely, NO. Alcohol in any form is harmful to our body. But, at 70% concentration (known as Rubbing Alcohol), it's dangerous and can cause serious harm to your body and brain. If rubbing alcohol is consumed, it can quickly lead to alcohol poisoning—even death. claim_text: When the mosquitoes come out everyone, WEAR BUG SPRAY OUTSIDE. I might be wrong, but I personally think that if a mosquito sucks the blood of a person with #coronavirus and then bites you, the virus could spread to you. I'm not smart, but just do it to be safe.

doctor_explanation:
Though there is a lot we still do not know about the new Coronavirus, but it is unlikely that mosquitoes will be able to carry the virus. The World Health Organization (WHO) website has clearly mentioned that, 'To date, there has been no information nor evidence to suggest that the new coronavirus could be transmitted by mosquitoes. The new coronavirus is a respiratory virus which spreads primarily through droplets generated when an infected person coughs or sneezes, or through droplets of saliva or discharge from the nose. To protect yourself, clean your hands frequently with an alcohol-based hand rub or wash them with soap and water. Also, avoid close contact with anyone who is coughing and sneezing.' (Source: WHO advice-for-public/myth-busters page)

Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and The American Mosquito Control Association (AMCA) both have echoed similar opinion saying that the mosquitoes are not a vector of COVID-19.

Yes, mosquitoes can carry many viruses including dengue, yellow fever, chikungunya, Zika and Ross River virus. Mosquitoes can also carry parasites that cause Malaria. But at the same time, mosquitoes cannot carry HIV viruses that cause AIDS.

The process lies in how mosquitoes digest. Mosquitoes do not suck blood from one person and then push that same blood into some other person. They suck blood in with one tube and push in saliva into the host from another tube. Now, if the mosquito sucks up blood of a person who has a certain virus in their blood, that virus needs to go inside the mosquito's body and infect it first. Once the mosquito gets infected then the virus will reach the salivary gland of the mosquito and thereby has a chance to be pushed into the body of another human being. title: Fact Check: Is Alexis Lorenze's reaction to vaccines a typical vaccine response?
claim_text: A video posted by chiropractor Ben Tapper on X claims that 23-year-old Alexis Lorenze suffered severe symptoms after receiving vaccines for DTaP (Diphtheria, Tetanus, and Pertussis), meningitis, and pneumonia. The video suggests that her condition was caused by these vaccines and represents a typical vaccine reaction.
quick_take: A social media post claims that a woman named Alexis Lorenze suffered a typical vaccine response due to DTaP, meningitis and pneumonia vaccines. Our fact check reveals this is Mostly False.
doctor_explanation: Alexis Lorenze was diagnosed with Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PNH), a rare blood disorder, in January 2024. PNH causes red blood cells to break apart prematurely, leading to complications such as blood clotting. The symptoms Lorenze described—temporary blindness, severe nausea, and nosebleeds—are consistent with PNH, not a typical reaction to vaccines. Vaccines can sometimes trigger reactions in people with underlying conditions like PNH, but these responses are rare and do not represent typical reactions in the general population. Dr Somil Singhal, MBBS, MD, Haematologist, AIIMS, New Delhi, explains: 'In this condition, red blood cells (RBCs) break down prematurely, leading to an excessive release of hemoglobin. People with this disease have blood cells missing a gene called PIG-A. This gene helps certain proteins attach to cells. Without PIG-A, proteins cannot connect to the cell surface to protect the cells by forming a shield against substances in the blood called complement, resulting in the early breakdown of RBCs. The red blood cells leak hemoglobin into the blood, which then passes into the urine, often occurring during the night or early morning.' Regarding vaccine safety for PNH patients: 'Vaccinations are generally safe for PNH patients, but if symptoms worsen, cross-matching is essential. This involves checking for antibodies in the patient that may react with transfused red blood cell antigens. Serum from the patient and red blood cells from the donor are required for this cross-matching procedure.' Dr Somil Singhal also explains the Eculizumab treatment: 'Eculizumab is usually administered to patients in home care itself. The homecare nurse attends the patient's home, sets up an intravenous line, and flushes it with saline. The prescribed amount of eculizumab (10mg/mL) is then mixed with saline and administered over a 30-minute period. After the eculizumab has been infused, the line is flushed again with saline. Throughout the process, blood pressure and temperature are monitored before and after the infusion to check for any changes that might indicate an adverse reaction.' While vaccines can occasionally trigger clotting in individuals with PNH due to their condition, this is specific to her blood disorder and not something that happens to most people after vaccination. Healthy individuals rarely experience such severe side effects from vaccines. The DTaP vaccine, which protects against diphtheria, tetanus, and pertussis, is considered safe for most people. Common side effects include mild reactions such as pain or swelling at the injection site, mild fever, tiredness, or fussiness. In rare cases, individuals may experience moderate side effects such as prolonged crying in children, fever over 40°C, or seizures, though these are temporary and resolve without long-term effects. Severe reactions such as allergic responses are extremely rare. Dr Anusha Dewan, Practising General Physician and Public Health Professional, Jeevan Anmol Hospital, New Delhi, says, 'Vaccines are one of the best ways to keep ourselves and our communities safe from serious diseases. For example, the DTaP vaccine helps protect us from dangerous infections like diphtheria, tetanus, and whooping cough. These diseases can be life-threatening if left unchecked. When people choose not to get vaccinated, it increases the chances of these diseases spreading, putting everyone at risk, especially the most vulnerable. Vaccines keep these infections under control, making them essential for public health.' The claimant, Ben Tapper, is a chiropractor known for spreading vaccine misinformation. He lacks medical qualifications in immunology or vaccinology. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Tapper became infamous for spreading false information about vaccines and masks. In 2021, he was named in the 'Disinformation Dozen' by the Center for Countering Digital Hate, which highlighted him as one of the leading sources of anti-vaccine content online.

title: Fact Check: Is cranberry juice effective for treating stomach ulcers?
claim_text: Cranberry juice can be used to treat stomach ulcers. A YouTube video titled 'You Can Cure Stomach Ulcer With 5 Foods' lists five all-natural ways to treat stomach ulcers with an emphasis on cranberry juice consumption.
verdict_original: Thus, the assertion is mostly false.
quick_take: According to a YouTube video, cranberry juice can be used to treat stomach ulcers. When we fact-checked the accuracy of the claim, we found that it was Mostly False.
doctor_explanation:
When asked General Physician, Dr. Kashyap Dakshini, about whether cranberry juice could be used to treat stomach ulcers, he responded that there is some evidence from some randomised trials that suggests regular cranberry juice consumption may help potentiate the suppression of H. pylori infection, which is known to cause peptic ulcers in susceptible populations. However, more research would be necessary to confirm its use in the treatment of stomach ulcers.

A stomach ulcer is a sore that develops on the lining of the stomach or small intestine. The stomach secretes a potent acid to aid in food digestion and ward off microbes, along with a thick layer of mucus to shield body tissues from this acid. Stomach ulcers occur when the mucus layer becomes worn down and ceases to function properly, allowing stomach acid to damage stomach tissue. The two main contributors to stomach ulcers are H. pylori bacteria and a class of painkillers known as non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). Other causative factors include genetics, smoking, stress, specific foods, and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.

The currently available triple antimicrobial therapy, consisting of two antibiotics and a proton pump inhibitor, can get rid of H. pylori. However, certain studies have demonstrated that the components of cranberry juice inhibit the adhesion of a variety of microbial pathogens, including Helicobacter pylori. Researchers discovered that compounds in cranberry juice inhibited the growth of three different strains of H. pylori. Despite the fact that this effect was significant in naturally infected humans, the rate of eradication was still much lower than that of conventional triple therapy. A recent study discovered that cranberry's polyphenol compounds have the ability to eradicate H. pylori and could support the conventional triple therapy used for the medical management of stomach ulcers, though more research is required. The effect is stronger in females than in males.

Therefore, while cranberry juice could be supportive for conventional triple therapy, and may play a relieving or preventive role for stomach ulcers, it is NOT an established treatment for stomach ulcers. A person may be able to find relief from or prevent the formation of ulcers using some home remedies, but in order to determine the cause and receive medical care, people should visit their doctor. An ulcer treatment strategy can only be developed by a doctor.

title: Fact Check: Is Deepak Chopra promoting a miracle weight loss drink?
claim_text: Deepak Chopra is promoting a miracle weight loss drink and recommending salt elimination for rapid weight loss. Cutting out salt can lead to effortless weight loss of 1–2 kg per day without changes in diet or lifestyle. Additionally, this method eliminates belly fat and makes a person look younger and slimmer within seven days.
quick_take: A social media post claims that Deepak Chopra is promoting a miracle weight loss drink and recommending salt elimination for rapid weight loss. However, this claim is false.
doctor_explanation:
## Is Deepak Chopra a doctor?
Deepak Chopra holds a medical degree and specialised in internal medicine and endocrinology, and he has a history of practicing medicine, including holding positions such as a chief of staff at a hospital. However, he is now primarily recognised as an author and advocate for alternative medicine and spirituality, and he is most widely known for those pursuits. Therefore while possessing medical doctor credentials, his current prominent role is that of an author and speaker, dealing with holistic health topics.
## Did Deepak Chopra promote a weight loss drink or salt elimination for weight loss?
No, there is no credible evidence that Deepak Chopra has endorsed such a weight loss remedy. The video falsely attributes these claims to him and appears to be AI-altered. The original footage, titled The Illusion of Matter, discusses consciousness, neuroscience, and philosophy—not weight loss. The embedded video is available at: https://www.youtube.com/embed/oEwS1XZowj4?feature=oembed&enablejsapi=1. Furthermore, there is no evidence that Rajat Sharma or Deepak Chopra have promoted this remedy on social media, in the news, or on any credible platform. Similarly, other AI-altered videos have falsely claimed that celebrities are endorsing liver detoxes for rapid weight loss, further highlighting the spread of misinformation.
## Can eliminating salt lead to rapid weight loss of 1–2 kg per day?
No, this claim is scientifically inaccurate. While reducing salt intake may cause temporary water loss, it does not lead to significant fat loss. The body retains water when consuming salt, so cutting back may result in mild water weight reduction, but this effect is temporary and unsustainable for long-term fat reduction. Evidence: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6584671/. Moreover, the 'learn more' link in the video redirects to a page selling Scorpion Activ for pain relief, suggesting that the claim is merely a marketing tactic to promote the product. Notably, the video itself fails to provide any actual details about the supposed weight loss remedy.
## Does weight loss depend only on salt intake and not diet or lifestyle?
No, weight loss is influenced by multiple factors, including diet, physical activity, and metabolism. Scientific research consistently shows that sustainable weight loss requires a combination of a balanced diet, calorie control, and physical activity. Eliminating a single nutrient like salt will not lead to permanent fat loss.
## Is there any evidence supporting the seven-day belly fat reduction claim?
No, there is no strong scientific evidence to support this claim. The idea that the body can selectively burn fat from specific areas (spot reduction) remains controversial, with mixed research findings. While some studies suggest minimal effects, most experts agree that targeted fat loss is largely unscientific. Healthy weight loss generally occurs at a rate of 0.5–1 kg per week, making the claim of 1–2 kg per day highly unrealistic and misleading.
## THIP Media Take
The claim that Deepak Chopra is promoting a miracle weight loss drink is false. There is no credible evidence supporting this claim, and the weight loss method described in the video is scientifically unfounded. Furthermore, the post appears to be a misleading advertisement for an unrelated product. Sustainable weight loss requires a balanced diet, physical activity, and overall lifestyle changes—not a drastic and unrealistic salt restriction.

title: Fact Check: Is gender affirmation care a one-time therapeutic session?

doctor_explanation:
Gender affirmation care is a crucial aspect of healthcare that aims to support transgender individuals in aligning with their gender identity. It addresses the health disparities faced by LGBTQIA+ individuals through a comprehensive approach that includes medical, psychological, and social interventions. These interventions may involve hormone therapy and mental health support. It is important to note that gender-affirming care goes beyond medical treatments and encompasses respecting an individual's chosen name and pronouns, creating a safe and inclusive healthcare environment, and providing support for fertility preservation when necessary. Gender affirmation care is essential for creating a more equitable healthcare system by promoting inclusivity, reducing disparities, and improving the well-being of transgender individuals. 

Therapists play a critical role in gender affirmation care. They provide mental health support and facilitate the gender affirmation process, helping establish a safe, comfortable, and tailored therapeutic environment that builds trust and understanding between the therapist and the patient. Therapists also address ethical considerations when it comes to gender-affirming care, which is particularly important when working with transgender and gender-nonconforming (TGNC) youth. This ensures that care is provided in an affirmative and non-discriminatory manner.

Gender-affirming therapy does NOT necessitate just one session. Gender affirmation care is a multifaceted and continuous process that goes beyond a single therapy session. It covers a range of healthcare measures aimed at assisting transgender individuals in living and being recognised in accordance with their gender identity and expression. By offering mental health assistance, addressing emotional wellbeing, and helping people through their gender journey, therapists play a critical part in gender affirmation care. The phase of gender affirmation frequently goes through various stages and might involve hormone therapy, gender-affirming surgery, and social transformation. These actions usually take place over time and necessitate ongoing monitoring and support from healthcare professionals, including therapists. Transgender and gender-nonconforming individuals require ongoing, patient-centred management due to the unique challenges they face.

Dr. Sameer Kalani, Senior Consultant Psychiatrist, HOD Mental Health and Behavioural Sciences, Fortis Memorial and Research Institute, Gurugram, stated: Supporting people who are looking for gender affirmation is a rigorous and continuing process that involves many different forms of healthcare. It is imperative to have a comprehensive and ongoing strategy in order to adequately accompany people on their gender affirmation journey. Hence, it could take more than one appointment to improve their general well-being and affirm their gender identification.

Dr. Manisha Gaur, psychologist, stated: Gender affirmation care involves multiple healthcare elements that call for an ongoing and comprehensive approach. Therapists are essential in supporting individuals throughout their gender affirmation journeys, as it is not a one-time event. The ultimate goal is to improve individuals' overall well-being and validate their gender identity, which requires an ongoing and evolving process.

Regarding safety: Access to gender-affirming care (also known as transition-related care) is an essential aspect of healthcare for individuals who identify as transgender, regardless of their age or gender. title: Is greater burdock root 100 times more effective than chemotherapy?
claim_text: Greater burdock root can destroy cancer cells and is 100 times more effective than chemotherapy.
quick_take: A social media post claims that greater burdock root is 100 times more effective than chemotherapy. We fact checked this claim and found this to be false.
doctor_explanation: No, there is no solid scientific proof that burdock root can kill cancer cells in humans. It contains antioxidants like quercetin, luteolin, and phenolic acids, which may help protect cells from damage. Some lab studies suggest potential anti-cancer properties, but these findings are based on isolated cells, not human trials. A 2023 study on rats found that arctiin, a compound in burdock root, reduced tumour size, slowed cancer growth, and increased survival time. It also helped lower inflammation and prevent cancer cells from spreading. Similarly, a 2019 study on mice showed that burdock root extract reduced inflammation, slowed tumour growth, and improved survival by regulating immune cell activity. However, both studies were conducted on animals, not humans. There is no reliable evidence that burdock root can cure or kill cancer in real-world conditions. Dr P. Rammanohar, Research Director at Amrita School of Ayurveda, Kollam, explains that cancer is a complex group of diseases, each requiring specific treatments. He says, 'Different types of cancer need different treatments, and chemotherapy is carefully developed to target specific cancers. No single drug can treat all cancers.' Dr Pooja Khullar, Radiation Oncologist at Dharamshila Narayana Super Speciality Hospital, New Delhi, emphasises that there is no strong evidence to support burdock root as a cancer treatment. She explains, 'Burdock root is often promoted as a natural remedy, but there is no strong evidence that it can replace proven cancer treatments. While some lab studies suggest potential benefits, these do not translate directly to humans. Relying on burdock root alone could delay effective treatment and make cancer harder to control. It\u2019s always safest to follow treatments backed by solid scientific research.' Is it 100 times more effective than chemotherapy? No, this claim is entirely false. Chemotherapy is a well-researched and medically approved treatment for cancer. While it has side effects, it has been tested in rigorous clinical trials to prove its effectiveness in shrinking tumours and improving survival rates. There is no study comparing burdock root to chemotherapy, let alone proving it to be 100 times more effective. Can burdock root be used as a cancer treatment? No, burdock root is not an approved cancer treatment. Some alternative medicine supporters suggest burdock root as a complementary therapy, meaning it can be used alongside standard treatments to support overall health. However, relying on burdock root alone instead of proven cancer treatments can be dangerous and may allow cancer to spread unchecked. Dr Rakesh Sharma, Senior Consultant and HOD Medical Oncology, SHALBY Sanar International Hospital, Gurugram, explains, 'Chemotherapy is a well-researched and effective cancer treatment when given under expert supervision. While early drugs had toxic origins, modern chemotherapy has advanced significantly and remains a crucial, safe, and proven method to fight cancer.' Are there any risks to using burdock root? Yes, burdock root is generally safe in food or tea, but it carries some risks. It may interact with medications (like diabetes), trigger allergies, and act as a diuretic, increasing dehydration risk. Pregnant women, children, and those allergic to daisies should avoid it. Using it as a cancer treatment instead of medical care is dangerous. Only buy from trusted sources, as it resembles toxic belladonna. Supplements aren\u2019t well-regulated, so it is important to follow medical advice.

title: Fact Check: Is HMPV causing a new pandemic similar to COVID-19 in China?
claim_text: A viral social media post (Instagram) claims that Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) is spreading rapidly in China, causing overcrowded hospitals and high demand for beds. The post labels HMPV as "COVID2.0" and warns of a potential lockdown due to a new pandemic.

doctor_explanation: HMPV (Human Metapneumovirus) is NOT a new virus. It was first discovered in 2001 in the Netherlands and belongs to the same family as respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). HMPV typically causes respiratory illnesses ranging from mild cold-like symptoms to more severe conditions like bronchiolitis or pneumonia, especially in young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. HMPV has been circulating worldwide for decades and is not a newly emerging pathogen. As of now, the World Health Organization (WHO) has not issued an official statement specifically addressing the current state of HMPV cases in China. There is NO evidence of HMPV causing a pandemic in China or anywhere else. While respiratory viruses including HMPV can lead to seasonal outbreaks, they do not spread as widely or severely as COVID-19. The overcrowded hospitals in China shown in the viral video are likely due to seasonal respiratory infections, which are common during winter months. However, there is no data or credible evidence linking these events to an HMPV-driven pandemic. HMPV is not likely to cause widespread outbreaks or require drastic measures like lockdowns. Unlike COVID-19, which spread quickly and caused serious illness worldwide, HMPV is a well-known virus with clear seasonal patterns. It spreads slowly and usually causes mild illness. HMPV spreads like other respiratory viruses such as the flu or RSV, transmitted through respiratory droplets. The virus thrives in colder months, with cases peaking during winter and early spring. Overcrowded spaces and poor ventilation increase the risk of transmission. Preventive measures like good hygiene, wearing masks, and avoiding crowded spaces can reduce the risk of HMPV and other respiratory infections. However, lockdowns are not necessary for controlling HMPV. Regarding India: HMPV cases have been reported in India but are not a cause for concern. As of 7 January 2025, only seven cases have been recorded. Health Minister JP Nadda has assured the public that HMPV is not a new virus and there is no need to panic. Dr Randeep Guleria, former AIIMS Director and Chairman at Medanta Gurugram, explained that HMPV is not a new virus and usually causes mild illness. While it is generally self-limiting, it can lead to pneumonia in infants, the elderly, or those with other health issues, causing breathing problems and hospitalisation. He advised symptomatic treatment, staying hydrated, and avoiding crowded places to prevent the spread. Dr Soumya Swaminathan, former Chief Scientist at the World Health Organisation, reassured the public about HMPV on X: "#HMPV is nothing to panic about. It's a known virus that causes mostly mild respiratory infections." The Union Health Secretary reviewed the situation after reports from China and confirmed there is no unusual rise in cases in India. States have been advised to strengthen monitoring and raise awareness about simple precautions like handwashing, wearing masks in crowded places, and avoiding close contact with sick individuals. The government reassured the public that India is well-prepared to handle any respiratory concerns. Unlike COVID-19, HMPV does not have the potential to cause a pandemic or require lockdowns.

title: Is immunotherapy a better option to chemo in Cancer treatment?
claim_text: According to an Instagram reel, cancer can be managed with immunotherapy. The post further emphasises the detrimental effects of chemotherapy and the need to switch to immunotherapy instead.
quick_take: A social media post suggests that immunotherapy is a better option than chemotherapy. After verifying the assertion, we determined that it is half true. Chemotherapy cannot be completely dismissed — it is a cornerstone of cancer treatment and necessary for aggressive or systemic malignancies. The decision to use immunotherapy versus chemotherapy depends on the patient's stage, severity, and overall well-being.
doctor_explanation: Chemotherapy, often known as systemic therapy, is the mainstay of cancer care. The therapeutic intervention employs the use of cytotoxic drugs to destroy the rapidly dividing cancer cells. In contrast to the localised implications of radiation therapy and surgery, chemotherapy addresses cancer cells that have spread beyond the primary site. The treatment approach works by interfering with rapidly dividing cells. Despite these advantages, chemotherapy often comes with several detrimental effects that require immediate attention. However, this therapy method is associated with enhanced survival rates in certain cancer types, indicating a potential cure. Suggesting immunotherapy as an alternative to chemotherapy is oversimplifying the complexity of cancer treatment. While in certain cases, immunotherapy can be a treatment option, in some other cases chemotherapy is a must. This decision should be made based on the patient's medical condition and cannot be applied as a general rule. Cancer is a progressive, life-threatening condition that needs to be timely addressed. Tumour histology, genetic mutations, disease progression, patient age, comorbidities, and overall health constitute the basis of cancer therapy. Certain localised or premalignant tumours may be addressed by radiation therapy or surgery. In a similar vein, immunotherapies and targeted therapeutics have transformed the curative process of cancer. Chemotherapy, however, remains the cornerstone of cancer treatment and is necessary for aggressive or systemic malignancies, such as lymphomas and leukaemias. Additionally, chemotherapy substantially enhances survival and lowers the risk of cancer recurrence when combined with radiation or surgery. Conversely, refusing chemotherapy when treatment is clearly recommended might result in expedited progression of the condition, diminished survival, and the loss of potentially curative outcomes. Dr. Nishith Vaddeboina, Senior Consultant Medical Oncologist at Renova Century Hospitals in Banjara Hills, Hyderabad, adds more credence to this by stating that while not all cancers need chemotherapy, the type and stage of the condition usually determine the course of treatment. Radiation and surgeries may be beneficial in certain circumstances. Novel approaches such as immunotherapy and targeted therapy may demonstrate benefits for tumours of the liver, kidney, lung, and uterine cancers with fewer adverse effects. Chemotherapy, however, is still essential for many malignancies, particularly those that are aggressive or extensive. Therefore, claiming that cancer may be cured without chemotherapy may be harmful. It is critical to acknowledge that chemotherapy is a more customised therapeutic strategy. By optimising its dosages, combinations, and supportive therapy, related toxicities may be reduced. Chemotherapy is not a universal option; rather, it is a medical decision that is carefully made depending on the particular requirements of each patient. Immunotherapy is a novel treatment that leverages the body's own immune system to fight illnesses, primarily cancer, by enhancing or suppressing immune responses to eliminate abnormal cells. The therapeutic approach makes use of specific medications, antibodies, vaccinations, or even cells that have been customised to help the immune system identify and eliminate disease-causing cells more efficiently. When applied to cancer, the procedure makes use of monoclonal antibodies, CAR T-cell therapy, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and cancer vaccines, which improve immune surveillance and target tumour cells specifically. While immunotherapy has improved the prognosis for several cancers, including melanoma, non-small cell lung cancer, and certain haematologic malignancies, chemotherapy cannot always be replaced with immunotherapy. This could be explained by the direct cytotoxic effects of the chemotherapy and its apparent efficacy in rapidly reducing the tumour load. Dr. Nishith Vaddeboina further elucidates the role of immunotherapy in the management of cancer by pointing out that immunotherapy can substitute chemotherapy for some malignancies but not all of them. Chemotherapy is still frequently used either by itself or in conjunction with immunotherapy to achieve enhanced outcomes. Furthermore, he emphasises that while immunotherapy usually has fewer side effects than chemotherapy, it is not completely free of them. Since it activates the immune system, it can sometimes cause immunological-related reactions that impact the liver, lungs, or skin. The effects are less common and often manageable if caught early. Treatment decisions are always made based on the cancer type and the patient's profile. It is crucial to understand that the intervention is most effective when paired with chemotherapy, radiation therapy, or targeted medications. However, there are risks linked with this procedure, including those that could impact the lungs, gastrointestinal tract, endocrine organs, or skin. Just like any other therapeutic approach, chemotherapy has downsides. While these adverse effects vary based on the type of medication, dosage, and individual patient characteristics, some of them include fatigue, nausea, hair loss, immunosuppression, and organ toxicity. Maintaining stringent oral and personal hygiene, following a nutritious, medically regulated diet, ensuring optimal hydration, and undergoing routine medical evaluations can all help reduce the severity of chemotherapy-related side effects. Dr. Roma Kumar, Senior Consultant Psychologist at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital and Max Hospital in New Delhi, lends more support to this in an interview with THIP Media, emphasising that cancer therapy is beyond medical management. She advises that, apart from controlling the symptoms, the psychology of the patients also needs to be addressed. This mostly entails acknowledging that their emotions of dread, despair, and helplessness are normal and that they are not facing this challenge alone. Furthermore, giving patients the freedom to make decisions such as – what to eat, when to sleep, or who will accompany them to the hospital – could help them regain their sense of control and self-confidence. We do not intend to downplay the fact that, like any other therapeutic method, chemotherapy is associated with side effects; the patients undergoing the intervention need to be both physically and mentally fit; however, we cannot dispute its life-saving effectiveness. Cancer is a potentially dangerous illness, and refusing or skipping treatment when advised can have fatal consequences.

title: Is inflammation the root cause of every mental health disorder?
claim_text: Cortisol triggers inflammation, which is the root cause of all mental health disorders. Dietary changes can manage cortisol levels and 'heal' mental health conditions.
quick_take: A social media post claims that inflammation is the root cause of every mental health disorder. After careful fact-checking, we found this claim to be mostly false.
doctor_explanation: Cortisol, often called the 'stress hormone,' is produced by the adrenal glands and helps regulate stress, blood sugar, and the immune system. Cortisol has both pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory effects. When cortisol spikes temporarily (as during acute stress), it can reduce inflammation. However, chronic stress can disrupt cortisol levels, potentially increasing inflammation over time. Scientific evidence supports this nuanced role, but it is inaccurate to claim cortisol always 'causes' inflammation. Inflammation is not the root cause of all mental health disorders. Some studies link inflammation to certain conditions like depression, bipolar disorder, and schizophrenia. However, mental health disorders arise from a mix of factors, including genetics, life experiences, and brain chemistry. Anxiety disorders often stem from overactivity in brain circuits, while OCD has strong genetic and neurological links. Oversimplifying these complex conditions as solely inflammation-driven is misleading. Nutrition alone cannot treat mental health conditions. While diet influences mental health, it is not a substitute for treatments like therapy or medication. Nutrients like omega-3 fatty acids, B vitamins, and antioxidants can support mental well-being but work best as part of a broader treatment plan. The claim that managing inflammation through diet can 'heal' conditions like ADHD or OCD does not have scientific evidence and could delay necessary medical treatment, making symptoms worse. Inflammation is a factor—but not the only one—in mental health. Research shows that some people with depression or other conditions have elevated levels of inflammatory markers, like C-reactive protein (CRP) or cytokines. This supports the 'inflammatory hypothesis of depression.' However, not everyone with mental health disorders has inflammation, and not everyone with inflammation develops mental health issues. Reducing inflammation may help relieve symptoms for some individuals. Strategies like eating anti-inflammatory foods (fruits, vegetables, nuts, and fatty fish), exercising regularly, and managing stress through yoga or meditation can be beneficial—but these lifestyle changes should complement, not replace, medical treatments. Dr. Roma Kumar, Senior Consultant Psychologist at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital & Max Hospital, New Delhi, says: 'Inflammation isn't the cause of all mental health disorders. While it can contribute to conditions like depression or anxiety, mental health issues are usually caused by a mix of factors, including genetics, life experiences, and brain chemistry. Other factors like stress, trauma, and imbalances in brain chemicals also play a big role. Effective treatment involves addressing all of these factors, not just focusing on inflammation.' Dr. Swati Dave, PhD in Food and Nutrition, explains: 'Nutrition is an important part of supporting mental health, as certain nutrients like omega-3s, B vitamins, and antioxidants can positively influence brain function and mood. However, it is not a standalone solution. Mental health conditions are complex and often require a combination of approaches, including therapy, medication, and lifestyle changes. While a well-balanced diet can complement these treatments, it's essential to seek personalised care from healthcare professionals for effective management.' The THIP Media Take states: 'The claim that inflammation is the root cause of every mental health disorder is mostly false. While inflammation may contribute to some conditions, it's not the universal cause. Mental health disorders involve biological, psychological, and social factors. Effective treatment often requires a combination of approaches, including therapy, medication, and lifestyle adjustments—not just dietary changes.'

title: Fact Check: Is Pfizer's rennet for cheese production harmful to your health?
claim_text: Pfizer's bioengineered rennet (fermentation-produced chymosin, FPC) used in cheese production is harmful to human health. The pharmaceutical industry is motivated by profit and is intentionally using this rennet in cheese production to make people sick so they can earn more profit.
quick_take: A Facebook reel claims that Pfizer's bioengineered rennet used in cheese production is harmful to human health. Our fact check reveals it's False.
doctor_explanation: Pfizer rennet, especially the bioengineered version, is an important enzyme used in the cheese-making process. This enzyme, chymosin, curdles casein—a milk protein—separating milk into solid curds and liquid whey. This process is essential for transforming milk into cheese. Traditionally, rennet was obtained from the stomach lining of ruminant animals, but Pfizer's bioengineered rennet offers an efficient alternative. The US FDA approved rennet as the first bioengineered food product in 1990. Pfizer rennet, or fermentation-produced chymosin (FPC), is made through a fermentation process involving genetically modified microbes engineered to produce chymosin. Despite the use of genetic modification, the final enzyme is identical to the naturally occurring one found in animals, ensuring it is safe for use in cheese. There is no scientific evidence to support the claim that Pfizer's rennet is harmful to human health. FPC is classified by the US FDA as 'Generally Recognized As Safe' (GRAS). This classification confirms the safety of Pfizer rennet in cheese production, as it has been rigorously evaluated for safety. The enzyme produced through the FPC process is chymosin. It is the same as the enzyme naturally produced in the stomachs of ruminant animals. The final product used in cheese-making is purified chymosin, which has been proven safe for human consumption. There have been no credible reports of health issues directly linked to the consumption of cheese made with Pfizer's rennet. Scientific research or health authorities do not support the claim that FPC or bioengineered rennet is harmful. On the contrary, FPC has been used in cheese production for decades without any evidence of adverse health effects. According to the EFSA (European Food Safety Authority) CEF Panel (2009), chymosin produced via fermentation has been evaluated and found safe. The evidence overwhelmingly supports the safety of Pfizer rennet in cheese production. Rennet, whether derived from animals or produced through fermentation, is a catalyst in the cheese-making process. It is not present in significant amounts in the final cheese product, and the enzyme itself is broken down during digestion. Therefore, concerns about the safety of Pfizer rennet in cheese are baseless. The claim appears to stem from misunderstanding of bioengineering and its applications in food production. THIP Media Take: The claim that Pfizer's rennet used in cheese production is harmful to human health is false. Scientific evidence and expert opinions confirm that the safety of Pfizer rennet in cheese production is well-established. The fear mongering around this issue appears to come from misinformation.

Facelifts, also known as rhytidectomy, involve tightening facial skin and tissues to create a more youthful and harmonious appearance without removing tissue from others. They are usually performed under local or general anaesthesia, with a recovery time of about two weeks. Facial aesthetic surgery is growing globally, with India leading in this field.

In contrast, face transplants are intricate surgeries performed on patients who have suffered severe facial injuries or disfigurements, often due to trauma, burns, or congenital defects. They involve the surgical replacement of facial tissues—including skin, muscles, and bones—from a deceased donor. These life-changing surgeries aim to restore essential functions like speaking and eating, allowing individuals to regain a sense of normalcy. Face transplants are extremely rare and are reserved for cases where individuals have life-altering injuries that cannot be treated with traditional reconstructive methods. Since 2005, only around 47 face transplants have been performed worldwide, with just one in China. Face transplants require patients to take a lifelong course of immunosuppressants to prevent the body from rejecting the transplanted tissue. This important aspect of the procedure highlights the serious medical implications and risks involved, making it unsuitable for mere cosmetic desires. The claim about face transplants for cosmetic enhancements seems false.

Dr Ekansh Shekhar, Dermatologist, Cosmetologist, Trichologist, and Aesthetic Medicine Consultant, Lucknow, adds that it is important to know the differences between facelifts and face transplants. Facelifts are cosmetic surgeries that aim to improve how someone looks by tightening the skin and reducing signs of ageing. This can help boost a person's confidence and overall happiness. Surgeons generally consider these surgeries safe and design them for healthy people who want to enhance their natural appearance. In contrast, face transplants are reserved for individuals who have suffered serious facial injuries, such as severe burns or trauma from accidents. These surgeries are complex and require a long recovery time, as they aim to restore both the appearance and function of the face. The idea of harvesting children's faces is not only baseless but also deeply concerning. The viral video does not provide any evidence to substantiate such claims. Instead, it showcases women recovering from facelift surgeries, while any references to children seem sensationalised for shock value. Misinformation—like false claims about harvesting children's faces—can be very harmful. Such untrue stories can create fear and confusion about cosmetic surgery, making people hesitant to consider safe and effective options that could truly improve their lives. In the case of cosmetic surgeries, patients seeking facelifts are generally in good health and have no underlying traumatic injuries. They simply wish to rejuvenate their appearance. The recovery process for facelift patients involves managing swelling and bruising, and they do not face the same life-threatening complications that face transplant patients might endure.

Diabetes management requires a comprehensive, individualised approach under medical guidance.'

Dr Ubaid ur Rahman, General Physician at Holy Mission Clinic, New Delhi, says: 'Diabetes is a long-term condition that needs ongoing management. Effective management involves a combination of medication, dietary adjustments, and regular monitoring.'

Dr Anusha Dewan, Practising General Physician and Public Health Professional, Jeevan Anmol Hospital, New Delhi, states: 'Managing the condition involves consistent treatment with prescribed medications, lifestyle modifications, and regular check-ups. title: Fact Check: Is Trump advising against lockdowns amidst Mpox outbreak?
claim_text: Former US President Donald Trump is advising against lockdowns and vaccine mandates to combat the 2024 Mpox outbreak, and that these health measures could be used to manipulate the upcoming 2024 US presidential election.
quick_take: A social media video shows Donald Trump advising against lockdowns and vaccine mandates in response to the 2024 Mpox outbreak. Our fact check says it's False.
doctor_explanation: The claim that Trump is advising against lockdowns tied to the 2024 Mpox outbreak is false. The viral video in question is from August 2023, over a year before the current Mpox outbreak. It features Trump speaking about the return of COVID-19 safety measures such as mask mandates, lockdowns, and vaccine requirements due to rising concerns over the spread of new COVID-19 variants like EG.5 (Eris) and BA.2.86 (Pirola). At the time, several institutions across the US reintroduced some of these protective measures to control the spread. Trump strongly opposed these measures. He further alleged that they were politically motivated and would possibly affect the outcome of the 2024 US election. He emphasised that people should resist any attempts to enforce lockdowns and vaccine mandates. Trump further said that they would take away personal freedoms. At no point in the video does Trump mention Mpox, which is why the claim linking this video to the Mpox outbreak 2024 is false. There is no factual connection between the Mpox outbreak and the upcoming US election. The World Health Organization (WHO) declared a global health emergency related to Mpox in August 2024. This declaration was mainly in response to a spike in cases across Africa. The timing of the video resurfacing caused some confusion, as it happened when people were already starting to worry about the new Mpox cases. The 2024 Mpox outbreak has become a growing concern, particularly in parts of Africa, where over 27,000 cases have been reported and more than 1,100 deaths have occurred, primarily in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The disease has spread to other countries, including Sweden, Pakistan, and the Philippines. Despite this, health officials stress that the risk of a large-scale outbreak in India remains low at this time. Mpox spreads mainly through close contact with infected individuals, their bodily fluids, or contaminated surfaces. Unlike COVID-19, which can spread rapidly through the air, Mpox is not airborne. In fact, Mpox spreads more through direct physical contact which makes it less likely to cause widespread outbreaks. Public health measures such as lockdowns and vaccine mandates are put in place to limit the spread of diseases and protect populations. Some political figures, including Trump, argue that such measures can be used for political control. But, there is no confirmed evidence to support the claim that health guidelines are manipulated for electoral gain. The politicisation of public health measures like vaccines, masks and hand hygiene lead to hesitancy among the public. This eventually weakens efforts to curb any disease, especially in a health emergency scenario. Public health agencies like the WHO and various national governments make decisions on the basis of scientific data and evidence, rather than political motives.

title: Is wearing AirPods like having a microwave on your head?
claim_text: AirPods emit the same frequency as microwave ovens (2.4 GHz), making them as harmful as microwaves. The post links AirPods to brain tumours, brain fog, Alzheimer's disease, and other neurodegenerative disorders, suggesting that electromagnetic fields (EMF) from these devices are dangerous for brain health, and advises people to throw away their AirPods.
quick_take: A social media post claims that wearing AirPods is like having a microwave on your head. Our fact check reveals that this is false.
doctor_explanation:
DOCTOR 1 — Dr Pooja Khullar, Radiation Oncologist, Dharamshila Narayana Super Speciality Hospital, New Delhi:
"No, AirPods do not cause brain tumours or cancer. They use low-level radiation that is too weak to damage cells or DNA. Studies have not found any clear link between using wireless devices like AirPods and brain cancer. There's no need to worry about them causing cancer. However, it's a good idea to limit their use to protect your ears. Listening at high volumes for long periods can harm your hearing. Using them in moderation is the safest approach."

DOCTOR 2 — Dr Almas Fatma, MBBS, Diploma in Family Medicine, PG in Digital Health, General Physician, Navi Mumbai:
"No, there's no need to throw away your AirPods for safety reasons. They use low-level radiation that is considered safe by international health standards. However, it's smart to use them in moderation to avoid ear strain or hearing problems from loud volumes. Taking regular breaks and keeping the volume at a safe level is the best way to use them safely."

SCIENTIFIC EVIDENCE CITED:
1. WHO states that RF radiation from Bluetooth devices is non-ionising, meaning it does not damage DNA or cause cancer. (https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/radiation-electromagnetic-fields)

2. IARC classified RF radiation as possibly carcinogenic in 2011, but this was based on limited evidence from heavy mobile phone use — not low-level Bluetooth devices. AirPods emit much lower RF levels compared to mobile phones. (https://www.iarc.who.int/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/pr208_E.pdf)

3. The National Cancer Institute and the UK Million Women Study found no consistent link between RF radiation from wireless devices and brain cancer. (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19959779/ and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35350069/)

4. Cancer Research UK states that the evidence does not support a connection between Bluetooth devices and cancer.

5. A 2010 study (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20061638/) found no evidence that high-frequency EMF exposure is harmful and even suggested that long-term EMF exposure might improve memory and protect against Alzheimer's in mice, though applicability to humans is unclear.

6. A 2022 study (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9738318/) showed that genes, environment, and behaviour all affect life expectancy and disease risk. Environmental and behavioural stressors can trigger genetic risks, but EMF's role is not established. Research on EMF's effects on neurological diseases is too varied to give clear answers. EMF might protect against stress or cause harm, but no solid proof exists.

KEY SCIENTIFIC DISTINCTION:
Microwave ovens use high-powered electromagnetic radiation to heat food. AirPods emit low-energy radiofrequency (RF) radiation. The power from AirPods is much lower and is considered safe by international standards. US FCC and ICNIRP ensure that RF exposure from Bluetooth devices stays within safe limits. Brain fog is usually linked to stress, poor sleep, or health issues, not EMF exposure. Alzheimer's disease occurs mainly due to genetics, lifestyle, and environmental factors like age and family history. No credible studies show that radiation from AirPods or Bluetooth devices causes Alzheimer's or other brain disorders. If headaches or ear pain occur, it is likely due to fit, volume, or prolonged use, not EMF exposure.

title: Miracle Mineral Solution cannot cure diseases; Do not drink it
claim_text: Drinking my miracle mineral solution. It has cured my autism, parasites and depression. You should too.
quick_take: A Facebook post claims that a Miracle Mineral Solution can cure various diseases such as autism, parasites and depression. We did a fact check and found that this claim is false.
doctor_explanation: Miracle Mineral Solution (MMS), also known as Miracle Mineral Supplement or Master Mineral Solution, is a concoction made by mixing sodium chlorite with an acid like citrus juice or vinegar to produce chlorine dioxide. This industrial bleaching agent has been misleadingly marketed as a cure for diseases such as HIV, cancer, and the common cold. However, chlorine dioxide is a toxic chemical that can cause severe side effects, including nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and dangerously low blood pressure due to dehydration. Sodium chlorite, which is used to create chlorine dioxide, is also harmful if ingested and can lead to acute kidney failure and serious gastrointestinal problems. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency has set a maximum safe level of chlorine dioxide in drinking water at 0.8 mg/L. There is no scientific evidence to support the claim that MMS can cure any disease. title: Fact Check: Should you avoid fever medications and use warm water therapy instead?
claim_text: A viral Instagram post advises against using antipyretic drugs during a fever due to their alleged severe side effects. The video claims these medications are "the worst in the world" and can cause kidney failure, liver damage, and brain damage. Instead, it recommends immersing the legs in warm water and drinking warm water simultaneously to lower fever in one attempt, stating this is a safer and better method than using medications.
quick_take: A social media post claims that you should avoid antipyretic drugs and use warm water therapy instead during a fever. Our fact check concludes that this claim is False.
doctor_explanation:
**What are antipyretic drugs?**
Antipyretic drugs, like paracetamol (acetaminophen) and ibuprofen, are medications that reduce fever. They act by lowering the body's temperature set point, which helps relieve discomfort. These medications are widely used and are generally considered safe when taken as directed. Fever is often a symptom of infections, and antipyretics help to make the patient feel better, though they do not treat the underlying cause of the fever.

**Do antipyretic drugs have severe side effects?**
No, when taken correctly, antipyretic drugs do not lead to severe side effects. However, misuse can cause serious health issues. For example, an overdose of paracetamol can harm the liver, but this risk is avoidable by following dosage guidelines. It's important to remember that while ibuprofen can affect kidney function, this risk primarily concerns those with pre-existing kidney problems. Additionally, there is a popular home remedy that suggests using basil leaves and black pepper to treat fever as an alternative to medications. While some people may find this helpful, it is still not a proven cure for fever at home.

Dr Kashyap Dakshini, General Physician from Mumbai, says, "Paracetamol is considered the safest antipyretic for treating fever. While other drugs like ibuprofen and NSAIDs also have antipyretic effects, it is important to use them with caution. Taking these drugs for prolonged periods can lead to adverse effects on the stomach, liver, and kidneys. It is not recommended to use NSAIDs in individuals with kidney problems, stomach ulcers, liver conditions, or cardiac issues."

**Can warm water immersion replace fever medications?**
Not quite. Soaking your feet in warm water can bring temporary comfort, but it won't actually lower your body temperature. Drinking warm water helps keep you hydrated, but it doesn't lower a fever either. For effective fever management, antipyretic drugs are still the most reliable choice.

The study (mentioned in the video) claiming that warm water foot immersion can lower body temperature by about 1.1°F suggests it might be a simple, non-drug approach for managing mild fevers. However, the study has significant limitations: it involved a small group of patients with only mild to moderate fever, and it did not compare the method directly with standard fever medications. While the therapy might offer some comfort, it is not as effective or well-studied as antipyretics, which are safe when used correctly. Therefore, relying solely on warm water therapy is not recommended, especially for persistent or high fevers.

**What are the risks of untreated fever?**
Untreated fever, especially when temperatures exceed 39°C (102°F) or persist for several days, can lead to serious complications. Ignoring a fever may result in dehydration, confusion, or febrile seizures in children. Elevated body temperature can cause inflammation and harm various organs. In the gastrointestinal tract, it may damage gut function and reduce blood flow. The kidneys can experience decreased function and a higher risk of acute kidney injury, particularly in athletes. Additionally, the cardiovascular system may be affected, resulting in low blood pressure and irregular heart rhythms that can harm the heart.

High temperatures can cause problems with thinking and memory, and some people may have long-lasting brain issues. The liver can get damaged too, and in serious cases, a transplant might be needed. Additionally, high fever can affect blood clotting, leading to problems in various organs. Fever often signals underlying infections, so managing it is important for both comfort and diagnosis.

Dr Ubaid ur Rahman, General Physician, Holy Mission Clinic, New Delhi, says, "Untreated fever can pose significant health risks. If a fever is high or lasts more than a couple of days, it can lead to dehydration and even serious conditions like confusion or seizures in young children. Fever is often a signal that something more serious is going on in the body. It's essential to monitor it closely and consult a healthcare professional to ensure appropriate management and prevent complications."

**Are antipyretic drugs truly among the 'worst in the world' for side effects?**
No, this statement is misleading. Antipyretic drugs, when used properly, are safe and among the most commonly prescribed medications. Paracetamol and ibuprofen have been extensively studied, and their side effects are well-known. Misusing these drugs can lead to issues, but that reflects poor usage, not a flaw in the medication itself.

**THIP Media Take:** The claim that antipyretic drugs should be avoided due to severe side effects is false. These medications are safe for managing fever when used as directed. Warm water immersion is not scientifically proven to reduce fever effectively. Always consult healthcare professionals for guidance on fever management.

title: Should you stay at home if you get vaccinated against the flu?
claim_text: Folks who get flu shots please have some courtesy and stay home for a minimum of 2 weeks while you are an active live walking virus. Also don't hug others and give kisses and please immediately tell others you were vaccinated so they don't come close to you.
quick_take: A viral post doing rounds on social media claims that if people get vaccinated by flu shots, it will cause them to be contagious. It further claims that such people should stay at home for a minimum of 2 weeks as they have an active live walking virus. Upon investigation, we found the viral post to be false.
doctor_explanation: We started our investigation and found some information about flu shots on the official website of the Government of Canada. The official website states that the flu shot is your best defence against the flu. It was further mentioned that a flu shot is recommended for everyone 6 months and older and that the flu shot is safe and one can't get the flu from a flu shot. We also found an article on Harvard Medical School's official website. The article suggested that the flu shot is made of an inactivated virus that cannot transmit infection. It takes a week or two to get protection from the vaccine. As per Dr Ubaid ur Rahman, a General Physician, from Holy Mission Clinic, New Delhi, this claim is false. He says, 'Vaccines help develop immunity and contain a version of the virus or bacteria that has been weakened so that it does not cause serious disease in people with healthy immune systems. In fact, it gives immunity to the body by producing antibodies. The claim which states that people who get vaccinated will be contagious for some weeks is fake.' According to the website of U.S. Department of Health & Human Services, vaccines help develop immunity by imitating an infection. This type of infection, however, almost never causes illness, but it does cause the immune system to produce T-lymphocytes and antibodies. Sometimes, after getting a vaccine, the imitation infection can cause minor symptoms, such as fever. Such minor symptoms are normal and should be expected as the body builds immunity. It was nowhere mentioned that the person who has got the vaccine can transfer the virus to someone he hugs or kisses or comes in contact with. Flu shots do not make people contagious. New strains emerge each year, which can make the previous year's vaccine less effective. Consequently, the vaccine is updated annually to target the most prevalent and virulent strains expected for the coming flu season. Moreover, the immune protection provided by the vaccine diminishes over time, making annual vaccinations vital for maintaining strong immunity. This is especially important for protecting high-risk groups such as children, the older people, and those with chronic health conditions. If you experience minor symptoms like a sore arm, low-grade fever, or slight fatigue after receiving a flu shot, these are usually normal signs of your immune system responding to the vaccine. Such symptoms should not be mistaken for contagion and usually resolve within a few days without the need for isolation. Yes, it is safe to be around vulnerable groups such as infants, pregnant women, and the older people after receiving a flu shot. The vaccine does not contain a live virus and therefore cannot spread the flu. Getting vaccinated is actually a proactive measure to protect these vulnerable populations from the flu.

title: Fact Check: Smallpox treatment MR – VAC, a slow poison for children?
claim_text: A post is widely circulated across social media warning people not to use the newly invented injection MR – VAC as it is a slow poison for their children and has been banned in many countries.
quick_take: A message is circulating on social media claiming that a newly invented injection for smallpox treatment MR – VAC is a slow poison for children and has been banned in many countries. We investigated and found that the message was false.
doctor_explanation: MR – VAC is a vaccine manufactured by the Serum Institute of India Pvt. Ltd. It is designed to protect against measles and rubella, two highly contagious viral diseases. The vaccine is a live attenuated virus vaccine, meaning it contains weakened forms of the measles and rubella viruses that stimulate the immune system to develop immunity without causing the diseases. Measles is a highly infectious viral disease that primarily affects children and can lead to serious complications such as pneumonia, encephalitis, and even death. Symptoms include high fever, cough, runny nose, red eyes, and a characteristic red rash that usually starts on the face and spreads to the rest of the body. Rubella, also known as German measles, is a contagious viral infection that is generally mild in children but can cause severe birth defects if a pregnant woman contracts the virus. Symptoms include a rash, fever, sore throat, and swollen lymph nodes. Both diseases are preventable through vaccination, making MR – VAC an essential tool in public health. No, MR – VAC is not a slow poison for children. It is a licensed vaccine for measles and rubella, not for smallpox. This vaccine is safe and well-tolerated according to the Serum Institute of India (SII), WHO, and UNICEF. THIP searched about the medicine MR – VAC on Google search and found that the medicine has been manufactured by SERUM INSTITUTE OF INDIA PVT. LTD. Upon visiting the company's website, the medicine's route of administration, safety information, its composition and immunisation schedule was clearly stated. It was mentioned that the medicine MR-VAC is recommended and is highly safe and well tolerated. The description also stated that all side effects of the medicine are usually transient and resolve completely. THIP further searched about the medicine and found that MR – VAC has been listed on the official website of World Health Organization (WHO). As per UNICEF, MR- VAC is a licensed vaccine. It is for measles rubella and not for smallpox. It is also among the WHO prequalified vaccines. The medicine is safe to use. The confusion may arise from the name similarity and lack of public awareness about vaccine types and their specific uses. Measles and rubella are distinct from smallpox, which has its vaccine known as the smallpox vaccine. Understanding the difference is important for avoiding misinformation. Yes, MR-VAC is safe for children. As per the Serum Institute of India and validated by WHO and UNICEF, the vaccine is well-tolerated, and any side effects are temporary. Its prequalification by WHO further ascertains its safety profile and effectiveness. The side effects of MR-VAC are generally mild and temporary. They may include minor reactions such as redness or swelling at the injection site, mild fever, or rash. These side effects usually resolve on their own without requiring medical intervention. Addressing vaccine misinformation involves making the public aware about the importance of vaccines, their safety, and their role in preventing diseases. Engaging with healthcare professionals and trusted organisations like WHO can help dispel myths and provide correct health information. Vaccines have been pivotal in saving lives and eradicating diseases like Smallpox (1980), Polio (2014), Plague, Rinderpest (the Cattle Plague), Yaws and Maternal And Neonatal Tetanus (2015) in India.

title: Social media posts claim masks can cause Hypoxia. What's the truth?
claim_text: Prolonged wearing of face masks causes hypoxia, oxygen deficiency in the body, and fatigue. The claim does not mention the type of mask (N95, Surgical, Homemade, etc.) — it is a blanket advisory against wearing masks in general for prolonged periods.
